children.translated_text: <s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness)
<s>Āpastamba Śulbasūtra</s> together with the commentary of <s>Kapardi</s>

children.text:
uktā yajñāḥ /
teṣāṃ agnyāyatanāni niyatapramāṇāni niyatadeśāni /
children.translated_text: The sacrifices have been described. Their fire-altars (<s>agnyāyatanas</s>) have fixed dimensions and fixed locations.
Wishing to state their lengths and breadths, he says — "the procedures of construction" —
We shall explain the <s>vihārayogas</s> (procedures of construction). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.1]

children.text: vihiyante 'sminnagnaya iti vihārāḥ prāgvaṃśādayo gārha patyādayaś ca /
children.translated_text: That in which the fires are placed is a <s>vihāra</s> (construction-ground) — namely the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (east-facing hall) and the like, and the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) and the like.

children.text:
yujyate 'neneti yogaḥ rajjuviśeṣaḥ /
vihārāṇāṃ yogo vihārayogaḥ /
viharaṇameva vā vihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: That by which [something] is connected is a <s>yoga</s> (instrument) — a particular kind of cord. The <s>yoga</s> of the <s>vihāras</s> is the <s>vihārayoga</s>. Or, <s>vihāra</s> is the act of construction itself.

children.text:
teṣāṃ yogo vihārayogaḥ /
tasya kṛtsnaṃ pratipādanamityarthaḥ /
yogāniti bahuvacanaṃ bahubhiḥ prakārairdarśayitum /
darśanaṃ ca prādhānya pratipacyartham /
yathā rathādayo niyatāṅgapramāṇā ekasiminn aṅge 'pi mātrayā vihīyamāne samyakū na gacchanti evamagnyāyata nādīnyapi mātrayā vihīyamānāni sādhanabhāvaṃ na gacchanti tasmādyatnena sampādanīyāni. sarvatra vijñāyata iti śrutīnāmupanyāsātsarvathā āyāmādaya iktaireva margaiḥsamyaksampādanīyāḥ /
āyatanānāṃ bhreṣe ca prāyaśvittena bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: Their <s>yoga</s> is the <s>vihārayoga</s>. The meaning is: the complete exposition of that. The plural "yogān" [is used] to indicate [that they will be] demonstrated in many ways. And the demonstration is for the purpose of [establishing] primacy. Just as chariots and the like, having fixed proportions of their limbs, do not function properly when even one limb deviates even slightly in measure, so too fire-altars and the like, when deviating even slightly in measure, do not attain the status of being instruments [of sacrifice]; therefore they must be accomplished with care. Since the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedic texts) are cited everywhere [saying] "it is known," the lengths and the like must be properly accomplished by the prescribed methods alone. And in case of error in the altars, an expiatory rite must be performed.

children.text: amumevārthaṃ pradarśayituṃ śulbāntare "athātaḥ' śabdau prayuktau--"athāto vihārayogān' iti /
children.translated_text: To demonstrate this very point, in another <s>Śulba</s> [text], the words "atha ataḥ" (now, therefore) are employed — "now, therefore, the procedures of construction."

children.text:
āditastāvaddiśāṃ grahaṇaṃ vaktavyamanenāyāryeṇa noktam /
tacchulbāntarato grāhyam /
""kṛttikāḥ khalvimāḥ prācīṃ diśaṃ na paricahati /
tāsāṃ darśanena māpayedityekam /
śroṇādarśa nena māpayedityekam /
citnāsvātyorantarālenetyaparam /
"iti bhagapatā bodhāyanena prāgvaṃśamānamadhikṛtyoktam /
kṛttikādayo yatra nilīyante sā prācī digiti citrāsvātyor madhye udakamapasthāpya pradibimbaṃ dṛṣṭva grāhyam /
atha vā yatra devayajanaṃ, mṛjjalena taṃ deśaṃ samīkṛtya madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya śaṅkupramāṇayā ravjjā maṇḍalaṃ parilikhya śaṅkucchā yāgraṃ pūrvāhne yatra maṇḍalalekhāṃ spṛśati tatra śaṅkuṃ nihatya nirgamavelāyāṃ cāparahṇe /
tau pūrvāparau /
sūkṣmamicchan śvobhūte-pūrvāhte śaṅkucchāyāgrarekhāyāmeva lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkulakṣaṇayorantarālaṃ pratīcyāṃ diśi yaḥśaṅkuḥ taṃ pratsapasārayet upakramadeśaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: First, the determination of the cardinal directions must be stated; this was not stated by the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) here. That must be taken from another <s>Śulba</s> [text]. "These <s>Kṛttikās</s> (Pleiades) do not deviate from the eastern direction. One [method] is to measure by their sighting. One [method] is to measure by the sighting of <s>Śroṇā</s> (Aquila). Another is by the interval between <s>Citrā</s> (Spica) and <s>Svātī</s> (Arcturus)." Thus said the venerable <s>Baudhāyana</s> with reference to the measurement of the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (east-facing hall). The direction where the <s>Kṛttikās</s> and the like set is the eastern direction; [or] by placing water between <s>Citrā</s> and <s>Svātī</s> and observing the reflection, it should be determined. Alternatively, where the sacrificial ground is to be [prepared], leveling that place with wet clay, fixing a <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon) in the center, drawing a circle with a cord equal in length to the gnomon, [observing] where the tip of the gnomon's shadow touches the circle's outline in the forenoon — there fix a gnomon, and similarly in the afternoon at the time of exit. Those [two points] are east and west. One desiring precision should, the next day in the forenoon, make a mark on the line of the gnomon-shadow-tip, and from the interval between the gnomon and the mark, [extending] in the western direction, the gnomon which [was there] — he should move it back toward the starting point.
Commentary on the <s>Āpastamba Śulbasūtra</s> called <s>Karavindīyā</s>
I salute the One known by the single syllable <s>Om</s>, beyond the reach of speech and mind.

children.text: paśyanti kavayo yaddhi tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: That which the seers behold — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, having the complexion of a flax-flower, eternal,
may that light, lotus-eyed, be in my heart always.
Salutation to the sage <s>Āpastamba</s>, the ground of Vedic meaning,
to whose <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms) the maidens of sacrificial <s>Śruti</s> (revelation) are attached.
This commentary on the <s>Śulbasūtra</s> of that [sage], illuminating the meaning of [each] syllable,
is now composed by the lord of <s>Karavinda</s>, following the view of the <s>bhāṣya</s>-author.

children.text:
yajñavyākhyāpratijñāṃ kurvatā bhagavatā'pastambena vyākhyeyatayā haviryajñāḥ somayajñāḥ pākayajñāś ca pratijñātā vyākhyātāś ca /
tatra tāvadaiṣṭikasaumikapāśubandhikadārvīhaumikāḥ samaviṣama dhanirmaṇḍalacaturaśratrayaśranānāśrayo gārhapatyāyatanaprabhṛticityeṣṭakāparyantā niyataparimaṇadeśaviśeṣāstatratatroktāḥ, te 'pi mātavyā iti tadvimānaṃ prati sādhanabhūtaravjjādīnāṃ sādhanabhūtasyaitāvatī rajjuretāvataḥ kṣetrasya karaṇīti svarūpamātreṇa jñātumaśakyatvāttatpratipādanamapaśyaṃ kartavyamiti yajñavyākhyānānantaraṃ vihārayogavyākhyā kriyate--
children.translated_text: When the venerable <s>Āpastamba</s> undertook to explain the sacrifices, he promised and explained the <s>haviryajñas</s> (oblation-sacrifices), <s>somayajñas</s> (Soma-sacrifices), and <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-offering-sacrifices). Therein, the <s>aiṣṭika</s> (connected with <s>iṣṭi</s>), <s>saumika</s> (connected with Soma), <s>pāśubandhika</s> (connected with animal-binding), and <s>dārvīhaumika</s> (connected with ladle-offerings) — [these involve] the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar and other [altars] up to the <s>citi</s> (altar-bricks), based on even, uneven, curved, circular, quadrilateral, and various other shapes, with specific dimensions and locations stated here and there — those too must be measured; and since the nature of the cord and other instruments that are the means for their measurement — such as "this much cord constructs this much area" — cannot be known merely from their form, seeing that exposition [to be] necessary, the explanation of <s>vihārayoga</s> is undertaken after the explanation of the sacrifices.
<s>Vihāra</s> is construction. <s>Yoga</s> is its means. The <s>yogas</s> of the <s>vihāras</s>
are the <s>vihārayogas</s>; we shall explain them, i.e. expound them. The root "hṛ" with the prefix "vi-"

children.text:
krīḍāprajvalanabandhanasaṃcaraṇavimānādyanekārthakaḥ /
tatkriyāviśeṣasambandhādeva deśādiṣu tatratatrārthe vihāravyapadeśaḥ /
atra tuvimānavācī /
yujiś ca dvividhaḥ--samādhivācī
children.translated_text: has many meanings: play, kindling, binding, moving about, measurement, and others. From the particular connection with a specific action, the designation <s>vihāra</s> is applied in various senses to places and other [referents]. Here, however, it denotes measurement. And <s>yuji</s> (the root "yuj") is of two kinds: denoting <s>samādhi</s> (proper arrangement)

children.text:
saṃbandhavācī ca /
atra tu samādhivācī /
vedyādeḥsamyagavasthānaṃ samādhiḥ, "sa samāviḥ' ityatra vakṣyate /
yujyante ebhiriti yogāḥ, viharaṇopāyabhūtā ravjjādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: and denoting connection. Here, however, it denotes <s>samādhi</s> (proper arrangement). The proper positioning of the <s>vedī</s> (altar-ground) and the like is <s>samādhi</s> — as will be stated in "sa samādhiḥ" (that is the proper arrangement). <s>Yogas</s> are "those by which [things] are joined" — the cords and other [instruments] that are the means of construction.

children.text:
"pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ' ityādinā vimātavyasya vedyādikṣetrasya śroṇyaṃsānāṃ vividhasaṃpādanāvacchedo viharaṇam /
tatsādhanabhūtā ravjjādayo vihārayogāḥ, tānvacākhyāsyāmaḥ /
vyārūyānaṃ nāma sati sandehe balavatā hetunopapādya vivaraṇaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: By [the passage] beginning with "pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ" (at the ends of the back), the construction (<s>viharaṇa</s>) is the delimitation of the various configurations of the hips (<s>śroṇī</s>) and shoulders (<s>aṃsa</s>) of the <s>vedī</s> and other areas to be measured. The cords and other [instruments] that are the means for that are the <s>vihārayogas</s>; we shall explain them. Explanation means: where there is doubt, establishing [the meaning] with a strong reason and elucidating it, as in —

children.text:
"sama caturaśrā anupapadatvācchabdasya mānārtheṣu yathākāmiśabdārthasya viśayitvāt, ityevamādikam /
nanu kuto vihārasya bhāvavā citvaṃ, kuto vā tasya vimānaparyāyatvaṃ, kuto viharaṇasya vedyādisaṃbandhaḥ, kuto vā tatra ravjjādīnāṃ karaṇatvaṃ, kuto vā
children.translated_text: "The term "sama caturaśra" (even quadrilateral) [is interpreted thus] because the word cannot [stand] without [such interpretation], since in measurement-contexts, the word's meaning ranges freely" — and so on. Now, how does <s>vihāra</s> have the sense of an action-noun? How is it synonymous with measurement (<s>vimāna</s>)? How is construction (<s>viharaṇa</s>) connected with the <s>vedī</s> and the like? How are the cords and the like instrumental therein? How

children.text: yujeḥsamādhivacanatā, kathaṃ vā ravjjādiṣu yogavāyavahāraḥ? ucyate--"uktaṃ viharaṇaṃ "vyākhyātaṃ viharaṇam' iti bhāvapratyayanirdeśāt bhāvavacano vihāraśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: does the root <s>yuj</s> denote <s>samādhi</s> (proper arrangement)? And how is the term <s>yoga</s> applied to cords and the like? It is answered: "The construction has been stated," "The construction has been explained" — from the indication of the action-suffix, the word <s>vihāra</s> denotes an action.

children.text: "tadekaravjjā viharaṇaṃ' "ravjjā vā vimāya' iti ravjjakārye vimānaviharaṇayoratra
children.translated_text: "That single cord is the construction," "having measured with a cord" — since in the operation of cords, both <s>vimāna</s> (measurement) and <s>viharaṇa</s> (construction) are

children.text:
darśanādubhayoḥ paryāya tvām /
"etāvanti jñeyāni vediviharaṇāni bhavanti' ityanena viharaṇasya vedyādisambandhaḥ /
"āgantucaturthamāyāmaśvākṣṇayārajjuḥ pramāṇamātrī rajjuṃ' iti tatra tatra karaṇīṣu rajju vyapadeśitvavaśāt pārśvamānī tiryaṅbhānīdi karaṇyaṣṭādaśakaraṇīti tatratatra rutrīliṅganirdeśāt rajjveti tṛtīyāśruteś ca
children.translated_text: seen here, they are synonymous. By "these are to be known as the constructions of the <s>vedī</s>," the connection of construction with the <s>vedī</s> and the like [is established]. By "the cord of the approaching fourth [of the] length, the diagonal cord, the standard cord" — since the cord is designated [as an instrument] in the various constructions here and there, such as <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure), <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure), <s>karaṇī</s> (constructing cord) of eighteen [units], from the indication of the feminine gender in the <s>sūtras</s> here and there, and from the instrumental case-ending of "rajjvā" (by the cord),

children.text:
rajjūnāṃ viharaṇe sādhanatvaṃ ata eva hetoretatkarma śulbamityācakṣate /
ācāryā etaṃ grantharāśiṃ "sa samādhiḥ' "athāparo yogaḥ' iti vakṣyanti /
tena jñāyate yujeḥsamādhivacanatā /
yujerarthasya samādherviharaṇasādhyatvāt /
viharaṇasādhanānyapi yogasādhanāni bhavantīti ravjjādayo yogā ityucyante /
vi hārayogaparatāṃ jñāpayituṃ viharaṇasādhaneṣu yogavyavahāraḥ /
yogagrahaṇaṃ kimarthaṃ ? sādhanatvapratītyarthamityuktam /
children.translated_text: the instrumentality of cords in construction [is established]; for this very reason, the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) call this work "<s>Śulba</s>" (cord-science). The teachers will state [later] "sa samādhiḥ" (that is the proper arrangement) and "athāparo yogaḥ" (now another method). From that, the denotation of <s>samādhi</s> by <s>yuj</s> is known. Since <s>samādhi</s> (the meaning of <s>yuj</s>) is achievable by construction, the means of construction are also the means of <s>yoga</s>; hence the cords and the like are called <s>yogas</s>. To indicate the orientation toward <s>vihārayoga</s>, the term <s>yoga</s> is used for the instruments of construction. What is the purpose of the word <s>yoga</s>? It is said: for the understanding of instrumentality.

children.text:
evaṃ tarhi na vaktavyaṃ darśapūrṇamāsau vyākhyāsyāma ityādiṣu pratijñānantaraṃ sādhanānyeva vyākhyeyatayāvagamyante /
evaṃ tarhi yogagrahaṇaṃ mānasādhaneṣu prādhānyakhyāpanārthaṃ /
kiṃ tat prādhānyam ? yadyapi padaveṇvādīni mānasādhanāni santi, tadhāpi tairvimāne bahu prayatnasādhyā samyagvedyādikṣetrasamādhisiddhiḥ, pajjusīrādibhir vimāne tasyāḥ siddhirīṣatkarītyetadatra prādhānyaṃ /
nanu ravjjādīnāṃ viharaṇasādhanatvaṃ lokato 'pi setsyati, kimarthamidamucyate vihārayogānvyākhyāsyāma iti? ucyate--satyaṃ setsyati /
tathāpi
children.translated_text: If so, then it need not be stated [separately] — since in [formulas like] "We shall explain the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifices]," after the announcement, the instruments themselves are understood as what is to be explained. If so, then the word <s>yoga</s> is for the purpose of declaring the primacy among measuring instruments. What is that primacy? Although rods, bamboos, and the like are also measuring instruments, the proper accomplishment (<s>samādhi</s>) of the <s>vedī</s> and other areas by measurement with them requires great effort, whereas by cords and the like, its accomplishment in measurement is easy — this is the primacy here. Now, since the instrumentality of cords and the like in construction would be known even from common experience, why is it stated "We shall explain the <s>vihārayogas</s>"? It is answered: True, it would be known.
Nevertheless, since place, like time, is an ancillary [factor], and since even a sesame-seed's measure of deficiency or excess in a place of stated dimensions

children.text:
satyaṅgavaiguṇyaṃ syāditi manyamāna ācāryo ravjjādīnāmasandigdhamīṣatkaramupāyabhāvaṃ svayameva pratipādayitumidaṃ brūte /
ato nyūnādhikabhāve pariharaṇīye sati pramādādasāmatharyādvā yadi bhreṣa upajāyate tatrāvaśyaṃ prāyāśvittaṃ kartavyamityetadarthamidamucyate "vihārayogānvyākhyāsyāmaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: would constitute a defect in the ancillary — thinking thus, the <s>ācārya</s>, in order to demonstrate the unambiguous and easy instrumental nature of the cords and the like himself, says this. Therefore, when deficiency or excess is to be avoided, if due to carelessness or inability an error occurs, an expiatory rite must certainly be performed — it is for this purpose that "We shall explain the <s>vihārayogas</s>" is stated.

children.text:
athavā vihriyanta iti vihārāḥ /
yogāś ca tatsaṃpādanopāyabhūtāsta eva rajjvādayaḥ /
atra kecinniyatadiksaṃyogādīnāṃ vedyādīnāmajñātadigviśeṣaiḥ puruṣairviharaṇaṃ kartum aśakyamiti digviśeṣajñāpanārthamādāveva diśaṃ lakṣaṇīkurvanti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, [the places] in which [fires] are placed are the <s>vihāras</s>. And the <s>yogas</s> that are the means for their accomplishment are those very cords and the like. Here, some [authorities], since construction cannot be performed by persons ignorant of the particular directions when the <s>vedī</s> and the like require fixed directional orientations, prescribe the cardinal directions at the very beginning.

children.text:
yathā'ha bhagavān kātyāyanaḥ-- "same śaṅkuṃ nikhāya śaṅkusaṃmitayā ravjjā maṇḍalaṃ parilikhya yatra lekhayoḥśaṅkagravacchāyā nipatati sā prācī /
tatra śaṅkuṃ nikhāya tadanantaraṃ ravjjābhyasya pāśau kṛtvā śakṅvoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya madhyamaśaṅkurevamuttarataḥsodīcī'' iti /
children.translated_text: As the venerable <s>Kātyāyana</s> says: "On level ground, fix a <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon); draw a circle with a cord equal to the <s>śaṅku</s>; where the shadow of the gnomon falls on the [circle-]lines, that is the east (<s>prācī</s>). Fix a gnomon there; then stretching a cord, making loops at both ends, fastening the loops on the gnomons, drawing [it] southward with the mark [at its center], the middle gnomon — thus also northward — that is the north (<s>udīcī</s>)."

children.text: asyārthaḥ--atha yatra śucau deśe devayajanaṃ kīraṣyan bhavati taṃ deśaṃ jalena samīkṛtya madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya śaṅkusaṃmitāmekataḥ pāśāṃ rajjuṃ kṛtvā śakṅau pratimucya tayā maṇḍalaṃ parilirūya maṇḍalarekhāyāṃ pūrvāhne yatra śakṅvagracchāyā nipatati tatra binduṃ kuryāt tau pūrvaparau bindū sā ca pracī dik /
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: Now, on a clean place where the sacrificial ground is to be prepared, leveling that place with water, fixing a gnomon in the center, making a cord equal to the gnomon with a loop at one end, fastening it on the gnomon, drawing a circle with it, making a dot where the tip of the gnomon's shadow falls on the circle-line in the forenoon — those are the eastern and western dots, and that is the eastern direction.

children.text:
bindvordvayoḥśaṅkuṃ nikhāya tadantaradviguṇāṃ rajjumubhayataḥpāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā śakṅvoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya lakṣaṇe śaṅkuṃ kuryād evam uttarato 'pi lakṣaṇenāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ kuryāt /
tau śaṅkū dakṣiṇottarau sā udīcī digiti /
tathā jyotirjñāne /
children.translated_text: Fix a gnomon at each of the two dots; make a cord twice the interval [between them] with loops at both ends; make a mark at the middle; fasten the loops on the gnomons; draw [the cord] southward by the mark; at the mark, fix a gnomon; likewise draw northward by the mark and fix a gnomon. Those two gnomons [mark] south and north; that is the northern direction. Similarly in astronomical determination:
"By the two [points where the] tip of the gnomon's shadow [falls on] the circle drawn around the gnomon standing at the center,"

children.text:
yogābhyāṃ kṛtamatsyena jñeye yāmyottare diśau' iti /
evamanyairapi bahuprakāraṃ diśāṃ grahaṇaṃ tatra tatroktamiti
children.translated_text: "with the fish-figure made by those two [arcs], the southern and northern directions are to be known." Thus, the determination of directions has been stated in many ways by others in various places,
and because it is well known, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) has not stated it here.

children.text: pramīyate 'neneti vyutpacyā pārśvamānyādīnāṃ pramāṇatve siddhe pramāṇāmiti paribhāṣyate //
children.translated_text: That by which [something] is measured is [called] <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure) by derivation; although the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure) and the like are already established as standards, the term <s>pramāṇa</s> is used as a technical designation.
Commentary on the <s>Āpastamba Śulbasūtra</s>
[called] <s>Sundararājīyā</s>

children.text: āpastambena yo 'yaṃ vyaraci bhagavatā śulbasaṃjño gabhīraḥ praśno 'rthaṃ tasya bhāṣyaprabhṛtiṣu kathitaṃ vīkṣya kṛtsnam /
children.translated_text: This profound topic named <s>Śulba</s> (cord-science), composed by the venerable <s>Āpastamba</s>, having examined the meaning stated in its entirety in the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) and other [works],

children.text: saṃkṣipyobdodhanārthaṃ kuśikakulanidhermādhavāryasya yaṣṭuḥ putraḥ śulbapradīpaṃ vivaraṇamadhunā sundaro nirmimīte //
children.translated_text: condensing [it] for easy understanding, <s>Sundara</s>, son of <s>Mādhavārya</s> the sacrificer, a treasure of the <s>Kuśika</s> lineage, now composes this elucidation [called] <s>Śulbapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Śulba).

children.text:
vihāro viharaṇaṃ, caturaśrādirūpeṇa bhmeḥ karaṇam /
tasya yogāḥ upāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vihāra</s> is construction — the shaping of the ground into a quadrilateral and other forms. Its <s>yogas</s> are the methods.
Commentary of <s>Kapardi</s>
The <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure) is as long as the length (<s>āyāma</s>). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.2a]
"Yāvad-āyāmam" is an indeclinable compound. "Yāvad" means "to the extent of" — a delimiting [particle]. What is delimited here? The length (<s>āyāma</s>).

children.text:
āyāma eva pramāṇamiti na, tiryaṅbhānyakṣṇayā rajjū /
tābhyāmapi piharaṇasya śakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: It is not that the length alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard); [there are also] the transverse [measure] and the diagonal cord. Because construction is possible by those [other measures] also.
The purpose of the technical term <s>pramāṇa</s> is [seen in the rule] "Increase the <s>pramāṇa</s> by a third" — for the recognition of the length [as the referent].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
"Yāvad-āyāmam" [as long as the length].
The word "yāvat" denotes quantity; the word "āyāma" denotes the counterpart to breadth (<s>vistāra</s>).

children.text:
"yāvadavadhāraṇe iti samāsaḥ /
yāvānāyāmastāvat pramāṇaṃ bhavati, kimatrāvadhāryate?
children.translated_text: "Yāvad-avadhāraṇe" — thus is the compound. The <s>pramāṇa</s> is as great as the length. What is delimited here?

children.text:
āyāmaparimāṇameva pramāṇamiti /
tadatrā'yāmasya dviguṇatvāttadāśrayabhūtarajjvādipramāṇam iti /
asya pramāṇaṃ tiryagādiṣu prayojanam,
children.translated_text: The dimension of the length alone is the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Since the length here is twofold, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is the cord and the like that are its basis. The purpose of this <s>pramāṇa</s> [designation] is in the transverse and other [measurements].
Commentary of <s>Kapardi</s>
Doubling that half and in the other third, diminished by a sixth, he makes the mark. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.2b]

children.text:
taditi pramāṇaṃ rāmṛśyate /
tadardhaṃ abhyasya prakṣipya pramāṇasyopari
children.translated_text: That [cord] is taken as the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure). Having doubled its half and placed it above the <s>pramāṇa</s>,
in the other [part], in the third [section] diminished by one-sixth, one makes a mark.

children.text: abhyāsasahitaṃ pramāṇaṃ ubhayataḥ pāśau kṛtvāparasmin bhāge tṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ tirañjanaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>pramāṇa</s> together with its doubling into loops on both sides, in the other part, in the third [section], one makes a mark — a line drawn across.
One should make a mark at [a distance] diminished by one-sixth of the length.

children.text: pṛṣṭhyāntayorantau niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya nimitaṃ karoti || ĀpŚus_1.2c ||
children.translated_text: Fixing [the cord] at the ends of the spine-line, drawing it to the south by the mark, one makes a point. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.2c]
<s>Pṛṣṭhyā</s> means 'that which is on the spine' (the central line).

children.text: tasyā antayoḥśaṅkū nihatya tayoḥ pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya nimittaṃ karoti, lakṣaṇena prasārya yathā ṣaḍbhāgonā tiryaṅbhānī śiṣṭākṣṇayā rajjuḥ evamapasārayati /
children.translated_text: Having driven stakes at its two ends, and fastening the loops of [the cord] to those [stakes], drawing it to the south by the mark, one makes a point; having stretched [the cord] by the mark so that the breadth diminished by one-sixth — with the remaining diagonal cord — thus one draws it aside.
One should drive in the stake at the point.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
One makes the half of that.

Now, since the <s>aiṣṭika</s> (optional), <s>saumika</s> (related to Soma), and <s>pāśubandhika</s> (animal-sacrifice) [altars] are generally rectangular, the construction appropriate to them is stated —

children.text:
pramāṇamityeva tacchabdenāyāmabhūtaṃ pramāṇaṃ parāmṛśyate /
tasyārdhaṃ tadardhaṃ, abhyasanamuparikṣepaḥ, aparasmina paścāddhāvi nyāgantau, tṛtīye pramāṇārdhābhyāṃ saha tṛtīye, ṣaḍbhāgone--ṣaṣṭho bhāgaḥṣaḍbhāgaḥ tena bhāgena hīne tasminneva tṛtīye, lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyate yena tallakṣaṇaṃ vimātavyakṣetrasya koṭiparijñānopāyabhūtaṃ cihnaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: By the word 'that' [in the sūtra], the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure) which constitutes the length is referred to. Its half is 'half of that'; <s>abhyasana</s> means 'placing above'; 'in the other' means 'in the subsequent, westward end'; 'in the third' means 'in the third [part] together with the half of the <s>pramāṇa</s>'; 'diminished by one-sixth' — the sixth part is one-sixth, in that very third [section] diminished by that portion — 'a mark' means that by which [a point] is marked: a sign that serves as a means for knowing the corner of the area to be measured — 'one makes'

children.text: kuryāt, pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ--vimātavyakṣetrasya madhyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ, kuta etadavagamyate?
children.translated_text: means 'one should make.' 'At the ends of the spine-line' — the middle of the area to be measured is the 'spine.' From what is this understood?

children.text:
tadavayaveṣu śroṇyaṃsapārśvavyapadeśādyathā śroṇyaṃsadeśapārśvānāṃ madhyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ epamidamapīti! tatra bhavā rekhā pṛṣṭhyā /
tadantayoḥśaṅkuṃ nikhāya rajjvantau pāśau kṛtvā tayorniyamya pratimucya lakṣaṇena cihnena dakṣiṇāpāyamya--dakṣiṇato 'pakṛṣya rajjuṃ tatra nimittaṃ kṣetrakoṭijñānahetuṃ śaṅkuṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: From the designation of hip, shoulder, and side among its parts — just as the middle of hip, shoulder, side, and flank is the spine, so is this also. The line that exists there is the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s> (spine-line). Having driven a stake at its two ends, making the two ends of the cord into loops, fixing them to those [stakes] and fastening, drawing it to the south by the mark — that is, pulling the cord to the south — there one should make a point, a stake which is the means of knowing the corner of the area.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
Likewise drawing northward and reversing on the other side — that is the <s>samādhi</s> (alignment/fitting). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.2d]

children.text:
evamudagapasārya pūrvavatkuryāt /
viparyasyetarataḥ pūrvesmācchaṅkāḥ pāśamunmucyāparasmin śakṅau pratimuñcet /
aparasmāc chaṅkāḥ pāśamunmucya pūrvasminpratimuñcet /
sa viparyāsaḥ /
taṃ kṛtvetarataḥ aṃsau tenaiva prathamakṛtena ṣaḍbhāgonena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ udagapasāryottaramaṃsamiti sa samādhiḥ /
uktena mārgaviśeṣeṇāpāditāḥ pārśvamānyādaya iti samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise drawing northward, one should do as before. 'Reversing on the other side' — releasing the loop from the former stake and fastening it on the other stake; releasing the loop from the other stake and fastening it on the first — that is the reversal. Having done that, 'on the other side': one [determines] the shoulders by that very first [mark] diminished by one-sixth, drawing the southern shoulder northward and the northern shoulder — that is the <s>samādhi</s> (alignment). The side-measurements and other [dimensions] produced by the specified particular method — that is the <s>samādhi</s>.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary

children.text:
evamuttarato 'pi vikṛṣya rajjuṃ nimittaṃ kuryāt, viparyāso rajjvantayoḥ pūrvaṃ pāśaṃ paścime śakṅau paścimaṃ ca pūrvasmin kṛtvā itarataḥ kṛtanimittāt pradeśādanyatra tatra ca dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca vikṛṣya nimitte kuryāt /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--ayāmārthaṃ pramāṇe prakṣipya prakṣiptaṃ ṣoḍhā vibhajya tasmin antādārabhya pañcasu bhogeṣvatīteṣu lakṣaṇasyāntau pāśau kṛtvā pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥśaṅkuṃ nikāya tayoḥ pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ kuryāt, uttarato 'pyevameva vikṛṣya śaṅkuṃ kuryāt, rajjvantau viparyasyetarasminnapi pradeśe śaṅkudvayaṃ kuryaditi, nanu aparagrahaṇaṃ pūrvatṛtīye lakṣaṇavyāvṛcyarthaṃ kiṃ na syāt, tatrāpi tasyāvirodhādeva na syāt /
tarhi madhayamatṛtīyaṃ vyākartya pūrvāparayoḥ pradarśanārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cennaitatyadyevamiṣṭamabhaviṣyattarhi spaṣṭataraṃmadhyame tṛtīya ityevāvakṣyat, na cāsau tattathoktavān /
atha manyase? tadarthamabhayasyāparasminn ityukte 'bhyāsādanyat, pramāṇamaparaṃ pratīyate, sāmarthyāttatra tṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ bhavatviti, naitadapi yuktaṃ--yadayamāgantvāyāmābhyāsaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Likewise drawing the cord to the north also, one should make a point. The reversal [means]: having made the former loop at the cord-ends onto the western stake, and the western [loop] onto the eastern — 'on the other side,' at a place different from where the point was previously made, there too drawing to the south and north, one should make points. This is what is stated: Having added [the extension] to the <s>pramāṇa</s> for the purpose of the length, dividing the added [cord] into six parts, and when five portions from the end have passed, making the two ends of the mark into loops, driving a stake at the two ends of the spine-line, fastening [the loops] to those [stakes], drawing to the south by the mark, one should make a stake; likewise drawing to the north, one should make a stake; and reversing the cord-ends, at the other place too one should make a pair of stakes. Now, could not the word 'other' (apara) be for distinguishing from the mark in the first third [section]? [No], because it is not contradicted there either. Then, could it be for demonstrating [the procedure in] the first and last [sections], explaining the middle third? If it is objected that if this were intended it would have been stated more clearly as 'in the middle third' — but he did not say it that way. Or do you think: since 'in the other [part] from the doubling' implies something other than the doubling, another <s>pramāṇa</s> is understood, and by implication the mark should be in its third [section]? — This too is not correct, because this [text states] 'the additional [portion] of the length constitutes...'

children.text:
āgantvavayavasyākṣṇayārajjuśeṣatāṃ vakṣyati /
pahāvedimāne ca ṣaṭātriṃśikāyāmaṣṭādaśopa śamasyetyādau pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamya śroṇyaṃsānāṃ viharaṇaṃ vakṣyāti, tenātrābhyāsāganturevāparaḥ, tatra ṣaḍbhāgone nirañjanamiti vijñāyate /
children.translated_text: He will state that the additional part has the character of the diagonal cord with the rest [of the cord]. And in the <s>Pāhā-vedi</s> measurement: 'of a thirty-six [unit area] with an eighteen [unit] extension' etc., he will state the construction of hips and shoulders by a fifteen-[unit measure] drawn aside. Therefore here the 'other' is indeed the additional portion, and in it, 'diminished by one-sixth' is understood as the line-mark.

children.text: nanu yadyāgantuparo 'paraśabdaḥ tarhi ṣaḍbhāgone lakṣaṇamityetāvadevālaṃ, kimarthaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, if the word 'other' refers to the additional portion, then 'diminished by one-sixth, one makes a mark' alone would suffice — what is the purpose

children.text:
tṛtīyaśabdaḥ, naivāsya prayojanaṃ paśyāmaḥ, ucyate--astyevāsya prayojanaṃ, kuṃ tat, atrocyamā naviharaṇasya sarvābhyāsaviṣayatvakhyāpanārthaṃ, tatkathaṃ, atra tāvadācāryeṇa sarvajñena sarvānugrahakāriṇā prayuktasyākṣarāvayavasyāpi nānarthakatā yuktā, kiṃ punaḥ padasya /
ato mukhyayā vṛcyā yathā śabdor'thavān bhavati tathā vyākhyeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: of the word 'third'? We do not see its utility. It is answered: this [word] indeed has a purpose. What is it? Here it is for the purpose of declaring that the stated construction applies to all extensions. How so? Here, since not even a syllable-component employed by the omniscient, all-beneficent teacher should be purposeless — how much less a word! Therefore it should be explained according to the primary meaning such that the word becomes meaningful.

children.text:
ata evāyaṃ śabda evaṃ vyākhyāyate--āgantusamānādhikaraṇībhūtatṛtīyaśabdasyāvayavabhūtatriśabdavācyena tritvena sābhyāsasya pramāṇasyāgantuparimitā yāvanto bhāgāḥsaṃbhavanti tāvatāṃ bhāgānāṃ sakhṅyā lakṣyate, tathā--ṣaḍbāgaśabdāvayavabhūtaṣaṭachabdavācyena ca ṣaṭtvena tadanurūpatvāya tritvalakṣitasakhṅyādviguṇībhūtābhāgasaṃkhṅyā lakṣyate /
etenāyamarthaḥsaṃpadyate--
sarveṣvabhyāseṣu sābhyāsasya pramāṇasyāgantuparimitā yāvanto bhāgāḥsampadyante tāvaddviguṇabhāgamāgantuṃ kṛtvā tasmin bhāgenaikena hīne lakṣaṇakaraṇamiti /
children.translated_text: Hence this word is explained thus: by the number denoted by the word 'tri' (three), which is a component of the word 'third' (tṛtīya) that has the same reference as the additional portion — [it shows that] so many parts as are possible when the <s>pramāṇa</s> together with the extension is measured relative to the additional portion — their number is indicated. Similarly, by the number six denoted by the word 'ṣaṭ' (six) which is a component of the word 'one-sixth' (ṣaḍbhāga) — correspondingly, the number of parts doubled from the number indicated by 'three' is marked. By this, this meaning is obtained: In all extensions, however many parts result when the <s>pramāṇa</s> together with its extension is measured relative to the additional portion, making the additional portion with twice that number of parts, the marking should be made at [a point] diminished by one part.

children.text:
tadyathā--ardhābhyāse tāvadardhameko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇantu tattulyau bhāgau, adaḥsābhyāsasya pramāṇasyāgantutulyāstrayo bhāgāḥ, āgantau taddviguṇacchede tasya ṣaḍbhāgāḥ, tatra bhāgenaikena hīne lakṣaṇam, tathā āyāmābhyāse āyāma eko bhāgaḥ, ca tatsadṛśa eko bhāgaḥ /
tena sābhyāsasya pramāṇāsya dvau bhāgau taddviguṇacchede abhyāse catvāro bhāgāḥ /
tatra caturbhāgone lakṣaṇam /
tathā--tṛtīyābhyāse abhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇaṃ tattulyāstrayo bhāgāḥ, dviguṇacchede 'bhyāse 'ṣṭau bāgāḥ, tatrāṣṭabhāgone lakṣaṇam, evameva turīyādyabhyāse 'ṣṭau pramāṇasyābhyāsavaśenaiva bhāgakalpanam, āgantau taddviguṇasakhṅyayā bhāgaka lpanam, bhāgone lakṣaṇaṃ ca draṣṭavyam /
nanu yatrābhyāse 'bhyāsatulyatā pramāṇasya na sambhavati kathaṃ tatra pramāṇe cāgantau ca bāgakalpanaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca, yathādhikābhyāse chedanaṃ nyūnābhyase ca ?
children.translated_text: Thus: In a half-extension, the half is one part, and the <s>pramāṇa</s> has two parts equal to it; thus the <s>pramāṇa</s> with its extension has three parts equal to the additional [portion]; in the additional portion, with a cut of double that [number], it has six parts; in [the sixth part] diminished by one part, [one makes] the mark. Similarly, in an extension equal to the length: the length is one part, and [the extension] is one part equal to it; thus the <s>pramāṇa</s> with extension has two parts; with a cut of double that in the extension, four parts; at [the point] diminished by one-fourth, the mark. Similarly, in a third-extension: the extension is one part, the <s>pramāṇa</s> has three parts equal to it; with a double cut in the extension, eight parts; at [the point] diminished by one-eighth, the mark. Similarly in fourth- and other extensions, having calculated the parts, one should make the mark in the additional portion correspondingly. Similarly, in a three-quarter extension: the extension is one part, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is one part and one-third equal to it; with a cut equal to one portion in the <s>pramāṇa</s> with extension, [there are] seven thirds; at [the point] diminished by three of those, the mark. In the same way in other fractional cuts also, the calculation of parts and marking should be observed. This too should not be forgotten: in all extensions, the additional portion has unit-part status; based on that, the <s>pramāṇa</s> has unit-part status and multi-part status and mere [diagonal-]cord status. Thus the applicability of this construction to all extensions should be understood. If this is so established, how is it known that this principle is accepted? It is answered: from [the sūtra] 'the fourth added to the length is the diagonal cord,' since [this] teaches that in an extension equal to the length, the fourth of the extension has the character of a diagonal cord — and from the presentation of irregular extensions in statements like 'the seventeen-[unit] diagonal cord established from the half-extension and full-length by means of a fifteen-[unit] and eight-[unit measure]' — it is known that this principle is accepted. Enough of digression. And for distinguishing the breadth from the diagonal cord: for what purpose are the words 'south' and 'north' used? For demonstrating the transverse [line]; otherwise there would be contradiction in the <s>sadaḥ</s> (sacrificial hall) and other [constructions].

children.text: ucyate--tatrāpyayameva prakāraḥ, kintu sābhyāsaṃ pramāṇamaṃśena ca sadṛśacchedaṃ kṛtvā āgantum api chedasakhṅyādviguṇasakhṅyayā chedaṃ kṛtvā tatra yāvadbhir aṃśairhīnaireko bhāgo hīno bhavati tāvadbhiraṃśairnyūne 'bhyāse nihañjanaṃ kuryāt, adhikābhyāse tāvaddviguṇābhyāse 'bhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇaṃ bhāgārthaṃ, tatrārdhena ca sadṛśacchede sābhyāse pramāṇe trayor'dhacchedāḥ, tatsakhṅyādviguṇacchede tatra ṣaḍardhacchedāḥ, teṣu dvābhyāmūnābhyāmeko bhāgo hīyata iti taḍhūne lakṣaṇaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: It is answered: the same method applies there too, but one makes the <s>pramāṇa</s> with its extension into cuts proportional to the portion, and also makes cuts in the additional portion with double the number of [those] cuts, and wherever by so many portions diminished one part is diminished, by that many portions diminished one should make the mark in a reduced extension; in an increased extension — thus, in a double extension: the extension is one part, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is half a part; with cuts proportional to one-half in the <s>pramāṇa</s> with extension, three half-cuts; with double that number of cuts, six half-cuts; of these, when two are diminished, one part is diminished — so at [the point] diminished by that, the mark should be [made].

children.text:
triguṇābhyāse 'bhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇaṃ tu tṛtīyāṃśakaḥ, tatsadṛśā abhyāse trayastṛtīyāṃ śakāḥ, tena sābhyāsasya pramāṇasya catvārastṛtīyāṃśāḥ, taddviguṇacchede āgantāvaṣṭau tṛtīyāśāḥ, tatra tribhiraṃśairūne lakṣaṇam /
evaṃ caturguṇābhyāseṣu bhāgānunnīya tadanuṃrūpamā gantau lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt /
tathā tripādābhyāse 'bhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇaṃ tatsadṛśa eko bhāgastṛtīyāṃśaśva, aṃśena ca sadṛśacchede sābhyāsapramāṇe sapta tṛtīyāṃśāḥ, taistribhirūne tatra lakṣaṇam /
evam evānyeṣvapi sāṃśacchedeṣu bhāgakalpanaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca draṣṭavyam /
etadapi na vismartavyaṃ sarveṣvabhyāseṣvāgantubhāgaikyaṃ tadvaśenana pramāṇe bhāgaukyaṃ bhāgānekatvaṃ kevalāṃ śatvaṃ ceti, evamasya viharaṇasya sarvābhyāsaviṣayatvamavagantavyam /
yadyevam upapadyate, kuto jñāyate nyāyo 'ṅgaīkṛta iti, ucyate--āgantucaturthamāyāmaśvākṣṇayārajjuriti āyāmābhyāso 'bhyāsacaturthasyākṣṇayārajjuviśeṣatvapratipādanādardhābhyāsāyāmābhyāṃ siddhasya pañcadaśikāṣṭikayoḥsaptadaśikākṣṇayārajjurityāderviṣamābhyāsopanyāsācca jñāyate nyāyo 'yamaṅgīkṛta ityalamatirthaṃ, tiryaṅbhānyakṣṇayārajjuvivekārthaṃ ca, dakṣiṇottaragrahaṇaṃ kimarthaṃ, pradarśanārthaṃ tiraśvyāḥ, itarathā sadaḥprabhṛtiṣu virodhāt /
children.translated_text: In a triple extension: the extension is one part, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is one-third portion; there are three one-third portions equal to it in the extension; thus the <s>pramāṇa</s> with extension has four one-third portions; with a double cut, eight one-third portions in the additional portion; at [the point] diminished by three portions, the mark. Similarly, in quadruple and other extensions, having calculated the parts, one should make the mark in the additional portion correspondingly. Similarly, in a three-quarter extension: the extension is one part, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is one part and one-third equal to it; with a cut proportional to the portion in the <s>pramāṇa</s> with extension, seven one-third portions; at [the point] diminished by three of those, the mark. In the same way in other fractional cuts also, the calculation of parts and marking should be observed. This too should not be forgotten: in all extensions, the additional-portion unit — based on that, the unit in the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the multiplicity of parts, and the mere cord-nature. Thus the applicability of this construction to all extensions should be understood. If it is established thus, how is it known that the principle is accepted? It is answered: from [the sūtra] 'the fourth of the additional portion constitutes the length and the diagonal cord' — since the extension-equal-to-length [case establishes] the diagonal-cord character of the fourth of the extension — and from 'the seventeen-[unit] diagonal cord established from the half-extension and the length by the fifteen-[unit] and the eight-[unit]' and from the presentation of irregular extensions — it is known that this principle is accepted. Enough of digression; and for distinguishing the breadth and the diagonal cord — and the words 'south' and 'north' for what purpose? For demonstrating the transverse; otherwise there would be contradiction in the <s>sadaḥ</s> and other [constructions].
At the end of this construction, for teaching another [point], it says 'that is the <s>samādhi</s>' (alignment).
This [sūtra] has two feet (is a two-part statement).

children.text: tacchabdena viharaṇamucyate, samādhyābhiprāyaḥ puṃlliṅganirdeśaḥ, saṃśabdaḥ samyagarthe samaśabdārthe vā, āṅ samantatobhāve, dadhātiḥ karotyarthe samaśabdārthe vā, āṅ samantatobhāve, dadhātiḥ karotyarthe, samyaganyūnānatiriktaṃ kṣetraṃ samantādāpādayatīti samādhiḥ, yadvā--samānānāmādhiḥ samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the word 'that' the construction is denoted; the intention behind <s>samādhi</s> is [explained by] the masculine gender reference. The prefix 'sam' is in the sense of 'properly' or in the sense of the word 'sama' (equal); 'ā' denotes 'on all sides'; <s>dadhāti</s> is in the sense of 'making.' [The compound means:] 'that which brings about the area properly, neither deficient nor excessive, on all sides — that is <s>samādhi</s>.' Alternatively: <s>samādhi</s> means 'the placing together of equals.'

children.text: pārśvamānyau tiryaṅbhānyau akṣṇayārajjuś ca parasparamanyonyasamāḥsaṃpādayatīti, caturdikṣu samaṃ kṣetramāpādayatīti samādhiḥ, ayamarthaḥ--
children.translated_text: The side-measurements, the breadths, and the diagonal cord — [the construction] makes them mutually equal to one another. [It means:] that which produces the area equally in the four directions is <s>samādhi</s>. The meaning is this:

children.text: vimīyamānakṣetrasyānyunānatirekitvenāvasthānaṃ samādhānam, tacca samyagupāyasya viharaṇasya phalam, taddhetutvādviharaṇasya, hetuphalayorabhedopacāreṇa tadeva viharaṇaṃ samādhirityucyate, yoga iti ceti, kimarthamidamucyate? śrotṝṇāṃ pratipattiprarocanārthaṃ, yadedadṛktaṃ viharaṇaṃ sa samādhiḥ, samīcaḥ śroṇyaṃsān saṃpādayati tasmādidaṃ niḥsaṃdigdamanena vihartavyamiti //
children.translated_text: The establishment of the area to be measured as neither deficient nor excessive is <s>samādhāna</s> (correct alignment), and that is the result of the properly [applied] construction method. Since the construction is the cause of that [correct result], by the metaphorical identification of cause and effect, that very construction is called <s>samādhi</s>, and also <s>yoga</s> (joining). For what purpose is this stated? For inspiring conviction in the listeners — that this stated construction is the <s>samādhi</s>, [which] correctly produces the hips and shoulders; therefore one should construct with this [method] without doubt.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
The decrease or increase caused by that [point/mark]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.2e]

children.text:
nimittaṃ karaṇaṃ prakṛtiḥ iti paryāyāḥ /
tadeva nirañjanārthaṃ yasya sa tannimittaḥ /
nirhrāsaḥ tiryaṅbhānyāḥ /
vṛdvirvā tiryaṅbhānyā eva /
kimuktaṃ bhavati? uktena mārgeṇa prāgāyatāḥ tiryagāyatāḥsamāścaturaśrāḥ kṛtā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nimitta</s> (point/cause), <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument), and <s>prakṛti</s> (source) are synonyms. That which has that [mark] as its cause is <s>tannimitta</s> (caused by that). <s>Nirhrāsa</s> (decrease) [refers to] the breadth. <s>Vṛddhi</s> (increase) also [refers to] the breadth itself. What is being said? The meaning is: by the stated method, the oblong [rectangles] and the transversely extended [shapes] have been made into equal quadrilaterals.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(Caused by that —)

children.text:
taditi samādhirheturviharaṇamucyate--nimittaṃ kāraṇaṃ heturiti paryāyāḥ, nirhrāso 'pacayaḥ, vivṛddhirupacayaḥ, tau tannimittau syātāṃ, lāghavārthamidamucyate, mahati caturaśre vihṛte tadekadeśabhūtaṃ caturaśraṃ saṃpādīyatumicchan mahataścaturaśrasya śroṇyaṃsādisaṃsthita śaṅkvanirūpamabimata pradeśeṣu śaṅkūnnihatya śaṅkuṣu rajjuṃ prabaddhaca yāvadabhimataṃ prasārya tābhiralpaṃ caturaśraṃ sampādayet, vivṛddhau caturaśrapārśvamānyādibhiryāvadabhimatā dīrgharajjūḥ prabaddhya tāstatkūṭasaṃsthitaśaṅkvanurūpāḥ prasāryābhimatapradeśeṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tadantaraṃ gṛhṇīyāt, pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ karaṇīṣu cābhimatapradeśeṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tadanurūpāṇi nimittāntarāṇi kṛtvā rajjuḥ prasārya kṣetrasyāpacayamupacayaṃ vā kuryādityarthaḥ /
nirhrāsodāharaṇaṃ mahāvedyuttaravedidhiṣṇyādayaḥ /
vivṛdbhuyadāharaṇaṃ mahāvedyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here '<s>tat</s>' (that) refers to <s>samādhi</s> (construction/alignment), and '<s>hetu</s>' (reason/cause) is called <s>viharaṇa</s> (extension/manipulation). '<s>Nimitta</s>' (indication), '<s>kāraṇa</s>' (cause), and '<s>hetu</s>' (reason) are synonyms. '<s>Nirhrāsa</s>' (reduction) is decrease; '<s>vivṛddhi</s>' (augmentation) is increase; both would be caused by that [procedure]. This is stated for the sake of brevity: when one wishes to construct a [smaller] quadrilateral that is a portion of a large quadrilateral that has been extended, one should fix pegs at the desired locations conforming to the pegs placed at the corners, shoulders, etc., of the large quadrilateral, and binding a cord to the pegs and extending it as far as desired, one should construct the smaller quadrilateral by those [cords]. For augmentation, binding long cords as desired from the sides and measures of the quadrilateral, extending those conforming to the pegs placed at its corners to the desired locations, fixing a peg, one should take the intervening [measurement]. On the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s> (spine-cord) and in the <s>karaṇīs</s> (constructive cords), fixing a peg at the desired locations and making corresponding indications, extending the cord, one should make the decrease or increase of the field — this is the meaning. Examples of reduction are the <s>mahāvedī</s> (great altar), <s>uttaravedī</s> (northern altar), <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (minor fire-altars), etc. Examples of augmentation are the <s>mahāvedī</s> and the like.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]
(On '<s>tannimitvā</s>' [that being the cause].)

children.text:
abhīṣṭakṣetrāyāmasaṃmitā rajjuḥ pramāṇam /
sā sarvamāneṣūbhayataḥpāśā prācī /
sā pūrvāparayoḥśaṅkvorniyatā bhavati /
saiva pṛṣṭhabhavatvāt pṛṣṭhyetyapi vyapadiśyate /
tadyāvadāyāmaṃ tāvadāyāme śulbāntare tasyārdhamabhyasyopari prakṣiṇya antayoḥ pāśau kuryāt /
tatra trīṇi pramāṇārdhani bhavanti /
teṣāmaparabhāgabhāvitṛtīyamardhdhaṃ ṣoḍhā mbhujya pāśādārabhya pañcasu bhāgeṣviti teṣu lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt /
asya śulbasyāntau pṛṣṭhyāntayorniyamya kṛtena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā prasārya nimittaṃ karoti śaṅkuṃ nihanti /
evamuttarataḥ pāśau viparyasya pūrvānte 'pyevaṃ śaṅkum /
sa samādhiḥ sa eko vihārayogaḥ /
asyodāharaṇam--
children.translated_text: The cord commensurate with the length of the desired field is the standard measure. That [cord], with loops at both ends, is the east-west line (<s>prācī</s>) in all measurements. It is fastened to the eastern and western pegs. It is also designated as '<s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>' (spine-cord) because of being on the back [of the altar]. Taking a second cord of the same length as that, folding it over its half, throwing it above, one should make loops at the two ends. Therein are three half-measures. Of these, the last third half-portion, folded sixfold, starting from the loop, at five parts — at those, one should make a mark. Having fixed the two ends of this cord at the ends of the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>, extending southward by the mark made, one makes the indication — one fixes a peg. Likewise northward, reversing the loops; and at the eastern end, likewise a peg. That is the <s>samādhi</s> (alignment); that is one method of extension.

children.text:
"ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāmaṣṭādaśe' tyādi /
evaṃ kṛte yadi tiryaṅbhānyā nirhrāso vivṛddhirveṣyate so 'pi tannimittaḥ /
ye dakṣiṇottarā nimittabhūtāḥśaṅkavaḥ tāneva cihnīkṛtya kartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: An example is 'in one of thirty-six, eighteen,' etc. When this is done, if a reduction or augmentation of the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure) is desired, that too is caused by that [same method]. The pegs that are the southern and northern indicators — those very ones should be marked and made.

children.text:
nirhrāsasyodāharaṇam--"pañcadaśikenaikāpāyamyārdhena tataḥ' ityādi /
pracī tu sarvatra lokala eva grāhyā /
tatra bodhāyanaḥ "kṛttikāḥ khalvimāḥ prācīṃ na jahati kadācana /
tāsāṃ sandarśanena māpayedityekam /
śroṇāsandarśanenamāpayedityekam /

children.translated_text: 'Another is to measure by the interval between <s>Citrā</s> (Spica) and <s>Svātī</s> (Arcturus).'

children.text: etani lakṣaṇāni deśaviseṣetu vyavatiṣṭhante, sarvadeśasādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇamāha kātyāyanaḥ "same kṣetre śaṅkuṃ nikhāya śaṅkusaṃmitayā rajjvā maṇḍalaṃ parilikhya yatra lekhayoḥśaṅkvagracchāyā nipatati sā prācī' iti /
children.translated_text: These criteria apply in specific regions. The universally applicable criterion is stated by <s>Kātyāyana</s>: 'On level ground, fixing a peg, drawing a circle with a cord equal to the peg [in length], wherever the shadow of the peg-tip falls on the [two intersections of the] circle-line — that is the east-west line.'
'On the [two] lines' means:
on the eastern and western parts of the circle-line — this is the meaning.

An example of reduction is 'with a [cord of] fifteen, half of one being removed from it,' etc. The east-west line (<s>prācī</s>) should everywhere be taken as the true east. There, <s>Baudhāyana</s> [says]: 'These <s>Kṛttikās</s> (Pleiades) never deviate from the east. One method is to measure by their observation. Another is to measure by the observation of <s>Śroṇā</s> (the star Altair).'
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)

children.text: āyāmaṃ vābhyasyāgantucaturtham āyāmaścākṣṇayā rajjus tiryaṅbhānīśeṣaḥ | vyākhyātaṃ viharaṇam || ĀpŚus_1.3a ||
children.translated_text: 'Or, extending the length, the additional fourth — and the length is the diagonal cord; the transverse [cord] is the remainder.' The <s>viharaṇa</s> (extension) has been explained. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.3a]

children.text:
pramāṇaṃ vābhyasya āyāmamātrīṃ rajjumāyāme prakṣipya āgantoścaturthamabhyastacaturthaṃ bhāgaṃ āyāme saṃyojya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sapāda āyāmo 'kṣṇayā rajjuḥ /
śeṣaḥ--pādonāyāmaḥ /
sā tiryaṅbhānī /
vyākhyātaṃ viharāṇaṃ /
vistaraṇavidhiruktaḥ iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ aṃsau pūrvaṃ māpayitavyau /
viparyasya śroṇī samamanyat /
vācoyuktibhedena vidānasyaitat prayojanam--āyāmatṛtīyamabhyasya pūrvasmiṃścaturthe 'ṣṭabhāgone lakṣaṇamityevamādīnāmupasaṅgahārtham /
tatra ślokaḥ--
children.translated_text: Or, extending the measure, taking a cord equal to the length, placing it along the length, adding to the extension a fourth of the extension — that is, the extended fourth part — joining it to the length, making a mark: the length plus a quarter is the diagonal cord. The remainder — the length minus a quarter — that is the transverse cord. The reference by feminine gender is because cord (<s>rajju</s>) is intended. The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) is for combining with the alternative method. The length, doubled, tripled, a third, or a fourth, etc. — the word '<s>vā</s>' indicates various specific extensions. The meaning is: whatever cord is the standard measure, whether less than it, greater than it, or equal to it, is extended — in each case, by the previously stated method, making that many divisions, marking at [the place] deficient by one part, fixing [the cord] at the ends of the spine-cord, etc. — thus one should extend. Examples of these will be shown in the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>. The special point here is: the shoulders should be measured first. Reversing, the hips [are measured] — the rest is the same.
The mark made with half of the extension, and the parts it creates here —
that is fixed: having made one extension less than the additional [amount], [it becomes] the alignment.

children.text: vikalpavidhinokte siddhe "vyākhyāta viharaṇam' iti kimarthamuktam? śulbāntaroktānāṃ saptamamamḍalādīnāṃ gauravapratipādanārdhamuktameva viharaṇaṃ laghīya iti pratipādayitum /
children.translated_text: When the result is already established by the alternative rule, why is 'the extension has been explained' stated? It is stated to demonstrate that among the seventh-circle and other [methods] stated in other <s>Śulba</s> texts, the extension [method] explained [here] is lighter [simpler].
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary
For an overview of this very extension, another method of practice is stated — (length... remainder)

children.text:
āyāmapramāṇaṃ kṛtsnamabhāyasya kimataḥ kartavyaṃ, pūrvokta prakāreṇa lakṣaṇādi kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ /
ayamarthaḥ--āyāmamabhyasyāparasmin dvitīye caturthabhāgone lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāditi /
evaṃ kṛte satyāgantucaturthamāgantau caturthaṃ pratīkamāyāmaśvākṣṇayārajjuḥsyāt /
akṣṇayeti nipāto vibhaktipratirūpakaḥ koṇavācī. koṇagatā rajjurakṣṇayārajjuḥ, karmarajjurityarthaḥ /
śeṣaḥ akṣṇayārajjubhūtapratīkādanyāni trīṇi prīkāni /
tiryak mīyate anayeti tiryaṅbhānī, tiryagavaśtitā rajjuḥ /
rajjvabhiprāyaḥ strīliṅganirdeśaḥ /
vā śabdo 'bhyāsāntarasamuccayārthaḥ /
āyāmaṃ vā dbiguṇaṃ vā triguṇāṃ vā tṛtīyaṃ vā turīyaṃ vetyevamādyabhyāsaviśeṣārthaṃ vāghaṇam /
ayamrthaḥ--yāvatīrajjuḥ pramāṇaṃ tasmāt nyūnā tadadhikā vātatsamā vābhyasyate tatra tatra pūrvoktaprakāreṇa tāvatastavato vargān kṛtvā bhāgenaikena hīne lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhyāntayorantauniyamyetyādinā prakāreṇa viharediti /
eṣāmudāharaṇānyuttarasūtre darśayiṣyante /
nanuca lakṣaṇanimittararthaṃ rajjavāmapāyātāyāṃ lakṣaṇapūrvabhavinaḥ pramāṇādanantarasya ekasya bhāgasyākṣṇayārajjutā, bhāgāntarāṇāṃ tiryaṅbhākṣmayārajjustiryaṅbhānī śeṣa iti /
children.translated_text: Having extended the entire length-measure, what is to be done further? — the intent is that one should make marks etc. by the previously stated method. The meaning is: having extended the length, one should make a mark at [a point] deficient by a fourth part on the other, second [cord]. When this is done, the fourth of the extension — the fourth part corresponding to the extension — the length would be the diagonal cord. '<s>Akṣṇayā</s>' (diagonally) is an indeclinable substitute for the case-ending, denoting a corner. The cord going to the corner is the diagonal cord, i.e., the working cord. The remainder: apart from the part that becomes the diagonal cord, there are three other parts. '<s>Tiryaṅmānī</s>': that by which the transverse is measured — the transversely situated cord. The feminine reference is because cord is intended. The word '<s>vā</s>' is for accumulating with another method. The meaning is: when a cord divisible by six or by four is used — one part being the diagonal and all remaining parts being the transverse — this is understood. 'The extension has been explained' means: the extension [method] already explained is [the one to use], not any other extension, even though there may be multiple applications in the extension.

children.text:
ucyate--prathamabhūter'dhābhyāse ṣaḍbhāgone lakṣamamityetāvanmātramityabhi matam, tāvatārdha ūnabhāgaḥ kimarthaḥ, kimabhyāso mūlato hīyate utāntataḥ, anye ca bhāgāḥ kimarthaṃ, te ca kuta iti na jñāyate, tatra niyamahetorabhāvāt /
apravṛttiraniyamo va syādihāgantucaturthamāyāmaśvākṣṇayārajjuḥ tiryaṅbhānī śeṣa iti ataḥsa eko bhāgo 'bhyāsamūlataḥ, itare bhāgasyākṣṇayārajjutve bhāgāntarāṇāṃ tiryaṅbhānitve ca pṛthagbhūtābhyāsa eva vaktavye kasmāttadviparītaṃ kṛtaṃ, ucyate--ardhābhyāsārdhāyāmābhyāsayonyāyamabhyāsaviṣaye sūtrāvayavairdraḍhayituṃ viparītaṃ kṛtam /
kiṃ cātrābhyāsasya ṣoḍhā vibhāge caturdhā vibhāge ca ekasya bhāgasyākṣṇayārajjutā bhāgāntarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tiryaṅbhāni tā ca pratipadyate /
vyākhyātaṃ viharaṇamityatra vyākhyātameva viharaṇaṃ nānyadviharaṇamityayamarthaḥ, āgantau nyūgānāmanekaviṣayatve 'pi parvoktameva, viharaṇaṃ nānyadviharaṇamiti /
children.translated_text: It is said: in the half-extension, the mark is at [a point] deficient by a sixth — only this much is intended. What is the purpose of the remaining deficient part? Does the extension decrease from the base or from the end? And what purpose do the other parts serve? And whence [are they derived]? This is not known, due to the absence of a reason for the restriction. There would be non-application or non-restriction. Here, 'the fourth of the extension, the length, is the diagonal cord; the transverse is the remainder' — therefore that one part is from the base of the extension; the diagonality of other parts, and the transverse-nature of [remaining] parts — rather than stating [these as] separate extensions, why is the reverse done? It is said: to strengthen by the components of the <s>sūtra</s> the principle of half-extension and half-length-extension in the domain of extension, the reverse is done. Moreover, in the sixfold division and fourfold division of the extension here, the diagonality of one part and the transverse-nature of all remaining parts is established.
On this, the verses:
The parts of the measure including extension, as many as are commensurate with the extension —
in the additional [portion], twice as many exist; the mark is at one less than that.
If those [parts] of the measure including extension have fractions, then by the number of fractions,
one should cut the additional portion doubled; the mark is at one part less — this very [rule].
When the additional [portion] is less or more, how in the measure including extension
would the determination of parts be? And how would the alignment be?
Whether equal, less, or more, in the additional [portion] there is always unity;
depending on that, in the measure there would be unity of parts or hundredths of fractions.
When the additional is greater, the measure alone would always be a single part;

children.text: nyune bhāgaikyanānātve syātāṃ sāṃśe ca kevale // .5 //
children.translated_text: when less, there would be unity or multiplicity of parts, in both fractional and whole [cases].
When deficient by three-quarters, there is a fractional nature; when deficient by half, there is alignment;
when equal, there would be unity of parts only — thus is the determination of parts.
Having made the measure including extension with a cut equal to the fraction,
then also [cut] the additional with a number of cuts twice that number.
By however many fractions the part is deficient by one here,
by that many fractions deficient, the marking operation [occurs] in the additional.
The part by which the extension falls short in completing [the measure] —
that part is for the mark; its filling requires twice as many parts.
The sage, while taking a third, together with a sixth part,
considers the parts of the measure including extension as belonging to a double-extension here.
Having first trisected the measure including extension,
stating the extension as one-third, [it is] considered as having a sixth.
Having accepted that, he established the mark at one part less;
therefore, by the number of parts of the measure including extension,
one should cut the additional doubled; at one part less would be the alignment.
Following the number three, by the sage who states the number six,
the number pertaining to the parts of the measure including extension is doubled in the additional;
since, in the statement of third and sixth, two [arise] in the domain including extension.
They stated the extension from the measure including extension as having double-cut;
since that, conjoined with the number one, by the number of the deficient-part place,
doubled — such would be the determination of parts in the additional;
or, making the measure including extension with a part equal to half the extension,
cutting the additional by that number, at one less — here is the mark;
by the force of the word 'third,' this principle is derived.
And the statement of 'a fifteen and an eight,' etc.,
is the equality-measure of the fifteen and the eight;
or another: that of the twelve and the thirty-five;
with triple additional and preceded by the former third extension, endowed [thus],
applied to the latter by the fifth — or endowed with a quintuple,
these are within the domain of length-extension for the purpose of manipulation.
Where those two would not apply, those having the principle of extension as cause,
in half-extension, likewise for length-extension — mutually
the dependent subsidiary rule, and likewise the basis of this principle,
even when the additional is of diverse kinds, and its parts are of such nature,
why is the alignment procedure [done] by omitting one part?

children.text: ardhabhyāse tu bhāgone lakṣaṇaṃ yat tṛtīyake // 23 //
children.translated_text: In half-extension, the mark which is at [a point] deficient by one part in the third —
having set that aside, in the length-extension, those sharing its result,
the one-part distinction of transverse-cord and diagonal-cord —
relying on [that], he states the determination; therefore the mark is at one less here.
Enough of excessive detail.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]
(On 'the length or... extension')

children.text:
atha yogāntaramāha--
pramāṇamātre śulbe (pramāṇamevābhyaśca tāṃ rajjuṃ caturdhā saṃbhujya tṛtīyacaturthayormadhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāparayoḥ pāśau pratimucya caturthamāyāmaśva) viharaṇakāle 'kṣṇayārajjuḥ kāryā /
śeṣaḥ pādona āyāmastiryaṅbhānīsthānīyaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--āyāmaṃ dviguṇaṃ kṛtvānyatarasminnarghe caturthabhāgena lakṣaṇamiti /
yathā gārhapatyaciterāyatane caturaratnau caturaratnimabhyaśca triṣvaratniṣu lakṣaṇamiti kṛtvā viharet /
children.translated_text: Now another method is stated: on a cord equal to the measure (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — (extending the measure itself and folding that cord in four, making a mark between the third and fourth [parts], attaching loops at the two ends, the fourth of the length) — at the time of extension, the diagonal cord should be made. The remainder: the length minus a quarter — this stands in place of the transverse cord. This is what is stated: having doubled the length, on one half, [the mark is] at a fourth part — thus one should make the mark and then extend. For example, in the site of the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar of four <s>aratnis</s> (cubits): extending four cubits, at three cubits the mark — thus one should extend.
This has been explained.
By [the rule beginning with] 'the ends of the lateral [sides]' and so on.
Here, two verses for the purpose of construction (<s>viharaṇa</s>) with a cord of the desired repeated length:
On the desired lateral length (<s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>), one should add the desired additional cord (<s>āgantu-rajju</s>);
as many parts as are equal to half the repeated length, together with the excess in length. // 1 //
The repeated length, having been divided into that many [parts], a mark should be made at [the point] one less [than the total];
one part is the length; the diagonal (<s>karṇa</s>) is the crosswise [line]; the remainder shall be [the breadth]. // 2 //
<s>Kapardi</s>'s commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pārśvamānī tiryaṅmānī ca yat pṛthagbhute kurutas tad ubhayaṃ karoti || ĀpŚus_1.4a ||
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord (<s>akṣṇayā-rajju</s>) of a rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>) produces separately what the lateral measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) and the transverse measure (<s>tiryaṅmānī</s>) [each produce] -- it produces both combined. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.4a ||

children.text:
dīrghacaturaśrasyetyarthaḥ /
samamaṇḍalasya pārśvamānyādīnām abhāvād viṣamacaturaśrāccāyāmāḥ parigṛhyante /
pārśvamānī tiryaṅbhānī kuruta iti nirdeśādakṣṇayārajjurityekavacananirdeśācca yasya caturaśrasya pārśvamānyekā tiryaṅbhānyekaivākṣṇayārajjuḥsaṅgṛhyate pārśvamānyā kṛte caturaśre yāvat kṣetraṃ bhavati tiryaṅbhānyā ca, tadubhayamakṣṇayārajjuḥ karoti--pārśvamānīkṣetraṃ tiryaṅmānīkṣetraṃ ca karotītyarthaḥ /
vakṣyati ca "trikacatuṣkayoḥ' ityādinā /
trikasya vargo nava (3n3u9);
children.translated_text: The meaning is: of a rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>). Since a circle (<s>samamaṇḍala</s>) lacks lateral measures and the like, the measures are taken from the oblong quadrilateral (<s>viṣama-caturaśra</s>). From the instruction 'the lateral measure and transverse measure produce,' and from the singular usage 'the diagonal cord,' it is understood that the quadrilateral whose lateral measure is one and transverse measure is one, and whose diagonal cord is [also] one, is meant. By the area produced by the lateral measure and that by the transverse measure -- the diagonal cord produces both, that is, it produces the area of the lateral measure and the area of the transverse measure. And it will state 'of [the sides] three and four' and so on. The square of three is nine (3x3=9);

children.text:
catuṣkasya vargaḥ ṣoḍaśa (4n4u16) /
ṣoḍaśasu navake kṣipte (16a9u25)pañcaviṃśatiḥ /
pañcakā vargāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ (5u5n5)evaṃ savatra draṣṭavyam /
pṛthaggrahaṇaṃ saṃsargo mā bhūdityevamartham /
bhūtagrahaṇaṃ kimarthaṃ? pṛthakkuruta ityucyamāne saṃsargaviśeṣo 'pi syāt /
bhūtagrahaṇe satyetaddoṣo na bhavati /
children.translated_text: the square of four is sixteen (4x4=16). When nine is added to sixteen (16+9=25), [the result is] twenty-five. The squares of five are twenty-five (5x5=25) -- thus it should be seen everywhere. The word 'separately' (<s>pṛthak</s>) is used so that there be no mixing. What is the purpose of the word 'produced' (<s>bhūta</s>)? If one says 'separately produces,' even a particular mixing might [be implied]. With the word 'produced' being present, this fault does not arise.
The construction (<s>viharaṇa</s>) is stated by means of those knowable [measures]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.4b ||

children.text:
tābhiruktābhistasṛbhiruktaṃ viharaṇam /
jñeyābhiḥ jñātuṃ śakyābhiḥ--manasā parikalpitābhiḥ /
uktena mārgeṇa viharedityathaḥ /
praugādiṣu karaṇaparijñānārthametatsūtramihāpyupakariṣyatītyatroktam /
children.translated_text: The construction stated by those three stated [measures] that are knowable -- that is, capable of being known, mentally conceived. The meaning is that one should construct by the stated method. This <s>sūtra</s> will be useful here also for the purpose of understanding the procedure in [constructing] the <s>prauga</s> (chariot-shaped altar) and other [fire-altars] -- thus it is stated here.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
This construction (<s>viharaṇa</s>) is called <s>samādhi</s> (solution) because of the equalization of areas. Showing the causal relationship of this [with the solution], he says:
(Construction of the rectangle)

children.text:
dīrghasya--dīrghacaturaśrasya, samasyeti ca sāmarthyāllabhyate, tadatrraivaṃ vyākhyāsyate--akṣṇayārajjustiryaṅmānī coktā, pārśvaṃ yayā mīyate sā pārśvamānī, yat pṛthagbhūte--nānābhūte, kurutaḥ--saṃpādayataḥ tadubhayamubhayakṣetraparimitaṃ ekaṃ kṣetraṃ karoti--saṃpādayatītyarthaḥ, dīrghasya caturaśrasya pārśvamānī svayameva pāśvamānī svayameva pārśvamānī tiryaṅnānīca bhūtvā yatkṣetraṃ karoti akṣṇayā rajjuḥsvayameva pārśvamānī tiryaṅ mānī ca bhūtvā tadubhayakṣetraparimitaṃ kṣetraṃ karoti /
tābhir jñeyābhiruktaṃ viharaṇaṃ--yā evaṃbhatāḥ pāśvamānītiryaṅmānyakṣṇayārajjavaḥ
children.translated_text: Of the rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>) -- and the word 'of the square' (<s>samasya</s>) is obtained by implication -- this will be explained as follows: the diagonal cord and transverse measure have been stated; the lateral measure is that by which the side is measured. 'Separately produced' means 'made distinct'; 'produce' means 'accomplish' -- [the diagonal] accomplishes one area measured by both areas, that is, the lateral measure of the rectangle, itself becoming both the lateral measure and the transverse measure, produces the area [equal to both]; the diagonal cord, itself becoming both the lateral measure and the transverse measure, produces an area measured by both those areas. Those knowable lateral measures, transverse measures, and diagonal cords --

children.text:
tābhirjñeyābhirjñātuṃ śakyābhiḥ, uktaprakārapārśvamānītiryaṅmānyakṣṇayārajjūnāmanyatarayoḥ parimāṇajñānenānyatarā jñātuṃ śakyeti tā jñeyāḥ /
tatkathaṃ, yathā iyatkaraṇī pārśvamānī iyatkaraṇi tiryaṅmānīti jñāte 'kṣṇayārajjustadubhayaphalakṣetrakaraṇīti jñāyate /
evamiyatkaraṇī pārśvamānī iyatkaraṇyakṣṇayārajjuriti jñāte 'kṣṇayārajjuphalabhūtakṣetrāt pārśvamānīphalabhūtakṣetre śodhite śiṣṭakṣetrasya karaṇī tiryaṅmānīti jñāyate, tatheyatkaraṇī tiryaṅmānī iyatkaraṇyakṣṇayārajjuriti
children.translated_text: by those knowable [measures], that is, capable of being known: by knowing the measurement of any two among the lateral measure, transverse measure, and diagonal cord stated in this manner, the third can be known. How so? When the lateral measure of a certain magnitude and the transverse measure of a certain magnitude are known, the diagonal cord is known as the producer of the area [equal to] the product of both those. Similarly, when the lateral measure of a certain magnitude and the diagonal cord of a certain magnitude are known, subtracting the area produced by the lateral measure from the area produced by the diagonal cord, the producer of the remaining area is known as the transverse measure. And when the transverse measure of a certain magnitude and the diagonal cord of a certain magnitude are known,

children.text:
jñāte 'kṣṇayārajjuphalabhūtakṣetrāttiryaṅmānīphalabhūtakṣetre śodhite śiṣṭakṣetrasya karaṇī pārśvamānīti jñātuṃ śakyate /
evametā jñeyāḥ, tābhirjñeyābhiruktaṃ viharaṇaṃ--yaduktaṃ viharaṇaṃ tattābhirjñeyābhirnājñeyābhirityarthaḥ, evamuktasya viharaṇasyasamādhihetutvamavagantavyamityabhiprāyaḥ /
athavā jñeyābhiḥ manasi kalpitumucitābhiḥ pūrvoktaṃ viharaṇaṃ kartavyam /
ayamarthaḥ--pārśvamānītiryaṅmānyakṣṇayārajjūnāṃ pramāṇaṃ jñātvā tiryaṅmānyakṣṇayārajjūbhayapramāṇāmekāṃ rajjuṃ mītvā tiryaṅmānyante lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tayā pūrvoktaṃ viharaṇaṃ kartavyamiti /
pūrvoktānāmārdhābhyāsādīnāṃ kāni cidudāharaṇānyatrocyante /
ardhābhyāse tathā--dvādaśaṅgulapramāṇe ṣaḍaṅgulamabhyaste tadaṣṭādaśāṅgulam /
tatrāgantunā ṣaḍaṅgulena pramāṇe paricchinne sābhyāsasya pramāṇasya ṣaḍaṅgulāstrayo bhāgāḥ /
tatra bhāgasa yāstisraḥ, tābhistisṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: subtracting the area produced by the transverse measure from the area produced by the diagonal cord, the producer of the remaining area can be known as the lateral measure. Thus these are 'knowable'; the construction stated by those knowable [measures] -- the stated construction is [performed] by those knowable [measures] and not by unknowable ones. The intent is that the causal relationship with the solution of the construction stated thus should be understood. Alternatively, by those 'knowable' -- fit to be conceived in the mind -- the previously stated construction should be performed. This is the meaning: knowing the measurements of the lateral measure, transverse measure, and diagonal cord, measuring a single cord with the combined measurements of the transverse measure and diagonal cord, making a mark at the end of the transverse measure, the previously stated construction should be performed with that [cord]. Some examples of the previously stated half-addition and other [methods] are given here. In the half-addition, thus: when the measure is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths), six <s>aṅgulas</s> added gives eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. When the measure is divided by the additional six <s>aṅgulas</s>, there are three parts of the six <s>aṅgulas</s> of the added measure. The parts therein are three; with those three

children.text:
dviguṇābhiḥṣaḍbhirāgantau ṣaḍaṅgule cchinne tasyaiko bhāga ekaikamaṅgulaṃ /
tatra ṣaḍbhāgone lakṣaṇe kṛte bhāgenaikena sahita āyāmaḥ trayodaśāṅgulaṃ akṣṇayārajjuḥ śeṣāḥ pañcabhāgāḥ /
pañcāṅgulī tiryaṅmānī, tatra dvādaśāṅgulaṃ pramāṇam, caturaśrāṇi catuścatvāriṃśacchatamaṅgulikṣetrāṇi karoti /
tathā trayodaśāṅgulākṣṇayārajjuḥ, tadubhayamekonasaptatyādhikaśatamaṅgulikṣetrāṇi karoti /
āyāmābhyāse yathā--āyāmo dvādaśāṅgulaḥ /
āgantuś ca tāvāneva /
sābhyāsaśca pramāṇasyāgantuparimito dvau bhāgau /
taddviguṇasaṅkhyayā'gantau chinne tryaṅgulāścatvāra āgantau bhāgāḥ /
tatrāgantucaturthamāyāmaśvākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcadaśāṅgulā, śeṣatiryaṅmānī navāṅgulā, tatra navāṅgulaikāśītimaṅgulikṣetrāṇi karoti, āyāmaḥ pūrvavadeva, pañcadaśāṅgulā akṣṇayārajjuḥ tadubhayaṃ pañcaviṃśatyadhikaśatamaṅgulikṣetrāṇi karoti /
āyāmadviguṇābhyāse yathā--āyāmo dvādaśāṅgulaḥ, dviguṇaścaturviṃśatyaṅgulaḥ, tatrābhyāsena pramāṇe paricchidyamāne abhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ, pramāṇaṃ tadardhaṃ, ardhenaikasmin paricchidyamāne trīṇyardhāni taddviguṇacchedāḥ, tatraikaikamardhaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ dve ardhe aṣṭāṅgule eko bhāgaḥ, tadane lakṣaṇaṃ, tena yuktaṃ pramāṇaṃ, viṃśatyaṅgulamakṣṇayārajjuḥ, tadna āgantau caturaṅgulaṃ pārśvacatuṣṭayaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulaṃ, sā tiryaṅmānī tatra ṣoḍaśāṅgulā ṣaṭpañcāśacchatadvayamaṅgulikṣetrāṇi karoti, āyāmo dvādaśāṅgulaḥ, catuśvatvāriṃśacchataṃ tadubhayaṃ catvāriṃśacchatāni viṃśatyaṅgulākṣṇayārajjuḥ karoti, yadvābhyāsa eko bhāgaḥ pramāṇaṃ tadardhamekasmin bhāge dviguṇe dve saṃkhye, arghe dviguṇite dve ardhe /
tatraikā saṃkhyā trisaṃkhyayā'gantau caturviṃśatyaṅgule chinne tasyaikaiko bhāgaḥ aṣṭāṅgulaḥ, tenaikena sahitaṃ pramāṇaṃ, viṃśatyaṅgulā'kṣṇayayārajjurityāti pūrvoktameva /
tṛtīyābhyāse yathā--pramāṇaṃ caturviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ, tasyatṛtīyamaṣṭāṅgulaṃ, tasmiṃścaturviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ, tasmiṃścaturviṃśatyaṅgule prakṣipte sābhyāsaṃ pramāṇaṃ dvātriṃśadaṅgulaṃ, tatra sābhyāsasya pramāṇasyāganatusahitāśvatvāro bhāgāḥ, taddviguṇacchede āganturaṣṭabhāgāḥ, tatraiko bhāga ekāṅgulaṃ, tatra bhāgenaikena sahitaṃ pramāṇaṃ pañcaviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ, akṣṇayārajjuḥ saptāṅkulāni tiryaṅbhānī saikonapañcāśatkaroti /
caturviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ pramāṇaṣaṭsaptatiṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ ṣaṭ śatāni ca karoti evamevābhyāsāntareṣvapi draṣṭavyam /
trikacatuṣkayorityādinā kānicidudāharaṇānyuttaratra svayameva vakṣyati /
alamati prasaṅgena /
children.translated_text: doubled to six, when the additional six <s>aṅgulas</s> are divided, one part thereof is one <s>aṅgula</s> each. When a mark is made at [the point] less by six parts, the length together with one part is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> -- [this is] the diagonal cord; the remaining five parts, five <s>aṅgulas</s>, is the transverse measure. There, the measure of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> produces one hundred and forty-four square <s>aṅgula</s>-areas. Likewise, the diagonal cord of thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> produces both, [totaling] one hundred and sixty-nine square <s>aṅgula</s>-areas. In the length-addition, thus: the length is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>; the additional [cord] is also that much; the added measure has two parts measured by the addition. When divided by twice that number, four parts in the additional [cord] are three <s>aṅgulas</s> each. There, one-fourth of the addition plus the length is the diagonal cord of fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>; the remaining transverse measure is nine <s>aṅgulas</s>. Nine <s>aṅgulas</s> there produce eighty-one square <s>aṅgula</s>-areas; the length as before; the diagonal cord of fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> produces both -- one hundred and twenty-five [sic] square <s>aṅgula</s>-areas. In the double-length addition, thus: the length is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, doubled is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; when the measure is divided by the addition, the addition is one part, the measure is its half; when one half is divided, there are three halves; double divisions thereof [give] one-half being four <s>aṅgulas</s> each, two halves being eight <s>aṅgulas</s> -- one part; [at] one part less, the mark; the measure combined with that is twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> -- the diagonal cord; thus the four sides of four <s>aṅgulas</s> each in the additional [portion] total sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> -- that is the transverse measure. The sixteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [transverse measure] produces two hundred and fifty-six square <s>aṅgula</s>-areas; the length is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, [producing] one hundred and forty-four; the diagonal cord of twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> produces both -- four hundred. [...] In the one-third addition, thus: the measure is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; its third is eight <s>aṅgulas</s>; when that eight <s>aṅgulas</s> is added to the twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>, the measure with addition is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>. The added measure has four parts including the addition; with double division, the addition has eight parts, each part being one <s>aṅgula</s>. The measure combined with one such part is twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> -- the diagonal cord; seven <s>aṅgulas</s> is the transverse measure, which produces forty-nine. Twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> as the measure produces five hundred and seventy-six; twenty-five produces six hundred and twenty-five. Thus it should be seen in other additions too. He himself will state some examples later with 'of [the sides] three and four' and so on. Enough of this digression.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]:
(The diagonal construction of the rectangle)
Now he states the construction with its rationale, of many kinds:

children.text: dīrghasya caturaśrasya pārśvamānyā samacaturaśre kṛte yat kṣetraṃ saṃpadyate,yacca tiryaṅbhānyā tadubhayaṃ akṣṇayārajjvā samacaturaśre kṛte saṃpadyate kṣetraṃ /
children.translated_text: The area produced when a square is made with the lateral measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) of a rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>), and that [produced] by the transverse measure (<s>tiryaṅmānī</s>) -- the diagonal cord (<s>akṣṇayā-rajju</s>) produces both [combined] when a square is made with it.
The example beginning with 'of [the sides] three and four' [illustrates this].

children.text:
evañcāsāṃ dvayorjñātayostṛtīyā jñātuṃ śakyate /
yathā pārśvamānītiryaṅbhānyorjñātayoḥ te pṛthagvargayitvā saṃyojya tadvargamlamakṣṇayārajjuḥ /
tathā pārśvamānyakṣṇayārajjvorjñātayoḥ akṣṇayārajjuvargātpārśvamānīvarṅga viśodhya (vi) śiṣṭasya mūlaṃ tiryaṅbhānī /

children.translated_text: Similarly, subtracting the square of the transverse measure, [the square root of the remainder] is the lateral measure.
By such knowable [measures], the previously stated construction [is performed].
The examples beginning with 'of [the sides] three and four' [illustrate] this very [principle].
The two preceding applications (<s>yoga</s>) are also elaborations of this very [theorem].

And thus, when two of these [three measures] are known, the third can be known. For instance, when the lateral measure and transverse measure are known, squaring them separately and adding [the results], the square root of that sum is the diagonal cord. Likewise, when the lateral measure and diagonal cord are known, subtracting the square of the lateral measure from the square of the diagonal cord, the square root of the remainder is the transverse measure.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):
