children.text: caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjurdvistavatīṃ bhūmiṃ karoti | samasya dvikaraṇī || ĀpŚus_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord of a square produces twice the area. The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (the producer of double [the area]) of the square. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.5 ||

children.text: pramāṇaṃ tṛtīyena vardhayet tac caturthenātmacatustriṃśonena saviśeṣaḥ || ĀpŚus_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: One should increase the measure by its third; that [result] by its fourth, diminished by its own thirty-fourth part -- [this is] <s>saviśeṣa</s> (the approximate [value]). || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.6 ||

children.text:
samasya dvikaraṇī /
samasya caturaśrasya akṣṇayārajjuḥ samacaturaśrasya kṣetraṃ yāvadbhavati tasya dviguṇaṃ karoti /
samasya grahaṇaṃ kimartham? dīrghanivṛcyarthamiti cenna, uktārthatvāt /
akṣṇayārajjorabhāvānmaṇḍalasyāprasaṅgaḥ /
sarvātmanā samasya pratipacyarthamiti, tadapyaprayojakam /
akṣṇayārajjurityekavacananirdeśāt /
pramāṇaṃ tṛtīyena vardhayet pramāṇaṃ tṛtayiṃ prakṣipet /
taccaturthena /
taditi prakṣiptatṛtīyaṃ parāmṛśyate /
tṛtīyaṃ svacaturthena varghayediti śeṣaḥ /
ātmacatustriṃśonena--etat caturthasya viśeṣaṇam, taccaturthaṃ catustriṃśaddhā vibhajyaikaṃ bhāgamutsṛjya śiṣṭenetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (producer of double) of the square: the diagonal cord of a square produces double the area of the square. What is the purpose of the word 'square' (<s>samasya</s>)? If [one says] it is to exclude the rectangle -- no, because [that] has already been stated. Since a circle has no diagonal cord, there is no occasion [for confusion]. [Perhaps] it is to fully establish [the rule] for the square specifically -- but that too is unnecessary, because of the singular usage 'the diagonal cord.' 'One should increase the measure by its third' -- one should add a third to the measure. 'That by its fourth' -- 'that' refers to the [measure] with the third already added. The rest is: one should increase the third by its own fourth. 'Diminished by its own thirty-fourth' -- this is a qualifier of the fourth: that fourth should be divided into thirty-four parts, and one part discarded -- this is the meaning.

children.text:
saviśeṣaḥ--saviśeṣa iti saṃjñā /
evaṃ saṃvargitasya saha viśeṣaṇa vartata iti anvarthā saṃjñā /
dvādaśe catvāri caturṣu ekaṃ catustriṅkṣaddhā vibhajya ekaṃ bhāgamutsṛjya, evaṃ tilonasaptadaśāṅgulaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: In twelve [<s>aṅgulas</s>], four; in four, one; dividing into thirty-four parts and discarding one part -- thus it becomes seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> less one <s>tila</s> (sesame seed).

children.text: dvādaśāṅgulasya tilavargaḥ ; ekaṃ niyutaṃ ṣaḍayutāni ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni ṣaṣṭiḥ catvārīti (166464) tilapramāṇāni saptadaśāṅgulamānasya tilonasya tilavargaḥ-- trīṇi niyutāni trīṇi niyutāni trīṇyayutāni dve sahasre nava śatāni vaṃśatirnava ca (332929) atraikatrikayoḥśeṣo na bhavatīti veṇoḥsaviśeṣe gṛhyamāṇe daśatilakṣetrāṇyatiriktāni /
children.translated_text: The <s>tila</s>-square of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>: one <s>niyuta</s> (million), six <s>ayutas</s> (ten-thousands), six thousand, four hundred, and sixty-four (1,66,464) <s>tila</s>-measures. The <s>tila</s>-square of the seventeen-<s>aṅgula</s> [diagonal] less one <s>tila</s>: three <s>niyutas</s>, three <s>niyutas</s>, three <s>ayutas</s>, two thousand, nine hundred and twenty-nine (3,32,929). Here, in [the comparison of] one and three, no remainder exists; thus when the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> is taken with the approximation (<s>saviśeṣa</s>), ten <s>tila</s>-areas are in excess.
Therefore even half a <s>nīvāra</s>-<s>śūka</s> (wild-rice awn) is in excess.

children.text: tasmādviśeṣa iti vyavahārārthameva bhaviṣyatīti pragaṇayya saṃjñā kṛtācāryeṇa //
children.translated_text: Therefore '<s>viśeṣa</s>' (remainder/approximation) is a designation made by the <s>ācārya</s> (master) for practical purposes only, having [already] calculated [the excess].

<s>Saviśeṣa</s> (approximate) -- '<s>saviśeṣa</s>' is the technical name. Thus, [it is called] 'with a remainder' (<s>sa-viśeṣa</s>) because it exists together with a remainder -- the name accords with its meaning.
Now another [method]: || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.7a ||
The rest is: 'we shall state a construction (<s>vihāra</s>).'

children.text: pramāṇamātrīṃ rajjum ubhayataḥ pāśāṃ karoti || ĀpŚus_1.7b ||
children.translated_text: One makes a cord of the measure of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard), with loops on both sides. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.7b]

children.text: yatpramāṇaṃ caturaśraṃ kartumicchati tāvatpramāṇāṃ rajjumubhayataḥpāśāṃ kṛtvā-
children.translated_text: Having made a cord of the measure of the square one wishes to construct, with loops on both sides —

children.text: madhye lakṣaṇam ardhamadhyamayoś ca pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ rajjum āyamya pāśayorlakṣaṇeṣviti śaṅkūn nihaty upāntyayoḥ pāśau pratimucya madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ nimittaṃ karoti | madhyame pāśau pratimucya, uparyupari nimittaṃ madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamaṃsam āyacchet | unmucya pūrvasmād aparasmin pratimucya madhyamenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇim āyacchet | evamuttarau śroṇyaṃsau || ĀpŚus_1.7c ||
children.translated_text: Making a mark at the middle and at the midpoints of each half, stretching the cord along the spine-line, driving stakes at the loops and marks — [making] five [stakes]; fastening the loops at the second and fourth [stakes], drawing to the south by the middle mark, one makes a point. Fastening the loops at the middle [stake], [making] a further point above, drawing to the south by the middle mark, one should determine the southern shoulder. Releasing from the first [stake] and fastening on the last, by the same middle mark one should determine the southern hip. Likewise the northern hip and shoulder. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 1.7c]
First section.

children.text:
madhye lakṣaṇamardhamadhyamayośva--pāśalakṣamayormadhya ityarthaḥ /
pāśayorlakṣaṇeṣviti śaṅkuṃ nihatya, upāntyayordvitīyacaturthayoḥ pāśau pratimucya madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpasārya, nimittaṃ sādhyanimittaṃ kākapadaṃ kṛtvā, madhyame pāśau pratimucya, uparyupari kākapadaṃ tenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpasārya, śuṅkaṃ nihatya, tasminnekataraṃ pāśaṃ pratimucya, pūrvasmin śaṅkāvitaraṃ pāśantenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣimamaṃsamāyacchet /
tatra śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
sa dakṣiṇāsaḥ /
evamuttarataḥ pūrvasmātpāśamunmucyāparasmin pratimucya, tenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā śroṇī /
evamuttarataḥ pakṣaḥ /
tatra iyānviśeṣaḥ--śroṇī pūrvaṃ paścādaṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A mark at the middle and at the midpoints of each half' — the meaning is 'at the middle of the two loops and marks.' Having driven a stake 'at the loops and marks,' fastening the loops at the second and fourth [stakes], drawing to the south by the middle mark, having made a point — a crow's-foot mark — as the intended point, fastening the loops at the middle [stake], above that [first point], drawing further to the south by that same mark, driving a stake, fastening one loop on that [stake] and the other loop on the first stake, by that same mark one should determine the southern shoulder. There one should drive a stake. That is the southern shoulder. Likewise to the north: releasing the loop from the first [stake] and fastening on the last, by that same mark [one determines] the southern hip. Likewise the northern side. Here is the distinction: the hip [comes] first, the shoulder after.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary

children.text:
nanu caturaśrasyeti kathaṃ labhyate? tatkaraṇībhūtapārśvamānyādidarśanāt /
samasyeti kathaṃ? kurata iti dvivacananirdeśāt, akṣṇayārajjurityekavacananirdeśācca /
kuruta iti dvivacananirdeśe kṛte sati ekaprakārā pārśvamānī tiryaṅbhānī coti gamyate /
tathākṣṇayārajjurityekavacananirdeśāt sācāpyekaprakāroti jñāyate /
viṣamo 'pi dīrghacaturaśro vidyata eva /
yakyākṣṇayārajjū anyoyaṃ same bhavataḥ sa nivartyate /
samasyeti labhyate /
pṛthaggrahaṇasya saṃsargaviśeṣaṇatvanivṛcyartham /
dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuriyatkarotītyuktaṃ, samasya sā kiyatkarotītyata āha--
children.translated_text: Now, how is 'of a square' obtained? From the showing of side-measurements etc. that are its constituent means. And how [is it known to be] 'equal'? From the dual-number usage of '<s>kuruta</s>' (make [two]), and from the singular-number usage of '<s>akṣṇayārajju</s>' (diagonal cord). When the dual-number usage of '<s>kuruta</s>' is made, it is understood that the side-measurement and the breadth are of one kind. Likewise, from the singular-number usage of '<s>akṣṇayārajju</s>,' it is known that it too is of one kind [i.e., both diagonals are equal]. Even an unequal rectangle does exist. But that in which the two diagonal cords are mutually equal — that is excluded [from being 'unequal']. Thus 'of an equal [square]' is obtained. The separate mention [of 'sama'] is for the purpose of preventing [confusion with] a qualifying conjunction. Having stated what the diagonal cord of a rectangle does, [the author] states what it does for an equal [square] —
(And it makes [the area] quadruple.)

children.text:
samasya caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuddviṃstāvatīṃdviguṇāṃ /
yasyā bhūmeriyamakṣṇayārajjuḥ tāvaddvigūṇāṃ bhūmiṃ karoti /
dviguṇāyā bhūmeḥ karaṇībhavatītyarthaḥ /
dvistāvatīti mayūravyaṃsakādilakṣaṇaḥsamāsaḥ /
nanvakṣṇayārajjurityekavacananirdeśāt samacaturaśrā "anupapadatvā cchabdasyeti' nyāyācca dvitīyāpi tādṛśyeveti vijñāyate /
tena samasyeyaṃ na viṣamasyeti gamyate /
ataḥ kimartaṃ samaśabdaḥ? /
ucyate--evaṃ tarhi miśraṇārthaḥ samaśabdaḥ /
dvistāvīṃ bhūmiṃ yugapadeva ekīkṛtya karatīti /
uttarārtho vā sama śabdaḥ /
nanu pūrvasūtra eva dīrghaśabdamapahāya caturaśrasyetyastu tenāsyāpi siddhirbhavatyeva, satyaṃ--tathāsatyuktanyāyena samasyaiva tatsyābha dīrghasya, tasmāt pṛthagevameva vaktavyam /
prakṛtopajīvanena saṃjñāṃ vidhātumāha--
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord of an equal square [produces an area] twice as much — doubled. Whatever area this diagonal cord [represents], it produces an area double of that. It becomes the <s>karaṇī</s> (producer/root) of the doubled area — that is the meaning. '<s>Dvistāvatī</s>' (twice as much) is a compound of the <s>mayūravyaṃsaka</s> type. Now, since from the singular-number usage of '<s>akṣṇayārajju</s>' and by the principle 'because the word would be inapplicable otherwise,' it is understood that the second [diagonal] is also of the same kind. Thereby it is understood that this [rule applies] to an equal [square], not to an unequal [rectangle]. Then for what purpose is the word 'sama' (equal)? It is answered: In that case, the word 'sama' is for the purpose of combining — it produces the doubled area simultaneously, making it one. Alternatively, the word 'sama' is for the subsequent [rule]. Now, [one might say] in the previous sūtra itself, removing the word 'dīrgha' (oblong) and having just 'of a quadrilateral,' the same result would follow. True — but then, by the stated principle, it would apply only to an equal [square], not to an oblong. Therefore it must be stated separately in this very manner. Using the current [topic] as a basis, [the author] states the technical term —
(<s>Saviśeṣa</s> [with the remainder/excess].)

children.text:
samasya caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ sā dvikaraṇīsaṃjñā bhavati /
anvarthaiṣā saṃjñā, dvayoḥkaraṇī dvikaraṇīti /
nanu pūrvasūtreṇaiva dvikaraṇītve siddhe ayuktā saṃjñā, satyaṃ, dvikaraṇītvaṃ siddhantathāpi dīrghatrikoṇādīnāmapi dvikaraṇyaḥsanti, tatra dvikaraṇītyukte asyā eva grahaṇaṃ yathā syādityevamarthaṃ saṃjñā /
nanu sā dvikaraṇītyeva vaktavyaṃ, samagrahaṇaṃ kimarthaṃ? vakṣyamāṇāpi saṃjñā samadvikaraṇīviṣayā yathā syāditi /
samagrahaṇasya pūrvasūtraviṣayatve atra sāmarthyāttatsiddhiḥ /
dvikaraṇyā eva prakārāntaramāha--
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord of an equal square — that receives the designation <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (the double-producer, i.e., √2 times the side). This designation is meaningful: 'the producer of two [areas]' is <s>dvikaraṇī</s>. Now, since the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>-nature is already established by the previous sūtra, the [separate] designation seems redundant. True, the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>-nature is established; nevertheless, even oblongs, triangles, and other [figures] have <s>dvikaraṇīs</s>. So that when '<s>dvikaraṇī</s>' is mentioned, only this one [of the square] is taken — for that purpose the designation [is given]. Now, [one might say] 'that is the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>' alone should be stated — for what purpose is the word 'sama' (equal) included? So that the designation to be stated [later] may also pertain to the <s>sama-dvikaraṇī</s> (the √2 of a square). Since the word 'sama' pertains to the previous sūtra, here [the designation] is established by implication. Of the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> itself, another aspect is stated —

children.text:
samacaturaśrasya pramāṇamāyāmaṃ tattṛtīyena vardhayedvṛddhiṃ gamayet, tacca tṛtīyaṃ svacaturtheṃna tṛtīyasya caturthabhāgenetyarthaḥ /
ātmacatustriśonena ātmaśabdena caturtho bhāgaḥ parāmṛśyate /
vardhayedityeva, sa viśeṣaḥ--tasya viśeṣa iti saṃjñā /
tṛtīyādinā yena vṛddhaṃ pramāṇaṃ tasya viśeṣasaṃjñā /
yathā--dvādaśāṅgulaṃ pramāṇaṃ caturaṅgulena vardhayet, taccaturaṅgulamekāṅgulena tilonena vardhayet /
caturviṃśattilāḥ pṛthusaṃśliṣṭā aṅguliriti pramāṇavido manyante /
vakṣyati, "ardhe tadviśeṣamabhyasya bāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ parigṛhṇīyāt' ityādi /
kathaṃ, madhyame saviśeṣaṃ pratimucya caturthena caturthasaviśeṣeṇetyevamādi /
atra saha viśeṣeṇa vartata iti sa viśeṣaḥ /
viśeṣasahitaṃ pramāṇameva saviśeṣa ityavagantavyam /
kimarthaṃ mahatī saṃjñā, anvarthaiṣā yathā syāditi, tatkathaṃ vipūrvaḥśiṣiratiśayavācī, " śiṣirasarvopādāne, vipūrvo 'tiśaye ' ityupadeśāt /
akṣṇayārajjubhūtadvikaraṇyāḥ pramāṇātiriktādaṃśāt kiñcidvisiṣyate atiricyata iti viśeṣaḥ /
yadvā tataḥ kiñcit kṣetraṃ viśeṣayati atirecayati mānakāla iti vā viśeṣaḥ /
tathāhi--catustriṃśattilā aṅgulirityuktam /
dvādaśāṅgulasya tilavargaḥ--ekaṃ niyutaṃ ṣaḍayutāni ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi catuvāri śatāni /
tilonasaptadaśāṅgulasya tilavargaḥ--trīṇi niyutāni trīṇyayutāni dve sahasre nava śatāni viṃśatirnava ca tilapramāṇāni caturaśrakṣetrāṇi /
atraikaṃ tilaṃ caturaśrakṣetradviguṇādatiricyate /
tatastasya viśeṣa iti saṃjñā /
veṇunā saviśeṣeṇa mīyamāne 'gnau pramīyamāne tvātmani yat kṣetramatiricyeta tena nīvāraśūkamātramapi sarvathātiriktaṃ na bhavati tannathūne tato 'lpataramiti dvikaraṇīkārye saviśeṣavyavahāraḥ /
idānīṃ prāsaṅgikamekaṃ viharaṇaṃ vyākhyāya viharaṇāntaramāha--
children.translated_text: One should increase the <s>pramāṇa</s> (side-measure) of an equal square by its third — make it grow; and that third [should be increased] by its own fourth, that is, by the fourth part of the third. Diminished by its own thirty-fourth — by the word 'own' (<s>ātma</s>) the fourth part is referred to. 'One should increase' — that is the <s>saviśeṣa</s>: the designation 'viśeṣa' (remainder/excess) [applies to it]. The <s>pramāṇa</s> increased by the third etc. receives the designation <s>viśeṣa</s>. For example: a <s>pramāṇa</s> of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> should be increased by four <s>aṅgulas</s>, and that four <s>aṅgulas</s> should be increased by one <s>aṅgula</s> diminished by a sesame-seed (<s>tila</s>). 'Twenty-four sesame-seeds placed side by side touching make one <s>aṅgula</s>' — so hold the authorities on measurement. He will state: 'Having doubled the <s>viśeṣa</s> on the half, one should enclose it with the outer <s>viśeṣas</s>' etc. How? 'Fastening at the middle with the <s>saviśeṣa</s>, by the fourth, by the fourth-with-<s>viśeṣa</s>' — thus etc. Here, 'that which exists together with the <s>viśeṣa</s> is <s>saviśeṣa</s>.' The <s>pramāṇa</s> itself combined with the <s>viśeṣa</s> is to be understood as <s>saviśeṣa</s>. For what purpose the elaborate designation? So that it may be meaningful — and how is that? The prefix 'vi' denotes excess, from the teaching: '<s>śiṣ</s> — with <s>vi</s> prefix, denotes excess.' From the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> which serves as the diagonal cord, the portion exceeding the <s>pramāṇa</s> — it exceeds somewhat — hence <s>viśeṣa</s> (excess). Alternatively, it distinguishes (exceeds) a certain area at the time of measurement — hence <s>viśeṣa</s>. For instance: it has been stated that thirty-four <s>tilas</s> make one <s>aṅgula</s>. The <s>tila</s>-square of a twelve-<s>aṅgula</s> [square] is: one <s>niyuta</s>, six <s>ayutas</s>, six thousand, four hundred [= 166,400]. The <s>tila</s>-square of seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a <s>tila</s> is: three <s>niyutas</s>, three <s>ayutas</s>, two thousand, nine hundred and twenty-nine <s>tila</s>-measure square areas [= 333,929]. Here one <s>tila</s> square-area exceeds the double of the square area [332,800]. Hence its designation is <s>viśeṣa</s>. When [the altar] is measured with a bamboo-rod with the <s>saviśeṣa</s> — when the fire[-altar] is being measured — whatever area exceeds in itself, by that [amount], not even a rice-husk in extent does it exceed in any way; [but] diminished from that, it is less — [this is] the use of <s>saviśeṣa</s> in the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> operation. Now, having explained one incidental construction, [the author] states another construction —
(Now another [method]: hips and shoulders.)

children.text:
athāparaṃ viharaṇaṃ--vyākhyāsyāma iti śeṣaḥ, pramāṇamātrīṃ ayāmamātrīṃ rajjuṃ ubhayataḥpāśāṃ ādyantayoḥ pāśayuktāṃ, madhye lakṣaṇaṃ nirañjanārthaṃ, ardhamadhyayoḥ pūrvārdhamadhye aparārdhamadhye ca lakṣaṇadvayaṃ nirañjanaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ mātavyabhūtalamadhyalekhāyāṃ rajjumāyamya--prasārya pāśayorlakṣaṇoṣviti pañca śaṅkvoḥ pāśau pratimucya madhyena nirañjanabhūtena dakṣiṇāpāyamya, nimittaṃ--cihnaṃ karoti /
nimittaṃ diksaṃdarśanārtham /

madhyame śaṅkau pāśau pratimucya, uparyuparinimittaṃ tasyopariṣṭādāsannataraṃ dakṣiṇāpāyamya, rajjuṃ tadante śaṅkuṃ nikāya, madhyamācchaṅkoḥ pāśāvunmucya, dakṣiṇaśaṅkāvekaṃ pāśaṃ pratimucya, pūrvasmin śaṅkānitaraṃ pāśaṃ pratimucya, nirañjanena dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ pratyāyacchet /
children.translated_text: Fastening the loops at the middle stake, [making] a further point above — closer above that; drawing to the south, driving a stake at the end of the cord; releasing the loops from the middle stake, fastening one loop on the southern stake and the other loop on the first stake, by the alignment-mark one should determine the southern shoulder.
One should stretch the cord such that the southern shoulder is established.

children.text: evameva dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇimāyacchedityevamādīni unmucya, pūrvasmādityādīnyuttarāṇi sūtrāṇi /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise [one determines] the southern hip' — thus etc.; 'releasing from the first' etc. are the subsequent sūtras for the northern [side].
This method with five stakes pertains to the equal square.

Now another construction — 'we shall explain' is to be supplied. A cord of the measure of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — that is, of the measure of the length — with loops on both sides, that is, furnished with loops at both ends; a mark at the middle — for the purpose of alignment; and at the midpoints of the halves — marks at the middle of the first half and the middle of the second half, two alignment-marks having been made; stretching the cord along the spine-line — the central line of the ground to be measured — having stretched it, 'at the loops and marks' — five stakes; fastening the loops at the second and fourth [stakes], drawing to the south by the middle alignment-mark — one makes a point, a sign. The point is for the purpose of indicating direction.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]
(And it makes [the area] quadruple.)

children.text:
caturaśrasyetyaviśeṣāt samasyetyatrāpi saṃbadhyate /
athavā uttarasūtragataṃ samasyeti padamatrāpi saṃbadhyate /
children.translated_text: Since 'of a quadrilateral' is unqualified [as to type], 'of an equal [square]' is also connected here. Alternatively, the word 'samasya' (of an equal [square]) occurring in the subsequent sūtra is also connected here.
The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (√2) of an equal [square].

children.text:
anantaroktā samasya caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ dvikaraṇīsaṃjñisā /
tāvatordvayoḥ kṣetrayoḥ karaṇāt /
tasya jñānopāyamāha--
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord of an equal square just mentioned [receives] the designation <s>dvikaraṇī</s>. Because it produces two areas equal to it. The method of knowing it is stated —
(The <s>pramāṇa</s>... diminished by [a thirty-fourth].)

children.text:
yathā--dvādaśāṅgulasya pramāṇasya tṛtīyaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ, tasya caturthamaṅguliḥ aṅguleśvatustriṃśo bhāgastilamātram /
evaṃ dvādaśāṅgulasyākṣṇayārajjustilonasapradaśāṅgulā /
tathā aṣṭācatvāriṃśadaṅgulasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ catustilonā aṣṭaṣaṣṭyaṅguletyādi /
children.translated_text: For example: the third of a <s>pramāṇa</s> of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> is four <s>aṅgulas</s>; its fourth is one <s>aṅgula</s>; the thirty-fourth part of an <s>aṅgula</s> is a <s>tila</s>-measure. Thus the diagonal cord of a twelve-<s>aṅgula</s> [square] is seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> minus a <s>tila</s>. Similarly, the diagonal cord of forty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> is sixty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> minus four <s>tilas</s> — and so forth.
(<s>Saviśeṣa</s> [with the remainder].)
The portion by which the diagonal cord exceeds the <s>pramāṇa</s> — that has the designation <s>viśeṣa</s> (excess).
'Having doubled that <s>viśeṣa</s> on the half' etc. is the illustration.
(Now another [method]: hips and shoulders.)
'At the midpoints of the halves' means 'at the midpoints of the [two] halves.' 'At the second and fourth' — at the second and fourth stakes.
<s>Nimitta</s> means 'sign' (point-mark).
The rest is clear.
This method pertains to the equal square.
Likewise to the north.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
Now another method. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.1a]
The meaning is: a particular construction method.

children.text: pṛṣṭhyāntayor madhye ca śaṅkūn nihatyārdhe 'rdhe tadviśeṣam abhyasya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvārdhamagamayet | antyayoḥ pāśau kṛtvā madhyame saviśeṣaṃ pratimucya pūrvasminn itaraṃ lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamaṅkam āyacchet | unmucya pūrvasmād aparasmin pratimucya lakṣaṇenaiva dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇim āyacchet | evam uttarau śroṇyaṃsau || ĀpŚus_2.1b ||
children.translated_text: Having driven stakes at the two ends of the spine-line and at the middle, having doubled the <s>viśeṣa</s> (excess) on each half and made marks, one should restore the half. Making the loops at the end[-stakes], fastening at the middle with the <s>saviśeṣa</s>, [fastening] the other on the first [stake], by the mark one should determine the southern shoulder. Releasing from the first [stake] and fastening on the last, by the same mark one should determine the southern hip. Likewise the northern hip and shoulder. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.1b]

children.text: caturaśrapramāṇāntayoḥśaṅkuṃ nihatya tayormadhye ca śaṅkuṃ nihatya ardhe--pramāṇārdhe, tadviśeṣaṃ--tasyārdhasya viśeṣaṃ, pramāṇaṃ tṛtīyena vardhayediti nyāyena lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā punarāgamayet prakṣipet /
antyayoḥ pāśau kṛtvā madhyame śaṅkau saviśeṣaṃ pāśaṃ pratimucya pūrvasmin śaṅkau itaraṃ pāśaṃ pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇenāpasārya śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
children.translated_text: Making loops at the end[-stakes], fastening the loop at the middle stake with the <s>saviśeṣa</s>, fastening the other loop at the first stake, drawing to the south by the mark, one should drive a stake.
That is the southern shoulder.

children.text: pūrvasmācchaṅkoḥ pāśamaparasmin śaṅkau pratimucya tenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇaṃ śroṇimāyacchet /
children.translated_text: Fastening the loop from the first stake onto the last stake, by that same mark one should determine the southern hip.
Drawing northward by the same [mark, one determines] the northern hip; and by reversal, the northern shoulder.

Having driven a stake at the two ends of the square's <s>pramāṇa</s>, and driven a stake at their middle, on the half — half of the <s>pramāṇa</s> — the <s>viśeṣa</s> of that, i.e., the <s>viśeṣa</s> of that half; having made a mark by the principle 'one should increase the <s>pramāṇa</s> by a third,' then one should restore it — place it back.
These two methods together are correct [i.e., complete] for the equal square.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(Now another [method]: hips and shoulders.)

children.text:
pramāṇamātrīṃ rajjumityeva, viharaṇopāyo yoga ityuktaṃ, pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ madhye ca śaṅkuṃ nihatya /
vyākhyātametat /
ardhepramāṇāmātracā rajjvā ardhe tadviśeṣamabhyasya saṃyojya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sūtrasaviśeṣārdhānte ardhaṃ āgamayet śiṣṭaṃ yathā pramāṇaṃ bhavati tathā'gamayet, ayamarthaḥ--ardhadvikaraṇīmātrīṃ kevalārdhamātrīṃ ca ekāṃ rajjuṃ mītvārdhadvikaraṇī mātre lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā rajjvantau pāśau kṛtvā madhyame śaṅkau saviśeṣamardhaṃ pratimucya pūrvasmin śaṅkau kevalamardhaṃ pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamaṃsamāyacchet--kuryāt /
unmucya pūrvasmāditi spaṣṭārthaḥ /
ayamapi yogaḥsamacaturaśraviṣaya eva /
ardhe tadviśeṣamiti pramāmasaviśeṣayoḥ prastutatvāt prasaṅgenocyate /
children.translated_text: A cord equal to the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure) — thus, the method of construction is called <s>yoga</s>. Having driven a gnomon at the two ends of the spine-line and at its center — this has been explained. With a cord equal to half the <s>pramāṇa</s>, having doubled that half with its extension and joined [the halves], making a mark, at the end of the cord-with-extension half, one should add the other half so that the remainder equals the <s>pramāṇa</s>. The meaning is: having measured a single cord equal to half the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (square-root-of-two cord) and equal to a plain half, making a mark at the half-<s>dvikaraṇī</s> measure, making loops at the cord-ends, fastening the extension-half on the central gnomon, fastening the plain half on the first gnomon, one should draw the southern shoulder by the mark. "Releasing from the first" — the meaning is clear. This <s>yoga</s> (method) also applies only to the even quadrilateral. "In the half, its extension" — since the <s>pramāṇa</s> and the extension are the subject at hand, this is stated incidentally.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> [commentary]
(Now another [method for] hips and shoulders)

children.text:
ardhe--pramāṇārdhamātre śulbe /
tadviśeṣaṃardhasyaiva viśeṣaṃ abhyasya tadviśeṣānte lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā anyadardhaṃ nirviroṣamāgamayet /
yathā--gārhapatyaciteḥ ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulāyā antayayormadhye ca śaṅkūnnihatya arve 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśadaṅgule tadviroṣaṃ catustilonaṃ viṃśatyaṅgulamabhyasya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvānyadardhaṃ aṣṭācatvāriṃśadaṅgulaṃ saṃyojayet /
evaṃ catustilonaṣoḍaśakottaraśatāṅgulaṃ śulbam /
antayorityādi spaṣṭam /
children.translated_text: "In the half" — in a cord equal to half the <s>pramāṇa</s>. Having doubled the extension of that very half, making a mark at the end of the extension, one should add the other half without extension.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: pramāṇaṃ tiryag dvikaraṇy āyāmas tasyākṣṇayārajjus trikaraṇī || ĀpŚus_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard) is the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure); the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (square-root-of-two [cord]) is the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure) of that [same standard]; the diagonal cord (<s>akṣṇayārajju</s>) of that [rectangle] is the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (square-root-of-three [cord]). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.2]

children.text:
pramāṇaṃ--prakramādestiryaṅnānī /
dvikataṇī--pārśvamānītasyaiva prakramādeḥ /
tasyaivaṃbhūtasya dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjustrikaraṇī--triguṇāṃ bhūmiṃ karoti /
tasya tiryaṅbhānībhūdasya /
kathaṃ ? pramāṇamekaṃ karoti pārśvamānī dvikaraṇī sā dvau karoti /
tadubhayamakṣṇayārajjuḥ karoti /
taduktaṃ dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ /
iti--
children.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s> — of the standard unit (<s>prakrama</s>), the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure). The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> — the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure) of that very standard unit. Of that oblong rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>) thus constituted, the diagonal cord is the <s>trikaraṇī</s> — it produces an area three times [the unit square]. Of that [rectangle] whose transverse measure has become [the standard]. How? The <s>pramāṇa</s> produces one [unit area]; the <s>pārśvamānī</s>, the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>, produces two. The diagonal cord produces both of those [together]. This is what is stated [by the rule]: "the diagonal cord of an oblong [rectangle]."
The <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> (square-root-of-one-third [cord]) is explained by this; but the division is ninefold. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.3]

children.text:
etenaiva mārgeṇa tṛtīyakaraṇī vyākhyātā /
anayaiva trikaraṇyā tṛtīyakaraṇyapyavagantuṃ śakyetyarthaḥ /
kathamityāha--trikaraṇīkṣetraṃ navadhā vibhajya ekaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
pramāṇatṛtīyaṃ bhavati /
trikaraṇyāḥ tṛtīyaṃ karoti /
tatra ślokaḥ--
children.translated_text: The <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> is explained by this very method. The meaning is that by this <s>trikaraṇī</s> itself, the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> too can be ascertained. How? He says: dividing the <s>trikaraṇī</s>-area ninefold, one should take one part. That is one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s>. [The side of that part] produces one-third of the <s>trikaraṇī</s> [area]. Herein is the verse:
"The diagonal cord is declared to be the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (triple-producer) of the <s>pramāṇa</s> and its extension;

children.text: asyā eva tṛtīyaṃ tu tṛtīyakaraṇīṃ viduḥ //
children.translated_text: one-third of this very [cord] is known as the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> (third-producer)."
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
(<s>Pramāṇa</s> ... <s>trikaraṇī</s>)
The <s>pramāṇa</s>, the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>, and the diagonal cord have been stated.

children.text: yasya caturaśrasya praṇāṇaṃ tiryaṅbhānī dvikaraṇī pārśvamānī tasya caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pramāṇapārśvamānī tiryaṅbhānī kṣetrasya trikaraṇībhavati //
children.translated_text: Of a quadrilateral whose <s>pramāṇa</s> is the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure) and whose <s>dvikaraṇī</s> is the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure), the diagonal cord of that quadrilateral — the area of the field [defined by] the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the <s>pārśvamānī</s>, and the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> — becomes the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (triple-producer).
The <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> is explained by this.

children.text:
trikaraṇīvyākhyāne tṛtīyakaraṇyapi vyākhyātā /
kathaṃ ? tṛtīyaṃ tiryāgdvikaṇyāyāmaḥ, tasyākṣṇayārajjustṛtīyakaraṇī /
children.translated_text: In the explanation of the <s>trikaraṇī</s>, the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> is also explained. How? [When] one-third is the transverse [measure] and the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> [of that third] is the length, the diagonal cord of that is the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>.
For ascertaining the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>, he says:

children.text:
(vibhāgastu navadhā)
tṛtīyakaraṇyavagame iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ /
kṣetrasya navadhā vibhāgaḥ kāryaḥ, kasya kṣetrasya ? pramāṇakṣetrasya trikaraṇīkṣetrasya vā /
ayamarthaḥ--yasya kṣetrasya tṛtīyakaraṇī sādhyate tat kṣetraṃ navadhā vibhajya tatrakaisya bhāgasya pārśvamānīṃ tiryaṅbhānīṃ kṛtvā tasyaiva bhāgasyākṣṇayārajjuṃ pārśvamānīṃ kṛtvā tābhyāṃ caturaśre kṛte caturaśre navadhā vibhakte tatraikasya bhāgasya karaṇīpramāṇacaturaścakṣetrasya tṛtīyakaraṇī bhavati /
sa ca vibhāgaḥ pramāṇakṣetratṛtīyamiti pradarśanam /
etena catuṣkaraṇīcaturthakaraṇīprabhṛtīnāmapi /
tathāhi--pramāṇaṃ tiryak catuṣkaraṇyāyāmastasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcakaraṇī /
tathā pramāṇaṃ tiryakpañjakaraṇyāyāmastasyākṣmayārajjuḥ ṣaṭkaraṇītyāti draṣṭavyam /
tathāhidvikaraṇī tiryaṅbhānī trikaraṇyāyāmaḥ tasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcakaraṇī /
tiryaṅbhānī daśakaraṇyāyāmastasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcadaśakaraṇītyādyapi draṣṭavyam /
tathā turīyaṃ tiryak trikaraṇyāyāmastasyākṣṇayārajjusturīyakaraṇī /
tathā pañjamaṃ tiryakcatuṣkaraṇyāyāmastasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcamakaraṇītyādi draṣṭavyam /
trikaraṇītṛtīyakaraṇyoḥsautrāmaṇyādāvupayāgeḥ /
nanu dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjurityanena trikaraṇītṛtīyakaraṇīprabhṛtayaḥ siddhāḥ /
tatkimarthaṃ trikaraṇyādikaraṇīvidhirārabhyate /
ucyate--dviprakārāḥ karaṇyaḥ, śuddhamūlā aśuddhamūlāś ca /
śuddhaṃ mūlaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥśuddhamūlāḥ /
dvābhyāṃ catvāri, tribhirnavetyādivakṣyamāṇāśvatuṣkaraṇīnavakaraṇīprabhṛtayaḥ tāsāṃ tu sarvadā dvikaraṇī trikaraṇī pañcakaraṇītyeva vyapadeśa iti pradarśayitumidamucyate, dvayoḥ karaṇī dvikaraṇī, trayāṇāṃ karaṇī trikaraṇī, caturṇāṃ karaṇī catuṣkaraṇī, pañcānāṃ karaṇī pañcakaraṇīti /
kiñca dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjurityanena sāmānyena nāñjasā trikaraṇīprabhṛtīnāmavagatirbhavati /
uktaprakāreṇa saṃpannānāṃ karaṇīnāṃ tena saṃvādamātraṃ bhavati /
tadyujyata eva dvikaraṇyādikaraṇīviśeṣavidhyārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: (The division is ninefold.) For ascertaining the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>, the following distinction [applies]: a ninefold division of the area is to be made. Of which area? Of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-area or of the <s>trikaraṇī</s>-area. The meaning is: the area whose <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> is to be determined — dividing that area into nine parts, making the <s>pārśvamānī</s> and <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> of one part of those, then making the diagonal cord of that very part into a <s>pārśvamānī</s>, when a quadrilateral is made by those two, and when the quadrilateral is divided ninefold, the <s>karaṇī</s> (constructing cord) of one part thereof is the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-area quadrilateral. And that division represents one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-area — this is the demonstration. By this, the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> (fourth-root), <s>caturthakaraṇī</s> (quarter-root), and others are also [explained]. Thus: the <s>pramāṇa</s> [as] transverse, the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> as the length — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>pañcakaraṇī</s> (five-producer). Similarly, the <s>pramāṇa</s> [as] transverse, the <s>pañcakaraṇī</s> as the length — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>ṣaṭkaraṇī</s> (six-producer), and so on. Also: the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> [as] transverse and the <s>trikaraṇī</s> as length — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>pañcakaraṇī</s>. The transverse [is] the <s>daśakaraṇī</s> (ten-producer) and the length [is the same] — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>pañcadaśakaraṇī</s> (fifteen-producer), and so on. Also: one-fourth [as] transverse, the <s>trikaraṇī</s> as length — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>turīyakaraṇī</s> (quarter-root). Similarly, one-fifth [as] transverse, the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> as length — the diagonal cord of that is the <s>pañcamakaraṇī</s> (fifth-root), and so on. The <s>trikaraṇī</s> and <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> have their application in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> sacrifice and the like. Now, [one might object that] since the <s>trikaraṇī</s>, <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>, and the rest are already established by [the rule] "the diagonal cord of an oblong [rectangle]," what is the purpose of beginning the prescription of the <s>trikaraṇī</s> and other specific <s>karaṇīs</s>? It is answered: the <s>karaṇīs</s> are of two kinds — those with rational roots (<s>śuddhamūla</s>) and those with irrational roots (<s>aśuddhamūla</s>). Those whose roots are rational are <s>śuddhamūla</s>. The forthcoming ones — "two [produces] four, three [produces] nine" etc. — namely the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s>, <s>navakaraṇī</s>, and the like — for all of those, the designation is always just <s>dvikaraṇī</s>, <s>trikaraṇī</s>, <s>pañcakaraṇī</s>. To demonstrate this, it is stated: the <s>karaṇī</s> of two is the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>, of three is the <s>trikaraṇī</s>, of four is the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s>, of five is the <s>pañcakaraṇī</s>. Moreover, from [the rule] "the diagonal cord of an oblong [rectangle]," in general terms the <s>trikaraṇī</s> and others are not directly ascertained. For the <s>karaṇīs</s> accomplished by the stated method, there is only a verification [through that rule]. Therefore, the commencement of the specific prescriptions of the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> and other <s>karaṇīs</s> is justified.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> [commentary]
Now he states the <s>trikaraṇī</s>:
(<s>Pramāṇa</s> ... <s>trikaraṇī</s>)

children.text: yathā dvādaśāṅgulā tiryaṅbhānī taddvikaraṇī tironasatpadaśāṅgulā pārśvamānī /
children.translated_text: Just as twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> [constitute] the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure), so its <s>dvikaraṇī</s> — sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and some [fraction] — is the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure).
When an oblong rectangle is thus made, its diagonal cord is twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-seven <s>tilas</s> (sesame seeds).

children.text: sā trikaraṇī pramāṇaparimitaṃ kṣetraṃ triguṇaṃ karoti //
children.translated_text: That is the <s>trikaraṇī</s>; it makes the area delimited by the <s>pramāṇa</s> threefold.
(<s>Tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> ... ninefold)

children.text: tṛtīyakaraṇyā caturaśre kṛte navadhā vibhāgaḥ kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: When a quadrilateral is made with the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>, its ninefold division should be performed.
One part thereof becomes one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s>-area.
One-third of the <s>trikaraṇī</s> is the <s>karaṇī</s> (constructing cord) of that [part].
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: tulyayoś caturaśrayor uktaḥ samāsaḥ | nānāpramāṇayoś caturaśrayoḥ samāsaḥ || ĀpŚus_2.4a ||
children.translated_text: The combination (<s>samāsa</s>) of two equal quadrilaterals has been stated. The combination of two quadrilaterals of different measures [is now given]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.4a]

children.text:
samāsa ekīkaraṇam /
caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuriti sūtreṇaspaṣṭaḥ /
nānāpramāṇayoścaturaśrayoḥsamāsa ucyata iti śeṣaḥ /
dīrghasya samasya caturaśrasya samāsa ekīkaraṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>Samāsa</s> means unification (making into one). [This] is clear from the <s>sūtra</s> "the diagonal cord of a quadrilateral." The combination of two quadrilaterals of different measures is being stated — this is the remainder. [That is:] the unification of an oblong and an even quadrilateral.

children.text: hrasīyasaḥ karaṇyā varṣīyaso vṛddhram ullikhet | vṛddhrasyākṣṇayārajjur ubhe samasyati | tad uktam || ĀpŚus_2.4b ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>karaṇī</s> (constructing cord) of the smaller [quadrilateral], one should mark out an oblong (<s>vṛddhra</s>) on the larger; the diagonal cord of the oblong combines both. This has been stated. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.4b]

children.text: hrasīyasaḥ alpīyasaḥ kṣetrasya karaṇyā pramāṇena varṣīyasaḥ varṣīyasetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Of the smaller" — of the smaller area; by the <s>karaṇī</s>, by the measure [of its side]; "of the larger" — of the larger [area], that is the meaning.

children.text:
vṛddhraṃ dīrghamullikhet /
yathālpīyasaḥ karaṇī tiryaṅbhānī varṣīyasaḥ karaṇī pārśvamānī, tathā dīrghacaturaśramullikhet /
vṛddhrasyākṣṇayārajjurubhe samasyati /
uktaṃ--dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuriti /
children.translated_text: One should mark out an oblong (<s>vṛddhra</s>), a rectangle. Just as the <s>karaṇī</s> of the smaller is the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure) and the <s>karaṇī</s> of the larger is the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure), so one should mark out an oblong rectangle. The diagonal cord of the oblong combines both. This is stated [by the rule]: "the diagonal cord of an oblong [rectangle]."
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
(Of two equal ... combination)

children.text:
tulyayoriti /
samāso nāma samasanaṃ miśraṇaṃ ekīkaraṇaṃ karaṇītulyapramāṇayoḥsamāsaḥ /
karaṇyuktā caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjurddvistāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ karoti samasyeti /
uktamanubhāṣaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇārthaṃ, idamatra pariśiṣyate, tādidaṃ vakṣyāmīti /
children.translated_text: "Of two equal" — <s>samāsa</s> means combining, mixing, making into one [of two quadrilaterals] equal in their <s>karaṇī</s>-measures. By [the rule that] the <s>karaṇī</s>-stated diagonal cord of a quadrilateral produces twice as much area, it combines — this is restated. The restatement is for the purpose of what is to be stated [next]; what remains here is: "this I shall [now] state."
(Of different ... this has been stated)

children.text:
nānāpramāṇayorbhinnapramāṇayoḥsamāsaḥ karaṇyucyate, hrasīyasaḥ alpīyasaścaturaścasya karaṇyā--karaṇīpramāṇena, barṣīyasaḥmahataścaturaśrasya, vṛddhraṃ--cihnamekadeśamullikhet vṛddhrasyākṣṇayārajjurubhe nānāpramāṇe caturaśre samasyati ekīkaroti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--nānārapramāṇe caturaśre samasya alpīyasaścaturaśrasya karaṇīpramāṇena mahadaścaturaśrasya ekasyāṃ tiryaṅbhānyāṃ paricchindyāt /
tata ārabhyordhvāṃ lekhāṃ yathā parasyāṃ tiryaṅbhānyāṃ tāvati pradeśe nipatati tathā likhet /
lekhāvibhaktasyālpīyasaḥ karaṇīpramāṇaṃ tiryaṅbhānī /
kasya? mahataḥ karaṇīpramāṇapārśvamānīkasya dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjurume nānāpramāṇe caturaśre samasyati /
caturaśra iti vartamāne punaścaturaśragrahaṇaṃ maṇḍalayorapi caturaśraṃ kṛtvaiva samāsaḥsukara iti jñāpayituṃ /
taduktaṃ--dīrghasyetyādinā /
asyopayogo vidyābhyāsādiṣu /
children.translated_text: The combination of two [quadrilaterals] of different measures, of unequal measures, is stated by the <s>karaṇī</s>. With the <s>karaṇī</s> of the smaller quadrilateral — by the measure of the <s>karaṇī</s> — on the larger quadrilateral, one should mark out an oblong (<s>vṛddhra</s>), a mark on one side. The diagonal cord of the oblong combines both — the two quadrilaterals of different measures — it makes them one. What this means is: having combined the two quadrilaterals of different measures, with the <s>karaṇī</s>-measure of the smaller quadrilateral, one should cut off [a portion] on one <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure) of the larger quadrilateral. Then, from that [cut-off point], drawing a line upward so that it falls at the corresponding position on the other <s>tiryaṅmānī</s>, one should draw [it]. The <s>karaṇī</s>-measure of the smaller becomes the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> of the [oblong] divided by the line. Of which? Of the oblong rectangle whose <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure) is the <s>karaṇī</s>-measure of the larger — the diagonal cord of that combines the two quadrilaterals of different measures. The word "quadrilateral" is repeated even though it is already [understood] in context — to indicate that when [combining] two circles also, the combination is easy only after making them into quadrilaterals. "This has been stated" — by [the rule beginning] "of an oblong." Its application is in exercises of learning and the like.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> [commentary]
(Of two equal ... combination)

children.text:
dvikaraṇyā yathā dvipuruṣe 'gnau puruṣadvikaraṇyā dvayoḥ puruṣayoḥsamāsa ityādi /
trikaraṇyā trayāṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ samāsasyāpyetadupalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: With the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>: as in the two-<s>puruṣa</s> (man-unit) fire-altar, [where] by the <s>puruṣa-dvikaraṇī</s>, there is the combination of two <s>puruṣas</s> — and so on. With the <s>trikaraṇī</s>, the combination of three <s>puruṣas</s> is also indicated by this.

children.text:
dīrghacaturaśrayostu samāse ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
tiryaṅbhānyā dvikaraṇī tiryaṅbhānī, pārśvamānyāś ca dvikaraṇī pārśvamānīti /
yathā dvistāvāyāmāśvamedhavedyāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāḥ pṛṣṭhyāyā dvikaraṇī pṛṣṭhyā /
tiryaṅbhānyostriṃśikārāntareṇa vakṣyate /
prakramasya dvikaraṇī prakamasthānīyā bhavatīti /
evaṃ dīrghacaturaśrāṇāṃ samāse tiryaṅmānyāstrikaraṇī tiryaṅmānīti /
pārśvamānyāś ca pārśvamānī /
yathā--tristāve 'gnau pakṣayoḥ puruṣamātrayāḥ tiryaṅmānyāstrikaraṇī aṣṭādhikaśatadvayāṅgulā pañcatilonā tiryaṅmānī bhavati /
pārśvamānyāś ca ṣaḍaratneḥ trikaraṇī pañcāśahdviśatāṅgulā viṃśatitilonā pārśvamānī bhavati /
pucchasya pārśvamānyā ekādaśaprādeśāyāḥ trikaraṇī aṣṭāviṃśatidviśatāṅgulā pārśvamānī /
evamanyatra /
children.translated_text: But in the combination of oblong rectangles, this is the distinction: the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> becomes the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s>, and the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>pārśvamānī</s> becomes the <s>pārśvamānī</s>. For example, in the double <s>aśvamedha-vedī</s> (horse-sacrifice altar), the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the thirty-six [unit] back becomes the back. The <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> of thirty with an interval will be stated. The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>prakrama</s> (standard step) takes the place of the <s>prakrama</s>. Similarly, in the combination of oblong rectangles, the <s>trikaraṇī</s> of the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> becomes the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s>, and the <s>pārśvamānī</s> [derived from the <s>trikaraṇī</s>] becomes the <s>pārśvamānī</s>. For example, in the triple fire-altar, the <s>trikaraṇī</s> of the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> of the wings becomes the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> — two hundred and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by five <s>tilas</s>. And the <s>trikaraṇī</s> of the six-<s>aratni</s> (cubit) <s>pārśvamānī</s> — two hundred and fifty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by twenty <s>tilas</s> — becomes the <s>pārśvamānī</s>. The <s>trikaraṇī</s> of the eleven-<s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) <s>pārśvamānī</s> of the tail — two hundred and twenty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> — becomes the <s>pārśvamānī</s>. Similarly in other cases.
(Of different [measures] ... combination)
"Is being stated" is the remainder.
(Of the smaller ... this has been stated)

children.text:
hrasīyasaḥ karaṇīṃ tiryaṅmānīṃ kṛtvā varṣīyasaḥsaṃbandhinaṃ vṛrdhaṃ dīrghacaturaśramullikhet, varṣīyasaḥ karaṇyeva pārśvamānī /
evaṃ kṛtasya dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥsamastuyoḥ karaṇī bhavati /
taduktaṃ "dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ' ityādinā /
yathā pañcavidhe 'gnau kliyamāṇe dvipuruṣeṇa caturaśre kṛte catuṣpuruṣo bhavati /
tatra puruṣamātraścaturaśraḥ prakṣeptavyaḥ /
tatra dvipuruṣakaraṇike caturaśre tadāyāmaṃ puruṣavyāsaṃ dīrghacaturaśramullikhet /
tasyākṣṇayārajjuraṣṭaṣaṣṭiśatāṅgulā saikādaśatilā, sā pañcavidhāgneḥ karaṇī bhavati /
children.translated_text: Making the <s>karaṇī</s> of the smaller into the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> and the <s>karaṇī</s> of the larger as the associated element, one should mark out an oblong rectangle; the <s>karaṇī</s> of the larger itself is the <s>pārśvamānī</s>. The diagonal cord of the oblong rectangle thus made becomes the <s>karaṇī</s> of both [combined]. This has been stated by [the rule beginning] "of an oblong" etc. For example, in the five-fold fire-altar being constructed, when a quadrilateral is made with a two-<s>puruṣa</s> [measure], it becomes four <s>puruṣas</s> [in area]. There, a quadrilateral of one <s>puruṣa</s> is to be added. In the quadrilateral whose <s>karaṇī</s> is the two-<s>puruṣa</s>, one should mark out an oblong rectangle whose length is that [two-<s>puruṣa</s> <s>karaṇī</s>] and whose breadth is one <s>puruṣa</s>. Its diagonal cord — one hundred and sixty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> with eleven <s>tilas</s> — that becomes the <s>karaṇī</s> of the five-fold fire-altar.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: caturaśrāc caturaśraṃ nirjihīrṣan yāvan nirjihīrṣet tasya karaṇyā varṣīyaso vṛddhramullikhet || ĀpŚus_2.5a ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to subtract a quadrilateral from a [larger] quadrilateral — however much one wishes to subtract, with the <s>karaṇī</s> of that, one should mark out an oblong on the larger. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.5a]
Wishing to subtract a square from a former square, one should mark out a rectangle (<s>vṛdhra</s>) with the measure of the [smaller] square.

children.text: vṛrdhasya pārśvamānīm akṣṇayetarat pārśvam upasaṃharet || ĀpŚus_2.5b ||
children.translated_text: One should bring the lateral measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) of the rectangle diagonally to the other side. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.5b ||
One should join [them].

children.text: sā yatra nipatet tad apacchindyāt || ĀpŚus_2.5c ||
children.translated_text: Where it falls, one should cut off [the excess]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.5c ||

children.text: sā pārśvamānī itarasmin pārśva yatra nipatati spṛśati tatrāpacchindyāt /
children.translated_text: That lateral measure, where it falls on -- touches -- the other side, there one should cut off.
By [the portion] cut off, the [area to be] removed is removed. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.5d ||
By means of the cut-off [portion], when the removal is made, that becomes removed.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(Removal from a square by cutting)

children.text:
caturaśrāditi /
idamapi karaṇīvidhānameva /
mahataścaturaśrādalpaṃ caturaśraṃ nirjihīrṣan vihartumicchan yāvat pramāṇaṃ caturaśramapanetumicchati tasyālpasya saraṇyā māhataścaturaśrasyaikadeśaṃ yathā chinnaṃ bhavati tathollikhet /
evaṃ kṛte chinnaṃ nirasi tavyakṣetrapramāṇatiryaṅbhānīkaṃ mahatkṣetrapārśvamānīkaṃ pramāṇapārśva mānīkaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ bhavati /
asya kṣetrasya pārśvamānīmakṣṇayetarat pārśvamupasaṃharet--gamayet, sā pārśvamānīmakṣṇayetaratā yatretarasyāḥ pārśvamānyāḥ pradeśe nipatati tadapachindyāt--pārśvamānīmapācchityādhikaṃ tyajet, chinnayā nirastaṃ--chinnaṃ pārśvamānīnirasitavyakṣetrasya karaṇī bhavati /
tayā pārśvamānyā caturaśre kṛte nirasitavyakṣetraṃ nirastaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From a square' -- this too is a procedure involving the <s>karaṇī</s> (producer/square root). Wishing to subtract a small square from a large square -- wishing to construct [the difference] -- one should mark out a portion of the large square such that it is cut by the side of the small [square] that one wishes to remove. When this is done, the cut [portion] forms a rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>) whose transverse measure equals the side of the area to be removed and whose lateral measure equals the side of the large area. The lateral measure of this rectangle should be brought diagonally to the other side -- made to reach [it]. Where the lateral measure brought diagonally falls on the other side, there one should cut -- cutting off the lateral measure and discarding the excess. By [the portion] cut off, the removal is accomplished -- the cut [portion] becomes the <s>karaṇī</s> (square root / producer) of the area to be removed. When a square is made with that lateral measure, the area to be removed is removed -- this is the meaning.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
Removal from a square by cutting.

children.text:
nirhāro--nirasanam /
yathā nividhe 'gnau kriyamāṇe dvipuruṣeṇa caturaśre kṛte catuṣpuruṣo bhavati /
tatraikapuruṣatyāgārthaṃ puruṣamātratiryaṅbhānyā vṛdhramullikhya tasyottarāṃ pārśvamānīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ prācīmitaratpārśvaṃ gamayet /
sā ca tatra dvipuruṣapramāṇāyāṃ catvāriṃśacchatadvayāṅgulapramāṇāyāṃ pañcatilāśvāpacchindyāt /
pariśi ṣṭayā karaṇyā caturaśre kṛte puruṣo nirasto bhavati /
children.translated_text: <s>Nirhāra</s> means removal. For example, when a <s>nivīdha</s> fire[-altar] is being made, a square made with two <s>puruṣas</s> (man-lengths) gives four <s>puruṣas</s> [of area]. To remove one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area] from that, having marked out a rectangle with a transverse measure of one <s>puruṣa</s>, one should bring its northern lateral measure diagonally to the southern eastern side. And where it falls there, in the measure of two <s>puruṣas</s>, [which is] two hundred and forty <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s>, one should cut off. With the remaining <s>karaṇī</s> (producer), when a square is made, one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area] is removed.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):
As he himself demonstrates:

children.text: upasaṃhṛtākṣaṇayārajjuḥ sā catuṣkaraṇī chinnā cetarā ca yat pṛthagbhūte kurutas tad ubhayaṃ karoti || ĀpŚus_2.6a ||
children.translated_text: The diagonal cord brought together -- that is the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> (producer of four [puruṣas]); the cut-off [portion] and the other -- what they separately produce, [the diagonal] produces both combined. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.6a ||
The [cord] brought together is the former lateral measure.

children.text: idānīmakṣṇayārajjuś ca raśrasyasā catuṣkaraṇī dvipuruṣāt chinnā pārśvamānī itarātiryahbhānī yatpṛthagbhūte kurutaḥ tadubhayaṃ karoti //
children.translated_text: Now as the diagonal cord, that is the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> (producer of four [puruṣas of area]); cut from the two-<s>puruṣa</s> [square], the lateral measure and the other -- the transverse measure -- what they separately produce, [the diagonal] produces both combined.
He states how:
The transverse measure [produces] one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area]; the remainder, three. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.6c ||
The transverse measure produces one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area].
The remainder, that is, the diagonal cord, [produces] two.
Both together -- its diagonal cord thus produces three.
That has been stated. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.6d ||
And that too has been stated.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
Intending to make this method clear by means of an example, he says:

children.text:
urasaṃhatā taduktam upeti /
sarvato dvipuruṣapramāṇaṃ catuṣpuruṣaṃ caturaśraṃ viṣayīkṛ tyodāharati /
ekasya caturaśrasyāvayavabhūte dīrghacaturaśre yā pārśvamānyakṣṇayopasaṃhṛtā sā catuṣkaraṇī catuṣkaraṇī catuṣpuruṣakaraṇīti pratijñātā /
asya tiryaṅbhānī ca puruṣamātrakaraṇīti /
asya dīrghacaturaśrasya chinnā pārśvamānī kiyatkaraṇīti na jñātā, saivātrāvagantavyā /
atra puruṣapramāṇaṃ tiryaṅbhānyā pṛthagbhūtayā yatkriyate chinnayā pārśvamānyā pṛthagbhūtayā yatkriyate akṣṇayārajjuḥ tadubhayakṣetrakaraṇīti nyāyato 'vagatā /
tatrākṣṇayārajjuphalabhūtāccatuṣpuruṣāccaturaśrādekapramāṇaṃ tiryaṅbhānīphale tvekasminnapanīte trayaḥ puruṣāḥ pariśeṣyāt sā tripuruṣakaraṇītyavagantavyā /
ata idamuktaṃ tiryaṅbhānī puruṣaṃ karoti śeṣaḥ chinnā pārśvamānī /
trīn puruṣān iti pulliṅganirdeśaḥ puruṣabhiprāyaḥ /
puruṣanirdeśaśvāgnau puruṣeṇa vimānaṃ puruṣābhyāsāpacayau samāsanirhārayoḥ udāharaṇamiti /
ayamarthaḥ--sarvato dvipramāṇāccatuṣpuruṣāccaturaśrādekaṃ puruṣamapanīya tripuruṣaṃ samacaturaśraṃ kartumicchan taccaturaśraṃ puruṣapramāṇayā rajjvā madhye paricchidya dvidhā kṛtvā tadarghasyaikāṃ pārśvamānīmaparāṃ pārśvamānīṃ pratyakṣṇayopagamayitvā tayoryatra saṃpātaḥ tatrāvasthitāṃ pārśvamānīṃ chicvāvaśiṣṭaṃ nirasya śiṣṭayā pārśvamānyā samacaturaśre kṛte taccaturaśraṃ tripuruṣacaturaśraṃ bhavati /
tathā sarvataśvatuṣpuruṣāccaturaśrāccaturaḥ puruṣānapanīya dvādaśapuruṣaṃ samacaturaśraṃ kartumicchaddvipuruṣapramāṇayā tiryaṅbhānyā samacaturaśraṃ vibhajyārdhasyaikāṃ pārśvamānīmanyāṃ prati gamayitvā tayoḥsannipāte 'vasthitāṃ pārśvamānīmavacchidya chedaṃ nirasya śiṣṭayā pārśvamānyā caturaśre kṛte tat kṣetraṃ dvādaśapuruṣasamacaturaśraṃ bhavati /
chinnaśiṣṭā pārśvamānī tatkaraṇī bhavatītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ pramāṇakṣetre tṛtīyadvikaraṇīmapanīya tṛtīyakaraṇī bhavati /
evameva sarvatra catuṣkaraṇīcaturthakaraṇīprabhṛtayaḥ karaṇyo 'vagantavyāḥ /
taduktaṃ "dīrghasyākṣmayārajjurityanena /
asyopayogo droṇādiṣu, sundararājīyā vyākhyā
children.translated_text: Having brought together -- that stated -- it follows. Taking as subject matter a square of four <s>puruṣas</s>, with a measure of two <s>puruṣas</s> on all sides, he gives the example. In the rectangle that is a component of one square, the lateral measure brought together diagonally is declared to be the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> (producer of four <s>puruṣas</s>). Its transverse measure is the <s>karaṇī</s> of one <s>puruṣa</s>. Of the cut lateral measure of this rectangle -- how much it produces is not known; that very thing is to be understood here. Here, by the transverse measure of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure, what is separately produced, and by the cut lateral measure separately -- the diagonal cord is the <s>karaṇī</s> of the area [equal to] both: this is understood by the principle. From the four-<s>puruṣa</s> square [area] produced by the diagonal cord, when one measure -- the product of the transverse measure -- namely one, is subtracted, three <s>puruṣas</s> remain by the remainder [principle]; thus it is to be understood as the <s>tripuruṣakaraṇī</s> (producer of three <s>puruṣas</s>). Therefore it is stated: 'The transverse measure produces one <s>puruṣa</s>; the remainder is the cut lateral measure; three <s>puruṣas</s>' -- the masculine usage refers to <s>puruṣas</s>. The use of '<s>puruṣa</s>' measurement is [relevant] in the fire[-altar], measuring by <s>puruṣa</s>, the addition and subtraction by <s>puruṣa</s> [units] being examples in combination and removal. This is the meaning: wishing to make a three-<s>puruṣa</s> square from a four-<s>puruṣa</s> square with two [<s>puruṣas</s>] on all sides, by removing one <s>puruṣa</s>, dividing that square in the middle with a cord of one-<s>puruṣa</s> measure, making it in two, bringing one lateral measure of one half diagonally to the other lateral measure, cutting the lateral measure at their intersection and discarding the remainder, when a square is made with the remaining lateral measure, that square becomes a three-<s>puruṣa</s> square. Similarly, wishing to make a twelve-<s>puruṣa</s> square from a four-<s>puruṣa</s> square [of area] with four [<s>puruṣas</s>] on all sides by removing four <s>puruṣas</s>, dividing the square with a two-<s>puruṣa</s> transverse measure, bringing one lateral measure of the half toward the other, cutting the lateral measure at their intersection, discarding the cut-off [portion], when a square is made with the remaining lateral measure, that area becomes a twelve-<s>puruṣa</s> square. The remaining lateral measure after cutting becomes its <s>karaṇī</s> -- this is the meaning. Thus from the area-measure, subtracting the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the third, it becomes the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> (producer of the third). In the same way everywhere, the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s>, <s>caturthakaraṇī</s> (producer of the fourth), and other producers are to be understood. That is stated by 'the diagonal cord of the rectangle.' Its application is in the <s>droṇa</s> (trough-shaped altar) and others.
He illustrates that very thing:
Brought together -- that stated.

children.text:
yā akṣṇayopasaṃhṛtā-ekībhūtā rajjuḥsā catuṣkaraṇī dvipuruṣāpacchinnā pārśvamānī apacchinnā pañcatilonāṣṭaśatadvayāṅgulā /
itarā--puruṣamātrī tiryaṅbhānī ca yatpṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṃ karati karṇarajjutvāt /
tatra tiryaṅbhānī spaṣṭameva hi puruṣamātraṃ karoti /
pāriśeṣyātpārśvamānī trīn puruṣān karotīti jñātuṃ śakyate /
taduktaṃ "dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ' ityādinā /
children.translated_text: The cord brought together -- made one -- diagonally, that is the <s>catuṣkaraṇī</s> (producer of four); the lateral measure cut from the two-<s>puruṣa</s> [side], the cut-off [portion], is two hundred and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> less five <s>tilas</s>. The other -- the one-<s>puruṣa</s> transverse measure -- and what they separately produce, [the diagonal] produces both, being the hypotenuse cord. The transverse measure clearly produces one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area]. By the remainder principle, it can be known that the lateral measure produces three <s>puruṣas</s>. That is stated by 'the diagonal cord of the rectangle' and so on.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: dīrghacaturaśraṃ samacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣan tiryaṅmānyāpacchidya śeṣaṃ vibhajyobhayata upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_2.7a ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to make a rectangle into a square, one should cut off [a portion] by the transverse measure, divide the remainder, and place [the pieces] on both sides. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.7a ||

children.text: dīrghacaturaśraṃ samacaturaśraṃ kartumicchan tiryaṅbhanyā tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇenāpacchidya śeṣaṃ vibhajya--dvidhā kṛtvā tadubhayataḥ agrataḥ pārśvataśropadadhyāt--nikṣipet /
children.translated_text: Wishing to make a rectangle into a square, cutting off by the transverse measure -- by the measure of the transverse side, dividing the remainder -- making it in two -- one should place it on both sides, in front and on the side.
The gap (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) should be filled with the additional [piece]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.7b ||
The gap should be filled with the additional excess [piece]. Having filled it, the excess additional [piece] should be discarded.
The removal of that has been stated. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 2.7c ||
The method of discarding that has been stated.
Thus ends the second section.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
Rectangle -- removal has been stated.

children.text:
dīrghoti--sarvatastulyapramāṇaṃ samacaturaśraṃ ekata āyāmato 'dhikaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ samacaturaśraṃ kurvan tiryaṅbhānyā tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇayā rajjvā parimite pradeśe madhye dakṣiṇottaramapa cchidya śeṣaṃ purvabhāgaṃ madhye diryak dvidhā vibhajya tayoḥ paścimaṃ bhāgaṃ tathaivāvasthāpya pūrvabhāgaṃ prathamasyottarataḥ prācīnamupadadhyāt /
uttarapūrvabhāgaṃ śūnyabhūtaṃ khaṇḍamāgantunā saṃpūrya samacaturaśraṃ saṃpādya adhikamāgantubhūtaṃ khaṇḍaṃ tato nirharet--nirgamayet /
tasya nirhāra uktaḥ "caturaśrāccaturaśraṃ nirjhihīrṣan' iti /
tasyopayogo rathacaktrādiṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Rectangle' -- a [figure with] equal measure on all [four] sides is a square (<s>sama-caturaśra</s>); one that is extended on one side in length is a rectangle (<s>dīrgha-caturaśra</s>). Making a rectangle into a square: cutting with a cord of the transverse measure's dimension at the middle [of the rectangle] in the north-south direction; dividing the remaining front portion in the middle transversely into two parts; keeping the western part as it is; and placing the eastern part north of the first [part] in the eastward direction. The empty gap in the north-eastern corner should be filled with the additional [piece] to complete the square, and the excess additional gap should be removed from it. 'The removal of that has been stated' by 'wishing to subtract a square from a square.' Its application is in the chariot-wheel [altar] and others.
Thus ends the second section.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
Rectangle -- removal has been stated.

children.text: tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇena pārśvamānīmapacchidya samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā śeṣaṃ vibhajya purastāduttarataśvopadadhayāt, yathottarapūrvakoṇe samacaturaśraṃ āgantuḥ khaṇḍo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Having cut off by the measure of the transverse side from the lateral measure and made a square, one should divide the remainder and place [the pieces] in front and to the north, so that in the north-eastern corner there will be a square [gap] -- the additional piece.
The removal of that has been stated by 'from a square, a square' and so on.
Thus ends the second section.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ cukīrṣanā yāvaccikīrṣet tāvatīṃ pārśvamānīṃ kṛtvā yadadhikaṃ syād yathāyogam upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to make a square into a rectangle, having made the lateral measure as long as one desires, whatever is excess should be placed as appropriate. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.1 ||

children.text:
samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ kartumicchan yāvatā dīrghabhūtena prayojanaṃ tāvatpārśvamālikhya yadadhikakṣetraṃ tadyathāyogaṃ yathā tatkṣetraṃ cujyate tathā kṣipet /
caturaśraṃ vibhajya ubhayataḥprauge viniyogaḥ, avakīrṇipaśau ca /
children.translated_text: Wishing to make a square into a rectangle, having marked the lateral [measure] as long as the purpose requires for the elongated [shape], whatever excess area [there is] should be added as appropriate -- in such a way that the area is consumed. Dividing the square and [placing it] on both sides is the application for the <s>prauga</s> (chariot-shaped altar), and also for the <s>avakīrṇi-paśu</s> (scattered-animal sacrifice).
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:

children.text: samacaturaśraṃ dvidhā kṛtvā tasyaikasmin bhāge bhāgāntarasyoparyupari nihite dīrghacaturaśraṃ bhavatīti manvānastasya prakāramāha--
children.translated_text: Considering that when a square is divided in two and one part is placed on top of the other, a rectangle is formed, he states the method:

children.text:
samacatuhaśraṃaupadadhyāt sameti /
tiryaṅbhānyā apacchidya śeṣaṃ vibhajedityeva /
samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ kardumicchan samacaturaśraṃ tribhāgādvibhāgārdhādīnāmanyatamenaikāṃśena parimitatiryakpramāṇaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṅkartumicchati tāvatyā tiryaṅbhānyā samacaturaśramekato 'pacchidya śeṣasya samacaturaśrakaraṇīsamāṃ pārśvamānīṃ tāvatīmuktayā tiryaṅbhānyā samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tatra śeṣaṃ vibhajya yadadhikaṃ syāttadyathāyogamupadadhyāt /
adhikasya yathā vibhāge kṛte vibhāgā ekaikaśo vā sarvāḥ saṃhasya vā bhāgāntarasyopari nidhīyamānāstadvistāraṃ vyāpyānyonyasaṃghaṭitāstaddīrghaṃ saṃpādayanti tathā vibhajya sarvaṃ śeṣaṃ bhāgāntarasyopari nidadhyāditi /
ayamarthaḥ--samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣan ktriyamāṇasya cikīrṣitavistārapramāṇayā tiryaṅbhānyā samacaturaśramekato 'vacchidya śiṣṭasya ca pārśvamānīṃ tāvatīṃ kṛtvā tadadhimekayānekayā vā vibhajya tesarve bhāgā dīrghacaturaśraṃ yathā saṃpādayanti tathā sarvaśeṣaṃ bhāgāntarasyoparyupari nidadhyāditi /
atrādhikṛte śeṣaśabde karmavācinyapi sannidheḥsāmarthyācca tasya ṣaṣṭhyartho 'pipratīyate /
tāvatīmityādiśabdasya śeṣasaṃbandhitve sāmañjasyādyāvaccikīrṣedityapi dīrghavistāraviṣayaḥsyāt /
eka eva nyā yo dīrghasyāpi dīrghavīdhāvavagantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Square... should place' -- 'equally' and so on. The [rest is] just: 'cutting off by the transverse measure, one should divide the remainder.' Wishing to make a square into a rectangle: wishing to make a rectangle with a transverse dimension equal to one part -- whether a third, half of a division, or other fraction -- of the square, cutting the square on one side by that much transverse measure, making the lateral measure of the remainder equal to the <s>karaṇī</s> (side) of the square, making a square with the stated transverse measure, then dividing the remainder and placing whatever is excess as appropriate. The excess should be divided such that the divisions, placed one by one or all combined on top of the other portion, spanning its width and joined together, accomplish that length. Thus, dividing all the remainder, one should place it on top of the other portion. This is the meaning: wishing to make a square into a rectangle, cutting the square on one side with the transverse measure equal to the desired width of the rectangle to be made, and making the lateral measure of the remaining [part] that much, dividing that excess by one or many [cuts], all those parts should be placed on top of the other portion such that they accomplish the rectangle. Here, with the word 'remainder' (<s>śeṣa</s>) being in the objective case, by context and capacity, the genitive meaning is also understood. With the word 'that much' and others being connected to the remainder, 'as long as one desires' would also pertain to the length and width of the rectangle. The very same principle is to be understood also in making a rectangle into [another] rectangle.
Here are verses [summarizing]:
Having divided a square into two, [placing] one portion on top of the other,
when the other portion is placed, that becomes a rectangle.
With a side-measure equal to the width of the rectangle to be made,
dividing and [placing] the excess remainder -- that is the proper procedure.
And of the remainder, the lateral measure [should be] that much, from a fitting division;
of the rectangle to be made, the transverse [measure should be] as much as desired.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]:
(Square -- should place)

children.text: ayamatra prakāraḥ-- yāvadicchaṃ pārśvamānyā prācyau vardhayitvā uttarapūrvāṃ karṇarajjumāyacchet, sā dīrghacaturaśramadhyasthāyāṃ samacaturaśratiryaṅbhānyāṃ yatra nipatati tata uttaraṃ hitvā dakṣiṇāṃśaṃ tiryaṅbhānīṃ kuryāt, taddīrghacaturaśraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The method here is: having extended the two east-west lines (<s>prācīs</s>) by the lateral measure as much as desired, one should stretch the northeast diagonal cord; where it falls on the transverse measure of the square [inscribed] within the rectangle, from that point, discarding the northern portion, one should make the southern portion the transverse measure — that becomes the rectangle.
The same method applies also for the elongation of the oblong [into a longer oblong].
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)

children.text: caturaśraṃ maṇḍalaṃ cikīrṣan madhyāt koṭyāṃ nipātayet || ĀpŚus_3.2a ||
children.translated_text: One who wishes to make a square into a circle should let [the cord] fall from the center to the corner. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.2a ||

children.text:
yaccaturaśraṃ maṇḍalaṃ kartumicchet /
rathacaktracidādau viniyogaḥ /
madhyātkoṭ- cāṃ nipātayet--madhyame śaṅkau pāśaṃ pratimucya koṭyāmāyacchet karṇenā'yacchet /
apasārya tatra lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā--
children.translated_text: One who wishes to make a square into a circle — the application is in the chariot-wheel fire-altar (<s>rathacakracit</s>) and the like. 'From the center to the corner one should let fall' — fixing the loop on the central peg, one should stretch [the cord] to the corner — stretch by means of the diagonal. Drawing it aside, making a mark there —

children.text: pārśvataḥ parikṛṣyātiśayatṛtīyena saha maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet || ĀpŚus_3.2b ||
children.translated_text: Drawing it along the side, together with a third of the excess, one should draw the circle. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.2b ||

children.text:
tenaiva lakṣaṇena pārśvataḥ ākarṣet /
parikṛṣṭaṃ yāvacca turaśramatītya śete so 'tiśayaḥ /
tasyātiśayasya tṛtīyena saha caturaśrārghena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet--sarvato likhet /
children.translated_text: With that very mark, one should draw along the side. What has been drawn beyond the square — that is the excess. With a third of that excess, together with the half-[side] of the square, one should draw the circle — draw it all around.
That [cord] is a permanent [approximation for] the circle. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.2c ||
That permanent [cord] makes the circle.
The inexact one is approximate.
Whatever is lacking [in the corners], that much is added [on the sides]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.2d ||

children.text:
straktiṣu yāvaddhīyate tāvatpārśve na gacchati /
etacca vacanamāsannataratvakhyāpanārtham /
children.translated_text: Whatever is lacking in the [corner] portions, that much does not extend to the sides. And this statement is for the purpose of indicating the nearness [of the approximation].
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary
(On 'a square into a circle... that much is added')

children.text:
samacaturaśraṃ maṇḍalaṃ cikīrṣana kartumicchan tasya caturaśrasyākṣṇayārajvarghapramāṇāt kiñcidadhikāmekataḥpāśāṃ rajjuṃ mītvā tatpāśaṃ caturaśrasya madhyame śakṅau pratimucya tāmakṣṇayākoṭyāṃ nipātya tatra lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pārśvapradeśādatiriktalakṣaṇayorantarālaṃ tredhā vibhajya antato dvau bhāgāvutsṛjya bhāgenaikena sahitāyāṃ caturaśrārddhapramāṇayā rajjvā yathā bhūmimaṇḍalaṃ bhavati tathā paritaḥsarvato likhet /
evaṃ kṛte sā nityā maṇḍalaṃ--caturaśrakṣetratilyakṣetraṃ bhavati /
sā nityā--sā bhūmirnityā, yāvat caturaśre bhūmiḥ maṇḍale 'pi sā bhavatī tyarthaḥ /
tatra hetumāha--yāvaddhīyate tāvadāgantu--yāvatpramāṇaṃ kṣetraṃ hīyate hīyamānatayā (iti) ṭṛśyeta caturaśabhaktiṣu tāvanmaṇḍalasya pārśveṣvāgantu ṭṛśyate, tasmānnityeti /
nanu viṣkambhārdhena pariṇāhārdhamabhyasya phalāvagatirityanena nyāyena bhūmeḥ nātyantatulyatā, tatkathaṃ nityeti? ucyate--yadyapyanityā, tathāpyanyeṣāmupāyāntarāṇāmatisthūlatvādasya copāyasyāsannatvāt samyagupāyasya vahuprayatnasādhyatvena aśakyatvāccaivaṃ vadata ācāryasyāyamevopāyaḥsādhurityabhiprāyaḥ /
yāvadiha hīyate tāvadāgantu iti
children.translated_text: One wishing to make a square into a circle — wishing to make [it] — having measured a cord with a loop at one end, slightly longer than the half-diagonal measure of that square, fixing its loop on the central peg of the square, letting it fall diagonally to the corner, making a mark there, then drawing it to the side-region, dividing the interval between the excess-mark [and the side] into three, discarding the outer two parts, with a cord of half-square measure combined with one part, one should draw a circle all around so as to form a ground-circle. When this is done, 'that is a permanent circle' — the area of the square becomes the area of the circle. 'That is permanent' — that ground is permanent, meaning that whatever area is in the square, the same is in the circle. There he states the reason: 'whatever is lacking, that much is added' — whatever amount of area appears to be lacking in the portions of the square, that much is seen added on the sides of the circle; therefore it is permanent. But by the principle 'the area [of a circle] is obtained by multiplying half the circumference by half the diameter,' there is no absolute equality; then how can it be called 'permanent'? It is said: although it is inexact, nevertheless because other alternative methods are too crude, because this method is near [to the true value], and because an exact method would require too much effort and is thus impractical, the <s>ācārya</s> (master) speaking thus intends that this method alone is adequate.

children.text:
tayoralpavaiṣamyāttāvadeveti /
pravṛttirocanārthamanityāpi nityetyuktetyadoṣaḥ /
athavā yā rajjurmaṇḍalaṃ karoti sā rajjuriti rajjvabhiprāyo 'pi tacchabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the small discrepancy between the two, it is indeed just that much. There is no fault in calling the inexact 'permanent' for the purpose of encouraging practice. Alternatively, 'that' (<s>sā</s>) refers to 'that cord' which makes the circle — thus the word '<s>tat</s>' has the meaning of cord.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
(On 'a square into a circle... that much is added')

children.text: caturaśramadhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin rajjuṃ pratimucya koṭyāmakṣṇayāṃ nipātya cihnaṃ kṛtvā pārśve kṛtvā pārśva ca parikṛṣya tasmin cihnaṃ kṛtvā cuhnayorantarālaṃ tredhā kṛtvā ekabhāgasahitena caturaśrārghena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhetsā rajjuranityā maṇḍalaṃ karoti yāvaddhīyate koṭiṣu tāvatpramāṇaṃ pārśvaṣvāgacchati //
children.translated_text: Having fixed a peg at the center of the square and attaching a cord to it, letting it fall diagonally to the corner, making a mark, then drawing it to the side, making a mark on the side, dividing the interval between the marks into three, with a half-square [measure] combined with one part, one should draw a circle. That cord, though inexact, makes the circle. Whatever is lacking at the corners, that much area comes to the sides.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ caturaśraṃ cikīrṣan viṣkambhaṃ pañcadaśa bhāgān kṛtvā dvāv uddharet | trayodaśāvaśiṣyante | sā nityā caturaśram || ĀpŚus_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: One wishing to make a circle into a square: having divided the diameter into fifteen parts, one should remove two. Thirteen remain. That is the permanent [approximation for] the square. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.3 ||

children.text:
maṇḍalaṃ caturaśraṃ kartumicchan maṇḍalasya viṣkabhyaṃ vyāsaṃ pañcadaśadhā vibhajya dvau bhāgau tyajet /
trayodaśabhāgāḥśiṣyante /
taistrayodaśabhirmitā rajjuḥ tāvatkṣetraṃ caturaśraṃ karoti /
sā cānityā sthūlatarā /
trayodaśāvaśiṣyanta iti vacanaṃ śulbāntaroktādapi mānasaṃ varamiti khyāpanārtham /
tīvrasutasome viniyogaḥ /
tatra prācyekādaśini mātavyā /
tatrāṅgulena prādeśamātraṃ vedikhaṇḍamupādātavyam /
yadi dvādaśāṅgulā uparavāḥ ardhaprādeśāṅkordakṣiṇataḥṣaḍaṅgule śaṅkuṃ nihatya tāvadvayāsa catustriṃśatprakramāyāmā prācī vedirmantavyā /
daśānāṃ kṣetram /
sūtrakāropadeśena pañcaśatāni catvāriṃśadadhikāni aṅgulakṣetrāṇi /
tadardhāṅgulaṃ gṛhyate /
tena vedicchedor'dhamāneṣu /
pūrvārdhānāṃ vedisaṃskāro na kriyate /
atiriktakṣetraṃ nirastaṃ bhavati /
vedeśrvāvaṭeṣu vicchittirbhavati--
children.translated_text: One wishing to make a circle into a square: having divided the diameter (breadth) of the circle into fifteen [parts], one should discard two parts. Thirteen parts remain. A cord measured by those thirteen [parts] makes a square of that extent of area. And that too is inexact — rather approximate. The statement 'thirteen remain' is to indicate that this measure is preferable to [the method] stated in other <s>Śulba</s> [texts]. The application is in the <s>tīvrasutasoma</s> ritual. There, the east-west line is to be measured at eleven [units]. There, a <s>vedī</s> (altar-portion) of one <s>prādeśa</s> (span) measure should be taken per <s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth). If the <s>uparavas</s> (bricks) are of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, fixing a peg six <s>aṅgulas</s> to the south of the half-span marking, the east-west altar should be taken as having that diameter and a length of thirty-four <s>prakramas</s> (paces). [This gives] an area of ten [square units]. By the instruction of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the aphorisms), five hundred and forty <s>aṅgula</s>-areas. Half an <s>aṅgula</s> is taken. By that, the altar-cut [is made] at half-measures. The altar-preparation of the front halves is not done. The excess area is discarded. In the altar-trenches, there is division —
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary
(On 'wishing to make a circle into a square... the square')

children.text:
maṇḍalasya vistārapramāṇaṃ viṣkambhaḥ /
tatpañcadaśadhā vibhajya dvau bhāgāvapanayet /
śiṣṭāstrayodaśa bhāgāścaturaśrasya karaṇī bhavati /
atrāpi sā nityetyādi samānaṃ /
tāveva codyaparihārau /
children.translated_text: The extent of the width of the circle is the <s>viṣkambha</s> (diameter). Having divided that into fifteen parts and removing two parts, the remaining thirteen parts become the <s>karaṇī</s> (constructive measure) of the square. Here too, 'that is permanent' and so on — the same [reasoning applies]. The objections and their refutations are also the same.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
(On 'wishing to make a circle into a square... the square')

children.text:
trayodaśa bhāgāḥ karaṇī caturaśrasya anityā caturaśraṃ karoti /
anayoranityatvaṃ vijñāyate gaṇitavirodhātparasparavirodhācca /
tathāhi--saptavidhasya sāratniprādeśasya rathacakracitāvagneḥ kṣetraṃ lakṣamaṣṭau ca sahasrāṇyaṅgulayaḥ, tasya caturaśrīkṛtasya karaṇī trīṇi śatānyaṣṭāviṃśatiśrvāṅgulayor'dhadvāviṃśāśrva tilāḥ /
tasminnuktena margeṇa maṇḍale kṛte trīṇi śatāni catuḥsaptatiśrvāṅgulayo viṣkambho bhavati /
tasya pariṇāhaḥsahasraṃ pañcasaptatiśatāṅgulayaḥ /
yathā'huḥ--
children.translated_text: Thirteen parts are the constructive measure of the square — [but it is] inexact; it makes a [merely approximate] square. The inexactness of both [procedures] is known from the contradiction with calculation and from mutual contradiction. Thus: of the chariot-wheel fire-altar (<s>rathacakracit</s>) of [<s>Agni</s>], [the area being] seven and a half <s>aratnis</s> with a <s>prādeśa</s>, the area is one <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000) and eight thousand <s>aṅgulas</s>. Its <s>karaṇī</s> (constructive measure) when made into a square is three hundred and twenty-eight and a half <s>aṅgulas</s>, twenty-two and a half <s>tilās</s>. When a circle is made from that by the stated method, the diameter becomes three hundred and seventy-four <s>aṅgulas</s>. Its circumference is one thousand and seventy-five hundred <s>aṅgulas</s>. As they say:
One hundred increased by four, multiplied by eight, and sixty-two thousand —
this is approximately the circumference of a circle of diameter twenty thousand.

children.text:
iti /
asya maṇḍalasya phalaṃ lakṣaṃ navasahasramaṣṭau śatāni ṣaṣṭiśvāṅgulayo ṭṛśyante uktaṃ ca --
children.translated_text: The area of this circle is seen to be one <s>lakṣa</s>, nine thousand, eight hundred and sixty <s>aṅgulas</s>. And it has been said:
Half of the equal circumference, multiplied by half the diameter, is indeed the area of the circle.

children.text:
iti /
evamagnikṣetre rathacakracidādau maṇḍale kṛte ṣaṣṭyadhikāni aṣṭaśatāni sahasraṃ cāṅgulayo 'tiricyante /
tathā ca parasparavirodhaḥ /
ardhadvāviṃśatitilasahitāṣṭāviṃśatiśatatrayāṅgulakaraṇīkasyāgnermaṇḍalīkṛtasya viṣkambhaḥ catuḥsaptatiśatatrayāṅgula uktaḥ /
tasyaiva maṇḍalasyoktena mārgeṇa caturaśrīkaraṇe trīṇi bhavatīti pūrvoktāyāḥ karaṇyāḥsāṣṭādaśatilāścatasro 'ṅgulayo hīyante /
tasmātsūkṣmamicchatā caturaśrasya maṇḍalakaraṇe sūtroktādatiśayatṛtīyabhāgasahitādviṣkambhārdhādaṣṭādaśaśatāṃśastyājyaḥ /
evaṃ kṛte rathacakracitau biṣkambhaḥ ṣaṭratilonaikasaptatiśatatrayāṅgulo bhavati /
pariṇāhaś ca pañcaṣaṣṭiśatasahasrāṅgulayaḥ /
tasya maṇḍalasya samapariṇāhasyetyādinā pūrvoktena ānītaṃ phalaṃ lakṣamaṣṭau sahasrāṇi bhavanti /
maṇḍalasyāpi caturaśrakaraṇe sūtrokte viṣkambhe svasmāt triguṇāt trayastriṃśacchatāṃśaṃ yuñjyāt /
tatra ślokāḥ--
children.translated_text: Thus, when a circle is made in the fire-altar area for the chariot-wheel fire-altar and the like, one thousand eight hundred and sixty <s>aṅgulas</s> are in excess. And thus there is mutual contradiction. [When] the <s>karaṇī</s> of the fire-altar of three hundred and twenty-eight and three-hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-two and a half <s>tilās</s> is made into a circle, the stated diameter is three hundred and seventy-four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
