When that same circle is made into a square by the stated method, the <s>karaṇī</s> [should return] three — but four <s>aṅgulas</s> and eighteen <s>tilās</s> are lost from the previously stated <s>karaṇī</s>. Therefore, one desiring precision should, in making a square into a circle, discard an eighteenth-hundredth from the half-diameter stated in the <s>sūtra</s> together with the third of the excess. When this is done, in the chariot-wheel fire-altar, the diameter becomes three hundred and seventy-one <s>aṅgulas</s> less six <s>tilās</s>. And the circumference is one thousand and sixty-five hundred <s>aṅgulas</s>. The area of that circle, obtained by the previously stated [formula] 'half of the equal circumference,' etc., is one <s>lakṣa</s> and eight thousand. In making a circle into a square too, in the diameter stated by the <s>sūtra</s>, one should add from its own tripled [value] a thirty-third hundredth. On this, verses:
In making a square into a circle, an eighteenth-hundredth should be discarded
from the half-diameter stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — this is the half-diameter of the circle.
Or, in the diameter of the square, having added a thirtieth-hundredth,
then adding an eighth of that — this is the diameter of the circle.
In making a circle into a square, to the diameter prescribed by the <s>sūtra</s>, one should add
from its own tripled value a thirty-third plus the excess — this is [the diameter] of the circle.
Discarding a thirty-second hundredth from the diameter of the circle,
then discarding a ninth of the remainder — this is the diameter of the square.
When this is done, even in a fire-altar of one hundred types with the circle-diameter,

children.text: sa tiladvitayaviśeṣo na ca bhavati parasparadhirodhaḥ //5 //
children.translated_text: the difference is [only] two <s>tilās</s>, and there is no mutual contradiction.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)
By [a single] measure, the area is determined. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.4 ||

children.text:
caturaśraṃ pramīyate kṣetramaneneti pramāṇaṃ prakramādi /
yatra pramāṇenaiva codanā tatra tenaiva caturaśraṃ vidhīyata iti pratyetavyam /
puruṣaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣaḥ ityādiṣu ca saṃkhyā vivakṣitā /
children.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s> (measure) is that by which a square field is measured — the <s>prakrama</s> (pace) and the like. Where the instruction is given by a single measure, there it should be understood that a square is determined by that [single] measure alone. 'A <s>puruṣa</s> (man-height) on the southern wing' — and in such [cases], a [specific] number is intended.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary
The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (producer of double) and other <s>karaṇīs</s> have been stated. To understand their results, he says 'by measure' —
(By measure, the area is determined.)

children.text: yatra pramāṇenaikena vimānaṃ tatra sarvatastenaikena parimitaṃ caturaśraṃ phalaṃ bhavati yathā "puruṣaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe' ityādi,
children.translated_text: Where the measurement is by a single measure, there the square, fully measured by that single [measure] on all sides, is the result-area. As in 'a <s>puruṣa</s> on the southern wing,' etc.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
He states the result-area of squares:
(By measure, the area is determined.)
By a rod of a single measure, an area of a single measure is determined — is made.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)
Other than a square, [the area is known] from instruction. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.5 ||

children.text:
ādiśatītyādeśo vidhiḥ /
vidheranyaddhavati--yatra vidhīyate tatrānyadapi bhavati tenaiva pramāṇena gārhapatyacityuparavādiṣu
children.translated_text: 'That which instructs' is the <s>ādeśa</s> (instruction), i.e., the rule. Something other than the rule exists — where it is prescribed, there too something else exists, by that same measure, as in the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar bricks and the like.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary
(Other than a square, from instruction.)

children.text:
ādiśatītyādeśaḥ--upadeśaḥ /
tenānyaccaturaśrāt prāgādiphalatvamavagamyate /
athavā ādiśatītyādeśo--gaṇitaśāstram /
tato viṣamādīnāṃ phalamavagantavyamiti /
uktaṃ ca tatra sarveṣāṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ prasārya pārśvaphalaṃ tadabhyāse iti, asyārthaḥ--sarveṣāṃ viṣamakṣetrāṇāṃ pārśve--pārśvamānītiryaṅbhānyau prasāryasaṃpādya /
tadabhyāse--tayoranyānyaguṇakāle phalamavagantavyamiti /
trikaṃ dvidhā pracchidyānyataracchedamanyatropadadhyāt /
tatra sā dīrghā caturaśrā /
"tathāyuktāṃ saṃcakṣate' vakṣyamāṇena nyāyena phalāvagamaḥ, dīrghacaturaśrasya pārśvamānīpramāṇena tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇamabhyasya phalāvagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They thus declare it to be combined' — by the principle to be stated, the result is understood; for the rectangle, the result is understood by multiplying the lateral measure by the transverse measure.
For the circle, the result is understood by multiplying half the circumference by half the diameter.

children.text: śarārdhapramāṇena dhanurardhamabhyasya dhanuṣaḥ phalāvagama ityādi gaṇitaśāstrādavagantavyamiti /
children.translated_text: By a measure of half the arrow [height], multiplying by half the arc, the result of the arc-segment is understood — and so on, to be understood from the science of mathematics.
Let us return to the main subject.

'That which instructs' is the <s>ādeśa</s> — the teaching. From that, the pre-eminence of the square's result is understood as compared to other [shapes]. Alternatively, 'that which instructs' means the <s>ādeśa</s> — the science of mathematics. From that, the results of irregular and other [shapes] are to be understood. And it is said there: 'of all fields, having extended the side-result, and in its repetition' — the meaning of this is: of all irregular fields, having extended and established the lateral measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) and the transverse measure (<s>tiryaṅmānī</s>) as the two sides, in the product of one by the other, the result is to be understood. Having cut a triangle in two, one should place one cut-piece upon the other — there, that is the rectangle.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary]
(Other than a square, from instruction.)
Everywhere, only a square is constructed; circles and the like [are derived] from its procedure alone.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)
By two, four. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.6a ||

children.text:
dvābhyāṃ prakramābhyāṃ caturaśre kṛte catvāri puruṣapramāṇāni bhavanti /
maṇḍalānāṃ caturaśrakaraṇamuktam /
caturaśrāṇāṃ maṇḍalakaraṇamidaṃ noktaṃ iyatyā rajjvā iyat kṣetraṃ bhavatīti /
ata idamucyate
children.translated_text: When a square is made with two <s>prakramas</s> (paces), there are four <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [areas]. The making of squares from circles has been stated. The making of circles from squares has not been stated [in the form] 'with a cord of this measure, an area of this size results.' Hence this is stated:
By three, nine. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.6b]

children.text:
tribhiḥ prakramaiḥ caturaśre kṛte nava puruṣakṣetrāṇi bhavanti /
tathā bhūmāvālikhya draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: When a square is made with three <s>prakramas</s>, there are nine <s>puruṣa</s>-areas. This should be verified by drawing on the ground.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(By two, [four]; by three, nine.)

children.text:
upalabdhiḥ yatra dvābhyāṃ dviguṇapramāṇena vimānaṃ tatra sarvato dvipramāṇe caturaśre dvipramāṇaparimitāni catvāri caturaśrāṇi phalaṃ bhavati /
tripramāṇe caturaśre tripramāṇaparimitāni nava caturaśrāṇi phalam /
children.translated_text: The verification: where [a square is made] with two — with a measure of double the <s>pramāṇa</s> — there, in a square of two <s>pramāṇas</s> on each side, the result is four squares each bounded by two <s>pramāṇas</s>. In a square of three <s>pramāṇas</s>, the result is nine squares each bounded by three <s>pramāṇas</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
(By two, [four]; by three, nine.) With a rod of two <s>pramāṇas</s>, four <s>pramāṇa</s>-areas result.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: yāvatpramāṇā rajjus tāvatastāvato vargān karoti || ĀpŚus_3.8a ||
children.translated_text: A cord of whatever measure produces that many rows of that many [squares]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.8a]

children.text:
yāvatpramāṇā--yāvadāyāmā rajjuḥ tāvato vargānkaroti--paṅktīḥ karoti--yāvatsaṃkhyāyuktaṃ pramāṇaṃ tāvatsaṃkhyāyuktāḥ paṅktīḥ karoti /
pañcamānāṃ pañcasakhyāyu ktānvargānkaroti /
evaṃ sarvatra yojanīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Of whatever measure' — a cord of whatever length produces that many rows — produces rows [equal in number to] the number associated with the measure. [A cord] of five measures produces rows of five in number. Thus it should be applied everywhere.
And thus is the verification.

children.text:
bhūmāvālikhya prekṣite tathaivopalabhyate /
dyābhyāṃ kṛte ubhayato likhaite catvāri śṛṅgāṇi bhavanti, pañcabhiḥ kṛte pañcadhā, ubhayato likhite pañcaviṃśatiśṛṅgāṇi bhavanti /
evaṃ sarvatra draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: When examined by drawing on the ground, it is verified exactly so. When made with two [units], having drawn [lines] in both directions, there are four corner-points; when made with five, [dividing] fivefold, having drawn in both directions, there are twenty-five corner-points. Thus it should be observed everywhere.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(A cord of whatever measure... thus the verification.)

children.text:
yāvanti pramāṇāni yasyā rajjvāḥ sā rajjustāvatastāvataḥ pramāṇasaṃkhyāyuktān tāvataḥ--tatsaṃkhyāguṇitānvargān samacaturaśrān karoti /
"vargasamacaturaśraḥ' iti gaṇitaśāsreṣu vyavahāraḥ /
tathā catuṣpramāṇā rajjuścaturbhirguṇitāścaturo vargān ṣoḍaśa karoti /
pañcapramāṇā pañcabhirguṇitān pañca vargān pañcaviṃśatiṃ, ṣaṭpramāṇā ekonapañcāśataṃ, aṣṭapramāṇā catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ, navapramāṇā ekāśītiṃ, daśapramāṇā śataṃ, ekādaśapramāṇā ekaviṃśottaraśataṃ, dvādaśapramāṇā catuśvatvāriṃśacchatami tyādi draṣṭavyam /
pramāṇamāha--upalabdhistathā--tathopalabhyate /
ukteṣvartheṣu pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇamityarthaḥ /
tathā dvipramāṇaṃ caturaśraṃ dvidhāpacchidya catvāryupalabhyante /
tripamāṇaṃ tridhāpacchidya nava, catuṣpramāṇaṃ caturdhāpacchidya ṣoḍaśa, evaṃ pañcapramāṇādi ṣvapi /
tathā dīrghasyākṣṇayārajjurityādiṣu tathātathopalabhyante /
dvābhyāmekamabhyasya phale dve upalabhyete /
tribhirdve abhyasya ṣaṭa /
caturbhirdve abhyasyāṣṭau /
tathāhi--dvipramāṇapārśvamānīkamekapramāṇatiryaṅbhānīyakaṃ dvidhāpacchidya dve upalabhyete /
dvipramāṇapārśvamānīkaṃ tripramāṇatiryaṅbhānīkaṃ pramāgdvidhodaka tridhāpacchidya ṣaḍupalabhyante /
evamanyeṣvapi pārśvamānīpramāṇasaṅkhyayodagavacchedaḥ tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇasaṅkhyayā prāgavaccheda iti kṛtvā phalāvagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: A cord having as many <s>pramāṇas</s> — that cord produces that many squares (<s>vargas</s>), multiplied by that number, i.e., multiplied by the <s>pramāṇa</s>-number — equal squares. '<s>Varga</s> means equal square' — such is the usage in mathematical treatises. Thus a cord of four <s>pramāṇas</s> produces four multiplied by four <s>vargas</s> — sixteen. One of five <s>pramāṇas</s> produces five multiplied by five <s>vargas</s> — twenty-five; one of six <s>pramāṇas</s>, forty-nine [sic, should be thirty-six]; one of eight <s>pramāṇas</s>, sixty-four; one of nine <s>pramāṇas</s>, eighty-one; one of ten <s>pramāṇas</s>, one hundred; one of eleven <s>pramāṇas</s>, one hundred twenty-one; one of twelve <s>pramāṇas</s>, one hundred forty-four — and so on should be observed. The authority states: 'The verification is thus' — it is thus verified. In the stated matters, direct perception is the authority — that is the meaning. Thus, cutting a square of two <s>pramāṇas</s> in two [directions], four are obtained. Cutting one of three <s>pramāṇas</s> in three [directions], nine; cutting one of four <s>pramāṇas</s> in four, sixteen; similarly for five <s>pramāṇas</s> and more. Likewise in [the rules] 'the diagonal cord of an oblong' etc., they are thus verified. Doubling one by two, the result two is obtained. Doubling two by three, six. Doubling two by four, eight. For instance: a [rectangle with] side-measure of two <s>pramāṇas</s> and breadth of one <s>pramāṇa</s>, cutting in two [directions], two are obtained. One with side-measure of two <s>pramāṇas</s> and breadth of three <s>pramāṇas</s>, cutting by the <s>pramāṇa</s> in two directions and in three, six are obtained. Similarly in others also: cutting northward by the number of side-measure <s>pramāṇas</s> and cutting eastward by the number of breadth <s>pramāṇas</s> — thus the result is understood.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
(A cord of whatever measure... thus the verification.)
By four, sixteen; by five, twenty-five — and so on. Here the authority [is]:
Thus the verification.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
A cord of one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> produces two with a quarter.

children.text: adhi--uparyardhaṃ yasyāḥsā adhyardhā, tayā kṛte caturaśre savādau dvau karoti (1 1ñ2 n 1 1ñ2 u 9ñ4 u 2 1ñ4)ekasya vargaḥ ekaḥ (12u1)tasyāgrataḥ pārśvataś ca dvāvardhau /
children.translated_text: '<s>Adhi</s>' means 'above,' [a cord] whose [additional part] is half — that is <s>adhyardhā</s> (one-and-a-half). With that, when a square is made, it produces two with a quarter (1½ × 1½ = 9/4 = 2¼). The <s>varga</s> (square) of one is one (1² = 1); before it and beside it are two halves.

children.text: pūrveṇa saha dvau, ardhena yaccaturaśraṃ kṛtaṃ, koṭyāṃ sapādam /
children.translated_text: Together with the former, [that makes] two; and the square made by the half — at the corner, [produces] a quarter.
By that, it produces two quarters [i.e., two quarter-areas total, but combined = one quarter extra].
The subsequent sūtra should be applied in the same way.
A cord of two-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> [produces] six with a quarter. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.8b]
Now the universal rule. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.9a]
The universal method (5/2 × 5/2 = 6¼)

children.text: yāvatā yāvatādhikena parilikhati tatpārśvayor upadadhāti | yac ca tena caturaśraṃ kriyate tat koṭyām || ĀpŚus_3.9b ||
children.translated_text: By whatever [measure] one draws [the square], and by how much it is increased — that [excess] one places on two sides; and the square made by that [excess] — that [goes] at the corner. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.9b]
By half the <s>pramāṇa</s>, a quarter-<s>pramāṇa</s> [area] is produced. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.10a]

children.text:
yāvatā thedenādhikena parilikiti tatpārśvayoragrataśvopadadhāti /
yattena caturaśraṃ kriyate tatkoṭyāṃ--evaṃ vihitena yaccaturaśraṃ koṭyāṃ tenaiva saha sākhyā boddhavyoti /
maṇḍalapūraṇe caikenai kaṃ bhavati /
ardhe cārdhamiti kasyacibhdrāntiḥsyāt atastaṃ pratyāha--
children.translated_text: By whatever excess beyond [the base unit] one draws — that [excess] one places on two sides and in front. The square made by that [excess] — that at the corner. Thus, the square [area] produced at the corner by the method prescribed — its count should be understood together with [the rest]. And in filling the circle, one by one it becomes [complete]. And lest someone have the confusion that 'half of a half' [makes a quarter] — to that he says:
By half the <s>pramāṇa</s>, a quarter-<s>pramāṇa</s> [area] is produced.
By the half-<s>pramāṇa</s>, a quarter-<s>pramāṇa</s> [area] is produced. The reason for this he states:
Because of filling the quarter of [a cord] whose length is two <s>pramāṇas</s> [i.e., the half fills one-fourth of the area of the two-unit square]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.10b]
By the third, a ninth portion. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 3.10c]

children.text:
ardhasya dvipramāṇā puruṣamātrī /
pādānāṃ pūraṇaṃ yataḥ /
taduktaṃ--"dvābhyāṃ catvāri' iti /
tṛtīyena navamī kalā, pramāṇatṛtīyena navamī kalā -- navamoṃ'śa ityarthaḥ /
tadapyuktaṃ-- tribhirnaveti.
children.translated_text: 'The half whose length is two <s>pramāṇas</s>' — is one <s>puruṣa</s> in measure. Because it fills the quarters. As was stated: 'by two, four.' 'By the third, a ninth portion' — by one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, a ninth portion — a ninth part is the meaning. That too was stated: 'by three, nine.'
Thus in the <s>Kapardi</s> commentary on the <s>Āpastamba</s> sūtra exposition,
in the inquiry called <s>Śulba</s>, the first <s>paṭala</s> (section),
third <s>khaṇḍa</s> (chapter).
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary.
Now the results for fractional measures are stated — '<s>adhyardha</s>' (one-and-a-half) etc.
(A cord of one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>... a ninth portion.)

children.text:
adhyardhapuruṣapramāṇenādhyardhapuruṣamabhyasya phalaṃ dvau sapādau--pādasahitau dvaupu ruṣau karoti /
ardhatṛtīyapuruṣā ṣaṭ sapādān, ardhaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yeṣāṃ te ardhatṛyīyāḥ, te ca pramāṇaṃ yasyāḥ sār'dhatṛtīyapuruṣā /
sā yenābhyastāḥ phalaṃ sapādān ṣadpuruṣān karoti /
upalabdhirapi tathā adhyardhapuruṣacaturaśrasyārdhena caikena cāpacchedaḥ prākcodakca eka me kena dvāvardhau pādaśva, evamanyadapi ubhyataḥ sacchede sapādarajjumadhyardhaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ karoti /
caturaśrakṣetravipṛddhau vṛddhakṣetraparijñānaprakāramāha--antaḥsamīpaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tadatītya vartata ityatyantaḥ atyantaḥ pradeśaḥ vidhiryasya so 'tyantapradeśaḥ--sārvatrika ityarthaḥ /
samacaturaśra viṣayo 'yam /
yāvatā--yāvatpramāṇena, yāvatādhikena--yāvatpra māṇonādhikena /
eko yāvacchabdaḥ pramāṇamātraviṣayaḥ, anyo yāvacchabda āganduviṣayaḥ /
yāvatā pramāṇena yāvanmātrādhikenetyarthaḥ /
parilikhati yaccaturaśrakaraṇārthaṃ parilikhati tatra tat adhikamāgantumūlacaturaśrakṣetraṃ pārśvayoḥ prācī codīcī ca kṣetramupadadhāti--saṃyojayati /
yacca tenadhikamātreṇa caturaśraṃ kriyate tatkṣetraṃ koṭyāṃ saṃyojayati /
etaduktaṃ bhavati--sarvatra samacaturaśrakṣetravivṛddhau vivṛddhasya caturaśrasya ca dakṣiṇapa śvima bhāge mūlapramāṇakṛtacaturaśraṃ parikalpya tasyatasya pūrvottarapārśvayostatpār śvamitapārśvamānīkaṃ pramāṇādhikamātratiryaṅbhānīkaṃ kṣetraṃ parikalpya yacca tenā dhikamātreṇa ekenaikaṃ dvābhyāṃ catvāri tribhirnavetyādiphalakaraṇaṃ caturaśraṃ kriyate tatkṣetraṃ prāgudakkoṭyā parikalpayediti /
evaṃ sarvatra samacaturaśrasya kṣetravṛddhau kṣetrasya parigaṇanaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: With a measure of one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>, multiplying [it by] one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>, the result is two with a quarter — it produces two <s>puruṣas</s> together with a quarter. 'Two-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> [produce] six with a quarter' — those whose half is the third [i.e., 2½] are <s>ardhatṛtīya</s>; and that which is the measure of such [a cord] is <s>ardhatṛtīyapuruṣā</s>. When multiplied by itself, the result produces six <s>puruṣas</s> with a quarter. The verification is also thus: a square of one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>, cut in half and by one both east-west and north-south — one piece has two halves and a quarter; and likewise the other [piece]; cutting with the <s>sapāda</s> (one-and-a-quarter) cord on both sides, it makes one-and-a-half sixteenths. For the increase of a square area, [the author] states the method of knowing the increased area: '<s>Anta</s>' means 'near the end'; the topic that goes beyond that is '<s>atyanta</s>'; 'the rule whose range is universal is <s>atyantapradeśa</s>' — meaning 'universally applicable.' This pertains to equal squares. 'By whatever' — by whatever <s>pramāṇa</s>; 'by however much increased' — by however much in excess of the <s>pramāṇa</s>. One 'yāvat' word refers to the <s>pramāṇa</s> [itself]; the other 'yāvat' word refers to the additional [portion]. Meaning: by whatever <s>pramāṇa</s>, [increased] by that much additional. 'Draws' — what one draws for the purpose of making a square, there: that additional root-square area one places on two sides — the eastern and northern sides — joins [it]. And the square made by that additional amount alone — that area one joins at the corner. This is what is stated: everywhere in the increase of equal square areas, having conceived the original <s>pramāṇa</s>-square at the south-west portion of the increased square, and having conceived on its eastern and northern sides an area with side-measurement measured by that side and breadth equal to the additional amount, and whatever square is made by that additional amount alone — 'one by one makes one, by two makes four, by three makes nine' etc. — that corner area one should conceive at the northeast corner. Thus everywhere in the increase of a square area, one should calculate the area — that is the meaning.

children.text:
ardhapramāṇena--pramāṇārdhenāpādapramāṇaṃ--pādo 'tra caturthobhāgaḥ, tatpramāṇaṃ vidhīyate saṃpādyate pramāṇārdhamitaṃ kṣetraṃ prameyasya catu rthabhāgo bavati /
kutaḥ? ardhasya dvipramāṇāyāḥ pādapūraṇatvāt ardhasya dvipramāṇakatayā bhūmeścaturbhāgaḥ pūryate /
children.translated_text: 'By half the <s>pramāṇa</s>' — by half of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, 'a quarter-<s>pramāṇa</s> [area]' — here <s>pāda</s> means the fourth part; that measure is produced — an area measured by half the <s>pramāṇa</s> becomes the fourth part of the [full] area to be measured. Why? 'Because of filling the quarter of [a cord] whose length is two <s>pramāṇas</s>' — because the half fills the fourth part of an area whose length is two <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text: tṛtīyena navamī kalā--pramāṇatṛtīyena kṣetrasya navamoṃ'śaḥ pūryate /

children.translated_text: The verification is thus.

children.text: ekapramāṇāyā bhūmerardhena prākyodakcāpacchede kṛter'dhapramāṇakṛtā bhūmirekapramāṇāyāḥ pādo dṛśyate, tasyā evaṃ prākcodakcāpacchede pramāṇatṛtīyamitā bhūmirekapramāṇāyā navamāśo dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Cutting an area of one <s>pramāṇa</s> by its half, both east-west and north-south, an area of half-<s>pramāṇa</s> dimension is seen to be one-fourth of the one-<s>pramāṇa</s> area. Similarly, cutting it east-west and north-south, an area measured by one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is seen to be one-ninth of the one-<s>pramāṇa</s> area.

children.text: tathā caturthena ṣoḍaśa kalā, pañcamena pañcaviṃśatikalā, ṣaṣṭhena ṣaṭratriṃśoṃ'śaḥ pūryate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, by the fourth, a sixteenth portion; by the fifth, a twenty-fifth portion; by the sixth, a thirty-sixth part is filled.
Similarly, other cutting-results should also be observed.
'By the third, a ninth portion' — by one-third of the <s>pramāṇa</s>, a ninth part of the area is filled.
Thus ends the first <s>paṭala</s> (section) in the <s>Śulbapradīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Karavinda Svāmin</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
Now he states the results for fractional [measures] —
(One-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> [produce] six with a quarter.)

children.text:
evaṃ ardhacaturthapuruṣād dādaśa sapādān, ardhapañcamapuruṣā viṃśatiṃ sapādānityādi /
sapādapuruṣā adhyardhaṃ ṣoḍaśabhāgaṃ cetyādi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, three-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> [produce] twelve with a quarter; four-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> [produce] twenty with a quarter — and so on. One-and-a-quarter <s>puruṣas</s> [produce] one-and-a-half plus a sixteenth — and so on should be observed.

children.text:
sārvatriko 'yaṃ vidhiḥ--kṛtsnaṃ caturaśraṃ vardhayitumicchan yāvatā pramāṇena vardhayitumicchati tatpurastāduttarataśvopadadhāti /
adhikapramāṇena yaccaturaśraṃ kriyate taduttarapūrvasyāṃ koṭyām /
idānīṃ tacchedānāṃ phalamāha--
children.translated_text: This is the universal method: one who wishes to increase the entire square — by whatever <s>pramāṇa</s> one wishes to increase it, one places that in front and to the north. The square made by the excess <s>pramāṇa</s> — that at the northeast corner. Now he states the results of those cuts —
(Now the universal rule.)

children.text: dvipramāṇāyā rajjvāḥ ardhasya pramāṇamātrasya pādapūraṇa tvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the half of a cord of two <s>pramāṇas</s> fills one quarter [of the total area],
the result of a cord of two <s>pramāṇas</s> is four.
Its quarter is one; because it fills that — that is the meaning.
(By the third, a ninth portion.)
The fractional part — because one-third of a cord of three <s>pramāṇas</s> fills one-ninth — since this is understood, it is not [separately] stated.
By the fourth, sixteen; by the fifth, twenty-five — and so on should be observed.
Thus in <s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary on the <s>Āpastamba Śulbasūtra</s>,
the <s>Śulbapradīpa</s>, the first <s>paṭala</s> (section).
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text:
pūrvamaviśeṣeṇa mānamuktam, asyeyānāyāmaḥ iyānvistara evaṃ ca vihartavyamiti /
viśeṣavidhānārthamāha--
children.translated_text: Previously, the measure was stated without specification [of particular values] — 'its length is such, its breadth is such, and thus one should construct.' For the purpose of specifying particular values, he states:

children.text: āgnyādheyike vihāre gārhapatyāhavanīyayor antarāle vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_4.1a ||
children.translated_text: In the construction pertaining to the <s>āgnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment ritual), the interval between the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fires] is known [from scripture]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.1a]

children.text:
gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālaṃ yathā syānnāhavanīyadakṣiṇāgnayoḥ dakṣiṇāgnigārhapatyayorvā mā bhūdityevamarthaṃ gārhapatyāhavanīyagrahaṇam /
vijñāyate--śrūyate /
śrutirvakṣyamāṇā /
children.translated_text: The mention of '<s>Gārhapatya</s> and <s>Āhavanīya</s>' is for the purpose that the interval should be [specifically] between <s>Gārhapatya</s> and <s>Āhavanīya</s>, and not between <s>Āhavanīya</s> and <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>, or between <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> and <s>Gārhapatya</s>. 'Is known' — is heard [from scripture]. The scripture [reference] will be stated.

children.text: aṣṭāsu prakrameṣu brāhmaṇo 'gnim ādadhīta | ekādaśasu rājanyaḥ | dvādaśasu vaiśyaḥ || ĀpŚus_4.1b ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should establish the fire at [a distance of] eight paces; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> at eleven; a <s>Vaiśya</s> at twelve. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.1b]

children.text: caturviṃśatyām aparimite yāvatā vā cakṣuṣā manyate tasmān nātidūram ādheya iti sarveṣām aviśeṣeṇa śrūyate || ĀpŚus_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: [Also heard is:] 'At twenty-four, or at an unlimited [distance], or at whatever [distance] one considers [reachable] by the eye — therefore it should not be too far' — this is heard without distinction for all [varṇas]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.2]

children.text:
prakrameṇa pramāṇaṃ vakṣyati /
aṣṭau prakramānatītya gārhapatyādāhavanīyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati /
evamekādaśasu rājanyasya /
vaiśyasyadvādaśasu /
caturviṃśatyā vā parimite vā yāvātā vā cakṣuṣā manyate /
tasmānnādidūramādheyaḥ iti sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇa śrūyate /
yāvatā veti sarveṣāṃ vidhirvikalvena /
iyatāntarālena vihārasaṃpattirbhavatīti mananam /
atidūrapratiṣedho vyavāyaparihārārthaḥ /
yadyatidūramādhīyate tadā śvādayo vyaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: He will state the <s>pramāṇa</s> (standard measure) by means of the <s>prakrama</s> (step). Having passed eight <s>prakramas</s>, one establishes the <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering-fire) from the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire). Similarly, [at] eleven [<s>prakramas</s>] for a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior). At twelve for a <s>vaiśya</s> (commoner). Or at twenty-four, or at an unlimited [distance], or as much as one judges by sight. Therefore "it should not be placed too far" — this is heard for all without distinction. "Or as much as" — this is the rule for all, with an option. The reflection is: by this much interval, the accomplishment of the construction is achieved. The prohibition of excessive distance is for the purpose of avoiding interruption. If it is placed too far, then dogs and the like might intervene.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary

children.text:
uktāḥsāmānyato vihārāḥ /
idānīṃ darśapūrṇamāsādiṣu viśeṣavivakṣayā prathamabhūtāgnayādheyavihārayāgavidhirucyate /
agnaya adhīyante 'smin karmaṇīti tadagnayādheyaṃ /
tabhdava āgnayā dheyikaḥ /
vihriyante 'smin agnaya iti vihāraḥ, devayajanedaśaḥ, tamadhikṛtya /
gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarāle--gārhapatyāhavanīya śabdābhyāṃ tattadāyatane lakṣaṇā antarāla śrutisāmarśyāt, antarāle antarālaṃ prastutya vijñāyate śrūyate /
sarvatra vijñāyata ityasyāyamevārthaḥ gārhapatyāhavanīyagrahaṇāt, tayorevāntarāle /
śrutirevaṃ paṭhyate--
children.translated_text: The constructions (<s>vihāras</s>) have been stated in general. Now, with the intention of specifying particular details in the <s>Darśa-Pūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon sacrifices) and other rites, the rule for the construction of the <s>Agniyādheyā</s> (fire-establishment) sacrifice, which is primary, is stated. That sacrifice in which the fires are established is the <s>Agniyādheya</s>. Derived from that is <s>āgneyādheyika</s> (pertaining to fire-establishment). That in which the fires are placed is the <s>vihāra</s> (construction-ground) — the place of the <s>devayajana</s> (sacrificial ground); with reference to that. In the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> — by the words "<s>gārhapatya</s>" and "<s>āhavanīya</s>," the respective altar-sites are indicated figuratively, from the implication of the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) [mentioning] "interval"; the interval is understood as the interval that is the subject at hand. "It is known everywhere" — this very meaning follows from the mention of <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>: in the interval between those two alone. The <s>Śruti</s> reads thus:

children.text: aṣṭāsu prakrameṣu brāhnaṇo 'gnīnādadhītaikādaśasu rājanyo dvādaśasu vaiśyaḥ caturviṃśatyāmaparimite yāvatā vā caśruṣā manyate tasmānnātidūramādheya iti //
children.translated_text: "At eight <s>prakramas</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priest) should establish the fires; at eleven, a <s>kṣatriya</s>; at twelve, a <s>vaiśya</s>; at twenty-four, or at an unlimited [distance], or as much as one judges by sight; therefore it should not be placed too far."

children.text:
sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇ.a śrūyate /
prakramaṃ vakṣyati dvipadastripado veti /
aṣṭaprakramādayo 'ntarālaviśeṣaṇaṃ /
aṣṭāsu prakrameṣvantarāle ityādi /
aparimitasaṃkhyāyāṃ taccaturviṃśateḥ parataḥ tadānantaryāt, aparimitaṃ pramāṇāt bhūyaḥ, iti kātyāyanaḥ /
yāvatā vā cakṣuṣā manyate tāvatā pramāṇena cakṣuṣā gṛhītena manyate yathā iyāṃścaturviṃśati prakrama iti cakṣuṣā mānaṃ /
yadyapi caturviśateḥ parata eva paṭhyate tathāpi dvādaśasu vikrameṣvityārabhya yaṃ dvādaśasu vikrāmeṣu ityāditaittirīyakaśrutyanurodhādaṣṭaprakramādīnamapi sarveṣāṃ grāhyaṃ, tena iyānaṣṭaprakrama iyānekadaśa iyāndvādaśaprakrama iti saṃbhavati /
tasmāccaturviṃśateradūramatidūrenādheyaṃ /

children.translated_text: By this, the excessive distance that would follow from the statement "unlimited" is prohibited.
From the prescription of twenty-four, the methods [for distances] before this are [for places] not too far.
The four prescriptions beginning with twenty-four apply to all — <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the others — without distinction.
"At twelve <s>vikramas</s>" is also obtained for all without distinction.

This is heard for all without distinction. He will state the <s>prakrama</s> [as being] "of two feet or three feet." Eight <s>prakramas</s> and the like qualify the interval. "At eight <s>prakramas</s> in the interval" and so on. For the unlimited number, being after twenty-four and because of its sequence, "unlimited" means more than the <s>pramāṇa</s> — thus says <s>Kātyāyana</s>. "As much as one judges by sight" — by that measure which is grasped by the eye, one judges: "this much is eight <s>prakramas</s>," "this much is [eleven or twelve]" — thus measuring by sight. Although this is read after twenty-four, nevertheless, in accordance with the <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>Śruti</s> reading "at twelve <s>vikramas</s>" etc., beginning from "at twelve <s>vikramas</s>," it should be understood as applicable to all, starting from eight <s>prakramas</s>; thereby "this much is eight <s>prakramas</s>, this much is eleven, this much is twelve <s>prakramas</s>" becomes possible. Therefore it should not be placed too far from twenty-four.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
(In the fire-establishment [rite] ... <s>vaiśya</s>)

children.text: gārhapatyasya purastādeteṣu prakrameṣvatīteṣviti vijñāyate atha sāvarṇikī śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: It is understood that to the east of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, at these many <s>prakramas</s> passed — now the co-variant <s>Śruti</s> [reading]:
(At twenty-four ... is heard.)

children.text:
aparimitaṃ "pramāṇābhdūya' iti kalpāntaram /
cakṣuṣā manyata iti daṇḍādimānaniṣedhaḥ /
iyānaṣṭau prakramāḥ, iyānekādaśa iyān dvādaśeti cakṣukṣā yāvantaṃ deśaṃ manyate tasmānnātidaraṃ tasyāvadheḥsamīpa ādheyaḥ /
etatsarvaṃ prayogakāla evoktamanūdyate /
children.translated_text: "Unlimited" [means] "more than the <s>pramāṇa</s>" — this is another ritual interpretation. "One judges by sight" — this prohibits measuring by a rod and the like. "This much is eight <s>prakramas</s>, this much is eleven, this much is twelve" — thus whatever extent of ground one judges by sight — therefore it should not be placed too far, but near to that limit. All this is recapitulated as already stated at the time of practice.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: dakṣiṇataḥ purastād vitṛtīyadeśe gārhapatyasya nedīyasi dakṣiṇāgner vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: To the south-east, at a place slightly less than one-third [of the interval] of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, nearer [to it], the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) is known. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.3]

children.text:
dakṣiṇataḥ purastāt dakṣiṇāprākkoṇe deśe vitṛtīyadeśe--īṣadūnatṛtīyadeśe--kasya vitṛtīyadeśaḥ--gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālasya nedīyasi āsannatṛtīyadeśe pārśvādityarthaḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇāgnerāyatanamiti śrūyate /
children.translated_text: "To the south-east" — at the south-eastern corner; "at a place slightly less than one-third" — slightly less than a third [of the interval]; of whose third? — of the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>. "Nearer" — at a third-point near [to the <s>gārhapatya</s>]; the meaning is: from the side. There, the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) is known [from scripture].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
(To the south ... is known)

children.text: dakṣiṇataḥ purastāt dakṣiṇāprākkoṇadeśe tasya gārhapatyasya nedīyasi sannikṛṣṭe tasyaiva vitṛtīyadeśe viśabdo hīnavacanaḥ kiñciddhīnatṛtīyadeśāntarāle dakṣiṇāgrerāyatanaṃ śrūyate //
children.translated_text: "To the south-east" — at the south-eastern corner; of that <s>gārhapatya</s>, at the nearer, proximate, position; at the slightly-less-than-one-third point of that very [interval] — the prefix "vi-" denotes "somewhat less"; at a slightly-less-than-one-third portion of the interval, the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) is known [from scripture].
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
Now he states the prescription for the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire):
(To the south ... is known)
"At a place slightly less than one-third" — at a place of a deficient third, meaning a position slightly less than one-third.

children.text: gārhapatyasya dakṣiṇataḥ purastāttasyaiva nedīyasi vitṛtīyadeśe dakṣiṇāgrerāyatanamiti //
children.translated_text: To the south-east of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, at the nearer, slightly-less-than-one-third point of that very [interval], is the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire).
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
How is that [location] determined? He says:

children.text: gārhapatyāhavanīyayor antarālaṃ pañcadhā ṣaḍdhā vā saṃvibhajya ṣaṣṭhaṃ saptamaṃ vā bhāgam āgantum upasamasya samaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajyāparasmiṃs tṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā gārhapatyāhavanīyayor antau niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya nimittaṃ karoti tad dakṣiṇāgner āyatanam | śrutisāmarthyāt || ĀpŚus_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: Dividing the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> into five or six parts, adding a sixth or seventh part as the extension (<s>āgantu</s>), dividing [the total] evenly into three, making a mark at the farther (western) third, fixing [the cord] at the ends of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>, drawing [it] to the south by the mark, one makes a point — that is the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire); [this is known] by the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.4]

children.text:
gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālaṃ pañcadhā vibhajya ṣaḍdhā vā vibhajyetyanvayaḥ /
yadi pañcadhā tadā ṣaṣṭho bhāga āgantuḥ /
ṣaṣṭhaṃ saptamaṃ vā bhāgaṃ āgantumupasamasya samaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya /
yadi ṣoḍhā tadā saptamo bhāgaḥ āgantiḥ /
tamupasamasya saṃyojya, samaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya; āgantunā saha viṣamaṃ mābhūditi samagrahaṇam /
aparasmiṃstṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā gārhapatyāvahanīyayorantau niyamya pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkaṃ nihanyāt /
dakṣiṇāgnisthānaṃ śrutisāmarthyāt /
sāmarthyamabhidhānaśaktiḥ asyāḥśruterayamevārthaṃ iti /
tena gārhapatyāhavanīya yorantarālaṃ, triprathamavistārāyāmāni trīṇi caturaśrāṇi kṛtvāparasmin caturaśre uttarasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ gārhapatyaṃ dakṣiṇeṃ'sedakṣiṇāgnayāyatanaṃ pūrvasmin caturaśre, uttareṃsa āhavanīyamityevamādayo nirastā bhavanti /
sarvatrāgnayāyatanāni caturaśrāṇi maṇḍalāni vā /
iha tu maṇḍalaṃ gārhapatyamardhamaṇḍalākāramanvāhāryapacanaṃ /
caturaśramāhavanīyamiti smaranti maṇḍalacaturaśrayorukto vidhiḥ /
idānīṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ dhanurākāra ucyate--piśīladvikaraṇyā caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvoktena vidhānena maṇḍalaṃ kuryāt /
tasya maṇḍalasya viṣkambhacaturbhāgaṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ pūrvanihatācchaṅkorudagapasārya śaṅkaṃ nihatya tasminpāśaṃ pratimucya viṣkambhārdhena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhyottaramardhaṃ tyajet /
tatra ślokau bhavataḥ----
children.translated_text: The interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> — dividing it into five parts or into six parts — this is the construction. If into five, then the sixth part is the extension (<s>āgantu</s>). "Adding a sixth or seventh part as the extension, dividing [the total] evenly into three" — if into six, then the seventh part is the extension. Adding that, combining [it]; dividing evenly into three — the word "evenly" [is used so] that it should not be uneven together with the extension. Making a mark at the farther (western) third; fixing [the cord] at the ends of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>; fastening the loops, drawing [the cord] to the south by the mark, one should drive in a stake. [That is] the location of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>; [known] by the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s>. The "capacity" is the expressive power; the meaning is: of this <s>Śruti</s>, this is precisely the meaning. Therefore — having made three quadrilaterals with breadth and length each one-third of the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>, [the configurations where] the <s>gārhapatya</s> is at the northern hip of the farther quadrilateral, and the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar at the southern shoulder, and the <s>āhavanīya</s> at the northern shoulder of the nearer quadrilateral — such and similar [configurations] are ruled out. The fire-altar sites everywhere are either quadrilaterals or circles. Here, however, the <s>gārhapatya</s> is circular; the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern cooking-fire) is semicircular. The <s>āhavanīya</s> is square — thus they hold. The method for circles and quadrilaterals has been stated. Now the bow-shape of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> is stated: having made a square with the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>piśīla</s> (quarter unit), one should make a circle by the previously stated method. Moving a gnomon northward from the gnomon previously fixed at the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> [location] by one-fourth of the diameter of that circle, fixing a gnomon, fastening the loop on it, drawing a circle with half the diameter, one should discard the northern half. Herein are two verses:
"From the gnomon fixed at the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>, northward, a gnomon at ten <s>aṅgulas</s>
diminished by eleven <s>tilas</s> — equal to the arc of the [bow-shaped altar];"
"Fastening the loop on it, one should draw [a circle] with twenty [<s>aṅgulas</s>] of extension,
diminished by twenty-two <s>tilas</s>; one should discard the northern half."
Thus.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> — by the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s>.
He states the construction of this [<s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site]:

children.text:
gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālamaṣṭaprakramādikaṃ dañcadhā ṣoḍhā vā saṃbhujya guṇayitvā ṣaṣṭhaṃ saptamaṃ vā bhāgamāgantumupasamas pañcadhā guṇane ṣaṣṭhaṃ ṣoḍhā guṇane bhāgamumasamasya saṃyojyāgantun tṛtīye gārhapatyasannihite tṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ nirañjanaṃ kṛtvā gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantau niyamya rajjvantau pāśau gārhapatyasya pūrvaśaṅkau paścimaṃ pāśamāhavanīyasya paścimaśaṅkau pūrvaṃ pāśe pratimucya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya nimittaṃ cihnaṃ tatra kuryāt /
tannimittaṃ dhanurākṛterdakṣiṇāgnermadhyamaṃ, viśeṣāśravaṇāt /
gārhapatyāhavanīyayormadhyamaśaṅkvorantau niyamyeti kecit /
śrutisāmarthyāt /
"dakṣiṇataḥ purastāt' ityādi śrutibalādityarthaḥ /
atra pañcadhāpakṣe gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālasya dakṣiṇāgnayāyatanamadhyopakrāntāddakṣiṇottaralambāt paścimo bhāga ekatriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ tribhāgonasaptatilāś ca /
pūrvabhāgo 'ṣṭāviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ tribhāgādhikasaptaviṃśatitilāś ca /
lambakaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ pādonaṣoḍaśatilāś ca /
ṣaḍdhāpakṣe dvātriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ sārdhasaptaviṃśatitilāś ca pūrvabhāgaḥ /
lambakastriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ saptatilāś ca /
pādāṣṭakamite 'ntarālavat prakramite ekādaśādiṣu ca bhāgayorlambakasya pramāṇamunneyaṃ, unnayanaprakāraṃ cātraiva vakṣyāmaḥ /
atrāpyāyatanāni piśīlamātrāṇi, athavā asyaiṣa dhiṣṇyo līyata iti prājahitasyāpi dhiṣṇyatvadarśanādāyatanānāṃ caturaśramaṇḍalatvayoraniyamena prāptayorapi maṇḍajalameva gārhapatyāyatanaṃ agnanayo vai trayī vidyetyatrānuvākaparyāye tasya pṛthivīstuteḥ tadākāratvāccatasyāḥ ardhamaṇḍalākāraṃ dhanurākāraṃ dakṣiṇāgnayāyatanaṃ, tatraivāntarīkṣastuteḥ tadākāratvācca nabhasaścaturaśramāhavanīyam, tatraiva dyulokastuteḥ caturaśramaindrasthānamiti śāstrāntare darśanācca sabhyāvasathyayorapi caturaśrameva, tayostaddvikāratvāt /
atra yogaḥ gārhapatyāyatane piśīlamātraṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya maṇḍalaṃ kuryāddakṣiṇāgnerapi vacanāt, viśīladvikaraṇyā caturaśraṃ vihṛtya maṇḍalakṭitya maṇḍalaviṣkambhacaturbhāgena dakṣiṇāgnanayāyatanaṃ tannimittāduttarataḥśaṅkuṃ nihatya tatra śaṅkau tadviṣkambhamadhyaṃ niyamyāntau samau kṛtvā maṇḍalaṃ vilikhya maṇḍaladhye prācīṃ lekhāṃ vilikhya udagardhaṃ tyajet /
dakṣiṇārdha āyatanaṃ gārhapatyasya purastādaṣṭaprakramādīnatītya piśīlamātraṃ caturaśramāhavanīyaṃ kuryāt tatpurastāt sañcaramavaśiṣya āhavanīyavat sabhyaṃ tatpurastādāvasathyamapi /
tadvat piśīlapramāṇaṃ ca /
dviprādeśaṃ piśīlam /
muṣṭikṛto 'ratniḥ piśīlamityeke /
bāhvorantarālaṃ piśīlamityeka iti kecit /
prakramyata iti pakrama iti padasyāpi prakramatāmicchanti /
tathāpi labhyate, ayamatra vimānakramaḥ--gārhapatyāhavanīyadhiṣṇiyau vimāya gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālamityādi dakṣiṇāpāyamya niyamya nimittaṃ kṛtvā tenaiva lakṣaṇenottarataś ca nimittaṃ viparyasya dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca nimittaṃ kṛtvā piśīladvikaraṇīcaturaśramaṇḍalīvaṣkambhacaturthāṃśena dakṣiṇayornimittayorudakkṛtanimittadvayānukūlyena śaṅkuṃ nikhanet /
anayoḥ paścimaśaṅkau piśīladvikaraṇī caturaśramaṇḍalaviṣkambhārdhena maṇḍalamālikhya purvaśaṅkvānukūlyena prācīṃ jñātvā maṇḍalasyottarārdhaṃ tyajet /
dakṣiṇārdho dakṣiṇāgnidhiṣṇiyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: The interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> [fires], beginning with eight <s>prakramas</s> (paces), having multiplied fivefold or sixteenfold, the sixth or seventh part [respectively] should be the additional [length]. In the fivefold multiplication, adding the sixth part as the additional [length]; in the sixteenfold multiplication, adding the [seventh] part as the additional [length]; in the third [portion] near the <s>gārhapatya</s>, having made a mark at the third, fixing the ends [of the cord] at the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>, with the loops at the ends of the cord — fastening the western loop at the front peg of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and the eastern loop at the western peg of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, stretching southward by the mark, one should make a marker-sign there. That marker is the midpoint of the bow-shaped <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) [altar], by the absence of a specific instruction [to the contrary]. Some [authorities say]: fixing the ends at the middle pegs of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> — by the force of the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural passage). 'To the south, in front' and so on — the meaning is: by the authority of scripture. Here, in the fivefold option, from the perpendicular (<s>lamba</s>) dropped from the center of the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site southward in the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>: the western portion is thirty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> and seventy <s>tilās</s> minus a third. The eastern portion is twenty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-seven <s>tilās</s> plus a third. The perpendicular is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> and sixteen <s>tilās</s> minus a quarter. In the sixfold option, the eastern portion is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-seven and a half <s>tilās</s>. The perpendicular is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> and seven <s>tilās</s>. In intervals measured by quarter-eighths of <s>prakramas</s>, and in eleven and other [intervals], the measure of the perpendicular is to be derived; and the method of derivation we shall state here itself. Here too, the altar-sites are of <s>piśīla</s> measure; or, since 'this is his <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-seat) where [the fire] is deposited,' and because even the <s>prājahita</s> fire is seen to have the nature of a <s>dhiṣṇya</s>, of the two options — square and circular — for the altar-sites, which arise without restriction, only a circle is the <s>gārhapatya</s> altar-site, because in the <s>Anuvāka</s> passage 'The fires are indeed the threefold knowledge,' being a praise of the earth, and because of its [circular] shape; a semicircle — bow-shaped — is the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site, because in that very [passage] being a praise of the atmosphere, and because of its shape; a square is the <s>āhavanīya</s>, because of the praise of the heavenly world there and because a square <s>Aindra</s> altar is seen in other <s>śāstras</s>; and for the <s>sabhya</s> and <s>āvasathya</s> [fires] too, only a square, because those are modifications of it. Here the method: in the <s>gārhapatya</s> altar-site, having constructed a square of <s>piśīla</s> measure, one should make a circle — as prescribed even for the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>; having constructed a square with the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (diagonal) of the <s>piśīla</s>, making a circle, with a quarter of the circle's diameter [as the offset for] the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site, fixing a peg to the north from that marker, tying the cord there at the peg, fixing it at the center of that diameter, making the ends equal, drawing a circle, inscribing an east-west line through the center of the circle, one should discard the northern half. The southern half is the [<s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>] altar-site. In front of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, passing beyond eight <s>prakramas</s> and more, one should make a <s>piśīla</s>-measure square — the <s>āhavanīya</s>; in front of that, leaving a passage (<s>sañcara</s>), a <s>sabhya</s> [fire-altar] like the <s>āhavanīya</s>; in front of that, an <s>āvasathya</s> also. And that too of <s>piśīla</s> measure. A <s>piśīla</s> is two <s>prādeśas</s> (spans). Some say: a cubit with a closed fist is a <s>piśīla</s>. Others say: the distance between the [outstretched] arms is a <s>piśīla</s>. Some desire that the word <s>pakrama</s> should also be read as <s>prakrama</s> (pace). Even so, [the meaning] is obtained. Here is the measuring procedure: having measured the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> <s>dhiṣṇya</s> [fire-seats], 'the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>' — stretching southward and fixing, making a marker, and by that same mark making a marker to the north by reversing [the procedure], having made markers both to the south and to the north, with a quarter of the diameter of the circle [derived from] the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>-square of the <s>piśīla</s>, a peg should be driven in alignment with the two markers made to the north of the southern markers. At the western peg of these, drawing a circle with half the diameter of the circle [derived from] the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>-square of the <s>piśīla</s>, determining the east-west line in alignment with the eastern peg, one should discard the northern half of the circle. The southern half becomes the <s>dakṣiṇāgni dhiṣṇya</s> (southern fire-seat).
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
(On the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> -- by the force of scripture.)
How should that be taken? To this he says:

children.text:
samaṃ sarvaṃ, gārhapatyāhavanīyayoḥ gārhapatyasya paurastye śaṅkau āhavanīyasya pāśvātye śaṅkau ca dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇāgnayāyatanam /
tadāyatanamadhyamityanye /

children.translated_text: In that case, the measurement is taken only at the midpoints of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>.

children.text: sarvāṇyevāgrayāyatanāni piśīlamātrāṇi caturaśrāṇi parimaṇḍalāni vā dhiṣṇiyatvānmaṇḍalaṃ gārhapatyasya /
children.translated_text: All the primary altar-sites are of <s>piśīla</s> measure -- square or circular; because of being <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>, the <s>gārhapatya</s> is circular.
The <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> is semicircular, the <s>āhavanīya</s> is square -- thus say the traditionalists (<s>aitihāsikas</s>); and they state that all altar-sites are equal in area.

children.text: tatrokto maṇḍalavidhiḥ āhavanīyasyākṣṇayārajjvā caturaśraṃ vihṛtya vidhānena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā uttarārvaṃ jahyāttaddakṣiṇāgnayāyatanam //
children.translated_text: The stated circular procedure there: having constructed a square with the diagonal cord of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, making a circle by the [prescribed] method, one should discard the northern half -- that is the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site.

Everything is equal. Of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>: at the front peg of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and at the rear peg of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, to the south is the <s>dakṣiṇāgni</s> altar-site. Others say: that is the midpoint of the altar-site.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: yajamānamātrī prācy aparimitā vā yathāsannāni havīṃṣi saṃbhaved evaṃ tiraścī prāñcau vedyaṃsāv unnayati | pratīcī śroṇī purastād aṃhīyasī paścāt prathīyasī madhye saṃnatataraivam iva hi yoṣeti dārśikyā veder vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prācī</s> (east-west line) is of the measure of the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), or unlimited; the transverse [line] is such that the oblations are closely [accommodated]. He raises the front <s>vedī</s>-shoulders (<s>aṃsas</s>) forward. The western <s>śroṇīs</s> (hips) going westward: narrower in front, broader at the back, contracted in the middle -- 'thus indeed is a woman' -- this is known regarding the <s>vedī</s> of the <s>darśa</s> (new-moon) [sacrifice]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.5 ||

The passage beginning with 'of the measure of the sacrificer' is the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) regarding the <s>vedī</s> of the <s>darśa</s> (new-moon sacrifice). He explains the meaning of this scripture by the very method of measurement.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
After the construction of the altar-sites, the construction of the <s>vedī</s> for the primary <s>darśa-pūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon) [sacrifices] is stated.
(Of the measure of the sacrificer -- is known regarding the <s>vedī</s>.)
'Of the measure of the sacrificer.'

children.text:
yajamāmātrī ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulā prāktvenāpari mitā /
tadadhikā prācī prāṅmukhā, saṃbhavo vyāptiḥ, yathā havīṃṣi parasparasaṃbandhena āsannāni bhavanti tathā tiraśvī tiryaṅbhānī syāt, āyāmasya tribhāgonā paścattiraśvī /
"āyāmāsyārdhena purastāttiraśvī' iti bodhāyanaḥ /
paśubandhe ca tathā dṛśyate, aratnibhirvā caturbhiḥ paścāt ṣaḍbhiḥ prācī tribhiḥ purastāditi, vikṛtiṣu vahuhaviḥṣu bhahuvistārā, alpahaviḥ ṣu prakṛtivat /
prāñcau vedyaṃsāvunnayati prāktvena pūrvāntamatītāvaṃsau kuryāt pratīcī śroṇī tathā pṛthaktvena śroṇyākuryāt aṃhīyasī--tanvī prathīyasī-- vistīrṇā sannatatarā atiśayena tanuḥ, evamiva hi yoṣeti /
evamivahīti śabdo nipātasamudāyaḥ prasiddhavacanaḥ /
yathā--evamiva hi paśuḥ, evamiva hyannamadyata iti /
etadeva hi yoṣā sādṛśyamasyāḥ /
yanmadhye kṛśatvaṃ pṛthvaṃsatvaṃ pṛthutaraśroṇītvaṃ ca /
etat "catuḥśikhaṇḍā yuvatiḥsupeśā' iti mantravarṇācca labhyeta, dārśikyā vedeḥ darśapurṇamāsayoḥsādhāraṇā ' pi vediḥ darśe pūrvedyurddaśyatayā dārśikītyucyate /
yadvā--darśapūrṇamāsayorekaśeṣaṃ kṛtvā nirdeśaḥ,
children.translated_text: Of the measure of the sacrificer: ninety-six <s>aṅgulas</s> in the east-west direction, unlimited [meaning 'as needed']. More than that is the east-west length, facing east; <s>saṃbhava</s> (capacity) means accommodation -- the transverse [measure] should be such that the oblations are closely placed in relation to each other. The rear transverse [measure] is the length minus a third. <s>Bodhāyana</s> [says]: 'The front transverse [measure] is half the length.' In the animal sacrifice (<s>paśubandha</s>) too, it is so seen: four <s>aratnis</s> (cubits) at the back, six for the east-west length, three in front -- in variant [rituals] with many oblations, [the <s>vedī</s> is] wider; with few oblations, as in the primary [form]. 'He raises the front <s>vedī</s>-shoulders forward' -- beyond the eastern end, he should make shoulders [projections]. 'The western hips' -- likewise, he should make hips separately to the west. 'Narrower' means slender; 'broader' means wide; 'more contracted' means exceedingly thin [in the middle]. 'Thus indeed is a woman' -- <s>evam-iva-hi</s> is a recognized compound of particles, a well-known expression. As in: 'thus indeed is an animal,' 'thus indeed is food eaten.' This is the resemblance to a woman: that there is slenderness in the middle, broad shoulders, and broader hips. This is also obtained from the mantra-text 'four-tufted, youthful, well-formed.' The <s>vedī</s> of the <s>darśa</s> sacrifice: though common to both <s>darśa</s> and <s>pūrṇamāsa</s>, it is called <s>dārśikī</s> because it is seen [first] on the day before the <s>darśa</s>. Or: the designation is by retaining one of [the pair] <s>darśa-pūrṇamāsa</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
(Of the measure of the sacrificer -- is known.)

children.text:
yajamānamātrī caturaratniḥ pañcāratnirvā yathā'sannāni havīṣi saṃbhavet saṃgṛhṇīyāt /
evaṃ tiraśvī ardhalakṣaṇaṃ tiryagityarthaḥ /
unnayati dīrghaṃ nayati /
pratīcī pratīcyā yoṣāsādṛśyaṃ ca "catuḥśikhaṇḍā' iti mantravarṇāt darśikyāḥ-- darśapūrṇamāsikyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the measure of the sacrificer: four <s>aratnis</s> (cubits) or five <s>aratnis</s> -- such that the oblations are accommodated. Thus the transverse [measure] -- 'half-mark' means transversely. 'Raises' means extends lengthwise. 'Western' -- by the western [direction]. And the resemblance to a woman [is known] from the mantra-text 'four-tufted.' Of the <s>dārśikī</s> -- [meaning] of the <s>darśa-pūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifice].
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: apareṇāhavanīyaṃ yajamānamātrī dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya tāvatīṃ rajjum āyamya madhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇayoḥ śroṇyaṃsayor antarā niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya nimittaṃ karoti | nimitte rajjuṃ niyamyāntau samasya | dakṣiṇāyāḥ śroṇer dakṣiṇam aṃsam ālikhet | evam uttarataḥ | tiryaṅmānīṃ dviguṇāṃ tathā kṛtvā paścāt purastāc copalikhet | vimitāyāṃ purastāt pārśvamānyāv upasaṃharet | śrutisāmarthyāt || ĀpŚus_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: To the west of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, having constructed a rectangle of the sacrificer's measure, extending a cord of that length, making a mark at the middle, fixing [the ends] between the southern hip (<s>śroṇī</s>) and shoulder (<s>aṃsa</s>), stretching southward by the mark, he makes a marker. Having fixed the cord at the marker and made the ends equal: he should draw [a curve] from the southern hip to the southern shoulder. Similarly to the north. Having made the transverse measure double in the same way, he should draw at the back and front. When [the <s>vedī</s>] is measured, he should bring the lateral measures together in front. By the force of scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 4.6 ||
Thus ends the fourth section.

children.text:
apareṇāhavanīyaṃ ekarajjvādibhidīrṅghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya saṃpādya yajamānamātrī pārśvamānī yathā sannāni havīṃṣi saṃbhavet parasparāsaṃghaṭitāni tiṣṭhanti tathā tiryaṅbhānī /
tasyāstribhāgona vā tiraśvīti bodhāyanīye śulbāntare pratipāditam /
tāvatīṃ rajjumabhyasya ubhayataḥ pāśau kṛtvā dakṣiṇayoḥśroṇyaṃsayorantau niyamya pāśau pratimucya lakṣaṇena jakṣiṇāpāyamya nimittaṃ śaṅkuṃ nihatya tāsmin śaṅkau rajjuṃ saṃyojya pāśāvunmucya tena hastena gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇimārabhya yāvaddakṣiṇāṃsamālikhet /
evamuttarapārśvamālikhet /
etatsannatatvaṃ vedeḥ /
tiryaṅbhānyāpyevaṃ kuryāt /
tiryaṅbhānīpramāṇāṃ rajjumabhsya madhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā śroṇyorante pāśau pratimucya pārśvādapasārya tatra śaṅkuṃ nihatya tatra rajju prabadhyāntau samasya dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇimārabhya yāvaduttarā kṣoṇī tāvadālikhet /
evaṃ purastādapi karoti /
evamunnayanaṃ śroṇyaṃsau /
evaṃprakārā hi yoṣā /
hiśabdo rūpaprasiddhau /

children.translated_text: A woman of old [time] is indeed just so -- this is the meaning.
Of the measured [<s>vedī</s>] -- when thus made into a quadrilateral, in front one should bring the lateral measures together -- contract [them].
By the force of scripture -- by the authority of that scripture which says 'narrower in front.'
Otherwise, even the resemblance to a woman would not hold.

To the west of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, having constructed and completed a rectangle by the single-cord method and other means -- the lateral measure being of the sacrificer's measure, the transverse measure being such that the oblations are closely accommodated without mutual contact. The [rear] transverse being the length minus a third is established in the other <s>Śulba</s> [text] of <s>Bodhāyana</s>. Having extended a cord of that length, making loops on both ends, fixing the ends between the southern hip and shoulder, fastening the loops, stretching southward by the mark, fixing a marker-peg, tying the cord at that peg, releasing the loops and holding [the cord] by hand, starting from the southern hip he should draw [a curve] up to the southern shoulder. Similarly he should draw the northern side. This is the contraction of the <s>vedī</s>. With the transverse measure too, he should do the same: extending a cord of the transverse measure, making a mark at the middle, fastening the loops at the [ends of the] hips, stretching sideways, fixing a peg there, tying the cord and making the ends equal, starting from the southern hip he should draw up to the northern hip. Similarly he does in front also. Thus the raising of the hips and shoulders [is accomplished]. Such indeed is a woman. The word <s>hi</s> indicates well-known appearance.
Thus ends the fourth section.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
He explains with this construction procedure:
(To the west of the <s>āhavanīya</s>... similarly to the north.)
Although there is a large interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s>, the <s>vedī</s> is near the <s>āhavanīya</s> only.
Some desire the rectangle to have a length double the width.

children.text: uktapramāṇaṃ dīrghacaturaśramāhavanīyamapareṇa vihṛtya śroṇyaṃseṣu śaṅkunnihatya yāvadāyāmaḥ tāvatīṃ rajjumabhyasya āyāmadviguṇāṃ rajjuṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ nirañjanaṃ kṛtvā dakṣimayoḥśroṇyaṃsayorantau niyamya nirañjanena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin rajjuṃ pratimucya pāśāvekīkṛtya śroṇyā ārabhya yāvadaṃsaṃ vṛttamārgeṇālikhet /
children.translated_text: Having constructed a rectangle of the stated measure to the west of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, fixing pegs at the hips and shoulders, extending a cord of the length's measure, making a cord of double the length, making a mark at the middle, fixing the ends between the southern hip and shoulder, stretching southward by the mark, fixing a peg, tying the cord at that peg, releasing and uniting the loops, holding [the cord] by hand, starting from the hip he should draw [a curve] up to the shoulder by a circular path.
For the northern side, stretching northward, he should do the same.
'To the west' -- to the west of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, near the <s>āhavanīya</s>, behind [it].
(The transverse measure doubled -- should draw.)
'The transverse measure' --

children.text: pūrvāṃ tiryaṅbhānīṃ pūrvavaddviguṇāṃ kṛtvā purato 'pāyamya dakṣiṇasmadaṃsāt prakramya uttaramaṃsamālikhet, paścimayā tiryaṅbhānyā paścādapyevameva kuryāt, vediprācīmitāṃ rajjuṃ gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālamityuktaprakāreṇa vedyā dakṣiṇottaramāyamya pūrvavaddvitṛtīyadeśe lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt udagbahirvederuttarataḥ uttarārthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca kṛtvā vedyāḥ paścādapyavemeva vitṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt. gārhapatyāhavanīyayormadhyaṃ--madhyadeśaḥ tatra lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Having doubled the front transverse measure as before and drawing it forward, one should draw a line from the south shoulder to the north shoulder; with the rear transverse measure, one should do likewise at the back. Having stretched a cord measured [to the length of] the altar's east-west line, the interval between the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire) and <s>āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), by the stated method of the altar's north-south [measurement], one should make a mark at the second-third position as before, and having made a mark to the north outside the altar for the northern [side], one should likewise make a mark at the second-third behind the altar. The middle between the <s>gārhapatya</s> and <s>āhavanīya</s> — in the middle region, there one should make a mark.
(On 'having measured... by the authority of the Vedic text')

children.text:
vimitāyāmiti /
vimitāyāṃ caturaśrīkṛtamātrāyāṃ lekhākaraṇāt prāgeva pārśvamānyau purastātpurata upasaṃhāret--saṃkocayet /
children.translated_text: 'Having measured' — on the [altar] that has been measured, i.e., already made into a quadrilateral, before the drawing of lines, one should contract — draw together — the lateral measures from the front.
Thus [ends] the fourth section.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(On 'to the west... by the authority of the Vedic text')
He states the extension (<s>viharaṇa</s>) of that [altar]:

children.text:
nimitte rajjuṃ rajjumadhyaṃ niyamya pratimucya dakṣiṇāyai dakṣiṇasyāḥ śroṇerārabhya dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ pratyālikhet /
tiryaṅbhānyorapi madhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā śroṇyoraṃsayośvāntau niyamya paścātpurastāccāpāyamyetyādi draṣṭavyam /
etadeva śroṇyaṃsayorunnayanam /
vimitāyāṃ caturaśrīkṛtāyāṃ saṃnamanātpūrvameva kiñcidupasaṃharet, "purastādaṃhīyasī' iti śrutisāmarthyāt /
atra bodhāyanaḥ--
children.translated_text: Having fastened a cord at the midpoint of the indicator pegs, starting from the south hip (<s>śroṇi</s>) on the south side, one should draw a line to the south shoulder (<s>aṃsa</s>). Having made marks at the midpoints of the transverse measures too, and fixing the ends at the hips and shoulders, drawing [the cord] backward and forward — and so on should be seen. This itself is the elevation of the hips and shoulders. On the [altar] that has been measured and made quadrilateral, before the bending, one should contract [the sides] somewhat, by the authority of the Vedic text 'narrower in front.'  Here <s>Baudhāyana</s> [states]:

children.text: "yajamānamātrī prācī, tasyā evārdhaṃ purastāttiraśvī, tribhāgonā paścāt tiraśvī triṃśatpadāni' iti //
children.translated_text: 'The east-west line is measured by the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer); half of it is the front transverse [measure]; the rear transverse diminished by a third; thirty <s>padas</s> (feet).'
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>)

children.text: triṃśat padāni prakramā vā paścāttiraśvī bhavati | ṣaṭtriṃśat prācī caturviṃśatiḥ purastāt tiraścīti saumikyā veder vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Thirty <s>padas</s> (feet) or <s>prakramas</s> (paces) is the rear transverse measure. Thirty-six is the east-west line; twenty-four is the front transverse — thus is known of the <s>saumikī vedī</s> (Soma altar). || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 5.1 ||

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśikāyām aṣṭādaśopasamasya aparasmād antād dvādaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ pañcadaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ pṛṣṭhyāntayor antau niyamya pañcadaśakena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ nihantyevam uttarataḥśroṇī | viparyasyāṃsau pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamya dvādaśike śaṅkuṃ nihanti | evam uttaratastāv aṃsau || ĀpŚus_5.2a ||
children.translated_text: On a cord of thirty-six: having added eighteen [to itself], from the far end, a mark at twelve, a mark at fifteen; having fixed the two ends at the ends of the spine-cord, having made the alignment; having drawn southward with the fifteen[-mark], one fixes a peg — thus the southern hip. Likewise northward — the [other] hip. Reversing, the shoulders: having drawn with the fifteen[-mark] itself, one fixes a peg at the twelve[-mark] — thus the northern [side]; those are the shoulders. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 5.2a ||

children.text:
padānītyasmadīyā śrutiḥ /
triṃśatpadāni prakramā vā paścāttiraśvīti /
tiryaṅbhānī bhavati /
ṣaṭtriṃśatpṛṣṭhyā prācī caturviṃśatiḥ purastāt tiryaṅbhānī bhavatīti saumikyā vedeḥ some śrutiḥ /
ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāṃ rajjvāṃ aṣṭādaśopasamasya prakṣipyāntayoḥ pāśau kṛtvāparasmādantāddvādaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ pañcadaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ nirañjanaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhyāntayoḥ prāgvaṃśasya madhyamāllālāṭikāttīnprācaḥ prakramān prakramya śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmācca purastāt ṣaṭtriṃśatprakrame śaṅkū nihatya tayoḥ pāśau pratimucya pañcadaśakena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkaṃ nihanyāt /
sā dakṣiṇā śroṇī /
evamuttarato 'pasārya śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
sottarā śroṇī /
viparyastayāṃsau /
pañcadaśikenaivopāyamya dvādaśake śaṅkū nihantyaivamuttaratastāvaṃsau /
śaṅkoḥ pāśāvunmucya pūrvapāśamaparasminpratimuñcet /
aparaṃ pūrvasminpratimuñcet /
sa viparyāsaḥ /
viparyastayā--evaṃ kṛtayā rajjvāṃ'sau mātavyau /
tenaiva nirañjanena dakṣiṇāpasārya dvādaśake śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
tenaivodagapasārya dvādaśake śaṅkuḥ /
tāvaṃsau /
mahāvedyā mānaṃ kimirthamidamucyate /
yāvatā siddhametat? anekarajjuviharaṇavivakṣayoktamiti kecitpariharanti /
āyāmaṃ vetyasmin pakṣe dvādaśake lakṣaṇam /
pañcadaśake lakṣaṇe ca saptaviṃśatau nirañjanamiti lakṣaṇabāhulyapratipādanārthamityapare /
samacaturaśrāṇāṃ dīrghacaturaśrāṇāṃ ca viharaṇamuktam /
iha tu dīrghaviṣamacaturaśrasyetyanye /
children.translated_text: '<s>Padas</s>' is our Vedic text. Thirty <s>padas</s> or <s>prakramas</s> is the rear transverse measure. The <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure). Thirty-six is the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s> (spine-cord), the east-west line; twenty-four is the front transverse measure — thus is the Vedic text (<s>śruti</s>) regarding the <s>Soma</s> [altar]. On a cord of thirty-six: having added eighteen [to itself], throwing it over, making loops at the two ends — from the far end, starting from the west end, a mark at twelve for the shoulders, a mark at fifteen for the hips; having made the alignment. Having fixed [the cord] at the ends of the spine-cord — [proceeding] from the <s>lālāṭika</s> (forehead-post) in the middle of the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (front beam), going three <s>prakramas</s> eastward and fixing a peg, then from that, thirty-six <s>prakramas</s> ahead, fixing pegs, attaching the loops to them — having drawn southward with the fifteen[-mark], one should fix a peg. That is the south hip. Likewise, drawing northward, one should fix a peg. That is the north hip. Reversing [the loops] for the shoulders. Drawing with the fifteen[-mark] itself, one fixes pegs at the twelve[-mark] — thus the northward, those are the shoulders. 'Reversing' the loops: removing the loop from the peg and attaching the front loop to the back [peg], and the back [loop] to the front [peg] — that is the reversal. With the reversed [cord], the shoulders are to be measured. Drawing southward with the same alignment, at the twelve[-mark], one should fix a peg. Drawing northward likewise, a peg at twelve[-mark]. Those are the shoulders. Why is the measurement of the <s>mahāvedī</s> (great altar) stated, since it is already established? Some resolve this by saying it is stated with the intention of demonstrating multiple-cord extension. In the position 'the length or...': the mark at twelve and the mark at fifteen, and at twenty-seven the alignment — others say it is to demonstrate the abundance of marks. For squares and rectangles, the extension has been stated. But here, it is for an irregular rectangle — [say] others.
That [is done with] a single cord — [that is] the extension. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 5.2b ||

children.text: trikacatuṣkayoḥ pañcikākṣṇayārajjuḥ | tābhis trirabhyastābhir aṃsau | caturabhyastābhiḥśroṇī || ĀpŚus_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: For [the sides] three and four, the diagonal cord is five. With those [numbers] tripled, the shoulders [are measured]; with [those] quadrupled, the hips. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 5.3 ||

children.text:
yasya caturaśrasya trikā tiryaṅbhānī catuṣkā pārśvamānī tasyā akṣṇayā rajjuḥ pañcikā /
tābhiraṃsau mātavyau /
trikaṃ trirabhyāsayuktaṃ dvādaśa bhavanti /
catuṣkaṃ (ṣoḍaśa pañcikā) viśatiḥṣa /
yupāvaṭīyācchaṅkoḥ paścāt ṣoḍaśasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin pañcikāṃ sābhyāsaṃ pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye sābhyāsaṃ trikaṃ pratimucyāṃsāvāyacchet /
children.translated_text: From the sacrificial-post-pit peg, fixing a peg sixteen [paces] to the rear, attaching to it the five[-cord] with the extension, and attaching to the sacrificial-post-pit [peg] the three[-cord] with the extension, one should stretch [the cord] for the shoulders.
With those quadrupled, the hips.
With those very [numbers] quadrupled, the hips are to be measured.

children.text: viṃśeṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin pañcikāṃ sābhyāsaṃ pañcaviṃśatiṃ pratimucya pañcadaśikāṃ pratimucya tābhiḥśroṇī viharet //
children.translated_text: Fixing a peg at twenty, attaching to it the five[-cord] with the extension — twenty-five — and attaching the fifteen[-cord], with those one should extend the hips.

The rectangle whose transverse measure is three and lateral measure is four — its diagonal cord is five. With those [tripled], the shoulders are to be measured. Three tripled is twelve; four [tripled is] sixteen; five [tripled is] twenty.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
After the extension of the <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new- and full-moon) altar, the measurement of the <s>saumikī vedī</s> (Soma altar), which is the main topic, is stated.
(Thirty <s>padas</s> or <s>prakramas</s>... is known of the altar)
'Thirty' —
'Thirty <s>padas</s> is the rear transverse' — this is the <s>Taittirīyaka</s> Vedic text.

children.text: triṃśatprakrameti śāśāntarīyā, ato vikalpaḥ, yadyapi karmopateśaḥ prakramaśabdena prāgvaṃśasya madhyamāllālāṭikātrrīn prācaḥ prakramāniti tatrāpi śrutyorvaikalpikatvena pradarśanārthaḥ prakramaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thirty <s>prakramas</s>' is from another Vedic recension. Hence the alternative. Although the ritual instruction [uses] the word '<s>prakrama</s>' [in the context of] 'three <s>prakramas</s> from the <s>lālāṭika</s> (forehead-post) in the middle of the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s>,' even there the word '<s>prakrama</s>' is used for the purpose of demonstrating the alternative nature of the two Vedic texts.
There, '<s>prakrama</s>' is [derived from] 'that by which one strides' — thus the word '<s>prakrama</s>'.

children.text: paścāttiraśvī paścāttiryaṅbhānī prācī āyāmaḥ purastāstiraśvī tiryaṅbhānī vimānamucyate //
children.translated_text: The rear transverse is the rear <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure); the <s>prācī</s> (east-west line) is the length (<s>āyāma</s>); the front transverse is the front <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> — the measurement is stated.
(On 'a cord of thirty-six... the shoulders')
'A cord of thirty-six' —

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśikā ṣaṭtriṃśatpramāṇā rajjuḥ, tasyāmaṣṭādaśopasamasya saṃyojyāparasmāt paścimādantādārabhya dvādaśasu lakṣaṇamaṃsārthaṃ, pañcadaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ śroṇyarthaṃ, prāgvaṃśasya madhyamāllālāṭikātrrin prācaḥ prakramānatītya tataḥ purastāt ṣaṭtriṃśatpramāṇāṃ prācīṃ lekhāmālikheta sā pṛṣṭhyā tadantayoḥ śaṅku nihatya tayoḥ pāśau pratimucya pañcadaśikena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇāpāyamya śaṅkuṃ nihanti sā dakṣiṇā śroṇī, evamuttara to 'pāyamya śaṅkuḥ, sottarā śroṇī, viparyastayāṃsau viparyastapā śayāṃ'śau mātavyau /
pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamya dvādaśike śaṅkuḥ, dakṣiṇataḥ uttarataś ca tāvaṃsau /
children.translated_text: Drawing with the fifteen[-mark] itself, the peg at the twelve[-mark] — southward and northward, those are the shoulders.

children.text: nanu "tadarthamabhyasyāparasmin' itya nenaiba viharaṇenāsminviharaṇe siddhe kimarthamiha punarvacanam, ucyate--saṅkhyāpūrvāgamārthamiti kecitpariharanti, anekarajjuvivakṣayā ityanye, āyāmābhyāseṣu dvādaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ pañcadaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ saptaviṃśatyādau niraḍhañjanamiti lakṣaṇabāhulyapratipādanārthamityapare /
children.translated_text: Now, since this extension is already established by the [method] 'for that purpose, extending to the other,' etc., why is it stated again here? It is said: some resolve this by saying it is for the purpose of the prior introduction of numbers; others, with the intention of multiple-cord [extension]; yet others say it is to demonstrate the abundance of marks in length-extensions — the mark at twelve, the mark at fifteen, the alignment at twenty-seven, etc.
The extension of rectangles has been stated there.
But here it is for an irregular rectangle — [say] others.

'A cord of thirty-six' — a cord of thirty-six units in measure. On that, having added eighteen [to itself] and combining, starting from the far — the western — end, a mark at twelve for the shoulders, a mark at fifteen for the hips. Having drawn from the <s>lālāṭika</s> (forehead-post) in the middle of the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s>, going three <s>prakramas</s> eastward beyond that, then from that, ahead, drawing an east-west line of thirty-six units — that is the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s> (spine-cord). Having fixed pegs at its two ends and attaching the loops to them, having drawn southward with the fifteen[-mark], one fixes a peg — that is the south hip. Likewise, drawing northward, the peg — that is the north hip. 'Reversing [the loops] for the shoulders': the shoulders are to be measured with the reversed loops.
(On 'that, with a single cord — the extension')
'That' —

children.text: ekā cāsau rajjuśvetyekarajjuḥ, ekayaiva rajjvā śroṇyaṃsānāṃ viharaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'A single cord' (<s>ekarajju</s>) — [it is both] one and a cord. With a single cord alone, the extension of the hips and shoulders [is performed].

children.text: dviśaṅkunā triśaṅkunā pañjaśaṅkunā vā yogena yadviharaṇamuktaṃ tadidamityuktamanubhāṣate anekarajjuvidhitsayā //
children.translated_text: The extension which was stated by the method of two pegs, three pegs, or five pegs — he restates this with the intention of prescribing multiple-cord [methods].
(On 'for three and four — five is the diagonal cord')
'Three' —

children.text: trikā triprāṇā catuṣkā catuṣpramāṇā pañcikā pañcapramāṇā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Trika</s>' means of three units; '<s>catuṣka</s>' means of four units; '<s>pañcika</s>' means of five units.

'For three and four' — what is obtained by the length-extension [theorem] is restated here, for the purpose of prescribing the hips and shoulders by that extension — likewise in the subsequent extensions.
(On 'with those tripled, the shoulders')

children.text: tābhiḥ pṛthakpṛthakrirabhyastābhiḥ trirupari nikṣeptābhiḥ, trikāt trirabhyastāt dvādaśa, catuṣkātrrirabhyastāt ṣoḍaśa, pañcakāttrirabhyastāt viṃśatiḥ, tābhiraṃsau mātavyau //
children.translated_text: 'With those' — with those tripled individually, i.e., placed upon [themselves] three times: three tripled is twelve; four tripled is sixteen; five tripled is twenty. With those, the shoulders are to be measured.
(On 'with [those] quadrupled, the hips')

children.text: trikāccaturabhyastāt pañcadaśa, catuṣkādviṃśatiḥ, pañcakāt pañcaviṃśatiḥ, tābhiḥśroṇyau mātavyau /
children.translated_text: Three quadrupled is fifteen [sic, i.e., 3+3×4=15]; four [quadrupled] is twenty; five [quadrupled] is twenty-five. With those, the hips are to be measured.

children.text: yūpāvaṭīyācchaṅkoḥ paścāt ṣoḍaśasu śaṅkuṃ nnihatya tasmiṃstrirabhyastāṃ pañcikāṃ caturabhyastāṃ pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye trirabhyastāṃ trikāṃ caturabhyastāṃ pratimucya prathamanihitaśaṅkau caturabhyastāṃ trikāṃpratimucya tābhyāṃ śroṇyau, āyāmābhyāsasiddhamidam /
children.translated_text: From the sacrificial-post-pit peg, fixing a peg sixteen behind, attaching to it the tripled five[-cord, i.e., 20] and the quadrupled [five-cord, i.e., 25], and to the sacrificial-post-pit [peg] attaching the tripled three[-cord, i.e., 12] and the quadrupled [three-cord, i.e., 15], and at the first-fixed peg attaching the quadrupled three[-cord, i.e., 15] — with those two, the hips. This is established by the length-extension.
Or established by the double-length extension.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(On 'thirty <s>padas</s> or <s>prakramas</s>... is known of the altar')

children.text:
padaṃ ca dvividhamuktaṃ bodhāyanena--"daśāṅgulaṃ kṣudrapadaṃ padaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulam' iti /
dvādaśāṅgulamiti kātyāyanaḥ /
etānitrividhāni padāni laukikena padena vikalpyante /
tathā vakṣyati--"pade yuge 'radnau' ityādi /
etānyeva caturvindhāni padāni dviguṇāni triguṇāni ca prakramāḥ /
te ca saptavidhāḥ /
tatra sāgnicitye some padairvimānaṃ na labhyate agnikṣetrāsaṃbhavāt /
evaṃ saptavidhe 'gnau viṃśatyaṅgulasya nivṛttir vyākhyātā, anagnicitye tu sarveṣāmeva pradaprakramāṇāmicchayā vikalpa iti kecit /
anye punarevaṃ vyavasthāmicchanti--padaiścaturvidhairviṃśatyaṅgulena vā prakrameṇa mānamanagnicitye /
ekavidhāgnau viṃśatyaṅgulena, dvividhādiṣu pañcavidhaparyanteṣu caturviṃśatyaṅgulena, ṣaḍvidhādiṣu dvāda śavidhaparyanteṣu viṃśatyaṅgulena laukikena vā dvipadena, trayodaśavidhādiṣu ṣaṭ triṃśadaṅgulenetyādi /
sarveṣāmapi pakṣe agnayaḥ pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulena prakrameṇa saṃbhavanti /
tatrāgnyanuguṇā vede rvivṛddhiḥ kartavyā /
yṛpaiphādaśinyāṃ nyāyasya prakramāsthānīyaḥ, ekaśatavidhe aśītyaṅgula ityādi /
children.translated_text: <s>Pada</s> (foot) is of two kinds, as stated by <s>Baudhāyana</s>: 'the small <s>pada</s> is ten <s>aṅgulas</s>; the <s>pada</s> is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.' 'Twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>' [says] <s>Kātyāyana</s>. These three types of <s>padas</s> are alternative options with the common <s>pada</s>. Thus he will state: 'in <s>pada</s>, in <s>yuga</s>, in <s>aratni</s>,' etc. These same four types of <s>padas</s>, doubled and tripled, are the <s>prakramas</s> (paces). They are thus of seven types. Among these, in the fire-altar construction with <s>Soma</s>, measurement with <s>padas</s> cannot be obtained, due to the impossibility of the fire-altar area [matching]. Thus in the seven-fold fire-altar, the elimination of the twenty-<s>aṅgula</s> [<s>pada</s>] has been explained; but without fire-altar construction, there is an optional choice among all <s>padas</s> and <s>prakramas</s> — [say] some. Others wish for this arrangement: with four types of <s>padas</s> or with the twenty-<s>aṅgula</s> <s>prakrama</s>, the measurement is without fire-altar construction. In the single-fold fire, with twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>; in the double-fold and up to the five-fold, with twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; in the six-fold and up to the twelve-fold, with twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> or with the common double-<s>pada</s>; in the thirteen-fold and beyond, with thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>, etc. In all these positions, the fire-altars are possible with a <s>prakrama</s> of forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>. There, the augmentation of the altar should be made in accordance with the fire-altar. The standard for the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post) at eleven [units] would be the <s>prakrama</s>; in the hundred-fold, eighty <s>aṅgulas</s>, etc.
Now he states the extension of this altar:
(On 'a cord of thirty-six... the extension')
This is the elaboration of the measure stated as 'the measure [cord] of as much length [as desired].'
Now he states the extension of this same altar with multiple cords:
(On 'for three and four... the hips')
