children.text:
trikacatuṣkayostiryakpāśvamānyoḥ abhyastābhiḥ upakṣiptābhiḥ, yathā-- trikā trirabhyastā dvādaśikā, catuṣkā trirabhyastā ṣoḍāśekā, pañcikā trirabhyastā viṃśatikā /
etābhistisṛbhirabhyastābhiraṃsau mātavyau /
etābhireva caturabhyastābhiḥ pañcadaśikayā viṃśikayā ca śroṇī mātavye /
dvirabhyastābhirapyetābhiraṃsau mātuṃ śakyete /

children.translated_text: Everywhere, twelve [is the measure] of the shoulders.
The transverse measure [of the hips] is fifteen.
The other [measure] of the hips is on the spine-cord — the lateral measure. Thus, the extension is with six cords.
Likewise in what follows.

Of the three and four — the transverse and lateral measures — with those multiplied, i.e., placed upon [themselves]: three tripled is twelve; four tripled is sixteen; five tripled is twenty. With these three [sets of] multiplied [numbers], the shoulders are to be measured. With those same quadrupled — with fifteen and twenty — the hips are to be measured. Even with those doubled, the shoulders can be measured.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>).
At the first-fixed peg, the three[-cord] with extension.

children.text: dvādaśikāpañcikayos trayodaśikākṣṇayārajjuḥ, tābhir aṃsau dvirabhyastābhiḥ śroṇī || ĀpŚus_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: Of [a combination of] a twelve-measure and a five-measure, the diagonal cord is a thirteen-measure. By these, the shoulders [are marked]; by double of these, the haunches. || ĀpŚus 5.4 ||

children.text:
yupāvaṭīyācchaṅkoḥ paścātpañcasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin trayodaśikāṃ pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye pañcikāṃ dvādaśikāṃ ca pratimucya tābhiraṃsau mātavyau /
dvirabhyastābhiḥśroṇī /
yūpāvaṭīye trayodaśikāṃ sābhyāsāṃ pratimucya sābhyāsāṃ dvādaśikāṃ ca prathamanihate pañcikāṃ ca sābhyāsām, tābhiḥ śroṇī mātavyau /
children.translated_text: From the peg at the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> (sacrificial-post pit), to the west, having fixed a peg at five [units], fastening a thirteen-measure cord to that [peg] and a five-measure and twelve-measure cord to the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> [peg], by these the shoulders are to be measured. By double of these, the haunches. Fastening a thirteen-measure cord with its repetition to the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> [peg], and a twelve-measure with its repetition and a five-measure with its repetition to the first-fixed [peg], by these the haunches are to be measured.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
(The twelve-measure cord)
The meaning of this is clear.
(By these, the haunches)

children.text:
yūpāvaṭīyaśaṅkoḥ paścāt pañcadaśasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmiṃstrayodaśikāṃ pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye dvādaśikāṃ pratimucya tābhyāmaṃsau /
tathā prathamanihataśaṅkau dvirabhyastāṃ pañcikāṃ pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye dvirabhyastāṃ trayodaśikāṃ pratimucya tābhyāṃ śroṇyau /
children.translated_text: From the peg at the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s>, to the west at fifteen [units], having fixed a peg, fastening a thirteen-measure cord to that and a twelve-measure to the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> [peg], by these two the shoulders [are marked]. Likewise, fastening a doubled five-measure to the first-fixed peg and a doubled thirteen-measure to the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s>, by these two the haunches [are marked].
This is obtained from the half-repetition, or from the quadrupled-length repetition.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(The twelve-measure... the haunches)
By 'doubled,' [meaning] twenty-six and so on.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.
Of [a combination of] a fifteen-measure and an eight-measure, the diagonal cord is a seventeen-measure. By these, the haunches. || ĀpŚus 5.5a ||

children.text: prathamanihatācchaṅkoḥ purastādaṣṭasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin saptadaśikāmāmaṣṭikāṃ ca pratimucya prathamanihate pañcadaśikām /
children.translated_text: From the first-fixed peg, to the east at eight [units], having fixed a peg, fastening a seventeen-measure and an eight-measure cord to that, and a fifteen-measure to the first-fixed [peg],
by these, the haunches.
Of [a combination of] a twelve-measure and a thirty-five-measure, the diagonal cord is a thirty-seven-measure. By these, the shoulders. || ĀpŚus 5.5b ||

children.text: prathamanihatācchaṅkoḥ purastātprakrame śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin saptātriṃśikāṃ pañcatriṃśikāṃ ca pratimucya yūpāvaṭīye dvādaśikām /
children.translated_text: From the first-fixed peg, to the east at one <s>prakrama</s> (pace), having fixed a peg, fastening a thirty-seven-measure and a thirty-five-measure cord to that, and a twelve-measure to the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> [peg],
by these, the shoulders are to be measured.
These many altar-expansions are to be known. || ĀpŚus 5.6 ||

children.text:
etāvantyeva śuddhamūlāni jñātuṃ śakyāni vediviharaṇāni bhavanti /
anye śuddhamūlāḥ kalpayitumaśakyāḥ /
tasmādetāvantītyavadhāryante--
children.translated_text: These many altar-expansions having pure [rational] roots can be known. Other pure roots cannot be devised. Therefore, these many are determined —
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
(The fifteen-measure... the haunches)

children.text: prathamanihataśaṅkau pañcadaśikā, tataḥ purastādaṣṭāsu saptadaśikā, tābhyāṃ śroṇyau /
children.translated_text: At the first-fixed peg, a fifteen-measure; from there to the east at eight [units], a seventeen-measure; by these two, the haunches.
This is obtained from the tripled-length repetition, or from the repetition of the length-third and two.
(The twelve-measure... by these the shoulders)

children.text:
dvādaśiketi /
idamapi gatārtham /
yūpāvaṭīye dvādaśikā, prathamanihataśaṅkoḥ purastātprakramamātre śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin saptatriṃśikā, tābyāmaṃsau, pañcamadvayābhyāsaprāptamidaṃ, pañcaguṇābhyāsaptāptaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: 'Twelve-measure' — this too is understood. At the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s>, a twelve-measure; from the first-fixed peg to the east at one <s>prakrama</s> measure, having fixed a peg, fastening a thirty-seven-measure to it; by these two, the shoulders. This is obtained from the five-double repetition, or from the five-fold repetition.
(These many... are to be known)
'These many' —

children.text:
śuddhamūlatay.ā jñātuṃ śakyāni etāvantye vetyavadhāraṇā /
etāvantyuktāni, anyānyapi unneyāni, sacchedābhiḥ rajjubhirnirhrāsavṛddhibhyāṃ ca vediviharaṇāni bhavantyeva, yadyapi idaṃ viharaṇamekarajjvā dvisayogenaiva vyākhyatam, tathā tri śaṅkupañcaśaṅkubhtyāmapi nirhrāsavṛddhibhyāṃ yathā yogaṃ vihartavyaḥ, itarathā tayorvidhānasyādṛṣṭārthatvakalpanāprasaṅgāt, ato nidarśanametat sarvaviharaṇānām /
children.translated_text: The determination is that 'these many can be known' due to having pure roots. These many have been stated; others too can be derived. With cut-cords, through diminution and increase, altar-expansions indeed exist. Although this expansion has been explained with a single cord by a two-peg method, likewise with three pegs and five pegs also, through diminution and increase, the expansion should be performed as appropriate; otherwise, there would be the objection of purposelessness in their prescription. Therefore, this is an illustration for all expansions.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary].
(The fifteen-measure... are to be known)
Without cuts, these many. With cuts, many others too exist, such as:

Of a half-twelve-measure and a half-four-measure, the diagonal cord is a half-thirteen-measure; by these, the shoulders. Of a fifteen-measure and an eleven-and-quarter-measure, the diagonal cord is a nineteen-less-a-quarter-measure; by these, the haunches — and so on.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.
A thousand <s>padas</s> (units of measure) less twenty-eight is the <s>mahāvedī</s> (great altar). || ĀpŚus 5.7a ||

children.text:
navaśatāni dvisaptatiś ca (972) padakramāṇi prakramapramā ṇāni vā caturaśrāṇi mahāvedeḥ /
mahadrahaṇaṃ kimartham? padapramitāyāṃ mahāvedyāṃ sadohavirdhānādīnāmapi padanevai mānārthaṃ, prakramamitāyāmaratniprakramaireva navāratniḥ tiryaṅbhānatyiratnimānaṃ sadaso vihitam /
navāratni tiryagiti niyatapramāṇavidhānāt aratninaina vidhānamanumīyate /
tathā havirdhānasya tryaratni vistāraṃ navāratnayāyāmamityanumīyate /
tatkathaṃ padena tayor mānaṃ labhyate ityucyate, catvāriṃśadadhikāni pañcadaśāṅgulamiti vacanāt /
sadasaḥ paścāt pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulaṃ ṣoḍasādhikaṃ śatadvayaṃ sadohavirdhānayormadhyaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulaṃ ṣoḍaśādhikaṃ śatadvayaṃ sadohavirdhānayormadhyaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśatsaṃcaraḥ /
havirdhānasya ṣoḍaśādhikaṃ śathadvayam /
avaśiṣṭamaṣṭādaśāṅgulam /
tasmāduttaravedisadohavirdhānānāṃ antarvedyasaṃbhavāt vṛddhiḥ kalpanīyā /
aratnervā hrāsaḥ kalpanīyaḥ /
tadubhayamacoditaṃ bhavati /
atoyena vedirmitā tenaiva teṣāṃ mānārthaṃ pahadrahaṇaṃ sthitam /
children.translated_text: Nine hundred and seventy-two (972) <s>pada</s>-measures or <s>prakrama</s>-measures, square, constitute the <s>mahāvedī</s>. What is the purpose of the word 'great'? When the <s>mahāvedī</s> is measured in <s>padas</s>, the <s>sadas</s> (assembly shed) and <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation shed) etc. are also to be measured in <s>padas</s> only, not in <s>aratnis</s> (cubits). When measured in <s>prakramas</s>, the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> are prescribed by <s>aratni</s>-<s>prakramas</s>: the <s>sadas</s> is nine <s>aratnis</s> in the transverse dimension with a width of nine <s>aratnis</s>. Since the transverse measure of nine <s>aratnis</s> is a prescribed fixed measure, the <s>aratni</s>-based prescription is inferred. Similarly, the <s>havirdhāna</s> is inferred to have a breadth of three <s>aratnis</s> and a length of nine <s>aratnis</s>. How then is the measurement of those obtained by <s>padas</s>? It is said: 'forty plus fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>' — thus. Behind the <s>sadas</s>, forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>; two hundred and sixteen [is] the interval between the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s>; forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>; two hundred and sixteen [is] the interval between the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s>; forty-five is the passage. The <s>havirdhāna</s> is two hundred and sixteen. The remainder is eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. Therefore, since the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar), <s>sadas</s>, and <s>havirdhāna</s> are contained within the altar, an increase must be devised. Or, a decrease of the <s>aratni</s> must be devised. Both of those are unprescribed. Therefore, the word 'great' stands for the purpose of measuring those by whatever [unit] the altar is measured.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
(Twenty-eight less... the <s>mahāvedī</s>)

children.text:
dvisaptatiḥ navaśatāni ca padaparimitāni kṣetrāṇi mahāvodeḥ, prakramamāne 'pyevam /
padagrahaṇaṃ kimarthaṃ, ucyate--padagrahaṇamahadvrahaṇāmyāmetat jñāyate--vedyāḥ padena māne sadohavirdhānayo rapi padena mānaṃ nāratnibhiḥ, uttaravediś ca yugamātrī na sarvato daśapadeti prakramamitāyāṃ vedyāmaratnivihitayoḥsadohavirdhānayoḥsarvato daśapadāyā uttaravedeśvāsaṃbhavāt padenaiva sadohavirdhāna. yorvimāna yugamātrottaravediriti siddham /
saṃkhyānaprayojanam vodantṛtīye yajata ityādiṣu /
children.translated_text: Seventy-two plus nine hundred <s>pada</s>-measured fields constitute the <s>mahāvedī</s>; likewise in <s>prakrama</s> measure. What is the purpose of the word '<s>pada</s>'? It is said — by the word '<s>pada</s>' and the word 'great,' this is understood: the altar is to be measured by <s>padas</s>, and the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> too are to be measured by <s>padas</s>, not by <s>aratnis</s>. And the <s>uttaravedī</s> is of one <s>yuga</s> (yoke-length), not 'ten <s>padas</s> on all sides.' Since, when the altar is measured in <s>prakramas</s>, the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> prescribed by <s>aratnis</s> and a ten-<s>pada</s> <s>uttaravedī</s> on all sides would be impossible, it is established that the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> are to be measured by <s>padas</s> and the <s>uttaravedī</s> is of one <s>yuga</s> measure. The purpose of enumeration is in [passages like] 'one should sacrifice at the third of the altar,' etc.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary].
(Twenty-eight less... the <s>mahāvedī</s>)
The word '<s>pada</s>' is also an indication of <s>prakrama</s>.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: dakṣiṇasmād aṃsād dvādaśasu dakṣiṇasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ nipātayet | chedaṃ viparyasyottarata upadadhyāt | sā dīrghā caturaśrā | tathā yuktāṃ saṃcakṣīta || ĀpŚus_5.7b ||
children.translated_text: From the southern shoulder, at twelve [units], one should drop [a line] on the southern haunch. Reversing the cut, one should place it on the north. That is an oblong rectangle. Thus one should compute it. || ĀpŚus 5.7b ||

children.text:
dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādārabhya dvādaśasveva śroṇyāṃ vipādayet /
trīṇi padāni śroṇideśe, viparyasyottarasminnaṃse manasā sthāpayet /
evaṃ kṛte saptaviṃśativistārā ṣaṭtriṃśadāyatā dīrghacaturaśrā bhavati /
tathābhūtāṃ vediṃ saptaviṃśatiṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatyā guṇite sati aṣṭāviṃśatyūnapadasahasraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Starting from the southern shoulder, one should drop [a line] on the haunch at exactly twelve [units]. Three <s>padas</s> at the haunch region — reversing, one should place [the cut] mentally on the northern shoulder. When thus done, it becomes an oblong rectangle of twenty-seven in width and thirty-six in length. Multiplying twenty-seven by thirty-six for the altar thus constituted, it becomes a thousand <s>padas</s> less twenty-eight.

children.text: saumikyā veditṛtīyadeśe yajeteti sautrāmaṇyā veder vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_5.8a ||
children.translated_text: In [the ritual] where 'one should sacrifice at the third portion of the altar' is known for the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, it is understood from the <s>Saumikī</s> (Soma) altar. || ĀpŚus 5.8a ||

children.text:
veditṛtīye yajeteti dārśikapāśalakayoraśaṃbhavātsaumikaṃ labhyate /
ataḥsaumikyā ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Since [the instruction] 'one should sacrifice at the third of the altar' cannot apply to the <s>Dārśikapāśala</s> [rituals], it pertains to the <s>Saumikī</s>. Therefore 'by the <s>Saumikī</s>' is stated.

children.text: prakramāsya dvikaraṇī prakramasthānīyā bhavati trikaraṇyā vā || ĀpŚus_5.8b ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (square root of 2) of a <s>prakrama</s> serves in place of a <s>prakrama</s>, or the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (square root of 3). || ĀpŚus 5.8b ||

children.text:
tṛtīyakaraṇī prakramasthānā, sthānāntādvibhāṣeti chapratyayaḥ /
tṛtīyakaraṇīṃ prakramaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāmityādinā viharet /
tṛtīyakaraṇyā vā vakṣyamāṇena vidhinā /
children.translated_text: The <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> (third-root, i.e., square root of 3) serves in the place of a <s>prakrama</s>; from another position, the optional <s>ca</s>-suffix [applies]. Having made the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> the <s>prakrama</s>, one should expand with 'the thirty-six-measure' and so on. Or [one may proceed] with the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> by the method to be stated.

children.text: aṣṭikā daśiketi tiryaṅmānyau | dvādaśikā pṛṣṭhayā || ĀpŚus_5.8c ||
children.translated_text: An eight-measure is the eastern transverse, a ten-measure [the western transverse]. A twelve-measure is the spine (longitudinal axis). || ĀpŚus 5.8c ||

children.text:
aṣṭikā purastāttiryaṅbhānī /
dvādaśikā pṛṣṭhayā /
dvādaśasu ṣaḍupasamasyāparasmādantātpañcasu lakṣaṇaṃ caturṣu lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhayāntayorantau niyamya pañcakena dakṣiṇā pasārya śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evamuttarataste śroṇī /
viparyastayāṃsau /
pañcakena dakṣiṇāpāyamya caturṣu śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evamuttaratastāvaṃsau bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: The eight-measure is the eastern transverse measure. The twelve-measure is the spine. Joining six to twelve, from the far end at five [units], making a mark at four [units], having fixed the end-points of the spine, extending to the south by five, one should fix a peg. Likewise to the north — those are the haunches. Reversing, the shoulders. Extending to the south by five, and [fixing a peg] at four — likewise to the north — those become the shoulders.

children.text: trīṇi caturviṃśāni padaśatāni sautrāmaṇikī vediḥ || ĀpŚus_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: Three [groups of] twenty-four — [i.e.,] seven hundred and twenty <s>pada</s>-measures — constitute the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> altar. || ĀpŚus 5.9 ||

children.text: dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādārabhya caturṣvava dakṣiṇasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ vipātya śeṣaṃ viparyasyetyādi pūrvāvat /
children.translated_text: Starting from the southern shoulder, dropping [a line] at exactly four [units] on the southern haunch, reversing the remainder — and so on, as before.
It becomes twelve <s>padas</s> in width and twelve <s>padas</s> in length — thus one should compute it.

children.text: dvistāvā vedir bhavatīty aśvamedhe vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_5.10 ||
children.translated_text: The altar becomes double in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) — this is known. || ĀpŚus 5.10 ||
Double of what? Of the <s>Saumikī</s>, since it is the current topic and since it is the prototype.
Thus ends the fifth chapter.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.

children.text: kṣetratṛtīyagrahaṇaṃ na pramāṇamiti tṛtīyagrahaṇamiti kathaṃ saṃkhyāyāta ityata āha--
children.translated_text: Since the taking of a third of the field is not [itself] a measure, how is 'the taking of a third' to be computed? To this he says —
From the southern shoulder... one should compute it.

children.text:
vedyā dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādārabhya dvādaśasu dakṣiṇasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ lekhā nipātayedrajjuṃ vā tāṃ nipātya tabdahiśchindyāt /
lekhāyā bahirbhūtaṃ chedaṃ viparyasya--viparyāsaṃ kṛtvā itarataḥ--itarasmāt pārśve sthāpayedevaṃ saptaviṃśativistārā ṣaṭtriṃśadāyatā dīrghacaturaśrā vedirbhavati, tathā yuktāṃ tathā bhūtāṃ gaṇayet /
etena viṣamacaturaśrāṇāṃ saṃkhyānaprakāro veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Starting from the southern shoulder of the altar, at twelve [units] one should drop a line or cord on the southern haunch; having dropped it, one should cut outside it. The portion outside the line — having reversed it, i.e., having made the reversal — on the other side, one should place [it]. Thus it becomes an oblong rectangle twenty-seven in width and thirty-six in length. One should compute — one should calculate — it thus constituted. By this, the method of computing irregular quadrilaterals is to be understood.
In connection with the altar, modifications are stated —
(From the <s>Saumikī</s>... is understood.)

children.text: sutrāmadaivatyā sautrāmaṇī, tasyā veditṛtīye yajeta iti śrūyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> has <s>Sutrāman</s> as its deity. [The instruction is:] 'One should sacrifice at the third of its (<s>Saumikī</s>) altar.'

children.text: vedyāstṛtīyo deśaḥ veditṛtīyadeśaḥ, sa kasyāḥ, saumikyāḥ, kimodanaṃ śālīnāṃ saktvāḍhakaparimitānāmiti vat //
children.translated_text: The 'third portion of the altar' is the third region of the altar. Of which [altar]? Of the <s>Saumikī</s>. As in 'an <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of <s>śālī</s> (rice) husked grains,' etc.
(The <s>prakrama</s>... the spine.)

children.text:
prakramatṛtīyakaraṇī vyākhyātā prakramāsthānīyā bhavati /
"sthānāntādvibhāṣā' ityādinā svārthe chapratyayaḥ /
tathā ṣaṭtriṃśatikāyāmityādinā kaumikavadvimānaṃ trikaraṇī coktā, aṣṭikādaśike tiryaṅbhānyā dvādaśikā pṛṣṭhayā tatpakṣe aṣṭapramāṇā purastāta tiryak, daśapramāṇā paścāttiryak, dvādaśāyāmaḥ dvādaśikāyāṃ ṣaḍupasamasya catusṛṣu pañcasu lakṣaṇaṃ pañcasu śroṇyā catasṛṣvaṃsau /
veditṛtīyatvaṃ kṣetrata ityāha- (triṇi caturviṃśāni padaśatāni sautrāmaṇikī vodiḥ.)
children.translated_text: The <s>prakrama</s>-<s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> has been explained as serving in place of a <s>prakrama</s>. By 'from another position' etc., the <s>ca</s>-suffix is in its own sense [i.e., optionally]. Likewise, the measurement is stated with 'the thirty-six-measure' etc., as for the <s>Saumikī</s>. The <s>trikaraṇī</s> is also stated: the eastern transverse is eight-measured, the western transverse is ten-measured, the twelve-measure is the length. In the twelve-measure, joining six, [making] a mark at four and at five, at five the haunches, at four the shoulders. The third-of-the-altar property is from the field — he says: (Three [groups of] twenty-four <s>pada</s>-measures — the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> altar.)

children.text:
caturviṃśatyadhikāni trīṇi śatāni sautrāmaṇikī vediḥ /
dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādityādi saumikavat /
prakramasya tṛtīyakaraṇīti darśanāt, atrāpi padaprakramau vikalpitau /
prakamaśabdenopakramya padaśabdenopasaṃhārādanyatrāpyaṣṭāsu prakrameṣvityādiṣu padenāpi vimānaṃ labhyata iti sūcitam /
children.translated_text: Three hundred and twenty-four constitute the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> altar. 'From the southern shoulder' — and so on, as for the <s>Saumikī</s>. From the statement that 'the <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s> of a <s>prakrama</s>,' here too <s>pada</s> and <s>prakrama</s> are optionally used. By beginning with the word '<s>prakrama</s>' and concluding with the word '<s>pada</s>,' it is indicated that elsewhere too, in 'at eight <s>prakramas</s>' etc., measurement by <s>padas</s> is also obtainable.
(The altar becomes double... in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> — is understood.)

children.text:
prakṛtatvāt prakṛtitvācca saumikyā eva dvistāvā--dviguṇā vediraśvamedhe bhavati, paśugaṇasaṃbandhādyūpānāṃ codakaprāptarathākṣamātrāntarālatā pratyakṣavihitadvistāvavacanāt bādhyate /
ato 'trayathā saṃbhavāntarālā eva ekaviṃśatiyūpāḥ /
tristāvānnītvā tripadakramaḥ dvistāvā /
yūpaikādaśinī pakṣe vedivivṛddhirbhavatītyeva /
children.translated_text: Since it is the current topic and since it is the prototype, the <s>Saumikī</s> alone becomes double — twofold — as the altar in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>. Due to the connection with the group of sacrificial animals, the distance between <s>yūpas</s> (sacrificial posts), which by injunction should be of one chariot-axle length, is overridden by the explicitly prescribed 'double' statement. Therefore, at whatever intervals are possible, the twenty-one <s>yūpas</s> [are placed]. Tripled and then reduced to three <s>pada-kramas</s> gives double. In the view of the eleven-<s>yūpa</s> [arrangement], it is precisely an increase of the altar.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
He states the method of computation —
(From the southern shoulder... one should compute it.)

children.text:
dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādārabhyāparānte pṛṣṭhacāyā dakṣiṇato dvādaśasu rajjuṃ nipātayet /
taddakṣiṇataśchedaṃ dīrghaṃ trikoṇaṃ manasā viparyasya uttarapārśva upadadhayāt, sā ṣaṭtriṃśitprācikā saptaviṃśativyāsā dīrghacaturaśrā bhavati, tathābhūtāṃ gaṇayet /
saptaviṃśatiṣaṭtriṃśatoḥsaṃvarge kṛte nava śatāni dvisaptatiś ca bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Beginning from the southern shoulder, at the far end, the shadow of the spine to the south — one should cast the cord at twelve [units]. Mentally reversing the long triangle cut to the south thereof and placing it on the northern side, it becomes a rectangle of thirty-six [units] in length and twenty-seven in breadth; one should calculate it as being of that form. When the product of twenty-seven and thirty-six is made, it becomes nine hundred and seventy-two.
(Of the <s>Saumikī</s> [altar].)

children.text: prakramāgrahaṇaṃ padasyāpyupalakṣaṇam, evaṃ padaśatānīti pada grahaṇaṃ prakramasyopalakṣaṇamiti śeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: The non-mention of '<s>prakrama</s>' serves as an indication of '<s>pada</s>' (foot) also; similarly, the mention of '<s>pada</s>' in 'hundreds of <s>padas</s>' serves as an indication of '<s>prakrama</s>' too — that is the remainder.
(Or by the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (√3) of the spine.)

children.text: daśāṅgulapadasya trikaraṇī saptadaśāṅgulayaḥ ekādaśa tilāś ca aṃ? 7 ti 11 dvādaśā ṅgulasya viṃśatyaṅgulayaḥ saptaviṃśatitirāś ca aṃ 20 ti 27 pañcadaśāṅgulasya tilonaṣaḍviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>trikaraṇī</s> (√3) of a <s>pada</s> of ten <s>aṅgulas</s> is seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> and eleven <s>tilas</s> [notation: aṃ 7 ti 11]. Of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>: twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-seven <s>tilas</s> [notation: aṃ 20 ti 27]. Of fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>: twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> minus a <s>tila</s>.
Similarly for <s>prakramas</s> also, it should be observed.
(Three [hundred]: the <s>Sautrāmaṇikī</s> altar.)
This [altar measurement] is also for the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> fires.
'The altar becomes twice as large' — this is known in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice).
Thus the fifth chapter.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.
The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (√2) of the <s>prakrama</s> takes the place of the <s>prakrama</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.1]

children.text: dvikaraṇyā pramāṇatṛtīyena vardhayedityādinā vardhitena tadeva viharaṇam /
children.translated_text: By the <s>dvikaraṇī</s>, increased by a third of the <s>pramāṇa</s> etc. [as previously stated] — the same construction [is applied] with that [increased measure].

children.text: prakramo dvipadastripado vā | prakrame yāthākāmī śabdārthasya viśayitvāt || ĀpŚus_6.2a ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prakrama</s> (step) is of two <s>padas</s> (feet) or three <s>padas</s>. In the <s>prakrama</s>, there is freedom of choice, because of the multiplicity of the word's meaning. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.2a]

children.text:
dvipadastriṃśadaṅgulaḥ /
tripadaḥ pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulaḥ /
padaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulamiti vacanād /
kāma icchā /
yathākāma eva yāthākāmī yathecchā tathā gṛhṇīyāt /
prakrame 'dhyardhaprakramo viprakṛṣṭaprakrama iti naivamanvarthasaṃjñā /
padādhikasya mānārthasya vācako yathā yaugikaḥ tathā dvipadaṃ tripadaṃ vā vakti, krāmatyaneneti kramaḥ /
prakṛṣṭaḥ kramaḥ iti nirūḍhaḥ, kalpanārthadravye vacanātpadādhikaṃ prakrama iti śabdārthasya viśayitvāt viśayitvaṃ kalpitārthānāmapi vācakatvādanekavācakatvaṃ /
śabdārthānāṃ viśayitvaṃ yataḥ, kasya padādayo grahītavyāḥ ityāha--
children.translated_text: 'Of two <s>padas</s>' means thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>. 'Of three <s>padas</s>' means forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>. Because of the statement 'a <s>pada</s> is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.' '<s>Kāma</s>' means 'desire.' '<s>Yāthākāmī</s>' means 'according to one's desire' — one should adopt whichever one wishes. In the <s>prakrama</s>, 'one-and-a-half <s>prakramas</s>' or 'extended <s>prakrama</s>' — these are not etymological designations. Just as a word etymologically denoting 'that which exceeds a <s>pada</s>' [as a measure-term] states two <s>padas</s> or three <s>padas</s>: '<s>krama</s>' means 'that by which one steps.' '<s>Prakrama</s>' means 'an excellent step' in conventional usage. Because of the statement [assigning meanings] to the word in the context of conventional meaning-substance, a <s>prakrama</s> is [whatever] exceeds a <s>pada</s>. The 'multiplicity' of the word's meaning is [the fact that it] denotes multiple [values], being expressive of conventional meanings as well. Since there is multiplicity of the word's meanings, [the question arises:] whose <s>pada</s> etc. should be taken? He says —

children.text: yajamānasyādhvaryorvā | eṣa hi ceṣṭānāṃ kartā bhavati || ĀpŚus_6.2b ||
children.translated_text: Of the sacrificer or of the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest). For he is the performer of the ritual acts. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.2b]

children.text:
yajamānasya padaṃ grāhyaṃ svāmitvāt /
adhvaryorvā--vāśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau /
na yajamānasya /
adhvaryureva kutaḥ? eṣa hi ceṣṭānāṃ kartā bhavati /
ceṣṭayanta iti ceṣṭāḥ karmāṇi /
sa karmaṇāṃ kartā yataḥ hiśabdo hetau /
tasmādadhvaryoreva na yajamānasya /
children.translated_text: The <s>pada</s> of the sacrificer should be taken, because of ownership. 'Or of the <s>adhvaryu</s>' — the word 'or' is for the exclusion of the [other] alternative. Not [the foot] of the sacrificer [but rather] of the <s>adhvaryu</s> alone. Why? 'For he is the performer of the ritual acts.' '<s>Ceṣṭā</s>' means 'those which are performed' — rituals. He is the performer of rituals; since the word 'hi' (for) denotes reason — therefore of the <s>adhvaryu</s> alone, not of the sacrificer.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary.
(The <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>prakrama</s>... takes its place.)

children.text: dvistāvāyāṃ vedyāṃ aśvamedhe prakraprasya dvikariṇī prakramasthāne bhavati pramāṇadvikaraṇyā viharet /
children.translated_text: In the altar that is twice as large, in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>prakrama</s> takes the place of the <s>prakrama</s>; one should construct with the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the <s>pramāṇa</s>.
(The <s>prakrama</s>... multiplicity of meaning.)

children.text:
padaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulam. dvipadaṃ triṃśadaṅgulam. tripadaṃ pañca catvāriṃśadaṅgulam, dvipade tripade ca prakramavyavahārādubhayamiha grāhyam /
athavā prakramaḥ padavikṣepavācī, padādayo 'tra māna sādhanabhūtā gṛhyante /
ato na vikṣepamātreṇa prayojanam /
kinatu tatmaṃbandhinā kenaciddravyoṇa, ato vikṣepaphalabhūtasaṃyogavibhāgābhyāmupalakṣitadeśāntarālaparimitarajjvādinā prayojanam, gacchan hi sarvo janaḥ ekaṃ padaṃ vikṣipya nidadhāti, tatra nirvikāraṃ saṃgacchana samaḥ puruṣaḥ, sthitanidhīyamānayoḥ padayorantarālaṃ yathā padaparimitaṃ bhavati tathā gacchati, ato vikṣiptena padena padadvayaṃ vyābtamiti dvipadaḥ prakramaḥ, sthitamapi padaṃ tatsahakārīti tābhyāṃ padatrayavyāptestripadaś ca bhavati /
prakrame yāthākāmīkāma icchā, tadanatikramo yathākāmam, tasya bhāvaḥ yathākāmyam, yātākāmyameva yāthākāmī--yatheṣṭamityarthaḥ, vividhaṃ śeta iti viśaya, ubhayatra prayogo dṛśyata ityarthaḥ /
nanu prakrameṣu vaiṣamyamapi dṛśyate, yathā caturo viṣṇukramām prācaḥ krāmatyuttaramuttaraṃ jyāyāṃsamiti /
nāyaṃ doṣa, tasya vacanasyotta rottaraṃ jyāyastvavidhiparatvāt, prakrame gṛhyamāṇe dvipadameva tripadameva vā gṛhṇīyāt, na miśrayedityarthaḥ, caturo viṣṇukamānityatra vācanikatvāt kramavaiṣamyasya na kramavaiṣamyānuyogaḥ /
ato viśeṣitaprakamavidhau dvitripadaprakamayorevānyataraṃ kṛhṇīyānna miśrayedityarthaḥ /
padādisūtre vakṣyamāṇaḥ padavikalpanibandhanaḥ prakramayorapi vikalpo bhavatītyeva /
children.translated_text: A <s>pada</s> is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. Two <s>padas</s> are thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Three <s>padas</s> are forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>. Since both two-<s>pada</s> and three-<s>pada</s> [measures] are used as '<s>prakrama</s>' [in different traditions], both should be taken here. Alternatively, <s>prakrama</s> denotes the 'casting of a step,' and <s>pada</s> etc. are taken here as the means of measurement. Therefore the purpose is not merely the stepping itself, but [is served] by some substance connected with that [step] — hence the purpose is [served] by a cord etc. of the measured interval between the positions marked by the conjunction and disjunction resulting from the step. For every person while walking casts one foot forward and places it; therein, the normal person walking without distortion — the interval between the stationary and the placed feet is a <s>pada</s>-measure — thus he walks. Hence, by the cast foot, two <s>padas</s> are spanned — thus a two-<s>pada</s> <s>prakrama</s>. The stationary foot too is an auxiliary of that — by those [two], three <s>padas</s> are spanned, thus a three-<s>pada</s> [<s>prakrama</s>]. In the <s>prakrama</s>, '<s>yāthākāmī</s>' — '<s>kāma</s>' is desire; non-transgression of that is <s>yathākāmam</s>; its state is <s>yāthākāmya</s>; <s>yāthākāmī</s> is <s>yāthākāmya</s> itself — meaning 'as one wishes.' '<s>Viśaya</s>' means '[the word] operates in various ways' — meaning: usage is seen in both senses. Now, irregularity is also seen in <s>prakramas</s>, as in: 'he takes four steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s> eastward, each successively larger.' This is no defect, because that statement has the purpose of prescribing successively increasing [steps]. When a <s>prakrama</s> is adopted, one should adopt only two-<s>pada</s> or only three-<s>pada</s> — one should not mix [them] — that is the meaning. In 'four steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' the irregularity of steps is [merely] verbal [i.e., prescribed for that specific context]; one does not question step-irregularity [in general]. Therefore, in the rule for a specified <s>prakrama</s>, one should adopt one or the other of the two-<s>pada</s> or three-<s>pada</s> <s>prakramas</s> — one should not mix — that is the meaning. The option regarding <s>pada</s>-alternatives to be stated in the <s>pada</s>-sūtra applies to the <s>prakramas</s> as well — just so.
(Of the sacrificer... takes its place.)

children.text:
cajamānādhvaryū prasiddhau, hi śabdo hetau, ceṣṭanta iti ceṣṭāḥ, karmāṇi /
ayamarthaḥ padādayo yajamānasya grāhyāḥ svāmitvāt, kutaḥ, yāthākāmirvāt, tasya adhvaryorvā /
vāśabdo vikalpārthaḥ /
yasmādeṣo 'dhvaryuśveṣṭānāṃ kartā bhavati tasmādasya padādayo grāhyāḥ ceṣṭākartṛtvāt, yajamānasya prāptayarthaṃ vacanamadhvaryostu bādhakavādhanārthamato vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sacrificer and the <s>adhvaryu</s> are well-known [persons]. The word 'hi' denotes reason. '<s>Ceṣṭante</s>' means 'they are performed' — rituals. The meaning is: the <s>pada</s> etc. should be taken from the sacrificer, because of ownership. Why? Because of the freedom of choice. Or of the <s>adhvaryu</s>. The word 'or' is for the purpose of option. Since this <s>adhvaryu</s> is the performer of the ritual acts, therefore his <s>pada</s> etc. should be taken, because of performer-status. The statement about the sacrificer is for what is already established [by proximity]; but for the <s>adhvaryu</s>, it is for the purpose of overriding [the default] — hence the option.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(The <s>prakrama</s>... multiplicity of meaning.)

children.text:
śabdārthasya--śabdapravṛttinimittasya viśayitvaṃ--anekavṛttitvam /
idaṃ prakame yāthākāmyaṃ śabdārthasya viśayitvāduktamityarthaḥ /
"dvipadaḥ prakamaḥ' iti bodhāyanaḥ /
"tripadaḥ prakramaḥ' iti kātyāyanaḥ /
ubhayamapyācāryasyānumatamiti vijñāyate /
children.translated_text: 'Of the word's meaning' — of the cause of the word's application — 'multiplicity' — multiple usage. The meaning is: this freedom of choice regarding the <s>prakrama</s> is stated because of the multiplicity of the word's meaning. '<s>Bodhāyana</s> [says]: the <s>prakrama</s> is of two <s>padas</s>.' '<s>Kātyāyana</s> [says]: the <s>prakrama</s> is of three <s>padas</s>.' It is understood that both are approved by the [present] teacher.
(Of the sacrificer or of the <s>adhvaryu</s>.)
The <s>prakrama</s> should be taken by the foot or by <s>aṅgulas</s>, because of ownership. He states the reason —
(For he... takes its place.)
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.

children.text: rathamātrī nirūḍhapaśubandhasya vedir bhavatīti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_6.3a ||
children.translated_text: 'The altar of the established <s>paśubandha</s> (animal-sacrifice) is of chariot-measure' — this is known [from scripture]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.3a]
'The altar of the established <s>paśubandha</s> is of chariot-measure' — this is the <s>Śruti</s> (scriptural statement).

children.text: tasya khalvāhū rathākṣamātrī paścāt tiryag īṣayā prācī | vipathayugena purastāt || ĀpŚus_6.3b ||
children.translated_text: Of that, indeed, they say: the rear breadth is of axle-measure; the length is by the pole; the front breadth is by the <s>vipatha</s>-yoke. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.3b]

children.text:
khaluśabdo 'laṅkāre /
tatra tasminnarthe rathapramāṇavido rathakārā āhuḥ /
rathākṣamātrī paścāt tiryagīṣayā prācī, vipathayugena purastāt, rathākṣaṇātrī paścāttiryaṅnānī /
rathagrahaṇaṃ śakaṭanivṛcyartham /
īṣāmātrī pṛṣṭhayā /
vipathayugena--vyāptaḥ panthā yena yugena tadvipathayugam /
abyantaraṃ yugachidrayorantarālam /
tatpramāṇaṃ purastāttiryaṅbhānī /
children.translated_text: The word 'khalu' (indeed) is ornamental. There, in that matter, the chariot-makers who know the chariot's measure say: the rear breadth is of axle-measure; the length is by the pole; the front breadth is by the <s>vipatha</s>-yoke. 'Of axle-measure in the rear' — the rear breadth. The mention of 'chariot' is for excluding a cart (<s>śakaṭa</s>). 'By the pole' — the spine [length]. '<s>Vipatha-yuga</s>' — the yoke by which the path is spanned is the <s>vipatha-yuga</s> (traveling-yoke). The inner [measurement] is the interval between the two yoke-holes. That measure is the front breadth.
Or by whatever [measure] the outer holes [of the yoke are set]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.3c]

children.text: yāvatā pramāṇena yugasya bāhye chidre bhavataḥ tāvadvā purastāttiryaṅbhānī vedeḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever measure by which the outer holes of the yoke exist — that is alternatively the front breadth of the altar.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary.
(Of chariot-measure... outer holes.)

children.text:
rathamātrī--rathapramāṇā nirūḍhapaśubandhasya vediriti śrutiḥ /
śrutyuktamabhiyuktoktayā darśayati /
children.translated_text: 'Of chariot-measure' — of chariot-<s>pramāṇa</s> — 'the altar of the established <s>paśubandha</s>' — this is the <s>Śruti</s>. He shows the scriptural statement through the words of the experts.

children.text:
khaluśabdo vākyālaṅkārārthaḥ /
tatrāhurabhiyuktāḥ--rathākṣamātrī rathapramāṇā paścāttiryaktiraśvī īṣayā saṃmitā prācī /
vyāptaḥ panthā yena sa vipathaḥ cāraṇaratha ityarthaḥ /
vipathasya yugo vipathayugaḥ /
tena saṃmitā purastāttiraśvī /
athavā yāvatā vā bāhye chidre yāvatā pramāṇena gṛhīte bāhye cchidre bhavataḥ tāvatī vā purastāttiryak /
children.translated_text: The word 'khalu' is for the purpose of sentence-ornamentation. There the experts say: 'Of axle-measure, of chariot-<s>pramāṇa</s>' — the rear breadth; 'measured by the pole' — the length. 'That whose path is spanned is <s>vipatha</s>' — meaning 'a traveling chariot.' The yoke of the <s>vipatha</s> is the <s>vipatha-yuga</s>. Measured by that — the front breadth. Alternatively, 'or by whatever the outer holes' — by whatever measure, when taken, the outer holes exist — that is alternatively the front breadth.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(Of chariot-measure... outer holes.)

children.text:
ityāhurācāryāḥ--paścāttiryaṅbhānī rathākṣamātrī, īṣāmātrī prācī, vipathayugamātrī purastāttiryaṅnānī /
vigataḥ panthā yasmādyugāt tadvipathayugam /
bāhyacchidrasahitaṃ ṣaḍaśītyaṅgulaṃ yugam /
yāvatā vā bāhye cchidre bāhyacchidrayorantarālamaśī tyaṅgulam /
children.translated_text: Thus say the teachers: the rear breadth is of axle-measure; the length is of pole-measure; the front breadth is of <s>vipatha-yuga</s>-measure. '<s>Vipatha-yuga</s>' — the yoke from which the path is departed [i.e., the yoke of the traveling chariot]. The yoke including the outer holes is eighty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>. 'Or by whatever the outer holes' — the interval between the outer holes is eighty <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
That [construction] is stated with one cord; drawing aside by the fifteen-[unit measure], by the half-axle, and the half-yoke, one should determine the hips and shoulders. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.4]

children.text:
tadekarajjuriti kiṃ saumikī gṛhyate āhosvitprathamasaumikī gṛhyate? pañcadaśikeneti darśanāt, tatra hi pañcadaśike lakṣaṇam, netaratra /
īṣāmātrī īṣāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaddhā vibhajya ekaṃ bhāgaṃ prakramastānīyaṃ kṛtvā saumikavatpañcadaśikenāmāyamya ardhākṣeṇa śroṇa śroṇīṃ minuyāt /
ardhayugenāsau minuyāditi kecit /
apare punaḥ prathamāmekarajjuṃ gṛhṇanti /
yadi saumikī gṛhyate adṛṣṭakalpanā prāptoti kathaṃ pañcadaśikeneti cet, lakṣaṇayā ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāmaṃ yatpañcadaśakaṃ tadapi ṣaḍbhāgonameva /
tasmātpañcadaśikeneti ṣaḍbhāgonāṃ lakṣayituṃ na śakyate /
tenādṛṣṭakalpanābhavati /
nanvanyatrāpi lakṣaṇā? sā tu laukikī, kiṃ ca sādhāraṇatvācca saivaikā rajjuḥsādhāraṇī /
tasmācca saiva grāhyā /
evamuttaratrāpi yojanīyam /
ardhakṣe ardhayuge ca lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍbhāgonenāpāyamya ardhākṣe śroṇī /
ardhayuge tvaṃsau /
children.translated_text: 'That with one cord' — is the <s>Saumikī</s> [cord] taken, or is the first <s>Saumikī</s> taken? From the indication 'by the fifteen-[unit],' [the answer is]: in that [first cord] indeed the mark is at fifteen, not in the other. Of pole-measure: dividing the pole into thirty-six parts, making one part take the place of the <s>prakrama</s>, drawing aside by the fifteen-[unit] as in the <s>Saumikī</s> [method], by the half-axle one should measure the hip. 'By the half-yoke one should measure [the shoulder]' — so say some. Others, however, take the first single cord. If the <s>Saumikī</s> is taken, the objection of unseen assumption arises — [if one asks] how [it can work with] 'by the fifteen-[unit]' — [the answer is:] by secondary usage, the fifteen out of thirty-six in length is itself diminished by one-sixth. Therefore, 'by the fifteen-[unit]' cannot indicate [a cord that is literally] diminished by one-sixth. Hence the unseen assumption occurs. Now, is there not secondary usage elsewhere too? But that [secondary usage] is worldly [obvious]; moreover, because of its commonality, that same one cord is the common [instrument]. Therefore that very [cord] should be taken. The subsequent [sūtras] should be applied similarly. Having made marks at the half-axle and half-yoke, drawing aside by [the cord] diminished by one-sixth — at the half-axle, the hip; at the half-yoke, the shoulders.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary.
(That with one cord... one should construct.)

children.text:
etādviharaṇamekarajjuviharaṇena vyākhyātam /
ekarajjuriti dvitripañcaśaṅkarajjvādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ, itarathā uttarayorvidhānasyādṛṣṭārthatvakalpanāprasaṅgaditi saumikyāṃ vyākhyātam /
tathā pañcadaśikeneti ṣaḍbhāgone kṛtalakṣamasya grahaṇam /
tacca nirañcanamātrapradarśanam /
itarathā adṛṣṭārthatvaprasaṅgāditi tatrrevoktam, tatrānekarajjubhirihāpi viharaṇasuktam, tadihāpyavirodhāt gṛhyata eva /
īṣāmātrā ṣaṭtriṃśadbhāgaṃ prakramaṃ kṛtvā tenaiva viharet /
children.translated_text: This construction is explained by the one-cord construction. 'One cord' implies the inclusion of two-, three-, five-stake cords, etc.; otherwise, [if it were literally 'one cord only,'] the absurd consequence of purposelessness for the subsequent [alternative] prescriptions would arise — thus it was explained regarding the <s>Saumikī</s>. Similarly, 'by the fifteen-[unit]' means taking [a cord] with its mark made at the diminished-by-one-sixth [point]. And that is merely a demonstration of the alignment-mark. Otherwise, the absurd consequence of purposelessness would arise — as stated there. There, [the method] with multiple cords was stated; here too [it applies] without contradiction. Having made the <s>prakrama</s> as one-thirty-sixth of the pole-measure, one should construct by that same [method].
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(That with one cord... one should construct.)

children.text:
"ṣaṭtriṃśikāyāmaṣṭādaśopasamasya' ityādinā ekarajjvā tanmānamuktam /
īṣāyāḥṣaṭtriṃśo bhāgaḥ pañcāṅgulamardhāṣṭamatilāś ca prakramasthāne draṣṭavyam /
yadvā ekarajjuśabdena yāvadāyāmamiti viharaṇamabhipretam /
atra pakṣe pañcadaśikeneti lakṣaṇayā ṣaḍbhāgonatṛtīyamevocyate /
some tatpañcadaśaprakramamabhūditi /
evamuttaratrāpi bāhyacchidrāntarālapakṣe tadardhenāṃsanirharaṇam /
children.translated_text: The measure of that [altar] with one cord was stated by [the sūtra beginning] 'of a thirty-six-[unit] length with an eighteen-[unit] extension.' The thirty-sixth part of the pole is five <s>aṅgulas</s> and three-and-a-half <s>tilas</s> — this should be observed as the <s>prakrama</s>-substitute. Alternatively, by the term 'one cord,' the construction [beginning with] 'as long as the length' is intended. In this alternative, 'by the fifteen-[unit]' means by secondary usage the one-sixth-diminished third itself is stated. In the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], that was fifteen <s>prakramas</s> [long]. Similarly in the subsequent [cases] also: in the alternative of the outer-hole interval, the shoulder-determination is with half of that.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
Moreover, they cite [this example]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.5a]
The word 'atha' (moreover) is in the sense of addition. Thus the chariot-makers who know the chariot-measure also cite [the following verse]:

children.text: aṣṭāśītiśatamīṣā tiryag akṣaścatuḥśatam | ṣaḍaśītiyugaṃ cāsya rathaścāraṇa ucyate iti rathaparimāṇam || ĀpŚus_6.5b ||
children.translated_text: 'The pole is one hundred and eighty-eight [<s>aṅgulas</s>]; the transverse axle is four hundred [<s>aṅgulas</s>]; and the yoke is eighty-six; the chariot is called a <s>cāraṇa</s> (traveling) [chariot]' — thus is the chariot's measurement. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.5b]

children.text:
evaṃ rathaparimāṇaṃ sarvato mānamudāharanti--bruvate /
sāmarthyasiddheśvāṅgulirgṛhyate /
ratheṣāpramāṇaṃ aṣṭāśītyuttaramaṅgulaśatam /
tiryakchabdaḥ pūraṇārthaḥ /
akṣapramāṇaṃ caturadhikaṃ śatam /
yugasya pramāṇaṃ ṣaḍasītiḥ /
evaṃlakṣaṇo yo rathaḥsa cāraṇaḥ, caratyaneneti cāraṇaḥ /
caraṇa eva cāraṇaḥ /
cāraṇagrahaṇaṃ krīḍādirathanivṛcyartham /
athavā asyaśabdasya sthāne yasyaśabdamadhyāhṛtya yojanīyam /
varṇavyatyāsena vā /
children.translated_text: Thus they cite — they state — the measurement of the chariot on all sides. The <s>aṅguli</s> (finger-breadth) is understood from what is established by capacity. The measure of the chariot-pole (<s>īṣā</s>) is one hundred and eighty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s>. The word "transverse" is used for completion. The measure of the axle (<s>akṣa</s>) is one hundred and four. The measure of the yoke (<s>yuga</s>) is eighty-six. A chariot having such characteristics is called <s>cāraṇa</s> (a vehicle for moving); "that by which one moves" is a <s>cāraṇa</s>. <s>Caraṇa</s> itself is <s>cāraṇa</s>. The word <s>cāraṇa</s> is used to exclude chariots for play and the like. Alternatively, supplying the word "yasya" (whose) in place of the word "asya" (its), it should be construed. Or [it is] by metathesis of letters.

children.text: aratnibhir vā caturbhiḥ paścāt ṣaḍbhiḥ prācī tribhiḥ purastāt | tad ekarajjvoktaṃ pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamya dvābhyām adhyardheneti śroṇyaṃsān nirharet || ĀpŚus_6.6 ||
children.translated_text: Or [the altar may be measured] by <s>araṭnis</s> (cubits): four at the back, six lengthwise, three at the front. "That by a single cord" — having drawn aside by the fifteen-[unit measure], by two and a half, one should determine the hips and shoulders. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.6]

children.text:
aratnibhirvā mātavyamiti śeṣaḥ /
caturbhiḥ paścāttiryaṅbhānī /
ṣaḍbhiḥ prācī pṛṣṭhayā /
tribhiḥ purastāttiryaṅbhānī /
tadekarajjvoktamityādi--gatametat /
children.translated_text: "By <s>aratnis</s>" — the remainder [of the sentence] is "it should be measured." Four at the back is the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure). Six lengthwise is the <s>pṛṣṭhyā</s> (spine-line). Three at the front is the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s>. "That by a single cord" etc. — this has been explained previously.

children.text: yajamānamātrī catuḥsraktir bhavatīti paitṛkyā veder vijñāyate, tadekarajjvoktaṃ pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamyārdhena tataḥ śroṇyaṃsān nirharet || ĀpŚus_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>paitṛkī vedī</s> (altar for the ancestors) is known [to be] as large as the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), [and] having four corners. "That by a single cord" — having drawn aside by the fifteen-[unit measure], by half of that, one should determine the hips and shoulders. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.7]

children.text:
paitṛkyā vedeḥ śrutiḥ--yathā dikṣu sraktayo bhavanti tathā mātavyā /
tadekarajjveti gatārtham /
children.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> regarding the <s>paitṛkī vedī</s> (altar for the ancestors): it should be measured such that the corners are in the [cardinal] directions. "That by a single cord" — the meaning has been explained.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary

children.text:
vedārthāvagamasya bahuvidyāntarāśrayatvāt /
takṣaśāstre gārgyā gastyādibhiraṅgulisaṃkhyayoktaṃ rathaparimāṇa ślokamudā harati--
children.translated_text: Since the understanding of Vedic meaning depends on many other sciences, he cites a verse on chariot measurement stated by <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, and others in the science of chariot-building (<s>takṣaśāstra</s>), with <s>aṅguli</s>-based numbers:
(Now also the measurement)

children.text:
athāpiśabdau samuccaye, udāharanti munayaḥ, aṣṭaśītiś ca śataṃ cāṣṭāśītiśataṃ, catvāri ca śataṃ ca catuḥśatam, ṣaṭcāśītiś ca ṣaḍaśīti, āyodhanapuṣyajaitracāraṇādibhedena rathasyānekavidhatāmupanyasta tairuktaṃ aṣṭāśītiśatamityādi, asyārthaḥ--asya bahuvidhasya madhye yasya īṣā aṣṭāśītiśatamaṅgulayaḥ, caturadhikaṃ śatamakṣaḥ, yugaṃ ca ṣaḍaśītiḥ, evaṃvidho rathaśvāraṇa ucyata iti /
evaṃ rathaparimāṇamudāharanti munayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The words "atha api" (now also) are for accumulation. The sages cite: one hundred and eighty-eight; one hundred and four; eighty-six. Having mentioned the manifold nature of chariots through the distinctions of battle-chariots (<s>āyodhana</s>), auspicious chariots (<s>puṣya</s>), victory-chariots (<s>jaitra</s>), transport-chariots (<s>cāraṇa</s>), etc., what they stated — "one hundred and eighty-eight" etc. — its meaning is: among these many types, that [chariot] whose pole is one hundred and eighty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, whose axle is one hundred and four, and whose yoke is eighty-six — such a chariot is called <s>cāraṇa</s> (vehicle). Thus the sages cite the chariot measurement.

children.text:
nanu akṣasya tiryaṅbhānītvamuktam, yugeṣayoḥ kā prācī kā tiraśvīti na jñāyate /
ucyate--akṣasya tiryaktvavidhānādevayugeṣayorapi yā drāghīyasī sā prācī, yā hrasīyasī sā tiraśvīti sāmarthyādīṣā prācīti gamyata iti manyante /
chidrāntarālapakṣe ṣoḍaśāṅgulahīnā purastāttiraśvī /
children.translated_text: Now, it has been stated that the axle has the character of the <s>tiryaṅmānī</s> (transverse measure); [but] of the yoke and the pole, which is the lengthwise (<s>prācī</s>) [measure] and which is the transverse (<s>tiraścī</s>) is not known. It is answered: from the very prescription that the axle is transverse, for the yoke and pole also, whichever is longer is the lengthwise, and whichever is shorter is the transverse — thus by logical capacity, the pole is understood to be the lengthwise. In the view of the inter-hole [interpretation], the front transverse [measure] is diminished by sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.
(By <s>aratnis</s> ... at the front) — this has been explained.
(That by a single cord ... one should determine)
This too has been explained. Here, the definition applies to the <s>aratni</s> (cubit) and to the pair of <s>aratnis</s>.
(As large as the sacrificer ... one should determine)
The <s>vedī</s> (altar) of the ancestors — <s>paitṛkī</s> — is the altar for the great ancestral sacrifice (<s>mahā-pitṛyajña</s>).
Even though the sacrificer's measure is already obtained by injunction, the repetition is because the breadth too is of the same nature.

children.text: (āyāmaḥ) pratidiśaṃ sraktayaḥ mahādikṣukoṇāḥ "sarvā hyanudiśaḥ' iti darśanāt, atra prayogaḥ--agreṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ kiñcidantaḥsañcaramavaśiṣaya tasya purastādyajamānamātraṃ dvikaramyā caturaśraṃ saṃpādya tasya karaṇīmadhyeṣu yathā sraktayo bhaveyuḥ tathā pañcadaśikenetyādinā vihṛtyārdhena tataḥ tasya yajamānamātrasyārdhena śroṇyaṃsānnirharettannimitto nirhrāso vivṛddhirvetyuktayornirhrāsaḥ, mahāvedyāṃ padañcaśikenaivāpāyamya ardhayajamānamātre śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt dakṣiṇāprācī vediḥ //
children.translated_text: The length — the corners (<s>sraktis</s>) [are placed] in each direction, the great corners at the cardinal points — from the observation that "all [corners are] in accordance with the directions"; here the procedure: leaving a slight passageway in front of the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern cooking-fire), to its east, having made a square with the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of the sacrificer's measure, having constructed by the method of "the fifteen-[unit measure]" etc. at the midpoints of its sides so that the corners [face] the directions, by half thereof — by half the sacrificer's measure — one should determine the hips and shoulders. The result is the decrease [not increase] of the two [alternatives] stated as "the decrease or increase caused by that." In the great <s>vedī</s>, having drawn aside by the fifteen-[unit measure] exactly, one should drive in a stake at half the sacrificer's measure — [this is] the south-eastern <s>vedī</s>.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
(Now also the measurement of the chariot)

children.text:
aṅgulayaḥsaṃkhyeyāḥ /
aṅguliśvordhvabāhoḥ puruṣasya viṃśatiśatatamo bhāga iti vakṣyate /
"pañcāratniḥ puruṣaḥ, catuviṃśatya ṅgulayo 'ratniḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) are to be counted. It will be stated that the <s>aṅguli</s> is the one-hundred-and-twentieth part of a <s>puruṣa</s> (man-unit) with arms raised upward. "A <s>puruṣa</s> is five <s>aratnis</s> (cubits); an <s>aratni</s> is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>"

children.text:
iti /
sā ca catustriṃśatattiletyācakṣate /
yathoktaṃ bodhāyanena--
children.translated_text: — and that [<s>aṅguli</s>] is thirty-four <s>tilas</s> (sesame seeds), they say. As stated by <s>Baudhāyana</s>:

children.text:
""aṅgulipramāṇaṃ caturdaśāṇavaḥ catustriṃśattilāḥ pṛthusāṃśliṣṭā ityaparam'' iti caturadhikaṃ śataṃ catuḥśataṃ yugamiti vipathayugamucyate prastutatvāt /
anyattu yugaṃ śatāṅgulamiti takṣaśāstravidaḥ /
ṣaṇṇavatyaṅgulamityācāryapādīyāḥ /
yathā'huḥ-- caturhasto dhanirdanḍo dhanurdhanvantaraṃ yugam /
children.translated_text: "The measure of an <s>aṅguli</s> is fourteen <s>aṇus</s> (atoms/grains); thirty-four <s>tilas</s> placed side by side in breadth — this is another [definition]." "One hundred and four" is the yoke — [this] is called <s>vipatha-yuga</s> (cross-path yoke), since it is the subject at hand. But the other yoke is one hundred <s>aṅgulas</s>, according to experts in chariot-construction science. Ninety-six <s>aṅgulas</s>, according to the followers of the <s>ācārya</s> [Āpastamba]. As they say: "The bow-stave is four <s>hastas</s> (hands); the yoke is the distance between [two] bows."
And: "A <s>hasta</s> (hand) is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>."
(By <s>aratnis</s> ... at the front)
Some [say this is] the <s>paśubandha-vedī</s> (animal-sacrifice altar).
(That by a single cord ... one should determine)
By two — the hips. By one and a half — the shoulders.
(As large as the sacrificer ... is known)
Five <s>aratnis</s>.
(That by a single cord ... one should determine)

children.text:
tata iti ṣaṣṭhayantāttasil /
dakṣiṇāprācī pṛṣṭhayā /
mahādikṣu śroṇyaṃsāḥ /
atra laghūpāyamāha kātyāyanaḥ--
children.translated_text: "Tataḥ" [from that] — the suffix <s>tasil</s> in the sense of the ablative. The south-eastern [direction is] the lengthwise (<s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>). The hips and shoulders are at the cardinal points. Here <s>Kātyāyana</s> states a convenient method:

children.text:
"paitṛkyāṃ dvipuruṣaṃ caturaśraṃ kṛtvā karaṇīmadhyeṣu śaṅkavaḥsasamādhiḥ' iti /
tatra prakāraḥ--puruṣamātradvikaraṇyā daśatilonayā saptatiśatāṅgulayā samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā karaṇīnāṃ madhyeṣu śaṅkūnnihatya daśāratnayo rajjvoḥ pāśāna pūrvāparayoḥ pratimucya tayormadhye dakṣiṇottarayorniyamya vahiḥspandamapacchindyāt /
etaṃ caturaratnamipi kecidicchanti /
tatra ājyaṃ puroḍāśā āsādayituṃ na śakyante /
children.translated_text: "For the <s>paitṛkī</s> [altar], having made a square of two <s>puruṣas</s>, [driving] gnomons at the midpoints of the sides — that is the <s>samādhi</s> (alignment)." The procedure there: having made an even quadrilateral with the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure — one hundred and seventy <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by ten <s>tilas</s> — having driven gnomons at the midpoints of the sides, stretching cords of ten <s>aratnis</s> with loops at the eastern and western [gnomons], fixing [the cord] at the southern and northern [gnomons] in the middle, one should cut off the excess outward. Some desire this [altar] to be four <s>aratnis</s> also. In that case, the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) and <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cakes) cannot be placed [due to insufficient space].
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: daśapadottarā vedir bhavatīti some vijñāyate | tad ekarajjvoktaṃ pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamyārdhena tataḥ śroṇyaṃsān nirharet || ĀpŚus_6.8 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vedī</s> (altar) is known to be ten <s>padas</s> (feet) larger in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice]. "That by a single cord" — having drawn aside by the fifteen-[unit measure], by half thereof, one should determine the hips and shoulders. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.8]

children.text:
padagrahaṇaṃ pradarśanārtham /
prakamamitāyāṃ mahānedyāṃ daśapadottaravediḥ sarvato daśapadā "pramāṇena pramāṇaṃ vidhīyata' iti vacanāt /
kṣetrato vā daśapatā /
tadā ekapadavistāraṃ tripadāyāmaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasyākṣṇayā rajjuṃ gṛhītvā caturaśraṃ kuryāt /
prakrame 'pyekaprakramavistāraṃ triprakramāyāmaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya tasyākṣṇayā rajjuṃ gṛhītvā caturaśraṃ kuryāt /
tadekarajjvoktaṃ--ardhena tataḥ--tasyetyarthaḥ ṣaṣṭhayarthe tasil /
children.translated_text: The word <s>pada</s> (foot) is used for illustration. In the great <s>vedī</s> measured by <s>prakramas</s> (steps), the <s>vedī</s> is ten <s>padas</s> larger on all sides — ten <s>padas</s> all around — because of the statement "the <s>pramāṇa</s> is prescribed by the <s>pramāṇa</s> as a quadrilateral." Or ten <s>padas</s> in area. Then, having made an oblong rectangle one <s>pada</s> wide and three <s>padas</s> long, taking its diagonal cord, one should make a square. In the <s>prakrama</s> [system] also, having laid out a rectangle one <s>prakrama</s> wide and three <s>prakramas</s> long, taking its diagonal cord, one should make a square. "That by a single cord" — "by half thereof" — "of that" is the meaning; <s>tasil</s> [suffix] in the sense of the ablative.

children.text: tāṃ yugena yajamānasya vā padair vimāya śamyayā parimimīte || ĀpŚus_6.9 ||
children.translated_text: One measures that [<s>vedī</s>] with a yoke or with the paces of the sacrificer; then one re-measures with a <s>śamyā</s> (measuring-rod). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.9]

children.text:
yugenoktapamāṇena yajamānasya vā padaiḥ /
yajamānagrahaṇādadhvaryorna labhyate /
yajamānagrahaṇaṃ pradarśanārthamiti kecit /
tasmādeva vacanāduttaravediryugamātrī labhyate /
some padamānāyāṃ mahāvedyāṃ uttaravediṃ yugena vā padairvā vimāya śaulbena mānena paścācchamyayā mānamadṛṣṭārthaṃ kartavyam /
śamyayā parimimīta ityetadvacanamadṛṣṭārthaṃ na pramāṇavidhiḥ iyuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: With a yoke of the stated dimension, or with the paces of the sacrificer. From the mention of "sacrificer," [this right] is not obtained by the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest). Some [say] the mention of "sacrificer" is for illustration. From this very statement, the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar) is obtained as yoke-sized. In the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], when the great <s>vedī</s> is measured in <s>padas</s>, having measured the <s>uttaravedī</s> with a yoke or with paces, the subsequent measurement with the <s>śamyā</s> (measuring-rod) by the <s>Śulba</s> measurement is to be performed for a transcendental purpose (<s>adṛṣṭārtha</s>). The statement "one re-measures with a <s>śamyā</s>" is for a transcendental purpose, not a prescription of measurement — this is appropriate.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
(Ten <s>padas</s> larger ... is known)

children.text: mahāvedyāṃ prathamanihatācchaṅkoḥ purastātpañcaviṃśatiṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tatpurastādṛśasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya pañcadaśikenetyādinā viharet //
children.translated_text: Having driven a gnomon twenty-five [units] east of the first gnomon driven in the great <s>vedī</s>, then driving a gnomon ten [units] east of that, one should construct by the method of "the fifteen-[unit measure]" etc.
(That by a single cord ... one should determine)

children.text:
tator'dhena pañcapadenetyarthaḥ /
"sarvato daśapadā' iti śatapathabrāhnaṇe śrūyate "pramāṇena pramāṇaṃ vidhīyate śaturaśramiti tadanirūpakṣe trato daśapada
children.translated_text: "By half thereof" — the meaning is: by five <s>padas</s>. "Ten <s>padas</s> on all sides" is heard in the <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s>. "The <s>pramāṇa</s> is prescribed by the <s>pramāṇa</s> as a quadrilateral" — in the absence of determining that, "ten <s>padas</s> in area"
— thus [says] <s>Kātyāyana</s>.

children.text: asmin pakṣe padavistāraṃ tripadāyāmaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya tasyākṣṇayārajjupramāṇottaravediḥ /
children.translated_text: In this view, having laid out an oblong rectangle one <s>pada</s> wide and three <s>padas</s> long, the <s>uttaravedī</s> has its dimension equal to the diagonal cord of that.
In this view too, the construction of hips and shoulders is by half the <s>karaṇī</s> [of this rectangle].
(That with a yoke ... one re-measures)

children.text: tena vā yajamānasya vā padairvimāya paścādadṛṣṭārthaṃ śamyayā sarvato mimīte /
children.translated_text: Having measured with that, or with the paces of the sacrificer, afterwards, for a transcendental purpose, one re-measures on all sides with a <s>śamyā</s> (measuring-rod).

children.text: śamyāpramāṇaṃ coktaṃ sūtrāntare "ṣaṭtriṃśacchamyā' iti paśubandhe tvanyasyābhāvāt parimāṇārthameva śamyāvidhānam /
children.translated_text: The measure of the <s>śamyā</s> is stated in another <s>sūtra</s>: "the <s>śamyā</s> is thirty-six [<s>aṅgulas</s>]." In the <s>paśubandha</s> (animal-sacrifice), however, since there is no other [measuring instrument], the prescription of the <s>śamyā</s> is for the purpose of measurement itself.
And from the [grammatical] indication [in the Śruti] "it is her measure."
From this very statement, the <s>uttaravedī</s> of the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] is also obtained as being yoke-sized.
That <s>uttaravedī</s>, by the yoke-measure. This has been stated: "the yoke is eighty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>."
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
(Ten <s>padas</s> larger ... one should determine)
Ten <s>padas</s> — on all sides. In area: one hundred <s>padas</s>.
(That with a yoke ... one re-measures)

children.text:
yugamapi daśapadāyā eva mānasādhanaṃ veṇuvat /
kecit tasyatantraṃ pramāṇamāhuḥ, atadvicāraṇīyaṃ sūribhiḥ /
yajamānagrahaṇaṃ adhvaryunivṛcyartham /
śamyayā parimāṇamadṛṣṭārtham /
children.translated_text: The yoke too is merely an instrument for measuring the ten-<s>pada</s> [altar], like a bamboo [rod]. Some say it is an independent (<s>tantra</s>) measure; that is not to be examined by the wise. The mention of "sacrificer" is for excluding the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest). The re-measurement with the <s>śamyā</s> is for a transcendental purpose.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: pade yuge 'ratnāv iyati śamyāyāṃ ca mānārtheṣu yathākāmī śabdārthasya viśayitvāt || ĀpŚus_6.10 ||
children.translated_text: Regarding the <s>pada</s> (foot), the <s>yuga</s> (yoke), the <s>aratni</s> (cubit), and in the <s>śamyā</s> (measuring-rod) — in measuring-terms, one may choose as one wishes, because the word's meaning has latitude. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.10]
In measuring-terms such as <s>pada</s> and the like, one may choose as one wishes — one should adopt [the definition] as one pleases.
What is being said?
Fourteen <s>aṇus</s> (atoms/fine grains) equal one <s>tila</s> (sesame seed);
thirty-four <s>tilas</s> equal one <s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth) (placed side by side in breadth — this is another [definition]);
twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span);
thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>vitasti</s> (span);
fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>pada</s> (foot);
twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>aratni</s> (cubit);
thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>jānu</s> (knee-height);
thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>śamyā</s> (measuring-rod);
eighty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> equal one <s>yuga</s> (yoke);
one hundred and four [<s>aṅgulas</s>] equal one <s>akṣa</s> (axle);
one hundred and twenty [<s>aṅgulas</s>] equal one <s>puruṣa</s> (man-unit).

children.text:
ityevamādiśulbāntaroktalakṣaṇamānārtheṣu pramāṇāvayavā gṛhyeran /
lakṣaṇe vargeṇa vimāya tatra yathākāmī śabdārthasya viśayitvāt /
pañcadaśāṅgulaṃ padamapi bhavati /
yajamānapadamapi /
tatrānyataradgrāhyamityādhāne /
iyaddvādaśavikrāmā iti /
tatra svasaṃvittiṃ aparasaṃvittiṃ lokaprasiddhiṃ śāstraprasiddhiṃ vā gṛhṇīyādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in measuring-terms, the sub-units of the standard measure may be adopted as defined in this and other <s>Śulba</s> [texts]. Having measured by the standard in the definition, one may choose [the specific unit] as one wishes, since the word's meaning has latitude. The <s>pada</s> (foot) may be fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, or it may also be the foot of the sacrificer. Either of those should be adopted — this [applies] to the fire-establishment. "This much is twelve <s>vikramas</s>" — there, one may adopt one's own perception, the perception of another, common understanding, or the authority of the <s>śāstra</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: vimitāyāṃ purastāt pārśvamānyā upasaṃharet | śrutisāmarthyāt || ĀpŚus_6.11 ||
children.translated_text: When [the area] has been measured, one should contract [it] at the front by the <s>pārśvamānī</s> (lateral measure); [this is known] by the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 6.11]

children.text: evaṃ caturaśre āpādite pārśvamānyā purastādu pasaṃharet, śrutisāmarthyāt--""catuḥśikhaṇḍe yuvatī kanīne'' iti yuvatisādṛśyānuvādaḥ sāmarthyam //
children.translated_text: When the quadrilateral has been thus produced, one should contract [it] at the front by the <s>pārśvamānī</s>; by the capacity of the <s>Śruti</s> — "four-crested like a young maiden" — the comparison to a young maiden stated [there] is the capacity [i.e., the basis for the contraction].
Thus ends the sixth section.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
(Regarding the <s>pada</s>, the <s>yuga</s> ... latitude)

children.text:
pade yuge 'ratnāviyati prādeśe prakrame śamyāyāṃ ceti hiraṇyakośiśulbe bodhāyanīyaśulbe ca /
athāṅgulīpramāṇaṃ caturdaśāṇavaḥ catustriṃśattilāḥ pṛthusaṃśliṣṭā ityaparam /
daśāṅgulaṃ kṣudrapadam /
dvādaśa prādeśaḥ /
pṛthottarayuge trayodaśike prakrāme ca (pañca) daśa /
aṣṭāśītiśatamīṣā /
ṣaḍaśītiryugam /
dvātriṃśajjānuḥ ṣaṭtriṃśacchamyā, bāhurddvipadaḥ prakāmaḥ, dvau prādeśāvaratniriti /
tathā pañcā ratniḥ puruṣaścaturaratnirvā yāma iti ca /
tatraiva iyatyagre juhoti, iyatyagre harati, iyantaṃ gṛhṇāti, iyantaṃ karoti, iyadbhavatītyādi brāhnaṇavyākhyānāvasara evācāryeṇa jānudaghnādibhiḥ parimāṇairvyākhyātaḥ /
tatra padādiṣu mānasādhanavayā nirdiṣṭeṣu yāthākāmī syādyathecchā tathā kuryādityarthaḥ /
śabdārthasya viśayitvāditi gatam /
ayamarthaḥ--padādiṣu yajamānasyādhvaryorvāvayavabhūtāṅgulyā parikalpitāni aṇutilaparikalpitāṅgulyā parikalpi tāni vā padādīni gṛhnīyāt /

children.translated_text: Because the word-meaning of <s>pada</s> and other [terms] is applied in both cases.
<s>Aṇus</s> (grains) are a particular type of grain (<s>dhānya</s>).

children.text: (ācāryeṇaiva nirūḍhapaśau ratha parimāṇajñānārthaṃ takṣaśāstroktādaṣṭāśītiśatamityudāharaṇāt, śyenepañcāratniḥ puruṣa ityādeḥ klptiśabdena pramāṇavidāṃ samayānukathanānna śāstrāntaraparigṛhītāṅgulipadādiparigrahānuyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: (Since the <s>ācārya</s> himself, in the context of the <s>nirūḍha-paśu</s> (established animal sacrifice), gives the example 'one hundred and eighty-eight' from the carpenter's manual (<s>takṣa-śāstra</s>) for the purpose of knowing the chariot's dimensions; and since 'five <s>aratnis</s> is a <s>puruṣa</s>' and such [statements] merely recount the conventions of those who know measurements using the word <s>klpti</s> (arrangement) -- there is no objection to accepting <s>aṅguli</s>, <s>pada</s>, and other [measures] as defined in other <s>śāstras</s> (treatises).

Since, in the context of the <s>prakrama</s> (pace), the statement 'of the sacrificer or the officiating priest' [indicates that] it is not merely the <s>pada</s> and other [measures] determined by finger-breadths calibrated by limbs [of the body] alone [that are to be taken].)

In the <s>pada</s> (foot-step), <s>yuga</s> (yoke), <s>aratni</s> (cubit), <s>iyati</s> (this-much), <s>prādeśa</s> (span), <s>prakrama</s> (pace), and <s>śamyā</s> (goad) -- [these measurements are stated] in the <s>Hiraṇyakeśi Śulba</s> and in the <s>Bodhāyana Śulba</s>. Now the measure of a finger-breadth (<s>aṅguli</s>): fourteen <s>aṇus</s> (grains) [or] thirty-four <s>tilās</s> (sesame seeds) placed closely side by side -- this is another [definition]. Ten <s>aṅgulas</s> is a small <s>pada</s> (foot-step). Twelve is a <s>prādeśa</s> (span). In the broad <s>yuga</s> of thirteen and in the <s>prakrama</s> (pace), [there are] fifteen. One hundred and eighty-eight [<s>aṅgulas</s> is] the yoke-pole (<s>īṣā</s>). Eighty-six is the <s>yuga</s> (yoke). Thirty-two is the knee-[height]; thirty-six is the <s>śamyā</s> (goad); the arm is two <s>padas</s>; the <s>prakāma</s> (extended step), two <s>prādeśas</s> is an <s>aratni</s> (cubit). And five <s>aratnis</s> is a <s>puruṣa</s> (man-height), or four <s>aratnis</s> is a <s>yāma</s> (extent). In the same [texts], 'he offers at this distance,' 'he carries at this distance,' 'he takes this much,' 'he makes this much,' 'it becomes this much' -- and so on: in the context of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> commentary, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) has explained [these] with measures such as knee-deep and the like. Regarding the <s>pada</s> and other [measurements] stated as instruments of measurement: there is free choice -- the meaning is: one may do as one wishes. Because the word-meaning has multiple domains -- this has been explained. This is the meaning: for the <s>pada</s> and other [measures], one should take [them as] determined by the finger-breadth that is a limb of the sacrificer or the officiating priest, or [as] determined by the finger-breadth calibrated through <s>aṇu</s> (grain) and <s>tila</s> (sesame seed).
Having completed the digression on <s>aṅguli</s> (finger-breadth), he states the remainder of the main topic:
(When measured -- by implication)
This has been explained in the <s>dārśikī</s> (new-moon) [section].

children.text: iha tu śrutisāmarthyāt "catuḥśikhaṇḍe yuvatī kanīne' idyasyāḥ śruterahīyasīṃ purastādityeka ityupasaṃhārācca vikalpaḥ karmopadeśa uktaḥ //
children.translated_text: But here, by the force of scripture -- by the <s>śruti</s> 'four-tufted, youthful maiden' -- and from the conclusion that '[it is] narrower in front' is merely one option, the operational instruction has been stated as an alternative.
Sixth section.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
(On <s>pada</s>, <s>yuga</s> -- having multiple domains.)

children.text:
padacāturvidhyamuktam /
yugatrauvidhyaṃ ca ṣaḍaśītiṣaṇṇavatiśatāṅgulaiḥ /
aratnirdvividhaḥ--caturviṃśatyaṅgulo hastaś ceti /
iyāniti prādeśo 'bhipretaḥ /
sa ca dvividhaḥ--dvādaśāṅgulaḥ prasārite aṅguṣṭhapredaśinyāviti /
śamyā trividhā--"catvāro 'ṣṭadvātriṃśadaṅgulā śamyā, iti kātyāyanaḥ /
"ṣaṭtriṃśacchamyā' iti hodhāyanaḥ, laukikī tṛtīyā /
eṣu māneṣu yāthā kāmyaṃ bhavati, śabdārthasyānekatra vṛttaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The fourfold nature of the <s>pada</s> has been stated. The threefold nature of the <s>yuga</s> too: eighty-six, ninety-six, and one hundred <s>aṅgulas</s>. The <s>aratni</s> (cubit) is of two kinds: twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> and the <s>hasta</s> (hand-cubit). The 'this much' (<s>iyān</s>) refers to the <s>prādeśa</s> (span). And that is of two kinds: twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> when the thumb and index finger are extended. The <s>śamyā</s> (goad) is of three kinds: '<s>śamyā</s> is four, eight, [or] thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>' -- thus <s>Kātyāyana</s>. 'Thirty-six is the <s>śamyā</s>' -- thus <s>Bodhāyana</s>; the common [goad] is the third. In these measures, there is free choice, because the word-meaning is applied in multiple [contexts].
(When measured -- by implication.)
That 'narrower in front' is optional has been stated earlier.
Sixth section.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: navāratni tiryak saptaviṃśatir udag āyatam iti sadaso vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Nine <s>aratnis</s> transversely, twenty-seven [<s>aratnis</s>] lengthwise to the north -- this is known regarding the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall). || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.1 ||
Eighteen, according to some. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.2 ||
That [is done] by the single-cord [method]: stretching [a cord] of fifteen [<s>padas</s>], with four and a half, one should mark out the hips and shoulders. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.3 ||

children.text:
navāratniḥ prācī tiryaṅbhānī, saptaviṃśatirudīcī pārśvamānī /
evaṃ mantavyamiti sadasaḥśrutiḥ /
padena prakrameṇa vā mātavyam /
karaṇamuktam /
prathamanihatācchaṅkordakṣiṇataḥ prakrame śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin pāśaṃ pratimucya tasya purastādardhāṣṭame pṛṣṭhayāyāṃ dakṣimataḥ prakmaśaṅguḥ /
tatsadaso madhyamaudumbarīsthānam /
prathamanihatācchaṅkoḥ pṛṣṭayāyāmeva purastādardhāṣṭame śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin pāśaṃ pratimucyoparyupari śaṅkumudagapasāryārdhacaturdaśe navasu vā śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
pṛṣṭhayāyāṃ yaḥśaṅkuḥ tasmin pratimucyoparyuparyaudumbarīsthānīyaṃ dakṣiṇāpasāryārdhapañcadaśe daśasu vā śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
sadasa āyāmaḥ /
taḥsinnāyāme tadardhamabhyasya yathāsūtraṃ virahet /
saptaviṃśatāvardhacaturdaśamabhyasya dakṣiṇasmādaṃsādekādaśasu padeṣu nihañjanamardhapañcame lakṣaṇaṃ śroṇyaṃ sādardhamaṣṭādaśasu vā nava prakṣipyārdhāṣṭame nirañjanamardhapañcamalakṣaṇaṃ śroṇyaṃsārdhamāyāmayorantau niyamya nirañjanam /
tena paścādapasāryārdhapañcame śaṅkuḥ /
purastādapasāryārdhapañcame śaṅkuḥ /
te śroṇī /
sadasaḥ viparyasyāṃsau /
prāgvaṃśamānaṃ havirthānam /
āgnīdhramānaṃ cānenācāryeṇa noktam. ataḥśulbāntaroktaṃ grāhyaṃ vaikṛtatvāt /
sadasaḥ purastāttiṣu prakrameṣu daśaprakramavistāraṃ dvādaśāyāmaṃ havirdhānaṃ minuyāt /
ekarajjvā pañcaśaṅkunā triśaṅkunā vā havirdhānasya pāśvātyamadhyamaśaṅkau pāśaṃ pratimucyodagapasārya dvādaśaprakame śaṅkuḥ /
tadāgrīdhrāyatanam /
tayā rajjvā dakṣiṇāpasārya dvādaśasu mārjālīyam /
pṛṣṭhayāyāṃ sadasaḥ paurastyaśaṅkau pāśaṃ pratimucyodagapasārya pādonaikādaśasu śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmāccottarataḥ ṣaṭsu śaṅkuḥ /
tābhyāṃ ca purastāt ṣaṭsu prakameṣu śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evaṃ pañcaśaṅkunā vā samacaturaśraṃ minuyāt /
aṣṭaprakamavistāraṃ dvādaśāyāmaṃ prāgvaṃśaṃ minuyāt /
dvādaśavistāraṃ ṣoḍaśāyāmamityanye /
children.translated_text: The <s>prācī</s> (east-west line), the transverse measure, is nine <s>aratnis</s>; the <s>udīcī</s> (north-south line), the lateral measure, is twenty-seven. This is the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural teaching) about the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall) -- thus it should be understood. It should be measured by the <s>pada</s> (foot-step) or by the <s>prakrama</s> (pace). The procedure has been stated. From the first fixed peg, fixing a peg one <s>prakrama</s> to the south, fastening the loop there, at the front in the half-eighth [part] of the spine-line (<s>pṛṣṭhayā</s>), to the south is the <s>prakrama</s>-peg. That is the location of the central <s>audumbarī</s> post of the <s>sadas</s>. From the first fixed peg, in the very spine-line, fixing a peg at the half-eighth in front, fastening the loop there, moving the peg northward successively, one should fix a peg at the half-fourteenth or at nine. At the peg in the spine-line, fastening [the loop], moving the <s>audumbarī</s>-position peg southward successively, one should fix a peg at the half-fifteenth or at ten. [That gives] the length of the <s>sadas</s>. In that length, having added half of it [as an extension], one should construct as per the <s>sūtra</s>. In the twenty-seven, having added the half-fourteenth, from the southern shoulder at eleven <s>padas</s>, fixing [a peg] at the half-fifth with a mark -- the half of the hip-and-shoulder, [or] at eighteen adding nine, at the half-eighth with a mark, the half of the hip-and-shoulder -- fixing the ends at both ends of the length, [stretching by] the mark: stretching westward by the half-fifth, a peg [is fixed] -- those are the hips. Of the <s>sadas</s>, reversing [the procedure], the shoulders [are marked]. The <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (front-hall) has the same measure as the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation-hall). The measure of the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's hall) has not been stated by this <s>ācārya</s>; therefore it should be taken from another <s>Śulba</s> [text], as it is a variant form. In front of the <s>sadas</s>, at three <s>prakramas</s>, one should measure the <s>havirdhāna</s> with a width of ten <s>prakramas</s> and length of twelve. By the single cord with five pegs or three pegs, fastening the loop at the western-middle peg of the <s>havirdhāna</s>, stretching northward, a peg at twelve <s>prakramas</s> -- that is the <s>āgnīdhra</s> altar-site. With that same cord, stretching southward, at twelve [<s>prakramas</s>] is the <s>mārjālīya</s> (purification site). In the spine-line, fastening the loop at the eastern peg of the <s>sadas</s>, stretching northward, fixing a peg at three-quarters of eleven, and from that further northward at six, a peg. And from those two, at six <s>prakramas</s> in front, one should fix a peg. Thus with five pegs or [otherwise], one should measure a square. One should measure the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (front-hall) with a width of eight <s>prakramas</s> and length of twelve. Others [say]: width of twelve, length of sixteen.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(Nine <s>aratnis</s>... according to some.)

children.text:
tiryaṅnānā navāratniḥ prāgbhavati udaksaptaviṃśatirāyataṃ /
aṣṭādaśāyatamityekeṣāṃ śākhinām /
children.translated_text: The transverse measure -- nine <s>aratnis</s> -- is the east[-west]; to the north, twenty-seven <s>aratnis</s> lengthwise. According to some <s>Śākhā</s> branches, eighteen lengthwise.
(That by the single [cord]... should mark out.)

children.text: padavimitāyāṃ vedyāṃ sadohavirdhānayorapi padenaiva mānamityuktaṃ, prakramamāne tvaratnivimānameva, havirdhānasyāparimitaṃ vati karmopadeśa uktaḥ, aparimitaṃ saptaviṃśateḥ paraṃ sadovimānamucyate, mahāvedeḥ paścāttiraśvayāḥ pṛṣṭhayāyā dakṣiṇato daśapadeṣvārabhya yāvatpurastāt tiraśvayāḥ tāvatīṃ leśāmālikhet, rajjuṃ vā pātayet, evaṃ pṛṣṭayāyā uttarato 'pi aṣṭāsu padeṣu paścimāntādārabhya tayoreva lekhayoḥ pūrvapaścimeṣu dakṣiṇata ārabhya yāvaduttaraṃ udīcīṃ leśāmālikhet, sā sadasaḥ pṛṣṭhayā bhavati /
children.translated_text: For the <s>vedī</s> measured by the <s>pada</s> (foot), the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> are also measured by the <s>pada</s> alone -- this has been stated. But when measuring by <s>prakrama</s> (pace), only the <s>aratni</s> measurement [applies]. As the <s>havirdhāna's</s> [measure] is unlimited, the operational instruction has been stated. Beyond the unlimited twenty-seven, the measure of the <s>sadas</s> is stated. From the rear transverse line of the <s>mahāvedī</s> (great altar), at ten <s>padas</s> to the south, starting and extending to the front transverse line, one should draw a line or lay a cord; similarly, from the north of the spine-line at eight <s>padas</s> starting from the western end, in those very lines east-west, starting from the south extending northward, one should draw a north-south line -- that becomes the spine-line of the <s>sadas</s>.

children.text: aṣṭādaśikāyāṃ navopasamasyārdhapañcameṣvardhāṣṭameṣu lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭhyāntayorityādinā vihṛtyārdhapañcameṣu śaṅkuṃ nnihanyāttatsado bhavati //
children.translated_text: In the eighteen-[<s>aratni</s> version], having made marks at the half-fifth of nine with [the extension of] the half-eighth, constructing with 'at the ends of the spine' and so on, one should fix a peg at the half-fifth -- that becomes the <s>sadas</s>.

children.text: havirdhānaṃ daśāyāmaṃ, daśavi stāramāgnīdhra, ṣaḍāyāmavistāramardhamantarvedyardhaṃ bahirvedirbhavati /
children.translated_text: The <s>havirdhāna</s> has a length of ten [and] a width of ten for the <s>āgnīdhra</s>; length and width of six -- half the <s>antarvedī</s> (inner altar); half [of that] becomes the <s>bahirvedī</s> (outer altar).
The <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> has a length of sixteen and width of twelve.
Or a length of twelve and width of nine.

children.text: prathamanihatāt śaṅkoḥ purastātpañcadaśasu śabhkuḥ, tatpurastāt navāyāmavistāraṃ havirdhānaṃ daśapadaṃ vā taddviśaṅkuprabhutīnāmanyatame na kuryāt //
children.translated_text: From the first fixed peg, at fifteen [paces] in front is a peg; in front of that, the <s>havirdhāna</s> with a length and width of nine and [a breadth of] ten <s>padas</s>; it should be constructed by any one of the methods beginning with two pegs.
The measures of the <s>havirdhāna</s>, <s>āgnīdhra</s>, and <s>prāgvaṃśa</s>, though not taught here by the <s>ācārya</s>, are to be taken as taught in other <s>Śulba</s> [texts].
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
