(Nine <s>aratnis</s>... according to some.)

children.text:
udagāyatamityeva /
navāratnireva prācī /
tatra viṃśaticatuviṃśatyaṅgulaprakrameṇa aṣṭāśāratniḥ /
uttareṣu kratuṣu saptaviṃśatya rātniḥ /
deśastu prayogakalpa evoktaḥ, "aparasmādve dyaṃsāt' ityādinā /
children.translated_text: 'Lengthwise to the north' indeed. The east[-west] is exactly nine <s>aratnis</s>. In that, with a <s>prakrama</s> of twenty or twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>, eighty-eight is [equivalent to nine] <s>aratnis</s>. In the later rituals, twenty-seven <s>aratnis</s>. The site [specification], however, is stated only in the ritual application manual (<s>prayoga-kalpa</s>), by 'from the rear altar-shoulder' and so on.
(That by the single [cord]... should mark out.)
The north[-south] -- [is] the spine-line (<s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>).
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: prādeśamukhāḥ prādeśāntarālā bhavantīty uparavāṇāṃ vijñāyate | aratnimātraṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya sraktiṣu śaṅkūn nihatyārdhaprādeśena taṃ taṃ parilikhec chrutisāmarthyāt || ĀpŚus_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: Of the measure of a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) at the opening, with intervals of a <s>prādeśa</s> between [them] -- this is known regarding the <s>uparavas</s> (pressing-stone pits). Having constructed a square of <s>aratni</s> (cubit) measure, fixing pegs at the corners, one should circumscribe each [pit] with a half-<s>prādeśa</s> [radius] -- by the force of scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.4 ||
The measurement of the <s>uparava</s> (pressing-stone pit) is also explained in the commentary style. The word <s>aratni</s> has already been explained.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(Of <s>prādeśa</s> [measure]... is known.)

children.text:
abhiṣavakāle grāvabhireṣāmupari ra(ya)vanta ityuparavāḥ /
uparāḥ--grāvaviśeṣāḥ, tena tadvanta iti vā uparavā avaṭaviśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Uparavas</s>: at the time of <s>abhiṣava</s> (Soma-pressing), the pressing-stones are used to press (<s>ravanti</s>) upon them -- hence <s>uparavas</s>. <s>Uparās</s> are special pressing-stones; [the pits are called <s>uparavas</s>] because they contain those (<s>tadvantaḥ</s>), or <s>uparavas</s> are special pits.
(Of <s>aratni</s> [measure]... by the force of scripture.)

children.text: dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya dakṣimasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ dviśaṅkvādīnāmanyatamenāratnipramāṇaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya koṇeṣu śaṅkūn nihatyārdhaprādeśena karkaṭena rajjvā vā tān śaṅkūn parito likhet /
children.translated_text: At the southern hip of the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>, having constructed a square of <s>aratni</s> measure by the two-peg or other method, fixing pegs at the corners, one should draw around those pegs with a half-<s>prādeśa</s> [compass] -- either with a divider (<s>karkaṭa</s>) or with a cord.
Thus they become of <s>prādeśa</s> measure at the opening, with intervals of a <s>prādeśa</s> between them.
This <s>śruti</s> (scripture) has this very meaning.
The <s>vedī</s> [is measured] by the <s>pada</s> measure.

children.text:
atha devayajanadeśavimānabhāgā ucyante--padamāne eka pañcāśat prācīṃ triṃśattiraśvīṃ devayajamānayogyāṃ bhūmiṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye tadāyāmāṃ devayajanayogyāṃ bhūmiṃ kṛtvā ntamadhye tadāyāmāṃ prācīṃ lekhāmālikhya rajjuṃ prasārya tadantayoḥ śaṅkuṃ nikhāya prāgvaṃśaprabhṛti tadanurūpaṃ tatkratukāle kuryāt, paścādante prāgvaṃśaṃ ṣoḍaśāyāmaṃ dvādaśavistāraṃ dvādaśāyāmaṃ navavistāraṃ vā nirmāya tasya lālāṭikātrrīn prāca ityādi tattraiva tacchaṅkorārabhya tripadā vahirvedistadante śaṅkuḥ, tatastatpurastāt ṣaṭtriṃśanmahāvediḥ prācī, triṃśatpaścāt tiraśvī, caturviṃśatiḥ purastāt tiraśvī, evaṃ mahāvediṃ vimāya paścimānte tripadaḥsañcaraḥ, tatpurastātprāktvena navapadamudaktvenāṣṭādaśapadaṃ sadaḥ, dakṣiṇottaramaṣṭādaśāyāmaṃ tanmadhye pṛṣṭhyāyā dakṣiṇataḥ padamātre bhavati /
tadoduṃbarīsthānaṃ, sadasaḥ pūrvārdhe purastādardhaṃ padamātraṃ saṃcaramavaśiṣya tatpaścātpṛṣṭhyāyāṃ hotrīyamityādayo dhiṣṇyā aratnimātrāḥ piśīlamātrā vā /
teṣāṃ ca tasya tasyottarataḥ visāṃsthita saṃcaraḥ sadasaḥ purastāt tripadaḥsaṃcaraḥ /
tatpurastāt navāyāmavistāraṃ havirdhānaṃ, tryaratnivistāraṃ navāyāmamiti madhyamaṃ madhyame chatiṣi tūṣṇīmitare chadiṣī iti darśanāt /
"daśāyāmavistāraṃ havirdhānam' iti bodhāyanaḥ /
yūpāvaṭīyācchaṅkoḥ paścātpadamātraḥsaṃcaraḥ /
tatpaścādyugamātrottaravodiḥ /
uttaravedihavirdhānayorantarālamantarvediḥ /
pṛṣṭhyāyā dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇahavirdhānaṃ, uttarata uttaraṃ havirdhānaṃ, dakṣiṇahavirdhānasya dakṣiṇaśroṇyāmuparavāḥ, havirdhānasya paścād āgnīdhrasya (dāgnīdhrīyaśva) bāhusamaṃ pṛṣṭhyāyā dakṣiṇato dvādaśasu pārjā līyaḥ /
tathaiva tasyā evodak dvādaśasvāgnīdhrīyaḥ, sarvadhiṣṇiyāḥ piśīlamātrāḥ sadasoṃ'sādut tarataḥ pādonatripade padonanavapade caśaṅkūḥ /
āgnīdhramaṇṭapasya te śroṇī /
havirdhānapaścimāntādārabhya prākrripadeṣu pṛṣṭyāyā uttarataḥ /
pādonaikādaśasu pādonasaptadaśasu śaṅkū, tāvāgnīdhrapaṇṭapasyāṃsau /
ṣaḍviṃśikāyāḥ paścāt pṛṣṭhyāyāḥ pūrvānte ardhamantarvedyardhaṃ bahirvediḥ /
tripadaviṣkambhastripadaparīṇāho yūpāvaṭa iti bodhāyanaḥ /
uttarasmādvedyaṃsādudakprakrame cātvāla uttaravedisaṃmitaḥ, cātvālamadhyo vedyaṃsatulyaḥ /
ardhānte cātvālāt paścāddādaśasu tadbahirvedyutkaraḥ, vedyaṅkotkarayormadhye uttarataḥ ṣoḍaśasu śāmitradhiṣṇyaḥ /
etatpadamāne /
prakramamāne tu sadohavirdhānayoraratnimānamagneruttaravedervā paścātrrīn pratīcaḥ prakramānatītya tiryagahavirdhānaṃ navāratnītyādi yāvat /
saṃbhavā yāmīvastāraṃ sadaḥ /
dhiṣṇyāḥ piśīlamātrāḥ prakrameṇaiva sarvamānaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaparimitā uttaravedistu daśapadā yugamātrī vā tatsthāne 'gnirvā /
anyatsarvaṃ prakramakṛtaṃ /
yūpaikādaśinīpekṣa daśarathākṣāmekādaśo (parāṃ)paravāṃ rajjuṃ mītvā tasyāścaturviṃśena bhāgena vediṃvimimīte /
prakramasthānīyā bhavatītyukta (ktaṃ prācyekādaśinyāṃ) mekādaśinyāṃ /
prācyekādaśinīpakṣe ardhaṣaṣṭhāni padānyaṃsau yūpārdhaṃ bedeḥ purastāt padārthamātramaṃsamapacchidya tatpurastāt prāñcaṃ nidadhyāditi bodhāyanaḥ /
ekādaśaikādīśanīpakṣe ardhaṣaṣṭhāni padānyaṃsāvapacchidya tānyekādaśadhā vibhajya pṛṣṭhyāntā pṛṣṭhyādā dārabhya ekaṃ vibhāgaṃ madhye prāñcannidadhyāt /
children.translated_text: In the eleven-<s>yūpa</s> arrangement, having cut five and a half <s>padas</s> as the shoulders and dividing those eleven-fold, starting from the end and the beginning of the spine, one should place one division in the middle, east-wise.

children.text: taddakṣiṇataḥ uttarataś ca pañcapañca vibhāgān prāñco nidadhyāt /
children.translated_text: To the south and north of that, one should place five divisions each, east-wise.

children.text: agnivivṛddhau mahāvedi vivṛddhiḥ, prāgvaṃśaḥprācī cāntarālabahutve vivardhate /
children.translated_text: When the fire [altar] is enlarged, the <s>mahāvedī</s> is enlarged; the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> and the east-wise intervals increase when there are many [fires].
Enough of elaboration.

Now the divisions of the measurement of the sacrificial ground are stated — in <s>pada</s> measure, having made a ground suitable for the sacrificer, fifty-one [units] east-west and thirty transverse, and in its middle, having made a ground suitable for the sacrificial rite of that length, drawing a line east-west of that length in its middle and stretching a cord, having fixed pegs at its ends, beginning from the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> (front-beam shed) and onwards, one should construct it appropriately at the time of that ritual. At the western end, having constructed the <s>prāgvaṃśa</s> of sixteen in length and twelve in width, or twelve in length and nine in width, [placing] its frontal-beams three [paces] east — and so on, there itself. From that peg, three <s>padas</s> constitutes the <s>bahirvedī</s> (outer altar); at its end a peg. Then, to the east of that, thirty-six [constitutes] the <s>mahāvedī</s> east-wise; thirty to the west transversely; twenty-four to the east transversely. Having thus measured the <s>mahāvedī</s>, at the western end, three <s>padas</s> [is] the passage. To the east of that, nine <s>padas</s> east-west, eighteen <s>padas</s> north-south [is] the <s>sadas</s> (assembly shed), eighteen in north-south length; in its middle, to the south of the spine (<s>pṛṣṭhyā</s>), at one <s>pada</s> distance. That is the place of the <s>audumbarī</s> (udumbara-wood post). In the eastern half of the <s>sadas</s>, leaving a passage of half a <s>pada</s> at the eastern front, behind that on the spine, the <s>hotrīya</s> (Hotṛ's fire-pit) and other <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (fire-hearths) of <s>aratni</s> (cubit) measure or <s>piśīla</s> (span) measure. For each of those, to the north of each is a passage of the width of a <s>visa</s> (rod). In front of the <s>sadas</s>, three <s>padas</s> [is] the passage. East of that is the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation shed) of nine in length and width, or three <s>aratnis</s> in width and nine in length — this being the middle one, in the middle [one] the [sacred] chant, [while in] the other two chants silence, according to this view. '<s>Bodhāyana</s> [states]: ten in length and width is the <s>havirdhāna</s>.' From the peg at the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> (post-pit), to the west, one <s>pada</s> [is] the passage. Behind that, one <s>yuga</s> (yoke-length) is the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar). The interval between the <s>uttaravedī</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> is the <s>antarvedī</s> (inner altar). To the south of the spine is the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>, to the north the northern <s>havirdhāna</s>. At the southern haunch of the southern <s>havirdhāna</s> are the <s>uparavas</s> (bricks). Behind the <s>havirdhāna</s>, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's station), at arm's length to the south of the spine, at twelve [units], is the <s>pārjālīya</s> (fire-pit). Likewise, to the north of the same [spine] at twelve [units] is the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s>. All <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are <s>piśīla</s>-measured. From the shoulder of the <s>sadas</s>, to the north at three <s>padas</s> less a quarter and at nine <s>padas</s> less a quarter, [fix] pegs — those are the haunches of the <s>āgnīdhra</s> pavilion. Starting from the western end of the <s>havirdhāna</s>, at three <s>padas</s> east, to the north of the spine, at eleven less a quarter and at seventeen less a quarter, [fix] pegs — those are the shoulders of the <s>āgnīdhra</s> pavilion. Behind the twenty-sixth, at the eastern end of the spine, half is <s>antarvedī</s> and half is <s>bahirvedī</s>. '<s>Bodhāyana</s> [states]: the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> (post-pit) is three <s>padas</s> in diameter and three <s>padas</s> in circumference.' From the northern shoulder of the altar, to the north at one <s>prakrama</s>, the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit) is equal in size to the <s>uttaravedī</s>; the middle of the <s>cātvāla</s> is level with the altar-shoulder. At the half-end, from the <s>cātvāla</s>, to the west at twelve [units], the <s>utkara</s> (refuse-heap) of the <s>bahirvedī</s> is located. Between the altar-corner and the <s>utkara</s>, to the north at sixteen, is the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughter-shed) <s>dhiṣṇya</s>. This is in <s>pada</s> measure. In <s>prakrama</s> measure, however, the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s> are in <s>aratni</s> measure; or, from behind the <s>uttaravedī</s> of the fire, having gone three <s>prakramas</s> westward, the <s>havirdhāna</s> is transversely nine <s>aratnis</s> — and so on. The <s>sadas</s> is of dimensions as feasible. The <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are <s>piśīla</s>-measured; by <s>prakrama</s> alone all measurements. The <s>uttaravedī</s> is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>-measured, or ten <s>padas</s>, or one <s>yuga</s> — or fire at its place. Everything else is by <s>prakrama</s> measure. In the eleven-<s>yūpa</s> arrangement, having measured a cord of ten chariot-axle lengths as the eleventh (outermost) boundary, with a twenty-fourth part of that one measures the altar. '[The <s>tṛtīyakaraṇī</s>] serves in place of a <s>prakrama</s>' was stated in the eastern eleven-<s>yūpa</s> [arrangement]. In the eastern eleven-<s>yūpa</s> view, five and a half <s>padas</s> are the shoulders; half the <s>yūpa</s> [distance being] before the altar, having cut a <s>pada</s>-and-a-half from the shoulder, one should place [the cut piece] to the east of that, as <s>Bodhāyana</s> [states].
<s>Sundararāja's</s> [commentary].
(By the capability of the <s>prādeśa</s> [span])

children.text:
deśastu darśita eva "dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya' ityā dinā /
sarvatrāpi prakramairmāne aparasmādvedyāntāt prakramatrayamavaśiṣya navārātni sadaḥ /
uttaravedeḥ paścātprakramatrayamavaśiṣya navārātni havirdhānam /
padamāne tūktapramāṇānāṃ sadohavirdhānottaravedīnāmasaṃbhavādvedyanuguṇo nirdvāsaḥ kartavyaḥ /
cātvālastu śamyāmātra eva sarvatrāpi /
"śamyāmātraśvātvālaḥ' iti bodhāyanavacanāt /
atra ślokāḥ----
children.translated_text: The position has been shown by 'of the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>' and so on. Everywhere, in <s>prakrama</s> measurement, leaving three <s>prakramas</s> from the last (western) end of the altar, nine <s>aratnis</s> is the <s>sadas</s>. Leaving three <s>prakramas</s> behind the <s>uttaravedī</s>, nine <s>aratnis</s> is the <s>havirdhāna</s>. In <s>pada</s> measure, however, since the stated dimensions of the <s>sadas</s>, <s>havirdhāna</s>, and <s>uttaravedī</s> are impossible [to fit], an adjustment proportional to the altar must be made. The <s>cātvāla</s> (pit) is always of <s>śamyā</s> (goad) measure, from <s>Bodhāyana's</s> statement: 'The <s>cātvāla</s> is of <s>śamyā</s> measure.' Here are verses —
The <s>Saumikī</s> (Soma) altar is measured by <s>prakramas</s> of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>;
first at three, then nine, two-one-moon [i.e., 12], two-arrow-earth-two [i.e., 25];
one-one-two-arrow-one [pegs], pegs — ten and five;
the thirty-six-measure cord, its mark at two-eight [i.e., 28].
In the measurement, between the two end-pegs, twelve <s>prakramas</s> are prescribed;
the haunches at five-less, the <s>sadas</s> at the next-fourth.
Its corner at five-less; at ten suns [i.e., 10 units],
at the third [position], the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> with two intervals; their error is from the <s>prādeśa</s>.
At seventeen <s>Rudras</s> [i.e., 11 units], pegs at quarter-less here;

children.text: āgnīdhraṃ tatpañcame tu dhiṣṇyau dvādaśasu smṛtau // .5 //
children.translated_text: the <s>āgnīdhra</s> at the fifth of those; the [two] <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are prescribed at twelve.
At the sixth, at five, is the [oblation] shed; at fifty plus two,
at the seventh, the <s>āgnīdhra</s> as before; at nine, the <s>utkara</s> for men.
At eleven, the <s>havirdhāna</s>; reversing the end-pegs, as before;
at sixteen less a half, the <s>śāmitra</s> should be at twelve.
From the northern half, at the third [position], at thirteen-fourteen,
from the peg the <s>uttaravedī</s> should be; at the two penultimate [positions] with a half.
At the last, at twelve, the shoulders; the <s>cātvāla</s> to the north of the shoulder, at one <s>prakrama</s>;
before and behind the <s>sadas</s> and <s>havirdhāna</s>, one should leave five <s>prakramas</s>.
At the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>, behind, three <s>prakramas</s> should be left;
on both sides, two <s>prakramas</s> with two <s>aṅgulas</s> added.
One <s>aratni</s> measure in the middle is the mark of the <s>uparavas</s> (bricks);
thus indeed the measurement should be, also by <s>padas</s> of four kinds.
A <s>pada</s> with a fifth added is the desired width of a <s>dhiṣṇya</s>;
the <s>cātvāla</s> is of <s>śamyā</s> measure — <s>Bodhāyana</s> stated clearly;
otherwise there would be contradiction in the fire [altar]; and no other measure is found.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.
'It should be of <s>vyāyāma</s> (fathom) measure' — this is known for the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar (<s>citi</s>). || ĀpŚus 7.5 ||
'Square,' according to some; 'circular,' according to others. || ĀpŚus 7.6 ||
A <s>vyāyāma</s> is four <s>aratnis</s> (cubits).
That is the measure of the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar.
The view of some <s>śākhins</s> (Vedic school followers) is that the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar is square.
The <s>śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) of others is that the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar is circular.

children.text: karaṇaṃ vyāyāmasya tṛtīyāyāmaṃ saptamavyāsaṃ kārayet || ĀpŚus_7.7 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>karaṇa</s> (brick-mould): one should make it one-third of a <s>vyāyāma</s> in length and one-seventh of a <s>vyāyāma</s> in width. || ĀpŚus 7.7 ||

children.text:
caturaśrāyāṃ karaṇamucyate /
vyāyāmatṛtīyā pārśvamānī vyāyāmasaptamī tiryaṅnānī /
evaṃ karaṇaṃ kārayet /
kuryāditi vaktavye kārayediti vacanādanyaistakṣādibhiḥ pravīṇairnādhvaryuṇetyavagamyate /
kiyante 'neneṣṭakā iti karaṇaṃ dārumayam /
children.translated_text: The <s>karaṇa</s> is stated for the square [altar]. The lateral measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) is one-third of a <s>vyāyāma</s>; the transverse measure (<s>tiryaṅmānī</s>) is one-seventh of a <s>vyāyāma</s>. Thus the <s>karaṇa</s> should be made. Since 'kārayet' (one should have made) is said instead of 'kuryāt' (one should make), it is understood that it is to be done by other experts such as carpenters, not by the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) [himself]. 'How many bricks by this' — the <s>karaṇa</s> is made of wood.
They become twenty-one. || ĀpŚus 7.8 ||

children.text: tena karaṇena kṛtā iṣṭakāḥ ekaviṃśatiḥ tasyāṃ gārhapatyacitau bhavantīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bricks made by that <s>karaṇa</s> — twenty-one become [required] in that <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar — this is the completion [of the statement].
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
(The <s>vyāyāma</s>... is known)
A <s>vyāyāma</s> is four <s>aratnis</s>.
(Square, according to some)
According to some <s>śākhins</s>, both [shapes] exist. (The <s>karaṇa</s>... become [twenty-one])

children.text: kriyante 'neneṣṭakā iti karaṇam, tacca dārumayaṃ lohamayaṃ vā /

children.translated_text: The length is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>; the width is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-four <s>tilās</s> (sesame seeds).
The height is a fifth part of a <s>jānu</s> (knee-height).
'Twenty-one' — he states the derivation of the count.
For understanding the total count in [passages like] 'having five layers' and so on.
'That by which bricks are made' is the <s>karaṇa</s> (mould); and it is made of wood or metal.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Now, regarding the fire-altar construction (<s>agniciti</s>) —
(The <s>vyāyāma</s>... is known)
A <s>vyāyāma</s> is four <s>aratnis</s>.
(Square... according to some)
For the square [gārhapatya] —
(The <s>karaṇa</s>... become [twenty-one])

children.text:
tṛtīye dvātriṃśadaṅgulam /
saptamaṃ daśatilonaṃ caturdaśāṅgulam /
tā ekavi śatirbhavantyekaikasmin prastāre /
children.translated_text: One-third is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>. One-seventh, less ten <s>tilās</s>, is fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. They become twenty-one in each layer.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.
In the first layer, [the bricks are laid] with their length east-west; in the other, with their length north-south. || ĀpŚus 7.9 ||

children.text:
prāgāyāmāḥ--prāgāyatāḥ prathame prastāre /
udagāyāmāḥ--udagāyatāḥ dvitīye prastāre /
evasupahite bhedo na bhavati /
anena jñāyate sarvatra bhedo varjanīya iti /
śabdenaivoktaṃ bhagavatā bodhāyanena ""sarvatra bhedo varjanīyaḥ'' iti /
adharottarayoḥ parśvasaṃsthānaṃ bheda ityupadiśantīti /
anenācāryeṇoktametat "vyatyāsaṃ cinuyāt' iti /
children.translated_text: 'East-lengthened' — lengthened toward the east — in the first layer. 'North-lengthened' — lengthened toward the north — in the second layer. When thus placed, there is no gap. By this, it is understood that gaps are to be avoided everywhere. The revered <s>Bodhāyana</s> has stated this in so many words: 'Gaps are to be avoided everywhere.' They teach that the coincidence of side-positions in the lower and upper [layers] constitutes a gap. By this, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) has stated: 'One should pile in alternation.'
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
(East-lengthened, in the first layer)
When being placed, they should be east-lengthened.
(In the other, north-lengthened)

children.text:
aparasmin dvitīye tu udagāyatā bhaveyuḥ bhedābhāvāya /
uktaṃ ca bodhāyanena "sarvatra bhedānvarjayeta' iti /
children.translated_text: In the other, the second [layer], they should be north-lengthened, for the avoidance of gaps. And <s>Bodhāyana</s> has said: 'One should avoid gaps everywhere.'
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(East-lengthened)
The bricks are to be placed.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: maṇḍalāyāṃ mṛdo dehaṃ kṛtvā madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatyārdhavyāyāmena saha maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet || ĀpŚus_7.10a ||
children.translated_text: For the circular [gārhapatya], having made a body of clay, having fixed a peg in the middle, one should draw a circle with the half-<s>vyāyāma</s>. || ĀpŚus 7.10a ||

children.text:
yadi maṇḍalā gārhapatyacitiḥ mṛdo bhṛttikāyāḥ "ha' iti nipātaḥ atretyetasminnarthe /
ullekhanaṃ kṛtveti dehabimbaṃ ślakṣṇīkṛtya tanmadhye śaṅkuṃ nihatyārdhavyāyāmena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet /
tadvyāyāmamātraṃ ṇaṇḍalaṃ bhavati /
kecidatra sahaśabdaśravaṇādatīyeneti varṇayanti /
kṣetrasamatvāya tadanī psitamihācāryasya ardhavyāyāmeneti vadataḥ /
yadīpsita mabhaviṣyat mṛdo dehaṃ kṛtvā maṇḍalaṃ kuryādityevāvakṣyat /
uktaṃ tvādeśādanyaditi /
tāvatīṃ bhūmimiti vakṣyāti ca /
kathaṃ sahetyucyate? yo maṇḍalaṃ cikīrṣet sa evaṃ kṛtvār'dhavyāyāmena parilikhet /
ha iti nipātaḥ /
evamadhyāhṛtya yojanīyam /
athavā śrutireveyamevaṃbhūtā /
children.translated_text: If the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar is circular — 'of clay,' from clay or brick; 'ha' is a particle meaning 'here.' Having made the marking — having smoothed the clay body — having fixed a peg in its middle, one should draw a circle with the half-<s>vyāyāma</s>. That circle becomes of <s>vyāyāma</s> measure [in diameter]. Some, hearing the word 'saha' (with/together), explain it as 'with another [i.e., additional measure].' For the purpose of equality of area, this is what the <s>ācārya</s> intends when saying 'with the half-<s>vyāyāma</s>.' If that had been intended, he would have said simply 'having made a body of clay, one should make a circle.' But it has been said: 'something other than the instruction.' And he will say: 'that much ground.' How is 'saha' used? One wishing to make a circle should do thus: draw with the half-<s>vyāyāma</s>. 'Ha' is a particle. Having thus supplied [the word], it should be connected. Or, this is simply the <s>śruti</s> as it is.

children.text: tasmiṃś caturaśram avadadhyād yāvat sambhavet tan navadhā vyavalikhya traidham ekaikaṃ pradhikaṃ vibhajet || ĀpŚus_7.10b ||
children.translated_text: In that [circle], one should inscribe a square as large as possible; having divided that into nine [parts], one should divide each third into three additional [parts]. || ĀpŚus 7.10b ||

children.text:
tasminniti maṇḍalaṃ parāmṛsyate /
tasminmaṇḍale caturaśraṃ yāvacchete tāvaccaturaśraṃ likhet /
samapariṇāhaṃ caturdhā vibhajya avāntaradikṣu lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā teṣu sraktayo yathā bhavanti tathā caturaśramālikhet /
dikṣu catvāri dhanuḥsamāḥ /
taccaturaśraṃ navadhā vyavalikhya ekasya pramāṇena samacaturaśraṃ karaṇaṃ kārayet /
traidhamekaikaṃ pradhikaṃ vibhajen /
gamanāya pradhīyata iti pradhikam /
tacca pārśvadhanuḥ /
tatpratikṛtitvāt pradhikamityucyate /
ekaikaṃ pradhikaṃ tridhā kṛtvā karaṇāni kārayet /
children.translated_text: Having divided each <s>pradhika</s> into three, one should have bricks made.
Sixty <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) less four <s>tilās</s> (sesame seeds) is the measure of the square.

children.text: ṇaṇḍalamadhye tasya tṛtīyenaikaṃ karaṇaṃ pradhikamadhyaṃ dvāviṃśatitrayodaśābhyāṃ kārayet /
children.translated_text: With a third of that, in the middle of the circle, one should make one brick — a <s>pradhika</s>-middle [brick] — with [the measures] twenty-two and thirteen.
But one should cut [a brick] with a measure of thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>.

'In that' refers to the circle. In that circle, one should draw a square as large as can fit. Having divided the circumference into four [parts], making marks at the intermediate directions, one should draw the square so that the corners are at those [marks]. At the [cardinal] directions, four [segments] are bow-shaped. Having divided that square into nine [parts], one should have bricks (<s>karaṇas</s>) made of the measure of one [such part] — a square brick. Each <s>pradhika</s> (arc-segment) one should divide into three. '<s>Pradhika</s>' is so called because it 'advances' — it is the arc-bow. It is called '<s>pradhika</s>' because of its resemblance to that [wheel-part].

children.text:
yath.ā dhanurākāraṃ yathā jyāphalakayormadhye tilonamaṅgulaṃ bhavati tathonaṃ tribhistrayodaśāṅgulamekaṃ karaṇaṃ aratnimātraṃ tilābhyāmekaṃ saptaviṃśatyaṅgulamaṣṭabhistilairūnamekaṃ takṣet /
pūrvamaṅguladvayaṃ agniphalakābhyāṃ saha madhye yathā bhavati tathā tṛtīyena karaṇena viparyasyānyamevamiṣṭakāḥ kārayet /
children.translated_text: As is bow-shaped — so that between the bowstring-plank [the straight edge] and [the arc], there is an <s>aṅgula</s> less one <s>tila</s> — thus diminished by three [<s>tilās</s>], one brick of thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, one brick of <s>aratni</s>-measure (cubit), one of twenty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> less eight <s>tilās</s> — one should cut. Previously, the two <s>aṅgulas</s> of the fire-planks, together with the middle — as it should be — with the third brick reversed, one should have the other bricks made likewise.

children.text: upadhāne caturaśrasyāvāntaradeśān prati sraktīḥ sampādayet || ĀpŚus_7.11a ||
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, one should align the corners of the square toward the intermediate directions. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.11a ||

children.text:
upadhānakāle prathame prastāre avāntaradeśān koṇadeśān prati caturaśrasya sraktīḥsampādeyat saṃyojayet /
caturaśre nārdheṣṭakāḥśarate /
caturaśre naveṣṭakāḥśerate /
pradhikeṣu dvādaśa /
navasu dvādaśasu ca ekaviṃśatirbhavanti /
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, in the first layer, one should align — join — the corners (<s>sraktīs</s>) of the square toward the intermediate directions — the corner-directions. No half-bricks lie in the square. Nine bricks lie in the square; twelve in the <s>pradhikas</s> (arc-segments). In the nine and twelve, [the total is] twenty-one bricks.
In the other [alternate] layer, the middles. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.11b ||

children.text: dvitīye prastāre madhyāni caturaśre madhyāni avāntaradeśaṃ pratisampādayet /
children.translated_text: In the second layer, the middles — the middle-parts of the square — should be aligned toward the intermediate directions.

children.text: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_7.11c ||
children.translated_text: One should pile alternately, for as many layers as one wishes to make. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.11c ||

children.text:
yāvataḥ prastārānkartumicchet tāvadyvatyāsaṃ cinuyāt /
yaḥ prathamaḥsa tṛtīyaḥ /
pañcamaś ca yo dvitīyaḥsa caturthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For as many layers as one wishes to make, one should pile alternately. What is the first is [also] the third and fifth; what is the second is [also] the fourth.
It is known that the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (minor fire-seats) are of <s>piśīla</s>-measure. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.12 ||
Some [say they are] square; some [say they are] circular. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.13 ||

children.text:
bāhvorantarālaṃ piśīlamiti kecit /
muṣṭikṛto 'ratniḥ piśīlamityanyo /
prādeśaḥ piśīlamityapare /
caturaśrā dhiṣṇyā ityekeṣāṃ śrutiḥ /
parimaṇḍalā ityekeṣām /
children.translated_text: The interval between the arms is a <s>piśīla</s> — [say] some. The <s>aratni</s> (cubit) made with a fist is a <s>piśīla</s> — [says] another. A <s>prādeśa</s> (span) is a <s>piśīla</s> — [say] others. 'The <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are square' — is the Vedic text of some. 'Circular' — of others.

children.text: mṛdo dehān kṛtvāgnīdhrīyaṃ navadhā vyavalikhya, ekasyāḥ sthāne 'śmānam upapadhyāt || ĀpŚus_7.14 ||
children.translated_text: Having made clay bodies [molds], dividing the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (the fire-kindler's altar) into nine, in the place of one, one should lay a stone. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.14 ||

children.text: yathāsaṅkhyam itarā vyavalikhya yathāyogam upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_7.15 ||
children.translated_text: Having divided the others according to their number, one should lay [them] as appropriate. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 7.15 ||

children.text: aśmanavamā iti siddhe ' pyekasyāḥ sthāna iti vacanaṃ dravyeṣṭakānāmavaṭeṣūpadhānasya jñāpanārtham /
children.translated_text: Although it is established that the stone is the ninth, the statement 'in the place of one' is for the purpose of indicating that material-bricks are to be laid in the pits.
It has been clearly stated by <s>Baudhāyana</s>:
'Materials that are obstacles to people should be laid in the pits.'

children.text: yathāyogamupadadhyāt agnikalpe yāvatsaṅkhyākā dhiṣṇiyā āmnātāḥ tāvatsaṅraṣyākā tā vyavalikhya karaṇāni kṛtvā yathāyogaṃ yathā yujyate tatho padadhyāt //
children.translated_text: 'As appropriate, one should lay' — in the fire-ritual (<s>agnikalpa</s>), as many <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fires as are prescribed, that many should be counted, divided, bricks made, and laid as is appropriate — as it is fitting.
'Clay bodies' is an illustration of [the rule] 'in that, a square,' etc.
Thus [ends] the seventh section.
Thus in the <s>Āpastamba Sūtra Vivaraṇa</s>, in <s>Kapardi Svāmī's</s> commentary, in the chapter called '<s>Śulba</s>,'
[this is] the second <s>paṭala</s> (chapter).
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.

children.text: maṇḍalāyāṃ gārhapatyacityāṃ karaṇaṃ bahuprayāsasādhyamiti prakārāntareṇeṣṭakāsampattiṃ brūte /
children.translated_text: Since in the circular <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar the brick-making requires much effort, he states the procurement of bricks by another method.
(On 'the circle... one should draw')

children.text: same śucau kacidbhūtale vyāyāmamātrādhikavistāraṃ jānupañcamordhvapramāṇaṃ saṃsarjanīyairdravyaiḥsaṃsṛṣṭāyāḥ saṃprakṛṣṭāyā mṛdo biṃmbaṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye vyāyāmacaturaśrakṣetraṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye śaṅkuṃ nikhāya ardhavyāyāmena saha atiśayatṛtīyena saha maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet //
children.translated_text: On some level, clean ground, having made a mold of clay mixed with <s>saṃsarjanīya</s> materials, of width slightly more than a <s>vyāyāma</s> (fathom) and height up to five [finger-breadths] above the knees, having made in its center the area of a <s>vyāyāma</s>-square into a circle, fixing a peg in its center, with half a <s>vyāyāma</s> together with the third of the excess, one should draw a circle.
(On 'in that... it would be')

children.text: tasminmaṇḍale yāvat pramāṇaṃ caturaśraṃ kartuṃ śakyaṃ tāvallikhet, evaṃ kṛte maṇḍalamadhye samacaturaśraṃ ekaṃ, tatpārśveṣu catvāri dhanurākārāṇi bhavanti, tāni pradhaya ityucyante /
children.translated_text: In that circle, one should draw as large a square as can be made; when this is done, in the center of the circle there is one square, and on its sides there are four bow-shaped [segments] — these are called <s>pradhis</s> (fellies/arc-segments).
A <s>pradhi</s> by name is a component of a chariot-wheel.
'<s>Pradhi</s>' is so called because 'one advances' or 'runs' by it.
Because of resemblance to that [wheel-part], the segments of the circle too are called <s>pradhis</s>.
(On 'that should be divided into nine')

children.text:
taccaturaśraṃ navadhā vibhajeta /
tribhāgāvalekhanena navadhā vibhajya pradhiṃ tvekaikaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajet /
caturaśraṃ naveṣṭakaṃ catvāraḥ pradhayaḥ tridhā vibhaktā dvādaśamācyaḥ ekaviṃśatiriṣṭakāḥ /
maṇḍalamadhye caturaśrakaraṇo 'yaṃ prayogaḥ /
maṇḍalamadhye prācyudīcīṃ sampādya maṇḍalalekhāyāḥ parīṇāhaṃ caturdhā saṃbhujya saṃbhogeṣu tatra lakṣaṇāni kṛtvā lakṣaṇāllakṣaṇaṃ likhet /
evaṃ kṛte maṇḍalamadhye caturaśraṃ bhavati /
tatra viṣkambhārdhaṃ catuḥ pañcadaśāṅgulayor'dhadvāviṃśatitilāś ca madhyacaturaśrakaraṇī /
(sapta) saptatiraṅgulayo 'ṣṭatilāś ca tasyāsya tṛtīyo bhāgaḥ /
pañcaviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāś ca karaṇāni kuryata, tānyucyante--sarvataḥ pañcaviṃśatitilasahitaṃ pañcaviṃśatyaṅgulamekaṃ karaṇaṃ pradhiṣu /
trīṇi karaṇāni /
pradhimadhyāścaturbhiḥ /
tasya pārśve caturdaśāṅgulayaḥ saptasaptadaśa tilāś ca /
pṛṣṭhaṃ pañcaviṃśatitilasahitaṃ pañcaviṃśatyaṅgulamukham /
ekonatriṃśadaṅgulaṃ (pādonatriṃśaduṅgalaṃ) taṃ viṣkambhārdhapramāṇayā rajjvā karkaṭena vā vilikhya takṣayet /

children.translated_text: At the ends of the <s>pradhis</s>, [the brick has] that very side-measure and a sixth[-portion].

children.text: mukhaṃ tu ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ, dakṣiṇasya dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ savyasyottaram /
children.translated_text: The face however is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>; the right side of the right [<s>pradhi</s>] and the left side of the left [correspond].
These very [bricks] are the bricks for the four <s>pradhis</s>.
Thus the four-brick-type circular fire-altar [is complete].

That square should be divided into nine. By drawing into thirds, having divided [it] into nine, each <s>pradhi</s> should be divided into three. The square has nine bricks; the four <s>pradhis</s>, divided into three, have twelve bricks — twenty-one bricks [in total]. This is the procedure for making a square within the circle. For [constructing] the square within the circle, having established the east-west and north-south [lines], dividing the circumference into four folds, making marks at those [points], one should draw from mark to mark. When this is done, a square exists within the circle. There, the half-diameter being four [units], sixty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-two and a half <s>tilās</s> is the constructive measure of the central square. Seventy-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> and eight <s>tilās</s> is its third part. Twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-five <s>tilās</s> — one should make the bricks; these are described: one brick of twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-five <s>tilās</s> on all sides, in the <s>pradhis</s>. Three bricks; the <s>pradhi</s>-middles are [made] with four. Its sides are fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, seven and seventeen <s>tilās</s>. The back is twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-five <s>tilās</s>, the face [likewise]. Twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> (or twenty-nine and three-quarter <s>aṅgulas</s>) — that should be drawn and cut with a cord of half-diameter measure or with a compass.
(On 'at the time of laying... [the] layer')

children.text: maṇḍalāyāmupadhānakāle prayamaprastāre caturaśrasya sraktīḥ koṭīḥ avāntaradeśāna koṇadiśaḥ prati saṃyojayet /
dvitīye prastāre caturaśrasya madhyāni avāntaradeśān prati saṃyojeyat /
children.translated_text: In the second layer, the middles of the square should be aligned toward the intermediate directions.
Thus there would be no splitting (<s>bheda</s>).

children.text: bhedo nāma prastārānvayagatānāmiṣṭakānāṃ prānteṣu sāmyaṃ, tatsarvatra pariharaṇīyamiti tatra tatra vyākhyānavacanāt jñāyate /
children.translated_text: 'Splitting' means the alignment of the edges of bricks across successive layers; that is to be avoided everywhere — this is known from the explanatory statements in those places.
And there is also the statement: 'One should avoid splitting everywhere.'
At the time of laying in the circular [altar], in the first layer, one should align the corners of the square — the points — toward the intermediate directions.
(On 'one should pile alternately... as many layers as one wishes to make')

children.text:
vyatyasya vyatyasyetyarthaḥ /
prastārā iṣṭakāḥsaṃghātavi śeṣāḥ /
te pañcacitīkaṃ cinvīteti vihitā yāvantaḥsyuḥ tāvanto vyātyasya vyatyasya cinuyāditi asmādevāvadhāraṇāt jñāyate, agnidharmā iṣṭakāyatanordhvapramāṇādayo 'tra prāpnuvantīti prastāreṣu prathamatṛtoyapañcamāḥsamāḥ /
dvitīyacaturthau samau nanu kathaṃ labhyate atiśayatṛtīyeneti /
ucyate--saha śabda sāmarthyāccaturaśrasya maṇḍalakaraṇe atiśayatṛtīyasya karaṇīśeṣatvavidhānāccātiśayatṛtīyena saha viṣkambārdhena maṇḍalakaraṇam /
etasyā eva gārhapatyaciteḥ caturaśramaṇḍalatayā prāpte kṣetrasya sāmyavabhimatamiti caturaśramaṇḍalakaraṇanyāyo 'nusartavyaḥ /
caturaśrapūrvakatvaṃ cāsya maṇḍalakaraṇasya dṛśyate /
tato 'pi sa evānusartavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having alternated repeatedly' — this is the meaning. 'Layers' are specific groupings of bricks. Those prescribed as 'one should pile five layers' — as many as there would be, that many one should pile alternating repeatedly. From this very restrictive statement it is known that the fire-properties, the <s>iṣṭakā</s> dimensions, the height-measures, etc. apply here in the layers. The first, third, and fifth are alike; the second and fourth are alike. Now, how is [the expression] 'with the third of the excess' obtained? It is said: by the force of the word 'together with,' and because in making a square into a circle, the third of the excess is prescribed as the remainder of the constructive measure, the circle is made with the half-diameter together with the third of the excess. Since in this very <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-altar, equality of area is desired for both the square and circular [forms], the principle of square-to-circle conversion should be followed. And this circle-making is seen to be preceded by the square. Therefore, that very [principle] should be followed.

children.text: kecittu saheti dvipadaṃ kṛtvā sārdhavyāyāmena sambandhayanti /
children.translated_text: Some, however, making 'together with' into two words, connect it with 'one and a half <s>vyāyāma</s>.'
In the specific purpose of these two words, we see no [advantage] for them.
Therefore, it is well-stated: 'with the third of the excess together [with the half-diameter].'
(On '<s>piśīla</s>... is known')
'The interval between the arms is a <s>piśīla</s>' — [says] <s>Baudhāyana</s>.

children.text: dhiṣṇyā agnayaḥ "agnayo vā atha dhiṣṇiyāḥ' iti darśanāt, tacchabdena tadāyatanāni lakṣyante /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhiṣṇyas</s>' are fires — from the statement '<s>agnayas</s> (fires) are indeed <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>.' By that word, their seats (altar-sites) are indicated.
The sites — the ground-areas of the fires — are of <s>piśīla</s>-measure.
In the absence of a specific exception, even when the shapes differ, the equality of the area holds.
Three <s>padas</s> is a <s>piśīla</s>; 'the <s>aratni</s> made with a fist is a <s>piśīla</s>' — [say] some.
(On 'square, say some... [circular], say some')
This has been covered. Here, in the ritual with fire-altar construction, he states a special point.
(On 'clay [molds]... one should lay')

children.text:
mudo dehān kṛtvā mṛtsambandhino dahānupacayān bimbāni kṛtyā āgnīdhrīyamekaṃ navadhā prāktvenodaktevana ca tridhā vyavalikhya madhyasthamekamekenāśmānā upadadhyāt /
anyāṃstatpramāṇābiraṣṭakābiritarān hotrīyādīnāṃ mṛdo dehān yathā sahkhyaṃ yasyayasya dhiṣṇiyāgneḥ yāyā saṅkhyā dvādaśa ṣoḍaśa ekaviṃśatiṃ caturviṃśatimityādyā tayā saṃkhyayā taṃ taṃ vyavalikhya yathāyogaṃ yatrayatra deśe yāyā iṣṭakā yujyate tatratatra tāṃ tāṃ iṣṭakāmupadadhyāt /
dvādaśa ṣoḍaśa ekaviṃśatiṃ caturviṃśatiṃ vā hotrīye, ekādaśa brāhnaṇācchaṃsīye, ṣaṭ mārjālīye, aṣṭāvaṣṭāvanyoṣu dhiṣṇiyeṣūpadadhātīti vijñāyate iti /
anyadhiṣṇyāḥ praśāstrīyapotrīyaneṣṭīyācchāvākīyacātvālaśāmitrāvabhṛthāḥ /
karaṇāni vā kṛtveṣṭakāḥ kuryāt /
caturaśrapakṣe sarvataḥ prādeśāḥ hotrīyasya, dvādaśapakṣe prādeśe dve navāṅgule dve, ṣoḍaśapakṣe sarbato navakāni, ekaniṃśatipakṣe navake dve saptāṅgulayaḥ saptatilāś ca dve, tadekaṃ sarvataḥ saptatilāḥsaptāṅgulaya ekaṃ, atra caturaśramekataḥ pañcadhā vibhajya caturo bhāgān prathamena caturdhā vibhajet /
dvitīyenaikaṃ pañcadhā /
caturviṃśatipakṣe 'yete eva karaṇe /
tatra pūrvavat pañcadhā vibhajya caturo bhāgān saptatilasaptāṅgulena pañcadhā vibhajet /
itareṇaikaṃ caturdhā /
brāhnaṇācchaṃsīyasyāṣṭau hotrīye dvādaśyaḥ, tisra āgnīdhrīyāḥ, mārjālīyaḥsyaikataḥ prādeśāḥ, anyato 'dhyardhāḥ ṣaṭ /
anyeṣāṃ potrūyādīnāṃ āgnīdhrīyeṣṭakāḥ ṣaṇmārjālīye aṣṭake dve /
maṇḍalapakṣe karaṇabāhulyaprasaṅgādyavalekhanamevocyate /
āgnīdhrīyasya prākcodakca tredhā vibhāgaḥ /
hotrūyasya dvādaśapakṣe ekatastridhā vibhāgo 'nyataścaturdhā /
ṣoḍaśapakṣe sarvataścaturdhā /
ekaviṃśatipakṣe tvekataḥ pañcadhā kṛtvā caturo bhāgāṃścaturdhā vibhajya caturo bhāgān pañcadhā kṛtvānyaṃbhāgaṃ caturdhā vibhajet /
ekādaśapakṣe tvekataśvaturdhā vibhajya trīna trodhā kṛtvā anyaṃ dvidhā vibhajet /

children.translated_text: In the six-brick option, on one side into three, the other into two.

children.text: aṣṭapakṣe caikatastridhā vibhajya dvau bhāgau tridhā kṛtvānyaṃ dvidhā kuryāt /
children.translated_text: In the eight-brick option, on one side dividing into three, the two parts into three, and the other into two.

children.text: dhiṣṇyānāmekacitīkatvāt sukaratvā ccaiṣa eva prakāro varamityācāryo manyate /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (subsidiary fire-altars) are of single-layer [construction], and because of the ease [of this method], the teacher considers this very procedure to be preferable.
Therein is a verse:

Having made clay bodies — i.e., molds made of clay-combined accumulations — having made the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> (fire-kindler's [altar]) into nine by drawing lines from east-to-west and north-to-south, dividing by three, one should lay one stone in the middle position. The other [positions] — with bricks of that measure, for the <s>hotrīya</s> (invoker's altar) and other [<s>dhiṣṇyas</s>], having divided the clay bodies, each <s>dhiṣṇya</s> fire's [altar] by its respective number — twelve, sixteen, twenty-one, or twenty-four — having divided each by that number, at whatever location whatever brick is appropriate, there one should lay that brick. [The numbers are:] twelve, sixteen, twenty-one, or twenty-four in the <s>hotrīya</s>; eleven in the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>; six in the <s>mārjālīya</s>; eight each in the other <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> — this is known. The other <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are: <s>prāśāstrīya</s>, <s>potrīya</s>, <s>neṣṭīya</s>, <s>acchāvākīya</s>, <s>cātvāla</s>, <s>śāmitra</s>, and <s>avabhṛtha</s>. Or, having made constructive measures, one should make bricks. In the square option, for the <s>hotrīya</s>, a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) on all sides; in the twelve-brick option, two of <s>prādeśa</s>-measure and two of nine <s>aṅgulas</s>; in the sixteen-brick option, nine [<s>aṅgula</s> bricks] on all sides; in the twenty-one-brick option, two of nine [<s>aṅgulas</s>] and two of seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with seven <s>tilās</s>, one of seven <s>tilās</s> and seven <s>aṅgulas</s> on all sides — there, dividing the square on one side into five, and four parts of those by the first into four; the second, one into five. In the twenty-four-brick option, these same bricks [apply]; there, dividing into five as before, the four parts by [a measure of] seven <s>tilās</s> and seven <s>aṅgulas</s> into five; the other, one into four. For the <s>brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>: eight <s>hotrīya</s> [bricks] of twelve[-measure], three <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> [bricks]; the <s>mārjālīya</s> has one side of <s>prādeśa</s>-measure, the other side one-and-a-half — six [bricks]. For the others — <s>potrīya</s> etc. — <s>āgnīdhrīya</s> bricks; in the <s>mārjālīya</s> of six, [and] in the [group of] eight, two. In the circular option, because of the proliferation of brick-types, only the [method of] drawing lines is stated. For the <s>āgnīdhrīya</s>: division from east and north into three. For the <s>hotrīya</s>: in the twelve-brick option, division on one side into three and the other into four; in the sixteen-brick option, into four on all sides; in the twenty-one-brick option, on one side into five, dividing the four parts into four, the four parts into five, and the other part into four.
'For the fire-altar of <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure (fathom-measure), the mold (<s>karaṇa</s>) should be of wood;
or of metal — it should be made of four planks; that is now stated.'
'The length is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>; [the width] should be thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s>;
twenty-four <s>tilas</s> should be the breadth of the mold.'
'For the circular [altars], the molds should be of four kinds:
one in the middle, three on the rim — these are stated in order.'
'Twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-five <s>tilas</s>
on all sides — one mold; in the middle, by this [measure], the brick-form [is made].'

children.text: pradhiṣu trīṇi tāni syuḥ pradhyante karaṇaṃ tribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'On the rims (<s>pradhis</s>), three of those should be; the rim is [formed] with three
planks; the middle-of-the-rim [mold] with four planks becomes the mold.'
'The back (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>): twenty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s>;
the sides: fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with seventeen <s>tilas</s>.'
'One-and-a-quarter [<s>aṅgulas</s>] minus a <s>tila</s>, thirty — twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s>
should be the face of the middle-of-the-rim mold, at both ends also.'
'In the back and sides, the face [of these] is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>;

children.text: antayoryatra yasya syātpārśvaṃ nānyasya tatra tat //
children.translated_text: at the ends, where one's side exists, the [side of] another does not exist there.'
'The faces of the molds here [are shaped] with a cord of half-diameter measure;
having drawn, one should carve; or one may draw with a compass.'
'The <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> are of thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> in length, equal on all sides;
therein, according to number, the molds are now stated.'
'From one side a <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span, 12 aṅgulas), from the other eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s> —
made by this [mold], in the <s>Mārjālīya</s> <s>dhiṣṇya</s>, there are six bricks.'
'A <s>prādeśa</s> on all sides — in the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>, [bricks] made by that;
twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> on one side, nine <s>aṅgulas</s> on the other —'
'In the <s>Hotrīya</s> [<s>dhiṣṇya</s>], with twelve [<s>aṅgulas</s>], twelve bricks are made by that.'
'Nine <s>aṅgulas</s> on all sides should be in the <s>Hotrīya</s>; by that, sixteen [bricks].'
'Seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s> on one side;
nine <s>aṅgulas</s> on the other side should be the mold, in the twenty-one [brick dhiṣṇya].'
'Seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s> on all sides —
this should be in the twenty-one [brick dhiṣṇya] here; in the twenty-four [brick], both of these [molds are used].'
'In the first, the twenty-one [brick type] should be — sixteen [bricks] by one [mold], and five [by the other];
in the twenty-four [brick type], by the second — twenty, and the rest otherwise.'
'Those [bricks] which are a <s>prādeśa</s> and [also] nine <s>aṅgulas</s> — eight of those and also three
[make] the <s>prādeśa</s>-[size] <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsi</s> <s>dhiṣṇya</s>; but with one [additional], ten.'
'The <s>prādeśa</s>-[size], six, <s>pada</s>-and-a-half, two... in the eight[-brick type], the rule;
in the <s>Potrīya</s> and others, the filling [with bricks] is as appropriate on all sides.'
'Since in the single-layer <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> there is no scope for [staggering] joints,
the multiplicity of molds would be due to the irregularity of numbers alone.'
'Having drawn [the lines] according to number, one should place the bricks here;
"as appropriate" — thus indeed did the teacher state regarding the circular [altar].'
'When the diagonal (<s>karṇa</s>) is diminished by the excess portion, [and the result] divided by the ground of the hypotenuse-pair,

children.text: hṛte phalena (phalone) hīnāyā yujo vā yadbhuvo daram //
children.translated_text: divided by the result [obtained from] the ground of the diminished [area], or the slight [difference] of the ground of the pair —'
'When the square of this diagonal is subtracted from the square of that [hypotenuse],

children.text: pariśiṣṭasya mūlaṃ tu lambakaṃ tadvido viduḥ //
children.translated_text: the square root of the remainder — the knowers know that as the perpendicular (<s>lambaka</s>).'
'A cord measured by the altar's eastward-line, enclosed by the half-interval,
stretched north-south — in the eastern and western halves of the <s>vedī</s> —'
'The two second [points] should be known as the upper altar (<s>uttara-vedī</s>) northward;
the middle region, the tri-middle, of the fire, in the eastern and western [parts] —'
'By the mark, for the purpose of the point, in the second one draws aside;
and in the western [part], to the north also, the point should be drawn aside.'
'Reversing in the eastern [part], the southern and northern points
having been made, the breadth in the fourth should be the mark of both.'
'At those two marks, one should cast a line or cord eastward;
to the south of the line should be taken for the circle-purpose; to the north one should discard.'
'In the circumference, [taking] one-fourth of six, [at] the bent-mark curve,
the line from mark to mark — that of the quadrilateral, with excess —'
'From the root of twice the square of the half-diameter,
the <s>karaṇī</s> (producer-line/side) of the quadrilateral in the circle is calculated.'
'Or, by the root of half the square of the diameter, the <s>karaṇī</s>-square
[is determined] for the quadrilateral in the circle, to the extent possible.'
'A cord placed diagonally, to the extent possible —
the diameter of the quadrilateral's [inscribed] circle, they declare indeed.'
'When the square of half the diameter is subtracted from
the square of the [full] diameter internally, the root of the remainder is the half-[segment] mark.'
'Of the diameter, [when] the arc-chord-half seized by the half[-segment] is squared,
and from the square of the former chord-half, the square of the half-diameter —'
'When subtracted, the root of the remainder is the head (<s>śiras</s>) of that bow [arc];
the square of the chord with six multiplied — and the square-of-the-square of that [head] —'
'The bow (<s>kodaṇḍa</s>) multiplied by the arrow (<s>śara</s>), halved — that is the result of the bow [arc-area].'

children.text: viṣkambha ātmadviguṇena('pi)yojyaḥ sa cātmaviṃśena sa pañcamākhyām /
children.translated_text: 'The diameter should be joined with its own double, and that with its own twentieth, and that receives the designation "fifth";

children.text: sapañcaviṃśena ca tau sametau vyāsena saiṣā pariṇāhallaptiḥ //
children.translated_text: and with its own twenty-fifth — those two combined with the diameter: this is the derivation of the circumference.'

children.text: nemidvirekādaśavātrakāryas tadbhāga ekaś ca tathā dvidhā ca /
children.translated_text: 'The rim (<s>nemi</s>) should be made as two-elevenths; one part of that, and likewise doubled;

children.text: vyāsaḥsvarāṃśāḥ paridheḥsaha syur bhāgāṃśaturyeṇa sa saptamena //
children.translated_text: the diameter with its own parts, together with the circumference-parts, with a fourth of the portion and a seventh.'
Thus in the <s>Karavindīya</s> commentary on the <s>Āpastamba</s> sūtra exposition, in the inquiry called <s>Śulba</s>,
the second <s>paṭala</s> (section).
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Since there is much to be said about the molds for circular [altars], he states the method of [laying] bricks without those [complex molds] —
'One should divide the circle...'

children.text:
deha--upacayaḥṣaḍuṅgalotsedhaḥ /
saheti nipāto vākyālaṃ kāre /
sa iti vā cchedaḥ /
"ardhavyāyāmena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet' ityeva satyāṣāḍhaḥ /
caturaśraṃ saviśeṣeṇa viṣkambhārdhena catustilonenāṣṭaṣaṣṭyaṅgulenāvadadhyāt /
caturaśraṃ navadhā kṛtvā prathikān tredhā vibhajhet /
prathireva prathikaḥ /
prathiśvakraparyantaḥ /
athavā karaṇaireveṣṭakāḥ kuryāt /
trīṇi karaṇāni--samacaturaśraṃ prathimadhyaṃ prathyantamiti /
atra samacaturaśraṃ dvāviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ saikaviṃśatitilam /
prathimadhyasya pārśvamānyāḥ pramāṇametadeva /
tiryaṅnānyā daśatilonatrayodaśāhgule ekaṃ pārśvaṃ phalakaṃ dhanurākāraṃ takṣet /
children.translated_text: The breadth of one side-plank is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> minus ten <s>tilas</s>; [that plank] should be carved in bow-shape,

children.text: yathā aṅguliḥ dvādaśatilāś ca śarapramāṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: such that the arrow-measure is one <s>aṅgula</s> and twelve <s>tilas</s>.
The rim-end, however — the measure [of its straight sides]

children.text: tasyāpi caturaśravadekaṃ pārśvaṃ, trayodaśāṅgulaṃ daśatilonamaparaṃ, ṣaḍviṃśakaṃ tiladvayonamaparaṃ, taddhanuriva takṣet, yathā aṅguliḥ saptaviṃśatiś ca tilāḥśaro bhavati //
children.translated_text: is the same as the [equal-]square on one side; the other is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> minus ten <s>tilas</s>; the third is twenty-six minus two <s>tilas</s>; that [curved side] should be carved like a bow, such that the arrow is one <s>aṅgula</s> and twenty-seven <s>tilas</s>.

'<s>Deha</s>' (body) — the thickness is six <s>aṅgulas</s> height. '<s>Saha</s>' is a particle for sentence-ornamentation. Or 'sa' is the section-marker. '<s>Satyāṣāḍha</s> [says]: "One should draw a circle with the half-<s>vyāyāma</s> (half-fathom)."' One should place the quadrilateral with the <s>saviśeṣa</s> (with-remainder) of the half-diameter — sixty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> minus four <s>tilas</s>. Having made the quadrilateral ninefold, one should divide the rims (<s>pradhis</s>) into three. The <s>pradhi</s> itself is the <s>pradhika</s>. The <s>pradhi</s> is the wheel-rim boundary. Alternatively, one may make bricks by molds alone. Three molds [are needed]: equal-square, rim-middle, and rim-end. Here the equal-square is twenty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-one <s>tilas</s>. The side-measure of the rim-middle is this same measure.
'In the filling, one should desire [to avoid joints].'

children.text:
maṇḍalacaturaśrayoḥsādhāraṇamidaṃ bhedaparihārāya, anenaiva jñāyate sarvatra bhedo varjanīya iti /
tathāca bodhāyanaḥ------
children.translated_text: This [rule] is common to both the circular and quadrilateral [altars], for the avoidance of joint-alignment. By this alone it is known that joints should be avoided everywhere. And so <s>Bodhāyana</s> [states] —

children.text: bhedān varjayedadharottarayoḥ pārśvasaṃdhānaṃ bheda ityācakṣate, tadādyānteṣu na vidyate--iti /
children.translated_text: 'One should avoid joints; the alignment of sides in upper and lower [layers] is called a joint (<s>bheda</s>); that does not exist at the beginning and end [of a row].'
'The <s>piśīla</s> (quarter-unit) is known [from scripture].'

children.text:
viśīlaṃ pañcadhā varṇayanti--bāhvorantarālamityekam, kṛtamu ṣṭimaratniṃ(kṛtamuṣṭirara tniḥ) dvitīyam /
akṛtamuṣṭimaratniṃ tṛtīyaṃ, dvātriṃśadaṅgulaṃ caturthaṃ, ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ pañcamamiti /
children.translated_text: The <s>piśīla</s> is described in five ways: 'the interval between the two arms' — that is one; 'the cubit with a made fist' — the second; 'the cubit without a made fist' — the third; 'thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>' — the fourth; 'thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>' — the fifth.
'Having made quadrilaterals —'
'One should make those' — this is to be supplied.
'The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (fire-priest) should place [them].'

children.text:
itarān dhiṣṇiyān yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vyavalikhya dvādaśa ṣoḍaśetyādi hotrīye, ekādaśa brāhnaṇācchaṃsīye, ṣaṇmārjālīye, aṣṭāvaṣṭāvanyoṣviti /
teṣāṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vibhāgā iti kecidāhuḥ /
sama catuhaśrāṇāṃ dhiṣṇiyānāṃ samacaturaśrā eveṣṭakāḥ kāryāḥ caturaśramādeśādanyaditi /
tavāratnīviṣkambhāṇāṃ dhiṣṇiyānā miṣṭakā aṣṭāṅgulā āgnīdhrīyasya /
hotrīyasya dvādaśakasya madhye catasraścaturaṅgulāḥ /
parito 'ṣṭāṅgulāḥ /
ṣoḍaśike ṣaḍaṅgulāḥsarvāḥ /
ekaviṃśakasya madhye nava caturaṅgulāḥ, parito dvādaśa ṣaḍaṅgulā /
caturviṃśakasya koṇe 'pvaṣṭāṅgulāḥ, śeṣo viṃśatiścaturaṅgulāḥ /
vlāhnaṇācchaṃsīye sapta ṣaḍaṅgulā, catasro navāṅgulāḥ /
mārjālīye pañcāṣṭāṅgulāḥ /
anye tvāhuḥ--yathāsaṃkhyamitarāniti vacanāt sarvā iṣṭakāstulyakṣetrā eva /
tatra samacaturakṣāṇāmeva kartumaśakyatvāddīrghacaturaśrā api kriyeranniti /
tanmate 'pyāgnīdhrī yasya pūrvavat /
hotrīyasya dvādaśakasyeṣṭakā aṣṭāṅgulāyāmāḥ ṣaḍaṅgulavyāsāḥ /
ṣoḍaśakasya pūrvavadeva /
ekaviṃśakasya tu aṣṭāṅgulāyāmā aratnisa(pta)mavyāsāḥ /
(caturviṃśakasya ṣaḍaṅgulā yāmāścaturaṅgulavyāsāḥ /
mārjālīyasya prādeśāyāmā aṣṭāṅgulir vyāsāḥ aṣṭakānāṃ prādeśāyāmāḥṣaḍaṅgulavyāsāḥ) /
brāhnaṇācchaṃsīyasya dve saraṇe aṣṭāṅgulāyāmaṃ sāṣṭādaśatilaṣaḍaṅgulavyāsamekaṃ karaṇam /

children.translated_text: By that, three bricks of six-<s>aṅgula</s> width result.
Another [mold] of nine-<s>aṅgula</s> length minus nine <s>tilas</s>.
By that, eight bricks.
For the others of <s>piśīla</s>-measure, bricks should be observed following this [pattern].

The other <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>, having drawn [the lines] according to number — twelve or sixteen in the <s>Hotrīya</s>, eleven in the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>, six in the <s>Mārjālīya</s>, eight each in the others. And their divisions are as possible — so say some. For the square <s>dhiṣṇyas</s>, only square bricks should be made — because of the prescription of 'quadrilateral' and nothing else. Of the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> with <s>aratni</s>-diameter: bricks of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> for the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>. For the <s>Hotrīya</s> of twelve [bricks]: four [bricks of] four <s>aṅgulas</s> in the middle, eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] around. In the sixteen-[brick type]: all of six <s>aṅgulas</s>. For the twenty-one [brick type]: nine [bricks of] four <s>aṅgulas</s> in the middle, twelve of six <s>aṅgulas</s> around. For the twenty-four [brick type]: eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] at the corners, the remaining twenty of four <s>aṅgulas</s>. In the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>: seven of six <s>aṅgulas</s>, four of nine <s>aṅgulas</s>. In the <s>Mārjālīya</s>: five of eight <s>aṅgulas</s>. Others, however, say: since the statement says 'the others according to number,' all bricks should be of equal area. There, since it is impossible to make all of them as equal squares, oblongs may also be made. In that view also: for the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>, as before. For the twelve-[brick] <s>Hotrīya</s>: bricks of eight-<s>aṅgula</s> length and six-<s>aṅgula</s> width. For the sixteen-[brick type]: as before. For the twenty-one [brick type]: of eight-<s>aṅgula</s> length and cubit-seventh width. (For the twenty-four [brick type]: of six-<s>aṅgula</s> length and four-<s>aṅgula</s> width. For the <s>Mārjālīya</s>: of <s>prādeśa</s>-length and eight-<s>aṅgula</s> width. For the eight-[brick types]: of <s>prādeśa</s>-length and six-<s>aṅgula</s> width.) For the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>: two rows — one mold of eight-<s>aṅgula</s> length and six-<s>aṅgula</s> width with eighteen <s>tilas</s>.

children.text:
atha parimaṇḍalānāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaviṣkambānāṃ āgnīdhrīyasya madhye prādeśavyāsaṃ parimaṇḍalamaśmānaṃ nidhāya parito 'ṣṭāviṣṭakāstāsāṃ karaṇaṃ, pārśve dvādaśāṅgule, caturdaśāṅgulamaṣṭatilonamekaṃ tiryakphalakaṃ, taddhanuriva takṣet, yathā aṅguliḥ dvādaśatilāś ca śaro bhavati /
saviṃśatitilaṃ caturaṅgulamanyattiryakphalakaṃ, tacca dhanuriva takṣet, antarvakraṃ tu bhavati yathā pañcadaśatilāḥśaraḥ /
evamiṣṭakā anyeṣāṃ dhiṣṇiyānāṃ trīṇi karaṇāni /
sarveṣāṃ ca dveṭve phalake aṣṭādaśāṅgule /
hotrīyasya dvādaśakasya tṛtīyaṃ phalake navāṅgulaṃ saikādaśatilaṃ, taddhanuriva takṣet, yathaika viṃśatitilāḥśaraḥ evaṃ ṣoḍaśakādīnāṃ ca draṣṭavyam /
brāhnaṇācchaṃsīyasya tṛtīyaṃ phalakaṃ daśāṅgulaṃ sapañcadaśatilaṃ, taddhanurivatakṣeta, pañcaviṃśatitilāḥśāraḥ, saptatilamiti vkacit /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya</s>: the third plank is ten <s>aṅgulas</s> with fifteen <s>tilas</s>; that should be carved like a bow; the arrow is twenty-five <s>tilas</s> (some [read] 'seven <s>tilas</s>').

children.text: mārjā līyasya tṛtīyamapyaṣṭādaśāṅgulaṃ, tadardhadhanuriva takṣet, vdyaṅgulaṃ caturdaśatilāḥśaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Mārjālīya</s>: the third [plank] is also eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>; that should be carved like a half-bow; two <s>aṅgulas</s> and fourteen <s>tilas</s> is the arrow.

children.text: aṣṭakānāṃ tṛtīyaphalakaṃ caturdaśāṅgulamaṣṭatilonaṃ, taddhanuriva takṣet, aṅgulirdvādaśatilāś ca śaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For the eight-[brick types]: the third plank is fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> minus eight <s>tilas</s>; that should be carved like a bow; the arrow is one <s>aṅgula</s> and twelve <s>tilas</s>.
For the other <s>piśīla</s>-[measurements] also, it should be observed following this [pattern].

Now, for the circular [<s>dhiṣṇyas</s>] of thirty-six <s>aṅgula</s> diameter: for the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>, having placed a circular stone of <s>prādeśa</s>-width in the middle, eight bricks around [it]; their mold [is as follows]: sides of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>; one transverse plank of fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> minus eight <s>tilas</s>; that should be carved like a bow, such that the arrow is one <s>aṅgula</s> and twelve <s>tilas</s>. The other transverse plank is four <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty <s>tilas</s>; that too should be carved like a bow, but concave inward, such that the arrow is fifteen <s>tilas</s>. Similarly for the bricks of the other <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> — three molds [each]. For all, two of the two planks are eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. For the twelve-[brick] <s>Hotrīya</s>: the third plank is nine <s>aṅgulas</s> with eleven <s>tilas</s>; that should be carved like a bow, such that the arrow is twenty-one <s>tilas</s>. Similarly for the sixteen-[brick type] and others, it should be observed.
Thus the seventh chapter.
Thus in <s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary on the <s>Āpastamba Śulbasūtra</s>, the <s>Śulbapradīpa</s>,
the second <s>paṭala</s> (section).
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.

children.text:
uktāni haviryajñānāṃ viharaṇani /
saumikāni ca sāgnicityasya kratoragnikṣetramānamiṣṭakānāṃ karaṇāni upadhānavi dhiś ca noktaḥ /
tadvaktukāmaḥ prastauti--
children.translated_text: The constructions for the <s>haviryajña</s> (oblation-sacrifices) have been stated. And for the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] together with fire-altar-piling — the measure of the fire-altar area, the molds for the bricks, and the placing-rule have not been stated. Wishing to state that, he introduces:

children.text: bhavatīva khalu vā eṣa yo 'gniṃ cinute iti vijñāyate | vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyata ityākṛticodanāt | pratyakṣavidhānādvā || ĀpŚus_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'He who piles the fire-altar becomes, as it were, [that fire]' — this is known [from scripture]. 'Or, it is piled in the likeness of birds' — because of the injunction regarding form. Or because of direct prescription. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.1]

children.text: yāvadāmnānena veṇunā caturaśre ātmani puruṣān avamimote || ĀpŚus_8.2a ||
children.translated_text: With a bamboo [measuring-rod], as [prescribed] by the Vedic text (<s>āmnāna</s>), one measures off the <s>puruṣas</s> (man-units) in the body [of the hawk-altar] within the quadrilateral. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.2a]

nityo 'gniruttaravedivat /

yadi prastāvo 'nayā śrutyā svīkriyate gārhapatyaciteḥ pūrvameva prastāvo na kartavyaḥ /

tasmādavirodhaḥ /
yāvadāmnānaṃ tāvadeva sārūpyaṃ /
pakṣapucchavattathā sārūpyaṃ gṛhītvā vayaḥśabdo vartate /
tasmātpuruṣamātrapakṣapucchavānagniriti tāmeva prakṛtiṃ niśvitya anye ākṛtiviśeṣā vakrapakṣādayaḥ kāmyā iti siddham /
vakṣyati "kāmyā guṇavikārā' iti /
veṇunā caturaśra ātmani puruṣānavamimīte--agnikalpe uktalakṣaṇena veṇunā mimīte--minoti sthaṇḍulārdhaṃ kṣetraṃ vakṣyamāṇena māgaiṇa sarvato dvipuruṣa ātmā dvābhyāṃ catvārīti vacanāccatavāri ca puruṣakṣetrāṇyātmani----
children.translated_text: By this <s>Śruti</s> (scriptural passage), only an introduction is made, not the determination of a result — because of the absence of a verbal injunctive [suffix]. The fire [-altar] is obligatory, like the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar). "The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [has] the <s>uttaravedī</s>; in subsequent rituals, the fire[-altar]" — from this statement of [its] obligatory nature. If this <s>Śruti</s> is accepted as the introduction, the introduction should not have been made already before [the discussion of] the <s>gārhapatya</s> altar. This is true. The purpose of the introductory statement here is: so that the forthcoming characteristics (<s>dharmas</s>) may belong to the great fire [-altar] itself. What are those [characteristics]? "Reaching up to the knee, the great fire" — in <s>Kātyāyana's</s> <s>Śulba</s>, it is clearly stated that these characteristics belong to the great fire [-altar] alone. Moreover, so that the characteristics enjoined here by the unqualified word "fire" may [properly] apply — for example: "The sacrificer himself should pile this" — the sacrificer is the agent only of the great fire [-altar], not of the <s>gārhapatya</s> and others. The <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) alone is the agent for the <s>gārhapatya</s> and the subsidiary fire-seats (<s>dhiṣṇyas</s>). This is the purpose of prescribing the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> to be ordained later before [their actual placement]. Whoever belongs to the fire, he indeed becomes [its performer]. Although "even if there are many rivals" is performed by this <s>Śruti</s> — of birds (<s>vayas</s>), meaning winged creatures, this fire is to be piled in the likeness (<s>pratimā</s>) of their natural form (<s>prakṛti</s>) — thus the prescription of the shape is made. And "by the shadow of [birds] in flight" — this is the meaning, as stated by <s>Baudhāyana</s>. The particle "vai" is for emphasis/certainty. This <s>ācārya</s> too will state: "with bent wings and spread tail." Therefore the hawk-altar (<s>śyena-cit</s>) is indeed the primary [form]. And in another <s>Śulba</s> [text] it is stated: "Among the hawk-altar fires, the hawk is the first fire." If the hawk is obligatory, how [can it be] "one desiring heaven"? Like the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) material — just as <s>khadira</s> (acacia) [wood] "for one desiring heaven" has both obligatory and optional character. From the explicit prescription, [it extends] as far as the Vedic text [reaches]. The particle "vā" is for excluding alternatives. Therefore, even this is not an independent injunction — the hawk is the primary form. Why? Because of the explicit prescription. What is explicitly prescribed here — beginning from "it becomes a bird" — the dimensions of the wings and tail have been prescribed. Therefore there is [no] contradiction. "Is this not an injunction of [a particular] shape?" — this is not an injunction; nor is it a prescription; because of the absence of an injunctive verbal [suffix]. It is indicated [merely] as "it is piled"; not as "one should pile" or "it is to be piled." And because it serves as a subordinate element of another prescription, we regard it as non-prescriptive. "The <s>Brahmavādins</s> (theologians) say: should the fire be piled facing down or facing up?" — beginning from this, "one places [the brick] in the shape of a man's head facing east and upward" — the placing of the human-head [-shaped brick] is prescribed. This [passage] is subordinate to that, not independently prescriptive. "The first among hawk-altar fires" — this is stated with reference to the tray-hawk (<s>piṭhaka-śyena</s>); the name "hawk" is the designation for [an altar with] wings and tail of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure. Therefore there is no contradiction. The resemblance [to a bird] extends as far as the Vedic text (<s>āmnāna</s>) [prescribes]. Taking the resemblance together with wings and tail, the word "bird" (<s>vayas</s>) is used. Therefore, the fire[-altar] has wings and tail of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure — having ascertained that very primary form (<s>prakṛti</s>), the other specific shapes such as curved wings etc. are optional — this is established. He will state: "The optional [forms] are modifications of qualities." With a bamboo [measuring-rod], in the quadrilateral, in the body (<s>ātman</s>), one measures off the <s>puruṣas</s> — with a bamboo of the characteristics stated in the fire-ritual procedure, one measures — that is, one measures out the threshing-ground area by the method to be stated: the body is two <s>puruṣas</s> on all sides; from the statement "by two, four" — [thus] four <s>puruṣa</s>-areas [constitute] the body.

children.text: puruṣaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe puruṣaṃ pucche puruṣam uttare || ĀpŚus_8.2b ||
children.translated_text: One <s>puruṣa</s> [in area] for the southern wing, one <s>puruṣa</s> for the tail, one <s>puruṣa</s> for the northern [wing]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.2b]

children.text: puruṣamekaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe puruṣaṃ pucche puruṣamuttare--vivaṃ trīṇi caturaśrāṇi puruṣapramāṇāni, ātmanā saha sapta puruṣakṣetrāṇi //
children.translated_text: One <s>puruṣa</s> [in area] for the southern wing, one <s>puruṣa</s> for the tail, one <s>puruṣa</s> for the northern [wing] — thus three quadrilaterals of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure; together with the body, seven <s>puruṣa</s>-areas.

children.text: aratninā dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ vardhayati | evam uttarata uttaram || ĀpŚus_8.2c ||
children.translated_text: By one <s>aratni</s> (cubit), one extends the southern wing to the south; likewise the northern [wing] to the north. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.2c]
By the measure of one <s>aratni</s>, one extends the southern wing to the south — makes it longer.
And the northern wing to the north.
By one <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) or one <s>vitasti</s> (span), one [extends] the tail to the west. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.2d]

children.text:
dvādaśāṅgulena trayodaśāṅgulena vā paścātpucchaṃ vardhayediti śeṣaḥ /
evamardhāṣṭamāni ṣuruṣakṣetrāṇi bhavanti /
children.translated_text: By twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> or by thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, one should extend the tail to the west — this is the remainder [of the sentence]. Thus there are seven and a half <s>puruṣa</s>-areas.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
The plain constructions from the <s>Agniyādheya</s> (fire-establishment) up to the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] have been stated.

Now, wishing to prescribe the specific constructions in rituals that include fire-altar piling (<s>agniciti</s>), he reads the <s>Śruti</s> that prescribes the <s>Agniṣvayana</s> (fire-piling sacrifice):
"He becomes [prosperous]"
The [root] "bhavati" is in the sense of prosperity.
The particle-group "iva khalu vai" functions in the sense of sentence-ornament and the like.

children.text: "rasa iva khaluvai tat yo 'rgni cinute--agniṃ cayanena saṃskaroti sa samṛddho bhavatīti vijñāyate //
children.translated_text: "Indeed, he who piles the fire — who consecrates the fire by [the act of] piling — he becomes prosperous: thus it is known [from scripture]."

children.text:
nan.u mantrasya vidheḥ stāvakatayār'thavādo 'yaṃ /
cinuta iti vartamānanirdeśaḥ /
ataḥ kathameṣā agrisaṃskārabhūtasya cayanasya vidhāyikā śrutiḥ kalpyate /
satyaṃ, taittirīyake asyā eva śrutermukhyatvādaprāptārthatvenānuvādatvāsaṃbhavāccayanamātrasyaiṣā vidhāyikā śrutiḥ kalpyate /
children.translated_text: True; [but] in the <s>Taittirīya</s> [recension], since this very <s>Śruti</s> is primary, since it conveys something not previously known (<s>aprāptārtha</s>), and since it cannot be [merely] reiterative (<s>anuvāda</s>), this <s>Śruti</s> is construed as prescriptive of piling itself.
And because of its lack of connection with desire, [the piling] is obligatory (<s>nitya</s>).
But is not the "becoming [prosperous]" result of the piling also to be prescribed?
It is not to be prescribed. Why? Because, since piling has the character of consecrating the fire, the restatement of its result is not possible.

Now, this is a <s>mantra</s> (sacred formula) that, being laudatory of the prescription, is an <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory statement). The present-tense indication [in] "is piled." Therefore how is this <s>Śruti</s> construed as prescriptive of the piling that constitutes the consecration of the fire?
Of birds ... injunction

children.text:
vayāṃsi--pakṣiṇaḥ śyenādayaḥ /
pratimā -- pratikṛtiḥsādṛśyamākṛtirūpaṃ codayatīti codanā vidhīyakā śrutiḥ /
eṣo 'gniryathā śyenākṛtirbhavati tathā yetavya ityarthaḥ /
śulbāntare ca -- śyenacidagnīnāṃ prathamo 'gnirityuktaṃ /
vakṣyati ca śyenaṃ prakṛtya vakrapakṣo vyastapuccho bhavatīti /
tasmādvakapakṣādiviśiṣṭaśyeno 'gniḥ prakṛtitvena kāryaḥ /
sa nityaḥ /
yūpaprakṛtibhūtakhādirādikat svargakāmasyāpi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Vayāṃsi</s> (birds) — winged creatures such as hawks and the like. <s>Pratimā</s> — likeness, resemblance, form. The injunctive <s>Śruti</s> enjoins the shape. The meaning is: this fire should be piled so as to have the form of a hawk. And in another <s>Śulba</s> [text]: "Among the hawk-altar fires, the hawk is the first fire" — this is stated. And he will state, presupposing the hawk: "it has bent wings and spread tail." Therefore, the hawk specifically characterized by bent wings and the like should be constructed as the primary form. It is obligatory. Like <s>khadira</s> (acacia wood), which is the primary material for the sacrificial post, it will apply even for one desiring heaven.
Explicit ... by this

children.text:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau /
naitadasti vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cāyate iti eṣā śyenādyākṛtiviśeṣacodaneti /
kutaḥ, pratyakṣavidhānāt /
yataḥ pakṣī bhavatītyādinā vākyena vyāyāmamātrapakṣapucchavadākṛtiḥ pratyakṣamevāgnervidhīyate /
ataḥ vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyata iti vayaḥsādṛśyamātramabhidadhāti, naiṣā śyainākṛtiyodanā bhavitumarhati /
kiñca cīyata iti vartamānārtha nirdeśādasya vākyasya puruṣaśīrṣopadhānavidhivākyaśeṣatvācca naiṣā vidhāyikā /
children.translated_text: The particle "vā" is for excluding alternatives. This is not the case — that "of birds, or, this one is piled in [their] likeness" is an injunction of the specific hawk-form and the like. Why? Because of the explicit prescription. Since by the statement beginning with "it becomes a bird" — having wings and tail of one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) measure — the shape is explicitly prescribed for the fire. Therefore, "of birds, or, this one is piled in [their] likeness" merely states the resemblance to birds; this cannot be an injunction of the hawk-shape. Moreover, since "is piled" is a present-tense indication and since this statement is subordinate to the prescription of placing the human-head [-shaped brick], this is not prescriptive.

children.text:
yaccoktaṃ śulbāntare -- "śyenacidagnināṃ prathamo 'gnirityuktamiti' nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
tatra hi vyāyāmamātrapakṣapuccho 'gnirityapi śyena ityucyate /
tasmādāmnānena vedena vyāyāmamātrapakṣapucchavattāyā yāvatsādṛśyaṃ vihitaṃ tāvadeva saṃpādayitavyaṃ /
tasmātpuruṣamātrapakṣapucchavānagniḥ prakṛtirnityaś ceti sthitam /
asyā gneḥsvarūpamāha /
children.translated_text: And what was stated in another <s>Śulba</s> [text] — "among the hawk-altar fires, the hawk is the first fire" — this is not a fault. For there too, a fire with wings and tail of one <s>vyāma</s> measure is also called a "hawk." Therefore, as much resemblance [to a bird] as is prescribed by the Vedic text (<s>āmnāna</s>) regarding wings and tail of one <s>vyāma</s> measure — that much alone is to be accomplished. Therefore, the fire[-altar] with wings and tail of one <s>puruṣa</s> measure is the primary form and is obligatory — this is established. He states the essential nature of this fire[-altar]:

children.text:
veṇunā cchaṃ vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa veṇunā'tmani caturaḥ puruṣānavamimīte /
avamānamapi vimānameva /
iyati śakṣyāmīti tvā avamāya yajanta iti darśanāt /
sarvato dvipuruṣa ātmā tābhyāṃ catvāri puruṣakṣetrāṇyātmā bhavati /
evaṃ vakṣayoḥ pucche ca puruṣasaṃmitāni trīṇi /
evaṃ sapta puruṣakṣetrāṇi aratninā dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ pravardhayati dakṣiṇato -- dīrghaṃ kuryāt /
evamuttarata uttaramapi pakṣamuttarato dīrghaṃ kuryāt /
prādeśena nitastyā vā paścātpucchaṃ /
prādeśoṅguṣṭhapradeśinībhyāṃ parimitaḥ vitastiraṅguṣṭhakaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ tayoranyatareṇa pucchaṃ pratīcīnaṃ vardhayet /
evamardhāṣṭamāni puruṣakṣetrāṇyagneḥ kṣetraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: With a bamboo [measuring-rod] — by the method to be stated, with a bamboo, one measures off four <s>puruṣas</s> in the body. Measuring off (<s>avamāna</s>) is indeed the same as measuring (<s>vimāna</s>). From the observation: "having measured you off [to determine] this much I can [accomplish], they sacrifice." The body is two <s>puruṣas</s> on all sides; by those two, the body has four <s>puruṣa</s>-areas. Similarly, in the wings and tail, three [areas] equal to one <s>puruṣa</s> [each]. Thus seven <s>puruṣa</s>-areas. By one <s>aratni</s>, one extends the southern wing to the south — makes it long. Likewise, one should also make the northern wing long to the north. By one <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) or one <s>vitasti</s> (span) — the <s>prādeśa</s> is measured by thumb and index finger; the <s>vitasti</s> by thumb and little finger — by either of those, one should extend the tail westward. Thus seven and a half <s>puruṣa</s>-areas become the area of the fire[-altar].
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
The measurement of the <s>Soma</s> altar, by steps of twice-twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>,
at the first, third, seventh [steps], at the second, third, moon(?), and second-yoke grounds, [verse 1]
at [counts of] five-three-earth, two-arrow, one — fifteen and ten gnomons;
the measuring cord, with six <s>tilas</s>, one <s>aratni</s> less a sixth, thirty-eight <s>aratnis</s>. [verse 2]
The mark on the measuring cord should be made; at its seventeenth [unit],

children.text: pāśau kāryau tayormadhye praktamā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ // .3 //
children.translated_text: loops should be made; between them, twelve <s>prakramas</s> are recognized. [verse 3]
Or the cord should be thirty-six [units], with marks at twelve and eight [for] measurement;
the hips at the first fifteen, the <s>sadas</s> (hall) at the next and fourth. [verse 4]
At ten and eight, those corners; at the third, one <s>aratni</s> measure;
the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (subsidiary fire-seats) are one <s>prādeśa</s> apart; the <s>āgnīdhra</s> (fire-kindler's hearth) is at the fourth. [verse 5]
At the <s>Rudra</s>[-seats], at [positions] seventeen, at [those] diminished by a quarter, here
two gnomons should be made at the fifth; at the <s>arka</s>[-seats], the <s>mārjālīya</s> and <s>āgnīdhra</s> fire-seats. [verse 6]
At the seventh, as before for the <s>āgnīdhra</s>; the grain-store at four and a half;
the refuse-heap at the tenth gnomon; in the <s>Manu</s>[-seats], at the step to the north. [verse 7]
The <s>ūvathya</s>, cow-tethering, and digging place at the eleventh, again;
the <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation-shed), as before here; from the loops in reversed order, additionally. [verse 8]
At sixteen diminished by half, the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughter-shed) should be at the twelfth;
from the two gnomons, the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar) should be at the two half-penultimates. [verse 9]
At the last twelve, the shoulders; the <s>cātvāla</s> (pit), from the shoulder northward by one step;
the <s>paśubandha</s> (animal-sacrifice) has the <s>cātvāla</s>; in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice] too — this is to be understood. [verse 10]
Without stating another measurement, from the declaration that "it has been explained,"
the <s>śamyā</s> measure [applies] everywhere — <s>Baudhāyana</s> clearly stated [this]. [verse 11]
Otherwise there would be a contradiction in the fire[-altar]; and no other measurement is found;
at the northern shoulder of the great <s>vedī</s>, the <s>āstāva</s> (praise-shed) is declared. [verse 12]
But at the southern <s>havirdhāna</s>, three steps should be left behind [to the west];
the pair diminished by a quarter at the sides; the <s>uparavas</s> (pressing-stones) are recognized as being at one <s>aratni</s>. [verse 13]
From half a <s>prādeśa</s> of those, the rotation at the corner-gnomons;
in front of the <s>uparavas</s>, leaving three steps diminished by a quarter. [verse 14]
The four corners are one <s>śamyā</s> in measure; and the passageway is closely fitted;
in the middle of the <s>audumbara</s> (fig-wood) <s>sadas</s> (hall), the back-line at one step to the south. [verse 15]
"He becomes" ... injunction

children.text:
pratimayā vayasāṃ utpatatāṃ chāyayā /
tathā ca bodhāyanaḥ--
children.translated_text: In the likeness of birds — by the shadow of [birds] in flight. And thus <s>Baudhāyana</s> [says]:
"By the shadow of birds in flight — this is the meaning."

children.text:
iti /
anena śyenacitirnityoti jñāyate /
mantravarṇāś ca bhavanti, "suparṇo 'si garutmān' ityādīni /
liṅgāni ca pucchācchi ro 'dhikṛṣati śirasi pakṣayorityādīni /
na hi caturaśre śirosta /
children.translated_text: By this, it is known that the hawk-altar (<s>śyena-citi</s>) is obligatory.
