And there are <s>mantra</s>-words [confirming this], such as "You are the eagle (<s>suparṇa</s>), the winged one (<s>garutmān</s>)" and the like. And there are indicators: "the head from the tail," "it extends to the head and the wings" and the like. For in a [mere] quadrilateral, there is no head.
Explicit ... or

children.text:
pakṣībhavati vyāmamātrau pakṣau ca pucchaṃ ca bhavatītyādi pratyakṣavidhānādvā ākṛtiḥ pratyetavyā /
anena caturaśro 'gnirvi dhīyate /
sa ca sarvāgnīnāṃ prakṛtiriti /
tameva tāvadāha --
children.translated_text: "It becomes a bird; the wings are one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) in measure, and the tail" — from this explicit prescription, or the shape should be understood. By this, a quadrilateral fire[-altar] is prescribed. And that is the primary form (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all fire[-altars]. That alone he states first:
As far as ... upper

children.text:
yāvadāmnānena yathāsamnātena puruṣamātreṇa vakṣyamāṇena pañcāratninā /
evaṃ kevalasaptavidhāgnermānamuktaṃ, pakṣāntaramāha --
children.translated_text: "As far as by the Vedic text (<s>āmnāna</s>)" — by the established one <s>puruṣa</s> measure, [which is] five <s>aratnis</s> as will be stated. Thus the measurement of the basic seven-[<s>puruṣa</s>]-fold fire[-altar] has been stated; he states an alternative:
By one <s>aratni</s> ... the <s>vitasti</s> is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>. As stated by <s>Kātyāyana</s>:
"The <s>puruṣa</s> is five <s>aratnis</s> or ten <s>vitastis</s> or one hundred and twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>."

children.text:
iti /
vitastirdvidaśāṅguletyeva naighaṇṭukāḥ /
prādeśenetyasya vyākhyānaṃ vitastyeti /
prādeśaśabdārthasya viśayisvāt vitastirevātra prādaśeśabdena grāhyā, natu prasārite aṅguṣṭhapradeśinyāvityarthaḥ /
athavā vājasaneyake "vitastyā pucchaṃ' iti śrutatvā dvitastiśabdasyaiva prasiddhatareṇa prādeśaśabdenana vyākhyānam /
vāśabdo vākyārthe 'vasaṃbadhyate /
tena sarvamidaṃ vikalpyate /
tathāhi -- pucchavṛddhestāvadvaikalpikatvamavagatam, taittirīyake pravṛddheranuktatvāt /
vyanakti ca kātyāyanastathā "aratninā pakṣau drāghīyāgaṃsau bhavataḥ' ityuktvā iti drāghīyastvamuktvā "vyāmamātrau pakṣau ca pucchaṃ ca bhavati' iti puruṣamātrasyaiva nigamanāt /
rupaṣṭa
children.translated_text: Thus. The <s>Naighāṇṭukas</s> (lexicographers) [say] that a <s>vitasti</s> (span) is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> only. The explanation of 'by a <s>prādeśa</s>' is '<s>vitasti</s>.' Because the word-meaning of <s>prādeśa</s> has multiple domains, only <s>vitasti</s> should be understood here by the word <s>prādeśa</s> -- not [the measure of] the extended thumb and index finger. Alternatively, since in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [Saṃhitā] the word <s>vitasti</s> is heard in 'the tail is a <s>vitasti</s>,' the explanation is given by the more well-known word <s>prādeśa</s> rather than the word <s>vitasti</s>. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is connected to the sentence-meaning. By that, all this becomes optional. For indeed: the optionality of the tail-extension is [already] understood, since in the <s>Taittirīya</s> [school] the extension is not stated. And <s>Kātyāyana</s> clarifies this: having stated 'by a cubit, the wings become longer with [raised] shoulders,' and having thus stated the extension, he concludes with 'the wings and the tail together are of <s>vyāma</s> (fathom) measure' -- confirming only the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [as the total].
And <s>Bodhāyana</s> makes this clear:

children.text: puruṣamātraiṇa veṇunā sapakṣapucchamaratninā vā pakṣau drāghīyāgaṃsau bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With a bamboo rod of <s>puruṣa</s> measure, including wings and tail, or by a cubit, the wings become longer with [raised] shoulders.'

children.text:
iti /
kecittu vitastiṃ trayodaśāṃṅgulāṃ manvānā dvādaśāṅgulena prādeśena vikalpayantaḥ pakṣapucchānāmaratnanyādipravṛddhiṃ nityāmāhuḥ /
teṣāmaṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ yadanyatsaptadhā vibhajya vidhāsaptamakaraṇīmityādi na saṃgacchate /
tattyodaśāṅgulavitastyabhyupagame pucche viṃśatiśatāṅgulamātraṃ kṣetramupadhātuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: Thus. But some, considering the <s>vitasti</s> to be thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, proposing an alternative with the twelve-<s>aṅgula</s> <s>prādeśa</s>, declare the cubit-and-other extensions of wings and tail as obligatory. For them, regarding the eight-fold and subsequent [fire-altars], what [is stated about] dividing into seven in other ways [and deriving] the <s>saptadhā-saptama-karaṇī</s> and so on -- does not work out. With the acceptance of a thirteen-<s>aṅgula</s> <s>vitasti</s>, the area of one hundred and twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> cannot be accommodated in the tail.

children.text:
tatra kaśvidāha -- purīṣeṇa pūryatāmiti, tatsūtrakāro na sahate /
yadāha "ardhāntaratvāt purīṣasya' iti "yatpacyamānānāṃ pratihraseta' iti ca /
kiñca purīṣeṇa cetsarvasya nyūnasya pūrtiḥ; kimiti mahatā granthena iṣṭakāpramāṇārdhamadhunā prayatyate /
tasmānna kiñci detatrrayodaśāṅgulā vitastiriti /
anye manyante -- dvādaśāṅgula yoreva vitastiprādeśayoḥ āmikṣāpayasyayoriva bidhibhedācchabdabhedaḥ /
tayoś ca parasparaṃ vikalpa iti /
teṣāmapi pūrvoktāsaṃgatiḥ spaṣṭaiva /
brāhnaṇavirodhaś ca /
taittirīyake hi pucchasya pravṛddhiḥ pākṣikatvenāpi noktā /
tasmādaratnaniprādeśānāṃ pākṣikatvameva jyāyo manyāmahe /
kiñca yadeveṣṭakānāmaṣṭāṅgulānāṃ pañcamaṃ karaṇaṃ tadapyasminnardhe liṅgaṃ katham? tatra hi prathamatṛtīyakaraṇābhyāmeva upadhāne śakye anyāni trīṇi karaṇāni bhedaparihārārthāni /
tatra pañcamena vināpyupadhānaṃ sukaram /
saratnyādipravṛddhau nityāyāṃ tatprakāraś ca darśito bhagavatā bodhāyanena --
children.translated_text: Regarding that, someone says: 'Let it be filled with <s>purīṣa</s> (loose earth filling).' The <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the aphorisms) does not accept that, since he states 'because the <s>purīṣa</s> is of half-interval' and 'whatever shrinks during firing.' Moreover, if all deficiency is filled with <s>purīṣa</s>, why is great effort now made with a large text to [specify] brick-measures and halves? Therefore the [assertion] that a <s>vitasti</s> is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> is of no [use]. Others think: <s>vitasti</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>, both of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, are like <s>āmikṣā</s> and <s>payasya</s> (two names for curdled milk) -- the word-difference is due to difference of ritual application; and the two are mutually optional. For them too, the inconsistency stated above is quite clear. And there is contradiction with the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. For in the <s>Taittirīya</s> [school], the extension of the tail is not stated even as optional. Therefore we consider the optionality of the cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions] as superior. Furthermore, the fifth construction of eight-<s>aṅgula</s> bricks -- how is there an indication of that in this half [of the text]? For there, placement can be done by the first and third constructions alone; the other three constructions are for the purpose of avoiding [monotonous] repetition. There, placement is easily done even without the fifth [construction]. And when the cubit-and-other extensions are obligatory, the method has been shown by the blessed <s>Bodhāyana</s>:
'In placing, on the front and back sides of the wing-flanks'

children.text:
ityādi /
anyaś ca prakāraḥ -- ātmani purastāt daśārdheṣṭakāḥ /
udagāyatāḥ pañcadaśa /
pakṣāgraryormadhye tisrastisraḥ prācyaḥ /
pucchāpārśvayoḥ pañcapañca /
pucchāgrakoṇayordve prādeśamātryau /
tābhyāmadhyardhe 'ṣṭake udīcyau /
pakṣāgrakoṇeṣvekaikā adhyardhā udagāyatā /
apyayoś ca pañcapañca yathāsūtraṃ /
pucchāgramadhye dve prācyau /
śeṣe pañcamyaḥ /
eṣa dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasmiṃstu pakṣapārśvayoḥṣaṭṣaḍardheṣṭakā udīcyaḥ /
ātmani dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca ṣaṭ ṣaṭ prācyaḥ /
śroṇyaṃseṣu dvedve adhyardhe udīcyau /
pucchāpyaye pañca prāgāyatāḥ ātmānamaratnaninopetāḥ /
śeṣe pañcamyaḥ /

children.translated_text: At the tail-tips, having removed the middle [brick], two half-eighth[-sized bricks] facing north.
This is the two-hundred layout.

children.text: evaṃ caturbhiḥ karaṇairupadhāne siddhe yatpañcamaṃ karaṇaṃ tadaratnaniprādeśābhāve 'pi bhedaparihāreṇa dviśatapūraṇārtham /
children.translated_text: Thus, when placement is accomplished with four constructions, the fifth construction is for completing the two-hundred [bricks] by avoiding repetition, even in the absence of cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions].
All this should be examined by scholars -- thus [the topic] is concluded.

and so on. And another method: in the body (<s>ātman</s>), in front, ten half-bricks; lengthwise northward, fifteen; at the middle of the wing-tips, three by three east-facing; on the tail-flanks, five by five; at the tail-tip corners, two of <s>prādeśa</s>-measure; between those, one-and-a-half eighth[-sized bricks] facing north; at the wing-tip corners, one each, one-and-a-half, facing north; and in the connecting portions, five by five as per the <s>sūtra</s>; at the tail-tip middle, two east-facing; in the remainder, fifth[-sized bricks]. This is the two-hundred layout. In the other [layer]: on the wing-flanks, six by six half-bricks facing north; in the body, to the south and north, six by six east-facing; at the hip-and-shoulder [corners], two by two one-and-a-half [bricks] facing north; in the tail-junction, five lengthwise east-facing, reaching the body by a cubit; in the remainder, fifth[-sized bricks].
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: ekavidhaḥ prathamo 'gnir dvividho dvitīyas trividhas tṛtīyaḥ ta evam evodyantyaikaśatavidhāt || ĀpŚus_8.3 ||
children.translated_text: The first [fire-altar] is <s>ekavidha</s> (one-fold); the second is <s>dvividha</s> (two-fold); the third is <s>trividha</s> (three-fold); thus they increase up to <s>ekaśatavidha</s> (one-hundred-fold). || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.3 ||

children.text:
ekaḥ puruṣo yasminniti ekavidhaḥ, ekapuruṣādekottaraṃ cinvīteti prathamātikrame kāraṇābhāvāditi prathama ekapuruṣavidhā iṣṭakā asminvidhīyante iti agnikṣetram /
"ātaśvopasarge' iryaṅ /
ekā cāsau vidhā locanīyam /
udyanti gacchanti ā ekaśata vidhāt /
abhividhāvāṅ /
children.translated_text: That in which there is one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area] is <s>ekavidha</s> (one-fold). In the first [ritual], one piles the <s>ekavidha</s>; in the first transgression [i.e., performance], because there is no reason [for more] -- thus the first is the <s>ekavidha</s>, in which one-<s>puruṣa</s>-measure bricks are prescribed -- this is the fire-altar area. 'In the context of an affix after a verbal root' -- [this is] the <s>yak</s> suffix. And that one is a <s>vidhā</s> (measure/fold) -- this should be examined. They 'increase' -- go up to the <s>ekaśatavidha</s> (hundred-fold). The <s>ā</s>-prefix indicates 'up to and including.'

children.text: tad u ha vai saptavidham eva cinvīta | saptavidho vāva prākṛto 'gniḥ | tata ūrdhvam ekottarān iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_8.4 ||
children.translated_text: Indeed one should pile only the <s>saptavidha</s> (seven-fold); the <s>saptavidha</s> alone is the primary (<s>prākṛta</s>) fire[-altar]; thereafter, one-fold increases -- this is known [from scripture]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.4 ||

children.text:
nipātasamūhaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau /
ekavidhādayo na cetavyā iti /
vāvetyavadhāraṇe /
saptavidha eva prākṛto 'gniḥ -- prakṛtirityarthaḥ /
svārtha eva taddhita /
saptavidhādūrdhvaṃ ekottarāniti vājasane yināṃ śrutiḥ /
saptārtha eva prathamaḥ prakṛtiś ca puruṣamātreṇetyārabhya saptārdhasya vidhānādupadhānavidhau dakṣiṇe pakṣe upadadhātīti śrūyate /
tata ūrdhvamekottarāniti ekapuruṣādhikāḥ paramiti, dvitīye prayoge ardhanavamaṃ, tṛtīyer'dhadaśamamityevaṃ draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: The cluster of particles [<s>tad-u-ha-vai</s>] indicates rejection of [the other] option. The <s>ekavidha</s> and others are not to be piled -- thus [it indicates]. <s>Vāva</s> is for emphasis. The <s>saptavidha</s> alone is the primary fire[-altar] -- <s>prākṛta</s> means 'being the original form' (<s>prakṛti</s>). The <s>taddhita</s> suffix is in its own sense. 'Thereafter, with one-fold increases' is the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) of the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>. The first is of seven-and-a-half [<s>puruṣa</s> areas]; it is the original form, because from 'with a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [rod]' onward, the prescription is for seven-and-a-half, and in the placement rule 'he places on the southern wing' is heard. Thereafter, with one-fold increases means [each] exceeding by one <s>puruṣa</s> [of area]: in the second performance, half-ninth; in the third, half-tenth -- thus it should be understood.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(One-fold, first... is known.)

children.text:
saptavidhasya prakṛtitvamāśaṅkya tenaiva prakṛtitvaṃ pratipādayitumāha vidhīyate mīyata iti vidhā agnanivimānaṃ, puruṣamātreṇa veṇunā puruṣakṣetrāṇi ekaikaśo 'tra mīyanta iti vidhāśabdaḥ puruṣakṣetravācī /
ekā vidhā yasyāgneḥ sa ekavidhaḥ /
prathamātikrame kāraṇābhāvāt prathama ekavidhaḥsa eva prakṛtiḥ, itare vikṛtayaḥ, te cāgnaya evamekapuruṣavṛddhyā udyanti adhikā bhavanti -- vardhanta ityarthaḥ /
ā ekaśatavidhāt /
āṅgābhividhau /
kathaṃ vidhāśabdasya vimā naparyāyatvaṃ, ucyate -- vidadhāti karotītyarthaḥ /
karaṇīvyāpāreṣu vimāneṣu karotiḥ tatratatrad daśyate /
ato vidhāvimā nayoḥ paryāyatvam /
tasmādekavidhaḥ prathamaḥ /
sa ekavidhaḥ prakṛtiś ca /
dvividhādayastadvikārā iti /
taduhavai saptavidhameva cinvīta -- taduhavā iti nipātasamudāyaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau /
naitadastyekavidhaḥ prathama iti /
kiṃ? tasmin saptavidhameva prathamaṃ cinvīteti /
kutaḥ? saptavidho vāva prākṛto 'gniḥ /
vāva ityavadhāraṇe /
"eṣa vāva sarvato rājā' ityādau darśanāt /
prakṛtireva prākṛtaḥ svārthe taddhitaḥ, tasmātsaptavidha eva prakṛtibhūto 'gniḥ /
tasmātsaptavidha eva prathamaṃ cetavyaḥ, naikavidhaḥ tasminneva pakṣapucchādyaṅgānāmupadeśādityabhiprāyaḥ /
saptavidha ityardhāṣṭama evocyate /
yāvānagniḥsāratniprādeśaḥsaptavidhaḥsaṃpadyata iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt /
tata ūrdhvaṃ tataḥsaptavidhādūrdhvamekottarānekenādhikānagnīṃśvinvīteti śrutiḥ /
agnirbaloktaṃ vājasaneyakamiti /
tasmāddvitīyādyāhāreṣu
children.translated_text: Suspecting that the <s>saptavidha</s> (seven-fold) has the nature of the primary form, in order to establish that very primary nature, he says: <s>vidhā</s> means 'that which is measured' -- the fire-altar measurement. With a bamboo rod of <s>puruṣa</s> measure, the <s>puruṣa</s>-areas are measured one by one here -- thus the word <s>vidhā</s> refers to <s>puruṣa</s>-areas. That fire[-altar] which has one <s>vidhā</s> (one <s>puruṣa</s>-area) is <s>ekavidha</s>. Because there is no reason for [beginning with] the first transgression, the first is the <s>ekavidha</s>; that itself is the original form (<s>prakṛti</s>); the others are modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>). And these fire[-altars] increase with one-<s>puruṣa</s> increments -- they become greater -- this is the meaning. Up to the <s>ekaśatavidha</s> (hundred-fold). The <s>ā</s>-prefix indicates 'up to and including.' How is the word <s>vidhā</s> synonymous with measurement (<s>vimāna</s>)? It is answered: <s>vidadhāti</s> means 'he makes/produces.' In the operations of <s>karaṇī</s> (construction), the word 'makes' is seen in various measurements. Hence the synonymy of <s>vidhā</s> and <s>vimāna</s>. Therefore the first is the <s>ekavidha</s>; that <s>ekavidha</s> is also the original form; the <s>dvividha</s> and others are its modifications. 'Indeed one should pile only the <s>saptavidha</s>' -- <s>tad-u-ha-vai</s> is a cluster of particles indicating rejection of [the other] option: it is not the case that the <s>ekavidha</s> is the first. What then? One should pile only the <s>saptavidha</s> as the first. Why? Because '<s>saptavidha</s> alone is the primary fire[-altar].' <s>Vāva</s> is for emphasis -- as seen in 'he alone is king everywhere' and such [usages]. <s>Prākṛta</s> means 'of the nature of the original' -- the <s>taddhita</s> suffix is in its own sense. Therefore only the <s>saptavidha</s> is the fire[-altar] that is the original form. Therefore only the <s>saptavidha</s> should be piled first, not the <s>ekavidha</s> -- because the instructions for wings, tail, and other parts are in that very [<s>saptavidha</s> context]. 'Seven-fold' actually refers to 'half-eighth' (<s>ardhāṣṭama</s>, i.e., seven-and-a-half). Because it will be stated that 'the fire[-altar] with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions] of such-and-such size is <s>saptavidha</s>.' Thereafter -- from that <s>saptavidha</s> onward -- one should pile fire[-altars] exceeding by one fold each -- this is the <s>śruti</s>. This is said to be from the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> -- the <s>Agni</s> <s>Bala</s> [text]. Therefore, in the second and subsequent performances,
one should pile only the <s>saptavidha</s> -- this is the tenth -- thus the one-fold increase should be understood up to the <s>ekaśatavidha</s> (hundred-fold).
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
(<s>Ekavidha</s>... up to <s>vidhā</s>.)

children.text:
vidhīyata iti vidhā -- puruṣamātraṃ kṣetram /
prathamāhāre ekavidhaḥ /
evaṃ dvividhādi /
ekaśatatama āhāre ekaśatapuruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidhā</s> (fold) is 'that which is prescribed' -- an area of <s>puruṣa</s> measure. In the first performance, [it is] <s>ekavidha</s>. Similarly <s>dvividha</s> and so on. In the one-hundred-and-first performance, [it is] one hundred <s>puruṣas</s>.
(Indeed... is known.)

children.text:
pakṣāntaramāha -- prakṛtireva prākṛtaḥ prajñādyaṇ /
saptavidhādūrdhvamekottarānekaśatavidhāt /
sarvatrāradniprādeśānāṃ na vṛddhiḥ, vidhānāmeva vṛddhivacanāt /
"ekaviṃśe puruṣābhyāso nāratnaniprāde śānām' iti liṅgācca /
vyaktoktametadbodhāyanena -- "ardhāṣṭamāḥ puruṣāḥ prathamo 'gniḥ ardhanavamā dvitīyor'dhadaśamāstṛtīyaḥ' ityādi /
yastvekavidhādikrameṇāharate tasya saptavidhādiṣvapyara tniprādeśānāmabhāvaḥ, ekottaratvāvirodhāt sāratniprādeśe saptavidha āhṛte uttare 'pi nāratniprādeśāḥ /
children.translated_text: He states the other option: <s>prākṛta</s> means 'of the nature of the original' -- the <s>prajñādi</s> [class] <s>aṇ</s> [suffix]. From the <s>saptavidha</s> onward, with one-fold increases, up to the <s>ekaśatavidha</s>. In all [cases], there is no increase of cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], since the increase is stated only for <s>vidhā</s> (folds). And from the indication 'in the twenty-first, the <s>puruṣa</s>-multiplication, not of the cubit-<s>prādeśas</s>.' This has been explicitly stated by <s>Bodhāyana</s>: 'Half-eighth <s>puruṣas</s> is the first fire[-altar]; half-ninth is the second; half-tenth is the third' and so on. But for one who performs in the sequence starting from <s>ekavidha</s>, even in the <s>saptavidha</s> and subsequent [fire-altars], there is absence of cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], since there is no contradiction with the one-fold-increase [principle]; when a <s>saptavidha</s> with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions] is performed, in the subsequent [fire-altars] too there are no cubit-<s>prādeśas</s>.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: vājasaneyikamiti agnivikalpavidhānāt vikalpaṃ saptārdhamapi dvitīye vihāre cinvītetyetadapi labhyate /
children.translated_text: Being from the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [school] -- since the fire-altar options are prescribed, the option that even half-seventh [fold] should be piled in the second performance is also obtained.

children.text: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ na pakṣapucchāni bhavanti | saptavidhavākyaśeṣatvāc chrutivipratiṣedhāc ca || ĀpŚus_8.5 ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>ekavidha</s> and subsequent [fire-altars], there are no wings and tail; because [they are stated as] the remainder of the <s>saptavidha</s> statement, and because of mutual contradiction of scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.5 ||

children.text:
itaś ca paśyāmaḥ saptārdhavidha eva cetavya iti /
yasmādekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ ṣaḍvidhaparyantānāṃ na pakṣapucchāni bhavanti /
kimuktaṃ bhavati? yataḥ pakṣapucchāni na bhavanti teṣu na śerata ityarthaḥ /
kuta ityāha -- sapteti /
saptavidhamagniṃ prakutya vidhīyanta ityarthaḥ /
rathantaraṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe upadadhāti bṛhaduttarapakṣa ityevamādayo na viyujyante /
tasmānna cetavyā ekavidhādayaḥ /
saptavidha eva cetavyaḥ /
teṣveva pakṣapucchāni kimiti na kriyerannityata āha -- śrutīti /
virodho -- vipratiṣedhaḥ /
yadyekavidhasyapakṣapucchātmanāṃ vibhāgaḥ kriyate; pakṣapucchatmanāṃ vyāyāmamātratā hīyate /
athaiṣa doṣo na bhavediti vyāyāmamātratā pakṣapucchātmanāṃ gṛhyeta; tadaikavidhatvaṃ hīyeta /
tasmādvirodhaḥ /
ataś ca viro dhānna kartavyā ekavidhādayaḥ ṣaḍvidhaparyantāḥ /
kathamaṣṭavidhādayo mātavyā ityata āha --
children.translated_text: From this too we see that only the half-seventh-fold [fire-altar] should be piled. Because for the <s>ekavidha</s> and subsequent [fire-altars] up to the <s>ṣaḍvidha</s> (six-fold), there are no wings and tail. What is meant? The meaning is: because they do not have wings and tail, one should not engage in [building] them. He asks why, [and answers] 'seven' -- meaning: [the wings and tail] are prescribed with reference to the <s>saptavidha</s> fire[-altar]. [Scriptural passages like] 'he places the <s>rathantara</s> on the southern wing' and 'the <s>bṛhat</s> on the northern wing' and such -- are not separated [from the <s>saptavidha</s> context]. Therefore the <s>ekavidha</s> and others should not be piled; only the <s>saptavidha</s> should be piled. As to why wings and tail should not be made in those [smaller fire-altars], he says 'scripture' -- <s>virodha</s> means <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (mutual contradiction). If a division into wing-tail-body is made for the <s>ekavidha</s>, the [principle that] the wing-tail-body [measures] are merely of <s>vyāyāma</s> (fathom) extent is violated. If, to avoid this fault, the <s>vyāyāma</s>-extent for wing-tail-body is accepted, then the <s>ekavidha</s> nature (one-fold area) is violated. Therefore there is contradiction. And because of this contradiction, the <s>ekavidha</s> and others up to the <s>ṣaḍvidha</s> should not be constructed.

children.text: aṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ yad anyat saptabhyas tat saptadhā vibhajya pratipuruṣam āveśayet || ĀpŚus_8.6a ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>aṣṭavidha</s> (eight-fold) and subsequent [fire-altars], whatever is other than the seven [<s>puruṣa</s>-areas] should be divided into seven and apportioned per <s>puruṣa</s>[-area]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.6a ||

children.text:
aṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ ekaśatavidhaparyantānāṃ yadanyatsaptabhyaḥ saptārdhebhyaḥ tatsaptadhā saptārdhadhā yadanyatsaptārdhebhyaḥ prakṣeptavyamāsīt tatsaptārdhadhā vibhajya saptārdhebhya iti kuta etallabhyate? saptavidha ityukter'dhāṣṭama eva gṛhyate /
aratniprādeśānāṃ tadantargatatvāt /
vakṣyati saptavidha iti /
aṣṭavidha ekaḥ prakṣeptavyaḥ navavidhe dvau /
daśavidhe traya ityevaṃ draṣṭavyamekaśatavidhāt puruṣāt /
puruṣaṃ saptārdhadhā vibhaktaṃ kṛtvā pratipuruṣameko bhāgaḥ kṣeptavyaḥ /
saptāsvardhapañcāratniprādeśeṣu puruṣe triṃśatpañcadaśabhāgīyāḥ /
ardha puruṣe pañcadaśa /
evamekasminpuruṣakṣetre dve śate pañcaviṃśatiś ca pañcadaśabhāgīyāḥśerate /
aṣṭavidhe tāḥ prakṣeptavyāḥ /
ekasminpuruṣakṣetre triṃśatpañcadaśabhāgīyāḥ /
tāsu prākṣiptāsu pañcapañcāśadadhikaśatadvayamāpadyate /
ṣoḍaśānāṃ vargaṃ ṣaṭpañcāśadadhikam /
taccaturaśrāccaturaśramityanena nyāyena ekasminpañcadaśabhāgayikṣetre 'panīte yā rajjuḥ sā puruṣasthānīyā /
tasyāḥ pañcamo bhāgo 'ratnisthānīyaḥ /
tena mānena kṛte sarvapuruṣakṣetraṃ liptaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ navavidhādiṣu draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: For the eight-fold and beyond, up to the hundred-and-one-fold: what is other than the seven and seven-and-a-halves — that should be divided into seven or seven-and-a-half [parts]; what is other than the seven-and-a-halves that was to be added — that should be divided into seven-and-a-half [parts] and [added] to the seven-and-a-halves. From where is this obtained? From the statement 'seven-fold,' the eighth half is taken. Because the <s>aratni</s> (cubit) and <s>prādeśa</s> (span) are included within it. He will state 'seven-fold.' In the eight-fold, one [<s>puruṣa</s>-area] is to be added; in the nine-fold, two; in the ten-fold, three — thus it should be seen, up to the hundred-and-one-fold <s>puruṣa</s>. Having divided the <s>puruṣa</s> into seven-and-a-half [parts], one part per <s>puruṣa</s> is to be added. In the <s>puruṣa</s> of seven halves, five <s>aratnis</s> and a <s>prādeśa</s>, there are thirty fifteenths. In half a <s>puruṣa</s>, fifteen. Thus in one <s>puruṣa</s>-area, two hundred and twenty-five fifteenths lie. In the eight-fold, those are to be added. In one <s>puruṣa</s>-area, there are thirty fifteenths. When those are added, two hundred and fifty-five plus one hundred results. The square of sixteen is fifty-six plus [two hundred]. By the principle 'from one square, another square,' when one fifteenth-area is subtracted from one [<s>puruṣa</s>-area], the cord [obtained] stands in place of the <s>puruṣa</s>. Its fifth part stands in place of the <s>aratni</s>. With that measure, when made, all <s>puruṣa</s>-areas are covered. Thus it should be seen in the nine-fold and so on.
Because the modification of shape is not [prescribed in] the Vedic texts. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.6b ||

children.text: puruṣamātreṇa vimimīte' veṇunā vimimīte, iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_8.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'One measures with a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure'; 'one measures with a bamboo rod' — this is known. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.7 ||

children.text:
yadi puruṣakṣetramekatra kṣipyate, vikriyetākṛtiḥ /
na vidyate śrutiryasyāḥsā aśrutiḥ /
ākṛtivikārasya śruterabhāvāt ityarthaḥ /
puruṣamātreṇeti dravyamapekṣate /
veṇuneti ca mātrāmapekṣate /
tayornaṣṭāśvadagdharathavatsaṃbandhaḥ /
puruṣamātreṇa veṇunā minoti /
children.translated_text: If the <s>puruṣa</s>-area is added to one place, the shape would be modified. A <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) that does not exist is an '<s>aśruti</s>' (non-text). Because there is no Vedic text [prescribing] the modification of shape — this is the meaning. 'With a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure' pertains to the material [of measurement]. 'With a bamboo rod' pertains to the measure. The relation between them is like [the case of] 'the lost horse and the unburnt chariot.' One measures with a bamboo rod of <s>puruṣa</s>-measure.

children.text: yāvān yajamāna ūrdhvabāhus tāvad antarāle veṇoś chidre karoti madhye tṛtīyam || ĀpŚus_8.8 ||
children.translated_text: As tall as the sacrificer with arms raised upward — at such an interval, he makes holes in the bamboo rod, [and] a third in the middle. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.8 ||

children.text:
yajamānagrahaṇādadhvaryupramāṇo veṇurna gṛhyate /
chidrayorantarālaṃ yajamānamātraṃ yathā bhavati tathā chidre karoti /
tayormadhye veṇośchidramekaṃ karotīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the specification 'the sacrificer,' the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest's) measure for the bamboo rod is not taken. The interval between the holes should be of the sacrificer's measure — thus he makes holes. Between those [two holes], he makes one more hole in the middle of the bamboo rod — this is the remainder.

children.text: apareṇa yūpāvaṭadeśam anupṛṣṭhyaṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya chidreṣu śaṅkūn nihatyonmucyāparābhyāṃ dakṣiṇāprāk parilikhed āntāt || ĀpŚus_8.9 ||
children.translated_text: To the west of the sacrificial-post-pit site, having laid the bamboo rod along the spine-cord, fixing pegs in the holes, releasing [the rod], with the outer [pegs] one should draw [a line] southward and eastward, from the end. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.9 ||

children.text: sañcarasya paścādanupṛṣṭhyaṃ pṛṣṭhyā yathā tathā veṇuṃ nidhāya triṣu chidreṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya aparābhyāṃ śaṅkubhyāmunmucya dakṣiṇāprāksavyaṃ parilikhedāntāt agnikṣetrāt /
children.translated_text: Leaving a passage (<s>sañcara</s>) behind [the altar], having laid the bamboo rod along the spine-cord as appropriate, fixing pegs in the three holes, releasing the bamboo rod from the outer pegs, and inserting a pin in the far hole, attaching [the rod] to the near peg — with that very [rod], starting from the base of the far peg, one should draw leftward, southward and eastward, from the end — from the end of the fire-field.

children.text: unmucya pūrvasmād aparasmin pratimucya dakṣiṇā pratyakparilikhed āntāt || ĀpŚus_8.10 ||
children.translated_text: Releasing from the near [peg] and attaching to the far [peg], one should draw southward and westward, from the end. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 8.10 ||
Releasing from the near peg and attaching to the far peg, one should draw southward and westward, from the end.
Eighth section.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary

children.text: saptavidho 'gniḥ prakṛtiḥ,. anye 'gnayo vikṛtaya ityuktam, tatraikavidhādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ viśeṣamāha --
children.translated_text: The seven-fold fire-altar is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>); the other fire-altars are its modifications (<s>vikṛtis</s>) — this has been stated. Among these, of the six [types] from the one-fold onward, he states the special point:
(On 'of the one-fold and others... they do not exist')

children.text:
na bhaveyuḥ /
kutaḥ? saptavidhavākyaśeṣutvācchutivipratiṣedhācca /
pakṣībhavatītyādipucchavidhāyakavākyasya saptavidhaprakaraṇapāṭhāttaccheṣatvāvagateḥ /
kiñcaikavidhe pakṣādivibhāgakaraṇe vyāyāmamātratāhāniḥ vyāyāmamātrapakṣādikaraṇaikavidhatāhāniriti vyāyāmamātrapakṣapucchaikavidhatvavidhāyakayoḥ śrutyorvirodhānnaikavidhādīnāṃ pakṣādayo bhaveyuḥ /
teṣāṃ karaṇopadhānādīni ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāmityatra vakṣyati /
nanu sapakṣapuccheṣu vidhābhyāse 'pacaye ca visaptamakaraṇīṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā viharedityaṣṭavidhādyupacayamate ekavidhādau apacaye 'pisaptadhā vibhāgaṃ darśayati /
tatpakṣapucchavibhāgārthaṃ /
itarathā apacayaviṣaye 'pacayasyad daṣṭārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
tenaikavidhānāmapi bhavatīti gamyate /
tatkathaṃ teṣāṃ tāni na bhavantīti /
ucyate -- ekavidhaḥ prathamo 'gniḥ, taduhavai saptavidhameva cinvītetyevamādyorvi ruddhārthābhidhāyinyoḥśrutyoḥsamucchayābhāvādvikalpa evāvakalpate /
tasmādekavidho vā prathamaḥ saptavidho vā prathamaḥ /
tatra yadaikavidhaḥ prathamaḥ prakṛtiśva; tadā dvitīyādyahāreṣu ekottarā eva dvividhādayaḥ prayoktavyāḥ /
prakṛtibhūtaikavidhe pakṣapucchā nāmanāmnānādekavidhādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ pakṣapucchāni na bhavanti /
saptavidhe tu vidyanta eva /
evamaṣṭavidhādīnāṃ tadvikāratvātteṣu ca vidyanta eva /
yadā saptavidhaḥ prakṛtiḥ, itare tadvikarārāḥ tadaikavidhādayo 'pyaṣṭavidhavat sapakṣapucchā eva bhaveyuḥ, evaṃ vidhāpacayoktaḥ saptavidhavibhāgo 'rthavān bhaviṣyati, tatrātirātravadvikṛterapi kadācit prathamato 'nuṣṭhānaṃ ekavidhasya labhyata eva /
asminnapi pakṣe ekottaraniyamo 'styeva /
yadaikavidhaḥ prakṛti /
prathamamāhāraḥ, tadāsāvapakṣapucchāḥ /
dvitīyādiṣvāhāreṣu dvividhādayo yāvatsaptavidhamapakṣapucchā eva /
saptavidhādayaḥsapakṣapucchā eva /
yadaikavidho vikṛtiḥ prathamāhāraḥ, tadāsau sapakṣapucchaḥ /
dvitī yādiṣvāhāreṣu dvividhādayaḥsarve sapakṣapucchā eva /
yadā saptavidhaḥ prakṛtirvā vikṛtirvā prathamaḥ, tadā tata ūrdhvamaṣṭavidhādayaḥsaptavidhā eva /
tasmādekavidhādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāmapakṣapucchatvaṃ sapakṣapuvchatvamubhayamapyastyeveti sarvamupapannam /
aṣṭavidhādiṣvekottareṣu kathamatiriktasya vibhāga ityata āha --
children.translated_text: They should not have [wings and tails]. Why? Because [those altar-types] are subordinate to the seven-fold statement, and because of the contradiction with Vedic texts. Since the statement prescribing wings — 'it becomes winged' and so on, along with the tail-prescribing statement — is read in the context of the seven-fold [altar], its subordination [to that context] is understood. Moreover, in the one-fold, if wing-segments are made, the <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure would be diminished; [conversely] if one-fold [wings] are made with <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure wings, the one-fold-ness would be diminished — thus because of the contradiction between the two Vedic texts prescribing <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure, wings, tails, and one-fold-ness, the one-fold and other [lower types] should not have wings and tails. Their bricks, laying, etc. — 'of the one-fold onward' — he will state this [later]. Now, in the view that holds augmentation [starting] from the eight-fold: in the augmentation and diminution of [altars] with wings and tails, having made the seven-minus constructive measure the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, one should extend — in the eight-fold and upward augmentation view, even in the one-fold onward diminution, he shows the seven-fold division. That is for the purpose of wing-and-tail division. Otherwise, in the domain of diminution, there would be the fault of the diminution being purposeless. From that, it is inferred that the one-fold types too have [wings and tails]. Then how is it that those [six types] do not have them? It is said: the one-fold is the first fire-altar. Since in the two conflicting Vedic texts — 'one should indeed pile a seven-fold' and so on — there is no accumulation [of meanings], only an option applies. Therefore, either the one-fold is first, or the seven-fold is first. There, when the one-fold is first and is the archetype: then in the second and subsequent offerings, the two-fold and others, each increasing by one, are to be employed. In the one-fold that is the archetype, because of the non-mention of wings and tails, the six [types] from the one-fold onward do not have wings and tails. But in the seven-fold, they certainly exist. Likewise, in the eight-fold and others, being modifications of that [seven-fold], they certainly exist there too. When the seven-fold is the archetype and the others are its modifications, then even the one-fold and others would have wings and tails just like the eight-fold. Thus the seven-fold division stated for augmentation and diminution would be meaningful. Moreover, just as an <s>atirātra</s> (overnight ritual), though a modification, is sometimes performed first, so too the one-fold can certainly be performed first. In this view too, the increase-by-one rule applies. When the one-fold is the archetype — the first offering — then it is without wings and tails. In the second and subsequent offerings, the two-fold and others up to the seven-fold are without wings and tails. The seven-fold and higher have wings and tails. When the one-fold is a modification, the first offering — then it has wings and tails. In the second and subsequent offerings, the two-fold and all others have wings and tails. When the seven-fold is the archetype or modification and is first, then from that upward, the eight-fold and others are indeed seven-fold [in type]. Therefore, of the six [types] from the one-fold onward, both the absence and presence of wings and tails exist — thus everything is consistent. In the eight-fold and higher, with increasing-by-one, how is the division of the excess [area]? To this he says:
(On 'the eight-fold... [one should] extend')

children.text:
asyārthaḥ -- aṣṭavidhādiṣvardhāṣṭamebhyo yadanyadadhikamāgantu tatsaptadhā saptārdhadhā vibhajya pratipuruṣaṃ -- puruṣe ṣuruṣe bhāgamekaikamāveśayet /
ardhamardhe yāvānagniḥsāratniprādeśaḥsaptavidha iti liṅgāl, kutaḥ? ākṛtivikārasyāśrutatvāt -- śruterabhāvāt pramāṇābhāvādityarthaḥ /
tatraikasmin puruṣakṣetre pañcaviṃśatirdve śate ca pañcadaśa bhāgīyāḥśerate, āsāṃ triṃśatrriṃśatpañcadaśabhāgīyāḥ puruṣepuruṣe prakṣeptavyāḥ /
ardhe pañcadaśa, ayamarthaḥ -- prakṣeptavyaṃ pañcadaśadhā vibhajya tasya dvibhāga hitaṃ, puruṣaṃ yaṃ karoti ākṛteravikāratvāya sā tasya puruṣasya karaṇī grahyā /
tāvānveṇurbhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: in the eight-fold and others, what is additional beyond the seven-and-eighth-halves — that additional amount should be divided into seven or seven-and-a-half [parts] and one part each should be incorporated into each <s>puruṣa</s>-[area]. The half into the half-[<s>puruṣa</s>]. The fire-altar with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> is seven-fold — by indication. From where? Because there is no Vedic text for the modification of shape — i.e., because there is no <s>śruti</s> (text), no authority — this is the meaning. In one <s>puruṣa</s>-area lie two hundred and twenty-five fifteenths, of which thirty by thirty fifteenths per <s>puruṣa</s> are to be added. In the half, fifteen. The meaning is: having divided what is to be added into fifteen parts and multiplied by two, the <s>puruṣa</s> one makes — for the non-modification of shape — its <s>karaṇī</s> (constructive measure) should be taken as that <s>puruṣa's</s>. The bamboo rod would be of that measure — this is the meaning.
Now the measurement is stated:
(On '<s>puruṣa</s>-measure... one measures')

children.text:
śrutidvayamidam /
atrrekā śrutirdravyāpekṣaṇī, anyā parimāṇāpekṣaṇī /
tayoḥ naṣṭāśvādagdharathavatsaṃprayogaḥ /
puruṣamātreṇa veṇunetyarthaḥ /
yāvān -- yatparimāṇo yajamāna ūrdhvabhūtabāhuḥ tatparimāṇaṃ yathā chidrayorantarālaṃ bhavati tathā veṇuchidre kuryāt /
pañcāratniḥ puruṣa iti vakṣyati /
sa caitaddhetukaḥ /
yūpāvaṭasya paścāt sañcaramavaśiṣyānupṛṣṭhyaṃ pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya chidreṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatyāparābhyāṃ śaṅkubhyāṃ veṇumunmucyāparasmin chidre kīlaṃ pratikṣipya pūrvasmin śaṅkau pratimucya tenaivāparaśaṅkumūlādāramya dakṣiṇāprāgāntāt parilikhet /
antastasyāḥ stasyā diśo 'ntaḥ veṇunā'rabdhā rekhā yāvaddigantarābhimukhī bhavati tāvatparili khedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: These are two Vedic texts. Here, one Vedic text pertains to the material; the other pertains to the dimension. Their combination is like [the case of] 'the lost horse and the unburnt chariot.' The meaning is: with a bamboo rod of <s>puruṣa</s>-measure. 'As tall as' — of whatever dimension the sacrificer with upraised arms [is], he should make holes in the bamboo rod so that the interval between the holes is of that dimension. 'A <s>puruṣa</s> is five <s>aratnis</s>' — he will state this. And that is derived from this. Having left a passage behind the sacrificial-post-pit, having laid the bamboo rod along the spine-cord, fixing pegs in the holes, releasing the bamboo rod from the outer pegs, inserting a pin in the far hole, attaching [the rod] to the near peg, with that very [rod] starting from the base of the far peg, one should draw leftward — southward and eastward — from the end. 'From the end' means: the line begun by the bamboo rod within that direction — one should draw as far as it faces the other direction — this is the meaning.

children.text: unmucya pūrvasmāc chaṅkor aparasmin śaṅkau pratimucya dakṣiṇā pratyakpūrvavat parilikhet /
children.translated_text: Releasing from the near peg and attaching to the far peg, one should draw southward and westward, as before.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(On 'the one-fold... and [so on]')

children.text:
śrutivipratiṣedho vyāmamātrau pakṣau ca pucchaṃ ca bhavatīti /
caturaśraviṣayaṃ caitat /
śyenacidādayastu sapakṣapucchā eva bhavanti, tadākṛtereva vidheyatvāt /
children.translated_text: The contradiction of Vedic texts [applies to the rule] 'of <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure, the wings and tail.' And this pertains to the square [altar-body]. But the hawk-shaped (<s>śyenacit</s>) and other [altars] certainly have wings and tails, because their very shape is what is to be prescribed.
(On 'the eight-fold... [one should] extend')

children.text:
yadadhikaṃ saptabhyaḥ puruṣakṣetrāṅgulayaś ca caturdaśasahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni 14400 /
tāḥsaptabhyo 'dhikaiḥ puruṣairhatvā saptabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ puruṣakṣetrāṅguliṣu saṃyojayet /
tāstatra puruṣakṣetrāṅgulayo jñeyāḥ /
yathā aṣṭavidhe purukṣetrāṅgulayaḥ caturdaśa sahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni ca saptabhyo 'dhikenaikena puruṣeṇa hatvā saptabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ dve sahasre saptapañcāśaccāṅgulayaḥ pañcatilayuktāḥ /
etāḥ puruṣāṅguliṣu saṃyojayet /
tāstatra puruṣakṣetrāṅgulayaḥ ṣoḍaśasahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni saptapañcāśaccāṅgulayaḥ pañcatilādhikāḥ 16457 ti 5. asya mūlaṃ aṣṭāviṃśatiśatamaṅgulayaḥ, daśatilādikāḥ 128 ti 10. /
etatpuruṣasthānīyasya veṇoḥ pramāṇamiti hetoḥ vakṣyate /
"vidhāsaptamakaraṇīṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā viharediti' /
evaṃ navavidhe puruṣāṅgulīḥ 14400 dvābhyāṃ hatvā saptabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ catvari sahasrāṇi śataṃ caturdaśāṅgulayaḥ daśatilādhikāḥ /
tadyuktāḥ puruṣāṅgulayaḥ aṣṭādaśā sahasrāṇi pañca śatāni caturdaśa daśatilādhikāḥ 18514 ti 10 tasya mūlaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśacchatamaṅgulayo dvau tilau 136 ti 2. evaṃ navavidhe puruṣapramāṇam /
evameva daśāvidhādiṣu draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: What is in excess of seven — the <s>puruṣa</s>-field <s>aṅgulas</s> are fourteen thousand four hundred (14,400). Those, multiplied by the [number of] <s>puruṣas</s> in excess of seven, and divided by seven, the result should be added to the <s>puruṣa</s>-field <s>aṅgulas</s>. Those become the <s>puruṣa</s>-field <s>aṅgulas</s> there. For example, in the eight-fold: the <s>puruṣa</s>-field <s>aṅgulas</s> — fourteen thousand four hundred — multiplied by one (the <s>puruṣa</s> in excess of seven) and divided by seven, the result is two thousand and fifty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilās</s>. These should be added to the <s>puruṣa</s> <s>aṅgulas</s>. The <s>puruṣa</s>-field <s>aṅgulas</s> there [become] sixteen thousand four hundred and fifty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> plus five <s>tilās</s> (16,457 <s>tilās</s> 5). Its [square] root is one hundred and twenty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> plus ten <s>tilās</s> (128 <s>tilās</s> 10). This is the measure of the bamboo rod that substitutes for the <s>puruṣa</s> — the reason will be stated: 'having made the seven-minus <s>karaṇī</s> the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, one should extend.' Similarly, in the nine-fold: the <s>puruṣa</s> <s>aṅgulas</s> 14,400, multiplied by two and divided by seven, the result is four thousand one hundred and fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> plus ten <s>tilās</s>. Combined with the <s>puruṣa</s> <s>aṅgulas</s>: eighteen thousand five hundred and fourteen plus ten <s>tilās</s> (18,514 <s>tilās</s> 10). Its root is one hundred and thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> and two <s>tilās</s> (136 <s>tilās</s> 2). Thus is the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure in the nine-fold. Likewise it should be seen in the ten-fold and so on.

children.text:
anyaḥ prakāraḥ -- yāvanto 'gneḥ puruṣāḥ tatsaṃkhyayā puruṣāṅgulīrhatvā saptabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ puruṣāṅgulayaḥ pūrvoktā eva ṣoḍaśasahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni saptapañcāśacca pañcatilādhikāḥ 16457 ti 5. /
evaṃ navavidhādiṣu /
ekasmiṃśvāṅgulikṣetre tilāḥṣaṭapañcāśat śataṃ sahasraṃ ca 1156 /
evamaratniprādeśarahitānāṃ sapakṣapucchāgnonāṃ puruṣaveṇuś ca /
atra caturaśrāgneḥ prastāvādekavidhāgnīnāṃ caturaśrāṇāṃ apakṣapucchatvādaṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāmityuktam /
yadā tu śyenacidādividheḥsādhāraṇatvāt "vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyate' ityākṛtivavidhānācca śyenādyākāratvena sapakṣapucchamakavidhādīnām /
tadā yannayūnaṃ saptabhyastatsaptadhā viyajya pratipuruṣaṃ jahyāditi draṣṭavyam /
tatra vyakta eva vimāgaprakāraḥ /
tathā sati ekavidhaśyenaciti dve sahasre saptapañcāśacca pañcatilayuktāḥ puruṣāṅgulayaḥ 2057 ti 5 /
tanmūlaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayo dvādaśa tilāś ca /
puruṣadvividhe tu puruṣāṃṅgulayaśvatvāri sahasrāṇi śataṃ caturdaśa ca triṃśattilasaṃyuktāḥ /
puruṣaveṇustu catustilādhikāśvatuḥṣaṣṭiraṅgulayaḥ /
evaṃ trividhādiṣu draṣṭavyam /
yo yatrāgnau purupasthānīyaḥ tatra tasya viṃśatitamo bhāgo viharaṇe iṣṭakānāṃ cāṅguliḥ kalpyā /
tilāś ca tasyāśvatustriṃśāḥ /
tatra ślokāḥ --
children.translated_text: Another method: however many <s>puruṣas</s> (man-measures) the fire [altar] has, multiplying <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> (man-finger-units) by that number and dividing by seven, the result is: the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> as previously stated are sixteen thousand four hundred and fifty-seven plus five <s>tilās</s> (16,457 and 5 tilās). Similarly for the nine-fold and other [altars]. In one <s>aṅguli</s>-field, one thousand one hundred and fifty-six <s>tilās</s> (1,156). Thus also for the <s>puruṣa</s>-reed of fire [altars] without wings and tail, devoid of <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>. Here, since the square fire-altar is the first occasion, for the one-fold square altars without wings and tail, it has been stated from the eight-fold onward. However, when [the prescription] is common to the <s>śyenaciti</s> (hawk-shaped altar) and other designs, from the Vedic text 'he piles it in the likeness of birds,' and because of the prescription of shape, the one-fold and other [altars] have the form of a hawk with wings and tail. Then, whatever is not less than seven should be divided into seven and discarded per <s>puruṣa</s> — this is to be seen. There the method of measurement is evident. Thus, in a one-fold <s>śyenaciti</s>, two thousand and fifty-seven plus five <s>tilās</s> are the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> (2,057 and 5 tilās). Its root is forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> and twelve <s>tilās</s>. In a two-fold <s>puruṣa</s> [altar], four thousand one hundred and fourteen <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> combined with thirty <s>tilās</s>. The <s>puruṣa</s>-reed is sixty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> plus four <s>tilās</s>. Similarly for the three-fold and others. Whatever <s>puruṣa</s>-equivalent applies in whatever fire [altar], there a twentieth-hundredth (1/2000) part of it should be designated as the <s>aṅgulī</s> for the expansion, and for the bricks likewise. And its <s>tilās</s> are thirty-four. On this, verses:
From [the area in] sky-space-ocean-Veda-one [units], multiplied by the desired <s>puruṣas</s>,
one should take a seventh part; its root becomes the <s>puruṣa</s> [measure].
For the square and <s>śyenaciti</s>, devoid of <s>prādeśa</s> and <s>aratni</s>,
the <s>aṅgulī</s> there should be reckoned as a twentieth-hundredth part of that.
For [the altar] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>, the division stated by <s>Bodhāyana</s> is:

children.text: "yadanyatprakṛtestatpañcadaśabhāgān kṛtvā vidhāyāṃ vidhāyāṃ dvaudvau bhāgau samasyet, tābhirardhāṣṭamābhiragniṃ cinuyāt' //
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is other than the prototype — having divided that into fifteen parts, in each layer one should add two parts; with those seven-and-a-half [units], one should pile the fire [altar].'

children.text:
ityādi /
tatra prakāraḥ -- ardhāṣṭamebhyo 'dhikaiḥ puruṣaiḥ puruṣāṅgulīśvadurhaśasahasrāṇi catvāri ca śatāni hatvā pañcadaśabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ dviguṇīkṛtya puruṣāṃṅgulīṣu saṃyojayet /
tāstatra puruṣāṅgulayaḥ /
yathā ardhanavame puruṣeṣu puruṣāṅgulīrekena hatvā pañcadaśabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ nava śatāni ṣaṣṭiśvāṅgulayaḥ, tā dviguṇāḥ puruṣāṅgulīṣu saṃyojya dṛṣṭāḥ puruṣāṅgulyaḥ ṣoḍaśasahasrāṇi trīṇi śatāni viṃśatiś ca 16320. tanmūlaṃ tatra puruṣapramāṇaṃ pādonāṣṭaviṃśatiśatamaṅgulayaḥ /
evamardhadaśapuruṣe aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi dve śate catvāriṃśacca puruṣakṣetrāṅgulayaḥ /
puruṣaveṇuś ca pañcatriṃśacchatāṅgulayaḥ tiladvayādhikā ityādi draṣṭavyam /
ye tvapakṣapucchāḥ praugacidādayaḥ teṣvaratniprādeśairyukteṣu viyukteṣu caivameva puruṣamānīya tasya viṃśatiśatatamabhāgamaṅguliṃ prakalpya viharaṇamiṣṭakāś ca /
yathā praugaciti -- 14400. ekavidhe ekaṃ sahasraṃ catuśvatvāriṃśacchatāṅgulayaḥ ṣaṭtilonāḥ puruṣaḥ, tasya viṃśatiśatatamo bhāgaḥ tatrāṅgulirityādi /
tatra ślokau ------
children.translated_text: And so on. The method there is: multiplying <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> by <s>puruṣas</s> exceeding seven-and-a-half — four thousand four hundred — and dividing by fifteen, doubling the result, one should add it to the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s>. Those are then the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s>. For example, in eight-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>, multiplying the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> by one and dividing by fifteen, the result is nine hundred and sixty <s>aṅgulas</s>; those doubled and added to the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> — the obtained <s>puruṣa-aṅgulīs</s> are sixteen thousand three hundred and twenty (16,320). Its root — the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure there — is twenty-eight hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> less a quarter. Similarly, in a nine-and-a-half <s>puruṣa</s> [altar], eighteen thousand two hundred and forty <s>puruṣa</s>-field-<s>aṅgulīs</s>. And the <s>puruṣa</s>-reed is three thousand five hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> plus two <s>tilās</s> — and so on, to be seen. For those without wings and tail, such as the <s>praugaciti</s> (wedge-shaped altar), whether with or without <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>, one should similarly derive the <s>puruṣa</s> measure; reckoning a twentieth-hundredth part of it as the <s>aṅgulī</s>, [one should determine] the expansion and the bricks. For example, in the <s>praugaciti</s>: 14,400. In the one-fold, one thousand four hundred and forty <s>aṅgulas</s> less six <s>tilās</s> is the <s>puruṣa</s>; a twentieth-hundredth part of that is the <s>aṅgulī</s> there — and so on. On this, two verses:
From sky-space-hearing-Veda-one [units], multiplied by doubled <s>puruṣas</s>,
one should take a fifteenth part; its root becomes the <s>puruṣa</s> [measure].
For the square and <s>śyenaciti</s>, endowed with <s>prādeśa</s> and <s>aratni</s>,
and for the <s>praugaciti</s> (wedge-shaped) and others, this method should apply for obtaining the <s>puruṣa-aṅgulī</s>.

children.text:
ye tvaratniprādeśavṛddhiṃ nityāmāhuḥ teṣāmetatsūtre bodhāyanenokter'the kleśena yojayitavyaṃ syāt -- saptabhyaḥsārdhasaptabhya iti, evaṃ saptavidhā ardhāṣṭamavidheti, evamuttaratra vidhāsaptamakaraṇīmiti /
atrādhikānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ pratipuruṣamāveśanamuktam /
tatra hetumāha --
children.translated_text: Those, however, who say the <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> increase is permanent — for them, in order to reconcile with <s>Bodhāyana's</s> statement in this <s>sūtra</s>, one would have to [adjust] with difficulty: 'from seven to seven-and-a-half,' thus 'seven-fold is the same as seven-and-a-half-fold' — and similarly later, 'the seventh <s>karaṇī</s> of the formula.' Here the incorporation of the additional <s>puruṣas</s> per <s>puruṣa</s> has been stated. He states the reason for this —
Because of the shape.

children.text:
prakṛtyā anyākṛtervikārasya śrutyabhāvāt /
yadi tvadhikāḥ puruṣāḥ kacidevaikasmin pradeśe ātmani pakṣe vā nidhīyeran /
prakṛtirhyagnyākṛtirvikriyate /
children.translated_text: Because there is no Vedic text for a modification — a different shape — from the prototype. If, however, the additional <s>puruṣas</s> were to be placed in some particular region, in the body or in the wings, the prototype — the fire's shape — would be altered.
It is measured by the <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: puruṣamātreṇa -- yāvān puruṣa ūrdhvabāhustāvatā veṇunāgniṃ vimimīta iti śrutidvayasyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure' — the meaning of the two Vedic texts is: 'one should measure the fire with a reed as tall as a <s>puruṣa</s> (man) with arms raised upward.'
As much as the additional [measure].
It is brought by the two outer holes for the convenience of [keeping] outside; and the holes are for external purpose.
To the west of the border.

children.text:
apareṇa yūpāvaṭadeśaṃ sañcaramavaśiṣyaiva veṇunidhānam /
āntādarvākcakṣurnimitāccaturaśrapūrvāntādunmucya pūrvasmādaparasmin pratimucya dakṣiṇā pratyakparilikhedāntāt /
children.translated_text: To the west of the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> (post-pit) area, leaving a passage, the reed is to be placed. From the end [going] toward [the altar], from the eye-marked square's front end, releasing from the front and fixing on the back, one should draw to the right (clockwise) and westward from the end.
Thus ends the eighth chapter.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: unmucya veṇuṃ madhyame śaṅkāv antyaṃ veṇoś chidraṃ pratimucyoparyupari lekhāsamaraṃ dakṣiṇā veṇuṃ nidhāyāntye chidre śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin madhyamaṃ veṇoś chidraṃ pratimucya lekhāntayor itare pratiṣṭhāpya chidrayoḥ śaṅkū nihanti || ĀpŚus_9.1a ||
children.translated_text: Releasing the reed at the middle peg, fixing the end hole of the reed, placing the reed downward from above to the meeting-point of the lines to the right, fixing a peg at the end hole, fixing the middle hole of the reed at that [peg], establishing the other [holes] at the line-ends, one fixes pegs at the holes. || ĀpŚus 9.1a ||

children.text: dakṣiṇe śaṅkau anyataraṃ veṇośchidraṃ pratimucyoparyuparilekhāsambhedaṃ dakṣiṇāgraṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya antye chidre śaṅkuṃ nihatya tamin śṅkakakakau
children.translated_text: At the southern peg, fixing one hole of the reed, placing the reed with its tip to the south, downward from above to the non-intersection of the lines, fixing a peg at the end hole, at that [peg]

children.text: madhyamaṃ veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya lekhāntarayorantara chidrepratiṣṭhāpya chidrayorlekhāntayoreva śaṅkū nihanti /
children.translated_text: fixing the middle hole of the reed, establishing the inner holes at the line-intervals, at the holes — at the line-ends themselves — one fixes pegs.
That <s>puruṣa</s> [area] is square. || ĀpŚus 9.1b ||
That square is the <s>puruṣa</s> [unit area].

children.text: evaṃ puradakṣiṇaṃ catura ātmani puruṣānavamimīte || ĀpŚus_9.2a ||
children.translated_text: Thus, clockwise, one measures four <s>puruṣas</s> on the body [of the altar]. || ĀpŚus 9.2a ||

children.text: evaṃ catvāri puruṣakṣetrāṇi ātmani yathā bhavanti tathā pradakṣiṇaṃ minuyāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, one should measure four <s>puruṣa</s>-fields clockwise on the body, in such a way that they [properly] exist.

children.text: puruṣaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe | puruṣaṃ pucche puruṣam uttare || ĀpŚus_9.2b ||
children.translated_text: One <s>puruṣa</s> on the southern wing; one <s>puruṣa</s> on the tail; one <s>puruṣa</s> on the northern [wing]. || ĀpŚus 9.2b ||

children.text:
dakṣiṇe pakṣe -- dakṣiṇe pārśve /
madhyameṣu triṣu veṇuṃ pratimucya aparābhyāmityādi pūrvavaccaturaśraḥ puruṣaḥ /
evamuttarapakṣe uttarapārśve, madhyameṣveva triṣu pratimucya uttaram /
pucche tu pāśvātyamadhayamaśaṅkau madhyamaṃ veṇocchidraṃ pratimucya tiryagveṇuṃ nidhāya chidrayoḥśaṅkū nihatyonmucyottarābhyāṃ prasavyaṃ parilikhet /
dakṣiṇasmādunmucyottarasmin puruṣamātre śaṅkau pratimucyāntyacchidraśaṅkuprabhṛti pradakṣiṇaṃ parilikhet /
unmucya veṇuṃ madhyame pratimucya uparyupari lekhāsambhedaṃ paścādveṇuṃ nidhāya antya ityādi samānaṃ tatpuccham /
children.translated_text: 'On the southern wing' — on the southern side. Fixing the reed at the middle three [pegs], 'with the two outer ones' and so on — as before — the <s>puruṣa</s> is square. Similarly on the northern wing — the northern side — fixing at the same middle three, to the north. For the tail, fixing the middle hole of the reed at the two side [pegs] and the middle peg, placing the reed transversely, fixing pegs at the holes, releasing, one should draw counterclockwise with the two northern [holes]. Releasing from the southern [peg], fixing at the northern [peg] at a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure, starting from the end-hole peg, one should draw clockwise. Releasing the reed, fixing at the middle, placing the reed behind downward from above to the meeting-point of the lines, 'at the end' and so on — the same; that is the tail.

children.text: aratninā dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇam ity uktam || ĀpŚus_9.2c ||
children.translated_text: 'By an <s>aratni</s> (cubit), to the south, the southern [wing]' — thus stated. || ĀpŚus 9.2c ||

children.text: evaṃ vimitasya dakṣiṇapakṣasya dakṣiṇataḥ uttarasyottarataḥ aratninā vardhayet, pakṣayostiryaṅbhānī sāratnanipuruṣamātrā pārśva mānī ca puruṣamātraṃ, evaṃ pucchasya paścādapi prādeśena vitastyā vā vardhayet, tattatsupārśvamānī sa prādeśaḥ puruṣaḥ, puruṣamātre tiryaṅbhānī //
children.translated_text: Of the thus-measured southern wing, to the south, and of the northern [wing], to the north — one should increase by an <s>aratni</s>. The transverse measure of the wings is a <s>puruṣa</s> measure with an <s>aratni</s>; the lateral measure is also a <s>puruṣa</s> measure. Similarly, the tail to the west should also be increased by a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) or <s>vitasti</s> (span). Its lateral measure with that <s>prādeśa</s> is a <s>puruṣa</s>; [its] transverse measure is a <s>puruṣa</s> measure.

children.text: pṛṣṭhyāto vā puruṣamātrasyākṣṇayā veṇuṃ nidhāya pūrvasminn itaram | tābhyāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ aṃsaṃ nirharet | viparyasya śroṇī || ĀpŚus_9.3a ||
children.translated_text: Or, from the spine, placing the reed at the diagonal of a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure, the other [end] at the front; by these two, one should carve out the southern shoulder. Reversing, the haunches. || ĀpŚus 9.3a ||

children.text: aparasmin śaṅkau puruṣamātra pratimucya dakṣiṇāṃ śroṇiṃ udagapasāryottarāmeva śroṇiṃ viharet /
children.translated_text: Fixing at the back peg a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure, extending the southern haunch northward, one should construct the very northern haunch.
The northern shoulder, as before. || ĀpŚus 9.3b ||
This has been covered.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.

children.text:
aparasmādunmucya veṇuṃ madhyame śaṅkāvanyaṃ veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya uparyuparilekhāsamaraṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya /
lekhāsamaraḥ -- lekhāyāḥsaṃpātaḥ /
tasyopariṣṭāt sannikṛṣṭaṃ nidhāyāntyachidre śaṅkūnnihatya tasmin madhyamaṃ veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya lekhāntayoritare chidre pratiṣṭhāpya chidrayoḥśaṅkuṃ niranti sa caturaśraḥ puruṣasaṃjño bhavati, evaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ caturaḥ puruṣānātmani kuryāt /
paścime śahkāvevaṃ veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya paścādanupṛṣṭhyaṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya paścimayorapi chidrayorapi śaṅkuṃ nikhāya pūrvavaddvitīyaṃ puruṣaṃ kuryādevamuttarato 'pi uttarāpratyaguttarāprākcālikhya puruṣadvayaṃ vimimīte /
apareṇa yūpāvaṭateśaṃ sañcaramavaśiṣya pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ śaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ veṇuṃ nipātya chidrayordvai śaṅkū /
paścime śaṅkau veṇoḥ chidraṃ pratimucya pṛṣṭhyāyāmeva paścānnanipātya dvau śaṅkū /
evaṃ pañca śaṅkavaḥ /
madhyamapūrvayoḥśaṅvkoḥ pratimucya ullikhya pūrvavatpuruṣa dvayaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Fixing at the middle and front pegs, drawing as before, one should make two <s>puruṣas</s>.

children.text: udakṣimata upāntyayoḥ chidraṃ pratimucya ullikhya dakṣiṇapakṣe puruṣaṃ uttarata upāntyayoḥ pratimucya uttarapakṣe puruṣaṇṭapucche tu paścime śaṅkau veṇormadhyamachidraṃ pratimucya dakṣiṇottaraṃ veṇuṃ nidhāya chidrayoḥśaṅkuṃ nihatya tayośchidraṃ pratimucya paścimottaraṃ paścimadakṣiṇaṃ cālikhya puruṣaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Fixing the hole at the southern [pegs] of the penultimate [pair], drawing, [one makes] a <s>puruṣa</s> on the southern wing. Fixing at the northern penultimate [pair], [one makes] a <s>puruṣa</s> on the northern wing. For the tail, fixing the middle hole of the reed at the back peg, placing the reed north-south, fixing pegs at the holes, fixing the hole at those, drawing northwest and southwest — one should make the <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā āratnaninā dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ pravardhayati /
children.translated_text: Having done thus, one extends the southern wing to the south by an <s>aratni</s>.

children.text: uttaramapi pakṣamuttarato 'ratninaiva prādeśena vitastyā vā paścāt pucchaṃ pravardhayati //
children.translated_text: The northern wing also to the north by an <s>aratni</s> itself; and to the west, the tail by a <s>prādeśa</s> or <s>vitasti</s>.

Releasing from the back [peg], fixing another hole of the reed at the middle peg, placing the reed downward from above to the meeting-point of the lines. 'Meeting-point of the lines' — the intersection of the lines. Having placed [the reed] close above that [point], fixing pegs at the end holes, fixing the middle hole of the reed at that [peg], establishing the other holes at the line-ends, one fixes pegs at the holes — that is called the <s>puruṣa</s> square. Thus, clockwise, one should make four <s>puruṣas</s> on the body. Fixing the hole of the reed at the back peg, placing the reed behind along the spine, fixing pegs at the two back holes also — as before, one should make the second <s>puruṣa</s>. Similarly to the north also, drawing north-west and north-east, one measures two <s>puruṣas</s>. To the west of the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> area, leaving a passage, having fixed a peg on the spine, fixing the reed's hole at that, dropping the reed on the spine, two pegs at the holes. At the back peg, fixing the reed's hole, dropping [it] westward on the spine — two pegs. Thus five pegs.

children.text:
pṛṣṭhyā masaṃ vā śabdo vikalpārthaḥ /
evamiha veṇumānam /
dvau tāvadveṇū bhavataḥ /
tayorakeḥ puruṣamātraḥ /
anyaḥ puruṣamātrasyākṣṇayā rajjusamaḥ /
tābhyāṃ vimānamapareṇa yupāvaṭadeśaṃ sañcaramavaśiṣyate /

children.translated_text: A peg on the spine.
Then, to the west of that, at the same distance, a peg.

children.text: madhyamaśaṅkāvakṣṇayāmātraṃ veṇuṃ pratimucya pūrvasmin puruṣamātraṃ prati mucya tābhyāṃ dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ nirharet /
children.translated_text: Fixing the diagonal-measure reed at the middle peg, and the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [reed] at the front [peg], by these two one should carve out the southern shoulder.

children.text: puruṣamātraṃ pūrvasmādunmucyāparasmin pratismin pratimucyottaramaṃsaṃ dākṣaṇottarapaścimamadhyamaśaṅkūnāṃ pārśvadvayeṣvarddhapuruṣamātreṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya pukṣapucchapuruṣānapyevameva kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Releasing the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure from the front [peg] and fixing at the back [peg], [one carves out] the northern shoulder. At the two sides of the southern, northern, western, and middle pegs, at half-<s>puruṣa</s> measures, having fixed pegs, the wing and tail <s>puruṣas</s> should be made in the same manner.

'From the spine, or' — the word 'or' is for the purpose of an alternative. Thus here is the reed-measurement. There are two reeds. Of those, one is of <s>puruṣa</s> measure. The other is equal to a cord of the diagonal of a <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [square]. By these two, the measurement is [done], leaving a passage to the west of the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> area.
'Releasing, one fixes' —

children.text: samaraḥ -- saṅgamaḥ pūrvāpare chidre lekhayoryatra nipatatastāveva lekhāntau /
children.translated_text: 'Meeting-point' — the junction. The front and back holes [correspond to] where the lines fall — those very [points] are the line-ends.
'He measures' —
On the spine, of the front two squares, the side-peg [is the same as] the eastern [peg] of the rear two.
'A <s>puruṣa</s> on the wing' —

children.text: dākṣiṇātyānāṃ pañcānāṃ śaṅkūnāṃ madhyameṣu triṣu veṇuṃpratimucya aparābhyāmityādi /
children.translated_text: Of the five southern pegs, fixing the reed at the middle three, 'with the two outer ones' — and so on.
'A <s>puruṣa</s> on the tail' —

children.text:
pāśvātyānāṃ trayāṇāṃ dakṣiṇayorantye chidre pratimucya madhyame chidre śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evamuttarayorevaṃ sthitānāṃ pañcānāṃ madhye madhyameṣu triṣu veṇuṃ pratimucyottarābhyāmityādi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Of the three side [pegs], fixing the end hole at the two southern ones, one should fix a peg at the middle hole. Similarly with the two northern ones. Of the five thus established, [fixing] the reed at the middle three, 'with the two northern ones' — and so on, to be seen.
'A <s>puruṣa</s> on the northern [wing]' —
As for the southern wing.
'By an <s>aratni</s>... thus stated' —

children.text:
veṇoḥ pañcame lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tena pakṣau pravardhayet, evaṃ daśame lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā /
pucchaṃ prakārāntaramāha ----
children.translated_text: Having made a mark at the fifth [division] of the bamboo-rod, by that one should extend the wings; similarly having made a mark at the tenth. He states another method for the tail —

children.text:
pṛṣṭhyānto maṃsaṃ dvāvatra veṇū ubhyataśchidau, puruṣamātraḥsaviśeṣaś ca /
pṛṣṭhyāyāṃ puruṣāntarālān trīn śaṅkūnnihatya madhyame saviśeṣaṃ pratimucya pūrvasminnitaraṃ tayorantye cchidre yatra saṃpatataḥsa dakṣiṇāṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the end of the spine-line is the shoulder. There are two bamboo-rods with holes at both ends: one of <s>puruṣa</s>-measure and one with the <s>saviśeṣa</s> (excess). Having driven three stakes at <s>puruṣa</s>-intervals on the spine-line, fastening the <s>saviśeṣa</s> [rod] at the middle [stake], the other at the first [stake] — where the two end-holes meet, that is the southern shoulder.

children.text:
viparyasya puruṣamātraṃ pāśvātye pratimucya śroṇī pūrvavaduttarāṃsaḥ /
evaṃ pakṣapuccheṣvapi /
saviśeṣo veṇuḥsaptatiśatamaṅgulayo daśatilonāḥ /
children.translated_text: Reversing, fastening the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [rod] by its loop at the far [stake] — [that gives] the hip. As before, the northern shoulder. Similarly in the wings and tail also. The <s>saviśeṣa</s> bamboo-rod is one hundred and seventy <s>aṅgulas</s> minus ten <s>tilas</s>.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.

children.text: rajjvā vā vimāyottaravedinyāyena veṇunā vimimīte || ĀpŚus_9.4 ||
children.translated_text: Having measured with a cord, one re-measures with a bamboo-rod by the rule of the <s>uttaravedī</s> (upper altar). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.4]
Having measured with one or another cord, one subsequently re-measures with a bamboo-rod as [done for] the <s>uttaravedī</s> — for a transcendent purpose (<s>adṛṣṭārtha</s>).

children.text: sapakṣapuccheṣu vidhābhyāse 'pacaye ca vidhāsaptamakaraṇīṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā viharet || ĀpŚus_9.5 ||
children.translated_text: For [fire-altars] with wings and tail, in [fold-]increase and in [fold-]decrease, having made the <s>vidhā-saptama-karaṇī</s> (the producer-line of the seventh of the folds) into the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, one should construct. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.5]

children.text:
vidhābhyāse 'ṣṭavidhaprabhṛtayaḥ /
vidhāpacaye ekavidhādayaḥ /
teṣvekavidhādiṣu vidhāsaptamakaraṇī yena veṇunā vimimīte tadardhāṣṭamaṃ bhavati /
sa puruṣasthānīyaḥ /
evaṃ caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvavadvibhajya viharet /
sapakṣapuccheṣviti vacanamekavidhānārtham /
eteṣvekavidhā diṣu śyenādiṣu kriyamāṇeṣu yadyekavidhā tatpañcadaśadhā vibhajya dvau bhāgau samasya caturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya mānena veṇunā gṛhṇīyāt /
sa puruṣasthānīyaḥ /
evaṃ sarvatra /
yāvadvidhaṃ tatkṣetraṃ samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya pramāṇaṃ gṛhṇīyāt; yathā catvāri sahasrāṇyaśītitilāḥ (4080) puruṣaḥ /
teṣāṃ vargaḥ-ekā koṭiḥ ṣaṭṣaṣṭirniyutāni catvāryayutāni ṣaṭsahasrāṇi catvāri śatāni (16646400) yadyaṣṭavidhaḥ aṣṭabhirguṇayitvā pūrvārdhaṃ saṃyojya pañcadaśalabdhaṃ dviguṇīkṛtya mūlaṃ gṛhṇīyāt /
sa tasya puruṣo bhavati /
apacaye tvardhasaṃyogo nāsti /
aratripādeśābhāvāt /
anyatsarvamuvacayena tulyam /
ardhatilena vā ūnādhike vā doṣo na bhavati viśeṣā darśanāt /
tatra ślokaḥ --
children.translated_text: 'In fold-increase' means from the eight-fold onward. 'In fold-decrease' means from the one-fold onward. In those [fire-altars] from the one-fold onward: the <s>vidhā-saptama-karaṇī</s> — the bamboo-rod by which one measures — its eighth-and-a-half [part] results. That is the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute. Having thus made the quadrilateral, one should divide and construct as before. The phrase 'with wings and tail' is for the purpose [of prescribing] the one-fold [fire-altars with appendages]. In these one-fold and other [fire-altars], when hawk-altars etc. are being made: if it is one-fold, dividing that one fold into fifteen parts, combining two parts [to make a square], having made an equal square, one should take its measure with the bamboo-rod. That is the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute. Similarly everywhere. Having made the area of whatever fold into an equal square, one should take its measure. Thus: four thousand and eighty <s>tilas</s> [equal] one <s>puruṣa</s>. Their square is: one <s>koṭi</s>, sixty-six <s>niyutas</s>, four <s>ayutas</s>, six thousand, four hundred (16,646,400). If eight-fold: multiplying by eight, adding the first half [i.e., the cubit-prādeśa portion], dividing by fifteen, doubling the quotient, and taking the root — that becomes the <s>puruṣa</s> [substitute] for that [altar]. In decrease, however, there is no addition of the half, because of the absence of cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions]. Everything else is the same as in increase. Whether [the result] is deficient or excessive by half a <s>tila</s>, there is no fault — from the observation of <s>viśeṣa</s> (approximation). Therein a verse:
'The square of sky-five-sky-Veda (4080),
increased by the desired [fold], divided by the <s>tithis</s> (15) —'

children.text: labdhasya vṛddhasya yamena mūlaṃ vṛddhau kṣaye tatpuruṣasya mānam //
children.translated_text: 'The root of the doubled quotient, in increase and decrease — that is the measure of the <s>puruṣa</s>.'
'Always in decrease and in increase ...'
Thus.

children.text:
nanvekavidhādayaḥ śyenādayo vakrapakṣapucchāḥ kartavyā iti pratipāditam /
tasmātkiṃ mahatā prayatnena hetūnāṃ darśanena? satyametat! kartavyā ekavidhādaya iti kṛtvā vkacitteṣu yadyekavidhādayaḥ kartavyāḥ tadā kratvarthakatayopādīyante /
tadā śyenādaya ākṛtivikārāḥ puruṣātmakāḥ santaḥ tadvikṛtyādhiśayeran /
yathā puruṣamātratāṃ vikṛtya pakṣapucchānāṃ saptārdhavidhe śyenādayaḥ pravartante evaṃ puruṣaṃ vikṛtya ekavidhādiṣu niviśeran /
tatra yadā sapakṣapucchatvamekavidhādīnāṃ tadāyaṃ vidhiriti aṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāmapi mārgāntareṇa vidhānādadoṣaḥ /
sapakṣapucchoṣviti vidhānāt /
praugādiṣvekavidhādayo na santi /

children.translated_text: But the eight-fold and others [do exist in those shapes] — so say some.
And he will state: 'as large as the fire[-altar] with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions].'

children.text: apare punarekavidhādiṣu na santi nāpacayeṣviti varṇayanti /
children.translated_text: Others, however, describe: in the one-fold and others they do not exist, nor in the decrease[-series].
Because of the statement 'with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions].'

Now, it has been established that the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars] such as hawks etc. are to be made with curved wings and tail. Therefore, what is the [need for] great effort in showing reasons? True! Having accepted that one-fold and other [fire-altars] should be made, sometimes when one-fold and others are to be made, they are employed for the purpose of the sacrifice. Then the hawk and other form-modifications, being based on the <s>puruṣa</s> [unit], would be superimposed upon that modification. Just as, having modified the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure, the hawk etc. proceed with wings and tail in the seven-and-a-half fold, so too, having modified the <s>puruṣa</s>, they would be installed in the one-fold and others. There, when the one-fold and others have wings and tail, this rule [applies] — therefore, since the eight-fold and subsequent [fire-altars] are also prescribed by another method, there is no fault. Because of the prescription 'with wings and tail.' In the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped) and other [altars], the one-fold and others do not exist.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(Having measured with a cord... one re-measures.)

children.text: athavā ekarajjvādīnāmanyatamayā rajvāgniṃ vimāya paścādadṛṣṭārthaṃ veṇunā vimimīte /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having measured the fire[-altar] with one of the cords — single-cord etc. — afterwards, for a transcendent purpose, one re-measures with a bamboo-rod.

children.text: uttaravedinyāyena yathottaravediryugenayajamānasya vā padairvimāya śamyayā parimimīte adṛṣṭārthaṃ; evamatrāpi rajjvā vimāya veṇunā mānamadṛṣṭārthaṃ syāt, tathottaravedivikāratvādagneḥ rajjvā vimāya veṇunā śamyayā cādṛṣṭārthaṃ vimānaṃ bhavediti //
children.translated_text: By the rule of the <s>uttaravedī</s>: just as the <s>uttaravedī</s>, having been measured by a yoke or by the paces of the sacrificer, is re-measured with a <s>śamyā</s> for a transcendent purpose — so here too, having measured with a cord, the [re-]measurement with a bamboo-rod would be for a transcendent purpose. And since the fire[-altar] is a modification of the <s>uttaravedī</s>, having measured with a cord, the re-measurement with a bamboo-rod and <s>śamyā</s> would be for a transcendent purpose.
With wings... [continuation]

children.text:
sapakṣapuccheṣu praugādivyatirikteṣvagniṣvabhyāse 'ṣṭavidhādāvapacaye caikavidhādau caikavidhādau vidhāvidhānaṃ karaṇīnāmucyate vidhāsaptamakaraṇīṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā viharet /
yāvatyo 'gnervidhāḥsanti tāsāṃ saptamaṃ yā karoti sā vidhā saptamakaraṇī tāṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā tayā'tmapakṣapucchāni viharediti /
ayamarthaḥ -- yadyekavidho 'gniḥ ; tamekavidhaṃ pañcadaśadhā vibhajya dvau bhāgau samasya samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya pramāṇaṃ puruṣakthāne kṛtvā anenātmapakṣapucchāni viharediti /

children.translated_text: Similarly one should do for the two-fold and others.
Four thousand and eighty <s>tilas</s> [equal] one <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ varga ekā koṭiḥ ṣaṭprayutāni ṣaṇṇiyutāni catvāryayutāni ṣaṭsasrāṇi catvāri śatāni (16646400) yadyaṣṭavidhaṃ puruṣavargamaṣṭabhirguṇitvā pūrvarāśyarghena ca saṃyojya tatpañcadaśabhirvibhajya labdhaṃ dviguṇīkṛtya mūle gṛhīte sa tasya puruṣo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Their square is: one <s>koṭi</s>, sixty-six <s>prayutas</s>, sixty <s>niyutas</s>, four <s>ayutas</s>, six thousand, four hundred (16,646,400). If eight-fold: multiplying the <s>puruṣa</s>-square by eight, adding [the area of] the first [i.e., cubit-prādeśa portion], dividing the total by fifteen, doubling the quotient, and taking the root — that becomes the <s>puruṣa</s> [substitute] for that [altar].
In decrease, however, because of the absence of cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], there is no addition of the half.

For fire-altars with wings and tail — those other than the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped) etc. — in fold-increase from the eight-fold onward, and in fold-decrease from the one-fold onward: the rule for folds is stated by means of <s>karaṇīs</s> (producer-lines). Having made the <s>vidhā-saptama-karaṇī</s> (the producer-line of the seventh of the folds) into the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, one should construct. However many folds the fire[-altar] has — the [line] that makes the seventh of those is the <s>vidhā-saptama-karaṇī</s>; having made that into the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, by it one should construct the body, wings, and tail. The meaning is: if the fire-altar is one-fold, dividing that one fold into fifteen parts, combining two parts [to form a square], having made an equal square, having made its measure into the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute, by this one should construct the body, wings, and tail.
Now, it was stated that the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars] do not have wings and tail — true, it was stated.

children.text: tadvyāyāmamātrarūpatvena ekavidhādau na ghaṭata ityevamarthamidamiti tatraiva vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: That [statement] is because the <s>vyāyāma</s>-measure form does not fit in the one-fold and other [fire-altars] — with this intention it was explained there itself.
And [it was stated] for establishing the primary-form nature of the one-fold.
Therefore it is not an absolute prohibition; the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars] do indeed have wings and tail.
The rest is the same as in increase.
Here they cite a verse:
'The square of sky-five-sky-Veda (4080),
increased by the desired [fold], divided by the <s>tithis</s> (15) —'

children.text: tasya pravṛddhasya yamena mūlaṃ sambhāvayetsāpacaye ca vṛddhau //
children.translated_text: 'The root of the doubled quotient — one should calculate this in both decrease and increase.'
Thus.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
(Having measured with a cord... one re-measures.)
In this view, like the <s>śamyā</s>-measurement, the bamboo-rod measurement is for a transcendent purpose.
Now he states the construction for the eight-fold and subsequent, and the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars]:
With wings... [continuation]

children.text:
sapakṣapucchā agnayaḥ caturaśraśyenakaṅkacidalajacitaś ca /
tatrāṣṭavidhādiṣu vidhānāmabhyāsaḥ /
ekavidhādiṣvapacayaḥ /
vidhānāṃ (ekībhūtānāṃ) samastānāṃ saptamasya karaṇī vidhāsaptamakaraṇī /
cīyamānasyāgneryoṃ'śaḥ tasya karaṇī puruṣasthānīyā /
sā cāṣṭavidhaprabhṛtīnāmityatraiva pradarśitā /
atrāpi sārātniprādeśapakṣe vidhārdhāṣṭamakaraṇīmiti draṣṭavyam /
apacayavacanaṃ śyenacidādyartham /
caturaśrāṇāmekavidhādīnāmapakṣapucchatvāt /
pūrvatra puruṣāveśanamuktaṃ, idānīṃ tasya viharaṇamucyate ityato na punaruktiḥ /
yadvā pūrvasūtramaṣṭavidhādiviṣayaṃ caturaśraviṣayaṃ ca /
ḍadamekavidhādīnāṃ śyenādīnāṃ ca sādhāraṇamityasti viśeṣaḥ /
idaṃ cānena jñāyate -- śyenacidādayo guṇavikārāḥsaptavidhādivadekavidhādiṣvapi bhavanti /
śakhāntarīyatvaṃ ca tasya pūrvamevoktam /
ata eva tasya pakṣasya yatnasādhyatvāt tatraivopadhāna prakāro vakṣyate -- "yāvānagniḥsāratniprādeśaḥ' ityādi /
children.translated_text: Fire-altars with wings and tail are: the quadrilateral, hawk, <s>kaṅka</s> (heron), <s>alaja</s> (kingfisher), and <s>cita</s> (pyre). Among these, in the eight-fold and subsequent — fold-increase. In the one-fold and subsequent — fold-decrease. The <s>karaṇī</s> (producer-line) of the seventh of all the combined folds is the <s>vidhā-saptama-karaṇī</s>. That portion of the fire-altar being piled — its <s>karaṇī</s> is the <s>puruṣa</s>-substitute. And that has been demonstrated for the eight-fold onward in this very [context]. Here too, in the option with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], one should observe the <s>vidhā-ardha-aṣṭama-karaṇī</s> (producer-line of the half-eighth of the folds). The mention of 'decrease' is for the purpose of hawk-altar and the like. Since the quadrilateral [fire-altars] of one-fold and other [sizes] are without wings and tail. The entry of the <s>puruṣa</s> [measure] was stated earlier; now its construction is stated — hence no repetition. Alternatively, the previous sūtra is for the eight-fold and subsequent, and for the quadrilateral [altars]. This [present sūtra] is common to the one-fold and others and to the hawk etc. — therein lies the distinction. By this it is also known: the hawk-altar and other shape-modifications occur in the one-fold and others just as in the seven-fold and subsequent. And its belonging to another branch [of Veda] was stated earlier. For that very reason, because that option requires effort, the placement-method for it will be stated — 'as large as the fire[-altar] with cubit-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions]' etc.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.
The molds for the eight [types of] bricks — one should have them made with the fifth [part] of the <s>puruṣa</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.6a]

children.text:
iṣṭakānāṃ karaṇāni vakṣyāma iti śeṣaḥ /
puruṣasya pañcamena aratninā kārayet /
children.translated_text: 'We shall state the molds for the bricks' — this is to be supplied. 'With the fifth of the <s>puruṣa</s>' — with the <s>aratni</s> (cubit), one should have [them] made.

children.text: tāsām evaikato 'dhyardhās tad dvitīyam | puruṣasya pañcamo bhāga ekataḥ prādeśa ekataḥ tat tṛtīyam || ĀpŚus_9.6b ||
children.translated_text: Of those same [bricks], one-and-a-half on one side — that is the second [mold]. The fifth part of the <s>puruṣa</s> on one side, a <s>prādeśa</s> on one side — that is the third. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.6b]

children.text:
tāsāmeveṣṭakānāṃ (katipayā) ekato 'dhyardhā ardhenādhikāstāsāṃ karaṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ triprādeśā pārśvamānī aratnimātrā tiryaṅbhānī dvitīyasya karaṇasya /
aratniḥ pārśvamānī /
prādeśastiryaṅbhānī tattṛtīyakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Of those same bricks, (some) are one-and-a-half on one side — greater by a half; their mold — the third: three <s>prādeśas</s> (36 aṅg.) is the side-measure, <s>aratni</s>-measure (24 aṅg.) is the breadth — of the second mold. <s>Aratni</s> (cubit) is the side-measure; <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) is the breadth — that is the third mold.

children.text: sarvataḥ prādeśas tac caturtham | samacaturaśrāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyās tat pañcamam || ĀpŚus_9.6c ||
children.translated_text: A <s>prādeśa</s> on all sides — that is the fourth. Equal-square [bricks] of one-fifteenth [of the <s>puruṣa</s>] — that is the fifth. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.6c]

children.text:
aṣṭāṅgulena kārikāstatpañcamaṃ karaṇam /
samacaturaśrā iti kimarthamiha saṅguhaṇam? yasminnagnau samacaturaśrā eveṣṭakāḥ tatrāpyāsāṃ praveśo yathā syādityevamartham /
vakṣyati ca "aṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna' iti /
aṇūkapañcadaśabhāgīyayorekaviṣayatvam /
children.translated_text: Of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> are the [bricks produced by] that fifth mold. Equal-square [bricks] — why is this specification made here? So that in whichever fire-altar only equal-square bricks [are required], there too these [bricks] may be introduced — for that purpose. And he will state: 'the <s>aṇūkas</s> (small bricks) take the place of the fifteenth-part [bricks].' The <s>aṇūka</s> and the fifteenth-part [brick] have the same domain.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
(Molds... one should have made.)

children.text:
