idānīmiṣṭakānāṃ karaṇānyucyante -- pāribhāṣikaḥ puruṣaḥ pañcāratniḥ /
tasya pañcamenāratninā /
pañcamenoti jātāvekavacanam /
pañcamairityarthaḥ /
kārayetkuśalaiḥ /
tairaratnibhiścaturbhiḥ prathamaṃ karaṇam
children.translated_text: Now the molds for the bricks are stated. The technical <s>puruṣa</s> is five <s>aratnis</s> (cubits). With its fifth — with the <s>aratni</s>. 'Fifth' — the singular is in the sense of the generic. The meaning is 'with fifths.' One should have [them] made by skilled [craftsmen]. With those four <s>aratnis</s> [i.e., forming an aratni-square] — the first mold.
Of those... the second.

children.text: tāsāṃ pañcamakṛtānāmeveṣṭakānāṃ yā ekataḥ -- ekasmin bhāge 'dhyarthāratnayāyāmāḥ tāsāṃ karaṇaṃ cattaddvitīyaṃ kārayet /
children.translated_text: Of those same bricks made with the fifth [mold]: those which on one side — on one part — are of one-and-a-half <s>aratni</s> length; their mold — that second one should be made.
'Of those same' is connected throughout.
The <s>puruṣa</s>'s... the third.

children.text: yāsāmekasmin pārśve caturviṃśatyaṅgulayaḥ ekato dvādaśāṅgulayastāsāṃ yatkaraṇaṃ tattṛtīyam /
children.translated_text: Those which have twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> on one side and twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> on the other — their mold is the third.
On all sides... the fourth.

children.text:
yāsāṃ sarvataḥ prādeśaḥ pramāṇaṃ tāsāṃ yatkaraṇaṃ taccatirtham /
sarvato grahaṇaṃ prādeśagrahaṇena vkacidghuhaṇaṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: Those whose measure is a <s>prādeśa</s> (hand-span) on all sides — their mold is the fourth. The word 'on all sides' together with the word '<s>prādeśa</s>' hints at [a <s>prādeśa</s>-measure] somewhere [in other contexts].
Equal... the fifth.

children.text:
puruṣasya pañcadaśabhāgo 'ṣṭāṅgulayaḥ /
tena parimitāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyā iṣṭakāḥ īṭṛśāḥsamacaturaśrāḥ, tāsāṃ yatkaraṇaṃ tatpañcamam /
samacaturaśragrahaṇādeva pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ kāryeṇūkādayaḥ prāptāḥ /
tatra prāgudakpaścimeṣu caturaśratvaniyamo nāstīti jñāyate /
dvitīyādivyavahāraḥ kimarthaḥ? adṛrṣṭārthameva /
tathopadhānādiṣu darśanāt /
children.translated_text: The fifteenth part of a <s>puruṣa</s> is eight <s>aṅgulas</s>. Those measured by that are the 'fifteenth-part bricks' — of this kind, equal-square; their mold is the fifth. By the specification 'equal-square' itself, [bricks] to be used in place of fifteenth-part [bricks] — such as <s>aṇūkas</s> — are obtained. There it is known that in the east, north, and west [directions], there is no restriction of being quadrilateral. For what purpose is the designation 'second' etc.? For a transcendent purpose alone. From the observation [of their use] in placement etc.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary
Now he states the molds for the bricks of the fire[-altar] thus measured:
(Molds... one should have made.)
This is one mold: of <s>aratni</s>-measure (24 aṅg.), equal-square.

children.text: tāsā tīyaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśikā pārśvamānī, tiryaṅbhānī catuviṃśikaiva /
children.translated_text: Of those... the second: thirty-six [aṅgulas] is the side-measure; the breadth is twenty-four itself.
The <s>puruṣa</s>'s... the third: thus half-bricks.
(On all sides... the fifth.)
Of eight <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.

children.text: ūrvdhvapramāṇamiṣṭakānāṃ jānoḥ jānoḥ pañcamena kārayet || ĀpŚus_9.7a ||
children.translated_text: The upward measure (thickness) of the bricks — one should have [them] made with the fifth of the knee(-height). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.7a]

children.text:
itsedhapramāṇamiṣṭakānāṃ jānupramāṇapañcamam /
dvātriṃśadaṅgulaṃ jānuḥ /
tasya pañcamabhāgena trayodaśatilādhikaṣaḍaṅgulena kārayet /
mahāgneriṣṭakānāmevaitanmahāgneḥ karaṇāni vidhāya vidhānāt /
children.translated_text: The thickness-measure of the bricks is the fifth of the knee-measure. The knee(-height) is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>. With its fifth part — six <s>aṅgulas</s> and thirteen <s>tilas</s> additional — one should have [them] made. This thickness is for the bricks of the great fire[-altar] alone — because of the prescription of molds for the great fire[-altar].
With half [of that], for the <s>Nākasad</s> (heaven-seated) and <s>Pañcacūḍā</s> (five-crested) [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.7b]

children.text: jānupañcamārdhena nākasadāṃ pañcacūḍānāṃ cotsedhaṃ saptatilādhikāṅgulatrayotsedhena kārayet //
children.translated_text: With half of the fifth of the knee(-height), the thickness of the <s>Nākasad</s> and <s>Pañcacūḍā</s> [bricks] — one should make [them] with a thickness of three <s>aṅgulas</s> and seven additional <s>tilas</s>.

children.text: yat pacyamānānāṃ pratihrasīta purīṣeṇa tat sampūrayed aniyataparimāṇatvāt purīṣasya || ĀpŚus_9.8 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever shrinks during firing — that one should fill with <s>purīṣa</s> (loose earth), because the <s>purīṣa</s> is of indeterminate measure. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 9.8]

children.text:
pacyamānānāmiṣṭakānāmutsedhataś ca parimāṇataś ca pratihrāso bhavettatpurīṣeṇa pūrayet /
kuta ityāha -- aniyataparimāṇatvātpurīṣasya -- niyataparimāṇā iṣṭakāḥ aniyataparimāṇaṃ purīṣam /
iyadetatpurīṣaṃ prakṣeptavyamiti niyamābhāvāt tenaiva pūracitavyam /
children.translated_text: When the bricks shrink during firing, both in height and in measure, that should be filled with <s>purīṣa</s> (loose earth). Why? He says: because the <s>purīṣa</s> has no fixed measure -- bricks have fixed measures, but <s>purīṣa</s> has no fixed measure. Since there is no rule prescribing 'this much <s>purīṣa</s> is to be added,' it should be filled with that very [material].
Ninth section.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(Height -- should have made.)

children.text:
sarvāsāmiṣṭakānāmūrthvāpramāṇamutsedhaṃ jānupañcamena kārayet /
aṅgulyadhikāre dvātriṃśajjānuriti bodhāyanaḥ /
tasya pañcamaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulayaḥ ardhacaturadaśāstilāś ca /
tena saṃmitamiṣṭakānām ūrdhvapramāṇaṃ bhavati /
jānudaghnaṃ cinvīta prathamaṃ cinvānaḥ, pañca citayo bhavantīti śrutyoḥsamāveśādūrdhvapramāṇe samaṃ syādaśrutatvāditi jānupañcamā iṣṭakā bhaveyuḥ /
jānudviguṇā nābhiḥ /
jānutriguṇamāsyam /
jānudaghne sahasrā iṣṭakāḥ nābhidaghne dvisāhasrā dviprastārāś ca /
āsyadaghne triṣāhasrāḥ triprastārāś ca /
tatra sarvatra viśeṣāśravaṇāt jānupañcamamevordhvapramāṇamiṣṭakānām /
iṣṭakānāṃ kārayediti ihānuvartamāne punarapi tayorgrahaṇaṃ gārhapatyadhiṣṇayeṣṭakānāmapi jānupañcamatvāya /
children.translated_text: The upward measure -- the height (<s>utseadha</s>) -- of all bricks should be made as one-fifth of the knee [height]. <s>Bodhāyana</s> says: 'In the <s>aṅguli</s>-domain, the knee is thirty-two [<s>aṅgulas</s>].' Its fifth is six <s>aṅgulas</s> and fourteen-and-a-half <s>tilās</s>. The upward measure of bricks is equal to that. Since the two scriptural statements 'one should pile knee-deep the first piling' and 'there should be five layers' can be reconciled [only] if the upward measure is equal -- since [otherwise] it is not prescribed -- the bricks should be one-fifth of the knee [height]. The navel is twice the knee. The mouth is three times the knee. At knee-depth, one thousand bricks; at navel-depth, two thousand and two layers. At mouth-depth, three thousand and three layers. In all those [cases], since no specific [height] difference is heard, the upward measure of bricks is only one-fifth of the knee. The recurrence here of 'should have bricks made' -- the repeated mention of both [height and measure] is to include the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire-seat bricks also in the one-fifth-of-knee [standard].
(By half -- of that.)

children.text:
ardhena pañcacārdhenana kārayedityeva /
nākasadaśvūḍopadhānamantraviśeṣāḥ /
tairupadheyāḥ /
pañcapaḍhceṣṭakā jānupañvramasyordhena kāryāḥ uttarā "nākasadbhaya upadadhāti' /
ityekasmin prastāre tāsāmuttarādharabhāvadarśanāt /
iṣṭakābhirakeva jānudaghnādisāmpādanāt, purīṣopadhānīmaṣṭakā samīkaraṇārthe citervṛddhayarthaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'By half' means 'should be made of half of five' -- that is all. The <s>nākasad</s>, <s>aśvūḍa</s>, and placement-<s>mantras</s> are specific [variations]. Those [bricks] are to be placed with them. Five-by-five bricks should be made at half of five -- the knee-height; the upper [bricks are placed with the mantra] 'he places for those who sit in heaven.' Because in one layer, the upper-lower relationship of those [bricks] is observed; by bricks alone the knee-depth and such [heights] are achieved; the <s>purīṣa</s> placement-brick is for the purpose of leveling and for increasing the piling.
(What when firing -- of that.)

children.text:
karaṇaparikḷptānāṃ iṣṭakānāṃ pākavaśāt pratihrāsaḥ -- kṣaya upajāyate /
tatpurīṣeṇa pūrayet, anenṣṭakā na duṣyanti avarjanīyatvāt, tasya "mitraitāṃ paceti' liṅgāt, vātātapābhyāmapi śoṣaṇaṃ pāka eva /
ata eva pākavaśāddhīnamiṣṭakāyāmavistārobhayamupadhānakāle purīṣeṇa pūrayet /
kutaḥ? aniyataparimāṇatvāt purīṣasya /
na hyetāvat purīṣaṃ prakṣepaṇīyamiti niyamaḥ /
tasmātpākavaśāddhīnasya purīṣeṇa pūraṇameva /
jalārdrā mṛt purīṣaṃ /
teneṣṭakānāṃ hrāsaṃ pūrayet /
children.translated_text: Of bricks fabricated according to the [prescribed] constructions, shrinkage occurs due to firing -- decrease arises. That should be filled with <s>purīṣa</s>. By this, the bricks are not damaged, because [firing] is unavoidable -- this is indicated by the expression 'O <s>Mitra</s>, bake this one.' Even drying by wind and sun is indeed 'firing.' Therefore, what is reduced by firing -- in the height, length, and breadth of the brick -- both [dimensions] should be filled with <s>purīṣa</s> at the time of placement. Why? Because the <s>purīṣa</s> has no fixed measure. For there is no rule that 'this much <s>purīṣa</s> is to be added.' Therefore, the filling of what is reduced by firing is by <s>purīṣa</s> alone. Water-moistened clay is <s>purīṣa</s>. With that, one should fill the shrinkage of bricks.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
(Height -- should have made.)

children.text:
"triṃśadaṅgulaṃ jānuḥ, ityāgniveśyaḥ /
tasya pañcamaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulam, "ṣaḍaṅgulotsedhā, ityeva kātyāyanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The knee is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>' -- thus <s>Āgniveśya</s>. Its fifth is six <s>aṅgulas</s>. 'Of six <s>aṅgulas</s> height' -- thus indeed <s>Kātyāyana</s>.
(By half also.)
By three <s>aṅgulas</s>.
(What when firing -- of that.)
This is an implicit indication [applying to] all [materials] when they are drying.
'Whatever shrinks by drying and firing' -- thus indeed <s>Bodhāyana</s>.
Ninth section.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: upadhāne 'dhyardhā daśa purastāt pratīcīr ātmany upadadhāti | daśa paścāt prācīḥ || ĀpŚus_10.1a ||
children.translated_text: In placing, he places ten one-and-a-half [bricks] in front in the body (<s>ātman</s>), facing west; ten at the back, facing east. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.1a ||

children.text:
ātmani purastādbhāge ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulāyāmena kāritādyārdhāḥ pratīcīḥ pratyagāyatāḥ daśopadadhāti /
ātpranyeva paścādbhāge tā eveṣṭakāḥ tatsaṃkhyākāḥ prācīḥ -- prāgāyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the body, in the front portion, he places ten [bricks] made with a length of thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>, being one-and-a-half [standard bricks], facing west -- extending westward. In the body itself, in the rear portion, those very bricks of the same number, facing east -- extending eastward.

children.text: pañcapañca pakṣāgrayoḥ | pakṣāpyayayoś ca viśayās tāsām ardheṣṭakāmātrāṇi pakṣayor bhavanti || ĀpŚus_10.1b ||
children.translated_text: Five by five at the wing-tips; and at the wing-junctions also. The distinguishing [bricks]: half-brick measures in the wings. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.1b ||

children.text:
pañcapañca pakṣāgrayordakṣiṇāyatāḥ udagāyatāś ca /
viśayāś ca pañca codagāyatāḥ dakṣiṇāyatāś ca /
iṣṭakāśabdena pañcabhāgīyā eva gṛhyānte nādhyardā "viparītā apyayā' iti liṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Five by five at the wing-tips, extending south and extending north. And the distinguishing [bricks], five, extending north and extending south. By the word 'brick,' only the fifth-part [bricks] are meant, not the one-and-a-half [bricks] -- this is indicated by 'reversed at the junction.'

children.text: pañcapañca pucchapārśvayor dakṣiṇā udīcīś ca || ĀpŚus_10.1c ||
children.translated_text: Five by five on the tail-flanks, to the south and to the north. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.1c ||

children.text: pañcapañcadhyardhā dakṣiṇāyatā udagāyatāś ca yathā samīpe pradeśamātramavaśiṣyate tathopadheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Five by five one-and-a-half [bricks], extending south and extending north, should be placed such that a <s>prādeśa</s> (span)-measure remains nearby.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(Placing... facing west.)

children.text:
upadhānakālo dvatīyakaraṇotpannā iṣṭakāḥ ātmani pūrvānte daśopadadhyāt /
pratīcīḥ pratyagāyātāḥ udīcīriti /
tā eva eśa paścāt prācīḥ ātmani paścimānte prāgāyātāḥ tā eva /
children.translated_text: At the time of placement, bricks produced by the second construction should be placed -- ten in the body at the front end. Facing west -- extending westward, meaning northward. Those very [bricks], in the rear, facing east -- at the body's rear end, extending eastward -- those very [bricks].
(Five, which...)

children.text:
tā eva prācyau rītyau /
pakṣāpyayayoś ca viśayāḥ /
pakṣāpyayaḥ -- pakṣamūlaṃ vividhamātmani pakṣe ca śerata iti viśayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those very [bricks form] the two eastern rows. And at the wing-junctions also, the distinguishing [bricks]. The wing-junction -- the wing-base -- is the varied [part] that lies in both the body and the wing; hence 'distinguishing' (<s>viśaya</s>).
As to how much [extends] into the body and how much into the wing, he says:
(Of those... ends.)
Of those distinguishing [bricks], half-brick measures are in the wings.
The body [has bricks] by a cubit, the wing by a <s>prādeśa</s> -- this is the meaning.
The two eastern rows.
(Five... and.)

children.text: pucchapārśvayoḥ pañcapañca uttarā dakṣiṇāmukhāḥ dakṣiṇā uttarāmukhāḥ prācyau rītyau! uttarasūtre bhedāmāvāya pucchāgraprādeśasyāpṛthaggrītitā pratipādayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: On the tail-flanks, five by five -- the northern [bricks] facing south, the southern [bricks] facing north -- the two eastern rows. In the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>, to prevent division, the non-separate treatment of the tail-tip <s>prādeśa</s> will be established.
Therefore these [bricks] should be placed starting from the tip.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary:
Facing west -- extending westward. 'Facing north' -- in the body itself.
These extend northward; otherwise, the accommodation of five [bricks] would be impossible.

children.text: pakṣe ātmani ca śerata iti viśayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that lie in both the wing and the body are called 'distinguishing' (<s>viśaya</s>).
They are of <s>aratni</s> (cubit) measure in the body.
Leaving a <s>prādeśa</s> in front.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>):

children.text: pucche prādeśam upadhāya sarvam agniṃ pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet || ĀpŚus_10.2 ||
children.translated_text: Having placed a <s>prādeśa</s> [brick] in the tail, one should cover the entire fire[-altar] with fifth-part bricks. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.2 ||
One should complete the count with fifteenth-part bricks. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.3 ||

children.text:
pucche prādeśamupadhāya ātmasamīpe yadavaśiṣṭaṃ tatprādeśamatrārdheṣṭakādvayaṃ madhye abhitaḥ prādeśāḥ ṣaṭ /
ṣaṭsu vitastyā ca virdhanamuktaṃ kathaṃ prādeśamātramupadhāyeti? ucyate -- yadyapi vitastyā vardhanamuktaṃ, tathāpi karaṇāntarasya vidhānāt prādeśakṣetrameveṣṭakābhiśvetavyamiti yadaṅgulimātraṃ parigṛhītaṃ tatpuraṣiṇe pūrayitavyam /
amumevārtaṃ pradarśayituṃ prādeśamupadhāyetyuktam /
sarvamagnimiti -- pañcāśadadhyardhaḥ sūtroktāḥ pūccher'dheṣṭakādvayaṃ pracchādayet /
daśettaraṃ śataṃ pañcamabhāgīyaḥ śerate /
pūrvābhiḥsahāṣṭaṣaṣṭayadhikaṃ śatam /
pañcadaśeti -- ekasminpañcamabhāgīyākṣetre nava pañcadaśabhāgīyāḥśerate /
catasraḥ pañcamabāgīyā navadhā vibhajya yatra vkāpi pañcadaśabhāgīyāḥ kṣeptavyāḥ tatrāpi mantrepadhānasaukaryārthaṃ prādeśa ucyate /
children.translated_text: Four fifth-part [bricks], each divided into nine, wherever fifteenth-part [bricks] are to be added -- there too, a <s>prādeśa</s> is mentioned for the ease of mantra-placement.
In the body, in the second row in the middle, having removed two, [there are] eighteen.
And in the eighth row, eighteen.
Thus is the two-hundred layout.

Having placed a <s>prādeśa</s> [brick] in the tail, what remains near the body is a <s>prādeśa</s>-measure pair of half-bricks in the middle; on both sides, six <s>prādeśas</s>. In the six, the extension by a <s>vitasti</s> has been stated -- how then 'having placed a <s>prādeśa</s> measure'? It is answered: although the extension by a <s>vitasti</s> has been stated, nevertheless, because another construction is prescribed, the <s>prādeśa</s>-area alone is to be covered with bricks; whatever <s>aṅgula</s>-measure has been taken [beyond that] is to be filled with <s>purīṣa</s>. To show this very meaning, 'having placed a <s>prādeśa</s>' is stated. 'The entire fire[-altar]' -- fifty-and-a-half one-and-a-half [bricks] stated in the <s>sūtra</s> plus a pair of half-bricks of the tail should cover [it]. One hundred and ten fifth-part [bricks] lie [in the remainder]. Together with the former [bricks], one hundred and sixty-eight. 'Fifteenth' -- in one fifth-part-brick area, nine fifteenth-part [bricks] lie.
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary:
(In the tail -- should have covered.)

children.text:
pucche yatpuruṣādhikaṃ prādeśakṣetraṃ tadupadhāya sarvamagniṃ pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet /
ayamāśayaḥ -- ātmapat pucche ca purastātprabhṛti pañcamabāgīyābhiḥ pracchādyamāne 'gre prādeśamaviśiṣyate /
asmin yogābhiriṣṭakābhirupahite pucche ca bahavo bhedā bhavantīti matvā ācāryaḥ tatparihārāyāgramārabhya pucche prādeśopadhānapūrvakaṃ pracchādayediti /
yadvā -- prādeśaṃ pucche upadhāya -- pucche saṃyojya yathā prādeśaṃ pucchāt pṛthaggrīti na bhavati tathā kṛtvetyarthaḥ /
yadvā prādeśaṃ puccha upadhāya pucche nidhāya sthāpayitvā, "tāsāṃ ṣaṭṭapradhā upadhāyoti' vat /
yadvāgragataṃ prādeśaṃ pucchamūle nidadhyāt /
bhedaṃ viparyasye tarata upadadhyāditi /
tadayamarthaḥ -- yāvatā vacanavyaktiḥ sarvathā bhedābhāvāya pucchāgraṃ pucchāt pṛthagrītiṃ na kuryāt iti tātparyārtha iti /
sarveṣu pakṣeṣu atiriktaṃ prādeśaṃ pucchapūle 'nupahitamavaśiṣyate /
tadabhitaḥ prādeśābhirardheṣṭakābhirupadadhayāt /
kiñca uparitanaprastāre "yathā prathame prastāre pakṣau tathā pucchamiti' vacanāt pucchamūle 'tideśaprāptānāmadhyardhānāṃ vaiparītyaṃ vakṣyati -- "viparītā apyayā' iti /
taccaivamupadhāne samañjajasaṃ syāt /
itarathā viruddhārthamanartaṃ ca syāt /
tasmāt
children.translated_text: In the tail, having placed the <s>prādeśa</s>-area that exceeds the <s>puruṣa</s>[-area], one should cover the entire fire[-altar] with fifth-part bricks. This is the intent: when the body and tail together are being covered from the front onward with fifth-part bricks, at the tip a <s>prādeśa</s> remains undivided. In this configuration, when placed with these bricks, many breaks [in pattern] would occur in the tail -- considering this, the <s>ācārya</s> [prescribes that] to avoid those [breaks], one should cover starting from the tip, placing the <s>prādeśa</s> first in the tail. Or: 'having placed the <s>prādeśa</s> in the tail' means having joined [it] to the tail so that the <s>prādeśa</s> does not become separate from the tail -- this is the meaning. Or: having placed the <s>prādeśa</s> in the tail, having deposited and fixed [it]. Or: one should place the <s>prādeśa</s> at the tip at the tail-base. Reversing the break, one should place the other on the other side. This is the meaning: in whatever way the statement is made explicit, in every way, to avoid breaks, the tail-tip should not be treated separately from the tail -- this is the purport. In all options, the excess <s>prādeśa</s> at the tail-base remains unplaced. On both sides of that, one should place <s>prādeśa</s> half-bricks. Moreover, in the upper layer, because of the statement 'as the wings [are arranged] in the first layer, so [should be] the tail,' reversals of the one-and-a-half [bricks] that are obtained at the tail-base by analogy will be stated -- 'reversed at the junction.' And this would be consistent only with this [method of] placement. Otherwise, it would be contradictory and meaningless. Therefore,

children.text:
pucche prādeśamupadhāyetyasya bhāgasyāyamevārtho grāhyaḥ /
nanu kathaṃ sarvasyāgneḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādanam? ucyate -- atropahitānāmiṣṭakānāmabādhena sarvasminnagnau pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādyāmāne tadekadeśe tāsāmasambhave satyākhyātānāmarthaṃ bruvatāṃ śaktiḥ sahakāriṇī nahi vacanaśatenāpyaśaṅkanīyārthaḥśakyo vidhātumiti caturaśrābhiḥ pracchādayitumaśakyatvāt prathamapratītasarvaśabdānurodhena jaghanyaḥ pañcamabhāgīyāśabdo bāhulyābhiprāyo varṇanīyaḥ /
tena tattatsahakāriṇībhiratratyābhiḥ sambhavantībhirapi pracchādanaṃ kāryamityevamarthaṃ prādeśānāmatra prāptiḥ /
eṣa nyāyastatrāṅgīkaraṇīyaḥ /
tatratyābhiranuraktābhirapi pracchādane kiṃ vār'dheṣṭakāḥ karaṇenotpannāḥ na kutracidviniyuktāḥ /
tāsāmupadeśabalādeva atra saṃkhyāpūraṇe pracchādane ca yathāyogaṃ viniyogaḥ kāryaḥ /
kiñca yaccaturaśraṃ trayaśri vā sampadyetārdheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhirvā pracchādayediti paribhāṣāṃ vakṣyati /
tathā vātra samupadhānaṃ syāt /
atrātmani sandhyantarāle catvāriṃśat pañcamabhāgīyāstāsāṃ purastāddaśa paścācca daśa /
pakṣayorviṃśatiḥ pucche daśa /
tā etā daśottaraśataṃ pañcamabhāgīyāḥ, pañcāśadardhāścatasror'dhāḥ dvau prādeśāviti ṣaṭṣaṣṭhiḥ śataṃ ceṣṭakāḥ /
children.translated_text: These are one hundred and ten fifth-part bricks; fifty half-bricks, four quarter-bricks, two <s>prādeśa</s> [bricks] -- [totaling] one hundred and sixty-six bricks.

children.text: "sāhasraṃ cinvīta prathamaṃ cinvāna' ityādibhirvākyaiḥ pratyagnīṣṭakānāṃ sāhasrādayaḥsaṃkhyā vidhāsyante /
children.translated_text: By statements such as 'one should pile a thousand [bricks] the first time one piles,' the counts of a thousand and so on for each fire[-altar] will be prescribed.

children.text: tāś ca praticiti pratiprastāraṃ ca bhidyānta iti ca tatraiva pratipādayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: And that those [counts] differ for each layer and each spread -- that too will be established there.
How is the thousand-count achieved here? He says:

this is the meaning to be taken for 'having placed a <s>prādeśa</s> in the tail.' But how can the entire fire[-altar] be covered with fifteenth-part [bricks]? It is answered: here, without displacing the placed bricks, when the entire fire[-altar] is being covered with fifth-part bricks, wherever those [fifth-part bricks] cannot fit in that area -- [the principle is:] the capacity of those who state the meaning of the received [text] is an auxiliary; for even with a hundred statements, an impossible meaning cannot be prescribed -- because it is impossible to cover with square [bricks alone], following the primary [meaning of] the word 'entire,' the secondary [meaning of] the word 'fifth-part bricks' should be explained as intended [in the sense of] 'majority.' Therefore, covering should be done with auxiliary bricks of that [region] that fit even when intermingled -- this is the meaning; and the <s>prādeśa</s> [bricks] are appropriate here for this reason. This principle should be accepted there. In covering with contextually appropriate intermingled bricks, what about half-bricks produced by the construction that are not deployed anywhere? By the very force of the instruction, their deployment should be made as appropriate here in completing the count and in covering. Moreover, the paribhāṣā (meta-rule) will be stated: 'whatever becomes square or triangular should be covered with half-bricks or quarter-bricks.' Thus the placement should be. Here, in the body, in the intermediate joints, forty fifth-part bricks; of those, ten in front and ten at the back. In the wings, twenty; in the tail, ten.
(Five... should have made.)

children.text:
pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiraṣṭāṅgulābhiḥsaṃkhyā pūrayet /
kā saṃkhyātra pūryate? kiṃ samudāyagatā? uta prastāragatā aviśeṣāt? na samudāyagatā ānantaryāt, pratiprastāraṃ śatadvayaniyamācca, prastāragataiva saṃkhyā tatra pūryate, asya vacanasya sāmarthyādavasīyate saṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ upadhānāya pracchādikāsu kāsāṃciduddharaṇaṃ pracālanaṃ vā yathāyogaṃ nyāyyamiti /
atra prastāraśatadvayasampattaye catustriṃśatsaṃkhyāsampādyā /
sā ca pracchāditāsu kāśviduddhṛtya yogneṣṭakopadhānena bhavati /
tatraikasmin pañcamabhāgīyākṣetre nava pañcadaśabhāgīyāḥśerata iti /
tatratatropadhāne deśāniyame taduddharaṇena tāsāmupadhāne kārye mantropadhānasaukaryāya uddharaṇopadhānadeśaniyama ucyate /
tatrāsmani prācyo daśa rītayaḥ, tatra madhyamarītyoḥ dvitīye uddhṛtya tatra aṣṭādaśa pañcadaśabhāgīyā āvapet /
tayoreva rītyorupānte uddhṛtyāṣṭādaśa āvapet /
pucche catasnaḥ prācyo rītyaḥ, tatra madhyamayoranta uddhṛtya catasror'dheṣṭakā udīcīrupadadhyāt /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ pūryate /
atraike pucchāgre daśa prādeśānupadhāya pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayanti, teṣāṃ ca viparītavacanānarthakyaprasaṅgo maidaprasaṅgaś ca bhavatīti tathā nopadheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here some [authorities], having placed ten <s>prādeśa</s>-[sized bricks] at the tail-tip, cover with fifth-part [bricks]; but their [interpretation] leads to the purposelessness of the reversed-order statement and to the problem of joints — therefore they should not be placed thus.

children.text: kiñca -- yadi pucchāgre prādeśānāmupadhānamapīṣṭamabhaviṣyattarhi pādeṣṭakāścaturmāgīyānāṃ pakṣāgrayoḥ pañcadaśa pucchāgra iti ca spaṣṭataraṃ pucchāgra ityevāvakṣyat /
children.translated_text: Moreover — if the placement of <s>prādeśa</s>-[sized bricks] at the tail-tip had also been intended, then it would have been stated more clearly as "quarter-bricks and fourth-part [bricks] at the wing-tips, fifteen at the tail-tip" — stating "tail-tip" explicitly.
But it was not stated thus.
Therefore, the order of placement is established as stated [above].

One should complete the count with fifteen-part [bricks] of eight <s>aṅgulas</s>. What count is being completed here? Is it the aggregate [total]? Or the count per layer? — there being no distinction. Not the aggregate, because of the sequential order and because of the rule of two hundred per layer. The count per layer is what is completed there; from the capacity of this statement it is determined that completing the count [involves] removing or shifting some of the covering [bricks] for the purpose of placement — as appropriate. Here, thirty-four in number are to be obtained for the completion of two hundred per layer. And that is accomplished by removing some of the coverers and placing the required bricks. In one fifth-part area, nine fifteen-part [bricks] would fit. Since there is no restriction on the location of placement in various places, the rule for the location of removal and placement is stated for the convenience of mantra-based placement. In this [body section], there are ten east-facing rows; in the second of the two middle rows, having removed [bricks], one should place eighteen fifteen-part [bricks]. At the ends of those same two rows, having removed, one should place eighteen. In the tail, there are four east-facing rows; having removed [bricks] at the ends of the two middle [rows], one should place four half-bricks facing north. Thus the layer of two hundred is completed.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary

children.text:
pucchādavaśiṣṭaṃ prādeśakṣetraṃ yāmiriṣṭakābhirmedaparihāreṇopadhātuṃ śakyate tābhirupadadhyāt /
tatra pārśvayordve prādeśamātrayau madhye catasror'dheṣṭakā udagāyatāḥ /
etadeva prādeśakaraṇasya prayojanam /
ataḥ prādeśābhāvena kiyate /
śiṣṭāgnau pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādite ṣaṭṣaṣṭiśatamiṣṭakā bhavanti /
aratniprādeśarahite pañcāśacchataṃ iṣṭakā bhavanti /

children.translated_text: There, in the northern [part of] the body, [there are] nine rows.

children.text: tatra ātmani madhyamāyāṃ madhyamāścatasra uddhṛtya catuḥpañcāśannidheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, in the body, having removed the four middle [bricks] of the middle row, fifty-four should be placed.

children.text: ubhayatrāpi pucchāgre dve pañcamyāvuddhṛtya catasror'dheṣṭakā upadheyā udagāyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: In both [versions], at the tail-tip, having removed two fifth-[part bricks], four half-bricks should be placed facing north.
Thus the layer of two hundred [is complete].

The <s>prādeśa</s>-area remaining from the tail can be laid with <s>Yāmi</s>-bricks while avoiding joints — one should place them. There, on the two sides, two [bricks] of <s>prādeśa</s> measure; in the middle, four half-bricks facing north. This is precisely the purpose of making the <s>prādeśa</s> [extension]. Therefore, in the absence of <s>prādeśa</s> [extension], it is stated. When the remaining fire[-altar] is covered with fifth-part [bricks], there are one hundred and sixty-six bricks. Without the <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], there are one hundred and fifty bricks.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: aparasmin prastāre 'dhyardhā daśa dakṣiṇata udīcīr ātmany upadadhāti | daśottarato dakṣiṇāḥ || ĀpŚus_10.4a ||
children.translated_text: In the other (second) layer, one places ten-and-a-half [bricks] from the south facing north in the body; ten from the north facing south. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.4a]

children.text: ātmani dakṣiṇata utīcīrudagāyatāḥ daśādhyardhāḥ upadadhāti ātmanyevottarataḥ daśadhyardhāḥ dakṣiṇāyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the body, from the south, ten-and-a-half [bricks] facing north are placed, extending northward; in the body itself, from the north, ten-and-a-half [bricks] extending southward.

children.text: yathā prathame prastāre pakṣau tathā puccham | yathā pucchaṃ tathā pakṣau viparītā apyaye || ĀpŚus_10.4b ||
children.translated_text: As the wings [are laid] in the first layer, so the tail [in the second]; as the tail [in the first], so the wings — reversed at the junctions. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.4b]

children.text:
pucchāgre paścādadhyardhāḥ prāgāyatāḥ /
dakṣiṇe pakṣe paścāt pañca prāgāyatāḥ purastācc pañca /
ṣaṭpratyagāyatāḥ /
uttarapakṣe caivaṃ prāgāyatāḥ
children.translated_text: At the tail-tip, [bricks] behind [facing] east, and-a-half. In the southern wing, five behind facing east, and five in front. Six facing west. In the northern wing likewise, facing east

children.text:
pratyagāyatāś ca /
pucchāpyaye 'dhyardhāḥ pañca prāgāyatāḥ pratyagāyatāś ca /
pucchāpyaye 'dhyarthāḥ pañca prāgāyatāḥ /
tāsāmardheṣṭakāmātrā ātmani bhavanti /
evaṃ viparītā apyaye /
tāsāṃ purastātpañcārdheṣṭakā udīcyaḥ /
children.translated_text: and facing west. At the tail-junction, five-and-a-half facing east and facing west. At the tail-junction, five-and-a-half facing east. Their half-brick portions are in the body. Thus reversed at the junctions. In front of them, five half-bricks facing north.
One should cover the entire fire[-altar] with fifth-part [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.5]
One should complete the count with fifteen-part [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.6a]
This has been explained. As before, the layer of two hundred [is completed].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
The other ... [bricks]

children.text: dvitīye prastāre 'dhyardhā ātmano dakṣiṇe bhāge daśopadadhyāduttare daśa //
children.translated_text: In the second layer, one should place ten-and-a-half [bricks] in the southern part of the body, [and] ten in the northern [part].
As in the first ... wings

children.text:
prathamaprastāre yathā pakṣāvupahitau tathā pucche /
yathā pucchamupahitaṃ tathā pakṣayoḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati -- pucchāgre pucchāgrasandhau pañca pañcādhyardhā upadheyāḥ /
pakṣayostu pārśvayoḥ adhyardhā upadheyāḥ, tatra viśeṣamāha --
children.translated_text: In the first layer, as the wings were placed, so [should be done] in the tail. As the tail was placed, so in the wings. This is what is stated: at the tail-tip and tail-tip junction, five-and-five-and-a-half [bricks] should be placed. But on the sides of the wings, and-a-half [bricks] should be placed; there he states the distinction:
Reversed at the junctions

children.text:
pucchāpyaye pakṣāpyayavadatideśaprāptānāmadhyardhānāṃ ātmani aratni mātratvaṃ puccher'dheṣṭakāmātratvaṃ ca prāptotītyata āha /
atra viparītā bhaveyurardheṣṭakā mātrāṇyātmani bhaveyuraradnanimātrāṇi puccha ityarthaḥ /
asya ca bhedābhāvaḥ prayojanamiti pūrvasminneva prastāra uktaṃ /
children.translated_text: At the tail-junction, by the extension-principle from the wing-junction, the and-a-half [bricks] obtained would be of <s>aratni</s> measure in the body and of half-brick measure in the tail — therefore he says: here they should be reversed — the half-brick measures should be in the body and the <s>aratni</s> measures in the tail — this is the meaning. And the absence of joints as the purpose was stated in the very first layer.
The entire ... should complete

children.text:
atra purastāt prabhṛtyātmani pracchādyamāne pucchāpyayaviśayānāṃ purataḥ puruṣamātre prādeśo 'vaśiṣyate /
tatra pañcamabhāgīyānāmasambhavāt bhedābhāvāya pañcārdheṣṭakā udīcya upadheyāḥ, tāsāmupadhāne heturuktaḥ /
atrātmanyadhyardhānāṃ madhye pañcaṣaṣṭiḥ pañcama
children.translated_text: Here, when covering the body starting from the front, a <s>prādeśa</s> [area] is left over in front of the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure [area] related to the tail-junction. Since fifth-part [bricks] cannot fit there, for the sake of avoiding joints, five half-bricks should be placed facing north; the reason for their placement has been stated. Here in the body, among the and-a-half [bricks], in the middle, sixty-five fifth-
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary

children.text: bhāgīyāḥ pañca cārdhāḥ, pakṣayordvādaśa dvādaśa pañcamabhāgīyāḥ, pucche pañcadaśa tā etāḥ caturuttaraśataṃ pañcamabāgīyāḥ, pañcacārdhāḥ, catuḥpañcāghadadhyardhāḥ /
children.translated_text: part [bricks] and five halves; in the wings, twelve-and-twelve fifth-part [bricks]; in the tail, fifteen — these total one hundred and four fifth-part [bricks], five halves, and fifty-four and-a-half [bricks].

children.text: tā etāḥ triṣaṣṭiḥ śataṃ ca, atra saptatriṃśatsaṃkhyā sampādyā //
children.translated_text: These total one hundred and sixty-three; here thirty-seven in number must be obtained.
Fifteen ... should complete

children.text: atra pakṣayorātmani pucche catasraḥ pañcamabhāgīyā uddhṛtya ṣṭtriṃśataṃ pañcadaśabhāgīyā upadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: Here in the wings, body, and tail, having removed four fifth-part [bricks], one should place thirty-six fifteen-part [bricks].

children.text: atmani pūrvasyāṃ rītyāṃ madhye pañcoddhatya daśārdheṣṭakā udīcīrupadadhyādevaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ //
children.translated_text: In the body, in the front row, having removed five in the middle, one should place ten half-bricks facing north. Thus the layer of two hundred [is complete].
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
In the other [layer] ... likewise the tail

children.text:
atrāpyayayoḥ pañcapañcādhyardhāḥ /
pārśveṣu pañcapañcādhyardhāḥ, aratnanivṛddhau ṣaṭṣaḍiti draṣṭavyam /
pucchāpyaye yā upadhīyante tāsāmardheṣṭakāmātrāṇyātmani bhavanti /
pucche 'ratnimātrāṇi /
etacca prādeśavṛddhau /
itarathā ardheṣṭakāmātrāṇyeva pucche /
children.translated_text: Here too, at the junctions, five-and-five-and-a-half [bricks]. On the sides, five-and-five-and-a-half [bricks]; in the <s>aratni</s>-extension, six-and-six — this should be understood. At the tail-junction, the [bricks] that are placed have half-brick dimensions in the body and <s>aratni</s> dimensions in the tail. And this [applies] with the <s>prādeśa</s> extension. Otherwise, half-brick dimensions only in the tail.
The entire fire[-altar] ... should complete

children.text:
pūrvavadātmani madhye catasraḥṣaḍvoddhṛtya ekaikasya sthāne navanavāṣṭāṅgulāḥ /
sāratniprādeśapakṣe pucchāpyayasthābhyaḥ prākpañcārdheṣṭakā udagāyatā upadheyāḥ /
ātmani pūrvarītyāṃ madhyamāḥ pañcod dhṛtya daśārdheṣṭakā udagāyatā upadadhyāt /
evaṃ dviśataḥ /
aratniprādaśābhāve tu catu pañcāśatā pañcataśabhāgīyābhiḥ dvayūnaṃ dviśataṃ bhavati /
pucchapārśvayorevaikaikāṃ pañcamīmapohya catasror'dheṣṭakāḥ prāgāyatāḥ /
evaṃ dviśataḥ /
children.translated_text: As before, in the body in the middle, having removed four or six, in the place of each, nine-by-nine eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. With <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> wing [extensions], at the tail-junction, in front of those located [there], five half-bricks should be placed facing north and extending lengthwise. In the body, in the front row, having removed the middle five, one should place ten half-bricks extending northward. Thus two hundred. Without <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], with fifty-four fifteen-part [bricks], two hundred minus two results. At the tail-sides themselves, having removed one fifth-part [brick] each, four half-bricks facing east. Thus two hundred.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_10.6b ||
children.translated_text: One should pile in alternation for as many layers as one wishes to make. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.6b]
This has been explained.

children.text: pañca citayo bhavanti | pañcabhiḥ purīṣair abhyūhatīti purīṣāntā citir arthāntaratvāt purīṣasya || ĀpŚus_10.7 ||
children.translated_text: There are five layers of bricks; one fills [the spaces] with five [applications of] loose earth (<s>purīṣa</s>). The layer ends with the earth-fill, because the earth-fill has a different purpose. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.7]

children.text:
iṣṭakāsandhānārthaṃ purīṣam /
tasmāttadantā citiḥ /
tadarthatvāttadghareṇa gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: The loose earth (<s>purīṣa</s>) is for binding the bricks together. Therefore the layer ends with it. Because it serves that purpose, it is included by the main [element].

children.text: jānudaghnīṃ sāhasraṃ cinvīta prathamaṃ cinvānaḥ || ĀpŚus_10.8a ||
children.translated_text: One who piles for the first time should pile [the altar] knee-high, with one thousand [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.8a]

children.text: yaḥ prathamaṃ cinoti sa jānudaghnīṃ cinuyāt sahasrasaṅkhyāyutaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: He who piles for the first time should pile it knee-high, with a count of one thousand.
Since the prescriptions are made with reference to the great fire[-altar] alone, the one-thousand count does not include the <s>śālāmukhīya</s> and other subsidiary fire-seats (<s>dhiṣṇyas</s>).
Nor [does it include] the knee-height [measurement of those].

children.text: nābhidaghnīṃ dviṣāhasraṃ dvitīyam āsyadaghnīṃ triṣāhasraṃ tṛtīyam uttaram uttaraṃ jyāyāmsam || ĀpŚus_10.8b ||
children.translated_text: Navel-high with two thousand for the second [piling]; mouth-high with three thousand for the third; each subsequent one larger [than the previous]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.8b]
At navel-measure in height, two thousand, for one piling the second [time].
At mouth-measure [in height], for one piling the third [time].
Three thousand for the third; each subsequent one larger [than the previous].

children.text:
nābhipramāṇamutsedhataḥ dviṣāhsraṃ dvalitīyaṃ cinvānaḥ /
āsyapramāṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ cinvānaḥ /
triṣāhasraṃ ca grīvadaghnamityasmadīyā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: At navel-measure in height, two thousand, for one piling the second [time]. At mouth-measure [in height], for one piling the third [time]. Three thousand — and neck-high, according to our <s>Śruti</s> (scripture).

children.text: mahāntaṃ bṛhantam aparimitaṃ svargakāmaś cinvīteti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_10.8c ||
children.translated_text: One desiring heaven should pile [the altar] great, vast, and unlimited — this is known. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.8c]

children.text:
uttaramuttaramāhāramāharet /
jyāyān vidhābhyāsena /
mahānutsedhataḥ /
bṛhatparimāṇataḥ /
aparimitaṃ sahasrādibhyaḥ /
"svargakāma' iti vacanādāgnikalpe "vājisaneyikamiti' pacanācca vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Each subsequent one, one should add an addition; larger through the practice of [ritual] methods. "Great" — in height. "Vast" — in dimensions. "Unlimited" — beyond one thousand and the like. From the statement "one desiring heaven" and from the reading "of the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>" in the fire-ritual procedure, there is an option [between the two traditions].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Alternation ... should wish
Explained.

children.text:
nanu vyatyāse nāma yasmin prastāre yatra yādṛśānāmupadhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tadanantare prastāre tatrānyāṭṛśānāmupadhānaṃ tādṛśānāmevānyato dīrghāṇām /
naca bhedābhāvaḥ prayojanam; sa cehācāryapravṛcyaiva siddhaḥ, tatkimarthamidamucyate vyatyāsaṃ cinuyāditi? ucyate -- anyaprastāradvaye sūtrakārasya vyatyāsopadhānavidheruparyupari prastāreṣvaniyamāśaṅkā mandadhiyāṃ na bhavediti vyatyāsavacanam /
kiñca mantropadhānottaramapi prāmādika bhedadarśane tatparijihīrṣayā lokavadupahitānāmeva pracālanādiprāptau ""sa indra iṣṭakāmāvṛhat /
te vā kīryanteti'' doṣadarśanādayālanāya śulbopadhānasamaya eva śulbakuśalairniyatadeśānāmabhādhena bhedābhāgavaḥ pariharaṇīya ityevamarthaṃ vyatyāsavacanam /
children.translated_text: Now, alternation means: in whichever layer, wherever, whichever kind of [bricks] were placed, in the next layer, in that place, a different kind is placed — [or] the same kind but with different orientation. And the purpose is not [merely] avoiding joints; that is already accomplished here by the <s>ācārya's</s> own arrangement. Then why is it stated "one should pile in alternation"? It is answered: the alternation statement is so that the dull-minded may not suspect that in the layers above the two [explicitly described] layers composed by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author), there might be no restriction [on alternation]. Moreover, even after mantra-based placement, when joints are noticed through carelessness, wishing to correct that — when shifting of the already-placed [bricks] as in common practice might be expected — "that <s>Indra</s> indeed moved the bricks; and they were scattered" — seeing the fault [in this], for the sake of preventing [it]: joints should be avoided by those skilled in <s>Śulba</s> at the very time of <s>Śulba</s>-based placement, without disrupting the fixed locations — for this purpose is the alternation statement.
Five ... of that

children.text:
jalādrā pṛt -- purīṣam /
abhyūhanamupalepaḥ /
upadhāyāpedhāya tāṃ tāṃ citiṃ jalārdrayā mṛdopalimpet /
dvābhyāṃ vākyābhyāmekā citiḥ purīṣopadhānaparyantā jñeyā /
na kevaletyarthaḥ /
arthāntaratvāt purīṣasya, arthaḥ -- prayojanaṃ /
antarā -- bhedaḥ /
prayojanānyatvādityarthaḥ /
citīnāmanyatprayojanaṃ purīṣāṇāṃ cānyat /
citīnāṃ prayojanabhūtāt jānudaghnavadutsedhakaraṇādanyat prayojanaṃ purīṣasya /
tacceṣṭakānāṃ śoṣapākāgalahrāsapūraṇaṃ parasparasaṃ śleṣaś ca /
ata eva cāniyataparimāṇaṃ purīṣam /
naca etāvadbhiḥ purīṣairhrāsaparihāraḥ parasparasaṃśleṣaś ca bhavatīti pramāṇamasti /
tasmādaniyatapramāṇaṃ purīṣam /
ata uktaṃ purīṣāntā citiriti /
tathāca śrūyate -- "purīṣeṇābhyūhati /
tasmānmāṃsenāsthi cchannamiti' /
ayamarthaḥ -- yathā śarīrāvayavabhūtānyasthīni māṃsaiśchannānyeva śarīrakārye prabhavanti /
evamavayavabhūteṣṭakāḥ sarvataḥ purīṣaiśchannā evāgnikārye prabhavanti /
tasmādabhyūhanaparyantā citiḥ /
kiñcayadi purīṣopadānaṃ svārthaṃ tadā jānudaghnādyatiriktapramāṇatāgneḥ syāt /
ataḥ uktameva prayojanam /
anena "daśa sampadyante dvādaśa sampadyanta' iti cārthavādadarśanena citipurīṣayorminnārthatāśaṅkā mābhūditi ekārthatā pratipaditā /
children.translated_text: Wet earth — that is <s>purīṣa</s> (loose fill-earth). <s>Abhyūhana</s> (filling up) is plastering. Having placed [the bricks of] each layer, one should plaster with wet earth. By the two statements [taken together], one layer is to be understood as ending with the earth-fill application. Not [the bricks] alone — this is the meaning. "Because the earth-fill has a different purpose" — <s>artha</s> means purpose; <s>antara</s> means difference. Because the purpose is different — this is the meaning. The layers have one purpose; the earth-fills have another. The purpose of the layers is different from the purpose of the earth-fills, which is [to produce] the height as in knee-high etc. And the purpose of the earth-fill is: filling the shrinkage from drying, baking, and breakage of the bricks, and mutual adhesion. For this very reason, the earth-fill has no fixed measure. And there is no standard for [determining] that with this much earth-fill, shrinkage-avoidance and mutual adhesion will be achieved. Therefore the earth-fill has no fixed measure. Hence it is stated: "the layer ends with the earth-fill." And thus the <s>Śruti</s> says: "One fills with earth; therefore the bones are covered with flesh." The meaning is: just as the bones, being components of the body, function for the body's purpose only when covered with flesh, so too the bricks, being components [of the altar], function for the fire[-altar's] purpose only when covered on all sides with earth-fill. Therefore the layer ends with the filling. Moreover, if the earth-application were for its own sake, then the fire[-altar] would have a measure exceeding knee-high etc. Therefore, the stated purpose [alone applies]. By this, and from the observation of the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory statement) "ten are accomplished; twelve are accomplished," the suspicion that layers and earth-fills have different purposes should not arise — their single-purposefulness is demonstrated.
Knee ... [sacrificer]

children.text:
atra "jānudaghnaṃ cinvīta prathamaṃ cinvāna' ityādyā utsedhavidhāyikā stisraḥśrutayaḥ /
tathā "sahasraṃ cinvīte' tyādyā agneriṣṭakāsaṅkhyāvidhāyikāstisraḥśrutayaḥ /
jānudaghnaṃ jānupramāṇaṃ, nābhidaghnaṃ nābhipramāṇaṃ āsyadaghnamāsyapramāṇam /
sāhasraṃ sahasrasaṅkhyā parimitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Here, the three <s>śruti</s> (Vedic passages) prescribing height are: "One performing the first piling should pile it knee-deep" and so forth. Likewise, the three <s>śruti</s> passages prescribing the number of bricks of the fire-altar are: "One should pile with a thousand" and so forth. "Knee-deep" (<s>jānudaghna</s>) means having the measure of the knee; "navel-deep" (<s>nābhidaghna</s>) means having the measure of the navel; "mouth-deep" (<s>āsyadaghna</s>) means having the measure of the mouth. "Of a thousand" (<s>sāhasra</s>) means delimited by a count of one thousand.

children.text:
dviṣāhasraṃ dvābhyāṃ sahasrābhyāṃ parimitam /
triṣaśāhasraṃ tribhiḥsahasraiḥ parimitam /
utsedhavidhayaḥ tatsampādanāpekṣāḥ /
saṅkhyāvidhayaḥ tadāśrayāpekṣāḥ /
teṣāṃ yathākramaṃ naṣṭāśvadagdharathavat parasparāpekṣayā melanena paṭhitāḥ /
jyāyāṃsamutkṛṣṭairmardanādikalpaiḥ utkṛṣṭaiś ca saṃsarjanīyaiḥ; mahāntamutsedhataḥ; bṛhantaṃ parimāṇataḥ; aparimitaṃ saṅkhyāta uktaṃ /
saṃkhyādikamaparimitaṃ parimitāt parimāṇāt bhūyaḥ pramāṇe sāhasraṃ śāstraṃ pramāṇamiti kātyāyanaḥ /
svargakāmasya tu viśeṣataḥ /
akāmasya tu nitya eva /
svargakāmasye tyukteḥ agnikalpe "vājasaneyikamiti' vacanācca dviṣāhasrādīnāṃ vikalpaḥ /
grīvadaghnamiti taittirīyake śrūyate /
ubhayamapyekārthameva /
iṣṭakotsedhakaraṇāntarāvidhānāt /
"samānaṃ hiśirogrīvamiti' brāhnaṇadarśanācca /
(kiñca grīvāsyayoḥ paryāyatvadarśanācca) /
kiñca grīvāsyayoḥ paryāytvaṃ loke ca dṛśyate -- daśāsyo daśagrīva iti /
tasmācchutyorekārthatā /
children.translated_text: "Of two thousand" (<s>dviṣāhasra</s>) means delimited by two thousands. "Of three thousand" (<s>triṣāhasra</s>) means delimited by three thousands. The prescriptions regarding height depend on how that height is to be achieved. The prescriptions regarding number depend on the substrate for that number. These are recited in mutual dependence, combined in sequence, like the lost horse and burnt chariot. The greater one is described as superior through superior methods such as pressing, and through superior <s>saṃsarjanīya</s> (combining rites); great in terms of height; extensive in terms of measurement; unlimited in terms of number, it is stated. That which is unlimited in number, being greater than the delimited measurement — "the teaching of a thousand is the standard" — thus says <s>Kātyāyana</s>. But especially for one desiring heaven. For one without desire, it is always obligatory. Because of the statement "for one desiring heaven," and because of the statement in the <s>Agnikalpa</s> "according to the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>," there is an option regarding the two-thousand and so forth. "Neck-deep" (<s>grīvādaghna</s>) is heard in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>. Both mean the same thing, because no alternative method of producing the height of bricks is prescribed, and because of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> statement "for the head and neck are the same." Moreover, the synonymy of neck and mouth is also seen in common usage — "ten-mouthed" (<s>daśāsya</s>) and "ten-necked" (<s>daśagrīva</s>) [both refer to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>]. Therefore the <s>śruti</s> passages have the same meaning.
Commentary of <s>Sundararāja</s>
The alternation of the filling material (<s>purīṣa</s>)

children.text:
iṣṭakāḥsthaṇḍilārthāḥ, tatsandhānārthaṃ purīṣaṃ /
ato bhinnaprayojanatvātsakhyāntaraṃ nāvagāhate /
children.translated_text: The bricks serve the purpose of the altar platform (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), and the filling material (<s>purīṣa</s>) serves to join them together. Therefore, since they have different purposes, one number does not encroach upon the other.

children.text:
jānudaghnīṃajyāyāṃsaṃ sāhasraṃ sahasraparimāṇam /
dviṣāhasraṃ triṣāhasramiti "pūrvapadāditi' ṣatvam /
uttaramuttaraṃ caturthaprabhṛti /
children.translated_text: Knee-deep, not greater, of a thousand — meaning delimited by a thousand. "Of two thousand" and "of three thousand" — the cerebral sibilant change occurs by the rule "from the prior member." The succeeding one is progressively greater, starting from the fourth.
Here he cites the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> as authority —
"The great one is known"

children.text:
mahāntaṃ vidhābhyāsena /
aparimitaṃ bṛhantaṃ ūrvapramāṇena /
atra bodhāyanaḥ -- ūrdhvapramāṇābhyāsaṃ jānoḥ pañcamasya caturviṃśenaike samāmananti /
children.translated_text: "Great" means by repetition of the procedure. "Unlimited" and "extensive" mean by the measure of the thigh. Here <s>Baudhāyana</s> states: "Some teach the repetition of the upward measure from the knee, with twenty-four of the fifth."
Commentary of <s>Kapardi</s>

children.text: dviṣāhasre dviprastārāś citayo bhavanti | triṣāhasra triprastārāś caturthaprabhṛtiṣv āhāreṣu nityam iṣṭakāparimāṇam || ĀpŚus_10.9 ||
children.translated_text: In the two-thousand [brick altar], there are two layers of piling. In the three-thousand, three layers. From the fourth [piling] onwards, the number of bricks is always fixed. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.9]

children.text: vijñāyate ca ḥna jyāyāṃsaṃ citvā kanīyāṃsaṃ cinvīteti' || ĀpŚus_10.10 ||
children.translated_text: And it is known: "Having piled the greater, one should not pile the lesser." [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 10.10]

children.text:
nigadavyākhyātametat /
caturthoti -- iṣṭakāparimāṇamiha triṣāhasramityucyate /
triṣāhasrameva niyataṃ /
nocyeta anīkavadāvṛttiḥsyāt /
anyasyāvidhānāt /
amumevārthaṃ darśayituṃ śrutiṃ darśayati -- vijñāyata iti /
jyāyāṃsaṃ -- dviṣāhasraṃ triṣāhasraṃ vā citvā kanīyāṃsaṃ -- sāhasraṃ na cinuyāditi pratiṣedhaḥ /
tathār'dhāṣṭamamardhanavamaṃ vā citvā ekavidhāptārghavidhaparyantā na cetavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: This is explained by the <s>nigada</s> (explanatory statement). "From the fourth" — here the number of bricks is said to be three thousand. Three thousand alone is fixed. If this were not stated, there would be repetition as in the case of the <s>anīka</s> (front portion), since no other is prescribed. To demonstrate this very meaning, he cites the <s>śruti</s> — "it is known." "Greater" — having piled the two-thousand or three-thousand, "lesser" — one should not pile the one-thousand: this is the prohibition. Similarly, having piled the eight-and-a-half or the nine-fold pressing, those from the single-fold to the six-fold should not be piled.
Thus in the commentary-exposition on the <s>Āpastamba</s> Sūtra, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> of <s>Kapardisvāmin</s>,
the third <s>paṭala</s> (chapter) of the section called <s>Śulba</s>.
Commentary of <s>Karavinda</s>
He states that excess in height does not occur when there is more than one layer —
"In the two-thousand, the layers"

children.text:
dviṣāhasre 'gnau dviprastārāḥ tūṣṇīṃ purīṣābhyūhanam /
" tāsu purīṣamabhyūhatīti 'gapḷ nākṣa anye ca citidharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the two-thousand fire-altar there are two layers; the filling material (<s>purīṣa</s>) is heaped up silently. "She heaps the filling material upon those" — and the other rules pertaining to the piling also apply.
"From the fourth, the measure"

children.text:
āhareṣu -- prayogeṣu /
caturthapabrabhṛtiṣu prayogeṣvanantaroktaṃ triṣāhasraṃ nityaṃ; na nyūnādikamityarthaḥ /
nanvanantarārthādeva triṣāhasraṃ caturthaprabhṛtiṣu nityaṃ bhaviṣyati kimarthamidamucyate? ucyateyadītaṃ nocyate, tarhi anīkavadāvṛttiḥ prasajyeta /
yadvā dvitīyatṛtīyanimittā vivṛddhiriti caturthādiṣu sāhasrameva vā prasajyet /
ata idamucyate -- "nityamiṣṭakāparimāṇamiti' /
amumevārthaṃ śrutyā prathayati --
children.translated_text: "In the pilings" means in the performances. In the performances from the fourth onwards, the three-thousand mentioned just before is constant; the meaning is: not less nor more. Objection: from the immediately preceding statement itself, the three-thousand will be constant from the fourth onwards — so what is the purpose of stating this? Reply: if this were not stated, then repetition as in the case of the <s>anīka</s> would follow. Or alternatively, the increase occasioned by the second and third might lead to the one-thousand alone being applicable from the fourth onwards. Therefore this is stated — "the number of bricks is always fixed." He confirms this very meaning with a <s>śruti</s> passage —
"It is known"
"Greater" means of superior measure; "lesser" means of inferior measure.

children.text: dviṣāhasraṃ triṣāhasraṃ vā kṛtvā na sāhasraṃ cinvīta /
children.translated_text: Having performed the two-thousand or three-thousand, one should not pile the one-thousand.
There one should pile only the three-thousand.
Here are the verses —
That which is stated in the sūtra, "having placed a <s>prādeśa</s> (span-measure) at the tail" —
that is for the purpose of non-division, prohibiting a separate course at the tip of the tail.

children.text: agrasya rītibhede syurbahvayaḥ pucche bhidā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: If the course of the front part were different, there would be many divisions in the tail, because
therefore the commencement is not from the tail, but begins from the tip of the tail.
Similarly, in the placing, the area that exceeds at the base of that —
one should cover it with four half-bricks together with the <s>prādeśa</s> (span-measure).
In the case of decrease, the statement of the reverse becomes meaningful in this way:
the <s>prādeśa</s>-measure ones should not be at the front, since that would cause many divisions.

children.text: chādane viniyuktānāṃ sāmarthyeṃ nāsti yatra tu /
children.translated_text: Where the bricks employed in covering do not have the capacity —
there the covering should be done with other capable bricks and those belonging to that place.
Since the statement "one should cover" applies to all fire-altars,
therefore the fifth-part bricks are occasioned by the abundance of hand-measures.
The repetition of the alternation of placement and of the statement regarding alternation,
in each respective case, has the single reason of absence of division.
Since the alternation is established from common practice, and he makes effort regarding that,
thereby it is understood that even the non-division of bricks is not to be disregarded.
Since here, having merely restated the number, he prescribes the completion,
therefore we consider that the equality pertains to all layers.
When deficient, one should complete with the prescribed [bricks], since equality has its basis in the established position;
in case of excess, since there is no sequence, the layers are equal in all respects.
Thus the third <s>paṭala</s> (chapter) in the <s>Śulbadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Karavindasvāmin</s>.
Commentary of <s>Sundararāja</s>
"In the two-thousand, three layers"

children.text:
pratiprastāraṃ saṃdhānārtaṃ purīṣaṃ bhavati /
cityante mantrataḥ /
children.translated_text: For each layer, filling material (<s>purīṣa</s>) is used for joining. They are piled with mantras.
"From the fourth, the measure"
The succeeding one is always three-thousand only —
"It is known: one should pile"

children.text:
sarevatrāgniṣu dakṣiṇottare pārśve sadṛśe evopadheye /
tathā pāśvātyapaurastye /
yadevamāha -- "adyardhā daśa purastāddaśa paścāt aṣṭāvaṣṭau pādeṣṭakāḥ pakṣāgrayosvatasraśvalatasraḥ pakṣāgrīyāḥ, ityādi /
tadāha bodhāyanaḥ -- "paśudharmā ha vā agniryathā vai paśordakṣiṇeṣamasthnaṃ yaddakṣiṇaṃ taduttareṣāmuttaram, ityādi /
etacca sati saṃbhave; yadāha -- "dvitīyacaturthayosvānyatarataḥ pratisaṃhitāmekaikāṃ triṃśatṣaṣṭayaḥ, ekaṃ pañcamīm' iti ca /
dviśatā eva sarve prastārāḥ. pratiprastāraṃ saṃkhyāpūraṇavacanāt rathacakre dviśatayoreva prastārayorvacanāt eṣa dviśataḥ prastāra iti śyenaciti vacanācca /
children.translated_text: All the layers consist of two hundred each. Because the statement about completing the number is for each layer, because in the chariot-wheel [altar] the statement is for layers of two hundred each, and because in the <s>Śyenaciti</s> (hawk-shaped altar) it is stated "this is a layer of two hundred."
Therefore the <s>coḍā</s> (crest bricks) and <s>nākasad</s> (heaven-seated bricks) should be counted as one unit together.
<s>Baudhāyana</s> however states: "In the fifth piling, the completion of the number — the layers are of two hundred each.
With the five crest-bricks, the <s>nākasad</s> (heaven-seated bricks) should be understood as having the same number."

In all fire-altars, the southern and northern sides should be placed symmetrically. Likewise the western and eastern sides. As he states: "eleven and a half in front, ten behind, eight and eight <s>pādeṣṭakā</s> (quarter-bricks), four and four at the wing-tips, <s>pakṣāgrīya</s> (wing-tip bricks)," and so forth. Thus <s>Baudhāyana</s> states: "The fire-altar has the nature of an animal; just as for an animal, what is on the right side is the same bone as what is on the left — what is right is also left," and so forth. And this applies when possible; as he states: "In the second and fourth [layers], from either side, each one fitted together, thirty and sixty, one fifth."
Tenth section.
Thus in the commentary on the <s>Āpastamba</s> Śulbasūtra by <s>Sundararāja</s>,
the third <s>paṭala</s> (chapter) in the <s>Śulbapradīpa</s> ("Light on the Śulba").
Commentary of <s>Kapardi</s>
Now the fourth <s>paṭala</s> (chapter).

children.text: caturaśrābhir agniṃ cinuta iti vijñāyata | samacaturaśrā anupapadatvāc chabdasya || ĀpŚus_11.1 ||
children.translated_text: "Build the fire-altar with square [bricks]" — thus it is known. They are equilateral squares, since the word [<s>caturaśra</s>] would be inapplicable otherwise. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.1]

children.text:
asyāḥśrulerarthastarkyate -- kiṃ samānānāṃ caturaśrāṇāṃ cāviśeṣagrahaṇaṃ āhosvit samānāmāmeveti? kutaḥ? viśeṣāgrahaṇāt /
na kaśvidviśeṣaḥ śrūyate /
tasmādaviśeṣeṇeti prāpte ucyate -- samacaturaśrā eva grāhyāḥ /
kutaḥ anupapadatvācchabdasya /
yatropapadaṃ na śrūyate dīrgho viṣama iti vā tatra samacaturaśrāṇāmeva mukhyatvāt mukhyerthe prathamaṃ pratyayo bhavati; yataḥ pratīyate tasyārtho bhavati /
itaratra gauṇaḥ /
tasmātsapacaturaśrābhirevopā dhātavyaḥ /
nādhyardhābhiriti sthitam /
children.translated_text: This has already been explained. The word <s>caturaśra</s> (four-cornered) denotes a square, since if it were merely four-sided, the term would be superfluous. Therefore, "square" (<s>samacaturaśra</s>) is the established meaning.

children.text: pādamātrayo bhavanti aratnimātrayo bhavanty ūrvasthimātrayo bhavanty aṇūkamātrayo bhavantīti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_11.2 ||
children.translated_text: "They are of the measure of a foot (<s>pāda</s>); they are of the measure of a cubit (<s>aratni</s>); they are of the measure of a thigh-bone (<s>ūrvasthi</s>); they are of the measure of a small unit (<s>aṇūka</s>)" — thus it is known. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.2]
These are four <s>śruti</s> passages. He explains them in this very manner —
The <s>aṇūka</s> (small brick) is a fourth-part. The <s>aratni</s> (cubit-brick) is a fifth-part. Likewise the thigh-bone [brick]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.3a]

children.text:
aṇūkaśabdaḥ puruṣacaturthasya vācasaḥ /
aratniḥ pañcamasya /
tathā -- tenaiva prakāreṇa ūrvasthi ṣaṣṭhasya /
ṣaḍbhāgīyā iti śulbāntare /
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>aṇūka</s> is one-fourth of the standard measure, the <s>aratni</s> is one-fifth, and so also is the <s>ūrvasthi</s> (thigh-bone measure). These fractional measures determine the brick sizes used in the fire-altar construction.
The <s>pādeṣṭakā</s> (quarter-brick) is of the measure of a <s>pāda</s> (foot). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.3b]
In that regard, one may choose as desired, since the meaning of the word has a [broad] scope. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.4]

children.text:
caturbhāgīyaḥ pāda iti saṃjñā vihitā śāstrāntare /
pāda śabdena pramāṇacaturbhāgo gṛhyate kṣetracaturbhāgaś ca /
pādaḥ pramāṇamasyāḥ pādamātrī /
pādaśabdasya saṃbandhaśabdatvāt puruṣacaturbhāgo 'pi gṛhyate aṇūkādicaturbhāgaś ca sannihitatvāt /
teṣāṃ pādeṣṭakābhirityukte puruṣacaturbhāgā aṇūkādicaturbhāgāś ca pratīyante /
kutaḥ? śabdārthasya viṣa(śa)yitvāta /
vakṣyati ca -- aṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna iti /
saṅkhyāpūraṇe 'ṇūkānāṃ praveśaṃ darśayati /
ūrvasthayaratnayoḥ ekārthatvaṃ kecidicchanti /
te pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiḥsaṅkhyāpūraṇaṃ kurvate /
teṣāṃ darśane prastārā na yujyante /
sahasrasaṅkhyā tu pūryate pratiprastāramiti vacanamanarthakamāpadyeta /
ye prastārā te dviśatā iti vajanāni na yujyante /
tasmātpūrvokta evārtho grahyaḥ /
sarvavacanānāmarthavacvāya /
children.translated_text: Here the term <s>yathākāmī</s> (as one desires) indicates that within the prescribed measures, there is latitude in selecting which brick size to employ, since the word encompasses all the specified measures within its scope.
Commentary of <s>Karavinda</s>
Now the fourth <s>paṭala</s> (chapter).
"With square [bricks] — it is known"

children.text:
catuṣkoṇābiriṣṭakābhiragniṃ cinute /
kīdṛśyo grāhyā ityata āha --
children.translated_text: This passage establishes through <s>śruti</s> authority that the fire-altar should be constructed with square bricks.
"Equal — of the word"

children.text:
tā iṣṭakā adīrghaviṣamāḥ samacaturaśrā grahyāḥ /
kutaḥ? anupapadatvācchabdasya /
na hyatropapadaṃ śrūyate dīrghābhiriṣṭakābirviṣamābhirveti /
ataḥ "samaṃ syādaśrutatvāditi' nyāyena samā eva syuḥ /
pūrvasminnagnau dīrghāś ca santi /
ato vidhibhedādvā vikalpaḥ pūrveṇāgninā /
nityaśvākāmaśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: The word <s>caturaśra</s> specifically means equilateral square (<s>samacaturaśra</s>), since the term would be inapplicable to a mere quadrilateral. The equal-sidedness is an essential characteristic denoted by the word.

children.text:
agnikalpasyaiva śravaṇaṃ pradarśanārtam /
āsāṃ śrutyaiva darśayannāha --
children.translated_text: The citation from the <s>Agnikalpa</s> itself is for the purpose of demonstration. Showing the <s>śruti</s> authority for these [brick types], he says —
"Of the foot-measure — it is known"

children.text:
etāśratasraḥśrutayaḥ iṣṭakānāṃ pramāṇaṃ vidavati /
sambhavācca tāsāṃ samuccayaḥ /
pādamātrayaḥ -- pāda pramāṇāḥ /
pādaśabdasvaraṇacaturthabhāgādau vartate /
iha caturmāgavācī /
sa caturbhāgo 'ṇūkādīnāṃ grāhya ityuttarasūtre pratipādayiṣyate /
pādapraṇāṇāḥ pādamātrayaḥ /
aratniḥ sakaniṣṭhikaḥ karaḥ /
sa ca puruṣasya pañcamabāgaḥ /
vakṣyati ca pañcāratniḥ puruvaḥ caturviṃśatyaṅgulayoratniriti /
tatpramāṇā aratnimātrayaḥ /
urvasthi -- ūrvorasthi /
aṇūkaṃ pṛṣṭhavaṃśaḥ /
tā ūrvasthijānvāsthināmptayornāṇūkasyetyatra vyākhyānāt /
puruṣasyaḥ ṣṭho bhāga -- urvasthi /
caturtho bhāgo 'ṇūkaḥ /
etacca uttarasūtre spaṣṭaṃ vakṣyati /
tatpramāṇā ūrvasthimātrayaḥ /
aṇūkāmātrayaś ca /
children.translated_text: These four Vedic texts prescribe the measure of the bricks. And since they are compatible, they are to be taken together. '<s>Pādamātrī</s>' — of <s>pāda</s> (quarter) measure. The word '<s>pāda</s>' is used in the sense of a fourth part, etc. Here it denotes a fourth. That fourth part is to be taken of the <s>aṇūka</s> (spine-bone) and the others — this will be explained in the next <s>sūtra</s>. Those of <s>pāda</s> measure are the <s>pādamātrīs</s>. The <s>aratni</s> (cubit) is the forearm with the little finger [extended]. And that is a fifth part of a <s>puruṣa</s>. He will say: 'Five <s>aratnis</s> make a <s>puruṣa</s>; twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> make an <s>aratni</s>.' Those of that measure are the <s>aratnimātrīs</s>. '<s>Ūrvasthi</s>' — the thigh-bone. '<s>Aṇūka</s>' is the spinal column. These [terms] are explained from the commentary on 'of the thigh-bone, the knee-bone, and the <s>aṇūka</s>.' A sixth part of a <s>puruṣa</s> is the <s>ūrvasthi</s>. A fourth part is the <s>aṇūka</s>. This will be clearly stated in the next <s>sūtra</s>. Those of that measure are the <s>ūrvasthimātrīs</s>. And the <s>aṇūkamātrīs</s>.
To prescribe the specific designations according to the dimensions of each, he says —
The fourth... the three...

children.text:
aṇūkāratnayūrvasthiśabdaiḥ tanmātraya iṣṭakā gṛhyante /
upasaṃhāre pādamātrīṣṭaketi darśanāt /
saṃjñāsu strīlihganirddeśācca /
kiñcāṇūkādiśabdairapīṣṭakānāṃ vyavahārā dṛśyante /
"aṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāne sandhyantarāle pañcamabāgīyāḥsapādāḥtā ātmani caturdaśabhiḥ pādairyathāyogaṃ paryupadadhyāt' ityādiṣu aṇūkamātrī caturbhāgīyā tatsaṃjñā bhavatītyarthaḥ /
pañcamabhāgīyārātniḥ -- aratnimātrī pañcamabhāgīyākhyā /
tathorvasthi -- urvasthimātrī ṣaḍbāgīyākhyā /
pādeṣṭakā -- pādamātrī /
nanu kathametallabhyate ṣaḍbhāgīyorvasthīti? tatheti prakārātideśāt /
kathamatideśaḥ? yathāratnimātrīsaṅkhyā sannikarṣeṇa svapūrvoktāratnimātrīpramā(ṇe)ṇānyūnānantaraparimāṇavacana saṃjñā syāditi tathorvasthimā6yapi saṃkhyā tatsannikarṣeṇa svapūrvoktāratnimātrī pramāṇānyūnānantaraparimāṇavacanasaṃjñā syāditi /
kiñca ṣaḍbāgīyorvasthīti vaktavya tathetyayamatideśaḥ prakṛtapuruṣāvayavapramāṇaprakārasamāptisūcanārthaḥ /
tenorvasthayantānāmevāvayavapramāṇaparimāṇatvaṃ na pādamātrīṇāmiti jñāyate /
ataḥsvavākyasannihitatvāt "upadhāne 'ṣṭāvaṣṭau pādeṣṭakāḥ caturbhāgīyānāṃ pakṣāgrayornidadhyāt /
sandhyantarāle pañcamabhāgīyāḥsapādāḥtā ātmani caturdaśabhiḥ pādairyathāyogaṃ paryupadadhyāt' iti darśanācca /
aṇūkārdānāṃ pādā iha pādatvena gṛhyante na caraṇādayaḥ /
kiñcaśvutidṛṣṭamapahāyāṇūkādīnāṃ vyutkrameṇa pāṭhapaurvāparye pūrvasya pramāṇādhikyajñāpanārthaḥ /
tenorvasthipramāṇānāmaratnimātrībhyo nyūnapramāṇatvaṃ pādamātrīṇāmaṇūkāratnacūrvāsthimātrībhyo nyūnapramāṇatvaṃ ca jñāpitaṃ bhavati /
etacca sarvamuktaṃ bhagavatā bodhāyanena "samacaturaśrābhiragniṃ' cinuta "ityupakramya tasyeṣṭakāḥ kārayet /
puruṣasya caturthena pañcamenaḥ ṣṭhena daśemana ca' itivadatā /
ato 'ṇūkādipādā iha pādatvena gṛhyante /
te ca teṣāmardhena grāhyāḥ /
ardhapramāṇena pādapramāṇaṃ vidhīyata iti nyāyāt /
ataḥ pañcadaśāṅgulāṇūkapādāḥ dvādaśāṅgulāratnipādāḥ daśāṅgulā ūrvāsthipādāḥ /
teneha ṣaḍvidhā iṣṭakāḥ /
tādṛśaiḥ karaṇaiḥ kāryāḥ /
nanvaṇūkādiśabdairāsāṃ parimāṇajñāne vyavahāre ca siddhe kimarthaṃ mahatyaḥ saṃjñāḥ kriyante? ucyate -- śrautanāmaṇūkādiśabdānāṃ pūruṣacaturbhāgādimātraparimāṇaparatvajñāpanena tasya tasya puruṣasya caturbhāgādiparimāṇairiṣṭakānirmāṇārtham /
tathāhi -- loke dvividhāḥ puruṣāḥ samāś ca viṣamāś ca /
tatra samāḥsāmudrīyāśeṣalakṣaṇopetāḥ /
katipayairvihīnā viṣamāḥ /
samāḥsāmudrīyāśeṣalakṣaṇopetāḥ /
katipayairvihīnā viṣamāḥ /
samānāmaṇūkādayaḥ /
tadapekṣayā niyataparimāṇatvānmukhyatayā gṛhītāḥ /
itareṣāṃ tu garbhādhānādikālastitaprākṛtādṛṣṭādivaśena nyūnādhikavakrādyaneka rūpāṅgatayāṇūkādiṣu caturbhāgādiniyamavyabhicārāttatpramāṇairutpāditānāmiṣṭakānāṃ upadhānakāle tatsaṃkhyākānāṃ tāsāṃ tatra tatropadhāne tābhistābhistaddeśapūraṇaṃ nyūnābhirvā pūraṇam /
bhinnajātīyānāṃ tatratyānāṃ tatra tatra saṅghaṭṭanamityevamādayo mahānto doṣāstatra sambhīvaṣyantīti /
ataḥśrutigatāṇūkādiśabdaistadvaiṣamyaparihārāya puruṣacaturmāgādayo lakṣyanta ityasyārthasya pratipādanāyānvarthā mahatyaḥsaṃjñāḥ kiyante /
tenāyamarthaḥsaṃpadyate -- ūrdhvabāhoḥ puruṣasya pramāṇaṃ gṛhītvātsya caturthena pañcamenaḥ ṣṭhena vā teṣāṃ ardheṣṭakāḥ kārayediti /
atra kecidvarvaśthyaratvayorekārthatāmicchīnta /
teṣāṃ mate 'gnikalpe tathorvasti śabdasyāratniśabdasya vā pṛthagupādānaṃ punarupādānaṃ śrutidarśanaṃ ca sūtrakārasya pramādakṛtamevāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: By the words <s>aṇūka</s>, <s>aratni</s>, and <s>ūrvasthi</s>, bricks of those measures are understood. This is because in the conclusion, the expression '<s>pādamātrī</s> brick' is found. And from the use of feminine gender in the designations. Moreover, usages of the words <s>aṇūka</s> etc. for bricks are observed. '<s>Aṇūkas</s> in the place of the fifteenth-part [bricks]; at the junctions, fifth-part [bricks] with a quarter — those, in the body, one should place with fourteen quarters as appropriate' — in such passages, <s>aṇūkamātrī</s>, the fourth-part [brick], has that designation; the meaning is [thus]. 'Fifth-part-<s>aratni</s>' — the <s>aratnimātrī</s> is called the fifth-part. Likewise '<s>ūrvasthi</s>' — the <s>ūrvasthimātrī</s> is called the sixth-part. '<s>Pādeṣṭakā</s>' — the <s>pādamātrī</s>. Now, how is it obtained that the <s>ūrvasthi</s> is a sixth-part? By the word 'tathā' (likewise), which transfers the method. How is the transfer? Just as the <s>aratnimātrī</s> count, by proximity, takes as its designation the word for the next smaller measure after its own previously-stated <s>aratnimātrī</s> measure; so too the <s>ūrvasthimātrī</s> count, by that proximity, takes as its designation the word for the next smaller measure after its own previously-stated <s>aratnimātrī</s> measure. Furthermore, one should say 'sixth-part <s>ūrvasthi</s>'; the word 'tathā' (likewise) is this transfer, [and] its purpose is to indicate the completion of the body-part-measure-dimension [series] of the <s>puruṣa</s>. By that, it is understood that only those ending in <s>ūrvasthi</s> are body-part-measure dimensions, not the <s>pādamātrīs</s>. Therefore, from proximity to its own sentence: 'At the time of laying, eight by eight <s>pāda</s>-bricks of the fourth-part [type], at the wing-tips one should place; at the junctions, fifth-part [bricks] with a quarter — those, in the body, one should place with fourteen quarters as appropriate' — and from this being observed. The <s>pādas</s> (quarters) of the <s>aṇūkas</s> and others are here understood as 'quarters,' not as feet etc. Furthermore, having set aside the Vedic text-observed [principle], the reverse ordering of <s>aṇūka</s> etc. is for the purpose of indicating that the preceding [term] has a greater measure. By that, it is indicated that the <s>ūrvasthi</s>-measure bricks are smaller than the <s>aratnimātrīs</s>, and the <s>pādamātrīs</s> are smaller than the <s>aṇūka</s>-, <s>aratni</s>-, and <s>ūrvasthi</s>-measure bricks. All of this has been stated by the revered <s>Bodhāyana</s>, who, beginning with 'one piles the fire with square [bricks],' and saying 'one should have the bricks made: by the fourth, fifth, sixth, and tenth of a <s>puruṣa</s>.' Therefore the <s>pādas</s> of <s>aṇūka</s> etc. are here understood as quarters. And those are to be taken as half of them. Because the <s>pāda</s> measure is prescribed as half the [full] measure — by this principle. Therefore: <s>aṇūka-pādas</s> are fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>; <s>aratni-pādas</s> are twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>; <s>ūrvasthi-pādas</s> are ten <s>aṅgulas</s>. Thus here there are six types of bricks. They are to be made with such moulds. Now, since the dimensions and usage of these are already established by the words <s>aṇūka</s> etc., why are elaborate designations created? It is said: By the understanding that the Vedic terms <s>aṇūka</s> etc. refer to fourth-part and other measures of a <s>puruṣa</s>, the bricks are to be manufactured according to the fourth-part etc. dimensions of each particular <s>puruṣa</s>. For indeed, in the world, <s>puruṣas</s> (men) are of two kinds: proportionate and disproportionate. Among them, the proportionate ones are those possessing all the characteristics of <s>sāmudrīya</s> (physiognomic science). The disproportionate lack some of those. For the proportionate, the <s>aṇūka</s> etc. [are defined]. In relation to those, since [the body parts] have fixed proportions, they are taken primarily. But for the others, due to variation in proportions of their <s>aṇūka</s> etc. body parts — caused by unseen [karmic] forces and other factors from the time of conception — with limbs of many forms including shorter, longer, crooked, etc., resulting in deviation from the fourth-part etc. rule in the <s>aṇūka</s> etc., the bricks produced by their measures, at the time of laying, when those bricks of those counts are placed here and there, by those bricks the filling of those places [would be] inadequate with fewer, and there would be collision of bricks of different types in those places — such great defects would arise there. Therefore, to avoid such unevenness, the Vedic terms <s>aṇūka</s> etc. are taken to indicate the fourth part etc. of a <s>puruṣa</s> — for establishing this meaning, the elaborate meaningful designations are created. By this, the meaning is achieved: having taken the measure of a <s>puruṣa</s> with arms raised, one should have bricks made by its fourth, fifth, sixth [parts], and by half of those. Here, some wish to equate <s>ūrvasthi</s> and <s>aratni</s>. In their view, the separate mention of the word '<s>ūrvasthi</s>' or '<s>aratni</s>' and [its] repeated mention in the fire-ritual procedure, and its appearance in the Vedic text, would be due merely to the carelessness of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author).
There, since it is so...

children.text:
gataṃ /
ayamarthaḥ -- caturbhāgādayaḥ puruṣacaturbhāgaparimitāḥ syuḥ /
puruṣakalpanānurūpāḥ syuriti caturbhāgīyāstriṃśadaṅgulāḥ pañcabhāgīyāścaturviṃśatyaṅgulāḥ ṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ viṃśatyaṅgulāḥ /
tāsāṃ pādāstadarthamitāḥ pañcadaśadvādaśāṅgulāś ceti /
children.translated_text: This has been covered. The meaning is: the fourth-part etc. should be of the measure of the fourth part etc. of a <s>puruṣa</s>. According to the <s>puruṣa</s> convention: the fourth-part [bricks] are thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>; the fifth-part [bricks] are twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; the sixth-part [bricks] are twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Their quarters — measured for that purpose — are fifteen and twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Now the fourth <s>paṭala</s> (chapter).
Now he states the piling of this same square [altar] by another method —
'With square [bricks]' — the word 'tu'
is inapplicable due to [the absence of] qualifiers such as 'oblong' etc.
'<s>Pādamātrīs</s> are known' —
He states the measure of these <s>pādas</s> and the rest —
'Fourth-part is <s>aṇūka</s>' —
A fourth-part of a <s>puruṣa</s>, thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>, is called an <s>aṇūkamātrī</s>.
'Fifth-part is <s>aratni</s>' —
Twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
'Likewise <s>ūrvasthi</s>' —

children.text:
tathā tenaiva mārgeṇorvasthi jñātavyaṃ, tacca ṣaḍhbhāgīyaṃ viṃśatyaṅgulam /
kecidūrvasthītyapi pañcamabhāgīyāmevāhuḥ, tadayuktam /
"kulmimātro 'ratniprādeśa ūrvasthīti' bhedena nirdeśāt /
"iṣṭakāḥ karoti prādeśamātrayo 'ratnimātraya ūrvasthimātra' iti prayogakalpe pṛthagvacanāt tadūrvasthītyādivacanācca /
vyaktoktatvācca bodhāyanena -- "tasyeṣṭakāḥ kārayet puruṣasya caturthena pañcamena ṣaṣṭhena daśamena' iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the same method, <s>ūrvasthi</s> is to be understood; and that is a sixth-part, twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Some say that '<s>ūrvasthi</s>' too is only a fifth-part — that is incorrect. From the separate mention: 'a <s>kulmi</s>-measure of <s>aratni-prādeśa</s> is <s>ūrvasthi</s>' as a distinct [category]. From the separate statement in the <s>prayogakalpa</s> (ritual manual): 'one makes bricks of <s>prādeśa</s>-measure, <s>aratni</s>-measure, <s>ūrvasthi</s>-measure.' And from the word '<s>ūrvasthi</s>' etc. being stated separately. And because <s>Bodhāyana</s> has clearly stated: 'One should have its bricks made: by the fourth, fifth, sixth, and tenth of a <s>puruṣa</s>.'
'<s>Pādeṣṭakā</s>' — the <s>pādamātrī</s> [brick].
Since the word '<s>pāda</s>' is unspecified, it applies to [the quarters of] <s>aṇūka</s> etc. and of all [brick types].
There, since the meaning of the word is indiscriminate —

children.text:
loke pādaśabdaścaturbhāgavacanaḥ prasiddhaḥ /
vkacidekadeśamātre /
"kṛcch pādaḥ prakīrtita' iti "ṛcaṃ pādagrahaṇa' iti ṛkṣu ca /
vede tvekadeśamātre dṛśyate -- "tripadā gāyatrī pañcapadā pāṅktirḥ ,capapadā śavkarī' iti /
iha tadubhayaṃ grāhyaṃ /
śabdārthasyobhayatra vṛtteḥ /
atra ca pādaśabdārthanirūpaṇaṃ kriyate ekavidhādyartham /
asmiṃ stvagnau caturbhāgavacane 'pi pāde na kaśviddoṣaḥ /
ye tu ṣaḍbhāgīyānnecchanti teṣāmevopayogaḥ, aṇūkāratnipādatvena daśāṅgulāṣṭāṅgulānāṃ grāhyatvāt /
children.translated_text: In common usage, the word '<s>pāda</s>' is well-known as meaning a fourth part. Sometimes [it means] a mere portion. 'A <s>kṛcch</s> [penance is called] a <s>pāda</s>' and 'the taking of a <s>pāda</s> of a <s>ṛc</s> (verse)' — thus in the <s>ṛc</s>-verses. In the Veda, however, it is seen in the sense of a mere portion: 'Three-footed is <s>Gāyatrī</s>, five-footed is <s>Paṅkti</s>, six-footed is <s>Śaṅkarī</s>.' Here, both meanings are to be taken. Because the meaning of the word operates in both contexts. And here the determination of the meaning of the word '<s>pāda</s>' is made for the purpose of [understanding] the one-fold [altar] and others. In this fire-altar, even though '<s>pāda</s>' means a fourth part, there is no defect. Those who do not accept the sixth-part [bricks] — for them only is there utility, since ten-<s>aṅgula</s> and eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] are to be taken as the <s>pādas</s> of <s>aṇūka</s> and <s>aratni</s>.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: upadhāne 'ṣṭāvaṣṭau pādeṣṭakāś caturbhāgīyānāṃ pakṣāgrayor nidadhyāt | sandhyoś ca tadvad ātmānaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulāpetāḥ || ĀpŚus_11.5a ||
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, eight by eight <s>pāda</s>-bricks of the fourth-part [type] one should place at the wing-tips. At the junctions too, likewise — [those bricks], reduced by six <s>aṅgulas</s> from the body [measurement]. || ĀpŚus 11.5a ||

children.text:
upadhānakāle aṣṭāvaṣṭau caturbhāgīyānāṃ pādeṣṭakāḥ pakṣāgrayorūpadadhāyāt /
aṣṭāvaṣṭāviti viśayāḥ /
atmānaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulamātramavetāḥ avagatā vyāptā iti yāvata /
navāṅgulamātraṃ pakṣayoḥ /
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, one should place eight by eight <s>pāda</s>-bricks of the fourth-part [type] at the wing-tips. 'Eight by eight' means sixteen. 'Reduced from the body by six <s>aṅgulas</s>' — [meaning] they span, they pervade, that extent. Of nine <s>aṅgula</s> measure in the wings.

children.text: śroṇyaṃseṣu cāṣṭau prācīḥ pratīciś ca || ĀpŚus_11.5b ||
children.translated_text: And at the haunches and shoulders, eight [each] — eastward and westward. || ĀpŚus 11.5b ||

children.text:
śroṇyaṃsayosvatasraścatasraḥ /
tāḥ pādāḥ /
pracīḥśroṇyoḥ /
aṃsayoḥ ptīcīḥ /
evaṃ caturbhāgīyapādā aṣṭācatvāriṃśat /
children.translated_text: At the haunches and shoulders, four each [at each corner]. Those are <s>pādas</s> (quarter-bricks). Eastward at the haunches. Westward at the shoulders. Thus, the fourth-part <s>pādas</s> total forty-eight.
At the junction-intervals, fifth-part [bricks] with a quarter. || ĀpŚus 11.6 ||

children.text:
pakṣasandhyorantarāle pañcamabhāgīyāḥ pādasahitāḥ /
madhye pādāḥ /
daśa pratīciḥ /
tāsāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ paṭhcaviṃśatiḥ pañcamabhāgīyāḥ /
uttarato viṃśatiḥ /
