children.translated_text: At the intervals of the wing-junctions, fifth-part [bricks] with a <s>pāda</s> (quarter) added. In the middle, <s>pādas</s>. Ten westward. To the south of those, twenty-five fifth-part [bricks]. To the north, twenty.
Thus, at the junction-intervals, fifty-five bricks are to be laid.

children.text: pucche prādeśamupadhāya sarvam agniṃ caturbhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet || ĀpŚus_11.7 ||
children.translated_text: Having laid a <s>prādeśa</s> (span) [area] in the tail, one should cover the entire fire [altar] with fourth-part [bricks]. || ĀpŚus 11.7 ||

children.text:
prādeśaśabdena kiṃ kṣetramabhidhīyate? pucche yatprādeśamiti? athavā iṣṭakāḥ prādeśena kāritāḥ? yadi kṣetramabhidhīyeta prādeśapaṅktirevopadhātavyā syāt /
tathā sati bhidyetāgniḥ /
itarasminpakṣe yathā na bhidyate tathā prādeśeṣṭakā bhaveyuḥ /
prādeśamiti jātāvekavacanam /
prādeśeṣṭakābhiḥsahāṇūkā na śerate /
śerate tu pañcabhāgīyāstābhiḥsaha /
ataścatasraścatasraḥ śroṇyoḥ pādeṣṭakāstrayodaśa pañcamabhāgīyāḥ /
pūrvārdhe 'ṣṭāvaṇūkāḥ /
evamekonatriṃśatpucche /
apare punarevaṃ varṇayanti -- yasya vitastayā vardhanaṃ kṛtaṃ tatrāpi caturaśraśrutisāmarthyāt prādeśa eveṣṭakābhirvyāpyata iti /
evamarthaṃ prādeśagrahaṇamiti /

children.translated_text: In that view too, the stated order of laying applies.
'The entire' — means thirty-two.
Twenty-eight are stated for the body.
Eight in the front half of the tail.

What does the word '<s>prādeśa</s>' refer to — a field (area)? That which is '<s>prādeśa</s>' in the tail? Or bricks made by a <s>prādeśa</s>? If a field is meant, then only a row of <s>prādeśa</s> [bricks] would need to be laid. In that case, the fire [altar] would be split (have gaps). In the other view, the <s>prādeśa</s>-bricks should be such that no splitting occurs. '<s>Prādeśam</s>' — the singular is used for the class. <s>Prādeśa</s>-bricks do not align with <s>aṇūkas</s>. But they do align with fifth-part [bricks], together with those. Therefore, four each at the haunches [as] <s>pāda</s>-bricks, thirteen fifth-part [bricks], eight <s>aṇūkas</s> in the front half. Thus twenty-nine in the tail. Others, however, explain thus: where the extension has been made by a <s>vitasti</s> (span), there too, by the authority of the Vedic text on 'square,' only the <s>prādeśa</s> is covered with bricks. For this purpose is the word '<s>prādeśa</s>.'
One should complete the count with <s>pāda</s>-bricks. || ĀpŚus 11.8 ||
One should complete the count with fifteenth-part [bricks].

children.text: ātmani dvitīyāyāṃ rītyāṃ madhyamāṃ caturbhāgīyāṃ madhyame dviśataḥ prastāraḥ //
children.translated_text: In the body, in the second <s>rīti</s> (course/row), the middle [brick is] a fourth-part one; in the middle, two layers each.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
One should lay —

children.text:
upadhānakāle pañcadaśāṅgulā aṣṭāvaṣṭau pakṣāgrayornidadhyāt /
pakṣātmasandhayoś ca tadvadātmani ṣaḍaṅgulāvetāḥ /
pakṣātmasandhyośvāṣṭāvaṣṭau /
tāḥṣaḍaṅgulāḥśyenātmani praviṣṭāḥśroṇyaṃseṣu ca /
cakāreṇa tadvadityākṛṣya sāmarthyādviśayābhāvaḥ /
śroṇyaṃseṣucatasraścatasraḥ /

śroṇyoḥ prācīḥ aṃsayoḥ pratīcīḥ /
nanu aṣṭāvaṣṭāviti vīpsayā prāptānāṃ sthānacatuṣṭayanirddeśe pratisthānamaṣṭāvaṣṭau kathaṃ na syuḥ? ucyate -- "aṣṭau prācīḥ pratisthānamaṣṭāvaṣṭau kathaṃ na syuḥ? ucyate --"aṣṭau prācīḥ praticīśveti' vacanasāmarthyāt prācīnāṃ pratīcīnāṃ cāṣṭatvamavagamyate na pratyekaṃ catasra eveti /

gatametat /

sarvathā tāvat ṣoḍaśaivopadheyāḥ /

tāsāṃ pādeṣṭakānāṃ dakṣiṇato viṃśatiḥ pañcamabhāgīyāḥ, uttarataḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ, viparītā vā //
pucchāgre yatpravṛddhaṃ prādeśakṣetraṃ tadupadadhyāt sāmarthayāddaśabhiḥ prādeśaiḥ //
tataḥ pucchasya pūrvārdhe pārśveyormadhye tisrastisraḥṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ pracīrupadadhyāt /
aparasmin prastāre pucchāpyaye pañcamabhāgīyā viśayāḥ || ĀpŚus_11.9a ||
dvitīye prastāre pucchāpyaye pucchātmasandhau viśayā ubhayasthāḥ pañcamabhāgīyā upadheyāḥ /
tā ātmani caturdaśabhiḥ pādair yathāyogaṃ paryupadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_11.9b ||

tāsāneva pādeṣṭakābhiḥ viśayāsaṃsṛṣṭābhiḥ caturdaśabhirupadadhyāt /
ātmani yathā yujyante /
iha ṣaḍbhāgīyānāṃ karaṇamuktam /
upadhānaṃ noktam yathā pūrvatrārdheṣṭakānāṃ purastāccopadheyāḥ pucchasya pūrvārdhe pārśvayostisrastisraḥ ṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ madhye catasraḥ /
śiṣṭe dvādaśa caturbhāgīyāḥ /

iha pādeṣṭakāśabdena puruṣasya pūrayitavyasya caturbhāgakārikā aṇūkā gṛhyante /
pañcamabhāgīyāś ca kṛtā upadheyā ityucyante /
dvādaśa caturbhāgīyā ātmani /
prathamā rītiḥ pañcamabhāgīyānām /
dvitīyā rītiścaturbhāgīyānām /
ṣaṣṭhī prādeśānām /
navamī caturbhāgīyānām /
śiṣṭe pañcamabhāgīyāḥ /
eṣa prastāro dviśataḥ /
atra kecana yājñikāḥ anupāśitaguravaḥ ācāryābhiprāyamajānantaḥ ūnāddūya(hya)dhikaprastāraṃ kurvanti /
asya tu sūtrakārasya pratiprastāraṃ pūrayediti vadatastadanabhipretameva /
yadyevamabhimatamabhaviṣyat sarvatra pratiprastāraṃ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayediti nāvakṣyat /
uktaṃ ca; tasmāddviśataḥ prastāraḥ
aṣṭau śroṇyaṃsayoś ca syuḥ pādāḥ sūtrakṛteritāḥ /
aṣṭau pucchasya pūrvārdhe caturthyaḥśiṣṭa eva tu /
dvitīyā navamī caiva catturthī nāma vātmani //
asyā eva sapādābhiḥ prastāro dviśataḥ kṛtaḥ //

tā viśayāścaturdaśabhiḥ pādaiḥ prakṛtatvāt pañcamabhāgīyānāṃ yathā yogaṃ paritaḥsarvataḥ upadadhyāt /
viśayānāṃ purastāddaśa /

pakṣayostriṃśattriṃśacpañcamabhāgīyāḥ purastātprabhṛtyātmani pracchādyamāne udagāyatāḥ pañcamabhāgīyānāṃ nava rītayaḥ /
caturdaśīyānāṃ pādānāṃ dakṣiṇato dve pañcamabhāgīye uttarataś ca dve /
pucche tu yathoktābhiḥ pracchādyāmāne bahubhedaprasaṅgāt ṣaḍbhāgīyā utpannā api na yuktā iti ṣaḍbhāgīyāstisrastisro viśayānāṃ paścāt pucchapārśvayoḥ pratīcīrupadadhāti ""tāsāṃ pārśve dvedve caturbhāgīye pratīcyau upadhāya tāsāṃ madhye tisraḥ ṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ pratīcīrupadadhthāt /
aparārdhe cāṣṭāvaṇūkeṣṭakā upadadhyāt /
evamātmani viśayābhiḥ saha ekonaśataṃ pañcamabhāgīyāścaturdaśaprādeśāḥ pakṣayostriṃśattiṃśat pañcamabhāgīyāḥ pucche dvādaśa caturbhāgīyā nava ṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ /
tā etāḥ ṣaḍūnaṃ dviśatam /
tatra ṣaṭsaṃkhyā sampādyā''

atra navapañcamabhāgīyārītīnāṃ madhyasthāmekāṃ pañcamabhāgīyārītimuddhṛtya madhye viṃśatiprādeśeṣṭakā udīcīrupadadhyāt /
atra catuḥsaṃkhyātiricyate /
atireke adhikapramāṇopadhānena saṃkhyāpūraṇasyānyāyyatvādaṇūkāḥ pañcamabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna iti paribhāṣayāṇūkopadhānena saṃkhyāpūraṇasya nyāyyatvācca /
tataḥ prādeśarotyā pūrvarītiḥ yathā saṃśliṣṭā bhavati tathā kṛtvā pūrvāntarītimuddhṛtya tatrāṣṭāvaṇūkā upadadhyāt /
evaṃ prādeśarītyāḥ paritastisro rītīḥ pracyāvya dvitīyāṃ rītimuddhtyāṣṭāvaṇūkā upadadhyāt /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
atra kecita -- prathame prastāre pucchāgre daśaprādeśānupadhāya pādeṣṭakāśvānādṛtya pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiḥsaṃkhyāṃ pūrayanti /
bhedamapi sahante /
kecitu pracchādanakāle saṃkhyāpūrakāṇāṃ sthānamavaśiṣya pracchādya saṃkhyāpūrakā upadadhati /
tatra tu sūtrāñjasyamasti vā naveti cintyam //

ūrvarsthiśabdasaṃyuktā śrutirmukhyātra yā kṛtā /
ācāryeṇaiva sūtrāṇāṃ ṣaḍbhāgīyā kṛte tu sā /
ākyātamarthaṃ cācāryaistathorvasthīti sūtritam /
ṣaḍbhāgīyāpadaṃ taddvadapyanyaiḥsūtrritaṃ paraiḥ /
hiraṇyakeśināṃ śulbe tathorvasthīti sūtritam /
vyākhyātāro 'pi tatraitat ṣaḍbhīgāyāparaṃ viduḥ /
bodhāyanaś ca bhagavān same tu caturaśrake /
turyapañcamaṣaṣṭhaiś ca sapādaiḥ karaṇaṃ vyadhāt /
urvasthināmadheyānāmupadeśabalādiha /
pracchāditānāmābhistadbādhaḥsūtrakṛteṣṭate /
aratnayo 'pyaṇūkāś ca chādane syurviparyayāt /
pūrvasminnaparasmiṃś ca prastāre saṃbhavo na hi /
na pañcadaśabhāgīyā śrūyate tra dvitīyake /
śrūyante tāstu pūrvāgnau na tatpūrvo dvitīyakaḥ /
prakṛtitvāddvayoragnayoḥ nityatvācca dvayorapi /
atastāsaṃ dvitīye 'gnau kathaṃ prāptirvimṛśyatām /
kintu tāsāṃ tu yatkāryaṃ tatrāṇūkāstu bodhitāḥ /
prathamāgnerato 'nyatra tatsthāne syuraṇūkikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) that was made primary here, joined with the word <s>ūrvasthi</s> (thigh-bone), by the teacher himself — that [applies] when the <s>ṣaḍbhāgīya</s> (sixth-part bricks) are employed. And the meaning stated by the teachers has been formulated as 'thus <s>ūrvasthi</s>.' The word '<s>ṣaḍbhāgīya</s>' was also similarly formulated by other [teachers]. In the <s>Śulba</s> of the <s>Hiraṇyakeśins</s>, it is formulated as 'thus <s>ūrvasthi</s>.' The commentators there also know this as [equivalent to] '<s>ṣaḍbhāgīya</s>.' And the blessed <s>Bodhāyana</s>, in the equal quadrilateral, prescribed the mold with the quarter, fifth, and sixth [parts] with [additional] quarters. Here, by the force of the teaching regarding those named <s>ūrvasthi</s> — which are concealed [in meaning] — by these [equivalent designations], the overriding [of the literal reading] is desired by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author). The <s>aratni</s>-[bricks] and also <s>aṇūkas</s> (small bricks) may be in the covering, by reversal. In the first and second layers, [their] occurrence is indeed [possible]. The fifteenth-part [brick] is not heard of in the second [layer]. But they are heard of in the first fire[-altar]; that first [layer] is not the second. Because of the primary nature of both fire[-altars], and because both are perpetual — therefore, how the attainment of those [fifteenth-part bricks] in the second fire[-altar layer] [is possible] — let it be considered! However, whatever function those [bricks] serve — there the <s>aṇūkas</s> (small bricks) are taught [as substitutes]. In fire[-altars] other than the first, <s>aṇūkas</s> would be in their place.

children.text: ye tvatra pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiḥsaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ kurvanti te kimupadeśato vā prāptaṃ manvate? atideśato vā? ubhayathāpi na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Those who here complete the count with fifteenth-part [bricks] — do they consider this obtained from direct teaching? Or from extension (<s>atideśa</s>)? In either case, it is not appropriate.
Because of the primary nature of both [layers], and because of the absence of the original-modification [relationship between them].

children.text: nanvaṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna iti vacanasāmarthyāttāsāṃ prāptirbhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: Now, from the force of the statement '<s>aṇūkas</s> take the place of fifteenth-part [bricks],' their attainment [in the second layer] should follow!

children.translated_text: In the second layer, those same rows facing east.

children.text: yatra dakṣiṇataḥ uttarataśvāṣṭāvaṣṭāvuddhṛtya pūrvavat pādā ardhāśvopadadhyādevaṃ dviśataḥ /
children.translated_text: Where, from the south and north, eight and eight are removed; as before, quarters and halves are placed — thus two hundred.

children.text: evameva praugādiṣvapi karaṇāni dvādaśabhāgīyābhistrayodaśabhāgīyābhirvā yathāyogamupadhāya pādeṣṭakābhirardheṣṭakābhiś ca saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet /
children.translated_text: Similarly in the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped) and other [fire-altars] also, having placed [bricks from] molds with twelfth-part or thirteenth-part [bricks] as appropriate, one should complete the count with quarter-bricks and half-bricks.
Enough of excessive digression.

If so, [we say:] no; the statement '<s>aṇūkas</s> take the place of fifteenth-part [bricks]' is meant to establish the attainment of <s>aṇūkas</s> for count-completion in [performing] the function of those [fifteenth-part bricks]. It does not establish the placement of those [fifteenth-part bricks themselves] merely for count-completion. Therefore this should be reflected upon. For what purpose was this stated by the teacher? It is answered: in [completing] the count of bricks being placed — not in [mere] count-completion in a layer when the brick-count is achieved. Should there be a component-division due to [a different] brick-division [than prescribed], that is to be tolerated — thinking thus, [the teacher] stated [this rule]. This will be demonstrated in the second hawk-altar. Some ritualists, however, make layers of more or less [than two hundred bricks] in the fire[-altar], thinking that count-completion [of one thousand etc.] is in the aggregate. That is incorrect. When a count of one thousand etc. is being achieved by layers of fifteen and more [bricks per row], in the absence of a specific statement [to the contrary], since 'it should be equal, because of the absence of [scriptural] statement [otherwise]' [applies], the two-hundred nature of layers alone is appropriate. And because in the chariot-wheel fire[-altar], by [the statement] 'with its <s>karaṇī</s>, by twelve' etc., the production of exactly two hundred [per layer] is shown. Now, wherever there is an additional statement 'one should fill the layer,' there let there be count-completion within the layer. But where there is none, the fill-count is for the aggregate — otherwise the fill-statement would be purposeless. It is answered: there is no purposelessness there. How? There, the count-completion that is established by logic is [already effective] — the prescription of fifteenth-part [bricks] serving as the means for that. If all layers are of two hundred, for what purpose is 'the two-hundred layer' stated? When [a layer of two hundred] is already established, the [statement] with mere introductory purpose [serves] to accomplish the two-hundred nature of all layers. Just as one one-fold layer is of two hundred, so all other layers too should be made of two-hundred count. Even though there is a fill-statement — this effort [of the teacher] is to strengthen by restatement what is already logically established. Therefore all layers should be made of two hundred — not more or less — thus the two-hundred nature of all layers is established. The primary (<s>prakṛti</s>) seven-fold [altar] has been stated. Now the permanent modifications (<s>vikṛti</s>) are stated — 'one-fold' etc. For the six fire[-altars] from one-fold through six-fold: with the twelfth and thirteenth [parts] of the <s>karaṇī</s> (side-measure) of each respective fire[-altar], one should have bricks made. Here, the <s>karaṇī</s> of the one-fold is one hundred and twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> (120). Of the two-fold: one hundred sixty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-four <s>tilas</s> (169 + 24t). Of the three-fold: two hundred seven <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-nine <s>tilas</s> (207 + 29t). Of the four-fold: two hundred forty <s>aṅgulas</s> (240). Of the five-fold: two hundred sixty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> and eleven <s>tilas</s> (268 + 11t). Of the six-fold: two hundred ninety-three <s>aṅgulas</s> and thirty-one <s>tilas</s> (293 + 31t). Of these <s>karaṇīs</s>: with the twelfth on all sides — one mold. With the thirteenth on all sides — one mold. Of those, the quarter-bricks are made by the [letter] 'ca' (and); half-bricks also — six-fold or nine-fold molds. The placement is stated: on both sides, quarter-[bricks]; three rows of twelfths; then five rows of thirteenths; then one [row of] thirteenths with quarters; then one [row of] thirteenths; then three rows of twelfths with quarters on both sides — thus thirteen rows. There, in the second row of twelfths, having removed the fourth and eighth bricks, one should place two half-bricks each. And there in the penultimate [row], having removed [bricks], four half-bricks. The layer is exactly two hundred. In the second layer: two rows of thirteenths; then one of thirteenths with quarters; then one of thirteenths with quarters on both sides; then four rows of twelfths; then one of twelfths with quarters on both sides; then three rows of thirteenths — thus thirteen rows. Here, in the middle [row], having removed six, one should place quarters. The layer is two hundred. Alternatively, the first layer with twelfths [alone], the second with thirteenths — as is stated. In the all-twelfths option: long quarter-bricks and half-bricks [are used]. There, in the first layer, seventeen rows facing east; all those of twelve bricks; all of them to the south with half-bricks; then one [row] with quarter-[bricks]; then three [rows] of twelfths; then one with quarters; then one with halves; then one with quarters; then three of twelfths; the last with halves — thus seventeen rows. There, from the fifth, sixth, and seventh rows, having removed the last three, one should place one twelfth-[brick]. Then from the eleventh, twelfth, and thirteenth [rows], having removed the last three, one should place an eleventh-[brick]. Thus two hundred. For the second [layer] with thirteenths: fourteen rows facing north; of those, the first with halves; twelfths and thirteenths; the last with halves — those fourteen rows. Thus one hundred and eighty-two bricks. There, in the first half, having removed six thirteenths, one should place twenty-four quarter-[bricks]. Thus two hundred. If all layers [are] with twelfths, then having placed the first layer in the manner described above, from the second layer onward, one should place the rows facing north. This is [a layer of] two hundred. If all [layers are] with thirteenths, then the row-arrangement stated for the second layer — placing [those rows] facing east in the first layer, in the latter half removing thirteenths and placing quarters, and in the next layer placing those [rows] facing north — this is two hundred. If on one [axis] thirteen, on the other twelve: then bricks of lengthwise orientation, thirteen rows facing north; those are one hundred and fifty-six; in the first row, and in the fifth, having removed eight and eight, twenty-eight quarters and two-and-two halves. Thus two hundred.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary

ubhayatra prādeśamātramaviśeṣāt /
tataḥ purastāddaśa prādeśāḥ pārśvayordvaidvau /

(One should fill the entire fire[-altar].)

ātmani viśayābhiḥsaha udīcyo daśa rītayaḥ, tāsāṃ dvitīyāṃ navamīṃ caturthībhirupadadhāyāt, ṣaṣṭhīṃ prādeśaiḥ /

children.translated_text: In the body, together with the [extension-]area bricks, ten rows facing north; of those, the second and ninth are placed with fourth-[bricks]; the sixth with <s>prādeśa</s>-[bricks]. In the remainder of the body and in the wings: fifth-part [bricks]. In the latter half of the tail, in the middle of the sides, nine sixth-part [bricks] facing east. In the remainder of the tail, twelve <s>aṇūkas</s> (small bricks). Thus a layer of two hundred.

children.text: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_11.11b ||
children.translated_text: One should pile in alternation, for as many layers as one wishes to make. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 11.11b]
This has been explained.
Eleventh chapter.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary.

children.text:
kratvarthenopādīyamānāmāmekavidhādīnāṃ pakṣapucchatvaṃ pratipāditam /
tathā teṣāmupadhānavidhiḥ kathaṃ bhavatītyucyate ----
children.translated_text: It has been established that the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars], being employed for the purpose of the sacrifice, have wings and tail. Now, how the placement-rule for them works is stated:

children.text: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ karaṇīnāṃ dvādaśena trayodaśenetīṣṭakāḥ kārayet || ĀpŚus_12.1a ||
children.translated_text: For the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars], one should have bricks made with the twelfth and thirteenth [parts] of the <s>karaṇīs</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.1a]

children.text:
karaṇānāṃ dvādaśena trayodaśena kṛtaiḥsamacaturaśraiḥ iṣṭakāḥ kārayet /
sarvato dvādaśenaikaṃ karaṇaṃ sarvatastrayodaśena dvitīyam /
children.translated_text: With equal squares made by the twelfth and thirteenth [parts] of the mold-[measures], one should have bricks made. With the twelfth on all sides — one mold; with the thirteenth on all sides — the second.

children.text: pādeṣṭakāś ca vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_12.1b ||
children.translated_text: And quarter-bricks — one should pile in alternation, for as many layers as one wishes to make. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.1b]

children.text:
pādeṣṭakāś ca dvādaśīvadhāstrayodaśavidhāśvārdheṣṭakāś ceti śulbāntaram /
asmākamapi prauger'dheṣṭakāḥ kāryāḥ /
ekavidhādiṣvapi yadi prathamaprastāro dvādaśabhiḥ dvitīyastrayodaśabhirityasminpākṣer'dheṣṭakāḥ kāryāḥ /
itarathā saṅdhayā na pūryata eva /
children.translated_text: Quarter-bricks of twelfth-type and thirteenth-type, and half-bricks — thus [states] another <s>Śulba</s> [text]. In our [tradition] also, half-bricks should be made for the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped) [altar]. In the one-fold and other [altars] also, if the first layer is with twelfths and the second with thirteenths — in this option, half-bricks should be made. Otherwise, the [edge-]joints simply cannot be filled.
Therein verses:

children.text: dvividhe mānikā rajjuḥsaptatyā ca śatena ca /
children.translated_text: 'For the two-fold, the measuring cord is one hundred and seventy
<s>aṅgulas</s> measured — of that fire[-altar], diminished by ten <s>tilas</s>.'
'For the three-fold, the measuring cord is two hundred and eight,
diminished by six <s>tilas</s> alone — so calculated by the mathematicians.'
'Of the fourth fold also, the measuring cord is stated
as measured by two hundred and forty [<s>aṅgulas</s>].'
'Of the fifth fold, this [cord is] two hundred sixty-eight;
the mathematicians know the measuring [cord] to be joined with eleven <s>tilas</s>.'

children.text: caturbhiś ca navatyā ca śatābhyāṃ ca mitā bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Measured by four and ninety and two hundreds [= 294],
diminished by three <s>tilas</s> alone — such is the measuring cord of the six-fold.'

children.text:
upadhāne 'bhitaḥ pādāstisro rītyo 'tha dvādaśyaḥ /
tataḥ pañca trayodaśyaḥ /
tata ekā trayodaśī /
pādarītiḥ tata ekā trayodaśī tatastisro 'bhitaḥ pādā rītyāṃ dvādaśyaḥ /
dvitīyasyāṃ ekā caturthī ca tebhyo 'nyo 'ṣṭamī /

children.translated_text: This is the [first] layer.

children.text: aparasmin prastāre dve rītyau trayodaśyekā trayodaśī pādā tata ekābhihitapādā trayodaśī /
children.translated_text: In the second layer: two rows of thirteenths; one thirteenth with quarters; then one with designated quarters, thirteenths.
Then four [rows of] twelfths.

children.text: atha madhyamāḥṣaḍiṣṭakāḥ caturbhedāḥ, eṣa dviśataḥ prattāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the middle six bricks are of four types — this is the two-hundred layer.

In placement: quarter[-bricks] on both sides; three rows of twelfths; then five of thirteenths; then one thirteenth with quarter-row; then one thirteenth; then three rows of twelfths with quarters on both sides. In the second [row]: one [brick at] the fourth and another at the eighth [position removed].
'In alternation' — this has been explained.

children.text: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ prathamāhāreṇa dvitīyena tṛtīyeneti yo yujyeta | sarveṣāṃ yathā śrutisaṅkhyā tathordhvapramāṇam || ĀpŚus_12.2 ||
children.translated_text: For the one-fold and subsequent [fire-altars], whichever is appropriate with the first, second, or third layer[-type]: the count for all is as per scripture, and likewise the height-measure. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.2]

children.text: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ ṣaḍvidhaparyantānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prathamāhāre dvitīyāhāre ca yathā saṅkhyāḥ śrūyante /
kimuktaṃ bhavati? yadi prathamāhāraḥsahasrasaṅkhyā jānudaghnatā ca /
children.translated_text: What is being said? If the first layer has the one-thousand count, and the [height is] knee-high —
Now, in the second [option], these [characteristics] are indeed applicable.
Those characteristics are indeed applicable to the seven-and-a-half-[fold] as its own form.
And that statement is for the purpose of indicating that the seven-and-a-half-[fold] is the primary form (<s>prakṛti</s>).
For all [fire-altars] from the one-fold through the six-fold, in the first and second layers, the counts are as heard [in scripture].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Alternation ... should pile

children.text:
gataṃ /
vikṛtiṣu punarvyatyāse vacanaṃ kimartham? ucyate -- prakṛtau citīnāṃ prastārāṇāṃ ca vaiṣamyāt kimayaṃ vyatyāsaḥ prastāradharmaḥ citidharma iti kasyacitsandehaḥsyāt /
vikṛtau tu dviprastārāśvitaya iti prastārayorvaiṣamyemāyaṃ vyatyāsaḥ kasya dharma iti sandehe yāvantaḥ prastārāstāvato vyatyasya cinuyāt bhedābhāvāya /
vyatyāsasya prastāradharmatāpratipādanāya punarvacanaṃ vyatyāsasya /
children.translated_text: Explained. In the modifications (<s>vikṛtis</s>), why is the alternation statement repeated? It is answered: in the primary form, because the layers (<s>citis</s>) and the arrangements (<s>prastāras</s>) are different, someone might doubt whether this alternation is a property of the arrangement or of the layer. But in the modification, where "two arrangements constitute a layer" — when there is dissimilarity between the arrangements, whose property is this alternation? In this doubt, one should pile by alternating as many arrangements as there are, for the purpose of avoiding joints. The repetition of the alternation [statement] is for establishing that alternation is a property of the arrangement.
One-fold ... measure

children.text:
ekavidhaprabhṛtiṣaḍvidhaparyantānāṃ prathamāhāraḥ prathamaprayogaḥ yo yujyeta bhṛśaṃ yukto bhavati /
yathāśrutisaṅkhyā śrutyuktena prakāreṇa saṅkhyā sahasrādiḥ yathā bhṛśaṃ yujyate tathordhvapramāṇaṃ jānudaghnādi ca yoyujyeteti ca sambandhaḥ /
ekavidhaprabhṛtiṣaḍvidhaparyantānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prathamāhāreṇa dvitīyāhāreṇa tṛtīyāhāreṇa "sāhasraṃ cinvīta prathamaṃ cinvānaḥ' ityādyāḥ śrūyamāṇāḥ sāhasrādisaṅkhyājānudaghnādiparimāṇāśvaiteṣu sampādyatayopadiśyante /
etena ekavidhasya
children.translated_text: For [the fire-altars] from <s>ekavidha</s> (one-fold) to <s>ṣaḍvidha</s> (six-fold), the first performance (<s>āhāra</s>) — the first application — whichever is appropriate, is very much applicable. The count according to scripture — the count such as one thousand etc. by the method stated in the scripture — whatever is applicable, along with the upward measure such as knee-high etc. — this is the connection. For all [fire-altars] from <s>ekavidha</s> to <s>ṣaḍvidha</s>, in the first, second, and third performances, the scriptural statements such as "one who piles for the first time should pile with one thousand" etc. are taught as applicable to these [smaller altars] regarding the counts of one thousand etc. and the dimensions of knee-high etc. By this,

children.text:
prakṛtitve dvividhādīnāṃ tatprakṛtitve ca sāhasrādisaṅkhyājānudaghnādi parimāṇatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /
ekavidhādayo 'pi nityā eva akāmasambandhāt /
prakṛtayo vikṛtayaś ca nityā uktāḥ /
itānīṃ kāmyāḥ praugādaya ucyante /
children.translated_text: when the <s>ekavidha</s> is the primary form, and when the <s>dvividha</s> and others are its primary forms, the counts of one thousand etc. and the dimensions of knee-high etc. are established. The <s>ekavidha</s> and others too are indeed obligatory, because of the absence of connection with desire [for a specific result]. The primary forms and the modifications have been stated as obligatory. Now the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) ones — the <s>prauga</s> (chariot-front) and the like — are stated.
The optional [shapes] are modifications of quality, because the [relevant] scripture pertains to quality. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.3]

children.text:
nityasya saptavidhāgnervikārāḥ praugādyākṛtiviśeṣeṇa guṇena vikṛtāḥ /
kutaḥ? guṇaśāstratvāt /
guṇaṃ śāsti vidadhātīti guṇaśāstram /
"praugacitaṃ cinvīta' iti vakṣyamāṇaṃ vākyaṃ praugasyāgneśvayanamanūdya tatra bhātṛvyāpanodanaphalārthaṃ praugādyākṛtiviśeṣaṃ guṇaṃ vidhatte /
tasmātkāmyāḥ praugādayaḥ /
godohanādivannityasyāgnerguṇavikārāḥ na nityāḥ naiva prakṛtaya iti /
children.translated_text: The <s>prauga</s> and other specific shapes are modifications of the obligatory seven-fold fire[-altar], modified by the quality of specific shape. Why? Because the [relevant] scripture pertains to quality. A <s>guṇa-śāstra</s> (scripture pertaining to quality) is one that teaches, prescribes, a quality. The forthcoming statement "one should pile the <s>prauga</s>-shaped [altar]" — restating the fire-piling [as the main act], prescribes the specific shape of <s>prauga</s> etc. as a quality for the purpose of the result of removing rivals. Therefore, the <s>prauga</s> and others are optional. Like cow-milking and the like, they are quality-modifications of the obligatory fire[-altar] — not obligatory, nor primary forms.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary (Alternation ... should pile)

children.text:
"sandhyantarāle pañcamabhāgīyāḥsapādāḥ' ityasyāparā vyākhyāpādaśabdena prastutā evāṇūkāpādā gṛhyante /
prastutāś ca pādā aṣṭasaṃkhyā iti tathaiveha grāhyāḥ /
tatraivamupadhānam -- prathame prastāre sandhyantarāle pārśvayostriṃśadaṅgulaṃ pariśiṣya madhyame pañcatriṃśatpañcamabhāgīyāḥ, pariśiṣṭayostriṃśadaṅgulayoḥ paścātpurastācca dvedve pañcadaśāṅgule udīcyau, madhye tasrastisro 'ṇūkāḥ, pañcamībhiḥ pūrayitumaśakyatvātpucchasya pārśvayoḥ purataḥṣaṭṣaṭpañcadaśāṅgulāḥ /
pucchaśeṣe trayodaśāṇūkāḥ, evaṃ kṛte aṣṭonadviśataṃ bhavati /
pucchamadhye 'ṇūkāmekāmuddhṛtya daśāṅgulā navopadadhyāt /
ātmani dvitīye madhye vā mantropadhānasaukaryārtham /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasmin pucchavarjaṃ yathāsūtramevātmani prācyo daśa rītyaḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇasyāṃ madhye pañcamīṃ nidhāya tataḥ prākpaścācca dvedve prādeśamāyau /
evamuttarasyāṃ pucchasyāparārdhe pārśvayormadhye ca tisrastisraḥṣaḍbhāgīyāḥ prācyaḥ, pucchaśeṣe dvādaśāṇūkāḥ /
ye tu ṣaḍbhāgīyā necchanti teṣāmapi pucchavarjamevamevopadhānam /
tatra pucche prādeśamupadhāyetyasya prādeśeṣṭakāmupadhāyetyevaṃ varṇayanti /
anyathā bhedaprasaṅgāt /
prādeśāścaturbhāgīyābhiḥsaha na śerata iti sāmarthyāt pañcamabhāgīyānāmākṣepaḥ /
tatraivamupadhānam -- pucchasyapūrvārdhe pārśvayoścatasraḥ pañcadaśāhgulāḥ /
madhye ṣaḍaṇūkāḥ /
aparārdhe pañcadaśa pañcamyaḥ /
pucchāgre madhyamā abhito dve uddhṛtyāṣṭau prādeśeṣṭakā upadheyāḥ /
evamaṣṭonadviśataṃ bhavati /
tataḥ pūrvavadekāṃ catuthīṃ pañcamīṃ voddhṛtya daśāṅgulā vāṣṭāṅgulā vopadadhyāt /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
dvitīye prastāre pucche ṣoḍaśāṇūkāḥ, ātmanyuttarasyāṃ rītyāṃ catasṛbhyaḥ pañcamībhyaḥ prāktisro 'ṣṭāhgulā udīcyaḥ tata ekā pañcamī /
tatastisro 'ṣṭāṅgulāḥ /
tatastisraḥ pañcamyaḥ /
dakṣiṇārītiḥ pūrvavadeva /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
evaṃ sāratniprādeśasyopadhānamuktamācāryeṇa /
tadrahitasyocyate -- pakṣāgrayostisrastisro 'ṇūkāḥ /
tāsāṃ pasvātpurastācca dvedve pañcadaśāṅgule /
evamnyayorapyātmānaṃ pradeśenopetāḥ pārśvayoḥ ṣaṭṣaṭ prādeśāḥ /
pakṣaśeṣe pañcamyaḥ /
sandhyantarāle catvāriṃśatpañcamabhāgīyā ātmaśeṣaḥ pūrvoktavadeva /
pucchasya pūrvārdhe pārśvayoraṣṭau pañcadaśāṅgulāḥ, padhye ṣaḍaṇūkāḥ /
aparārdhe ṣaḍbhāgīyābhirudīcyastisro rītayaḥ /
tāsu pūrvasyāṃ pārśvayordvedve daśāṅgule /
pucchasya pūrvārdhe ṣaḍbhāgīyā aṣṭādaśa /
aparārdhe pṛṣṭhayāmabhitaḥ pañcamyākuddhṛtya aṣṭau pādeṣṭakā upadadhyāt /
ātmani pūrvarītau madhye pañcamīṃ nidhāyābhitaścatasraḥ pādeṣṭakā upadadhyāt /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
athātrāpi ṣaḍbhāgīyāmanicchatāṃ pucchasya pārśvayoḥ purataḥṣaṭṣaṭ pañcadaśāṅgulāḥ /
pucchaśeṣe trayodaśāṇūkāḥ /
pakṣāgrayoścatasraścatasro 'ṇūkāḥ /
śeṣaṃ pūrvoktavadeva /
evaṃ kṛte caturaśītiśatamiṣṭakā bhavanti /
tatrātmani pṛṣṭhayānte caturthyau pañcamyāvuddhṛtyāṣṭādaśāṅgulā aṣṭāṅgulā vopadadhyāt /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
anyasmin prastāre pucchāpyaye pañcamabhāgīyā ityādi yathāsūtram /
ātmanaḥ pūrvarītiḥ pūrvoktavat /
pucchasya pūrvārdhe 'ṣṭāvaṇūkāḥ aparārdhe pañcamyāvṛddhṛtyāṣṭaṅgulā upadadhyāt /

children.translated_text: The layer of two hundred.
Thus, many different modes of placement have been stated.
Among those, the most appropriate mode should be favored by the learned.

children.text: sarveṣveva prakāreṣu pucchāpyaye pakṣāpyaye vā anyataratra viśayā iṣṭakā upadhīyanta ityanusandhātavyam //
children.translated_text: In all modes, it should be observed that special bricks are placed at either the tail-junction or the wing-junction.

Another interpretation of "at the joints, fifth-part [bricks] with quarters": by the word "quarter" (<s>pāda</s>), the very <s>aṇūkā</s> quarter-[bricks] under discussion are understood. And the quarters under discussion are eight in number — thus they should be understood here. The placement there [is as follows]: in the first layer, at the joints on the sides, leaving thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>, in the middle thirty-five fifth-part [bricks]; in the remaining thirty-<s>aṅgula</s> [areas], behind and in front, two-by-two fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] facing north; in the middle, three-by-three <s>aṇūkā</s> [bricks]. Since the tail cannot be filled with fifth-[part bricks alone], on the sides of the tail, in front, six-by-six fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. In the remainder of the tail, thirteen <s>aṇūkās</s>. When done thus, one hundred and ninety-two bricks result. In the middle of the tail, having removed one <s>aṇūkā</s>, one should place nine ten-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. In the body, in the second [row] in the middle, or [elsewhere] for the convenience of mantra-based placement. Thus the layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], excluding the tail, as per the <s>sūtra</s> — in the body, ten east-facing rows. In the southern [row], placing a fifth-[part brick] in the middle, then before and after it, two-by-two <s>prādeśa</s>-measure [bricks]. Likewise in the northern [row]. In the rear half of the tail, on the sides and in the middle, three-by-three sixth-part [bricks] facing east; in the remainder of the tail, twelve <s>aṇūkās</s>. Those who do not accept sixth-part [bricks] — for them too, the placement is the same except in the tail. There, in the tail, "having placed a <s>prādeśa</s>" is explained as "having placed a <s>prādeśa</s>-brick." Otherwise there would be the problem of joints. Since <s>prādeśa</s>-[bricks] do not fit with fourth-part [bricks] — by implication, fifth-part [bricks] are excluded. The placement there: in the front half of the tail, on the sides, four fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. In the middle, six <s>aṇūkās</s>. In the rear half, fifteen fifth-[part bricks]. At the tail-tip, having removed two [bricks] on either side of the middle, eight <s>prādeśa</s>-bricks should be placed. Thus one hundred and ninety-two bricks result. Then, as before, having removed one fourth- or fifth-[part brick], one should place nine ten-<s>aṅgula</s> or eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. The layer of two hundred. In the second layer, in the tail, sixteen <s>aṇūkās</s>; in the body, in the northern row, before the four fifth-[part bricks], three eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] facing north, then one fifth-[part brick], then three eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks], then three fifth-[part bricks]. The southern row is as before. The layer of two hundred. Thus the placement with <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions] has been stated by the <s>ācārya</s>. For [the altar] without those, it is stated: at the wing-tips, three-by-three <s>aṇūkās</s>. Behind and in front of those, two-by-two fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. Likewise for both [wings], the body accompanied by <s>prādeśa</s>-[extensions], on the sides six-by-six <s>prādeśa</s>-[bricks]. In the remainder of the wings, fifth-[part bricks]. At the joints, forty fifth-part [bricks]; the remainder of the body is as stated before. In the front half of the tail, on the sides, eight fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]; in the middle, six <s>aṇūkās</s>. In the rear half, three north-facing rows of sixth-part [bricks]. In the front [row] of those, on the sides, two-by-two ten-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. In the front half of the tail, eighteen sixth-part [bricks]. In the rear half, having removed one fifth-[part brick] on either side of the spine-line, eight quarter-bricks should be placed. In the body, in the front row, placing a fifth-[part brick] in the middle, on either side four quarter-bricks should be placed. Thus the layer of two hundred. Now, for those here too who do not accept sixth-part [bricks], on the sides of the tail in front, six-by-six fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. In the remainder of the tail, thirteen <s>aṇūkās</s>. At the wing-tips, four-by-four <s>aṇūkās</s>. The rest is as stated before. When done thus, one hundred and eighty-four bricks result. There, in the body, at the end of the spine-line, having removed the two fourth-[and] fifth-[part bricks], one should place eighteen or eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. The layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], at the tail-junction, fifth-part [bricks] etc. as per the <s>sūtra</s>. The front row of the body is as stated before. In the front half of the tail, eight <s>aṇūkās</s>; in the rear half, having removed a fifth-[part brick], one should place eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks].
Thus ends the eleventh section.
<s>Ekavidha</s> and subsequent ... and quarter-bricks.

children.text:
vyādhikaraṇaḥṣṭhayau /
ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ ṣaḍvidhaparyantānāṃ yāḥ karaṇyaḥ tāsāṃ dvādaśena trayodaśeneti samacaturaśrā iṣṭakāḥ kārayet pādeṣṭakāś ca /
children.translated_text: The sixth-case endings are in different grammatical agreement. For [the fire-altars] from <s>ekavidha</s> (one-fold) to <s>ṣaḍvidha</s> (six-fold), of those <s>karaṇīs</s> (constructing cords), by [dividing into] twelve and thirteen, one should have even-quadrilateral bricks made, and quarter-bricks too.
And those are of two kinds: fourth-part [bricks] and ninth-[part bricks].
Therein are verses:
The <s>karaṇī</s> (constructing cord) of the <s>ekavidha</s> (one-fold) is one hundred and twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>;
for the <s>dvividha</s> (two-fold), it is known to be one hundred and seventy, diminished by ten <s>tilas</s>.
For the <s>trividha</s> (three-fold), two hundred and eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, diminished by eight <s>tilas</s>.
The <s>karaṇī</s> of the <s>caturvidha</s> (four-fold) is two hundred and forty.
For the <s>pañcavidha</s> (five-fold), one hundred and sixty-eight, with eleven <s>tilas</s>.
For the <s>ṣaḍvidha</s> (six-fold), from three hundred, six <s>aṅgulas</s> and [some] <s>tilas</s> should be subtracted.

children.text:
ekavidhasya tāvat karaṇyā dvādaśena daśāṅgulenaikaṃ karaṇam /
tadardhena pañcāṅgulena dvitīyaṃ pādeṣṭakārūpam /
tṛtīyena ca saikādaśatilena tryaṅgulena tṛtīyam /
sā navamītyucyate /
evaṃ trayodaśena sāṣṭatilena navāṅgulenaikam /
tadardhena tatpādyāḥ /
caturaṅgulā saikaviṃśatitilā /
tṛtīyena ca navamī tryaṅgulā satilatrayā /
evaṃ dvividhādiṣu draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: First, for the <s>ekavidha</s>: by [dividing] the <s>karaṇī</s> into twelfths — one brick of ten <s>aṅgulas</s>. By its half — five <s>aṅgulas</s> — a second, in the form of a quarter-brick. And by its third — three <s>aṅgulas</s> with eleven <s>tilas</s> — a third. That is called the ninth-[part brick]. Similarly, by [dividing into] thirteenths — one [brick] of nine <s>aṅgulas</s> with eight <s>tilas</s>. By its half, the quarters: four <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-one <s>tilas</s>. And by its third, the ninth-[part brick]: three <s>aṅgulas</s> with three <s>tilas</s>. Similarly for the <s>dvividha</s> and others, it should be observed.
Alternation ... should wish to make

children.text:
tatra prastārayoranuktatvāt dvādaśītrayodaśīnāmeva sāvayavānāṃ prastāreṣu vyatyāsaḥ /
dvādaśībhiḥsāvayavabhirekaḥ prastāraḥ trayodaśībhirapara iti /
saṃkālitopadhānaṃ tu na bhavatyavacanāt etadatidiṣṭapraugacityasambhavācca /
tatra prathame prastāre agnimadhye navadvādaśīnāṃ navamyaścaturaśrīkṛtāḥ /
tāḥ paritaḥṣaṣṭiḥ pādyāḥ /
tāḥ parito 'ṣṭāviṃśatiśataṃ dvādaśyaḥ /
uttarāṃsa ekāmuddhṛtya cataslaḥ pādyāḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasmin trayodaśabhiḥ pracchādite navaṣaṣṭiśatamiṣṭakā bhavanti /
agnimadhyasthamuddhatya catasraḥ pādyāḥ /
pratikoṇaṃ catasraścatasraḥ pādyāḥ pṛṣṭhayāyāṃ paścātpurastāccaikaikāmuddhṛtya navanava navamyaḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
children.translated_text: There, since [specific] layers are not stated [for the ekavidha etc.], the alternation applies to the twelfth-[part] and thirteenth-[part bricks] with their sub-divisions in the layers. One layer with twelfth-[part bricks] and their sub-parts; the other with thirteenth-[part bricks]. But combined placement does not occur, because it is not stated, and because of the impossibility of this being extended to the <s>prauga</s>-altar and the like. In the first layer, at the center of the fire[-altar], the ninth-[part bricks] of the twelfth-[part system] are made into a square. Around those, sixty quarter-[bricks]. Around those, one hundred and twenty-eight twelfth-[part bricks]. Having removed one at the northern shoulder, four quarter-[bricks] [are placed]. The layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], when covered with thirteenth-[part bricks], one hundred and sixty-nine bricks result. Having removed the one at the center of the fire[-altar], four quarter-[bricks] [are placed]. At each corner, four-by-four quarter-[bricks]; on the spine-line, behind and in front, having removed one each, nine-by-nine ninth-[part bricks]. The layer of two hundred.
<s>Ekavidha</s> ... upward measure — for the <s>ekavidha</s> and others too, the count of one thousand etc. [applies].
And the upward measure of knee-high etc. applies to the seven-fold and higher [fire-altars] as well.
Even when the area decreases, the count and upward measure do not decrease — this is the meaning.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
The optional [shapes] are modifications of quality, because the [relevant] scripture pertains to quality. [12.3]

children.text: kāmyāḥ praugādayaḥ guṇena vikṛtāḥ -- kimuktaṃ bhavati? guṇasiddhirnāgneḥ /

children.translated_text: Why? Because the [relevant] scripture pertains to quality.
That which teaches (<s>śāsti</s>) is the scripture (<s>śāstra</s>).
Here, the quality is what is taught, not the fire[-altar].
Therefore, because the [relevant] scripture pertains to quality — like cow-milking and the like — these are quality-results.
The optional ones — the <s>prauga</s> (chariot-front) and others — are modified by quality. What is being said? The quality is established, not the fire[-altar itself].

children.text: praugacitaṃ cinvīta bhrātṛvyavān iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_12.4 ||
children.translated_text: One who has rivals should pile [the altar] in <s>prauga</s> (chariot-front) shape — this is known. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.4]

children.text:
praugaḥ śakaṭapurvabhāgaḥ /
tadākāraṃ cinvīta bhrātṛvyavānyasya bahavaḥ bhrātṛvyāḥ sa evaṃ cinvīta /
children.translated_text: The <s>prauga</s> is the front part of a cart. One who has rivals — one who has many rivals — should pile [the altar] in that shape.

children.text: yāvānagniḥ sāratniprādeśo dvistāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ caturaśrāṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhāc chroṇīṃ pratyālikhet | sā nityā praugam || ĀpŚus_12.5 ||
children.translated_text: Having made a quadrilateral area twice as large as the fire[-altar] with <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], from half the <s>karaṇī</s> (side) of the eastern [side], one should mark a line toward the hip. That constitutes the obligatory <s>prauga</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.5]
The making of bricks for the single-fold [altar] has been stated. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.6a]

children.text: pañcadaśabhiraṅgulairnavabhiś ca tilaiḥ antarā catuḥpuruṣā rajjuḥ dvistāvatīṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: With fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and nine <s>tilas</s> as the interval, a cord of four <s>puruṣas</s> produces twice that [area].

children.text: tathā caturaśraṃ vihṛtya sūtroktena mārgeṇa śroṇīṃ parilikhet /
children.translated_text: Having thus constructed the quadrilateral, one should draw the hip[-line] by the method stated in the <s>sūtra</s>.
And one should have the bricks (<s>karaṇas</s>) made.
By [dividing into] twelve and thirteen, with a quarter — [these form] the <s>prauga</s>-shape.
And this statement is for the purpose of indicating that the seven-and-a-half-[fold] is the primary form.
One should have <s>prauga</s> (triangular/chariot-front) bricks made. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.6b]

children.text:
catuḥpuruṣāratninā ca pañcadaśabhiraṅgulaistilairekaviṃśatyā parimitā rajjurīṣāmātrī bhavati vākṣayoḥ pramāṇam /
tasyā dvādaśena ca trayodaśena ca karaṇāni ca kārayet /
dvādaśyā prathame prastāre praugamukhyaḥ /
catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ pādeṣṭakāḥ catasraścatasraḥśroṇyoḥ /
evaṃ caturviṃśottaraṃ śataṃ /
catasror'dheṣṭakāḥśroṇyoreva /
children.translated_text: A cord delimited by four <s>puruṣas</s> and one <s>aratni</s> — [totaling] fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-one <s>tilas</s> — becomes the measure of the chariot-pole or that of the two axles. Of that, by [dividing into] twelve and thirteen, one should have the bricks made. With twelfth-[part bricks], the first layer features the <s>prauga</s>-front: sixty-four [bricks], and four-by-four quarter-bricks at the hips. Thus one hundred and twenty-four. And four half-bricks at the hips themselves.

children.text:
anyasmin prastāre trayodaśyaḥ śroṇyoḥ pādāśvatvāriṃśat dvāvardhau aṣṭapañcāśadadhikaśataṃ trayodaśyaḥ /
prastāro dviśataḥ /
evaṃ vyatyāsaṃ cinuyāt /
tatra ślokāḥ --
children.translated_text: In the other layer, with thirteenth-[part bricks], at the hips, quarter-[bricks] — forty; two halves; one hundred and fifty-eight thirteenth-[part bricks plus] the excess. The layer of two hundred. Thus one should pile in alternation. Therein are verses:
With nineteen <s>aratnīs</s> (forearm-lengths) and eight <s>aṅgulis</s> (finger-breadths),
together with twenty-five <s>tilas</s> (sesame-seed units), the western <s>vimānikā</s> (altar-part) is measured. //
With twenty-one <s>aratnīs</s> and fifteen <s>aṅgulis</s>,
and twenty-one <s>tilas</s>, one <s>vimānikā</s> is measured. //
These three, made equal, produce the <s>prauga</s> (triangular) fire-altar.
One should determine the brick-types (<s>karaṇas</s>) for these according to the <s>sūtra</s> (rule). //
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
The <s>prauga</s> is explained:
The <s>prauga</s> is the front part of a cart (<s>śakaṭa</s>).
One should pile a fire-altar of that shape.
[This is done by] one who has rivals (<s>bhrātṛvya</s>), who is oppressed by rivals and enemies.
By that [fire-altar], he drives away his rivals. //
As large as — [the sūtra text continues].

children.text: yāvānaratniprādeśābhyāṃ sahitaḥsaptavidhaḥ tāvaddviguṇāṃ samacaturaśrāṃ bhūmiṃ kṛtvā tasya caturaśrasya pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā madhyādārabhya śroṇī pratyakṣṇayā likhet /

children.translated_text: Twice the area of the half of the seven-fold [unit] is the ground-area of fifteen <s>puruṣas</s> (man-lengths).
Its <s>karaṇī</s> (diagonal/side) is three <s>puruṣas</s>, one hundred and four-and-twenty <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.

children.text: tayāpareṇa yūpāvaṭadeśaṃ sañcaramavaśiṣyānupraṣṭyaṃ samacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhācchoṇī pratyālikhet /
children.translated_text: With that [measure], leaving a passage-space to the west of the <s>yūpāvaṭa</s> (sacrificial-post pit), having laid out a square on the remaining visible [ground], one should draw lines diagonally from the midpoint of the eastern side toward the hip-corners.
That ground-area becomes the <s>prauga</s>-shaped [altar] measured by the seven-fold [unit]. //

Having made a square ground-area that is twice as large as seven-fold [the unit] combined with an <s>aratni</s> and a <s>prādeśa</s> (span), starting from the middle of the eastern side (<s>karaṇī</s>) of that square, one should draw lines diagonally toward the two hip-corners (<s>śroṇī</s>).
The brick-types — [the sūtra text continues].

children.text:
atra karaṇī karaṇīnāṃ dvādaśatrayodaśakṛtāni /
tābhiś ca yanaṃ prastāravyatyāsa ityevamādyekavidhavat grāhyamityarthaḥ /
viśeṣastu praugā iṣṭakāḥ kārayet /
karaṇāni praugākṛtīni bhaveyuḥ /
tā dvādaśatrayodaśabhāgīyāḥ pādā ardhāś ca praugākṛtīni bhaveyuḥ /
tā dvādaśatrayodaśabhāgīyāḥ pādā ardhāś ca praugākārā grāhyāḥ /
catvāraḥ puruṣā ekonacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ ekaviṃśatitilāś ca praugasyaiṣā mātrā /
sā praugasya pārśvamānī /
tasyāḥ dvādaśena trayodaśena ca karaṇāni kārayet /
pādā ardhāś ca dvādaśa bhāgīyānāmaṣṭatriṃśadahgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāś ca /
eṣāmātrī tanmukham /
pārśvamānyau tricatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ daśatilāś ca /
argheṣṭakānāmekāpārśvamānī /
saiva anyā aṣṭatriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāś ca /
ekonaviṃśatiraṅgulayor'dhatrayodaśatilāś ca mukham /
pādeṣṭakānāmekonaviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ dvāviṃśatitilāś ca /
atha trayodaśabhāgīyānāṃ tāsāṃ pañcatriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāścaikaṃ mukham /
pārśvamānyau tilonacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ /
ardheṣṭakānāmapi saivaikā pārśvamānī /
anyāḥ pañcatriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāś ca /
saptadaśāhgulayaḥ ekonatriṃśattilāś ca tilārdhāśvaikaṃ mukham /
pādeṣṭakānāṃ saptadaśāṅgulaya ekonatriṃśattilāśvaikaṃ mukham /
pārśvamānyau viṃśatiraṅgulayor'dhatilonāḥ /
upadhāne prathamaprastāre praugamukhe catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ pādeṣṭakā upadadhyāt /
śroṇyoścatasraścaturviṃśottaraṃ śataṃ dvādaśyaḥ catasror'dheṣṭakāḥ /

children.translated_text: This is the layer of two hundred.
In the other [layer], at the two hip-corners, twenty-and-twenty thirteenth-part quarters; two halves; one hundred fifty-eight thirteenth-part [bricks].
This is the layer of two hundred.
And the alternation [of layers] should be performed. //

Here the <s>karaṇī</s> (side-measure) of the brick-types is [obtained by dividing into] twelve and thirteen parts.
With those [brick-types], the arrangement and layer-alternation etc. should be understood as in the one-fold [altar] — this is the meaning.
The distinction is: one should make <s>prauga</s> (triangular) bricks.
The brick-types should be of <s>prauga</s> shape.
Those [bricks], being twelfth-parts and thirteenth-parts, with their quarter and half [sub-types], should be of <s>prauga</s> shape.
Those twelfth-parts and thirteenth-parts, with their quarters and halves, should be taken as <s>prauga</s>-shaped.
Four <s>puruṣas</s>, thirty-nine <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-one <s>tilas</s> — this is the measure of the <s>prauga</s>.
That is the side-measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) of the <s>prauga</s>.
One should make the brick-types by its twelfth and thirteenth [parts].
The quarters and halves of the twelfth-part [bricks measure] thirty-eight <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.
This is their measure; that is their face.
The two side-measures are forty-three <s>aṅgulis</s> and ten <s>tilas</s>.
One side-measure of the <s>argha</s>-bricks (boat-shaped bricks).
The other is the same: thirty-eight <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.
Nineteen <s>aṅgulis</s> and twelve-and-a-half <s>tilas</s> and thirteen <s>tilas</s> [is] the face.
The quarter-bricks are nineteen <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-two <s>tilas</s>.
Now, of the thirteenth-part [bricks]: their [measure is] thirty-five <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-five <s>tilas</s> for one face.
The two side-measures are thirty-nine <s>aṅgulis</s> less one <s>tila</s>.
For the half-bricks too, one side-measure is the same.
The others are thirty-five <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.
Seventeen <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-nine <s>tilas</s> and one half-<s>tila</s> [is] one face.
The quarter-bricks are seventeen <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-nine <s>tilas</s> and one [half-tila as] one face.
The two side-measures are twenty <s>aṅgulis</s> and a half less one <s>tila</s>.
In the placement, in the first layer, at the <s>prauga</s>-face, one should place sixty-four quarter-bricks.
At the two hip-corners, four [bricks]; one hundred twenty-four twelfth-part [bricks]; four half-bricks.
<s>Sundararājīya</s> commentary
The optional [fire-altars] are modifications of the primary form:

children.text:
kāmyāḥ chandaśvitprabhṛtayo 'gnayo nityasya caturaśrasya guṇavikārā, tasyaivāgneṇamātreṇa vikṛtatvāt guṇaphalaṃ svaphalaṃ ca sādhayanti /
yathā agniṣṭomasya guṇavikārā ukthyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The optional [fire-altars] — the <s>chandaścit</s> and others — are qualitative modifications (<s>guṇavikāra</s>) of the permanent square [altar]; since they are modified only in respect of the fire-nature of that very [altar], they accomplish both the accessory result and their own result.
Just as the <s>Ukthya</s> and other [sacrifices] are qualitative modifications of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
The <s>prauga</s>-fire-altar is explained:

children.text:
praugaṃ śakaṭasya mukhaṃ trikoṇaṃ, tadvaccīyata iti praugacit /
"karmaṇyagnayākhyāyām' iti vkip /
children.translated_text:
The <s>prauga</s> is the front (<s>mukha</s>) of a cart, which is triangular; [an altar] that is piled in that [shape] is the <s>praugacit</s> (triangular fire-altar).
'In [compounds denoting] action and fire-names' — the suffix <s>kvip</s> [is applied].
He states the measure of that fire-altar —
As large as — [one should] draw:

children.text:
sāratniprādeśasya saptavidhasya karaṇī trīṇi śatānyaṣṭāviṃśatiśvāṅgulayor'dhadvādaśatilāḥ /
tasyā dvikaraṇī pādonapañcaṣaṣṭicatuḥśatāṅgulayaḥ dvistāvatyāḥ pañcadaśapuruṣāyāścaturaśrīkṛtāyā bhūmeḥ karaṇī /
praṇagasya pārśvamānī catvāraḥ puruṣa ekonacatvāriṃśadaṅgulaya ekaviṃśatitilāś ca /
yāvānagnirityeva siddhe sāratniprādeśagrahaṇaṃ tasya pakṣasya śākhāntarīya tvena yatnasādhyatvāt ekavidhādiṣvekaśataparyanteṣu kevaleṣu kāratnipradeśeṣu ca yathākāmaṃ guṇavikārā bhavantyeveti pūrvameva pratipāditam /
tatra pakṣapuccharahitānāṃ praugacidādīnāṃ khākāśaśrutivedaikāmityādinā ānītasya puruṣasya viṃśatiśatatamo bhāgo 'ṅguliḥ kalpyā /
tasyāśvatustriṃśo bhāgastilaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The <s>karaṇī</s> of the seven-fold [unit] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> is three hundred and twenty-eight-and-a-half <s>aṅgulis</s> and twelve <s>tilas</s>.
Its double <s>karaṇī</s> is four hundred sixty-four-and-three-quarters <s>aṅgulis</s> — this is the <s>karaṇī</s> of the ground-area of twice that [measure], which is fifteen <s>puruṣas</s>, made square.
The side-measure (<s>pārśvamānī</s>) of the <s>prauga</s> is four <s>puruṣas</s>, thirty-nine <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-one <s>tilas</s>.
Since [the expression] 'as large as the fire-altar' alone suffices, the mention of 'with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>' is because that particular reading belongs to another <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic school) and requires effort [to establish]. It has already been demonstrated that among the one-fold and other [altars] up to the one-hundred-and-one-fold, qualitative modifications occur at will in those [measured] with <s>karaṇī-prādeśas</s> alone.
In that case, for the <s>praugacit</s> and others which lack wings and tail, the <s>aṅguli</s> should be reckoned as the one-two-thousandth part of the <s>puruṣa</s> obtained by [the method of] 'sky, space, hearing, <s>Veda</s>, one' etc.
Its thirty-third part is a <s>tila</s>.

children.text:
sā praugaṃ nityā prakṛtyeva /
sā bhūmirevaṃ kṛte praugaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
That [altar] is naturally a <s>prauga</s> by its very construction.
When the ground is thus prepared, it becomes a <s>prauga</s>.
The brick-types — as stated: 'the brick-type [is determined] by the twelfth and thirteenth [parts]' and so forth.
The <s>prauga</s> [bricks] — one should make:

children.text:
dvādaśyāḥ pārśve tricatvāriṃśadaṅgule sapādadaśītalayukte navatilonaṃ navatriṃśadaṅgulamaparam /
teṣāmardhaiḥ pādyāḥ /
tṛtīyairnavamyaḥ /
trayodaśyāstu catvāriṃśadaṅgule tilone pārśve tripādonaṣāṭtriṃśadaṅgulamaparam /
eteṣāmardhaiḥ pādyāḥ /
tṛtīyaiś ca navamyaḥ /
upādāne prathame prastāre catuśvatvāriṃśacchatena dvādaśībhirudīcyo dvādaśa rītayaḥ /
madhyamarīticatuṣṭaye madhyo ṣoḍaśoddhṛtya catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ pādyāḥ /
praugamukhyāmud dhṛtya nava navamyaḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasmin prastāre trayodaśībiḥ navaṣaṣṭiśatena trayodaśa rītayaḥ /
tāsu daśamyāṃ sapteṣṭakā uddhṛtya viṃśatiḥ pādyāḥ /
aṣṭādaśanavamyaś ca nidheyāḥ /
evaṃ dviśataḥ /
children.translated_text:
Of the twelfth-part [bricks], the two sides are forty-three <s>aṅgulis</s> joined with a quarter-and-ten <s>tilas</s>; the other [side] is thirty-nine <s>aṅgulis</s> less nine <s>tilas</s>.
With halves of these, the quarter-[bricks].
With thirds, the ninth-part [bricks].
Of the thirteenth-part [bricks], the two sides are forty <s>aṅgulis</s> less one <s>tila</s>; the other [side] is thirty-six <s>aṅgulis</s> less three-quarters.
With halves of these, the quarter-[bricks].
And with thirds, the ninth-part [bricks].
In the placement, in the first layer, with one hundred and forty-four twelfth-part [bricks], twelve northward rows.
In the middle four rows, having removed sixteen from the center, sixty-four quarter-[bricks].
At the <s>prauga</s>-face, having removed [some], nine ninth-part [bricks].
This is the layer of two hundred.
In the other layer, with one hundred and sixty-nine thirteenth-part [bricks], thirteen rows.
In the tenth [row], having removed seven bricks, twenty quarter-[bricks].
And eighteen ninth-part [bricks] should be placed.
Thus the layer of two hundred.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: ubhayayaḥ praugaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta prajātān bhrātṛvyān nudeya pratijaniṣyamāṇān iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_12.7 ||
children.translated_text: One should pile the <s>prauga</s> on both sides — one who desires to drive away rivals both born and yet to be born — thus it is known. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.7 ||

children.text: ubhayataḥśakaṭameva cinvīta yaḥ kāmayetotpannānutpatsyamānāṃś ca śatrūn bādheyeti /
children.translated_text: One should pile the cart-[shaped altar] on both sides — one who desires to subdue enemies both existing and yet to arise.
As in a cart with reversed face — || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.8 ||

children.text: tāvad eva tīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya pūrvāparayoḥ karaṇyor ardhāt tāvati dakṣiṇottarayor nipātayet | sā nityobhabhayataḥ praugam || ĀpŚus_12.9 ||
children.translated_text: Having laid out a rectangle of the same length, from the midpoint of the eastern and western sides, one should drop [lines] of the same [length] to the south and north sides. That is the permanent double-<s>prauga</s>. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.9 ||

children.text: praugacitoktīḥ (-ktaṃ) | ubhayataḥ praugā iṣṭakāḥ kārayet || ĀpŚus_12.10 ||
children.translated_text: As stated for the <s>praugacit</s>; one should make bricks that are <s>prauga</s>-shaped on both sides. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 12.10 ||

children.text:
tāvadeva saptādhesya dviguṇam /
iha tu dīrghacaturaśrasya dviguṇāyāmapramāṇavistāraḥ /
puruṣadvayena tribiraradnibhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiraṅgulaiḥ sārdhaikaviṃśatyā tilaiḥ mitā tiryaṅmānīmadhye ca śaṅkūnnihatya śaṅkuṣu rajjvā veṣṭayitvā bāhyatastyajet /
saptaṣaśaṣṭhiśatatrayamaṅgulīnāṃ caturdaśabhistilaiḥsārdhayīṣāprāmāṇyam /
āsāṃ dvādaśena karaṇāni kārayet /
praugacitobhayataḥ praugeṣṭakāḥ kārayet /
ubhayataḥ praughākārāḥ iṣṭakāḥ pādāśvobhayataḥ praughībhūtāḥ /
cayanavidhiruktaḥ prauge /
tatra ślokaḥ --
children.translated_text:
That same [measure], twice the seven-and-a-half.
But here, the breadth of the oblong rectangle is [equal to] the measure of twice the length.
With two <s>puruṣas</s>, three <s>aratnīs</s>, sixteen-and-a-half <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-one <s>tilas</s>, the transverse measure is measured; and having driven stakes at the middle, wrapping the cord around the stakes, one should extend it outward.
Three hundred and sixty-seven <s>aṅgulis</s> and fourteen <s>tilas</s> — that is the measure of the shaft (<s>īṣā</s>).
One should make the brick-types by the twelfth [part] of these.
For the <s>praugacit</s>, one should make <s>prauga</s>-shaped bricks on both sides.
Bricks that are <s>prauga</s>-shaped on both sides, and the quarter-[bricks] too are <s>prauga</s>-shaped on both sides.
The method of piling is as stated for the <s>prauga</s>.
Therein, the verse —
With three-times-seven <s>tilas</s>, joined with three hundred and twenty-eight,
the wise know the transverse measure of the northern <s>prauga</s> fire-altar. //
In the oblong rectangle of twice the length of the transverse [measure] of the fire-altar,
having driven stakes at the midpoints and at the four brick-type [divisions] — //
joining the cord at the stakes, one should discard the shoulder-portions at the two hip-corners.
The remainder is exactly seven-and-a-half, as in the reversed cart. //
With fourteen <s>tilas</s> joined with three hundred and sixty-seven,
this is determined as the shaft-measure of the northern <s>prauga</s>. //
By the twelfth part of the shaft, and likewise by [its] thirteenth part,
one should make <s>prauga</s>-shaped [bricks] on both sides, with their quarter-[bricks], here. //
<s>Karavindīya</s> commentary
On both sides — [the sūtra text continues]:

children.text:
ubhayataḥ praugaṃ -- ubhayataḥ śakaṭamukhaṃ /
prajātān śatrūna praṇudeyaṃ janiṣyamāṇāṃś ca praṇudeyaṃ yathā na jāyante tathā karavāṇītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
A <s>prauga</s> on both sides — a cart-face on both sides.
One should drive away existing enemies and drive away those yet to be born, meaning 'I shall act so that they are not born.'
He explains the scriptural passage —
As in — as stated:

children.text: vimukhe -- nānāmukhaghe śakaṭe yathā pṛṣṭhai saṃhite tiṣṭhete tādṛgākāramubhayatra praugaṃ tathā cinvītetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a reversed — a cart with faces in different directions, just as [two] backs joined together stand, one should pile the <s>prauga</s> of such a shape on both sides — this is the meaning.

children.text: tāvadeva pūrvoktaṃ sāratniprādeśaś ca saptavidhasya dviyuṇaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya tiryaṅnānīpārśvamānīnāṃ madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya pūrvasmācchaṅkoḥ dakṣiṇaṃ śaṅkuṃ pratyakṣṇayā liśeddakṣiṇataḥ paścimaṃ paścimataḥ uttaramuttarataḥ pūrvaṃ, evaṃ liśedubhayataḥ praugākṛtikṣetraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: That same [measure] as previously stated — the seven-fold [unit] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>, having laid out an oblong rectangle twice [as long], and having driven a stake at the middle of the transverse and side measures, one should draw a line diagonally from the [first] stake to the southern stake on the south side, to the western [stake] on the west side, to the northern [stake] on the north side, [and] to the eastern [stake]. Drawing thus, the ground-area becomes a <s>prauga</s>-shaped field on both sides.

children.text: vistāradviguṇāyāmaṃ dīrghaṃ pañcapuruṣāḥ saptadaśāṅgulāsvāyāmaḥ, dvau puruṣāvaṣṭaṣaṣṭiraṅgulaya ekaviṃśatitilāś ca tiryaṅbhānī dīrghacaturaśrasya //
children.translated_text: The oblong [rectangle] with length twice the breadth — five <s>puruṣas</s> and seventeen <s>aṅgulis</s> in length; two <s>puruṣas</s>, sixty-eight <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-one <s>tilas</s> as the transverse measure of the oblong rectangle. //
On both sides — [the sūtra text continues]:

children.text:
karaṇāni cayanavidhiś ca praugavat /
viśeṣastūbhayataḥ praugāḥ iṣṭakāḥ /
trayaḥ puruṣāḥsapta cāṅgulayaḥ saptadaśa tilāś ca eṣāṃ pramāṇam /
asya dvādaśo bhāgastriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ pañcaviṃśatitilāś ca /
trayodaśo bhāgo 'ṣṭāviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ tribhāgonā nava tilāś ca /
śatadvayaṃ aṣṭāviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ ekaviṃśatitilāśvobhayataḥ praugasya tiryaṅbhānī /
tasyā dvādaśabhāgena trayodaśabhāgena parimitaṃ karaṇaṃ yathā bhavati tathā bhavet karaṇam /

children.translated_text: The half-bricks of the twelfth-part and thirteenth-part [types] are equal in length to [those types] and half their breadth.
The quarter-bricks are half in both length and breadth.

children.text: prathame prastāre yāḥpādā upahitāḥ te dvitīye tadanyatropadheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the first layer, the quarter-[bricks] that are placed should be placed elsewhere in the second [layer].
In the twelfth-part brick series, four half-bricks; in the thirteenth-part series, two. //

The brick-types and method of piling are as for the [single] <s>prauga</s>.
The distinction is: the bricks are <s>prauga</s>-shaped on both sides.
Three <s>puruṣas</s>, seven <s>aṅgulis</s>, and seventeen <s>tilas</s> — this is their measure.
Its twelfth part is thirty <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.
The thirteenth part is twenty-eight <s>aṅgulis</s> and nine <s>tilas</s> less one-third.
Two hundred, twenty-eight <s>aṅgulis</s>, and twenty-one <s>tilas</s> — this is the transverse measure of the double-<s>prauga</s>.
The brick-type should be made such that [it fits] the measurement by the twelfth and thirteenth parts of that.
<s>Sundararājīya</s> commentary

children.translated_text:
Having laid out an oblong rectangle with length twice the breadth of the fire-altar area.
Three hundred and twenty-eight-and-a-half <s>aṅgulis</s> and twenty-two <s>tilas</s> is the transverse measure.
The side-measure is twice that.
Having thus laid out, from the midpoints of the eastern and western sides, one should drop [lines] to the midpoints of the southern and northern [sides].
One should cut off the exterior portions.
As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:
The bricks etc. are as stated for the one-fold [altar].

Of the thirteenth-part [bricks], four planks of twenty-eight-and-a-quarter <s>aṅgulis</s> — that is one diagonal-cord.

children.translated_text: Twelve fourth-part brick fields constitute a tenth of the [altar area] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s>. The transverse measure is sixty <s>aṅgulas</s>; its <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (square root of 2 times) is the lateral measure. With a cord of its diagonal, when a square is made, it becomes twelve fourth-part brick fields. That is the measure of the <s>tsaru</s> (handle). And tripled, that gives the <s>droṇa</s> (trough).

children.text:
tasya pucchena nirhāra uktaḥ -- pucchenaiva mānamārgo vyākhyātaḥ /
tasya karaṇyā dvādaśeṣṭakāḥ kārayot tasyeti droṇaḥ parāmṛśyate natsaruḥ sa ca trikoṇa samadeśena caturbhāgīyenetyarthaḥ /
adhyardhāḥ pādeṣṭekāś ca atra vipratipannā yājñikāḥ akṣṇayā pādamicchanti kecit /
keciddīrghapadapādamardheṣṭakāḥ kartavyāḥ tābhirvinā saṃkhyāpūraṇasyāśakyatvāt /
vktamuktaṃ śulbāntare "ardheṣṭakāsveti /
ihāpi cakārādardheṣṭakāśceti /
karaṇāni ca ṣṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ tilonamekaṃ karaṇañca; ekato 'dhyardhaṃ dvitīyaṃ; prathamakaraṇamubhayato 'bhṇayā caturdhā dīrghaṃ,' tena pādānāṃ tṛtīyaṃ karaṇaṃ, tṛtīyenaiva karaṇena dīrgheṇa vār'dheṣṭakānāṃ karaṇaṃ caturtham /
children.translated_text: Its extraction by the tail has been stated — the method of measurement is explained by the tail-region itself. Of that, by its <s>karaṇī</s> (constructive measure), one should have twelve bricks made. 'Of that' refers to the <s>droṇa</s>, not the <s>tsaru</s>. And the <s>tsaru</s> is triangular — with an equal region of fourth-part [measure] — this is the meaning. 'One-and-a-half' and '<s>pāda</s>-bricks also' — here the ritualists differ. Some wish the <s>pāda</s> to be diagonal. Some [say] oblong long-<s>pada</s>-<s>pādas</s> — half-bricks must be made, since without them it is impossible to complete the count. It has been stated in another <s>Śulba</s> [text]: 'with half-bricks.' Here too, from the word 'ca' (also), half-bricks [are included]. And the moulds: one <s>karaṇa</s> (mould) of thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> less one <s>tilā</s>; the second, one-and-a-half on one side; the first mould [divided] diagonally into four lengthwise — that gives the third mould for the <s>pādas</s>; and by the third mould itself [cut] lengthwise, the fourth mould for half-bricks.

children.text: upadhāne 'dhyardhāḥ purastāt pratīcīr ātmany upadadhāti | tsarvarge śroṇyoś ca prācīḥ || ĀpŚus_13.12 ||
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, one-and-a-half [bricks], eastward at the front, one lays in the body; at the handle-section and at the haunches, [facing] east. || ĀpŚus 13.12 ||
One should cover the entire fire [altar] with square [bricks]. || ĀpŚus 13.13 ||
One should complete the count with <s>pāda</s>-bricks. || ĀpŚus 13.14 ||

children.text: aparasmin prastāre 'dhyardhā dakṣiṇata udīcīr ātmany upadadhāty uttarataś ca dakṣiṇās tsarupārśvayor dakṣiṇā utīcīś ca || ĀpŚus_13.15 ||
children.translated_text: In the other (second) layer, one-and-a-half [bricks] from the south, northward, one lays in the body; and from the north, southward; at the sides of the handle, southward and northward. || ĀpŚus 13.15 ||
One should cover the entire fire [altar] with square [bricks]. || ĀpŚus 13.16 ||
One should complete the count with <s>pāda</s>-bricks. || ĀpŚus 13.17 ||
One should pile in alternation for as many layers as one wishes to make. || ĀpŚus 13.18 ||
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter.

children.text:
upādhāne yathāsūtramadhyardhā upadhāya pūrvārdhe saptadaśeṣṭakā akṣṇayā chindyāt dvāvar dhau /
yadi dīrghāśvet pādā uttarasyāṃ rītyāṃ nevaṣṭakāḥ chindyāt yathā prācīḥ prapādāḥ yathā dakṣiṇasyāmaṣṭau tathaiva prācīrekādvidhā /
tatra tathaiva pūrṇaḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasminprastāre paścādātmanyaṣṭādaśeṣṭakāḥ karaṇe chindyāt /
dve dve iṣṭake dvidhākaraṇenaiva /
yadi dīrghāḥ pādāḥ pūrvasyāṃ rītyāṃ naveṣṭakā bhindyāt /
yathā vā udīcyāḥśroṇyā dve dvetsaroḥ paścādevāgrataḥ pāśamadhyer'dhāḥ pādāśvodīcyaḥ /
evaṃ prastāro dviśataḥ /
tatra ślokā bhavanti ----
children.translated_text: At the time of laying, having laid the one-and-a-half [bricks] according to the <s>sūtra</s>, in the front half, seventeen bricks should be cut diagonally — two half-bricks. If the <s>pādas</s> are oblong, in the northern course nine bricks should be cut such that [they are] eastward; the front <s>pādas</s>, just as eight in the southern [course], so too the eastward one is of two types. There likewise the layer is complete. In the other (second) layer, at the back of the body, eighteen bricks should be cut in the mould. Two-two bricks [cut] by the bisecting mould itself. If the <s>pādas</s> are oblong, in the front course, nine bricks should be cut. Or, as at the northern haunch, two-two [bricks] at the <s>tsaru</s>; behind at the front, at the side-middle, one-and-a-half [bricks], <s>pādas</s> [facing] north. Thus the layer [totals] two hundred. On this, verses:
Measured by three [parts] less one <s>tilā</s>, by four, and by a hundred —
the measure of the <s>droṇa's</s> (trough's) <s>tsaru</s> (handle) is exactly triple of that.

children.text: pādā ardhāś ca bhedāsyuḥ karaṇāni vibhāvasau /
children.translated_text: <s>Pādas</s> and halves should be the [brick] types; consider the moulds well

children.text: droṇākhye tu smaśāne ca caturaśre havirbhuji //
children.translated_text: in the <s>droṇa</s>-named square fire-altar and in the cremation ground [altar].

children.text: prastāre prathame pādā yatra syustatra nottare /
children.translated_text: Where <s>pādas</s> are in the first layer, there they should not be in the next;
two half-bricks in the first layer, four in the upper layer.
And having laid in the upper layer beginning with the one-and-a-half [type],

children.text: adhyardhā yatra tatra syuḥ pādā dīrghā yadi tvatha //
children.translated_text: wherever one-and-a-half [bricks] are, there should be <s>pādas</s> if they are oblong.
In the first layer [they should face] east; in the upper layer, north;
on both sides, <s>pāda</s>-and-one-and-a-half [bricks] — seven courses in the upper [layer].
Thus.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
The entire... made.

children.text:
sarvasyāgnikṣetrasya daśamauśaḥtsaruḥ /
chāndasonapuṃsakaliṃṅganirdeśaḥ /
sāratnipradeśasya daśamobhāgo dvādaśabhāgīyākṣetram /
tasyatsarornirhāraḥ samudāyāt pṛthak karaṇaṃ pucchena pucchapradeśena bhavet /
children.translated_text: The extraction of its <s>tsaru</s> — making it separately from the aggregate — should be done by the tail, by the tail-region.
The stated extraction is: 'one wishing to extract a square from a square' — thus.
The <s>karaṇī</s> (constructive measure) of the square body is three hundred and eleven <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-six <s>tilās</s>.
And the <s>tsaru</s> is one hundred and three <s>aṅgulas</s> plus, and thirty-one <s>tilās</s>.

A tenth part of the entire fire-field is the <s>tsaru</s> (handle). The Vedic designation is in the neuter gender. A tenth part of [the altar] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> is the twelve-part field.

children.text: karaṇyaḥ kā tasya -- ka ś ca
children.translated_text: What are the <s>karaṇīs</s> (constructive measures) of that — and what else —
The <s>karaṇī</s> of the <s>droṇa</s> is ten [times], twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> less one <s>tilā</s>.

children.text: dvādaśabhīgīyānāṃ karaṇī ekataḥṣaḍviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ tilonāḥ anyatraikonacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ adhyardhatilonāḥ dvitīyaṃ karaṇaṃ pādeṣṭakā dvādaśabhāgīyānāmeva /
children.translated_text: The <s>karaṇī</s> of the twelve-part [bricks] is on one side twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> less one <s>tilā</s>; on the other, thirty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> less one-and-a-half <s>tilās</s> — the second mould. The <s>pāda</s>-brick is of the twelve-part [type] only.
From the word 'ca' (also), half-bricks too.

children.text: tābhirvināsaṅkhyāpūraṇāśakteḥ uktañca śulbāntare pādeṣṭakā ardheṣṭakāś ceti prathamakaraṇamakṣṇayā bhindyāt //
children.translated_text: Because without them the count cannot be completed. And it has been stated in another <s>Śulba</s> [text]: '<s>pāda</s>-bricks and half-bricks.' The first mould should be cut diagonally.
The <s>pāda</s>-brick [has the same] lateral measure as the twelve-part or [is obtained from it].
That is the fourth [mould].
The transverse measure is the <s>pāda</s>-brick.
'At the time of laying, eastward' —
In the body, in the front part, twelve bricks, westward-facing, one lays.
At the handle-section, four.
At the haunches, four each.
Thus twenty-four one-and-a-half [bricks].
The entire... should [cover].

children.text:
śiṣṭamagnikṣetraṃ dvādaśabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet pucche caturiṣṭake dve rītyau dvayoḥ purastār pucchāpya ya viśayarūpaikāḥ caturiṣṭakāś ca /
tasyāḥ purastāddiśyekā /
atmani dvādaśeṣṭakāḥ udīcyonavarītayaḥ /
ekaviṃśati śataṃ caturaśrāḥ /
caturviṃśatiradhyardhāḥ /
uttarasminpārśva navacaturaśrā udhṛtya ṣaṭtriṃśataṃ dīrghāḥ pādāḥ pratīcīrupadadhyāt /

children.translated_text: And on the southern side, removing nine, thirty-eight <s>pādas</s>.

children.text: ṣūrvasyāṃ diśi dvādhaśabhāgīyānāmupāntye uddhṛtyadveddve cārde upadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: In the eastern direction, at the edge of the twelve-part [bricks], removing two-two, one should place their halves.

children.text: akṣṇayāpādāśvet pūrvārdhe 'ṣṭādaśacaturaśrā udhṛtyadvisaptatipādāḥ dve iṣṭake uddhṛtya dve dve cārdhe /
children.translated_text: If the <s>pādas</s> are diagonal, in the front half, removing eighteen square [bricks], seventy-two <s>pādas</s>; removing two bricks, two-two halves [are placed].
This layer [totals] two hundred.

The remaining fire-field should be covered with twelve-part [bricks]. In the tail, four bricks [make] two courses at the front of the tail; also four single-type bricks. In front of those, one facing east. In the body, twelve bricks [make] nine courses going north. One hundred and twenty-one square [bricks]. Twenty-four one-and-a-half [bricks]. On the northern side, removing nine square [bricks], thirty-six oblong <s>pādas</s> should be placed facing west.
In the other [layer]... and northward.
In the body, twelve from the south.
Likewise from the north.
At the two sides of the tail, four each.
Eastward courses, thirty-two.
The entire... should cover.

children.text:
pucche catasraścaturaśrā ātmani dvādaśeṣṭakāḥ prācyonavarītayaḥ /
tādvādaśaśatam /
paścādātmani /
daśacaturaśrā uddhṛtya dvātriṃśatamakṣṇayāpādā upadadhyāt /
catasraśvārvāḥ dīrghāśvet pādāḥ pūrvasyāṃ rītyāṃ naveṣṭakā uddhṛtya ṣaṭatriṃśataṃ pādā utīcya upadadhyāt /
paścādātmanyaṣṭādaśa caturaśrāḥ navapādā utīcīrupadhāya tāsāṃ purastādabhito dvipādāḥ saptārdhāḥ upadhāyatāsāṃ purastādaṣṭādaśārdā upadhāyatāsāṃ purastānnavapādā upadadhyāt /
dviśata eṣaprastāraḥ /
children.translated_text: In the tail, four square [bricks]; in the body, twelve bricks [make] nine courses going east. That is one hundred and twelve. Behind in the body: removing ten square [bricks], thirty-two diagonal <s>pādas</s> should be placed. And four half-bricks. If the <s>pādas</s> are oblong, in the front course, removing nine bricks, thirty-six <s>pādas</s> should be placed facing north. Behind in the body, eighteen square [bricks], nine <s>pādas</s> facing north; having laid next to those, on both sides, two-<s>pāda</s> [bricks]; having laid seven halves next to those; having laid eighteen halves in front of those; in front of those, nine <s>pādas</s> should be placed. This layer [totals] two hundred.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Of the entire... stated.

children.text: pucchamivātmano vahirbhūtaṃ paścānminuyādityarthaḥ ta6 caturaśradroṇacit dvādhaśatriśatāṅgulenāṣṭhatilonena samacaturaśraḥ tasya paścānmadhyadeśe karaṇītṛtīyenatsarusamacaturaśram /
children.translated_text: Just as the tail extends outward from the body to the west, so one should measure — this is the meaning. That square <s>droṇaciti</s> (trough-altar) has a side of twelve [times] thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> less eight <s>tilās</s> as an equal square. At its western middle, a <s>tsaru</s> (handle) equal-square of a third of the <s>karaṇī</s> [measure].
'Its <s>karaṇīs</s>, one should have made' —
By the body-<s>karaṇī</s>, twelve [-fold], twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> less one <s>tilā</s>, equal-squares.

children.text:
adhyardhāḥ -- pādeṣṭakāś ca
tṛtīyena ca navamyaḥ pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: 'One-and-a-half... and <s>pāda</s>-bricks.' And the ninths, as before, by the third [mould].
'At the time of laying... one lays' —
With twelve-[part bricks], a northward course.
'At the handle-section... eastward' —

children.text:
tsarvargre catasro 'dhyardhāḥ, śroṇyaś ca catasraścatasraḥ /
evaṃ dvādaśa /
children.translated_text: At the handle-section, four one-and-a-half [bricks]; and at the haunches, four each. Thus twelve.
'The entire fire... should cover' —
When thus covered with twelve-[part bricks], one hundred and forty-eight results.
'With <s>pāda</s>-bricks... should complete' —

children.text:
ātmani prācyo dvādaśarītayaḥ /
tatra dadiṇasyāṃ paścāddvayaṃ hitvā pūrvāstisro navamya udīcyaḥ /
tato dvādaśa pādyāḥ /
tatastisro navamyaḥ /
tataḥ prākapādyā dvādaśa /

children.translated_text: Then three ninths, going north.
Then twelve and one-and-a-half [bricks facing] east.
Thus indeed the twelve-[brick] course.
Thus the layer [totals] two hundred.

In the body, twelve courses going east. There, in the southern [section], leaving two behind, the front three [are] ninths going north. Then twelve <s>pāda</s>-[bricks]. Then three ninths. Then twelve east-facing <s>pādas</s>.
'In the other [layer]... and northward.' —

children.text:
dvādaśa dvādaśa /
dakṣiṇeti dvitīyāvahuvacanasvīkāraḥ /
tsarupārśvayordakṣiṇā udīcīścatasraścatasraḥ /
children.translated_text: Twelve by twelve. 'Southward' — accepting the second [alternative with] plural. At the two sides of the <s>tsaru</s>, southward and northward, four each.
'The entire fire... should cover' —
One hundred and forty-four results.
'With <s>pāda</s>-bricks... should complete' —

children.text:
ātmanyudīcyo dvādaśa rītayaḥ /
atrāparasyāṃ dakṣiṇādhyardhāyā udaktisro navamyaḥ prācyaḥ /
tato 'ṣṭau pādyāḥ /
tatastisro navamyaḥ /
tato dvādaśī tatastisro navamyaḥ /
tato 'ṣṭau pādyāḥ tatastisro navamyaḥ /
tatodvādaśī /
tatastisro navamyaḥ /
tato 'dhyardhā /
evaṃ pūrvā rītiḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
children.translated_text: In the body, twelve courses going north. Here, of the western [section], to the north of the southern one-and-a-half [brick], three ninths facing east. Then eight <s>pāda</s>-[bricks]. Then three ninths. Then twelve-[part]. Then three ninths. Then eight <s>pāda</s>-[bricks]. Then three ninths. Then twelve-[part]. Then three ninths. Then one-and-a-half. Thus the front course. The layer [totals] two hundred.
'In alternation... should wish' —
Now the method of the circular <s>droṇaciti</s> (trough-altar) will be stated.

children.text:
ṣaṭsaptatiśatā ṅgulaśtrayastilono veṇurubhayatāśchidraḥ /
madhyeśaṅkuṃ nihatya tasmin veṇośchidraṃ pratimucya chidrāntareṇa parimaṇlaṃ parilikhet /
madhyaśaṅkoḥ paścādaṣṭaṣaṣṭiśatāṅgule satiladvaye śaṅkuḥ /
tasya paścātsaruḥ /
samacaraśraṃ tiladvayonacatuḥśatāṅgulaṃ kuryāt /
maṇḍalamadhyaśaṅkoḥ paścāccatuḥśatāṅgule tilatrayone śaṅkaṃ nihatya tasmin veṇochidraṃ pratimucyānyena cchidreṇatsaruṇo dakṣiṇāparakoṇādārabhya uttarāparakoṇādālikhet, yathātsarvagraṃ pradhyākāraṃ bhavati /
maṇḍalabhramaṇetsarupurvānter'dhe yāvaddhriyate tāvatpaścādāgacchati /
tato maṇjalamadhye pūrvavaccaturaśraṃ navacatvāriṃśad dviśatāṅgulamaṣṭatilonamavadadhyāt /
tasya karaṇyā dvādaśeneṣṭakāḥ ekaviṃśatyaṅgulā navītalonāḥ caturaśramadhye catuśvatvāriṃśacchatamiṣṭakāḥśerate /
tato dīrghamekaṃ karaṇam /
tasya tilonaṣaḍviṃśatyahgulā tilaśvī /
catustriṃśakaṃ dvāviṃśatitilaṃ pārśvam /
tāḥ pradhimūlamadhye catasraścatasro nidheyāḥ pūrvāparayoḥ prāgāyatā dakṣiṇottarayorudagāyatāḥ /
pradhiśeṣeṣu saptasapteṣṭakāḥ /
catasṛṇāṃ mukheṣu tisraḥ /
pārśvayordvedve iti tāsāṃ catvari karaṇāni /
