trikoṇamādyaṃ, tasya ṣaṭtilonamaṣṭāviṃśatyaṅgulamekaṃ phalakaṃ /
ṣaṭtriṃśakam saptatilonaṃ dvitīyam /
tryaṃśonitaṃ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadaṅgulaṃ tṛtīyaṃ karṇarūpaṃ, taddhanuriva takṣet, yathādhyardhāṅguliḥśaro bhavet /
dvidīyasya ṣaṭtilonamaṣṭāviṃśakamekaṃ tilyakphalakam /
tryaṃśonacatuśvatvāriṃśadaṅgulamanyat /
saptatilaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśakamekaṃ pārśvam /
sāṣṭādaśatilaṃ navatriṃśakaṃ pārśvāntaram /
taddhanuriva takṣet, yathā sa catustilāṅguliḥśaraḥ /
tṛtīyasya satilaṃ navakamekaṃ tiryakphalakamekam /
satilaṃ ṣoḍaśāhgulamanyat /
dvādaśatilonaṃ pañcatriṃśadaṅgulamekaṃ pārśvaṃ dvādaśatilayuktaṃ pañcatriṃśakaṃ pārśvāntaram, taddhanuriva takṣet /
triṃśattilāḥśaraḥ /
caturthasya satile ṣoḍaśike tiraśvayau pārśve ca daśatilonepañcatriṃśake /
ephaṃ pārśvaṃ dhanuriva takṣet /
ekānnatriṃśattilāḥśaraḥ /
eṣā iṣṭakā pradhimadhye sthāpyā, abhitastisrastisraḥ pūrvoktāḥ kramotkrameṇa /
evaṃ maṇḍalakṣetre aṣṭāśītiśatamiṣṭakā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: A bamboo reed of one hundred and seventy-six <s>aṅgulas</s>, diminished by three <s>tilas</s>, with holes at both ends. Having fixed a peg at the center and inserting the bamboo's hole onto it, one should draw a circle through the other hole. A peg [is placed] at one hundred and sixty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> with two <s>tilas</s>, west of the central peg. Behind that is the handle (<s>tsaru</s>). One should make an equal square of four hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by two <s>tilas</s>. Having fixed a peg at four hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> with three <s>tilas</s> west of the circle's central peg, and inserting the bamboo's hole onto it, with the other hole, starting from the south-western corner of the handle, one should draw up to the north-western corner, so that the handle-end becomes arch-shaped. In the revolution of the circle, whatever [area] is taken away from the front half of the handle, that much comes [back] behind. Then in the middle of the circle, as before, one should place a square of two hundred and forty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by eight <s>tilas</s>. With its <s>karaṇī</s> (side-measure), by twelve — bricks of twenty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by nine <s>tilas</s>; one hundred and forty-four bricks fit in the square area. Then one long mold (<s>karaṇa</s>). Its [length is] twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a <s>tila</s>, with a <s>tila</s>-width. The side is thirty-four [<s>aṅgulas</s>] with twenty-two <s>tilas</s>. These should be placed four by four at the base of the rim (<s>pradhi</s>), on the east-west [sides] extending eastward, on the south-north [sides] extending northward. In the remaining rim sections, seven bricks each. At the faces of the four [corner-bricks], three each. On the sides, two each — thus four molds for those. The first is triangular; its one plank is twenty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by six <s>tilas</s>. The second is thirty-six [<s>aṅgulas</s>], diminished by seven <s>tilas</s>. The third is forty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by one-third, in the form of a hypotenuse — one should carve it like a bow, so that the arrow (<s>śara</s>) is one and a half <s>aṅgulas</s>. Of the second [type]: one oblique plank of twenty-eight [<s>aṅgulas</s>] diminished by six <s>tilas</s>. Another of forty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by one-third. One side of thirty-six [<s>aṅgulas</s>] with seven <s>tilas</s>. The inner side is thirty-nine [<s>aṅgulas</s>] with eighteen <s>tilas</s>. One should carve that like a bow, so that the arrow is four <s>tilas</s> of an <s>aṅgula</s>. Of the third [type]: one oblique plank of nine [<s>aṅgulas</s>] with a <s>tila</s>. Another of sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with a <s>tila</s>. One side of thirty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by twelve <s>tilas</s>; the inner side of thirty-five [<s>aṅgulas</s>] joined with twelve <s>tilas</s> — one should carve that like a bow. The arrow is thirty <s>tilas</s>. Of the fourth [type]: the two oblique [planks] are sixteen [<s>aṅgulas</s>] with a <s>tila</s>; the sides are thirty-five [<s>aṅgulas</s>] diminished by ten <s>tilas</s>. One side should be carved like a bow. The arrow is twenty-nine <s>tilas</s>. This brick is to be placed in the middle of the rim; on both sides, three and three of the previously described [bricks], in order and reverse order. Thus in the circular field there are one hundred and eighty-eight bricks.

children.text:
tato 'parapradhermadhyāstisra uddhṛtyatsarvagre nidadhyāt /
tsaruśeṣe dvādaśa dīrgheṣṭakāḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
evamevāparaḥ prastāraḥ /
caturaśrasraktayastu mahādikṣu bhavanti /
tsaruṇastvanye dve karaṇe /
tatraikasya tilone ṣaḍviṃśatyaṅgule tilyakphalake /
catvāriṃśadaṅgule tryaṃśe pārśvai /
ekākṣṇayārajhjustricatvāriṃśadaṅgulā ṣaṭtilayuktā /
anyā tvekapañcāśadahgulā sadaśatilā /
ekaṃ pārśvaphalakaṃ dhanuriva takṣet /
sa catustilāṅguliḥśaraḥ /
anyadapi pārśvamevameva /
antaśvāpaṃ tu bhavati yathaivamiṣṭakārūpaṃ, etā iṣṭakāḥtsarupārśvayoścatasraścatasra udagāyatāḥ /
athānyattilonaṣaḍviṃśakaṃ samacaturaśraṃ tasyaikaṃ tilyakphalaṃ dhanuriva takṣet yathā ṣoḍaśatilāḥśaro bhavati /
evamevānyattiryakphalakaṃ. antaśvāvīṃ tu bhavati /
yathaivamiṣṭakāḥtsarumadhye etāścatasraḥ prastāro dviśataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, from the middle of the far rim, having removed three [bricks], one should place [them] at the handle-end. In the remaining handle, twelve long bricks. The layer is two hundred. The other layer is likewise. But the square edges (<s>srakti</s>) are at the cardinal directions. For the handle, there are two other molds. Of one: the oblique planks are twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a <s>tila</s>. The sides are forty <s>aṅgulas</s> with one-third. One diagonal is forty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> joined with six <s>tilas</s>. The other is fifty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> with ten <s>tilas</s>. One side-plank should be carved like a bow. Its arrow is four <s>tilas</s> of an <s>aṅgula</s>. The other side likewise. And the inner curve (<s>āpa</s>) is such that the brick-form [matches]. These bricks [are placed] four by four on the sides of the handle, extending northward. Now another: a square of twenty-six [<s>aṅgulas</s>] diminished by a <s>tila</s>; one oblique surface of it should be carved like a bow, so that the arrow is sixteen <s>tilas</s>. The other oblique surface likewise; and the inner curve is such [as needed]. These four bricks [go] in the middle of the handle — the layer is two hundred.
One should pile in alternation, for as many layers as one wishes. ||
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: samūhyaṃ cinvīta paśukāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires cattle should pile the heaped [altar] (<s>samūhya</s>)' — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.1 ||
He places the bricks by heaping together. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.2 ||

children.text: dikṣu cātvālā bhavanti | tebhyaḥ puraṣimabhyudūhatīti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.3 ||
children.translated_text: There are pits (<s>cātvāla</s>) in the [cardinal] directions; from those he digs up earth — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.3 ||

children.text:
samūhyaṃ ityupadhānaprakāraviśeṣo nākṛtiviśeṣaḥ /
prakṛtāvevāyaṃ vidhiḥ nākṛtivikāreṣu /
agnikṣetrasya parita iṣṭakāḥ sthāpayitvā yathā samūhanaṃ kriyate tathopadadhāti sarvata upādāyopadadhātīti yāvat /
sa evopadhānavidhiḥ -- "pratidiśaṃ cātvālā bhāvanti bahirvedi /
tebhyaśvātvālebhyaḥ purīṣaṃ pāṃśūnabhyudṛhatīti' śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: The term '<s>samūhya</s>' (heaped) refers to a particular mode of placement, not a particular shape. This rule applies to the primary [altar] form, not to shape-modifications. Having placed bricks around the fire-altar field, he places them as the heaping is done — meaning he places [bricks] taking from all sides. That very placement-rule [states]: 'In each direction there are pits (<s>cātvāla</s>) outside the <s>vedī</s>. From those pits he digs up earth (<s>purīṣa</s>) and loose soil' — [thus] the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: paricāyyaṃ cinvīta grāmakāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires a village should pile the circumambient [altar] (<s>paricāyya</s>)' — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.4 ||
This too is a placement-rule.

children.text: madhyamāṃ svayamātṛṇṇāṃ pradakṣiṇamiṣṭakāgaṇaiḥ paricinoti | sa pariyāyyaḥ || ĀpŚus_14.5 ||
children.translated_text: He piles the middle <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s> (self-perforated brick) with groups of bricks going clockwise — that is the circumambient [altar]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.5 ||

children.text:
tṛtīyasyāṃ citau svayamātṛṇṇāmupadhāya iṣṭakāgaṇaiḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tāṃ svayamātṛṇṇāṃ parita upadadhāti /
sa paricāyyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third layer, having placed the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>, he places groups of bricks clockwise around that <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s> on all sides. That is the <s>paricāyya</s> (circumambient [altar]).

children.text: upacāyyaṃ cinvīta grāmakāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires a village should pile the accumulated [altar] (<s>upacāyya</s>)' — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.6 ||
It is explained by the <s>paricāyya</s>. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.7 ||
The alternation is as with the <s>paricāyya</s>, as before.
<s>Karavindīya's</s> commentary.
'Heaped' — [commentary on sūtras up to] 'known from scripture.'

children.text:
samūhanamatra guṇo nākṛtiviśeṣaḥ /
tametamagniṃ cinvīta paśukāmaḥ /
samūhyaśabdasya pravṛttinimittamāha----
children.translated_text: The term 'heaping' here is a quality, not a shape-distinction. One who desires cattle should pile this fire[-altar]. He explains the basis for the application of the word '<s>samūhya</s>' —
'He places by heaping together.'

children.text: samūhanniva upadhāna itti parito 'gnikṣetramiṣṭakāḥsthāpayitvā samūhan -- sampādayanniva yathāyathā bāhyābhyantarā iṣṭakāḥ unnatā bhaveyuḥ tathātathopadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: As if heaping — as if assembling — he places [bricks]. Having placed bricks around the fire-altar field, he should place them so that the outer and inner bricks become progressively raised, as if heaping together.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ -- yathā sarvamagnikṣetramantarata unnataṃ bahirninataṃ bhavati tathā puriṣeṇa kṛtvā tatreṣṭakā upadhāya sapurīṣābiḥ kṣetrapūraṇaṃ kuryāditi //
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: having made the entire fire-altar field raised on the inside and sloping outward with earth-filling (<s>purīṣa</s>), and having placed bricks there, one should complete the field-filling with [layers of] bricks and earth-filling.
'In the directions, pits' — [commentary up to] 'known from scripture.'

children.text:
dikṣu catṛsṛṣvapi cātvālāḥ /
purīṣāṇāṃ vāhulyāccātvālabāhulayaṃ dikṣvekaikaṃ cātvālaṃ śamyayā vimāya kāla eva prakṛtivaduttaravediṣu yavayati /
tebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: In all four directions there are pits (<s>cātvāla</s>). Because of the abundance of earth-fillings, there is abundance of pits — one pit in each direction, measured out with a <s>śamyā</s> (yoke-pin). In due time, as in the primary [rite], he arranges on the subsequent fire-altars. From those —
having taken earth-fillings from all [pits], one should heap up the fire-altar layer.
The measurements, mold-making, and placements are as in the primary [form].
'Circumambient' — [commentary up to] 'known from scripture.'
The circumambulation here is a quality. He explains for the sake of clarification —
'The middle [<s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>]' — [commentary up to] 'circumambient.'

children.text:
tṛtīyasyāṃ citāvākramaṇādisvayamātṛṇṇāntamupadhāya hiraṇyeṣṭakābhirgaṇaiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ svayamātṛṇṇāṃ paricinuyāt /
prākṛtānāṃ sthānānāṃ vādhakaṃ paricayanam /
eṣa dviśataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third layer, having placed [bricks] from the step-bricks (<s>ākramaṇa</s>) up to the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>, with groups of gold bricks (<s>hiraṇyeṣṭakā</s>) going clockwise, one should pile around the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>. The circumambulation overrides the [normal] positions of the primary [altar bricks]. This is a two-hundred [layer].
'Accumulated' — [commentary up to] 'explained.'

children.text:
upacayanamapi guṇaḥ /
upacayanaṃ samīte cayanam /
tānyeva vimānakaraṇopadhānāni /
sarvaṃ paricāyyavat /
ayaṃ bhedaḥ -- ādyasya bahirārabhya svayamātṛṇṇāsamīpe samāptiḥ /
dvitīyasya svayamātṛṇṇāsamīpa ārabhya vahiḥsamāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: The accumulation too is a quality. Accumulation means piling in proximity. The measurements, mold-making, and placements are the same. Everything is as with the <s>paricāyya</s>. The difference is this: in the first [type], beginning from outside, completion is near the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>. In the second [type], beginning near the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>, completion is outside.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Now the fourteenth chapter.
'He places by heaping together.'

children.text: agnanikṣetraṃ parita iṣṭakāḥsthāpayitvā samūhan ekatra rāśīkūrvannivopadadhāti //
children.translated_text: Having placed bricks around the fire-altar field, he places [them] by heaping — as if making a single pile.
'Pits in the directions' — [up to] 'that is the circumambient.'

children.text:
svayamātṛṇṇāmupadhāyānyāḥsarvā iṣṭakāḥsvayamātṛṇṇāṃ parita upadadhāti /
na tu prācīḥ pratīcīrityādayo viśeṣāḥ /
pūrvaḥpūrvo gaṇaḥsavayamātṛṇṇāsamīpe /
tatastato bahiruttarauttaraḥ /
anayoḥsamūhyaparicāyyayoḥ prakṛtivadeva rūpaṃ iṣṭakāś ca viśeṣāvacanāt /
athavā samūhasya paritaḥsthitvā samūhane kriyamāṇe maṇḍalarūpa iṣṭakācayo bhavatītyarthānmaṇḍalarūpatvamagnerbhavati /
paricāyyasyāpi svayamātṛṇṇāparicayanaṃ maṇḍalarūpa evāgnāvupapadyate iti arthādeva maṇḍalarūpatvaṃ /
tathāca bodhāyanaḥ -- samūhyaparicāyyau pūrveṇa rathacakracitā vyākhyātāviti /
children.translated_text: Having placed the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>, all other bricks are placed around the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s> on all sides. But there are no specific distinctions such as 'eastward' or 'westward.' The first group [of bricks] is near the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s>; thereafter, each successive [group] is progressively outward. In both the <s>samūhya</s> and <s>paricāyya</s>, the form and the bricks are as in the primary [altar], because of the absence of a specific statement [otherwise]. Alternatively, by the force of the meaning — since in heaping, the brick-pile made while standing around takes a circular form — the fire[-altar] becomes circular in form. In the <s>paricāyya</s> too, the circumambulating of the <s>svayamātṛṇṇā</s> is fitting only in a circular fire[-altar] — thus the circular form [follows] from the meaning itself. And thus <s>Bodhāyana</s> [states]: 'The <s>samūhya</s> and <s>paricāyya</s> are explained earlier by the chariot-wheel altar (<s>rathacakraciti</s>).'
'Accumulated' — [up to] 'alternation.'
This is merely a different name from another <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic school) for the same [altar] as before — that is the meaning.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: śmaśānacitaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayet pitṛloka ṛdhnuyāmiti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires — "may I prosper in the world of the ancestors" — should pile the funeral-pyre altar (<s>śmaśānaciti</s>)' — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.8 ||

children.text: pitṛloke ṛdhyāsamiti yaḥ kāmayet sa evaṃ cinuyāt /
children.translated_text: One who desires 'may I prosper in the world of the ancestors' should pile thus.

children.text: dvayāni khalu śmamaśānāni caturaśrāṇi parimaṇḍalāni ca || ĀpŚus_14.9 ||
children.translated_text: Funeral-pyre [altars] are indeed of two kinds: square and circular. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.9 ||
There, [the choice is] as one desires, since the word applies to both. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.10 ||
Or square — for which the scripture of qualities [applies]. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.11 ||
That square [altar] is as stated for the trough-shaped altar (<s>droṇaciti</s>), excluding the handle. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.12 ||
Funeral altars (<s>śmaśāna</s>) are of square shape and also of circular shape, as seen in the world.
There, the choice [between them] is according to one's wish, since the word applies to both.
If of circular shape, [it is] like a chariot-wheel.
'Or square' — this has been discussed.

children.text: yasya guṇaśāstraṃ pitṛlokasambaddhaṃ taccaturaśre śmaśāne na vartule /
children.translated_text: The scripture of qualities connected with the world of the ancestors [applies] to the square funeral altar, not to the circular.
For there, pits (<s>khāla</s>) are dug.

children.text: yeṣu paitṛmedhikakriyā teṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ samvandhaḥ ṛdhyā ca /
children.translated_text: For those [deceased] for whom the ancestral rites (<s>paitṛmedhika</s>) are performed, the connection with the ancestors and prosperity [is established].

children.text: tasmāccaturaśra eva cetavyaḥ yadi caturaśrastadātsaruvarjaṃ droṇacitoktaḥ -- tatsarvaṃ droṇacityeva vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: Therefore one should pile only the square [form]. If square, then excluding the handle, it is as stated for the trough-shaped altar — all that is explained by the <s>droṇaciti</s> itself.

children.text: chandaścitaṃ cinvīta paśukāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_14.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires cattle should pile the metre-altar (<s>chandaściti</s>)' — so it is known from scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.13 ||

children.text: chandobhireva yatreṣṭakāsvīyante taṃ chandasvivaṃ paśukāmaśvinuyādityasyāḥ śruterarthaṃ śrutidvayena vyācaṣṭe --
children.translated_text: Where bricks are consecrated by Vedic metres (<s>chandas</s>) alone — that is the <s>chandaściti</s>. One who desires cattle should pile [it] — he explains the meaning of this <s>śruti</s> with two [other] <s>śrutis</s>:

children.text: sarvaiś chandobiś cinuyād ity ekam | prākṛtair ity aparam || ĀpŚus_14.14 ||
children.translated_text: 'One should pile with all metres' — that is one [<s>śruti</s>]. 'With the primary [metres]' — that is the other. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 14.14 ||
Fourteenth chapter.
One <s>śruti</s> [says] that one should pile with all the metres of the ten-fold [<s>dāśatayī</s>] [<s>Agnicayana</s>].

children.text: prākṛtaiḥ -- prakṛtau yāni chandāṃsi agrirmūrdhetyādīni tairevetyaparā śrutiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'With the primary [metres]' — the other <s>śruti</s> [says] that [one should pile] with those same metres that are in the primary [rite], such as '<s>Agni</s> is the head' and so forth.
Thus in the commentary (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) on <s>Āpastamba's</s> <s>sūtras</s>, in the chapter called <s>Śulba</s>, by <s>Kapardisvāmin</s>,
[ends] the fourth <s>paṭala</s> (section).
<s>Karavindīya's</s> commentary.
'Funeral-pyre [altar]' — [commentary up to] 'known from scripture.'
One should pile like a funeral pyre (<s>śmaśāna</s>) — [for] one desiring prosperity in the world of the ancestors.
'Of two kinds' — [up to] 'applies to both.'

children.text:
gataṃ /
agnayāyatanaprakārarūpāṇi dvayānyapi śmaśānāni loke dṛśyante caturaśrāṇi parimaṇḍalāni ca /
children.translated_text: That is explained. Funeral altars of both kinds — resembling the form of a fire-altar site — are seen in the world: square and circular.
'Square' — [up to] 'square.'

children.text:
prakṛtitvāccaturaśrameva cinvīta na maṇḍalamiti samāsa uktaḥ /
śmaśānāni droṇacitetivat kartavyāni /
tsaruṃ varjayedanyatsarvaṃ droṇavat vimānāni /
dvādaśabāgīyā adhyardhāḥ ardhāḥ pādāś ca dvādaśabhāgīyāḥsaptaviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥ trayodaśatilāś ca /
adhyardhā ekatastādṛśāḥ anyata ekacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ trayaś ca tilāḥ ardhāḥ pādāḥ ekato dvādaśabhāgīyāsadṛśāḥ anyatastadardhāḥ /
pādā ekato dvādaśabhāgīyāsadṛśāḥ anyato navāṅgulayaḥ sādhikāśvatvārastilāś ca /
children.translated_text: The quarters: on one side like the twelfth-part, on the other nine <s>aṅgulas</s> with slightly more than four <s>tilas</s>.

children.text: upadhāne prathamaprastāre purastāt paścāccādhyardhāḥ caturaśrābhaiḥ pracchādanaṃ /
children.translated_text: In the placement: in the first layer, on the east and west, one-and-a-half [bricks] cover with square-[bricks].
With quarter-[bricks] and half-[bricks], the count is completed.
In the second [layer], from the south and north, with one-and-a-half [bricks] and square [bricks], the covering etc. is as before.

Because it is the primary [form], one should pile the square, not the circular — this has been said in summary. The funeral altars should be made like the <s>droṇaciti</s>. One should omit the handle; everything else, the measurements, are as for the <s>droṇa</s> [altar]. The twelfth-part [bricks] and the one-and-a-half, half, and quarter twelfth-part [bricks are]: twenty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with thirteen <s>tilas</s>. The one-and-a-half [bricks] are of that [measure] on one side, and forty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> with three <s>tilas</s> on the other. The halves and quarters: on one side like the twelfth-part, on the other their half.
'Metre [altar]' — [commentary up to] 'known from scripture.'

children.text: chantobhiḥ ṛgbhiśvīyate iti cchandaśvit etāvāneva viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: it is consecrated with <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) having metres — thus it is <s>chandaścit</s> (metre-fire-altar). This alone is the distinction.
Everything else is just as in the primary [altar].
With all — [this is an abbreviation marker]

children.text:
savairndaśatayīgataiśchantobhiśvinuyāt /
tāni sahasradhā vibhajya teṣāmekaikena bhāgenaikaikāmiṣṭakāmupadadhyāt /

children.translated_text: In place of <s>Yajus</s>-formulae, the metres should be [used].

children.text: tatra yāvatyaḥ yajuṣmatyaḥ iṣṭakāḥ tāvatyaśchandāṃsi vibhajya teṣāmekaikena vibhāgenaikaikāmiṣṭakāṃ yajuṣmatīrūpadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: There, as many bricks as have <s>Yajus</s>-formulae, that many metres should be divided, and with each single portion one should place each single brick that [otherwise] has a <s>Yajus</s>-formula.
But the <s>Laukampṛṇā</s> [bricks are placed] just as before.

children.text: athavā daśatayīgataiḥsarvaiśchandobhirgāyatrībhīstriṣṭubbhirjagatībhiranuṣṭubbhirvṛhatībhiruṣṇigbhiḥ paṅktibhirakṣarapaṅktibhirviṣurupābhistredhā vibhaktābhiraticchandobhistridhā vibhaktaisarvābhirddvipadābhiś ca purastādāramya yājñasenībhirupadadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, with all metres belonging to the groups of ten — <s>Gāyatrīs</s>, <s>Triṣṭubhs</s>, <s>Jagatīs</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s>, <s>Bṛhatīs</s>, <s>Uṣṇiks</s>, <s>Paṅktis</s>, <s>Akṣarapaṅktis</s>, <s>Viṣurūpās</s> divided threefold, <s>Atichandas</s> divided threefold, and all <s>Dvipadas</s> — beginning from the front, one should place [the bricks] with <s>Yājñasenī</s> [verses].
One should consecrate with all metres belonging to the groups of ten. Having divided those into a thousand parts, with each single part one should place each single brick.
With the primary — [abbreviation marker]

children.text:
prākṛtaiḥ agnikāṇḍagataiḥ agnirmūrdhetyanuvākasthairgāyatrayādibhiḥ na daśatayībhirityaparam /
nāsmātparaṃ vibhajyata iti siddhāntitam /
atra ślokāḥ --
children.translated_text: With the primary [mantras] belonging to the <s>Agnikāṇḍa</s>, situated in the <s>anuvāka</s> 'Agnir mūrdhā,' beginning with <s>Gāyatrī</s> etc. — not with those of the groups of ten — this is the other [opinion]. 'Beyond this, one should not divide further' — thus it has been established. Here are verses:
The fire[-altars], increasing by one each, are successively one-fold [up to] one hundred and one.
They are stated in the third chapter; their distinctions [are given] from the fourth [chapter] onward.
The primary (<s>prakṛti</s>) of fire[-altars] is either the one-fold or the seven-fold.
If the one-fold is the primary, then the six [altars from two-fold to six-fold] do not have wings and tail.
If the seven-fold is the primary, then those [six altars] have wings and tail.
From the seven-fold onward, that alone would be the primary up to the one-hundred-and-one-fold.
With the twelfth parts of the <s>karaṇīs</s>, with those joined or not joined with the stated fractions,
with bricks of separately produced forms — the placement is threefold.
The three-fold [arrangement] of the one-fold and other [altars], and the four-fold [arrangement] when with wings —
thus the three-fold [arrangement] of the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped) pair; nothing else when without wings.
Two quadrilateral [altars], the <s>prauga</s> (trough-shaped), <s>rathacakra</s> (chariot-wheel), <s>droṇacit</s> (trough-altar), and the <s>samūhya</s> (collective altar);
the <s>paryupapūrva</s> [altars] and the last two — <s>śmaśānacit</s> (cemetery-altar) and <s>chandaścit</s> (metre-altar) and <s>śyena</s> (hawk) [altars];
the <s>kaṅka</s> (heron) and <s>alaja</s> (buzzard) — [these are] the seven-fold [altars]; the five as before [are] the ten fire[-altars].
The <s>praugacit</s> (trough-altar), <s>ubhayaprauga</s> (double-trough), <s>rathacakra</s> (chariot-wheel), <s>droṇacit</s> (trough-altar), and <s>śmaśānāgni</s> (cemetery-fire) —
these are without wings and tail. The <s>kūrmacit</s> (tortoise-altar) and others are as stated by others.

children.text: anye sapakṣapucchā agnaya uktāḥ pravakṣyamaṇāś ca //
children.translated_text: The other fire[-altars] are stated as having wings and tail, and [more] will be described.
I shall explain the fire[-altars] beginning with the hawk-shaped one, in the two subsequent chapters.

children.text: iti karavindasvāmi kṛtāyāṃ śulbapradīpikāyāṃ caturthaḥ ṣaṭalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the fourth chapter in the <s>Śulbapradīpikā</s> composed by <s>Karavindasvāmin</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
(cemetery — [abbreviated]) (two — [abbreviated]) (quadrilateral) — [section heading].

children.text:
atra caturaśratve trīṇi śatānyaṣṭāviṃśatiśvāṅgulāḥ ekavintitilāś ca karaṇī /
tasyā dvādaśena saptaviṃśatyaṅgulena trayodaśatilayuktena dvādaśabhāgīyāḥ /
tadardhena pādyāḥ tṛtīyena ca navamyaḥ /
adhārś ca pūrvavat /
upādhāne 'dhyardhā dvādaśapurastātpratīcyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the quadrilateral [altar], the <s>karaṇī</s> is three hundred twenty-eight <s>aṅgulas</s> and twenty-one <s>tilas</s>. With its twelfth — twenty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> joined with thirteen <s>tilas</s> — the twelfth-part [bricks are made]. With its half, the quarter-bricks; and with its third, the ninth-part [bricks]. The base is as before. In placement: one-and-a-half twelfth-[bricks], twelve [rows] facing west in front;

children.text:
pasvāddvādaśa prācyaḥ /
śeṣaṃ droṇateva /
tatra sarvābhāvāt ṣoḍaśeṣṭakā hīyante /
ato'gnimadhye dve uddhṛtyāṣṭādaśanavamyo nidheyāḥ /
dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
evamevāparaḥ /
children.translated_text: from behind, twelve [rows] facing east. The rest is as in the <s>droṇa</s> (trough-altar). There, because of the absence of all [required bricks], sixteen bricks are deficient. Therefore, having removed two from the middle of the fire[-altar], eighteen ninth-part [bricks] should be placed. The layer is two hundred. The other [layer] is likewise.
But in the eastward and northward [rows], there is reversal. The <s>śmaśānī</s> (cemetery-altar) and the <s>rathacakracit</s> (chariot-wheel altar) in circular [form] have been explained.
<s>Chandaścit</s> (metre-altar) —

children.text:
chandobhiśvīyat iti chandaśvit /
chāndasaḥ karaṇa upapade vkip /
anyatra karmaṇyagnayākhyāyāmiti /
children.translated_text: It is consecrated with metres — thus it is <s>chandaścit</s>. In the <s>Chāndasa</s> [grammar], with the <s>upapada</s>, the affix <s>kvip</s> [is applied]. Otherwise, 'in the <s>karmaṇi</s> [sense], and in naming fire[-altars]' [applies].

children.text: sarvaiḥ paraṃ tatra sarvairgāyatrayādibhi ścaturuttaraiḥ atidhṛti paryantaiḥ caturdaśabhirutkṛtiparyantairvaikaviṃśatyā trivṛtkakubhādiviśeṣayuktairdāśatayībhya āhṛtaiśchantaubiḥ sarvā iṣṭakāśvinuyādityekaṃ mataṃ /

children.translated_text: With the primary [mantras] learned in the <s>anuvāka</s> 'Agnir mūrdhā,' serving the purpose of the <s>Yājñasenī</s> [verses], repeated again and again — this is the other opinion.
The form of this fire[-altar] is just like the primary.

children.text: kecitu vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayetyasyāpi nityatvādvayasa ākāramapīcchanti /
children.translated_text: But some, since 'this is built in the likeness of birds' is also perpetual, desire the bird-shape as well.
As <s>Bodhāyana</s> states: 'Its form becomes hawk-shaped.'

With 'all' — beyond that, with all [metres] beginning with <s>Gāyatrī</s>, in groups of four up to <s>Atidhṛti</s> — that is fourteen; or up to <s>Utkṛti</s> — that is twenty-one; joined with the special types like <s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>Kakubh</s>, etc., brought from the groups of ten — with these metres one should consecrate all bricks — this is one opinion.
Thus the fourth chapter in the <s>Śulbapradīpikā</s> composed by the blessed <s>Sundararāja</s>.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: śyenacitaṃ cinvīta suvargakāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_15.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'One who desires heaven should pile the hawk-shaped altar' — thus it is known [from scripture]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.1]
It has curved wings and an expanded tail. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.2a]

children.text:
śyena iva cetavyaḥ śyanacit tadākāraṃ cinvīta /
ākṛtyāḥ phalamākārasaṃpādanaṃ svayameva vakṣyati /
anṛjupakṣaḥ vyastapuccho 'saṅkocitapucchaḥ /
children.translated_text: It should be piled like a hawk — [this is] the <s>śyenacit</s> (hawk-altar); one should pile it in that shape. The purpose of the shape — [namely] the accomplishment of the form — he himself will state. [It has] non-straight wings and an expanded, non-contracted tail.
How is the curvature [achieved]?

children.text: paścāt prāṅ udūhati | purastātpratyaṅṅ udūhati | evam iva hi vayasāṃ madhye pakṣanirṇāmo bhavatīti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_15.2b ||
children.translated_text: From behind, one draws forward [the cord]; from the front, one draws backward — for thus indeed the bending of wings is seen in the middle of birds — so it is known [from scripture]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.2b]
One raises [the cord]; from the front one raises it backward.

children.text: evameva vakrāḥ pakṣā yasya sa vakrapakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus one whose wings are curved in this manner is 'curved-winged.'
The word 'hi' [is used] in the sense of well-known [fact].

children.text: evamiva -- evameva vayasāmutpatatāṃ madhye pakṣanirṇāmo namanaṃ bhavatīti śrutiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Thus indeed' means 'in exactly this way' — of birds in flight, in the middle [of the wings], the bending of the wing, the downward curving, occurs — thus the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).

children.text: yāvān agniḥ sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate | prādeśaṃ caturtham ātmanaś caturbhāgīyāś cāṣṭau | tāsāṃ tisraḥ śira itarat pakṣayor vibhajet || ĀpŚus_15.3 ||
children.translated_text: The fire[-altar], as large as the seven-fold with the <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> [additions] turns out to be — one should take a <s>prādeśa</s>[-measure]; the fourth of its body [as] <s>caturbhāgīya</s> (fourth-part) [bricks] — and eight [of those]; of those, three [go to] the head, the rest one should distribute to the wings. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.3]

children.text:
aradninā prādeśena ca virdhito 'gniḥ prākṛto yāvān saṃpadyate prādeśa iti gṛhṇīyāditi śeṣaḥ /
sāratniprādeśāgnau yatprādeśaṃ pucche ātmani caturtaṃ puruṣakṣetraṃ caturbhāgīyāśvāṣṭau śiṣṭe puruṣe 'ṣṭau caturbhāgīyāḥ kṣetraṃ ca gṛhītvā tāsāṃ caturbhāgīyānāṃ disraścaturbāgīyāḥśirasi nidhātavyāḥ /
itaratsarvaṃ pakṣayorvibhajya kṣipet /
ṣaḍaṅgulamātraṃ prādeśe /
ṣaṣṭayaṅgulaṃ puruṣe /
caturbhāgīyāsu pañcasu pādonaṃ navadaśāṅgulam /
etadevaikaikasmina pakṣe kṣaipet /
children.translated_text: The fire[-altar] augmented by an <s>aratni</s> and a <s>prādeśa</s> — the primary one — as large as it turns out to be, one should take the <s>prādeśa</s> — this is the remainder [of the sūtra]. In the <s>sāratniprādeśa</s> fire[-altar]: the <s>prādeśa</s>[-area] in the tail, and from the body the fourth <s>puruṣa</s>-area, and eight <s>caturbhāgīya</s> (fourth-part) bricks — taking the area of eight <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> from the remaining <s>puruṣa</s> [area] — three <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> of those should be placed in the head. The entire remainder should be divided and assigned to the wings. Six <s>aṅgulas</s> [is] the <s>prādeśa</s>[-addition]. Sixty <s>aṅgulas</s> [is] the <s>puruṣa</s>[-area]. Among the five <s>caturbhāgīyas</s>, a quarter less than nineteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. This much should be assigned to each wing.

children.text: pañcāratniḥ puruṣaḥ | caturaratniḥ vyāyāmaḥ | caturviṃśatyaṅgulayo 'ratniḥ | tadardhaṃ prādeśa iti kḷptiḥ || ĀpŚus_15.4 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>puruṣa</s> is five <s>aratnis</s>; a <s>vyāyāma</s> is four <s>aratnis</s>; an <s>aratni</s> is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; half of that is a <s>prādeśa</s> — this is the convention. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.4]

children.text:
pañceti -- etatpuruṣasya pramāṇam /
caturiti -- etadaratnipramāṇam /
kḷptiḥ -- evaṃ kalpanā /
itiśabdaḥ prakāre /
anenana mārgeṇa kalpayedityarthaḥ /
triṃśadaṅgulaṃ caturbhāgīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Five' — this is the measure of the <s>puruṣa</s>. 'Four' — this is the measure of the <s>aratni</s> [in terms of the <s>vyāyāma</s>]. '<s>Kḷpti</s>' means 'thus is the arrangement.' The word 'iti' [is used] in the sense of 'manner.' By this method one should arrange — this is the meaning. The <s>caturbhāgīya</s> is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
<s>Śyena</s> (hawk) — [section heading].

children.text:
śyenaḥ -- pakṣiviśeṣaḥ /
tadākāramagniṃ cinvīta svargakāmaḥ /
vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyata iti vayomātrasadṛśaḥ prākṛto 'gniḥ /
ayaṃ tu śyenasadṛśaḥ /
kīdṛśaḥ śyena ityāha --
children.translated_text: <s>Śyena</s> means a particular bird. One who desires heaven should pile a fire[-altar] in its shape. 'This is built in the likeness of birds' — the primary fire[-altar] resembles birds in general. But this one resembles a hawk specifically. What kind of hawk? — he says:
Curved — [section heading].

children.text:
vakrau -- anṛjū pakṣau yasya sa vakrapakṣaḥ /
vyastaṃ vistīrṇaṃ pucchaṃ yasya mūlādārabhya uparyupari vistīrṇaṃ saḥ /
paścāt prāṅudūtīti udūhanamunnayanaṃ prathamapakṣārdhaṃ mūlādārabya paścātprabhṛti prāgunnayet /
purastātpratyaṅṅudūhati /
dvayaṃ pakṣārdhaṃ madhyādārabya purastāt prabhṛti pratyagunnayet /
evamivahīti nipādasamudāyaḥ prasiddhau /

children.translated_text: 'In the middle of birds' — in the middle of the wings of hawks.
<s>Nirṇāma</s> means bending downward, becoming inclined after extending outward.
'It is known' — it is heard [in scripture] or seen [in nature].

children.text: pakṣanirṇāma iti vacanasāmarthyāt pakṣayormadhye nirṇāmaḥ dṛśyate -- pakṣiṇāṃ dṛśyate iti //
children.translated_text: By the force of the expression 'wing-bending,' bending is seen in the middle of the wings — it is seen in birds.

Curved — [meaning] non-straight wings — one whose [wings are] non-straight is 'curved-winged.' Expanded (<s>vyasta</s>) — a tail that is progressively wider from the base upward — [one having] that [is <s>vyastapuccha</s>]. 'From behind, one draws forward' — the drawing forward is the raising; the first half of the wing, beginning from the base, one should raise forward from behind. 'From the front, one draws backward' — the second half of the wing, beginning from the middle, one should raise backward from the front. 'Evam iva hi' — this compound of particles [is used] in the sense of well-known [fact].
'As large as' — [section heading].

children.text:
prākṛtamagnimātmapakṣapucchaśiraḥsu vibhajet /
kān vibāgānityāha -- pucchāt prādeśakṣetramātmanaśvatuṣpuruṣādekapuruṣakṣetrama (ṣṭau) ṣṭādaśacaturbhāgīyāḥ yāvati kṣetre upadhīyante tāvaccātmakṣetraṃ saṃgṛhya tāsāṃ caturbāgīyānāṃ tisro(gneḥ)gre śiraḥ kuryāt /
avaśiṣṭapañca daśa(viṃśati)caturbāgīyāḥ puruṣaḥ prādeśaśvaprākṛtayoḥ adhyaratnipuruṣayoḥ pakṣayorvibhajet -- kṣipedityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: This being so, [each wing is] nine-and-a-half <s>aratnis</s> and <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter.
The body is two-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>.
The tail is one <s>puruṣa</s> in measure.
Three <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> [form] the head.

One should divide the primary fire[-altar] into body, wings, tail, and head. What divisions? — he says: from the tail, a <s>prādeśa</s>-area; from the body, one <s>puruṣa</s>-area out of four <s>puruṣas</s>; eight — [that is,] eighteen <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> in whatever area they are placed — taking that much body-area, of those <s>caturbhāgīyas</s>, three should be made the head of the fire[-altar]. The remaining fifteen (twenty-five) <s>caturbhāgīyas</s>, plus the <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> [additions] of the primary and the <s>adhyaratni-puruṣa</s> — one should divide [these] between the wings — meaning assign [them].
'Five <s>aratnis</s>' — [section heading for] '<s>kḷpti</s>.'

children.text:
"pañcāratniragnau puruṣaḥ /
yāvān puruṣa ūrdhvabāhustāvāna bhavatīti puruṣapramāṇaviśeṣavidheḥ /
anyatra caturaradniḥ /

children.translated_text: An <s>aratni</s> is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
Half of that is a <s>prādeśa</s>.
And that is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Kḷpti</s> means the convention of the teacher.

A <s>puruṣa</s> in the fire[-altar] is five <s>aratnis</s>. 'As large as a man with arms raised upward, so large it should be' — because of this special injunction regarding the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure. Elsewhere, [a <s>puruṣa</s> is] four <s>aratnis</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
<s>Śyena</s> (hawk) — [section heading].

children.text:
taittirīyake kāmyaprakaraṇe paṭhito 'pyayaṃ śyenacit nitya eva svargaphalakatvāt caturaśrāgnivattasyāpi svargaphalakatvaṃ /
"suvargāya vā eṣa lokāya cīyate /
yadagniḥ' iti liṅgāni cātra prāgeva darśitāni /
children.translated_text: Although this <s>śyenacit</s> (hawk-altar) is recited in the <s>Taittirīya</s> [Saṃhitā] in the section on optional [rites], it is indeed a perpetual [rite] because it yields the fruit of heaven — just like the quadrilateral fire[-altar], which also yields the fruit of heaven. 'For the heavenly world indeed this is piled — namely the fire[-altar]' — and such indicatory marks (<s>liṅgas</s>) have been shown earlier.
Curved — [section heading].

children.text:
śrutyanataranidaṃ śyenacidvākyasya śe,bhūtaṃ /
tatra vakratā pakṣamadhye /
vyāsaḥ pucchāgre /
pakṣayorvakrīkaraṇaprakāramapi śrutirevāha ----
children.translated_text: This is the remainder of the <s>śyenacit</s> statement [according to] scripture. There, the curvature is in the middle of the wing. The expansion (<s>vyāsa</s>) is at the tip of the tail. Scripture itself states the manner of curving the wings:
From behind, one draws forward — in the middle of the wing. From the front, one draws backward — at the wing-tips and joints.

children.text:
evamiva hi vayasāṃ pakṣasya madhye madhyapakṣaṃ nirṇāmo vakratā /
madhyepakṣanirṇāmaḥ -- vayasāmutpatatāṃ pakṣamadhye nirṇāma evamiva hi dṛśyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus indeed of birds, in the middle of the wing' — the middle wing has bending, curvature. 'Middle-wing-bending' — of birds in flight, in the middle of the wing, bending is seen thus indeed — this is the meaning.
'As large as' — [section heading].

children.text:
sāratniprodaśaścaturaśro 'gniryāvān sampadyate tāvānevāyaṃ śyenaciddhavati /
sāratniprādeśagrahaṇasya prayojanamuktameva /
children.translated_text: The <s>sāratniprādeśa</s> (with-<s>aratni</s>-and-<s>prādeśa</s>) quadrilateral fire[-altar], as large as it turns out to be — this hawk-altar is of that same [size]. The purpose of specifying '<s>sāratniprādeśa</s>' has already been stated.
Therein —
'<s>Prādeśa</s> — eight' [section heading].

children.text:
ādadhīteti śeṣaḥ pucche puruṣādadhikaṃ prādeśamātmanaścaturthaṃ puruṣaṃ caturbhāgīyāśvāṣṭau ātmana evādadhīta /
śiṣṭa ātmā /
ardhatṛtīyaḥ puruṣaḥ /
pucchaṃ puruṣapramāṇa(mātra)meva /
children.translated_text: 'One should place' — this is the remainder. In the tail, beyond a <s>puruṣa</s>, a <s>prādeśa</s>[-area]; from the body, the fourth <s>puruṣa</s>; and eight <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> — one should place [these] in the body itself. The remainder is the body — two-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s>. The tail is exactly one <s>puruṣa</s> in measure.
'Those' — 'head' [section heading].
Of those, three <s>caturbhāgīyas</s> one should fashion as the head.
'The rest' — 'to the wings' [section heading].

children.text:
pucchādātmanaśvātra śeṣaṃ dvedhā vibhajya pakṣayornidadhyāt /
ekaikasmin pakṣe prādeśārdhaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulaṃ ātmacaturthādardhaṃ ṣaṣṭirahgulayaḥ /
pañcānāṃ caturbhāgīyānāṃ madhye puruṣāyāme pakṣe nyaste pādenā ekānnatriṃśatirahgulayaḥ prākṛtaḥ pakṣaḥ /
catuśvatvāriṃśadadhikaśatāṅgulayaḥ /
ebhiḥ sahitaḥ pādonaikānnatriṃśacchatadvayāṅgulaḥ sampadyate /
tadetadvakṣyati ardhadaśamā aratnaya ityādi /
children.translated_text: Having divided the remainder from the tail and body into two, one should place [it] in the wings. In each wing: half of the <s>prādeśa</s> — six <s>aṅgulas</s>; half of the body's fourth — sixty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Of the five <s>caturbhāgīyas</s>, [each having] a <s>puruṣa</s>-length when placed in the wing — a quarter less than twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> [is] the primary wing. One hundred forty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>. Together with these, [the total] becomes a quarter less than two hundred twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s>. This he will state: 'nine-and-a-half <s>aratnis</s>' etc.
'Five <s>aratnis</s>' — '<s>kḷpti</s>.' [section heading]
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: ardhadaśamā aratnayo 'ṅgulayaś ca caturbhāgonāḥ pakṣāyāmaḥ || ĀpŚus_15.5 ||
children.translated_text: Nine-and-a-half <s>aratnis</s> and <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter — [that is] the wing-length. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.5]

children.text:
prādeśadaśamā aratnayo 'ṅgulayaś ca caturbhāgonāḥ pakṣāyāmaḥ -- pakṣayorāyamaḥ /
prākṛtāḥ ṣaḍaratnayaḥ ardhapuruṣe prādeśasahitāratnidvayamaṣṭādaśāhgulāścaturbhāgonāś ca prādeśe ṣaḍṅgulāḥ /
tā aṣṭādaśabhiḥsahāratniḥ sarvaṃ sambhūyārdhadaśamā aratnayo 'hgulāsva caturbhāgonāḥ /
eṣa pakṣayorāyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prādeśa</s>-and-nine <s>aratnis</s> and <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter — [that is] the wing-length, the length of the wings. The primary [wing is] six <s>aratnis</s>; in the half-<s>puruṣa</s> [addition], <s>prādeśa</s> together with two <s>aratnis</s> is eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter; in the <s>prādeśa</s>, six <s>aṅgulas</s>. Those eighteen together with the <s>aratni</s> — all combined — [give] nine-and-a-half <s>aratnis</s> and <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter. This is the length of the wings.

children.text: dvipuruṣāṃ rajjum ubhayataḥpāśāṃ karoti | madhye lakṣaṇam | pakṣasyāparayoḥ koṭyor antau niyamya lakṣaṇena prācīnam āyacched evaṃ purastāt | sa nirṇāmaḥ || ĀpŚus_15.6 ||
children.translated_text: One makes a cord of two <s>puruṣas</s> with loops at both ends; [makes] a mark at the middle; having fixed both ends at the two corners of a wing, one should stretch [the cord] eastward by the mark — and similarly in front. That is the bending (<s>nirṇāma</s>). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.6]
By this, the northern wing is explained. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.7]

children.text: dvipuruṣapramāṇāṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ; kuryāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having made a cord of two <s>puruṣas</s> in measure with loops at both ends, one should make a mark at the middle — this is the supplement.
By this very method, the bending of the northern wing too is explained.
This is the curvature of the wings. [15.7]
The body (<s>ātman</s>) is two <s>puruṣas</s> in length and one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> in breadth. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.8]

children.text: pucche 'rdhapuruṣavyāsaṃ puruṣaṃ pratīcīnam āyacchet | tasya dakṣiṇato 'nyam uttarataś ca || ĀpŚus_15.9a ||
children.translated_text: In the tail, one should extend [a rectangle] of half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> in breadth and one <s>puruṣa</s> westward; of that, another to the south and another to the north. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.9a]

children.text:
dvipjaruṣāyāma ātmā adhdhardhapuruṣavyāsaḥ /
evaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya pucchasthāner'dhapuruṣā tiryaṅbhānī puruṣapramāṇā pārśvamānī bhavati yathā tathā yacchet -- kuryādityarthaḥ /
tasya caturaśrasya dakṣiṇapārśve 'nyaṃ tādṛgvidhaṃ caturaśramuttarataśvānyam /
evaṃ trīṇi caturaśrāṇi ardhapuruṣavyāsāni /
children.translated_text: The body is two <s>puruṣas</s> in length and one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> in breadth. Having thus laid out the oblong quadrilateral, at the place of the tail, half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> becomes the transverse measure and one <s>puruṣa</s> the lateral measure — one should extend it in such a way. Of that quadrilateral, on the southern side another quadrilateral of the same kind, and on the northern side yet another. Thus three quadrilaterals, each half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> in breadth.
One should mark those diagonally, so that half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> results at the junction. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.9b]

children.text: śirasy ardhapuruṣeṇa caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhāt tāvati dakṣiṇayor nipātayet || ĀpŚus_15.10 ||
children.translated_text: At the head, having made a quadrilateral with half-a-<s>puruṣa</s>, from the midpoint of the eastern side (<s>karaṇī</s>), one should drop [a line] to the same extent at the two southern [corners]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 15.10]
Thus ends the fifteenth section.

children.text:
tau caturaśrau yau pārśvasthau /
tāvakṣṇayā karṇena ālikhet; yathāpyaye ātmapucchasandhau ardhapuruṣamātraṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvasya bhavati /
prācyamiva dakṣiṇaṃ prācyamivottaram /
evaṃ kṛte 'pyayer'dhapuruṣamātraṃ bhavati /
śiraḥsthāner'dhaṣuruṣapramāṇena caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhādārabya tāvatyevārdhe madhye nipātayet -- ālikhet /
tisraḥ pariśiṣyanta ityuparitane vakṣyati /
atrāpi tisraḥ śirasītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Those two quadrilaterals that are on the sides — one should mark them diagonally with the hypotenuse; so that at the junction (<s>apyaya</s>) of the body and tail, the result is exactly half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> in the forward [direction]. The southern [is drawn] forward like the eastern, and the northern likewise forward. When done thus, half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> results at the junction. At the place of the head, having made a quadrilateral with a measure of half-a-<s>puruṣa</s>, starting from the midpoint of the eastern side, one should draw [lines] to the same half-measure at the center — [i.e.] mark [them]. Three [triangles] remain, as will be stated below. Here too, "three at the head" has been stated.
Fifteenth section.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Half ... length

children.text:
apareṇa yūpāvaṭadeśaṃ saṃcaramavaśiṣyetyādi vimāya pakṣāpyayeṣu śaṅkuṃ nihatya dakṣiṇottarayā rajjvā navāratnīn prādeśamaṅgulaṃ caturbhāgonāṃ cāyāmaṃ kṛtvā pakṣāgreṣu śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evamekādaśabhiraṅgulībhiḥ prādeśena ca puruṣo hīyate /
tatrārdhāṣṭamābhiraṅgulībhirekā caturbhāgīyā bhavati /
tadardhenārdhadvipuruṣāyāmāṃ rajjumubhayataḥ pāśāṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā pakṣasyāparakoṭiśaṅkvoḥ pratimucya lakṣaṇena prācīmapasārya śaṅkuṃ nihanyāt /
evaṃ tasyaiva pūrvayoḥ koṭyoḥ pratimucya lakṣaṇena pratīcīmapasārya tatra śaṅkuḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, having fastened [the loops] at the two front tips of the same [wing], one should extend [the mark] westward — there a peg [is planted].

children.text: evaṃ kṛte paścimapārśvamānyāḥ purastāt pakṣmadhye caturviṃśatyaṅgule sārdhasaptatile lakṣaṇaṃ nipatati purataśvaivaṃ /
children.translated_text: When done thus, the mark falls at twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> and seven-and-a-half <s>tilas</s> at the center of the wing in front of the rear lateral measure — and likewise in front.
That is the curvature (<s>nirṇāma</s>) — the bending of the wing.

children.text: ardhadaśamā ityādi sa nirṇāma ityantenottaramapi pakṣaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: From "nine-and-a-half" etc. to "that is the curvature" — one should likewise make the northern wing.

Having measured west of the sacrificial-post pit, leaving the passage-space, and having planted a peg at the wing-junctions, with a cord [stretched] north-south measuring nine <s>aratnīs</s>, one <s>prādeśa</s>, one <s>aṅgula</s>, and diminished by a quarter — this being the length — one should plant a peg at the wing-tips. Thus the <s>puruṣa</s> is diminished by eleven <s>aṅgulas</s> and a <s>prādeśa</s>. Therein, by eight-and-a-half <s>aṅgulas</s>, one fourth-part [brick] results. By half of that, having made a cord of half-two-<s>puruṣas</s> in length with loops at both ends, and having made a mark at the middle, and having fastened [the loops] at the peg at the rear tip of the wing, one should extend [the mark] eastward and plant a peg.
The body, two ... breadth
One should measure the body as two <s>puruṣas</s> eastward and one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> northward along the spine.
In the tail ... should extend

children.text: pucche puruṣāyāmāni tadardhavistārāṇi pratyagāyatāni trīṇi caturaśrāṇi dakṣiṇottarāṇi vihṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ caturaśraṃ dakṣiṇāparakoṭiṃ pratyakṣṇayālikhet /
children.translated_text: In the tail, having laid out three quadrilaterals, each one <s>puruṣa</s> in length and half that in breadth, extending westward and [arranged] north-south, one should mark the southern quadrilateral diagonally from the south-western corner.
Likewise toward the north-western corner.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte pucchamūler'dhapuruṣavistāramagre 'dhyardhapuruṣavistāraṃ puruṣamātrāyāmaṃ caturaśraṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: When done thus, the tail becomes a quadrilateral with half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> in breadth at the base, one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> in breadth at the front, and one <s>puruṣa</s> in length.
The head ... should extend

children.text: ātmanaḥ pūrvakaraṇīmadhye pucchavadardhāyāmavistāraṃ caturaśraṃ kṛtvā tatpūrvakaraṇīmadhyād dakṣiṇottarakaraṇyormadhye rekhāṃ nipātayeta -- rekhayorbahistyajet //
children.translated_text: At the midpoint of the eastern side of the body, one should make a quadrilateral of half the length and breadth as in the tail, and from the midpoint of its eastern side, drop lines to the midpoints of the southern and northern sides — [and] discard what lies outside the lines.
Fifteenth section.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
Half ... length

children.text:
vyāsaḥ puruṣamātra eva /
atha tasya nirṇāmaḥ --
children.translated_text: The breadth is exactly one <s>puruṣa</s> in measure. Now its curvature (<s>nirṇāma</s>):
Two <s>puruṣas</s> ... curvature

children.text: koṭayoragrāpyayayorevaṃ purastātpūrvayoḥ koṭayorantau niyamya yatpaścādapacchidyate tatpurastādāgacchati /
children.translated_text: At the tips, the front and junction [ends]: thus at the front, having fixed [the cord] at the two tips, what is cut away at the rear comes to the front.
By this ... explained. The body ... breadth.
In the body likewise, three <s>puruṣas</s> are established.
In the tail ... should extend
In front of the body is the head.
Thus ends the fifteenth section.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
One should trim diagonally toward the junctions. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.1a]

children.text:
apyayaśabdena pakṣapucchaśirasāṃ sandhiruktaḥ /
tānpratyapacchi ndyāt -- śroṇyaṃsācyajet /

children.translated_text: Starting from the junction of the head, toward the wing-junction,
and likewise at the hips and shoulders.

children.text: evaṃ dve dve caturbhāgīye niraste bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus two-by-two fourth-part [bricks] are removed [from each junction].
It will be stated: "forty remain."
By the word "junction" (<s>apyaya</s>), the joints of the wings, tail, and head are denoted. Toward those, one should trim diagonally — cut away at the hips and shoulders.
For thus indeed is the hawk. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.1b]
This is well-known. And it will be stated: "as far as conformity with the handed-down [shape]."

children.text: karaṇaṃ puruṣasya pañcamāyāmaṃ ṣaṣṭhavyāsaṃ kārayed yathāyoganataṃ tatprathamam || ĀpŚus_16.2 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>karaṇa</s> (brick-type) should be made with one-fifth of a <s>puruṣa</s> as length and one-sixth as breadth, bent as appropriate — that is the first [brick-type]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.2]

children.text:
puruṣapañcamāyāmaṃ puruṣaṣaṣṭhavyāsaṃ -- aratnimātrī pārśvamānī ṣaḍbhāgā tiryaṅbhānī yathā yujyate tathā nataḥ; nataśabdena prajambhanamucyate /
tathā prajambhayet /
ekāmakṣṇayādīrghāṃ kuryāt /
yathā yujyata iti yathāyogaḥ /
tatprathamaṃ karaṇam /
prathamamityasya saṃjñā /
children.translated_text: One-fifth of a <s>puruṣa</s> in length and one-sixth in breadth — an <s>aratni</s>-measure lateral side and a sixth-part transverse side — bent as is appropriate; by the word "bent" (<s>nata</s>), curving (<s>prajambhana</s>) is meant. One should curve it thus. One [side] should be made long diagonally. "As is appropriate" means "as per the application" (<s>yathāyoga</s>). That is the first <s>karaṇa</s>. "First" (<s>prathama</s>) is its designation.

children.text: te dve prācī saṃhite | tad dvitīyam || ĀpŚus_16.3 ||
children.translated_text: Those two [placed] with tips facing east, joined together — that is the second [brick-type]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.3]

children.text: te dve viparyaste upasṛtya madhyamaphalake saṃsṛṣṭe yathā tiṣṭhataḥ tathāvidhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvitīyam /
children.translated_text: Those two, reversed and brought together, joined at the middle plank — a <s>karaṇa</s> such that they stand thus is the second.

children.text: prathamasya ṣaḍbhāgam aṣṭabhāgena vardhayet | yathāyoganataṃ tat tṛtīyam || ĀpŚus_16.4 ||
children.translated_text: One should augment the sixth-part of the first by an eighth-part, bent as appropriate — that is the third. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.4]

children.text:
prathamasya ṣaḍbāgakaraṇamaṣṭabhāgeva vardhayeddīrghaṃ kuryāt /
mātrā? tamakṣṇayā chindyāt /
chinnā yathā yujyate namanaṃ tatā yogaḥ /
yathā pakṣanamane 'dhyarghaṃ yujyate tathā nataṃ vakraṃ tṛtīyakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The sixth-part <s>karaṇa</s> of the first should be augmented by an eighth-part — made longer. The measure? One should cut it diagonally. The cut [produces] bending as is appropriate — that is the application. As half [is] appropriate in the wing-bending, so bent — curved — is the third <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: caturbhāgīyādhyardhā | tasyāś caturbhāgīyāmātram akṣṇayā chindyāt | tac caturtham || ĀpŚus_16.5 ||
children.translated_text: One-and-a-half of a fourth-part [brick]; of that, a fourth-part measure should be cut diagonally — that is the fourth [brick-type]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.5]
Having drawn one-and-a-half of a fourth-part [brick] on the ground, a fourth-part should not be removed.

children.text: tathābhūteṣṭakā yena karaṇena kiyate taccaturthaṃ karaṇam /
children.translated_text: A brick made by such a <s>karaṇa</s> — that is the fourth <s>karaṇa</s>.
It will be stated: "the sixteenth-part, by four."
This is that <s>karaṇa</s>.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Junction ... hawk
By the word "junction" (<s>apyaya</s>), the joint of the body with the wings, tail, and head is denoted.
Starting from the junction of the head, up to the wing-junction; starting from the tail-junction, up to the wing-junction.
"For thus indeed" — this is understood.
Brick-type ... the first
On the other side, twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> — [this is] the first <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: yathāyoganataṃ bhavet -- upadhāne yathāyujyate tathā kuryāt /
children.translated_text: It should be bent as appropriate — in placement, one should make it as is applicable.
The method of bending will be stated below in [the section on] the hawk[-altar].
The designations "first" etc. are for convenience of usage.
The fifth of a <s>puruṣa</s> is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> on one side.
Those two ... second

children.text:
prathamakaraṇe prāgāyate dakṣiṇamekamuttaramekamiti saṃhite caturviṃśatyaṅgule pārśvamānyau catvāriṃśadaṅgule tiryaṅnānyau /
tayorekānamanavidhinā madhye nirṇatā ekapārśve unnatā /
taddvitīyaṃ karaṇam /
children.translated_text: In the first <s>karaṇa</s>, [two bricks] with length facing east — one to the south and one to the north — are joined: twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> on the lateral sides, forty <s>aṅgulas</s> on the transverse sides. Of those, one is curved downward at the center by the bending method, raised on one side. That is the second <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: prathamakaraṇasya ṣaḍbhāgo viṃśatyaṅgulamaṣṭabhāgena pañcadaśāṅgulena yathāyoganatena vardhayet; yathā ṣaḍbāgaḥ pabhānurodhī vakraḥsyādaṣṭamabāga ātmānurūpa ṛjurbhavettattṛtīyaṃ karaṇam //
children.translated_text: The sixth-part of the first <s>karaṇa</s>, twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>, should be augmented by an eighth-part, fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, bent as appropriate; so that the sixth-part conforms to the wing[-curvature] and is curved, while the eighth-part conforms to the body and is straight — that is the third <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text:
caturbhā rthaṃ caturbhāgīyāṇūkākhyā /
sādhyardā kāryā /
tasyāścaturbhāgīyāmātramakṣṇayāmātramakṣṇayā chindyāt /
etadṛktaṃ bhavati--pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulāyāmaṃ triṃśadahgulavyāsaṃ kṛtvā triṃśadaṅgulamakṣṇayā chindyāt /
children.translated_text: This amounts to: having made [a rectangle of] forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> in length and thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth, one should cut thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> diagonally.
Thus one lateral side [is obtained].

children.text: pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ ekā tiryaṅbhānī triṃśadahgulayaḥ ekākṣṇayā sthitā dvicatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ caturdaśa tilāḥ /
children.translated_text: Forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> on one side; one transverse side of thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>; one diagonal of forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> and fourteen <s>tilas</s>.
This is the fourth <s>karaṇa</s>.
Fourth-part ... the name is <s>aṇūkā</s>. It should be made one-and-a-half [times]. Of that, a fourth-part measure should be cut diagonally.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
Junction ... should cut

children.text:
pakṣapucchaśiro 'pyayebhyaḥ anyonyaṃ pratyakṣṇayā paricchindyāt /
evamātmanor'dhapuruṣo nirasto bhavati /
children.translated_text: From the junctions of wings, tail, and head, one should cut diagonally toward each other. Thus half-a-<s>puruṣa</s> is removed from the body.
Thus indeed ... the first

children.text:
caturviṃśatyaṅgulaṃ /
pārśvaphalakam /
viṃśatyaṅgulaṃ tiryakphalakam /
yathāyoganataṃ yathā yujyate pakṣe tathā natam /
tasyaikākṣṇayārajjuḥ pañcatriṃśikā viṃśatitilayuktā /
aparā ṣaḍviṃśikā ṣaṭtilayuktā /
evaṃ kṛte pakṣāyāmasya dvādaśabhāgaḥ ekānnaviṃśatirahgulayaḥ tilau ca iṣṭakāvyāso bhavati /
tadetatprathamaṃ karaṇam /
aratniprādeśarahitaprakṛtike pakṣāyāmasya triṃśadaṅgulahāniḥ /
tadanuguṇaṃ ceṣṭakānāṃ namanaṃ bhavati /
tatra karṇau ekaviṃśakaikānnatriṃśakau tilatrayayuktau /
children.translated_text: Twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> — the lateral plank. Twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> — the transverse plank. Bent as appropriate — bent as is applicable in the wing. Its one diagonal cord is thirty-five with twenty <s>tilas</s>. The other is twenty-six with six <s>tilas</s>. When done thus, the twelfth part of the wing-length — nineteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and two <s>tilas</s> — becomes the brick-breadth. This is the first <s>karaṇa</s>. For [the altar] without <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], the wing-length is diminished by thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Accordingly, the bending of bricks follows proportionally. There the diagonals are twenty-one and twenty-nine, each with three <s>tilas</s>.
Those two ... second
They are joined such that [the result] becomes a hexahedron.
First ... third

children.text:
pañcadaśāṅgulavyāsaṃ aratnayāyāmaṃ samakarṇaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ prāgāyataṃ mūmau likhitvā prathamena prāgāyatena yuñjayāttattṛtīyam /
ṛjvavasthitameva prathamāpekṣayā natamityucyate yathāyoganatamiti /
children.translated_text: Having drawn on the ground an oblong quadrilateral of fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth, one <s>aratni</s> in length, with equal diagonals, extending eastward, one should join it with the first [brick] extending eastward — that is the third. It is called "bent" relative to the first, [though] it stands straight.
Fourth-part ... fourth

children.text:
ekā pārsvamānī pañcadaśāṅgulā /
anyā pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulā /
ekā tiryaṅnānī triṃśadaṅgulā /
anyā dvicatvāriṃśadaṅgulā sacaturdaśatilā /
children.translated_text: One lateral side is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>. Another is forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>. One transverse side is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>. Another is forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> with fourteen <s>tilas</s>.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
Half of a fourth-part [brick] is the fifth [brick-type]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.6]
Thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> on one side and fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> on the other — that is the fifth.
Its diagonal division is the sixth [brick-type]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.7]

children.text: tasya pañcamasyākṣṇayā karṇena vibhajyata iti bhedaḥṣaṣṭham /
children.translated_text: That fifth, divided diagonally by the hypotenuse — that division is the sixth.

children.text: puruṣasya pañcamabhāgaṃ daśabhāgavyāsaṃ pratīcīnam āyacchet | tasya dakṣiṇato 'nyam uttarataś ca | tāv akṣṇayā dakṣiṇāoarayoḥ koṭyor ālikhet | tat saptamam || ĀpŚus_16.8 ||
children.translated_text: One should extend [a rectangle] with one-fifth of a <s>puruṣa</s> [in length] and one-tenth in breadth, westward; of that, another to the south and another to the north; one should mark those diagonally at the south-western corners — that is the seventh. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.8]

children.text:
aratnimātrāyāmaṃ prādeśavyāsaṃ pratīcīnaṃ pratyagāyatamāyacchet /
bhūmau dakṣiṇapārśve 'nyaṃ tathāvidhamuttarataśvānyaṃ tathāvidham /
children.translated_text: One should extend [a rectangle] of one <s>aratni</s> in length and one <s>prādeśa</s> in breadth, facing westward. On the ground, another of the same kind on the southern side, and another of the same kind on the northern side.
Those should be marked diagonally with the hypotenuse, starting from the south-western corners, in the manner of a ladle (<s>sruc</s>).
That is the seventh.

children.text: evamanyat | uttaraṃ tūttarasyāḥ koṭyālikhet tad aṣṭamam || ĀpŚus_16.9 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise another; but the northern one should be marked from the northern corner — that is the eighth. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.9]

children.text: evameva kṛtvottaraṃ caturaśramuttarasyāḥ koṭyā ārabhya dakṣiṇāṃ koṭiṃ pratyālikhet srauvavattadaṣṭamam /
children.translated_text: Having done likewise, the northern quadrilateral should be marked starting from the northern corner toward the southern corner, in the manner of a spoon (<s>sruva</s>) — that is the eighth.
The diagonal divisions of a fourth-part [brick] on both sides — that is the ninth. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.10]

children.text: akṣṇayā ubhayataḥ karṇena bhedanaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ tasyāścaturbhāgīyāyāstathāvidhaṃ navamaṃ karaṇam /
children.translated_text: Diagonal on both sides — division by the hypotenuse — cutting — of that fourth-part [brick], such [a division] is the ninth <s>karaṇa</s>.
A foot-measure — the foot-brick, by three.

children.text: upadhāne ṣaṣṭiḥṣaṣṭiḥ pakṣayoḥ prathamā udīcīrnir upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_16.11 ||
children.translated_text: In the placement, sixty-by-sixty [bricks] in the wings — the first [bricks, placed] facing north, one should place. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.11]

children.text: pucchapārśvayor aṣṭāvaṣṭau ṣaṭhyayas tisro 'gre tata ekān tatas tisraḥ tata ekā || ĀpŚus_16.12 ||
children.translated_text: At the sides of the tail, eight-by-eight sixth-part [bricks]; three at the tip; then one; then three; then one. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.12]

children.text: pucchāpyaye caturthyau viśaye | tayos tu paścāt pañcamyāv anīkasaṃhite || ĀpŚus_16.12 ||
children.translated_text: At the tail-junction, fourth-part [bricks] in the domain; but behind those, fifth-part [bricks] joined at the front. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 16.12]

children.text:
upadhānakāle ekasmin pakṣe ṣaṣṭiḥ prathamā udīcīrudagāyatā nidadhyāt -- upadadhyāt triṃśatrriṃśadviparyasya kāritāḥ /
evamuttarapakṣe 'pi /
pucchasya pārśvayorubhayoḥṣaṣṭayaḥ aṣṭāvekasmin pārśve 'parasmiṃśvāṣṭau /
kathamityāha -- pucchāgre tisraḥ tāsāṃ purastādekām /
evamuttarasmin pārśve viparyasya kāritāḥ /
pucche cātmani ca sthite tiryak -- tayoś ceti tayoḥ paścātpucche anīkasaṃhite -- mukhasahinte meṣayūthavat /
children.translated_text:
At the time of laying, in one wing, sixty first-type [bricks] should be placed facing north, extending northward — one should place them in sets of thirty, alternating their orientation.
Likewise in the northern wing also.
On both sides of the tail, sixty [bricks] — eight on one side and eight on the other side.
How so, he says — three at the tip of the tail, one in front of those.
Likewise on the northern side, alternating their orientation.
Those placed in the tail and the body transversely — 'and of those two' means behind the tail, facing each other — joined face to face, like a flock of rams.
Sixteenth section.
<s>Karavinda</s>'s commentary.
[Sūtra:] 'The fourth... [is the] fifth.'
That which is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> in length and fifteen in width is the fifth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
[Sūtra:] 'Of that... the sixth.'

children.text: pañcamasyākṣṇayā bhedaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhaṃ karaṇaṃ bhavati sā pādeṣṭakā /
children.translated_text: By making a diagonal cut of the fifth [brick type], the sixth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type) is produced — that is the quarter-brick (<s>pādeṣṭakā</s>).
Of that, one [side measures] thirty-one <s>aṅgulas</s>, another fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, and the diagonal is thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> plus nineteen <s>tilas</s>.
This is the sixth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
[Sūtra:] '<s>Puruṣa</s>... [is the seventh].'

children.text: caturviṃśatyaṅgulāyāmaṃ tadardhavistāraṃ caturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca tādṛśe caturaśre /
evaṃ trīṇi caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā dakṣiṇottaracaturaśre dakṣiṇāparakoṭī pratyālikhet /
children.translated_text: Having thus made three squares, in the southern and northern squares one should mark off [a line] toward the south-western corner.
Thus the side measurements are twenty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> plus twenty-eight <s>tilas</s>.
The transverse measurements are twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
This is the seventh <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
Having made a square of twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> in length and half that in width, [one places] similar squares to its south and to its north.
[Sūtra:] 'Thus... the eighth.'

children.text: saptamavatrrīṇi caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇāparakoṭiṃ pratyālikheduttaramuttarāparakoṭiṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Having made three squares as in the seventh, one should mark off the southern [square] toward the south-western corner, and the northern toward the north-western corner.

children.text: evamapi te eva pārśvamānyau pūrvaṃ pārśvaṃ dvādaśāṅgulaṃ paścimaṃ tu ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus also for those, the side measurements: the front side is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, but the back is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>.
That indeed is the eighth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
[Sūtra:] 'The four-part... [is the ninth].'

children.text:
caturbhāgīyāyā ubhayato bhedo 'kṣṇayābhavet /
iyamapi pādeṣṭakā /
pārśvamānyau akṣṇayā ekaviṃśatyaṅgule saptatilasahite tiryagekaṃ triṃśadaṅgulam /
evaṃ navamaṃ karaṇam /
children.translated_text:
The <s>caturbhāgīyā</s> (four-part brick) should be cut diagonally on both sides.
This too is a quarter-brick (<s>pādeṣṭakā</s>).
The side measurements along the diagonal are twenty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> plus seven <s>tilas</s>; the transverse [measurement] is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>.
Thus the ninth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
Now the laying procedure is stated —
[Sūtra:] 'One should place...'

children.text:
upadhānakāle dakṣiṇe pakṣe ṣaṣṭiḥ prathamā udīcīrnidadhyāt /
uttare ca ṣaṣṭim /
chāndaso vibhaktivyatyayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
At the time of laying, sixty first-type [bricks] should be placed in the southern wing, facing north.
And sixty in the northern [wing].
The case-ending irregularity is Vedic usage.
[Sūtra:] 'In the tail... sixty.'
Eight [bricks] produced from the sixth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type) [are placed] on each side of the tail.
He states the manner of laying —
[Sūtra:] 'Three... one.'

children.text:
pucchapārśvayorityeva /
tisro 'gre pucchasya dakṣiṇaśroṇyāmekā prācī bāhyaviśeṣā /
tasyā uttarato dve nānāgre viśeṣasahite /
tayoḥ purastādekā bāhyaviśeṣā
children.translated_text:
'On the sides of the tail' is understood.
Three at the tip of the tail: at the southern hip (<s>śroṇi</s>), one [brick] facing east, with the distinguishing mark (<s>viśeṣa</s>) on the outer side.
To its north, two [bricks] with tips pointing in different directions, with distinguishing marks.
In front of those, one with the distinguishing mark on the outer side,
facing east.
In front of that, three as before.
In front of those, one as before.
Likewise on the northern side also.
[Sūtra:] 'At the tail... junction.'
At the junction of the tail and the body (<s>ātman</s>), two fourth-type [bricks serve as] distinguishing bricks (<s>viśeṣa</s>).
Without distinction, the body and the tail are level.
[Sūtra:] 'Of those two... joined.'
And of those two, as before, two fifth-type bricks serve the purpose.
<s>Anīka</s> means 'face'.
Thus joined [face to face], like rams fighting.
Sixteenth section.
<s>Sundararāja</s>'s commentary.
[Sūtra:] 'The four... the fifth.'

Thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> in length, fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in width.
A rectangle (<s>dīrghacaturaśra</s>) with equal diagonals.
[Sūtra:] 'Of that... the sixth.'
[Sūtra:] '<s>Puruṣa</s>... [the seventh].'

children.text:
yathā purastātprādeśastiryaṅbhānī paścāttu prādeśatrayam /
saptamāṣṭamayorubhayorapi pārśvaphalakāni saptaviṃśakāni ṣaṭtilonāni /
children.translated_text:
Such that in front it is one <s>prādeśa</s> (span) in the transverse measurement, but in the back it is three <s>prādeśas</s>.
For both the seventh and eighth [brick types], the side panels are twenty-seven [<s>aṅgulas</s>] minus six <s>tilas</s>.
[Sūtra:] 'The four-part... [the ninth].'

children.text:
caturbhāgīyāmubhayato 'kṣṇayābhinnāyāṃ catvāro navamā bhavanti trikoṇāḥ /
teṣāmekaṃ karaṇaṃ navamaṃ /
tasyaikaṃ phalakaṃ triṃśadaṅgulaṃ /
anye ekaviśake saptatile /
children.translated_text:
When the <s>caturbhāgīyā</s> (four-part brick) is cut diagonally on both sides, four ninth-type [bricks] are produced, which are triangular.
One of those constitutes the ninth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
One panel of it is thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The others are twenty-one [<s>aṅgulas</s>] plus seven <s>tilas</s>.
[Sūtra:] 'One should place...'
'First' means produced from the first <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type).
In 'thus sixty' and so on, [they are placed] facing north, extending northward.
[Sūtra:] 'In the tail... sixty.'

These extend eastward.
He states the manner of their laying —
[Sūtra:] 'Three... [bricks].'

Of the three, two face east.
One faces west.
[Sūtra:] 'At the tail... junction.'

children.text:
udagagrā dakṣiṇāgrā ca /
te ātmānaṃ pucchaṃ ca pañcadaśāṅgulāvete /
children.translated_text:
[One brick] with its tip northward, and [one] with its tip southward.
They [measure] fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> each, [spanning] the body and the tail.
[Sūtra:] 'Of those two... joined.'

'Joined face to face' means joined at the front.
[They are placed] extending northward.
Sixteenth section.
<s>Kapardi</s>'s commentary.

children.text: śeṣe daśa caturthyaḥ śroṇyaṃseṣu cāṣṭau prācīḥ pratīcīś ca || ĀpŚus_17.1 ||
children.translated_text: In the remainder, ten fourth-type [bricks]; and at the hips (<s>śroṇi</s>) and shoulders (<s>aṃsa</s>), eight [bricks] facing east and facing west. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.1]

children.text:
pucchaśeṣe caturthyo daśa tiryagāyatāḥ /
śroṇyaṃseṣu cāṣṭau śroṇyāścatasraḥ prāgāyatāḥ /
uttarasyāṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ ca viparyasya kāritāḥ /
aṃsayośvaivam /
children.translated_text:
In the remainder of the tail, ten fourth-type [bricks] extending transversely.
At the hips and shoulders, eight — four at each hip, facing east.
On the northern and southern [sides], alternating their orientation.
And likewise at the shoulders.

children.text: śeṣe ca ṣaḍviṃśatir aṣṭau ṣaṣṭayaś catasraḥ pañcamyaḥ || ĀpŚus_17.2 ||
children.translated_text: And in the remainder, twenty-six [fourth-type bricks], eight sixth-type, and four fifth-type [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.2]

children.text:
ātmani śeṣe śiṣṭe deśe ṣaḍviṃśatiścaturthyaḥ /
aṣṭau catasraḥ pañcamyaḥ /
tāsāmupadhānamārga ucyate -- viśayānāṃ mārge tiryagātmani caturdaśa caturthyaḥ /
tāsāṃ pārśvayordve dve prācyau ca viparyasya kārite /
uttare pārśve caturdaśānāmeva pārśvayormadhye dve dve tiryak /

children.translated_text: These twenty-six fourth-type [bricks] are thus laid.
Four [bricks] made from the <s>caturbhāgīyā</s> (four-part brick) are placed at the corners.
Among those, four fifth-type [bricks are placed] transversely.
And eight sixth-type [bricks] are placed transversely as well.

In the remainder of the body (<s>ātman</s>), in the remaining space, twenty-six fourth-type [bricks], eight [sixth-type], and four fifth-type.
The path of their laying is stated — along the path of the distinguishing bricks (<s>viśeṣa</s>), fourteen fourth-type [bricks are placed] transversely in the body.
Of those, two on each side facing east, alternating their orientation.
On the northern side, among the fourteen, two each in the middle of the sides, placed transversely.

children.text: śirasi caturthyau viśaye | tayoś ca purastāt prācyau || ĀpŚus_17.3 ||
children.translated_text: In the head, two fourth-type [bricks serve as] distinguishing bricks; and in front of those two, [two bricks] facing east. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.3]
This is the layer (<s>prastāra</s>) of two hundred [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.4]

children.text:
tayorviśayayoḥ purastātprācyau caturthyau viparyasya kāritā dakṣiṇataḥ /
eṣeti /
kirmathamidam yāvatā dviśata eva? paribhāṣeyam /
yo 'yaṃ prastāro dviśata(ḥsa) iti paribhāṣyate /
saṅkhyāṃ pūrayedityukte dviśata eva pūryate /
itarathā kā saṃkhyā pūrayitavyeti na jñāyate /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, what number is to be completed would not be known.
If one says 'there is the number one thousand' — no.
The statement 'one should complete [the number] for each layer' would become meaningless.
Therefore this is a governing rule (<s>paribhāṣā</s>).

In front of those two distinguishing bricks, two fourth-type [bricks] facing east, with their orientation alternated from the south.
'This' — this has been explained.
What is the purpose of this statement, since it is indeed two hundred? This is a governing rule (<s>paribhāṣā</s>).
This layer is declared to be of two hundred — thus it is defined as a rule.
When it is said 'one should complete the number,' exactly two hundred are to be completed.

children.text: aparasmin prastāre pañcapañca nirṇāmayordvitīyāḥ | apyayayoś ca tṛtīyā ātmānam aṣṭabhāgāvetāḥ || ĀpŚus_17.5a ||
children.translated_text: In the other layer, five and five second-type [bricks] at the bends (<s>nirṇāma</s>); and at the junctions (<s>apyaya</s>), third-type [bricks]; these extend [only] an eighth part into the body. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.5a]

children.text:
dvitīyā vakrībhūtāḥ /
nirṇāmo vakrapradeśaḥ /
tasmin pradeśe pañcapañca dvitīyāḥ /
apyayayoś ca tṛtīyāḥ -- pakṣāpyayayośtṛtīyā ātmānamaṣṭabhāgāvetā vyāptāḥ /
caturbhāgīyeṣṭakāmātramātmani sthitāḥ /
pañchapañca viparyasya kāritā uttare pakṣāpyaye /
children.translated_text:
The second-type [bricks] are curved.
<s>Nirṇāma</s> means the curved region.
In that region, five and five second-type [bricks].
'And at the junctions, third-type' — at the junctions of the wings (<s>pakṣāpyaya</s>), third-type [bricks] extend into the body by an eighth part.
They are positioned [only] to the extent of a <s>caturbhāgīyā</s> (four-part) brick within the body.
Five and five [bricks], alternating their orientation, at the northern wing-junction.
In the remainder, forty-five first-type [bricks] facing east. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.5b]

children.text:
dakṣiṇe pārśve pañcaviṃśatiḥ /
dakṣiṇe pakṣe uttare pārśve pañcaviṃśatiruttare pakṣeviṃśatiḥ /
children.translated_text:
Twenty-five on the southern side.
In the southern wing, on the northern side twenty-five; in the northern wing, twenty.
On the sides of the tail, five and five seventh-type [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.6a]
On the northern side, alternating their orientation.
In the second and fourth [rows], one [brick] joined on either side. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.6b]

children.text: dvitīyāyāṃ rītyāṃ catutharyāṃ ca rītyāṃ anyasminpārśve ekaikā saptamī /
children.translated_text: In the second row and in the fourth row, one seventh-type [brick] on the other side.
One on the southern side, with its orientation alternated.
Another on the northern side.
In the remainder, thirteen eighth-type [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.6c]
In the tail area, thirteen eighth-type [bricks] lie.

children.text: śroṇyaṃseṣu cāṣṭau caturthyo dakṣiṇā udīcīś ca || ĀpŚus_17.7a ||
children.translated_text: And at the hips and shoulders, eight fourth-type [bricks] facing south and facing north. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.7a]
At the southern [hip], [they are placed] extending southward, with their orientation alternated.
At the northern hip, [they are placed] extending northward.
At the southern shoulder, [they are placed] extending northward, with their orientation alternated.

children.text: śeṣe ca viṃśatis triṃśat ṣaṣṭhayaḥ ekāṃ pañcamīm || ĀpŚus_17.7b ||
children.translated_text: And in the remainder, twenty [fourth-type bricks], thirty sixth-type, and one fifth-type. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.7b]

children.text:
cakāreṇa caturthyo 'nukṛṣyante /
triṃśat ṣaṣṭhayaḥ ekā ca pañcamī /
tāsāmupādhānadeśa ucyate -- ātmano dakṣiṇe pārśve daśa catur thyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The place of their laying is stated — on the southern side of the body, ten fourth-type [bricks].

children.text: pañca prācīḥ pañca pratīcīḥ evamuttare pārśve /
children.translated_text: Five facing east, five facing west; likewise on the northern side.

children.text: madhye triṃśat ṣaṣṭhayaḥ prācīḥ ekā ca pañcamī /
children.translated_text: In the middle, thirty sixth-type [bricks] facing east, and one fifth-type.
Of those, fifteen face east.

By the word 'and,' the fourth-type [bricks] are carried over.
Thirty sixth-type and one fifth-type.

children.text: śirasi caturthyau tayoś ca purastāccatasro navamyaḥ || ĀpŚus_17.8 ||
children.translated_text: In the head, two fourth-type [distinguishing bricks]; and in front of those, four ninth-type [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.8]
This is the layer of two hundred [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.9]

children.text: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_17.10 ||
children.translated_text: One should build with alternation, for as many layers as one wishes to construct. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 17.10]

children.text:
navamyaścatasraḥ purastāt /
eṣeti -- gatametat /
kimarthamidam? niyamārtham /
kimatra niyamyate? viṣamadviśataprastāro niyamyate nopari śyenaḥ /
śyena eva niyamyate nānyaḥ /
kathamavagamyate nānya iti? prastārapūraṇavacanāt -- tatrāpi vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādityetadevoktaṃ na pūraṇavacanam /
tasmādanye dviśataprastārāḥ /
atraiva paribhāṣitatvāt /
iṣṭakākaraṇe pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulaṃ dakṣiṇena gṛhītvā caturthīḥ kārayet /
viparyastāḥ savye /
vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādyāvataḥ prastārāṃścikīrṣet iti /
gatametat /
atra ślokā bhavanti --
children.translated_text:
Four ninth-type [bricks are placed] in front.
'This' — that has been explained.
What is the purpose of this [statement]? It is for the sake of a restrictive rule (<s>niyama</s>).
What is restricted here? The odd layer of two hundred is restricted — not the upper hawk [altar].
Only the hawk [altar] is restricted, not another [form].
How is it understood that not another? From the statement about completing the layer — but even there, 'one should build with alternation' is what is stated, not a statement about completion.
Therefore the other layers are also of two hundred, since the rule is established here itself.
In making the bricks, taking forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> to the south, one should make fourth-type [bricks].
The reversed ones [are placed] on the left.
