'One should build with alternation, for as many layers as one wishes to construct' — this has been explained.
Here there are verses —
Nineteen <s>aṅgulas</s> transversely, plus two <s>tilas</s>,

children.text: yathā bhavettathā kāryā yathāyoganataṃ tu tat //
children.translated_text: it should be made accordingly; the curvature is as required.
Just as the northward [measurement] in the sixth part, the increase by the sixth part,
of the third <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type), the curvature should be as required.
The distinguishing [measurement] of the fourth [brick type] is forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>,
combined with fourteen <s>tilas</s> — this will be the [measurement] of the <s>karaṇa</s>.
The diagonal panel of the sixth [brick type] would be thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s>,
combined with eighteen <s>tilas</s>; the others are determined by the cord.
The side [measurements] of the seventh are twenty [<s>aṅgulas</s>] together with seven,
minus six <s>tilas</s>; and the panels of the eighth are likewise.
With the first and third [brick types], alternating again and again,
and likewise with the seventh and sixth, one should make bricks for the ritual.
Alternating thirty-five, one should also make [bricks] with the fourth [type].
This much the skilled ones know about the making of bricks.
In the tail, ten fourth-type [bricks] are to be placed transversely, as prescribed.
And those which are in between — fourteen fourth-type [bricks] should be placed transversely.
Fourth-type [bricks] on the sides of those, six on each side, transversely in the middle.
At the corners, fifth-type [bricks] transversely, and eight sixth-type [bricks] likewise.
From the junction of the tail likewise; in the head, thirty is prescribed.

children.text: prācyaśvaiva pratīcyaś ca prācīṣveva ca pañcamī //
children.translated_text: Both those facing east and those facing west; and a fifth-type among those facing east.

children.text: caturthyaḥ pārśvayostāsāṃ tathā śiṣṭe ca viṃśatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Fourth-type [bricks] on the sides of those, and likewise twenty in the remainder.
All else is according to the <s>sūtra</s>; the layer in the ritual is of two hundred.

children.text: śroṇyā caiva tathaivāṃsau ṣaṭsu tveva tatāvidhā /
children.translated_text: At the hip and likewise the shoulders, in [all] six, of the same type,
fourth-type [bricks] ... on the southern [side, they are] not overlapping.
At the hips, [the orientation] should be understood as southward; and likewise at the shoulders, northward.
Thus in the commentary on the <s>Āpastamba Sūtra</s>, in <s>Kapardisvāmin</s>'s <s>bhāṣya</s>, in the section called <s>Śulba</s>,
the fifth <s>paṭala</s> (chapter).
<s>Karavinda</s>'s commentary.

children.text:
śeṣer -- thyaḥ
pucche daśa caturthakaraṇaniṣpannāḥ tiryagāyatāḥ //
children.translated_text:
[Sūtra:] 'In the remainder... [fourth]-type.'
In the tail, ten [bricks] produced from the fourth <s>karaṇa</s> (brick type), extending transversely.
[Sūtra:] 'At the hips and shoulders... and.'
Thus four at the hips; on the northern side, alternating their orientation.
[Sūtra:] 'In the remainder... fifth-type.'

children.text:
śeṣe ceti cakārāccaturthyo 'nuṣajyante /
ātmaśeṣe ṣaḍviṃśatiścaturthyaḥ /
aṣṭau ca ṣaṣṭayaḥ /
catasraḥ pañcamyaḥ /
tā etā aṣṭātriṃśat /
asāmupadhānamucyate --
children.translated_text:
'And in the remainder' — by the word 'and,' the fourth-type [bricks] are carried over.
In the remainder of the body, twenty-six fourth-type [bricks].
And eight sixth-type.
Four fifth-type.
These are thirty-eight.
The laying [procedure] for them is stated —
[Sūtra:] 'In the head... placed.'

children.text:
pucchagataviśayānāṃ madhye tiryagātmani caturdaśa caturthyaḥ prācyo rītayaḥ /
tāsāṃ pārśvayoḥ paścāddvedve purastā dvedve dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca /
tā aṣṭau /
aṣṭānāṃ catasraḥ prācyaścatasraḥ pratīcyaḥ /
caturdaśānāmeva pārśvayormadhye dakṣiṇata uttarataś ca dvedve /
tāścatasraḥ /
evaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatiścaturthyaḥ /
atrānupahitāḥ koṇek /
catvāraśvatu rbhāgīyādeśāḥ /

children.translated_text: Among those, four fifth-[size bricks are placed] transversely.
In the sixty[-brick arrangement], eight [are placed] transversely only.

children.text: śirasi pratyekaṃ dakṣiṇottarataḥ prācyau tayorviṃśayayoḥ purataḥ prācyau caturthyau /
children.translated_text: At the head, on each side, south and north, [are] eastward [bricks]; in front of each group of twenty, two eastward fourth-[size bricks].
Thus [is] the outer modification.

In the middle of the tail-region, along the transverse body-line, fourteen fourth-[size bricks form] eastward courses.
On the sides of those, two-two behind, two-two in front, on the south and on the north.
Those are eight.
Of the eight, four face east, four face west.
Of the fourteen themselves, on the sides, in the middle, on the south and on the north, two-two.
Those are four.
Thus twenty-six fourth-[size bricks].
Here the corners are unfilled.
Four are the quarter-[brick] substitutions.
This is the two-hundred [brick] layer.

children.text: upadānavidhigatadeśādi saṃkhyāsamudāyavaśena prastāre śatadvaye siddhe 'pi dviśataḥ prastāra iti vacanaṃ prastāre dviśatatvasiddhikaraṇāya //
children.translated_text: Although the two hundreds in the layer are established by the aggregate count of positions etc. obtained through the placement-rule, the statement 'this is the two-hundred layer' serves to confirm the total of two hundred in the layer.
The curved portions —
The <s>nirṇāma</s> (curvature) is stated to be the curved region in the middle of the wings.
In that [region], second-[size bricks], five each on the south and north wings, should be placed conforming to the curvature.
And the curved [bricks] —
The curved third-mould [bricks], five each, having absorbed themselves by an eighth part increase, [absorb] the wing by a sixth part.
In the remainder — eastward —
On the southern side of the southern wing, twenty-five.
On the northern side of the northern wing, twenty-five; on the southern [side], twenty.
In the tail — [seventh-size bricks] —
On the southern side of the tail, five seventh-[size bricks].
On the northern side, five [form] eastward courses.
The second — [up to a certain number] —
By this, the placement of other seventh-[size bricks] in the other [positions] is stated.
In one of the seventh-[size brick] courses on the sides of the tail, [place] a second [brick],
one adjoined [brick] in one [course], and one adjoined fourth-[size brick] and one seventh-[size brick] should be placed in the other [course].
Thus twelve seventh-[size bricks] are placed.
In the remainder — eighth-[size bricks] —

children.text:
pucchaśeṣe aṣṭamakaraṇotpannāḥ trayodaśodīcyaḥ pañca rītayaḥ /
pucchāgre pārśvagatayoḥsaptamyormadhye pañcāṣṭamyau /
nanāgrā dvitīyāyām /
tisṛṇāṃ saptamīnāṃ madhye tisro 'ṣṭamyaḥ /

children.translated_text: And in the third [course], three.
In the fourth course, between three seventh-[size bricks], one.
In the fifth course, between [two] seventh-[size bricks], one.

children.text: evaṃ trayodaśāṣṭamyaḥ yathāyogaṃ prāgagrāḥ pratyagagrāś ca bhaveyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus thirteen eighth-[size bricks], as appropriate, should face eastward or westward.

In the remainder of the tail, thirteen [bricks] produced from the eighth mould, northward, [form] five courses.
At the tip of the tail, between the two side seventh-[size bricks], five eighth-[size bricks].
With different orientation in the second [course].
Between three seventh-[size bricks], three eighth-[size bricks].
From the haunches and shoulders — the haunches and [shoulders] —
At the haunches, four each — two-two on the southern [haunches] face south, on the northern [haunches] face north.
All are outer modifications.
In the remainder — [ninth-size bricks] —
In the remainder of the body, twenty.
By the word 'ca' (and), in the absence of [explicit] statement, two fourth-[size bricks] at the head.
And in front of those, four ninth-[size bricks].
This is the two-hundred [brick] layer.
The statement of 'two hundred' is to remove the doubt that the layer is not necessarily of two hundred.
In alternation — one should lay —
Already explained.

children.text:
atha phalakānāṃ prajambhanamucyate -- prathamakaraṇasya viṃśatyaṅgulā tiryaṅmānī prajambhite yathaikonaviṃśatiraṅgulayaḥsāṣṭādaśatiladvayaṃ ca ṛjvavasthitā bhavati, tathā karaṇaṃ prajambhayet /
vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa dvitīyasya karaṇasya pakṣanamnī caturviṃśatyaṅgulā sārdhasaptatilā /
tasyāḥṣaṣṭho bhāgaścatasro 'hgulayaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now the bending of the boards is stated — the first mould's transverse measure of twenty <s>aṅgulas</s>, when bent, should be bent such that nineteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and eight-eighteenths of two <s>tilās</s> stand straight.
By the method to be described, the second mould's wing-measure is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> and three-and-a-half <s>tilās</s>.
Its sixth part is four <s>aṅgulas</s>

children.text:
sapādatilaś ca /
tena dvitīyakaraṇasya dīrghatayā catvāriṃśadahgulayoḥ phalakayormadhye catuviṃśatyaṅgule ekasminnunnatiṃ ca kuryāt; yathā tasya bhāgadvayamekaikaśaḥ pūrvakarṇasadṛśaṃ bhavati tatheti /
dṛtīyasya tu ṣaṣṭhāṣṭabhāgasandhau namanaṃ /
ṣaṣṭhaṃ bhāgaṃ pūrvavannamayet /
aṣṭamasya tu namanamātmānurūpaṃ ṛjvavasthānameva /
tasminnamanaṃ ṣaṣṭhāpekṣayā /
children.translated_text:
and a quarter <s>tilā</s>.
Thereby, between the two boards of forty <s>aṅgulas</s> in the length of the second mould, one should make an elevation at one [board of] twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s>; such that each of its two parts becomes equal to the former diagonal — thus.
For the third [mould], the bending is at the junction of the sixth and eighth parts.
The sixth part should be bent as before.
For the eighth [part], the bending conforming to itself is simply standing straight.
The bending in that is relative to the sixth.
On this, the verses —
In the <s>śyenaciti</s> (hawk-altar), first, the bending of the first mould [is described],
and the board-bending of the second and third [moulds] is stated.
In this <s>śyenaciti</s>, the bending of the first mould,
the wing-<s>karaṇī</s> of the tail, and of the sixth [part], how [it should be made] straight.
The result of the bending of the wing-boards of the second and third [moulds],
the wing-<s>karaṇī</s> of the diameter — the bending in the first [is from] the sixth-[part] measure.
Nineteen <s>aṅgulas</s> and an eighth part with two <s>tilās</s> —

children.text: tiryaṅbhānī yatā sā syāttathā rajjvā prajambhayet //
children.translated_text: the transverse measure being thus, one should bend accordingly with a cord.
With [an amount] consisting of four <s>aṅgulas</s> joined with a quarter <s>tilā</s>,
the sixth [part] is the bending-measure of the wing — thereby the board-bending is [achieved].
Thus, having raised [the brick] by the method stated for the second <s>śyenaciti</s>,
the bending of the mould should be performed, and likewise the bending of the boards.
Thus [ends] the fifth chapter in the <s>Śulbapratīpikā</s> composed by <s>Karavinda Svāmin</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
In the remainder — [bricks] —
In the tail, northward-extending.
The haunches and shoulders —
At the haunches and shoulders of the body, two-two [are] outer modifications.
In the remainder, fifth-[size bricks] —

children.text:
ātmaśeṣe ṣaḍviṃśaticaturthyaḥ prācyaḥ pratīcyaḥ /
tatra madhyarītyoḥ saptasaptodagagrā dakṣiṇāgrāś ca /
dvitīyapañcamarītyoḥ pañcapañca matāḥ /
samamadhye dakṣiṇottare anyāḥ prākpratīcyaḥ /
ādyantarītyormadhye ekaikacaturthyau dakṣiṇottarayoḥ paścātpurastācca dvedve ṣaṣṭhayau /
tāśvāṣṭau dakṣiṇottarāḥ /
tadrītyoḥ śeṣe catasraḥ pañcamya udagāyatāḥ /
children.translated_text:
In the remainder of the body, twenty-six fourth-[size bricks], eastward and westward.
There, in the middle courses, seven-seven face north and south.
In the second and fifth courses, five-five are designated.
The rest in the equal-middle, on south and north, [face] east and west.
In the middle of the first and last courses, one-one fourth-[size brick] each; on south and north, behind and in front, two-two sixth-[size bricks].
Those eight [face] south and north.
In the remainder of those courses, four fifth-[size bricks] extending northward.
At the head, two fourth-[size bricks] in the field.
The junction [is] as the tail-junction.
Of those, two [face] eastward.
The outer modification [consists of] two fourth-[size bricks].
This is the layer.
Therefore, effort should be made here to complete the count — this is the meaning.
The other — one-one each —

children.text: anyatarataḥ dakṣiṇe pārśve uttare vā dvitīyacaturthībhyāṃ saptamībhyāṃ saṃhitāmekāṃ saptamīmantarupadadhyāt //
children.translated_text: On either side — on the southern side or the northern — one seventh-[size brick] adjoined with the second and fourth-[size bricks] should be placed inside.
In the remainder, eighth-[size bricks] —
In the remainder of the tail.
The haunches, shoulders, and [body] —
Two-two [are] outer modifications.
In the remainder, fifth-[size bricks] —
In the remainder of the body, twenty fourth-[size bricks] extending eastward.
In the middle, with eastward-extending sixth-[size bricks], thirty-two [form] two courses.

children.text: tayordakṣiṇasyāṃ dve uddhṛtya ekāṃ pañcamīṃ nidadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Of those, in the southern [course], removing two, one should place one fifth-[size brick].
At the head, two fourth-[size bricks],
extending northward.
Of those, [the seventh-size bricks] —
extending northward.
This is the layer — in alternation, one should lay.

children.text: iti śrī sundararājakṛtāyāṃ śulbapradīpikāyāṃ pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifth chapter in the <s>Śulbapradīpikā</s> composed by Śrī <s>Sundararāja</s>.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: śyenacitaṃ cinvīta suvargakāma iti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_18.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'One desiring heaven should construct the <s>śyenaciti</s> (hawk-shaped fire-altar)' — thus it is known from scripture.

children.text: vakrapakṣo vyastapuccho bhavati | paścāt prāṅ udūhati | purastāt pratyaṅ udūhati | evam iva hi vayasāṃ madhye pakṣanirṇāmo bhavatīti vijñāyate || ĀpŚus_18.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'It has curved wings and a spread tail. From behind it draws forward; from the front it draws backward. For thus indeed the wing-curvature occurs in the middle of birds' — thus it is known from scripture.

children.text:
asyāḥ śruteḥ punarupanyāso mārgāntaraṃ pratipādayitum /
athavā anyaivaiṣā śrutiḥ /
iyamevākāramārgatā /
vakreti -- gatametat /
children.translated_text:
This scripture is cited again to present an alternative method.
Or else, this is a different scripture altogether.
This one itself conveys the form-method.
'Curved' — this has been explained.

children.text: puruṣasya ṣoḍaśabhir viṃśaṃ śataṃ sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate | tāsāṃ catvāriṃśadātmani tisraḥ śirasi pañcadaśa puccha ekatriṃśad dakṣiṇe pakṣe tathottare || ĀpŚus_18.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'With sixteen [parts] of the <s>puruṣa</s>, one hundred and twenty together with an <s>aratni-prādeśa</s> [measure], seven-fold [division] is obtained. Of those, forty in the body, three in the head, fifteen in the tail, thirty-one in the southern wing, and likewise in the northern.'

children.text:
puruṣasya ṣoḍaśamāgaḥ ṣoḍaśī /
tābhirviṃśottaraṃ śataṃ saṃpadyate /
parigaṇanāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ etāvatyaḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ saptārdhe śerate /
sapta sthāpayitvā ṣoḍaśībhirguṇite dvādaśottaraṃ śatam /
ardhapuruṣe dvādaśasu aṣṭau /
kṣipte viṃśatiḥ /
evaṃ viṃśottaraṃ śataṃ sampannam /
tāsāmiti -- tāsāṃ ṣoḍaśīnāṃ catvāriṃśadātmanyupadheyāḥ; tisraḥśirasi; sarvatra nidheyā iti śeṣaḥ /
pañcadaśa pucche /
dakṣiṇe pakṣe ekatriṃśat tathottare /
ekatriṃśaduttare pakṣe /
kathametā nidheyā ityucyate --
children.translated_text:
A sixteenth of the <s>puruṣa</s> is a <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> (sixteenth-part).
With those, one hundred and twenty is obtained.
When the enumeration is carried out, this many <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> lie in seven-and-a-half.
Having established seven, multiplied by the <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, one hundred and twelve.
In the half-<s>puruṣa</s>, among twelve, eight.
When added, twenty.
Thus one hundred and twenty is completed.
'Of those' — of those <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, forty should be placed in the body; three in the head; the remainder [is] to be placed everywhere.
Fifteen in the tail.
Thirty-one in the southern wing, likewise in the northern.
Thirty-one in the northern wing.
How these should be placed is now stated —

children.text: adhyardhapuruṣas tiryag dvāv āyāmata iti dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya śroṇyaṃsebhyo dve dve ṣoḍasyau nirasyet | catvāriṃśat pariśiṣyante | sa ātmā || ĀpŚus_18.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having drawn a rectangular [figure] one-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> transversely and two [<s>puruṣas</s>] in length, one should remove from the haunches and shoulders two-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> each. Forty remain. That is the body.'

children.text: evaṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya śroṇībhyāmaṃsābhyāṃ ca dve dve ṣoḍaśyau pratyekaṃ nirasyet -- tyajet /
children.translated_text: Having thus drawn a rectangle, from the haunches and shoulders, two-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be removed — discarded — from each.

children.text: akṣṇayā .... yathā śroṇyaṃseṣu catvāri caturaśrāṇi ardhapuruṣapramāṇāni kṛtvā akṣṇayānyārdhāni nirasyet /
children.translated_text: Diagonally... having made four squares of half-<s>puruṣa</s> measure at the haunches and shoulders, one should remove their diagonal halves.
The remainder is forty.
That is the body.
One-and-a-half <s>puruṣas</s> is the transverse measure; two <s>puruṣas</s> is the side-measure.

children.text: śirasyardhapuruṣeṇa caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhāt tāvati dakṣiṇottarayor nipātayet || ĀpŚus_18.5a ||
children.translated_text: 'At the head, having made a square with half a <s>puruṣa</s>, from the middle of the forward side, one should drop [lines] of equal length to south and north.'
This has been explained.
'Three remain. That is the head.'

Three remain.
That is the head.

children.text: puruṣas tiryag dvāv āyāmataḥ ṣoḍaśabhāgaś ca dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | tathottaraḥ || ĀpŚus_18.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'One <s>puruṣa</s> transversely and two in length, and a sixteenth part — [that is] the southern wing. Likewise the northern.'
One <s>puruṣa</s>-measure is the transverse extent.
Two <s>puruṣas</s> is the side-measure.
The sixteenth part of a <s>puruṣa</s>, half being eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, is the <s>cāmā</s> (overlap) in the southern wing.
Likewise for the northern wing.

children.text: pakṣāgrepakṣāgre puruṣacaturthena catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā tāny akṣṇayā vyavalikhyārdhāni nirasyet | ekatriṃśat pariśiṣyante || ĀpŚus_18.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'At each wing-tip, having made four squares with a quarter <s>puruṣa</s>, having marked them diagonally, one should remove the halves. Thirty-one remain.'

children.text: pakṣayoragre pratyekaṃ puruṣacaturthapramāṇena catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā tānyakṣṇayā karṇemālikhya ardhāni nirasyet /

children.translated_text: The portions projecting outward like needle-points at the southern wing-tips should be removed.
In a two-<s>puruṣa</s> length, there are thirty-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
And one more by the sixteenth part.
Of those, with two discarded, thirty-one remain.
At the tip of each wing, having made four squares of quarter-<s>puruṣa</s> measure, having marked them diagonally with the hypotenuse, the halves should be removed.

children.text: pakṣāgram utsṛjya madhye pakṣasya prācīṃ lekhām ālikhet || ĀpŚus_18.8a ||
children.translated_text: 'Leaving aside the wing-tip, one should draw an eastward line in the middle of the wing.'
'Wing-tip' indicates the squares made with a quarter <s>puruṣa</s>.
The meaning is: leaving aside half of a quarter-<s>puruṣa</s> in the wing-length.
One should draw a line extending eastward in the middle of the wing.

children.text: pakṣāpyaye puruṣaṃ niyamya lekhāyāṃ puruṣānte nitodantukuryāt | nitodāt prācīnaṃ puruṣānte nitodaṃ nitodayor nānāntāv ālikhet | tatpakṣinamanam | etenottaraḥ pakṣo vyākhyātaḥ || ĀpŚus_18.8b ||
children.translated_text: 'At the wing-junction, having fixed a <s>puruṣa</s>[-measure] on the line, at the end of the <s>puruṣa</s> one should make a mark. From the mark, eastward, at the end of a <s>puruṣa</s>, [make another] mark. From the two marks, one should draw lines diverging to different ends. That is the wing-curvature. By this, the northern wing is explained.'

children.text:
ātmapakṣasandhau puruṣamātraṃ veṇuṃ niyamya lekhāyāmeva puruṣasyānte veṇorante lakṣaṇaṃ kuryāt /
tasmānnitodātpāgāyataṃ prācīnaṃ veṇuṃ lekhāyāmeva nidhāyāntye chidre śaṅkuṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vā nihatya nitodayorantau nānā ālikhet /

children.translated_text: From the latter mark, one should draw up to the farther end.
And from the former mark, one should draw up to the nearer end.
That is the wing-curvature — the bending of the wing.
By this, the curvature of the northern wing should also be done similarly.

At the body-wing junction, having fixed a <s>veṇu</s> (measuring reed) of one <s>puruṣa</s>-measure, on that very line, at the end of the <s>puruṣa</s>, at the end of the <s>veṇu</s>, one should make a mark or sign.
From that mark, extending eastward, having placed the <s>veṇu</s> eastward on that very line, at the other end, having fixed a peg or mark, one should draw [lines] diverging from the ends of the two marks.
Eighteenth section.

children.text: dvipuruṣaṃ pascādardhapuruṣaṃ purastāc caturbhāgonaḥ puruṣa āyāmo 'ṣṭādaśakaraṇyo pārśvayos tāḥ pañcadaśaparigṛhṇanti | tat puccham || ĀpŚus_19.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Two <s>puruṣas</s> behind, half a <s>puruṣa</s> in front, the length diminished by a quarter — eighteen <s>karaṇīs</s> on the sides — those encompass fifteen. That is the tail.'

children.text:
paścāttiryaṅbhānī dvipuruṣā /
purastādardhapuruṣā /
pādonapuruṣāyāmā /
pārśvayoraṣṭādaśaṣoḍaśīḥ karoti /
aṣṭādaśakaraṇī sā pārśvayoḥ /
tā etāḥ pañcadaśaṣoḍaśīḥ parigṛhranti /
kathamardhapuruṣavyāsā pādonapuruṣāyāmā ṣaṭkaroti? tasyābhiyo dve caturaśre same sarvataḥ pādonapuruṣamātre /
tāvakṣṇayā likhet /
ekaikamardhaṃ tyajet /

children.translated_text: The remainder makes four-and-a-half each.
Four-and-a-half plus four-and-a-half equals nine.
When six are added to nine, [there are] fifteen.
That is the tail.

Behind, the transverse [measurement] is two <s>puruṣas</s>. In front, half a <s>puruṣa</s>. The length is a <s>puruṣa</s> diminished by a quarter. On the sides, he makes eighteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> (sixteenth-parts). The <s>karaṇī</s> (diagonal) of eighteen — that is on the sides. These encompass fifteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. How does [an area] half a <s>puruṣa</s> wide and a quarter-less <s>puruṣa</s> long make six [<s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>]? On both sides of it, two equal squares, each of quarter-less <s>puruṣa</s> measure on all sides. One should draw those diagonally. One should discard one half of each.
<s>Karavindīya's</s> commentary.
'Hawk' — [commentary up to] 'known from scripture.'

children.text:
dvitīyaśyenamupadeṣṭuṃ saiva śrutiḥ punarapi paṭhitā /
tatra viśeṣamāha ------
children.translated_text: To teach the second hawk-altar, that same <s>śruti</s> is recited again. Therein, he states the distinction —
'Of a <s>puruṣa</s>' — [up to] 'with the addition.'

children.text:
ṣoḍaśīḥ -- ṣoḍaśabhāgaparimitāḥ /
tābhiḥ ṣoḍaśībiḥ /
sāratniprādeśaḥsaptavidho 'gnirviṃśatiśataṃ saṃpadyate /
tathāhi -- sapta sthāpayitvā ṣoḍaśībirguṇite dvādaśottaraṃ śataṃ bhavati /
ardhe ṣoḍaśībhirguṇite aṣṭau /
teṣvaṣṭasu kṣipteṣu viṃśatyuttaraṃ śataṃ ṣoḍaśyo bhavanti /
tāsāṃ catvāriṃśadātmani catvāriṃśat ṣoḍaśinīkṣetrāṇyātmetyarthaḥ /
tisrāḥśirasi ṣoḍaśyaḥsyuḥ /
pañcadaśa pucche /
pañcadaśaṣoḍaśyaḥ pucchakṣetram /
ekatriṃśaddakṣiṇe pakṣe /
tathottare pakṣe /
ekātriṃśat ṣoḍaśīkṣetraṃ dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣa uttaraś ca /
evaṃ vibhajya vimānamāha ----
children.translated_text: <s>Ṣoḍaśīs</s> — measured by the sixteenth part. With those <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, the seven-fold fire[-altar] with <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> [additions] turns out to be one hundred and twenty. Thus: having placed seven [rows], multiplied by <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, there are one hundred and twelve. When multiplied by <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> in the half, [there are] eight. When those eight are added, there are one hundred and twenty <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. Of those, forty in the body — forty <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>-fields in the body, is the meaning. Three <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> would be in the head. Fifteen in the tail. Fifteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> [form] the tail-field. Thirty-one in the right wing. Likewise in the left wing. Thirty-one <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>-fields [form] the right wing and the left [wing]. Having thus divided, he states the measurement —
'One-and-a-half' — [up to] 'body.'

children.text:
anupṛṣṭhayaṃ catvāriṃśaddve śate cāṅgulaya āyāmaḥ /
vistāro 'śītiśatamaṅgulyastiryak /
evaṃ dīrghaṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya śroṇyaṃseṣvardhapuruṣapramāṇāni catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā tānyātmapārśvamānīniṣṭhakoṇataḥ tiryaṅbhānīniṣṭhakoṇaṃ pratyakṣṇayālikhet /
lekhānāṃ bahirbhūtāstyajet /
catvāriṃśadavaśiṣyante /
sa ātmā bhavati /
katham? āyāmato 'ṣṭau ṣoḍaśyaḥ /
tiryak ṣaṭ /
aṣṭau ṣaḍguṇitā aṣṭācatvāriṃśat /
tatra śroṇyaṃsebhyo dvedve nirasyāṣṭau nirastā
children.translated_text: Lengthwise, two hundred and forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> is the length. The width is one hundred and eighty <s>aṅgulas</s> crosswise. Having thus laid out the long rectangle, at the hips and shoulders, having made four squares of half-<s>puruṣa</s> measure, drawing diagonally from the body-side inner corners to the transverse inner corners, one should discard [the portions] outside the lines. Forty remain. That is the body. How? Lengthwise, eight <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. Crosswise, six. Eight multiplied by six is forty-eight. From those, removing two each from the hips and shoulders, eight are removed,
[and they] become [the discarded portions].
The remaining forty are in the body.
'In the head' — [up to] 'the head.'

children.text: śiraḥ pradeśe ātmanoṃ'sayoḥ purataḥ pṛṣṭhayāyāmardhapuruṣeṇa caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyāḥ ityādikṛte tisraḥ pariśiṣyante /
children.translated_text: In the head region, in front of the body's shoulders, having made a square with the lengthwise half-<s>puruṣa</s> measurement, by the method starting with 'of the front <s>karaṇī</s>' etc., three remain.
That becomes the head.
'<s>Puruṣa</s>' — [up to] 'with the addition.'
The transverse length is one <s>puruṣa</s> measure.
Two <s>puruṣas</s> in length, and half-of-an-eighth <s>aṅgulas</s> [in addition].
Thus, having made a long rectangle for the right wing,
likewise also for the left.
'Wing-tip' — [up to] 'end.'

children.text:
pakṣsyāgre puruṣacaturthena triṃśadaṅgulena catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā tāni pratyekaṃ dakṣiṇāpratyagvyavalikhya pūrvāṇyardhāni nirasyet /
evamekatriṃśat ṣoḍaśyaḥ pariśiṣyante /
sa dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ /
kathaṃ? pakṣe dvātriṃśatṣoḍaśyaḥ /
ṣoḍaśo bhāgaśvaikaḥ /

children.translated_text: Those are thirty-three.
When from those two, four halves are removed, thirty-one remain.
The left wing is exactly the same.
There, [drawing] four diagonals from north-west [to south-east], one should discard the front halves.

At the tip of the wing, having made four squares with a quarter-<s>puruṣa</s> [measure] of thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>, drawing each diagonally from south-west [to north-east], one should discard the front halves. Thus thirty-one <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> remain. That is the right wing. How? In the wing, thirty-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. Plus one sixteenth part.
'Wing-tip' — [up to] 'bending.'

children.text:
pakṣāgramutsṛjya triṃśadaṅgulamapahāya madhye pakṣasya prācīṃ lekhāmālikhet /

sa paścima pakṣāntāt prākpañcāśadaṅgule pañcaviṃśatitilādhike nipatati /
tatra nitodaṃ--binduṃ kuryāt /
tasmācca prācīnalekhāyāmeva puruṣamātre dvitīyaṃ nitodaṃ kuryāta /
nitodayoḥ nānāntāvālikhet /
nitodayorārabhya pakṣāntāvabhi nānāpṛthak ālikhet /
paścimānnitodādārabhya paścimapakṣāgraṃ pakṣāpyayaṃ ca pratyagālikhet /
tatpakṣanamanaṃ -- tadetatpakṣasya namanaṃ bhavati /
pūrvasmannitodādārabhya pūrvaṃ pakṣāgraṃ pakṣāpyayaṃ ca pratyagalikhet /
tat pakṣanamanaṃ -- pakṣasya namanaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Setting aside the wing-tip, deducting thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>, one should draw a longitudinal line in the middle of the wing. With the wing-tip set aside, the remaining wing is two hundred and [some] <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by two-and-a-half <s>aṅgulas</s>, exceeding twenty [over a hundred pair]. At its middle, beginning from behind, with one hundred and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by a quarter-<s>aṅgula</s> plus a little, one should draw a line extending eastward past the wing. At the western wing-junction, having placed a bamboo of <s>puruṣa</s> measure and fixing it, one should drop the other end of the bamboo at the south-eastern point on the line. It falls at fifty <s>aṅgulas</s> east of the western wing-end, plus twenty-five <s>tilas</s>. There one should make a mark-point. And from that, at a <s>puruṣa</s> measure on the same eastward line, one should make a second mark. Between the marks, one should draw [curved lines] diverging apart. Beginning from the marks toward the wing-ends, one should draw separately apart. Beginning from the western mark, one should draw westward to the western wing-tip and wing-junction. That is the wing-bending — that is the bending of the wing. Beginning from the eastern mark, one should draw [to] the eastern wing-tip and wing-junction westward. That is the wing-bending — the bending of the wing.
'These' — [up to] 'explained.'
[The body is] straight.
'Two <s>puruṣas</s>' — [up to] 'tail.'

children.translated_text: Four-and-a-half plus four-and-a-half equals nine.
When six are added to nine, [there are] fifteen.
That is the tail — [meaning] it receives the name 'tail.'
The molds are now stated.

The tip of the tail is of two-<s>puruṣa</s> measure. Its base is of half-<s>puruṣa</s> measure. The length is a <s>puruṣa</s> diminished by a quarter. The <s>karaṇīs</s> of eighteen [<s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>] are on the sides. 'Makes eighteen' — that is the <s>karaṇī</s> of eighteen. Since <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> are primary, [this is] the <s>karaṇī</s> of eighteen of those. They are indeed the diagonals of a square of nine <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, measuring ninety <s>aṅgulas</s> and three <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> on each side. Thus: from the tail-base, southward and northward, the side-lines transverse, with quarter-less <s>puruṣa</s> measure. Three times nine — the diagonal cord of a nine-<s>ṣoḍaśī</s> field. Here, 'the diagonal cord of a square makes twice that area' — those are the <s>karaṇīs</s> of eighteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. Those are four <s>karaṇīs</s>. The two-<s>ṣoḍaśī</s> and eight-<s>ṣoḍaśī</s> transverse [lines] up to the <s>karaṇīs</s> of eighteen, and the side-lines — [these] encompass fifteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. How? [An area] half a <s>puruṣa</s> wide and a quarter-less <s>puruṣa</s> long makes six. On both sides of it, two equal squares, each of quarter-less <s>puruṣa</s> measure on all sides. One should draw those diagonally. The remainder makes four-and-a-half each.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.

children.text: athoktameva śyenacitaṃ prakārāntareṇa vyākhyātuṃ brāhnaṇaṃ punarupanyasyati------
children.translated_text: Now, in order to explain the same hawk-altar that has been described, by an alternative method, he re-introduces the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (explanatory text) —
'Hawk' — [section heading].
'Of a <s>puruṣa</s>' — [up to] 'known from scripture.'
<s>Ṣoḍaśīs</s> — the sixteenth parts.
Those <s>caturbhāgīya</s> (fourth-part) bricks [total] one hundred and twenty.
'Ending in six, of the twenties' — [this is the reading with] <s>ḍa</s>.

children.translated_text: The <s>sāratniprādeśa</s> seven-fold fire[-altar] — of the <s>puruṣa</s>-field, with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, one hundred and twenty is attained.
'Of those' — [up to] 'in the body.'
In the body, forty <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> are [placed].
'Three' — [up to] 'with the addition.'
Now he states the measurement of the body —
'One-and-a-half body.'
The method of removing <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> at the hips and shoulders toward the wing-junctions — which has been stated [before] — should be understood.
'Head' — [up to] 'with the addition.'

In the primary [altar] without <s>aratni</s> and <s>prādeśa</s> [additions], the thirty-<s>aṅgula</s> reduction of the wing-length should be observed as before. In the two-<s>puruṣa</s> length, thirty-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. Plus one by the sixteenth part. Thus thirty-three. From those —
'Wing' — [up to] 'the others.'
Of the southern [squares], one should discard the south-eastern halves. Of the northern [squares], the north-eastern [halves].

children.text: pakṣā namanaṃ pakṣāṅgra triṃśadaṅgulaṃ caturaśrakṛtamutsṛjya śirasi pakṣasya sārdhasaptadaśadviśatāṅgulasya madhye lekhāṃ kṛtvā pakṣāpyayasyāparānte puruṣamātraṃ veṇuṃ niyamya tasyāṃ lekhāyāṃ nipātayet /
children.translated_text: Wing-bending: setting aside the wing-tip thirty-<s>aṅgula</s> square, having drawn a line in the middle of the wing [measuring] two hundred and seventeen-and-a-half <s>aṅgulas</s> in the head[-ward direction], at the western end of the wing-junction, fixing a bamboo of <s>puruṣa</s> measure, one should drop [the other end] on that line.

In the first hawk[-altar], the bending was stated with a two-<s>puruṣa</s> cord — here [it is] stated by an alternative method; [one should] correlate [them].
'These' — [up to] 'explained.'

[is] the quarter-<s>saviśeṣa</s>. With halves of that. 'Wing' — a brick for the purpose of the wing is a wing-brick. One should encompass it with four [planks]. 'With two' — with two quarters, [and] with two sevenths of a <s>puruṣa</s>.

By 'with this and with that' — the eighth and the triple-eighth are the side-measures.
The quarter and its <s>saviśeṣa</s> are the transverse [measures].
The word 'quarter' [is repeated] for the purpose of deriving the <s>saviśeṣa</s> of the quarter itself.

That which stands at the sixteenth part of a <s>puruṣa</s> is a <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>. One should encompass — that is, produce — the <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> with four types of planks. With an eighth — because the <s>puruṣa</s> is primary — [meaning] with fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, that is. With three eighths: forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s>. With a quarter: thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>. With a quarter-<s>saviśeṣa</s>: forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> plus fourteen-and-a-half <s>tilas</s>, positioned diagonally.
Thus, with these four planks, one should have the <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> made.
'Half' — [up to] 'and thus.'
'One should encompass' — this is the remainder.
One should encompass a half-brick with three planks.

Wing[-brick] — [section heading].

And the bending of this will be stated below.
Wing[-brick] — [section heading].

That should be enclosed by three planks: one of thirty <s>aṅgulas</s>, one of forty-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> augmented by five <s>tilas</s>, and one of fifty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s> augmented by nineteen <s>tilas</s>. The wing-bricks, <s>pakṣamadhyīyās</s>, and <s>pakṣāgrīyās</s> — these three [types] are [specified] for suitability in placement at their respective positions, for equality of area.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Now the <s>karaṇas</s> (molds) —
Sixteenth — [abbreviation] [section heading].

pūrvaśyenacaturthyeṣā /

The distinctive fourth: the <s>dvikaraṇī</s> (diagonal) of the fourth is fourteen <s>tilas</s> [and] forty-two <s>aṅgulas</s>.

caturthe triṃśadaṅgule pārśvaphalake /
saptame sapañvratilasaptadaśāṅgule tiryakphalake /
children.translated_text: In the fourth [plank]: thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> — the lateral plank. In the seventh: seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s> — the transverse plank.
<s>Pakṣamadhyī</s> (wing-middle) — 'ca' [section heading].

children.text:
dve pakṣeṣṭake /
samaste eṣā /
pūvaśyene dvitīyāvadrūpaṃ /
children.translated_text: Two wing-bricks. This [relates to] the composite [brick]. In the first hawk[-altar], the form is like the second [type].
Wing[-tip] — 'ca' [section heading].
Wing-brick — half-brick. The composite is one.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: pakṣakaraṇyāḥsaptamaṃ tiryaṅmānī | puruṣacaturthaṃ ca pārśvamānī | tasyākṣṇayā rajjvā karaṇaṃ prajṛmbhayet || ĀpŚus_19.8a ||
children.translated_text: The seventh of the wing-<s>karaṇī</s> (wing-measure) is the transverse measure; the fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s> is the lateral measure; by its diagonal cord one should extend the mold. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 19.8a]

children.text:
dīrghīkuryāt /
anayeti karaṇī /
pakṣakaraṇī -- pakṣasya karaṇī pakṣakaraṇī iṣṭakā /
tasyā uktaṃ karaṇaṃ puruṣasaptamaṃ tiryaṅbhānī puruṣacaturthī pārśvamānīti /
pakṣeṣṭakāṃ caturbhiriti /
tameva dīrghībhūtaṃ karaṇaṃ prajambhayet -- dīrghīkuryāt /
kathamekayā kṣṇayā rajjvāyatayā dīrghīkuryātkaraṇam?
children.translated_text: One should elongate [it]. By which [cord] — that is the <s>karaṇī</s>. Wing-<s>karaṇī</s> means the <s>karaṇī</s> (measure-cord) of the wing — [that is] the wing-brick. Its stated mold has the seventh of a <s>puruṣa</s> as the transverse measure and the fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s> as the lateral measure. 'The wing-brick by four' [was stated previously]. That same mold, having been elongated, one should extend — elongate. How does one elongate the mold by a single diagonal cord stretched [across it]?
By the wing-bending [measure], one should bend the planks by the seventh. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 19.8b]

children.text:
pakṣanamanīti nitodalekhāmūlayorantarālam /
tatsaptadhā vibhajya ekena bhāgena /
kimuktaṃ bhavati? yāvatprajambhitena tasyāḥsaptamī tiryagbhavati tāvatprajambhayoditi /
evaṃ yathā bhavati tathā phalakāni namayet /
nataṃ namanaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Pakṣanamanī</s> (wing-bending measure) means the interval between the base-points of the incision-marks. Having divided that into seven parts, by one part [one bends]. What is being said? One should extend [the mold] until its seventh becomes the transverse [measure] when fully stretched — thus. In the manner that this works out, one should bend the planks — make the curvature.
That <s>pakṣanamanī</s> (wing-bending measure) [applies] to the wing-tip [bricks] in exactly the same way. Therein a verse:
The transverse [measure] should be sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by sixteen <s>tilas</s>;

children.text: tathā tathā caturbhyāṃ ca saptamābhyāṃ ca nāmayet //
children.translated_text: accordingly, one should bend by the fourth and seventh [parts].

children.text: upadhāne catasraḥ pādeṣṭakāḥ purastāc chirasi | apareṇa śiraso 'pyayaṃ pañca | pūrveṇa pakṣāpyayāv ekādaśa | apareṇaikādaśa pūrveṇa pucchāpyayaṃ pañcāpareṇa pañca pañcadaśa pucchāgre || ĀpŚus_19.9 ||
children.translated_text: In placement: four foot-bricks in front at the head; behind the head-junction, five; in front of the wing-junctions, eleven; behind [those], eleven; in front of the tail-junction, five; behind, five; fifteen at the tail-tip. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 19.9]

children.text:
upadadhyāditi śeṣaḥ /
purastācchirasi ghoṇākāre ekā /
tasyāḥ paścāttisraḥ /
apareṇeti -- karṇābharaṇavat /
pādeṣṭakā eva /
pūrveti -- ātmani pakṣāpyayayoḥ pūrastādekādaśa apareṇa pakṣāpyayāvekādaśa etā eva /
children.translated_text: 'In front' — in the body, at the wing-junctions in front, eleven; behind the wing-junctions, eleven — these same [foot-bricks].

children.text: pūrveti -- pūcchasyāpyayasya purastāt pañca paścācca pañca /
children.translated_text: 'In front' — in front of the tail-junction, five; and behind, five.
'Fifteen' — at the tail-tip, fifteen.
These are the fifty-six foot-bricks in total.
'One should place' — this is the remainder. In front at the head, in the beak-shape, one [foot-brick]. Behind that, three. 'Behind' means like ear-ornaments. [These are] foot-bricks themselves.
Nineteenth chapter.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
And [how] the curvature should be made — he says:
Wing-[brick] — should [section heading].

children.text:
prathamyāt sāmarthyācca pakṣeṣṭakākaraṇīviṣayamidam likhayā vibhaktasya pakṣārdhasya karaṇī pakṣakaraṇī /
sā sapādāṅgulona daśaśatāṅgulā /
tasyāḥsaptamaṃ sāṣṭādaśatilā pañcadaśāṅgulā ṛjvavasthitā prajambyamānasya karaṇasya yathā tiryaṅnānī bhavati tathā tatkaraṇaṃ ṛjvakṣṇayā prajambhayet -- prakarṣeṇa namayet /
pārśvamānī tu prajmbhyamāne 'pi karaṇe puruṣacaturthameva /
prajambhatiratrāpi mānārtha eva /
etaduktaṃ bhavati -- karaṇasya ekasyāṃ koṭyāṃ rajjuṃ prabadhya tāṃ koṭimitārāṃ koṭiṃ prati akṣṇayā balena karṣayet /
yathā ākarṣaṇe kṛte dvayoḥ koṭyoḥ sannikarṣeṇa pārśvamānyorantarālamṛjutvena pakṣkaraṇyāḥsaptamaṃ bhavati na nyūtaṃ nāpyadhikaṃ tathā prajambhayet /
tiryaṅnānyorantarālamṛjvavasthitamapi puruṣacaturthameva /
anena tiryaṅmānyā hrāsaḥ kriyate vakratvāya kṣetrasamatvāya ca /
athavā sāṣṭādaśatilaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulaṃ tiryaṅmānīṃ kṛtvā triṃśaḍhaṅgulaṃ pārśvamānīṃ ca kṛtvā tābhyāṃ caturśraṃ vihṛtya tasyākṣṇayārajjvā pakṣeṣṭakākaraṇaṃ prajambhayet /
etaduktaṃ bhavati -- uktaprakārākṣṇayārajjvadhikāṃ rajjuṃmītvā tayā pakṣeṣṭakākaraṇasyaikāṃ koṭiṃ badhvā tāṃ koṭiṃ anyā koṭiṃ pratyakṣṇayā jambhayet -- manayet /
children.translated_text: What is being said is: having measured a cord exceeding [the mold] by the diagonal of the stated type, and having tied that [cord] at one corner of the wing-brick mold, one should stretch that corner toward the other corner diagonally — bend it.

children.text: yathā tayoḥ koṭayorantarālaṃ etadakṣṇayārajjuḥsambhavati tathā namayedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should bend it such that the interval between those corners accommodates this diagonal cord — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte asya karaṇasyaikākṣṇayārajjuḥ sārdhaddvayaṅgulena drāghīyasī bhavati /
children.translated_text: When done thus, one diagonal cord of this mold becomes longer by two-and-a-half <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The other [diagonal] becomes shorter by that same [amount].

From the first [sūtra's] purport and from contextual force, this concerns the wing-brick-<s>karaṇī</s>. The <s>karaṇī</s> of the half-wing as demarcated by the line — [that is] the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s> (wing-measure). That is nine hundred and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> less a quarter-<s>aṅgula</s>. Its seventh, with eighteen <s>tilas</s>, is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> — [this is the measure] when [the mold] stands straight. Of the mold being stretched, so that [its seventh] becomes the transverse measure — one should stretch that mold by the straight diagonal — bend it forcefully. But the lateral measure, even when the mold is being stretched, remains exactly the fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s>. The stretching here too is just for the purpose of measurement. What is being said is: having fastened a cord at one corner of the mold, one should pull that corner toward the other corner diagonally with force. When the pulling is done such that the interval between the lateral sides, measured straight, becomes exactly the seventh of the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s> — neither less nor more — so should one stretch it. The interval between the transverse sides, even though [the mold] stands straight, remains exactly the fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s>. By this, a reduction in the transverse measure is made — for curvature and for equality of area. Alternatively, having made fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with eighteen <s>tilas</s> as the transverse measure, and thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> as the lateral measure, and having laid out a quadrilateral with these, by its diagonal cord one should stretch the wing-brick mold.
The second explanation, stated by some others, does not partake of straightforwardness.

children.text:
pakṣeṣṭakākaraṇasya prajambhanena namanavidhimuktvā pakṣamadhyīyāpakṣāgrīyākaraṇayornamanasid dhayarthaṃ tatphalakānāṃ natirucyate -- pakṣanamanī -- yayā mātrayā pakṣo namyate sā pakṣanamanī /
sā ca pakṣamadhyalekhāyāḥ prathamanitodāt paścimamātrā /
sā ca pañcaviṃśatitilādhikapañcāśadaṅguletyuktā /

children.translated_text: Its seventh is seven <s>aṅgulas</s> with three-and-a-half <s>tilas</s>.

children.text: tena phalakāni pakṣamadhyīyāpakṣāgrīyākaraṇayordīrghāni yāni phalakāni tāni namayet -- vakīkuryāt /
children.translated_text: By that [measure], the long planks of the <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s> and <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s> molds — one should bend those planks — curve them.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ -- yathā madhye kṛtena namanena pakṣmadhyīyāṃbhāgadvayaṃ pakṣakaraṇyā saptamaṃ tiryaṅmānī puruṣacaturthaṃ ca pārśvamānītyuktaprakāraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as by the bending made at the middle, the two parts of the <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s> [conform to] the seventh of the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s> as transverse measure and the fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s> as lateral measure — in the manner stated,

children.text: tathā dvisaptaphalakayormadhye saptamamātre pakṣanamanyāḥsaptamena ekasmin phalake natimekasminnudañcaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: so in the middle of the two-times-seven planks, at just the seventh measure, by the seventh of the <s>pakṣanamanī</s>, one should make curvature on one plank and straightness on [the other] one [plank going] northward.

Having stated the bending procedure through the stretching of the wing-brick mold, for establishing the bending of the <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s> and <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s> molds, the bending of their planks is stated. <s>Pakṣanamanī</s> — the measure by which the wing is bent, that is the <s>pakṣanamanī</s>. And it is the posterior measure from the first incision of the wing-middle line. And it has been stated as fifty <s>aṅgulas</s> augmented by twenty-five <s>tilas</s>.
Therein verses:
One should stretch the mold of the wing-brick with a cord in such a way
that its transverse [measure] becomes the seventh of the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s>.
In the <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s> mold, on the two longer planks,
by the seventh of the bending-measure, there should be curvature at the seventh measure.
The same bending procedure [applies] to the <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s> mold also;
the curvature is in the seventh portion; in the [remaining] portion-minus-one, the other [part] is straight.
The transverse [measure] being fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with eighteen <s>tilas</s>,
accordingly should be the bending procedure for the parts of the bricks.
In the first hawk[-altar], however, the stretching of the first mold [is such that the]

children.text: phalaṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pakṣakaraṇī ṣaṣṭhavyāso yathā bhavet //
children.translated_text: result [is that] the sixth — the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s> — [gives] the sixth[-part] as the breadth.
Of the second and third [molds], and those of the sixth [parts], the result of the bending
[is that] the <s>pakṣakaraṇī</s>'s sixth becomes the breadth; the curvature is not in the eighth.
These two verses concern the first hawk[-altar].
The wing-bricks here are four, and the foot-bricks also six,
made as the tenth of the <s>coḍā</s>, <s>nāka</s>, <s>sadā</s>, <s>mārdha</s>, and <s>jānu</s> [measurements].
Placement — head [section heading].

children.text: upadhānakāle catasraḥ pādeṣṭakāḥśira (si) saḥ pūrvabhāge purastādupadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: At the time of placement, four foot-bricks should be placed in front at the head.
Of those four, one [is placed] in front — with the tip pointing east, due to external distinction.
Behind that, three.
Of those, the middle one [has its tip] pointing west.
Behind — five [section heading].
Beyond the head-junction, five.
Two with tips pointing west.
From the tail, at the foot-junction — just so.
In front — eleven [section heading].
Behind — at the wing-junctions in front.
In the body, eleven.
Five with tips pointing west.
Behind — [section heading].
Behind the rear wing-junctions, to the back, eleven.
Six with tips pointing west.
In front — 'ca' [section heading].
In front of the tail-junction, five.
Of those, three with tips pointing west.
Behind — 'ca' [section heading].
In front of the tail-junction, five.
Of those, two with tips pointing west.
Fifteen — tip [section heading].
At the tail-tip, fifteen should be placed.
Of those, seven with tips pointing west.
These are the fifty-six foot-bricks.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Wing[-brick] — should [section heading].

children.text:
pakṣakaraṇī -- pakṣārdhasya tiryaṅmānī pādonanavaśatāṅgulā /
ardhe tasya saptamaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulaṃ sāṣṭādaśātilaṃ /
tasya karaṇasya yathā tiryaṅnānī bhavati pārśvamānī triṃśadaṅgulaiva tathākṣṇayā rajjvā karaṇaṃ prajambhayet -- namayet /
ekaḥ karṇaḥ catvāriṃśadaṅgulo dvādaśatilānvitaḥ /
aparaḥ saptaviṃśako viṃśatitilayuktaḥ /
āratni (prādeśa) rahite (ṣve)(tve) ekaḥ karṇaḥ sārdhatrayoviṃśakaḥ /
anyaḥ pañcatilonastricatvāriṃśadaṅgulaḥ iṣṭakāvyāsaś ca trayodaśāṅgulastrayodaśatilayuktaḥ /
atha pakṣāgrīyāpakṣamadhyayornamanamāha --
children.translated_text: <s>Pakṣakaraṇī</s> — the transverse measure of the half-wing is nine hundred <s>aṅgulas</s> less a quarter. Half of that, its seventh is fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with eighteen <s>tilas</s>. Of that mold, so that [its seventh] becomes the transverse measure — the lateral measure being exactly thirty <s>aṅgulas</s> — by a diagonal cord one should stretch the mold — bend it. One diagonal is forty <s>aṅgulas</s> with twelve <s>tilas</s>. The other is twenty-seven with twenty <s>tilas</s>. In [the version] without <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], one diagonal is twenty-three-and-a-half. The other is forty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> less five <s>tilas</s>. And the brick-breadth is thirteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with thirteen <s>tilas</s>. Now he states the bending of the <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s> and <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s>:
Wing [bending] — should [section heading].

children.text:
pakṣanamanī -- puruṣamātrī /
tasyāḥ saptamena pakṣāgrīyāpakṣamadhyayoḥ pakṣeṣṭakāṃśasya tiryakphalakāni namayet /
tasya sāṣṭādaśatilapañcadaśāṅgulavyāsasya pakṣeṣṭakāṃśasya tiryakphalake yathā sapañcatile saptadaśāṅgule bhavataḥ tathā phalakāni takṣet /
dve pakṣeṣṭake pārśvasaṃhite pakṣamadhyīyā ṣaḍaśriḥ pakṣeṣṭakāmuttarapūrvatīrghakarṇāṃ bhūmau likhitvā tasyā dakṣiṇataḥ triṃśadaṅgulaṃ samacaturaśraṃ kṛtvā tasya dakṣiṇapūrvamardhaṃ a (pūrvama) kṣṇayājahyāt /
sā pakṣāgrīyā pañcakoṇā /
atrāṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt aṇūkasaṃjñe dve karaṇe kārye /
triṃśadaṅgule dve sa macaturaśre dakṣiṇottare likhitvā dakṣiṇasya dakṣiṇapūrvamardhamakṣṇa yā nirasyet /
uttarasyottarāparaṃ /

children.translated_text: This is one <s>aṇūka</s>.
The triangular one is the second.
Of that, one plank is sixty <s>aṅgulas</s>.
The others are in the distinctive fourth[-part].

<s>Pakṣanamanī</s> — [it is] of <s>puruṣa</s>-measure. By its seventh, one should bend the transverse planks of the wing-brick portion of the <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s> and <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s>. Of that wing-brick portion having fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> breadth with eighteen <s>tilas</s>, the transverse planks should be fashioned such that they become seventeen <s>aṅgulas</s> with five <s>tilas</s>. Two wing-bricks joined at the sides — the <s>pakṣamadhyīyā</s> is hexahedral. Having drawn on the ground the wing-brick with its upper-eastern-long diagonal, and having made a thirty-<s>aṅgula</s> equal quadrilateral to its south, and cutting diagonally the south-eastern half of that — that is the <s>pakṣāgrīyā</s>, pentagonal. Here, since it will be stated that '<s>aṇūkas</s> take the place of fifteenth-part [bricks],' two molds designated as <s>aṇūka</s> should be made. Having drawn two thirty-<s>aṅgula</s> equal quadrilaterals, south and north, one should remove the south-eastern half of the southern one diagonally, and the north-western [half] of the northern one.
Now the placement:
Behind — at the head [section heading].
In front, one [foot-brick]. Behind that, three.
Behind — five [section heading].
Foot-bricks. The row [runs] northward.
In front — eleven [section heading].
The row [runs] northward, in the body itself.
Behind — tip [section heading].
These fifty-six also extend northward.
Nineteenth chapter.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: catasraścatasraḥ pakṣāgrīyāḥ pakṣāgrayoḥ pakṣāpyayayoś ca viśayāḥ || ĀpŚus_20.1 ||
children.translated_text: Four-by-four <s>pakṣāgrīyās</s> (wing-tip bricks) at the wing-tips and at the wing-junctions [respectively] are the domain. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.1]

children.text: tā ātmani catasṛbhiś catasṛbhiḥ ṣoḍaśībhir yathāyogaṃ paryupadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_20.2 ||
children.translated_text: Those [bricks] in the body, one should place around with four-by-four sixteenth-part [bricks] as appropriate. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.2]

children.text:
viparyasya kāritā uttare pakṣe /
catasraścatasro viśayāḥ /
pakṣasandhyordakṣiṇapakṣāpyaye viparyasya kāritā uttare pakṣeṣṭakā mātram /
pakṣayorātmanyardheṣṭakāmātraṃ /

children.translated_text: By "those," the special [bricks] are referred back to.
In the body, with four-by-four sixteenth-part [bricks], made reversed.
Those that are at the southern wing-junction — just as one would place with those four, so with [another] four at the northern wing-junction.
The prefix "pari" is in the sense of "in turn."

Made reversed in the northern wing. Four-by-four are the special [bricks]. At the wing-junctions, [those] at the southern wing-junction are reversed — made as northern wing-bricks in measure. In the wings, the body[-portion] is half-a-brick in measure.
Four-by-four wing-middle [bricks] at the wing-middles. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.3]
With wing-bricks [placed] facing east, one should cover the wings. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.4]

children.text: pakṣamadhye bhavā vakrabhūtāścatasro dakṣiṇe pakṣamadhye catasra evottarapakṣamadhye /

children.translated_text: Wing-bricks are of the characteristics stated [earlier].
With those, [placed] extending eastward, one should cover the wings.
One should place [them] in the wings.
And forty made reversed.
Those that are in the wing-middle, curved, are four in the southern wing-middle and four in the northern wing-middle.
The remainder one should cover with sixteenth-part [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.5a]
The remaining fire-altar area one should fill with sixteenth-part [bricks].
The outermost [bricks] have external projections (<s>bāhyaviśeṣa</s>), except at the head. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.5b]

children.text: aparasmin prastāre purastāc chirasi dve ṣoḍaśyau bāhyaviśeṣe upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_20.6a ||
children.translated_text: In the other layer, in front, at the head, two sixteenth-part [bricks] with external projections should be placed. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.6a]

children.text:
ante bhavā antyāḥ -- agnayantasthāḥ /
tā bāhyaviśeṣāḥ bāhyataḥsaviśeṣāḥ anyatra śirasaḥ -- śiro varjiyitvā /
ātmani madhye ṣaṭ prācyaḥ ṣaṭ pratīcyaḥ /
ātmani rītidvayam /
avaśiṣṭaṃ pucche ca /
tāsu yadi ṣoḍaśībirevopadhīyante saṃkhyāpūryate kiṃ tu bidyate /
catasṛṣvapi rītiṣu bhedo varjanīyaḥ /
tasmādardhāśvopadheyāḥ /
kathamanucyamānā upadhīyante nocyamānāḥ? uktā eva "yaccaturaśraṃ trayaśri vā sampadyetārdheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhirvā pracchādayet' iti vadatā /
nanu yadyardhāśvopadhīyante atiricyate saṃkhyā; naiṣa doṣaḥ; ūnādhikaprastāra ityuktaṃ pūrvasmin paṭale /
pucche rītidvayam /
tisrastisror'dheṣṭakā upadhāya ṣoḍaśyaḥ punaśvottare pārśve ekaikor'dhaḥ /
evamātmani dvayo rītyordakṣiṇatastisror'dheṣṭakāḥ /
tato dve ṣoḍaśyau ekaikordhaḥ /

children.translated_text: Then two sixteenth-part [bricks], one-by-one halves.
At the head, two sixteenth-part [bricks] placed transversely.

children.text: aparasminniti -- pūrvabhāge dve ṣoḍaśyau bāhyataḥsaviśeṣe ghoṇākāre upadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: Thus two hundred and eight.
"In the other" — in the front portion, two sixteenth-part [bricks] should be placed outward with projections, in beak-shape. Made reversed from the south.

Those that are at the end are "outermost" (<s>antyā</s>) — situated at the fire-boundary. They have external projections (<s>bāhyaviśeṣa</s>) — projecting outward — except at the head, excluding the head. In the body, in the middle, six [bricks] facing east and six facing west. In the body, two rows (<s>rīti</s>). The remainder in the tail as well. If among those only sixteenth-part [bricks] are placed, the count is fulfilled, but there would be joints (<s>bheda</s>). In all four rows, joints should be avoided. Therefore, half-bricks should be placed. How are unmentioned [bricks] placed when not [explicitly] stated? They are indeed stated — by the one who states: "Whatever becomes a quadrilateral or a triangle, one should cover with half-bricks or quarter-bricks." But if half-bricks are placed, the count is exceeded; this is no fault, for "layers with fewer or more [bricks]" has been stated in the previous section. In the tail, two rows. Having placed three-by-three half-bricks, then sixteenth-part [bricks], and again on the northern side one-by-one halves. Similarly in the body, in two rows on the south, three half-bricks.
Those, behind [them], are two special [bricks] with internal projections (<s>abhyantaraviśeṣa</s>). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.6b]
With two half-bricks, one should place around as appropriate. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.7a]
Behind those two, in the body, half-a-brick in measure; the rest in the head.
One should place [them] as is applicable on both sides.
These four are the special [bricks].
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Four ... [at the junctions]
Four at each [junction].
Wing ... [bricks]
By the word "ca" (and), the wing-tip [bricks] are implied.
At the wing-junctions, four-by-four wing-tip special [bricks] should be [placed].
Those lie in the wings by the seventh [<s>karaṇa</s>].
The remaining [lie] in the body by the fourth [<s>karaṇa</s>].
Those in the body ... should place

children.text: ātmani praviṣṭapakṣāgrīyāparitaścatasṛbhiḥ ṣoḍaśībhirḥ yathā yujyante tathopadadhyāt /
children.translated_text: In the body, around the wing-tip [bricks] that have entered [the body], with four sixteenth-part [bricks] one should place as is applicable.
The meaning is: one should place [them] so that the projections of the wing-tip [bricks] are joined together.
Four ... [at the junctions]
"As appropriate" — just so.
Understood.
Wing ... should cover
"As appropriate" — just so.

children.text: catvāriṃśatā catvāriṃśatā pakṣeṣṭakābhiḥ prāgāyatābhiḥ pakṣau pracchādayet //
children.translated_text: With forty-by-forty wing-bricks, [placed] extending eastward, one should cover the wings.
Remainder ... should cover

children.text:
avaśiṣṭaṃ anupahitamagnikṣetraṃ pucchāvaśiṣṭaṃ ṣoḍaśībhiḥ pracchādayet /
pucchamadhye dve rītyau /
pūrvāścaturiṣṭakāḥ /
paścimāḥṣaḍiṣṭakāḥ /
dve dve viśeṣasahite
children.translated_text: The remaining uncovered fire-altar area, the tail-remainder, should be covered with sixteenth-part [bricks]. In the tail-middle, two rows. The front [row has] four bricks. The rear [row has] six bricks. Two-by-two with joined projections

children.text:
syātāṃ /
tā etā daśa ātmani /
ātmamadhye tisro rītayaḥ /

children.translated_text: The front rows of four bricks [are] in the body itself.
Behind and in front, the two rows facing north, of four bricks each.
Those [total] twenty.
At the head, two sixteenth-part [bricks].
should be. These ten [are placed] in the body. In the body-middle, three rows.
Outermost ... head

children.text:
ante upadheyā antyāḥ /
pucche catasraḥ ātmani catasra /
bāhyaviśeṣāḥ -- bahirgataviśeṣāḥ /
na cātra saṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ; saṃkhyāḥ yāḥsthāne dviśataviniyogāt /

children.translated_text: Namely: fifty-six quarter-bricks — eight-by-eight wing-tip [bricks]; forty-by-forty wing-bricks.
Eight.
And wing-middle [bricks]: forty sixteenth-part [bricks].
Thus two hundred.

Those to be placed at the end are "outermost." In the tail, four; in the body, four. [They are] external projections — projections extending outward. And here there is no count-completion; the counts are [fulfilled] by the assignment of two hundred to each location.
Other ... should place

children.text: dvitīye prastāre śirasaḥ pūrvabhāge prāgagre bāhyaviśeṣe dve ṣoḍaśyau //
children.translated_text: In the second layer, at the front portion of the head, with tips facing east, two sixteenth-part [bricks] with external projections.
Those ... projections

children.text: tayoḥṣoḍaśyoḥ paścāt prāgagre śirasyardhapādeṣṭakāmātre viśaye viśeṣeṇātmani /
children.translated_text: Behind those two sixteenth-part [bricks], with tips facing east, at the head, half-quarter-brick measure special [bricks] with projections in the body.
Thus the two special [bricks] are sixteenth-part [bricks] with internal projections.
With two ... should place
"Those" — just so.

children.text: te viśaye iṣṭake dvābhyāmardheṣṭakābhyāṃ viśayābhyāṃ yathāyogaṃ parigṛhṇīyāt /
children.translated_text: Those special bricks — with two half-bricks, special [bricks] — one should encompass as appropriate.

children.text: ṣoḍaśyorardheṣṭakayoś ca yathā viśeṣāḥsaṃhitā bhaveyuḥ tathopadadhyādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: one should place [them] so that the projections of the sixteenth-part [bricks] and half-bricks are joined together.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
Four ... wing-tips
Of those, half-brick measures [are placed] in the body.
Those ... should place
With [tips] facing south, those at the southern junction [are placed]; the others face north.
Four ... wing-middle
Wing ... should cover — with eighty [bricks placed] extending eastward.
Remainder ... should cover

children.text: aṇūkāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ sthāna iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt aṇūkābhiḥ saha pracchādanabhedaparihārāya tatra pucchātmaśiraḥsu pūrvanihitābhiḥ pādarītibhiḥsaha ṣoḍaśa rītayaḥ udīcyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since <s>aṇūkās</s> (quarter-bricks) will be stated to take the place of fifteenth-part [bricks], in order to avoid joints in covering with <s>aṇūkās</s>, there in the tail, body, and head, together with the quarter-rows already placed, [there are] sixteen rows facing north.
At the tail-tip, the quarter-row has been stated.
In the second [row], <s>aṇūkās</s> on the sides, four sixteenth-part [bricks] in the middle.

children.text: evaṃ tṛtīyāṣaṣṭhītrayodaśyo 'ṇūkābhireva dviprakārābhiḥ sandhyantarāle dvādaśa ṣoḍaśyaḥ pragāyatāḥ śiraso 'parārdhe dve ṣoḍaśyau dviśataḥ prastāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the third, sixth, and thirteenth [rows] with <s>aṇūkās</s> alone of two types; at the intervals of joints, twelve sixteenth-part [bricks] extending eastward; at the rear half of the head, two sixteenth-part [bricks] — [yielding] a layer of two hundred.

children.text:
antyā -- śirasaḥ
ca śabdo 'trādhyāhartavyaḥ /
dvābhyāṃ viśeṣāḥ /
anteṣu yā upadheyāstā bāhyaviśeṣāḥ ṣoḍaśyo bhaveyuḥ /
etaccātmanyeva /
pakṣayoraśakyatvāt pucchabhedasambhavācca /
tasmādātmanaḥ śroṇyaṃseṣvaṣṭau ṣoḍaśīrdakṣi (ṇāgrā) ṇā udagagrāścopadadhyāt /
ekaikatra dvedve /
asmin pakṣe yaccaturaśraṃ tryaśri veti vakṣyamāṇābhiḥ pādyābhiḥ saṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ /
tatra pucchāpyayasya purastāddve ardhe śiraso 'pyayasya paścāddve ardhe /
tāsāṃ madhye caturviśatiḥ pādyāḥ /
pārśvayoḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ ṣoḍaśyaḥ /
yadvā etāḥ pādyāḥ ṣoḍaśīśvaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśatamuddhṛtya ṣaṭtriṃśadar (dhyār) dhā nidheyāḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇapārśvasthā prāguttaraviśeṣāḥ viparītā
children.translated_text: Outermost ... head — the word "ca" (and) should be supplied here. With two [bricks, there are] projections. Those that should be placed at the ends should have external projections and be sixteenth-part [bricks]. And this is in the body only, because it is impossible in the wings and because of the possibility of joints in the tail. Therefore, at the hips and shoulders of the body, eight sixteenth-part [bricks] should be placed with [tips] facing south and facing north — two at each [location]. In this interpretation, the count-completion is by the quarter-bricks to be stated as "whatever becomes a quadrilateral or triangle." There, two halves in front of the tail-junction, two halves behind the head-junction. In their midst, twenty-four quarter-bricks. On the sides, six-by-six sixteenth-part [bricks]. Alternatively, these quarter-bricks and sixteenth-part [bricks] — having removed thirty-six, thirty-six halves should be placed.
In the tail-middle, six sixteenth-part [bricks] extending eastward.
Then on the sides, three half-bricks each.
The rest is as before.

children.text: a(ta)tra ātmani prācyaḥ pañcarītyaḥ udīcyo vā aṣṭau //
children.translated_text: Here, in the body, five rows facing east, or eight facing north.
There, those on the southern side have projections to the east and north; those on the northern side are reversed.
Other ... should place
Those ... projections
These too with tips facing east.
With two ... should place

children.text: tayoḥ ṣoḍaśyormadhye śiraso 'pyaye dve ardheṣṭake ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Between those two sixteenth-part [bricks], at the head-junction, two half-bricks — this is the meaning.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary
One should encompass with [two bricks having] external projections. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.7b]

children.text:
ubhayatra tṛtīyāpadaśravaṇāt vidhyantarametat na pūrvayorviśeṣaṇam /
caśabdo 'dhyāhartavyaḥ bāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ ceti /
bāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ cārdheṣṭakābhyāṃ parigṛhṇīyāt /
śirasyanavakāśādātmanyeva /
children.translated_text: Since in both places the third-case ending is heard, this is a separate injunction, not a qualifier of the preceding [two]. The word "ca" (and) should be supplied: "and with [bricks having] external projections." With two half-bricks having external projections, one should encompass. In the head, there being no space, [this applies] in the body only.

children.text: ātmanaḥ karaṇīnāṃ sandhiṣu ṣoḍaśyo bāhyaviśeṣā upadadhyāt || ĀpŚus_20.8 ||
children.translated_text: At the joints of the body's sides (<s>karaṇī</s>), one should place sixteenth-part [bricks] with external projections. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.8]

children.text: ātmanaḥ karaṇyaḥ, tāsāṃ sandhiṣu śroṇyaṃseṣu catasraḥ ṣoḍaśyo bāhyaviśeṣāḥ pratyantaviśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: The sides of the body are its <s>karaṇīs</s> (edges). At their joints — at the hips and shoulders — four sixteenth-part [bricks] with external projections, [i.e.] projections at the extremities.
Four-by-four half-bricks at the wing-tips. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.9a]
At the claw-shaped [portions], half-bricks should be placed, four-by-four.
With wing-bricks [placed] facing north, one should cover the wings. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.9b]
With [bricks] extending northward, one should place [them] in the wings. Fifty-six, made reversed.
Three-by-three half-bricks at the tail-sides. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.10]
Three-by-three half-bricks at the tail-sides are external projections.
The remainder one should cover with sixteenth-part [bricks]. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.11a]
The remaining fire-altar area one should cover with sixteenth-part [bricks].
The outermost [bricks] have external projections, except at the tail. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 20.11b]
This is understood. Except for the tail.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
External ... tail
"Those" — just so.
Those same two sixteenth-part [bricks] should be encompassed by external projections — by the other two halves.
These halves, there being no space at the head, are in the body.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati -- viśayaṣoḍaśyoḥ purastādviśayabhūte bahirviśeṣe dve arve tathā'tmani viśayaṣoḍaśyordakṣiṇata uttarataś ca vahirviśeṣe anye ardhe iti //
children.translated_text: This amounts to saying: in front of the special sixteenth-part [bricks], at the special external projection, two halves; likewise in the body, to the south and north of the special sixteenth-part [bricks], at the external projections, two other halves.
Body ... should place

children.text:
ātmanaḥ karaṇya ātmakaraṇyaḥ /
tāsāṃ sandhiṣu śroṇyaṃseṣu ṣoḍaśyaḥ catasraḥ /

children.translated_text: Everywhere there are Vedic irregularities in case-endings.
In the body, near the wing-junctions, one should place four sixteenth-part [bricks] with external projections.

children.text: antyā bāhyaviśeṣā iti vakṣyamāṇe 'pi bāhyaviśeṣagrahaṇaṃ saṃkhyāpūraṇāya /
children.translated_text: Even though it will be stated "the outermost [bricks] have external projections," the [separate] mention of external projections [here] is for the purpose of count-completion.

children.text: pādānāṃ cārdhānāṃ ca upadhānārthaṃ ṣoḍaśīnāmuddhvaraṇe prasakte āsāṇuddharaṇaṃ mā bhūdityevamartham //
children.translated_text: The purpose is: when the removal of sixteenth-part [bricks] for the placement of quarter-bricks and half-bricks is entailed, these should not be removed.
The edges of the body are the body's <s>karaṇīs</s> (sides). At their joints — at the hips and shoulders — four sixteenth-part [bricks].
Four ... wing-tips
At each wing, four half-bricks are external projections — just so.
Wing ... should cover
In the wings, facing north, seven rows of wing-bricks.
Three ... tail-sides
[These are] external projections indeed.
Remainder ... should cover
The remainder in the body [has] thirty-three sixteenth-part [brick] positions; the tail [has] twelve sixteenth-part [brick] positions.
Outermost ... tail

children.text:
antyāḥsarvā bāhyaviśeṣā bhaveyuḥ pucchādanyatra /
pucche tvantyāḥṣoḍaśyo 'bhyantaraviśeṣā eva /
children.translated_text: All outermost [bricks] should have external projections, except at the tail. But at the tail, the outermost sixteenth-part [bricks] have internal projections only.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary
External ... should encompass

children.text: te ṣoḍaśyau bāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ dvābhyāmardheṣṭakābhyāṃ dakṣiṇata uttarataśvātmani parigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Those two sixteenth-part [bricks] should be encompassed by two half-bricks with external projections, to the south and north, in the body.
Body ... should place

children.text:
aṣṭāśrerātmano 'ṣṭau karaṇyaḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇottarapārśvakaraṇyoḥ śroṇyaṃsakaraṇībhiḥ saha catvāraḥ sandhayaḥ /
tatra śroṇisandhyordve pratyagagre ṣoḍaśyau /
aṃsasandhyordve prāgagre /
evaṃ catasraḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ /
ye tu catvāraḥ pūrvāpara (koṭyoḥ) karaṇyoḥsandhayaḥ tatra pūrvayostāvadbāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ parigṛhṇīyādityardheṣṭake ukte /
aparayorapi pūrvasādṛśyārthaṃ bhedaparihārārthaṃ cādhyardhe evopadheye /
children.translated_text: The octagonal body has eight edges (<s>karaṇīs</s>). Therein, the southern and northern lateral edges together with the hip and shoulder edges have four joints. At the hip-joints, two sixteenth-part [bricks] with tips facing west. At the shoulder-joints, two with tips facing east. Thus four sixteenth-part [bricks]. As for the four joints at the front and rear tip-edges, at the front two, one should encompass with external projections — [i.e.] the half-bricks are stated. At the rear two also, for similarity with the front and for avoidance of joints, only one-and-a-half [bricks] should be placed.
Four ... wing-tips
Wing ... should cover
Fifty-six for each [wing].
Three ... tail-sides
[These are] external projections.
<s>Kapardi</s> commentary

children.text: yac caturaśraṃ tryaśraṃ vā saṃpadyetārdheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhir vā pracchādayet || ĀpŚus_20.12 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever square or triangular [space] results, one should cover it with half-bricks or quarter-bricks.'

children.text:
sarvatra ṣoḍaśya eva śerate /
yadi tathā kṣipyeran bhidyeta sarvatra /
ato bhedaparihārāya yatne kriyamāṇe trikoṇaṃ caturaśraṃ vā prakāradvayaṃ sampadyate /
pūrvasmin prastāre cataraśraṃ sampadyate trikoṇaṃ ca /
iha trikoṇameva /
tatra ardheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhirvā pracchādayet upadadhyāt /
pucchāpyaye catasraḥ ṣoḍaśyo viśayāḥ /
prācyau dve pratīcyau dve /
tāsāṃ paścāt daśa ṣoḍaśyaḥ /
tiryakpucche 'pi /
viśayāmānabhito dvāvardhau dvāvātmi /
tāsāṃ purastāccatasraḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ prācyaścaturthyaḥ pratyarpitāḥ /
tāsāṃ purastādviparyastāḥ ṣaḍuttare pārśve /
tāsāṃ purastāccatasror'dheṣṭakāḥ /
tāsāṃ purastāccatasraḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ pratīcyastābhiḥ pratyarpitāḥ /
tāsāṃ purastād dve ṣoḍaśyau nānāgre prācyau /
tayormadhye dvāvardhau /
ātmanyardhapādeṣṭakāmātrī /
ātmani dvāvardhau viśayāvabhitaḥ /
ardhaṣoḍaśyau sahitau /
evaṃ dvādaśonaṃ śatadvayam /
iha keciddīrghāyuṣaḥsūtrametadanādṛtya svamanīṣikayā karaṇāntaramutpādya saṃkhyāpūraṇameva kurvanti /
kiṃ nāma teṣāmaśakyam? vayaṃ tu sūtrakāramatānusāreṇoktaṃ gṛhṇīmaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Everywhere only <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> (sixteenth-part bricks) lie.
If they were placed as such, there would be gaps everywhere.
Therefore, when effort is made to avoid gaps, two types of spaces result — triangular and square.
In the previous layer, square [spaces] result, and triangular ones.
Here, only triangular [spaces].
There, one should cover — place — with half-bricks or quarter-bricks.
At the tail-junction, four <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> are field-[bricks].
Two face east, two face west.
Behind those, ten <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
Also transverse in the tail.
Around the field-[bricks], two halves and two body-[bricks].
In front of those, four <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, eastward fourth-[size bricks], fitted back.
In front of those, reversed, six on the northern side.
In front of those, four half-bricks.
In front of those, four <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> facing west, fitted with those.
In front of those, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> with different tips facing east.
Between those two, two halves.
In the body, of the measure of half-quarter-bricks.
In the body, two halves as field-[bricks] on both sides.
Two half-<s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> joined together.
Thus two hundred minus twelve.
Here some long-lived [scholars], disregarding this <s>sūtra</s>, create alternative constructions by their own ingenuity and merely complete the count.
What indeed is impossible for them? But we accept what is stated following the intention of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras).
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.

children.text: evaṃ kṣetrapūraṇaṃ kṛtvā prakṛtitaḥ prāptaṃ saṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ evaṃ kartavyamityāha----
children.translated_text: Having thus completed the field-filling, he states that the count-completion obtained from the basic [procedure] should be done as follows —
'Whatever... should cover' —

children.text:
evaṃ ṣoḍaśībhiḥ pracchādyamāne saṅkhyāpūraṇāya kāsuciduddhṛtāsu ca yat kṣetraṃ caturaśraṃ tryaśri vā sambhavet tat kṣetramardheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhirvā pracchādayet -- tābhiḥsaṃkhyāṃ pūrayedityarthaḥ nanu pracchādayediti vacanena saṅkhyāpūraṇaṃ katham? ucyate /
tattadagnau pracchādanavidhyanantaraṃ saṅkhyāṃ pūrayoditi vidhānāt /
iha ca ṣoḍaśībhiḥ pracchādite saṅkhyāyā asamāptestatpūraṇāpekṣayā dvitīyapracchādanavacanaṃ saṅkhyāpūraṇārthameveti gamyate /
kiñca dvividhaḥ prākṛto 'gnaniḥ samacaturaśramātreṣṭakā asamacatu; raśramātreṣṭakāś ca /
prathame caturaśrāgnau pañcadaśabhāgīyābhirardheṣṭakā /
bhiś ca saṅkhyā pūritā /
dvitīye pādeṣṭakāṇūkāṣaḍbāgīyābhiś ca pūritā /
tadihāpe pādā ardhā aṇūkāś ca vihi /

children.translated_text: Those exist.

children.text: tasmāt pādeṣṭakābhirardheṣṭakābhiś ca saṅkhcā pūritādvitīye ṣoḍaśībhiś ca yathā yogaṃ saṅkhyāpūraṇaṃ yuktamiti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the count is completed with quarter-bricks and half-bricks, and in the second [layer] with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> as well — thus count-completion as appropriate is understood.

children.text: kiñca saṅkhyāpūraṇasya nyāyyatve sati atropadiṣṭeṣṭakābhyo 'nyābhiḥsaṅkhyāpūraṇasyāśakyatvāt pādābhirardhābhiś ca sukaratvāt tābhireva saṅkhyāpūraṇaṃ yuktataram /
children.translated_text: Moreover, since count-completion is proper, and since it is impossible to complete the count with bricks other than those prescribed here, and since it is easily done with quarter-bricks and half-bricks, count-completion with those very [bricks] is most appropriate.

children.text: ataḥ pracchāditāsu kāściduddhṛtya pādārdhaṣoḍaśībhairyathāyogaṃ yāvatsaṅkhyamupadheyā iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having removed some from the covered [layer], one should place <s>pāda</s>-bricks, half-bricks, and <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> as appropriate until the count [is reached].

When thus covering with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, for count-completion, when some [bricks] are removed, whatever field — square or triangular — results, that field should be covered with half-bricks or quarter-bricks — the meaning is: one should complete the count with those. Now, how is count-completion [achieved] by the statement 'one should cover'? It is said:
Because in each fire-altar, following the covering-rule, there is the injunction 'complete the count.'
And here, when covered with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, since the count is not completed, the second covering-statement, in view of completing it, is understood to be for count-completion only.
Moreover, the basic fire-altar is of two kinds: [one with] only equal-square bricks, and [one with] unequal-square bricks.
In the first square fire-altar, the count was completed with fifteenth-part bricks and half-bricks.
In the second, it was completed with quarter-bricks, <s>aṇūka</s>-bricks, and sixth-part bricks.
Here too, quarter-bricks, halves, and <s>aṇūkas</s> are prescribed.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
'Should... cover' —

children.text:
yaccaturaśraṃ trayaśri veti pādyārdhābhiḥ saṅkhyāpūraṇaṃ, tatrar(dhyār) dhābhiḥ pūraṇapakṣe ātmani prācyaḥ ṣaḍrītayaḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇottarayormadhye ṣaṭ ṣaḍar(dhyār)dhāḥ /
dvitīyasyāṃ paścātpurastācca dve ardhe ukte /
tayoḥ samīpe dve ṣoḍaśyau prāgāyate /
tayormadhye 'ṣṭāvardheṣṭakāḥ /
evameva pañcamī rītiḥ /
prāgāyatābhiḥ dvādaśabhiḥ ṣoḍaśībhirmadhyarītī dve /
pucchāpyaye dve ṣoḍaśyau /
pratyagagrapucchaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulena pūrvāccatasraḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ udagāyatāḥ /
pucchāgre dakṣiṇator'dheṣṭakā pūrvamuktā /
tasyā udak ṣoḍaśyudagagrā tasyā udagdve ardhe tato dve ṣoḍaśyau tato dve ar(dhyer)dhe tataḥ ṣoḍaśī /
tator(dhyār)dhā pūrvamuktā /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
pādyābhiḥ pūraṇapakṣe ātmani dakṣiṇapārśve dvādaśārdhyā uddhṛtya vā aṣṭau catasraḥ ṣoḍaśyo nidheyāḥ /
evamuttarapārśve 'pi /
asminnapi prastāre prakārāntaramāha ----
children.translated_text:
'Whatever square or triangular' — count-completion with <s>pāda</s>-bricks and half-bricks. In the case of completion with half-bricks: in the body, six eastward courses.
There, in the middle of the south and north, six-six halves.
In the second [course], behind and in front, two halves as stated.
Near those, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> extending eastward.
Between those, eight half-bricks.
Likewise the fifth course.
With twelve eastward-extending <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, the two middle courses.
At the tail-junction, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
In the tail with westward-facing tip, with fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, from the east, four <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> extending northward.
At the tail-tip on the south, a half-brick as previously stated.
North of that, a <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> with northward tip; north of that, two halves; then two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>; then two halves; then a <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>.
Then a half as previously stated.
Thus the layer of two hundred.
In the case of completion with <s>pāda</s>-bricks: in the body, on the southern side, removing twelve halves, four-four <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be placed.
Likewise on the northern side also.
In this layer too, he states an alternative method —
'The last — the outer' —

children.text:
atrāpi vāśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ /
yathā pūrvasmin prastāre antyā bāhyaviśeṣā iti ṣoḍaśyo vihitāḥ tathātrāpi śroṇyaṃseṣu dve dve ṣoḍaśyau prāgagre pratyagagre cetyaṣṭau nidheyāḥ /
etadapyaśakyatvātpakṣayorna bhavati /
asmin pakṣe śiro 'pyaye ardhenopadheye /
pucchāpyaye 'pyardhe dve upadheye /
pārśvasthāścatasro rītayordhe 'ṣṭakābhiḥpūraṇīyāḥ /
madhyamarītyoḥ ṣoḍaśaṣoḍaśyaḥ pucchāgramadhye ṣaṭ ṣoḍaśyaḥ /
tataḥ pūrvasyāṃ madhye dve ṣoḍaśyau /
śeṣer'dhyāḥ /
tataḥ pūrvasyāṃ madhye dve prācyau ṣoḍaśyau /
śeṣaṃ pūrvavadeva /
eṣa dviśataḥ /
pādyābhiḥ pūraṇapakṣe 'pi pūrvavatsarvatrāviśeṣāt pādāyābhiḥ sambhave 'pi viparītaviśeṣā upadheyāḥ /
kecittu antyā bāhyaviśeṣā iti pūrvamuktam /
tayoreva prastārayoḥ śeṣamāhuḥ /
tadanupapannaṃ, antyānāṃ ṣoḍaśīnāṃ aniyataviśeṣāṇāmabhāvāt /
ubhayasmin prastāre prāhuḥ antyā iti na kevalaṃ ṣoḍaśya eva gṛhyante /
apitu yāḥ kāśvāntyā upadheyāḥ tāś ca bāhyaviśeṣāḥ kāryā iti /
teṣāṃ śirasi dve ṣoḍaśyau bāhyaviśeṣe bāhyaviśeṣābhyāṃ parigṛhṇīyāt /
children.translated_text: Of those, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> at the head as outer modifications — one should encompass [them] with the outer modifications.

children.text: ātmakaraṇīnāṃ sandhiṣu ṣoḍaśyo bāhyaviśeṣā iti bāhyaviśeṣa śabdakaṃ anarthakaṃ syāt /
