children.translated_text: If [one says] '<s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> at the junctions of the body-<s>karaṇīs</s> are outer modifications,' the word 'outer modification' would be meaningless.
'Other than the head, other than the tail' — these two [statements] are contradictory.
Because outer modifications are desired only for <s>pāda</s>-bricks at the head and half-bricks at the sides of the tail.

Here too the word 'or' should be supplied.
Just as in the previous layer, <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> were prescribed as 'the last [are] outer modifications,' so here too at the haunches and shoulders, two-two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> with eastward tips and westward tips — eight — should be placed.
This alternative is not [applicable] for the wings, due to impossibility.
In this alternative, at the head-junction, halves should be placed.
At the tail-junction also, two halves should be placed.
The four courses on the sides should be filled with half-bricks.
In the two middle courses, sixteen <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> each; at the tail-tip middle, six <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
Then in the middle of the [course] before that, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
The remainder [consists of] halves.
Then in the middle of the [course] before that, two eastward <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
The rest is as before.
This [totals] two hundred.
Even in the case of completion with <s>pāda</s>-bricks, as before, since there is no difference everywhere, even when completion with <s>pāda</s>-bricks is possible, bricks with reversed orientation should be placed.
But some say: 'the last [are] outer modifications' was stated previously.
They state the remainder for those very two layers.
That is improper, because there are no last <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> of unspecified orientation.
In both layers they say: by 'the last,' not only <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> are meant,
but rather: whatever last [bricks] are to be placed, those should be made as outer modifications.
'Whatever... should' —

children.text: ṣoḍaśībhiḥ pūrayitumaśakyopi yāvaddviśatapūrti ardhāḥ pādyā upadheyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when unable to fill with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, halves and <s>pāda</s>-bricks should be placed until completing two hundred.
Because it is impossible to complete the count with <s>pāda</s>-bricks alone without halves.
Therefore, completion is with halves or with <s>pāda</s>-bricks mixed [with halves].
And that method has been stated previously once.
This is common to both layers.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.
'<s>Aṇūka</s>-bricks [are used] in place of fifteenth-part bricks.'

children.text: vyatyāsaṃ cinuyād yāvataḥ prastārāṃś cikīrṣet || ĀpŚus_20.14 ||
children.translated_text: 'One should lay in alternation for as many layers as one wishes to construct.'

children.text:
sthānaśabdaḥ prayogavācī /
aṇūkāścaturbhāgīyāḥ saṅkhyāpūraṇe coditāḥ pañcadaśabhāgīyāś ca saṅghayāpūraṇe coditā itī yāvat /
asmin prastāre saṅkhyā na pūritā sūtrakāreṇa /
tatra tābhiḥsaṅkhyā pūrayitavyā yadi tābhiḥ pūryate /
asminnagau tāvatā na śakyate aṇūkābhiḥsaṅkhyā pūraṇam /
śakyate tu prakṛtau /
tasmātprakṛtyarthau yogaḥ /
tatra śakyate dvitīye prastāre tābhiḥ pūrayitum /
tatra dviśatapūraṇamavaśyaṃ kartavyam /
pratiprastāraṃ pūrayediti vacanāt /
iha tu sahasrasaṃkhyaiva pūrayitavyā ityuktaṃ pūrvasmin paṭale /
tasmātprakṛto yogaḥ /
tatra ślokāḥ ----
children.translated_text:
The word <s>sthāna</s> (place) means 'application.'
<s>Aṇūka</s>-bricks, which are fourth-part [bricks], are enjoined for count-completion, and fifteenth-part bricks are also enjoined for count-completion — this is the purport.
In this layer, the count was not completed by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.
There, the count should be completed with those [bricks], if it can be completed with those.
In this fire-altar, to that extent, count-completion with <s>aṇūka</s>-bricks is not possible.
But it is possible in the basic [altar].
Therefore, the connection is for the basic [altar's] purpose.
There, it is possible to complete with those in the second layer.
There, the completion of two hundred must necessarily be done.
Because of the statement 'one should complete for each layer.'
But here, the count of one thousand itself should be completed — thus was stated in the previous chapter.
Therefore, the connection is with the basic [altar].
On this, the verses —
The mould of the wing-bricks should be made by reversing to half.
The wing-tip [bricks] likewise should be made by reversing to half.
And the <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be made reversed — [each] pair of <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.
In the thousand[-brick altar] and in the two-thousand, the wise know sixty-five.
In placement, according to the <s>sūtra</s>, [the wise know] how [many] <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> in the body, in the wings,

children.text: pucche śirasi śiṣṭe ca ṣoḍaśīnāṃ vidurbudhāḥ //
children.translated_text: in the tail, in the head, and in the remainder.

children.text: ṣaṭprācyaḥ ṣaṭprīcyaś ca ātmani dvādaśa kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Six eastward and six westward — twelve should be placed in the body.
Two should be placed transversely at the head — just those fourteen as stated.

children.text: śiṣṭaṃ rītidvayaṃ pucche tathā cātmanyapi dvayam /
children.translated_text: The remaining two courses in the tail, and likewise two in the body,
sixteen half-bricks — and those should be placed in three courses.
One each on the northern side, three-three on the southern side.
In the remainder, transversely ten only — two hundred and eight.
At the tail-junction, four field-[bricks] — one should place <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>.

children.text: ṣoḍaśyāvapyaye prācyau te cāgre śirasi kṣipet //
children.translated_text: Two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> facing east at the junction, and those at the tip should be placed at the head.

children.text: madhye tayoś ca dvāvardhau catasro viśayāḥ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: And between those two, two halves — four field-[bricks] should be placed.
In the remainder of the body, two halves — <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be placed at the head.
Everything else according to the <s>sūtra</s> — two hundred minus twelve.
On the southern side of the body, four [bricks] extending southward.

children.text: dvitīye cottare pārśve ṣaḍ dve śroṇyaṃsayorapi /
children.translated_text: And in the second [layer], on the northern side, six; two at the haunches and shoulders also.
And one at the junction of the head; and at the head also one [extending] southward.
These <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be placed reversed in the two layers.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
'<s>Aṇūka</s> — in place' —

children.text:
paribhāṣeyam /
pañcadaśabhāgīyāḥ prathamacaturaśre uktāḥ /
tāsāṃ sthāne kāryasaṃkhyāpūraṇe aṇūkā bhaveyuḥ /
tasyāḥ paribhāṣāyā atropadeśaḥ katham? ihopadiṣṭāḥ ṣoḍaśyo 'pi kṣetrasāmyādaṇūkāśabdena grāhyā bhaveyuḥ ityevamartham /
tena aṇūkābhiścaturaśre 'gnau saṃkhyāpūraṇam /
iha tu ṣoḍaśībhiśvoti siddham /
kecidyaccaturaśraṃ tryaśri vā sampadyate ityetadapi paribhāṣāmicchanti /
tena tatratatrāgnau tadapekṣyā tābhirapi saṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ manyante /
atra punaḥ pracchādayediti vacanaṃ pracchādane 'pi caitā yathā bhaveyurityevamartham /
tena tatratatrāgnau sati sambhave satyāṃ cāpekṣāyāṃ tābhiḥsahaubhirapi pracchādanaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text:
This is a general rule (<s>paribhāṣā</s>).
Fifteenth-part bricks were stated for the first square [altar].
In their place, for completing the required count, <s>aṇūka</s>-bricks should be [used].
How is this general rule applicable here? The <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> prescribed here too, because of equal area, should be understood by the term '<s>aṇūka</s>' — this is the purpose.
Thereby, count-completion in the square fire-altar is with <s>aṇūka</s>-bricks.
But here, it is established with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> as well.
Some consider 'whatever square or triangular [space] results' also to be a general rule.
By that, they hold that count-completion in various fire-altars should be done with those [bricks] too, keeping that [rule] in view.
Here however, the statement 'one should cover' has this purpose: that these [bricks] should be [present] in the covering also.
Thereby, in various fire-altars, when there is possibility and when there is need, covering should be done with both those [types of bricks] together.

children.text:
upadhānakramaḥ dvitīyacityāṃ śirasi prāṅbhukhe bāhyaviśeṣe dve ṣoḍaśyau upadadhyāt /
tayoḥ paścāt prāṅbhukhe bāhyaviśeṣe viśaye dve ardhe /
tayoḥ paścāttadviśeṣaśliṣṭaviśeṣe dve ṣoḍaśyau viśaye ātmani /
tayordakṣiṇasyā dakṣiṇato bāhyaviśeṣamekamardham /
uttarasyā uttarataś ca bāhyaviśeṣamekamardham /
tayordakṣiṇata uttarataś ca bāhyaviśeṣeṇaikaikamardham /
tataḥ paścādātmani prācyaḥṣaḍrītayaḥ /
tatra dakṣiṇasyāṃ rītyāṃ purastāt bāhyaviśeṣā prāgagraikā ṣoḍśī /
pasvācca bāhyaviśeṣā pratyagagraikā /
tayormadhye ṣaḍardheṣṭakāḥ /
tāsāṃ tisraḥ pratīcyastisra udīcyaḥ /
dvitīyasyāṃ rītyāṃ paścāt bāhyaviśeṣeṇa dakṣiṇāmukhe dve ardhe /
tatpurastādardhaviśeṣayuktaviśeṣāt pratyaṅbhukhaikā ṣoḍaśī /
tasyā /
purastāt ṣaḍardhāḥ /
tāsāṃ tisrastisraḥ prācya pratīcyaś ca /
tatpurastātuttarato viśeṣā prāgagraikā ṣoḍaśī /
tatpurastāttadviśeṣaśliṣṭaviśeṣamekamardham /
tatpurastāt pūrvopahitamardhamastyeveti dvādaśeṣṭakā eṣā /
tṛtīyasyāṃ rītyāṃ śiro 'pyayaṣoḍaśyāḥ paścādārabhya āpucchāpyayamaṣṭau ṣoḍaśya upadheyāḥ /
tāsāṃ catasraḥ prācyaścatasraḥ pratīcyaḥ /
evamevottarāstisro rītayaḥ /
tatra tṛtīyāvaccaturthī /
dvitīyāvatpañcamī /
prathamāvat ṣaṣṭhī /
tatra tisṛṇāṃ dakṣiṇarītīnāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvamuttararītīnāmuttaraṃ pārśvam /
dakṣiṇānāmuttarāṇaṃ ca dakṣiṇā pārśvarītidvayagatā /
atra pratīcyo mukulātmakāḥ /
tatpratīpamukāḥ prācyaḥ /
evaṃ śobhāṃ vitanvate /
pucche madhyamarītyantayorviśayaṣoḍasyordākṣiṇata uttarataś ca dve ardhe bāhyaviśeṣe /
tataḥ paścānmadhye dve ṣoḍaśyau /
te abhita(stitasra)stisro 'rdheṣṭakā ityaṣṭeṣṭakāḥ /
tataḥ pucchāgre ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣoḍaśībhirabhitor'dhābhiraṣṭeṣṭakāḥ /
pakṣāgrayoścatasraścatasror'dheṣṭakāḥ /
pakṣadvaye pakṣeṣṭakāḥsapta rītayaḥ /
tā dvādaśaśatamiṣṭakāḥ /
pādeṣṭakābhiś ca pūraṇapakṣe etā eva rītayaḥ /
tatra viśeṣaḥ pucchagatopāntarītyāṃ bāhyāsvatasror'dheṣṭakā dvidhā kuryāt /
ātmani prathamadvitīyapañcamaṣaṣṭheṣu tanmadhyagatārdheṣu paścimato dve dve ardhe /
avaśiṣṭānyeṣvardhasthāneṣu ṣoḍaśīyugmānyupadadhyāt /
dvitīyāpañcamyośvārdhā dvidhā bhidyāt /
nanu bhedo varjanīya iti tatratatrāgnau yatnena parihṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: But it was said that splitting should be avoided — and indeed in various fire[-altars] it was carefully avoided with effort.
Is it now manifesting in the tail? This is not essential.

children.text: niyatalokānāmiṣṭakānāmasaṃbādhena samuditābhiriṣṭakābiḥsaṅkhyāyāṃ pūritāyāṃ yadīṣṭakaikadeśe bheda upajāyate sa bhedo marṣaṇīya eva, avarjanīyatvādekadeśabhedasya /
children.translated_text: When bricks of fixed positions complete the count together with [other] bricks without crowding, if splitting arises in one part of a brick, that splitting should be tolerated, since partial splitting is unavoidable.

children.text: ata eva bhedavarjanaṃ svakaṇṭhenoktamācāryeṇa dviśata eṣa iti //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the avoidance of splitting was stated by the teacher in his own words: 'this is a two-hundred [layer].'

The order of placement in the second layer: in the head, one should place two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> facing east with external distinction. Behind those, two halves facing east with external distinction in the domain. Behind those, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> in the body with distinction adjoining that distinction. To the south of the southern one, one half with external distinction. To the north of the northern one, one half with external distinction. To the south and north of those, one half each with external distinction. Then behind, in the body, six rows (<s>rīti</s>) running east. There, in the southern row, in front, one <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> with tip pointing east, with external distinction. And behind, one with tip pointing west, with external distinction. Between those, six half-bricks. Of those, three facing west and three facing north. In the second row, behind, with external distinction, two halves facing south. In front of that, one <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> facing west, from the distinction joined with the half-distinction. In front of that, six halves. Of those, three each facing east and west. In front of that, to the north, one <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> with tip pointing east, with distinction. In front of that, one half with distinction adjoining that distinction. In front of that, the previously placed half is already there — thus twelve bricks in this [row]. In the third row, beginning behind the head-junction <s>ṣoḍaśī</s>, up to the tail-junction, eight <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> should be placed. Of those, four facing east and four facing west. The three northern rows are exactly the same. There, the fourth is like the third. The fifth is like the second. The sixth is like the first. There, the southern side of the three southern rows and the northern side of the northern rows [are at the edges]. The southern-side row-pair belongs to both the southern and northern [sets]. Here, the west-facing [bricks] have a bud-like (<s>mukula</s>) character. The east-facing ones are opposite in orientation. Thus they create beauty. In the tail, between the middle row and the end, to the south and north of the domain-<s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>, two halves with external distinction. Then behind, in the middle, two <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>. On both sides of those, three and three half-bricks — thus eight bricks. Then at the tail-tip, with six <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> and halves on both sides, eight bricks. At the wing-tips, four and four half-bricks. In both wings, seven rows of wing-bricks. Those are twelve hundred bricks. With quarter-bricks for count-completion, these same rows [apply]. Therein the distinction: in the penultimate row at the tail, the outer four half-bricks should be split in two. In the body, in the first, second, fifth, and sixth [rows], two and two halves at the back among those placed in their middles. In the remaining half-positions, one should place <s>ṣoḍaśī</s> pairs. In the second and fifth [rows], the halves should be split in two.
'In alternation' — [up to] 'should discard.'
This has been explained.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
'<s>Aṇūka</s>' — [up to] 'should place.'

children.text:
prakṛtau caturaśrāgnau pañcadaśabhāgīyānāṃ kāryaṃ bhedaparihāreṇa saṃkhyāpūraṇam /
iha tu tatkārye aṇūkā upadheyāḥ /
tatra samacaturaśrāṇāmaṇūkānāmupadhāne dviśataḥ kartuṃ na śakyate /
tasmādaṇūkakṣetrāṇāṃ grahaṇam /
tatrāpi ṣoḍaśyo na gṛhyante /
avaśiṣṭaṃ ṣoḍaśībhirityeva siddhatvāt bhedasambhavācca /
tasmāda (nyā ) ṇūkakṣetrādi (dvi) prakārā iṣṭakāḥ kartavyāḥ /
darśite ca tāsāṃ karaṇe (pūrvameva) /

children.translated_text: But the teacher has not prescribed their manufacture [explicitly].
In the option where 'the last [bricks have] external distinction,' there is no use for <s>aṇūkas</s>.
And the method of placement has been stated.

children.text: aṇūkābhirvinaiva tasmin pakṣe prathama eva prastāre aṇūkānāmupayogaḥ kartavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Without <s>aṇūkas</s> at all — in that option, the use of <s>aṇūkas</s> should be made in the first layer only.

In the primary quadrilateral fire[-altar], the function of fifteenth-part [bricks] is count-completion while avoiding splitting. Here, however, <s>aṇūkas</s> (small bricks) should be placed for that function. There, in the placement of square <s>aṇūkas</s>, making two hundred is not possible. Therefore, one should take <s>aṇūka</s>-fields. Even there, <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s> are not taken. Since 'the remainder with <s>ṣoḍaśīs</s>' is already established and splitting is possible. Therefore, <s>aṇūka</s>-field and other two-type bricks should be made. And their manufacture has been shown [earlier].
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: kaṅkacid alajacid iti śyenacitā vyākhyātau || ĀpŚus_21.1 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kaṅka</s>-altar (heron-altar) and the <s>alaja</s>-altar are explained by the hawk-altar. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.1 ||

children.text:
kaṅkaḥ pakṣiviśeṣaḥ alajaś ca /
kaṅka iva cetavyaḥ kaṅkacit /

children.translated_text: That which should be piled like an <s>alaja</s> is the <s>alajacit</s>.

children.text: tau śyenacitā vyākhyātau -- pūrveṇaiva śyenena vyākhyātau /
children.translated_text: Those two are explained by the hawk-altar — explained by the same hawk [described] earlier.

children.text: mukhyatvāddviśataprastāratvācca tasyaivākṛtiḥ tānyeva karaṇāni sa evopadhānamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because it is primary and because of the two-hundred-layer [rule], its very shape, those very molds, and that very method of placement [apply].

children.text: saṅkalpa eva bhedaḥ śyeno 'lajaḥ kaṅka iti //
children.translated_text: The difference is only in the ritual intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) — hawk, <s>alaja</s>, or heron.
The <s>kaṅka</s> (heron) is a particular bird, and the <s>alaja</s> also. That which should be piled like a <s>kaṅka</s> is the <s>kaṅkacit</s> (heron-altar).

children.text: evami va hi śyenasya varṣīyāṃsau pakṣau pucchād vakrau saṃnataṃ pucchaṃ dīrgha ātmā maṇḍalaṃ śiraś ca | tasmāc chrutisāmarthyāt || ĀpŚus_21.2a ||
children.translated_text: For thus indeed the hawk has wings larger than the tail, curved [wings], a narrow tail, a long body, and a round head — therefore, by the force of scripture. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.2a ||

children.text:
hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau /
śyeno 'pyevameva /
varṣīyāṃsau -- bṛhantau /
pakṣau /
kasmāt pucchāddīrghau? na kevalaṃ bṛlantau kiṃ tu tau vakrau /
sannataṃ samyaṅnataṃ ātmasamīpe 'lpīyaḥ agre śyene pṛthu ucyate tatsannatamiti /
dīrgha ātmā naṃ samacaturaśraḥ na maṇḍalaḥ nāpi dīrghacaturaśraḥ /
amaṇḍalamivādīrghacaturaśrabhūtaṃ śiraḥ /
evamprakāro loke śyenaḥ /
evameva kaṅkālajo loke /
tasmāttadākārāveva kaṅkālajau tenaiva vyākhyātau /
śrutisāmarthyāt /

children.translated_text: 'Force' means the power of expression.
This much alone is expressed by scripture.
Because it is impossible to achieve complete likeness.
For the <s>Veda</s> does not prescribe what cannot be accomplished.

The word 'hi' is used in the sense of well-known [fact]. The hawk too is exactly thus. 'Larger' — [meaning] great. The wings. Why longer than the tail? Not merely great but also curved. 'Narrow' (<s>sannata</s>) — properly narrowing; near the body [it is] smaller, at the tip of the hawk it is called broad — that is 'narrow.' The body is long — neither a square nor circular, nor an oblong rectangle. The head is not-circular — [meaning] not an oblong rectangle. Such is the hawk in the world. The heron and <s>alaja</s> are exactly the same in the world. Therefore the heron and <s>alaja</s> [altars] are of that very shape, and are explained by that same [hawk-altar]. By the force of scripture.
Or [they may be] headless, because [the head] is not mentioned. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.2b ||

children.text:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣavyāvṛttau /
aśiraska eva cetavyaḥ /
kuta ityāha -- ānāmnānāt /
na hi śira āmnāyate /
tasya kathamanāmnānamityatrāha ----
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) serves to exclude the [previous] option. [The altar] should be piled as headless. Why? — he says: because of non-mention. For the head is not mentioned [in scripture]. How there is non-mention of it — to this he says:

children.text: jñāyate ca | kaṅkacitaṃ śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta saśīrṣo 'muṣmiṃl loke saṃbhaveyam iti vidyamāne kathaṃ brūyāt || ĀpŚus_21.3 ||
children.translated_text: And it is known [from scripture]: 'one who desires "may I be born with a head in the other world" should pile the <s>kaṅka</s>-altar with a head' — when [a head] already existed, why would [scripture] say this? || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.3 ||

children.text:
yadi śirasa āmnānamasti śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīteti kathaṃ brūyādevetyarthaḥ /
yadi śirasa āmnānaṃ nāsti tadā yujyata evaitadviśeṣaṇam /
itarathā viśeṣaṇamanarthakameva syāt /
tasmādaśiraska eva cetavyaḥ /
cadyaśiraskaḥ kimākāraḥsa ityāha--
children.translated_text: If there is a mention of a head [in the basic form], then how would one say 'one should pile with a head' — that is the meaning. If there is no mention of a head, then this qualifying statement is fitting. Otherwise, the qualification would be meaningless. Therefore [the altar] should be piled as headless. If headless, what is its shape? — to this he says:

children.text: prākṛtau vakrau pakṣau saṃnataṃ pucchaṃ vikāraśravaṇāt || ĀpŚus_21.4a ||
children.translated_text: The wings are as in the primary [form], curved; the tail is narrow — because of the mention of modification. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.4a ||

children.text:
prakṛtyāṃ bhavau prākṛtau /
tāveva pakṣau vakrīkartavyau /
kutaḥ? vikāraśravaṇāt /
sannataṃ pucchaṃ -- pucchaṃ ca sannataṃ kartavyam /
children.translated_text: The tail is narrow — the tail should be made narrow.
'Curved-winged, expanded-tailed' — modification is heard [in scripture].

children.text: pakṣapucchānāṃ ca vaktatā vyastatā ca prakṛtau nāsti /
children.translated_text: And the curvature of the wings and expansion of the tail do not exist in the primary [form].
Therefore the wings and tail are modified.
'Primary' (<s>prākṛtau</s>) — belonging to the primary [form]. Those very wings should be made curved. Why? Because of the mention of modification.
The body is as in the primary [form], because of non-modification. || <s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.4b ||

children.text:
yathāprakṛtyātmā /
kutaḥ? avikārāt /
nahi tatra vikāraḥśrūyate /
tasmātpraṅkṛtivadevātmā catuḥpuruṣaḥsamacaturaśraś ca /
aratninār'dhaprādeśena vā pakṣau vivadheyet /
dvipuruṣāṃ rajjumityādiśyenavat /
nanu prakṛtāvaratninā vardhayedityuktam /
kimidamucyate aratninār'dhaprādeśena veti? aratninetyardhavikāratvapratipādanaparaṃ, na pakṣapucchānāṃ tāvanmātramāyāmamāpādayitum /
ātmanaścaturthaṃ caturbhāgīyāśvāṣṭau ityupadhātavyamiti
children.translated_text: The body is as in the primary [form]. Why? Because of non-modification. For no modification is heard there [in scripture]. Therefore the body is exactly as in the primary [form] — of four <s>puruṣas</s> and square. One should augment the wings with an <s>aratni</s> or with a half-<s>prādeśa</s>. 'A cord of two <s>puruṣas</s>' etc. — as in the hawk[-altar]. But in the primary [form], it was said 'one should augment with an <s>aratni</s>.' What is meant by saying 'with an <s>aratni</s> or a half-<s>prādeśa</s>'? 'With an <s>aratni</s>' is meant to convey the half-modification nature, not to establish that much length for the wings and tail. 'The fourth of the body and eight <s>caturbhāgīyas</s>' — this [rule] for placement

children.text:
śyenapratipāditaṃ na kartavyam /
yathāprakṛtyevātmā kartavyaḥ /
kiṃ ca prākṛtaṃ pucchamiti vacanācca upadhānavidhiś ca na ghaṭate /
śyena iva cetavya ityevaṃ kriyamāṇe prathamadvitīyānāmeva vikāro netareṣām /
itarathā caturthādayo 'pi vikṛtā bhaveyuḥ /
tathābhūtāś ca kartavyā bhaveyuḥ /
tasmācca karaṇānupraveśena cetavya ityuktam /
śyenavadeva puccham /
karaṇānyucyante -- caturthaṣaṣṭhābhyāṃ yathāyoganataṃ tatprathamam /
dve pūrvavatsaṃhite dvitīyamityādi /
athopadhānavidhiḥ -- aṣṭācatvāriṃśatprathamā udīcīḥ pakṣayoḥ /
śyenavatpuccham /
ātmanaḥśroṇyostisrastisraḥ pañcamya udīcyaḥ /
tataḥsaptasu rītiṣu ṣaṭpañcāśaccaturthyaḥ dakṣiṇāyatā udagāyatāś ca /
tāsāṃ purastādaṣṭau pañcamyaḥ udagāyatāḥ /
śroṇyoścatasraḥ pañcamya akṣṇayā bhindyāt /
aṣṭau ṣaṣṭhayaḥsampadyante /
eṣa dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
aparasmin prastāre catasraścatasro dvitīyā nirṇāmayorapyayayoś ca viśayāstṛtīyāḥ /
catasraścatasraḥ pūrvavadaṣṭabhāgāvetāḥ /
pakṣeṣṭakābhiḥ pakṣau pracchādayet /
taddvāsaptatiḥ pucche śyenavat /
saptāṣṭamābhiḥśroṇyaṃseṣu dve dve pañcamyau prācīḥ pratīcīś ca /
prācyaḥ sapta rītayaḥ /
caturmistṛtīyāpañcamyo rītyormadhye triṃśat ṣaṣṭhayaḥ ekā ca pañcamī /
ekatra ṣoḍaśāparatra caturdaśa /
evaṃ dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
athavā sa evānupucchamardhapuruṣavyāsaṃ saprādeśaṃ puruṣaṃ pratīcīnamāyacchet /
tasya dakṣiṇato 'nyamityādinā śyenavatpucchaṃ kuryāt /
pakṣau prākṛtau dvipuruṣāyāmau /
karaṇāni vakṣyāmaḥ -- dvādaśāṅgulā yathā bhavati tatā tiryak caturthaṣaṣṭhābhyāṃ namayet /
prathamaṃ te eva saṃhite yathā tiṣṭhataḥ tathā kārayet /
dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyamapi yat ṣaḍbhāgenāṣṭamabhāgena vā vardhayediti ta eva vā pucche caturthaṃ trayastriṃśadaṅgulavistāraṃ pañcacatvāriṃśadaṅgulāyāmaṃ caturdaśatilairūnaṃ saviśeṣaṃ pañcamaṃ ardhasaptāṅgulavyāsaṃ ṣaṭpārśvaṃ ekonatriṃśadāyāmaṃ tu ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaṃ caturdaśatilaiḥsaha pucchāpyaye viśayayoḥ aṣṭādaśāṅgulaṃ pucche pañcadaśāṅkumeva /
ātmāni caturthādayo vaikṛtāḥ /
pucche tu prākṛtā eva /
ātmanyupadhānavidhiḥsa eva /
tatra ślokāḥ ----
children.translated_text: as taught for the hawk[-altar] should not be applied. The body should be made as in the primary [form] only. Moreover, because of the statement 'the tail is as in the primary [form],' the placement-rule also does not apply. When [the altar] is made as 'it should be piled like the hawk,' the modification applies only to the first and second [parts — wings and tail], not to the others. Otherwise, the fourth and subsequent [parts] would also be modified. And [if so,] they would have to be made thus. Therefore it is said 'it should be piled by entry into the molds.' The tail is just as in the hawk[-altar]. The molds are stated: with the fourth and sixth [parts], bent as appropriate — that is the first. Two joined as before — the second, and so on. Now the placement-rule: forty-eight in the first [layer], facing north in the wings. The tail is as in the hawk[-altar]. At the hips of the body, three and three fifth-[part bricks] facing north. Then in seven rows, fifty-six fourth-[part bricks] extending southward and northward. In front of those, eight fifth-[part bricks] extending northward. At the hips, four fifth-[part bricks] should be split diagonally. Eight sixth-[part bricks] are produced. This is the two-hundred layer. In the other layer: four and four second-[type bricks]; at the bending-points and junctions, the domain-[bricks are] third-[type]. Four and four as before — these are eighth-part. The wings should be covered with wing-bricks. That is seventy-two. The tail is as in the hawk[-altar]. With seven-eighths at the hips and shoulders, two and two fifth-[part bricks] facing east and west. Seven rows facing east. With four-part and third-fifth-[part bricks] in the middle of the rows, thirty sixth-[part bricks] and one fifth-[part brick]. Sixteen on one side, fourteen on the other. Thus the two-hundred layer. Alternatively, that same [altar], without a tail, should be extended a half-<s>puruṣa</s> wide, a <s>puruṣa</s> with <s>prādeśa</s> [addition] westward. By 'to its south another' etc., one should make the tail as in the hawk[-altar]. The wings are as in the primary [form], two <s>puruṣas</s> in length. We shall state the molds: twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> as it should be, transversely; with the fourth and sixth [parts] one should bend [it]. The first: those same joined, as they stand, one should have made. The second, and also the third: that which one should augment by a sixth or eighth part — those same [apply] in the tail. The fourth: thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> in length, diminished by fourteen <s>tilas</s>, with <s>saviśeṣa</s>. The fifth: half-of-seven <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, hexahedral, twenty-nine in length — actually thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> with fourteen <s>tilas</s>. At the tail-junction, in the domains, eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>; in the tail, fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> only. In the body, from the fourth onward, [the bricks are] modified. But in the tail, [they are] as in the primary [form] only. The placement-rule for the body is the same. Therein, verses:
Half of thirteen [is] the width in the headless fire[-altar],
and with the fourth and sixth [parts] one should bend the first [mold].

children.text: te dve tu saṃhite prācī dvitīyaṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Those two joined, facing east — that becomes the second mold.
The third also — augmented by a sixth or eighth part.
The wing-bricks are the fourth; the tail is stated as for the tail [of the hawk-altar].
There should be fifty-six fourth-[part bricks], transverse, extending southward and northward.
In front, eight transverse, and at the hips one should place six fifth-[part bricks].
At the hips, four fifth-[part bricks] split — thus two hundred likewise.
Having placed [bricks] in the wings and tail as in the hawk[-altar], one should also place in the body.

children.text: prācyāṃ caiva pratīcyāṃ ca triṃśadekā ca pañcamī //
children.translated_text: In the eastern and western [halves], thirty [sixth-part bricks] and one fifth-[part brick].
Of those same, on the northern side, two [sets of] sixteen fourth-[part bricks],

children.text: prācyaśvaiva pratīcyaś ca tathā ṣoḍaśa dakṣiṇe //
children.translated_text: eastern and western, and likewise sixteen on the southern [side].

children.text: prācīśvaiva pratīcīś ca śiṣṭe pañcamīṃ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Eastern and western — in the remainder, one should place a fifth-[part brick].
The reversal of the mold is desired only for the fourth [type].

children.text: saprādeśe 'pi vā pucche vistāro dvādaśaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Or, even in [the version with] a tail having a <s>prādeśa</s> [extension], the breadth would be a twelfth;
accordingly, one should bend the first [mold] by the fourth and sixth [parts].

children.text: te dve tu saṃhite prācī dvitīyaṃ karaṇaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: Those two, joined eastward — that is indeed the second <s>karaṇa</s> (mold);
the third also [is] the sixth-part augmented by an eighth-part.
Twenty-two doubled, and also twenty <s>tilas</s>;
the distinctive [measure] of the fourth — the transverse [dimension] is truly greater.
The fifth should be known as the primary [type]; of the sixth, there are three modifications.
The lateral [measure] of the sixth is [thirty-]three plus three; the diagonal is thirty-six with eight [<s>tilas</s>].
The lateral [measure] of the seventh and eighth is desired here as twenty-nine less [one];
and the length also is thirty-six with fourteen <s>tilas</s>.
But the modifications from the fourth onward — one should assign [them] in the tail and body;
eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in the tail; of the other two [dimensions], the [assignment is] in the body.
<s>Karavinda's</s> commentary.
<s>Kaṅka</s> (heron) — both [section heading].

children.text:
kaṅkālajau pakṣiviśeṣau /
kaṅkavaccīyate alajavaccīyat iti kaṅkacidalajacitau śyenacitā vyākhyātau /
tayorvimāneṣṭakākaraṇopadhānāni śyenasyeva kāryāṇītyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Some [say]: with the first hawk [altar], because of its primacy.
Others [say]: with the second hawk, because of [textual] proximity.
Yet others [say]: with both, because there is no distinction.
He restates the form of the hawk that was stated [before], in order to establish the existence of the head right here.

<s>Kaṅka</s> and <s>alaja</s> (buzzard) are particular birds. 'It is piled like a heron,' 'it is piled like a buzzard' — thus the <s>kaṅkacit</s> (heron-altar) and <s>alajacit</s> (buzzard-altar) are explained by [reference to] the <s>śyenacit</s> (hawk-altar). The meaning is: their measurements, bricks, molds, and placement are to be done just as for the hawk.
'Thus indeed' — [section heading for] 'should be known'.

children.text:
evamivahīti gatam /
śyenasya varṣīyāṃsau dīrghatarau pucchādvakrau pakṣau sannataṃ pucchaṃ ātmasamīpe hrasīya agre vyastaṃ dīrgha ātmā na samacaturaśraḥ amaṇḍalaḥ na maṇḍalākāraḥ ---- īṣanmaṇḍalaḥ /
na vā śiraś ca vidyate /
taccāpi na maṇḍalaṃ nāpi samacaturaśram /
evamiva śyeno loke dṛśyate /
etāvadeva śyenasādṛśyamagneḥ /

children.translated_text: From where [is this known]? From the force of scripture — the force means the denotative capacity of the [scriptural] statement.
Just this much is prescribed by the <s>śyena</s>-scripture.
Namely: curved-wing-ness, expanded-tail-ness, elongated-body-ness, non-circular-ness, and having-a-head-ness.
Therefore the <s>kaṅka</s> and <s>alaja</s> too should be piled in that shape — this is the meaning.

'Thus indeed' — this has been explained. The hawk's wings are larger — longer — than the tail and curved; the tail is compressed — narrow at the body-junction, expanded and long at the tip; the body is not a perfect square — not circular, not circular in shape — slightly rounded. And a head exists. And that too is neither circular nor a perfect square. Thus indeed the hawk is seen in the world. Just this much is the resemblance of the fire[-altar] to a hawk.
Without head — because of non-mention [section heading].

children.text:
aśirasko vā śyenaḥ anāmnānāt /
nahi pakṣapucchātmagatavakratādivacchirasa āmnānamasti /
śyenavidhānasāmarthyācchiraso vidhānamastīti gamyata iti kecit /
vayasāṃ vā eṣa pratimayā cīyata iti prakṛtāvapi pakṣādivat śirovidhānaṃ prasajyet /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
tatra hi pakṣapacchavidhānaṃ parisaṃkhyānārtham /
tarhyatrāpi taccodakāgatameveti tasmāt saśiraskaḥśyenaḥ /
kiñca vijñāyate ca kaṅkacitaṃ śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīteti /
yadi codakaprāptayā kaṅke śiro vidyate tatkathaṃ brūyāt brāhyaṇaṃ kaṅkacitaṃ śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīteti? na brūyādevetyarthaḥ /
tasmādaśiraskaḥ śyenaḥ /
kaṅke śirovidhānāt /
tathā te vayomātrasādṛśye prakṛte prāpte śyenaprāptividhānasāmarthyādeva śyene śiro 'pyastīti gamyate /

children.translated_text: And because placement is taught in the head by '<s>trivṛt</s> is the head of the fire[-altar]' etc.
Considering that there is an alternative between these [two views], he states the word 'vā' (or).
Therein, <s>kaṅka</s>, <s>śyena</s>, <s>alaja</s> — the difference is only in the intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), not in form.
Like the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice etc. — [thus] 'the hawk without a head' is stated.

Or the hawk[-altar] may be without a head, because of non-mention [in scripture]. For there is no mention of the head in the manner of the curvature etc. stated for wings, tail, and body. Some [hold that] from the force of the hawk-form prescription, the prescription of a head is understood. [But if so,] since 'this is built in the likeness of birds' [applies], even in the primary [altar] the prescription of a head, like wings etc., would follow. This is not a defect. For there, the prescription of wings and tail is for the purpose of enumeration. 'Then here too that very [head] is obtained from the injunction' — therefore the hawk has a head. Moreover, it is known [from scripture]: 'One should pile the heron-altar with a head.' If the head in the heron[-altar] is obtained [merely] from the injunction, then why would [scripture] state 'one should pile the heron-altar with a head'? It would not state [it] — this is the meaning. Therefore the hawk[-altar] is without a head — because of the [separate] prescription of a head for the heron. And so, when resemblance to birds in general is the established [rule], from the force of the specific hawk-form prescription alone, it is understood that the hawk too has a head.
Primary — because of hearing [section heading].

children.text:
prakṛtivadeva pakṣau vakrau pucchāt sannataṃ vakrapakṣo vyastapuccha iti vikāraśravaṇāt /
ātmā tu yathā prakṛtyā /
yadvā yathāprakṛtiravikṛtaḥ samacaturaśraḥ catuṣpuruṣa ityarthaḥ /
avikārāt -- na hi vikāraḥ śrūyate /
pakṣapuccheṣu vikāragrahaṇaṃ nātmani /
tasmāt prākṛta evātmā /
aratninārdhaprādeśena ca ekaikaṃ pakṣaṃ pravardhayet /
yadyapi prākṛtau pakṣāvityuktaṃ tathāpi pucchasyāprākṛtatvaśraṇāduktaprakārā puruṣamātratā gamyate /
tasmātpucche prādeśamupadhāya pakṣayorvibhajediti kecinmanyante /
kecitpakṣayoḥ prakṛtitvavidhānādātmano 'vikāratvācca pucchaṃ saprādeśaṃ manyante /
ubhayasmin pakṣe 'pyuktaprakāreṇābhyunneyā ityācāryo manyate /
atra pucchasyāprakṛtitvapakṣe prathamadvitīyakaraṇānāṃ vikāraḥ /
itarathā teṣāmapi karaṇānyucyante /
caturthaṣaṣṭhābhyāṃ prathamaṃ karaṇaṃ yathārdhatrayodaśavyāsaṃ bhavati tathā prajambhayet /
te dve prācī saṃhite /
tadditīyaṃ prathamasya ṣaḍbhāgamaṅgulaṃ tṛtīyam /
upadhānamucyate ---- dakṣiṇe pakṣe aṣṭācatvāriṃśatprathamā
children.translated_text: The wings are curved just as in the primary; the tail is compressed from [behind] — because the modifications 'curved-winged, expanded-tailed' are heard. But the body is as per the primary [altar]. Or alternatively, [the body is] as per the primary, unmodified — a perfect square of four <s>puruṣas</s> — this is the meaning. Because of non-modification — for no modification is heard [for the body]. The mention of modification is for wings and tail, not for the body. Therefore the body is just as in the primary. One should augment each wing by an <s>aratni</s> and a half-<s>prādeśa</s>. Although it was stated that the wings are as in the primary, still, because of hearing that the tail is non-primary, the stated one-<s>puruṣa</s> measure is understood. Therefore some think: having assigned a <s>prādeśa</s> to the tail, one should divide [the remainder] between the wings. Others think: because of the prescription of primary-ness for the wings, and because of non-modification of the body, the tail has the <s>prādeśa</s> [extension]. In either view, one should infer [the construction] in the manner stated — so the teacher thinks. Here, in the view that the tail is non-primary, there is modification of the first and second <s>karaṇas</s>. Otherwise, those molds too are stated. One should stretch the first <s>karaṇa</s> by the fourth and sixth [parts] such that the breadth becomes twelve-and-a-half. Those two [bricks] joined eastward [form the second]. The third also [is] the sixth-part of the first, augmented by one <s>aṅgula</s>. The placement is stated: in the southern wing, forty-eight first-[type bricks]

children.text:

tāsāṃ purastācatur(thār)thīnāmardheṣṭakāḥ sapta rītayaḥ /
tāḥ ṣaṭpañcāśat /
tāsāṃ purastādaṣṭau pañcamyaḥ /
śroṇyaṃseṣu catasraḥ /
pañcamīrakṣṇayābhindyāt /
dviśata eṣa prastāraḥ /
dvitīyaprastāre catasraścatasro dvitīyāścatasraścatasra ātmānamaṣṭabhāgāvetāḥ /
pakṣeṣṭakābhiḥ prācībhiḥ pakṣau pracchādayet /
ekaikasmin pakṣe ṣaṭtriṃśat /
pucche tu pūrvavaddvādaśa saptamyastrayodaśāṣṭamyaś ca /
śroṇyaṃseṣu dve dve pañcamyau prācyau /
ātmaśeṣe caturthīnā maṣṭeṣṭakāḥ prācyaḥsapta rītayaḥ /
tṛtīyapañcamarītyormadhye catasraścaturthīruddhṛtya triṃśataṃ ṣaṣṭimekāṃ pañcamīmupadadhyāt /
tāsāmekatra ṣoḍaśa ṣaṣṭiriti /
tatra caturdaśa ekatra pañcamī /
eṣa dviśataḥ prastāraḥ /
sapradeśapakṣe pucche puruṣavyāsaṃ prādeśapuruṣaṃ pratīcīnamāyacchet /
tasya dakṣiṇato 'nyamuttarataśvetyādinā pucchaṃ kuryāt /
pakṣau prakṛtāveva /
karaṇaviśeṣo yathā tiryagṛjutvena dvādaśāṅgulaṃ bhavati tathā prathamaṃ karaṇaṃ prajambhayet /
te dve prājītyādinā dvitīyam /
tṛtīyasyāpi ṣaḍbāgamaṣṭabhāgena vardhitam /
caturthādīni dvividhāni -- pucchacaturthe trayastriṃśadahgulavistāraṃ /
tasya saviśeṣaḥ catuśvatvāriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ viṃśati tilādhikāḥ /
pañcamamardhasaptadaśaṅgulavyāsam /
ṣaṣṭhasya pārśvaṃ trayastriṃśadaṅgulakam /
tāḥṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ /
sāṣṭamayoḥsa eva vyāsaḥ /
pārśvamānyāvakṣṇayāvasthite ekonatriṃśadaṅgule /
āyāmaḥṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulayaḥ caturdaśa tilāś ca /
pucchāpyayaviśayayoraṣṭādaśāṅgulam /

children.translated_text: Fifteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in the tail; the body-<s>tila</s>-fourth and subsequent modifications should be placed in the tail.
The placement rule is just as in the primary, in the body.
This is the second hawk[-altar].
In the modification, having inferred and made the molds stated therein, one should pile [the altar].

facing north; and similarly in the northern [wing], facing south. In the tail, as stated for the headless version. Thirty in the body. At the hip-corners, three-by-three fifth-[type bricks] extending northward and southward. In front of those, half-bricks of fourth-[type]: seven rows. Those are fifty-six. In front of those, eight fifth-[type bricks]. At the hip-and-shoulder corners, four [bricks]. The fifth-[type brick] should be cut diagonally. This layer is two hundred. In the second layer: four-by-four second-[type bricks], four-by-four [covering] the body — these are the eighth-parts. The wings should be covered with wing-bricks facing east — thirty-six in each wing. In the tail, as before: twelve seventh-[type] and thirteen eighth-[type bricks]. At the hip-and-shoulder corners, two-by-two fifth-[type bricks] facing east. In the remainder of the body: eight bricks of fourth-type facing east, seven rows. Having removed four fourth-[type bricks] from the middle of the third and fifth rows, one should place thirty-one [and] sixty — one fifth-[type brick]. Of those, sixteen in one [group] and sixty [in another]. There, fourteen [and] one fifth-[type brick] in one [group]. This layer is two hundred. In the version with <s>prādeśa</s>-[extended] wings: in the tail, one should extend westward [a rectangle] of <s>puruṣa</s>-breadth and <s>prādeśa</s>-plus-<s>puruṣa</s> [length]. 'To the south of that, another, and to the north' etc. — thus one should make the tail. The wings are as in the primary. The distinctive mold — one should stretch the first <s>karaṇa</s> so that the transverse [measure] when straight becomes twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>. 'Those two joined eastward' etc. — [this gives] the second. Of the third also, the sixth-part augmented by an eighth-part. The fourth and subsequent [molds] are of two kinds: in the tail-fourth, thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth. Its distinctive [diagonal] is forty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty additional <s>tilas</s>. The fifth [has] half-of-seventeen-<s>aṅgula</s> breadth. The lateral [measure] of the sixth is thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s>. Those are thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s>. Of the seventh and eighth, that same breadth. The lateral measures in the diagonal position are twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s>. The length is thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> and fourteen <s>tilas</s>. For those concerning the tail-junction area: eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.
<s>Sundararāja's</s> commentary.
Transposition — would desire [section heading].
<s>Kaṅka</s> (heron) — explained [section heading].

children.text:
"kaṅkacitaṃ śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta śīrṣaṇvānamuṣmin loke syāmiti' /
alajacitaṃ cinvīta catuḥsītaṃ pratiṣṭhākāma' iti śrutāvagnī śyenacitā pūrveṇottareṇa vā vyākhyātau /
athoktasyaiva śyenacitaḥ prakārāntaraṃ vidhitsan uktau tāvatprakārau yuktatarāviti darśayitumāha --
children.translated_text: 'One who desires to have a head in the other world should pile the heron-altar with a head.' 'One who desires firm establishment should pile the buzzard-altar with four furrows' — these fire[-altars] mentioned in scripture are explained by [reference to] the <s>śyenacit</s>, by the preceding or the subsequent [description]. Now, wishing to prescribe another manner of the very hawk-altar already stated, in order to show that the two manners [already] stated are more appropriate, he says:
'Thus indeed' — 'from the force' [section heading].

children.text: yathāsmābhiruktaṃ evamiva hi patataḥ śyenasya pakṣau pucchādvarṣīyāṃsau vakrau ca madhyataḥ pucchaṃ ca sannatamapyayapradeśe ātmā ca āmaṇḍalaḥ īṣanmaṇḍalarūpaḥ śiraśvaivaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: As stated by us — 'thus indeed of a flying hawk, the wings are larger than the tail and curved in the middle; the tail is compressed at the junction area; the body is somewhat circular — slightly rounded in form; and the head is just so.'
Therefore — because of the hearing of the word 'tat' (that), the word 'yat' (which) should be supplied.
Or the word 'hi' [is used] in the causal sense.

children.text: yasmādevaṃrūpaḥ śyenasya pakṣapucchādiḥ pratyakṣeṇa dṛśyate tatmāt śyenacitaṃ cinvīteti śrutisāmarthyādevaṃrūpapakṣapucchātmaśiraskaḥ śyenacidityukta ityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since the wings, tail, etc. of the hawk are seen directly in this form, therefore, from the force of the scripture 'one should pile the hawk-altar,' [it follows that] the hawk-altar has wings, tail, body, and head of this form — this is the meaning.
Without head — because of non-mention [section heading].

children.text:
aśirasko vā śyenacidbhavitumarhati /
anāmnānāt; na(hi)ca śyenacitprakaraṇe śira āmnāyate /
ātmano 'pyavikārasyaitadupalakṣaṇam /
aśiraska (tve) kalpe pramāṇāntaramastītyāha----
children.translated_text: Or the hawk-altar may be without a head, because of non-mention — for the head is not mentioned in the <s>śyenacit</s> section. This is also indicative of the non-modification of the body. In the headless version, there is another measure — he says:
'It is known' — 'would state' [section heading].
If merely by the prescription of hawk-form the having-of-a-head would result,
then the heron-altar too would [automatically] have one.

children.text: tathā ca tatra śīrṣaṇvantamiti viśeṣo na vaktavyaḥsyādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And accordingly, the specification 'with a head' [for the heron] would not need to be stated — this is the meaning.
If it is headless, then what is its form? — he says:
'Primary' — 'because of hearing' [section heading].

children.text:
prākṛtāveva pakṣau pucchau ṣaḍaratniṃ pañcāratniṃ vā /
tau dvipuruṣāṃ rajjumubhayataḥpāśāmityuktaprakāreṇa vakrīkartavyau /
kecittu pūrvoktāyāma (bhāvāt) mārgāt ṣaṣṭiśatāṅgulayā rajjvā saṃnamana (mapī)micchanti /
pucchaṃ ca prākṛtameva sannataṃ ardhapuruṣavyāsam /
puruṣaṃ prādeśādhikaṃ pratīcīnamāyacchet /
tasya dakṣiṇato 'nyamityādi pūrvavat /
prādeśapravṛddhayabhāve pūrvavadeva /
vikāraśravaṇāditi ---- vakrapakṣo vyastapuccho bhavatīti vacanādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wings are just as in the primary — of six <s>aratnis</s> or five <s>aratnis</s>. Those should be curved in the manner stated by 'a cord of two <s>puruṣas</s> with loops at both ends.' But some, from the [previously] stated path of length, desire bending with a cord of one hundred and sixty <s>aṅgulas</s> also. The tail too is just as in the primary — compressed, of half-<s>puruṣa</s> breadth. One should extend westward [a rectangle of] one <s>puruṣa</s> plus a <s>prādeśa</s>. 'To the south of that, another' etc. — as before. In the absence of <s>prādeśa</s>-extension, just as before. 'Because of hearing the modification' means because of the statement 'curved-winged, expanded-tailed' — this is the meaning.
'As per the primary' [section heading].

children.text: catuḥ puruṣaḥ samacaturaśra eva śyenacityātmā vikārasyāśravaṇāt
children.translated_text: The body of the hawk-altar is a perfect square of four <s>puruṣas</s>, because of non-hearing of modification.
<s>Kapardi's</s> commentary.

children.text: yatho etac cheyanacitaṃ cinvīteti | yāvadāmnānasārūpyaṃ tad vyākhyātam || ĀpŚus_21.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Thus one should pile this hawk-altar' — whatever resemblance is mentioned [in scripture], that has been explained. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.5]

children.text: jātivācakānāṃ śabdānāṃ kimapi sāmānyameva pravṛttinimittaṃ dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Of words denoting a class, only some general [feature] is seen as the cause of [their] application.
Just as [the word] 'cow' [applies to] a draught-animal.

children.text: evamatrāpi yāvadāmnānameva sārūpyaṃ gṛhītvā śyenaśabdo vartate /
children.translated_text: Similarly here too, the word '<s>śyena</s>' (hawk) operates having grasped only as much resemblance as is mentioned.
And that resemblance has been explained by 'curved-winged' etc.
There, only as much resemblance as is mentioned [in scripture] should be taken.
'The fire[-altar] is of three layers' — this is known in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice). [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.6]
There, the repetition of all [rituals applies], because of non-distinction. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.7]

children.text:
tatra nāratniprādeśasya saptavidhasyābhyāsaḥ /
kutaḥ? aviśeṣāt; na hi kaśvidviśeṣo 'trāmnāyate /
tasmātsarvasyāvṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the repetition is of the <s>sāratniprādeśa</s> seven-fold [altar], not [just any altar]. Why? Because of non-distinction — for no distinction is mentioned here. Therefore there is repetition of everything.

children.text: dīrghacaturaśrāṇāṃ samāsena pakṣapucchānāṃ samāsa uktaḥ || ĀpŚus_21.8 ||
children.translated_text: The joining of the rectangular wings and tail has been stated in brief. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.8]
The rule for joining the rectangular wings and tail has been stated.
By 'whatever is other than the seven[-fold]' etc., and by 'the <s>vidhā</s>-seventh-<s>karaṇī</s>' etc.
Or one may construct [them] with the bamboo-triple-<s>karaṇī</s> — this is the meaning.
'The fire[-altar] is of twenty-one [layers]' — this is known in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.9]
This has been explained.

children.text: tatra puruṣābhyāso nāratniprādeśānāṃ saṅkhyāsaṃyogāt saṅkhyāsaṃyogāt || ĀpŚus_21.10 ||
children.translated_text: There, the repetition is of the <s>puruṣa</s>[-measure], not of the <s>aratni-prādeśa</s> [additions], because of conjunction with the number. [<s>ĀpŚus</s> 21.10]
The <s>Śulba</s>-chapter is completed.

children.text:
tatra puruṣābhyāsaḥ nāratniprādeśānāṃ /
kutaḥ? saṃkhyāsaṃyogāt -- ekaviṃśa iti /
na saptavidha ityatrāpi saṃkhyā vidhīyate /
vākyāntareṇa tatra aratniprādeśā niviśante /
na tatra saptasaṃkhyāyāṃ niviśante /
tasmātsaṃkhyāsaṃyogāt puruṣābhyāsa eva nāratniprādeśānām /
tatra śloko bhavati ----
children.translated_text: Therein, the multiplication applies to <s>puruṣas</s> only, not to <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s>. Why? Because of the connection with number — "twenty-one" is [the number]. The number "seven" is not prescribed in "seven-fold" [as a separate injunction]. By another statement, the <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s> are included there. They are not included in the number seven. Therefore, because of the connection with number, only <s>puruṣas</s> are multiplied, not <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s>. Therein is a verse:
By the three-fold, the man[-measure] is stated; in the triple [fire-altar], those two [dimensions are thus],

children.text: eka (viṃśe) vidhe tatau nyūnaṃ tilānāṃ caiva sapta (bhiḥ)tiḥ //
children.translated_text: In the twenty-one-fold, that much diminished by seven <s>tilas</s>.
The repetition [of the chapter ending] is for auspiciousness.
Thus in the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) of <s>Kapardisvāmin</s> on the <s>Āpastamba</s> <s>sūtra</s> explanation,
the sixth section (<s>paṭala</s>) of the chapter (<s>praśna</s>) called <s>Śulba</s>.
<s>Karavindīyā</s> commentary
Now ... explained

children.text: śyenacitamiti vihitaṃ yatprakāraṃ yāvaccāsyāmnānasārūpyaṃ mānavihitaṃ śyenasārūpyaṃ tatsarvaṃ vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: The hawk-altar that is prescribed — whatever its form and as far as its conformity with the handed-down [shape], the hawk-resemblance prescribed by measurement — all that has been explained.

children.text: tatra vakrapakṣādiguṇairāmnātena yacchayenasya sārūpyamuktaṃ; śyenāgagnerardhadaśamā aratnaya ityādinā cayanaprakāra uktaḥ, tena uktau kaṅkālajau syātāmityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein, the resemblance to the hawk that was stated through the qualities of curved wings etc. as handed down; the mode of piling stated by "the hawk-fire [is measured by] nine-and-a-half <s>aratnīs</s>" etc. — by that, the two [layers] would correspond to the skeleton — this is the meaning.
Triple ... because

For the <s>Aśvamedha</s> fire [-altar], in the triple-sized form, the multiplication is of [the altar] with <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], not of the <s>puruṣa</s>-measure alone, because of the absence of a distinguishing [statement].
The meaning is: because the tripling is prescribed without distinction for the primary fire-altar.
Oblong ... stated
The combination of oblong quadrilaterals has been stated.

children.text: evaṃ dve dīrghacaturaśre samasyete; tannimitto nirhrāso vivṛddhirveti /
children.translated_text: Thus two oblong quadrilaterals are combined; the resulting decrease or increase [is calculated] accordingly.
"As many oblong quadrilaterals as one wishes, one should combine."
By that, for the triple fire[-altar], the combination by the first expansion method is stated.
Twenty-one ... because

children.text:
aśvamedhe ekaviṃśāgniśrutau puruṣāṇāmevābhyāsaḥ nāratniprādeśānām /
"saptavidho vāva prākṛto 'gniriti' saptasaṃkhyā pṛthaksaṃniveśanī /
samānajātīyeṣu puruṣeṣveva saṃyuktaḥ nāratnayādiṣu /
aratniprādeśāstvaratninā dakṣiṇata iti vākyena svarūpamātreṇa vihitā nārdhasaṃkhyayā /
ataḥ prakṛtau puruṣāṇāmeva saṃkhyā saṃyogādaśvamedhe 'pyekaviṃśāgnau puruṣāṇāmeva saṃkhyāsaṃyogo yukta iti aratniprādeśāstvanabhyastā bhaveyuḥ /

children.translated_text: After the multiplication of <s>puruṣas</s>, one should apply "with an <s>aratni</s> to the south" — this is the meaning.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati -- tristāve ekaviṃśaprastāradvayavidhestristāva ekaviṃśa evāgniḥ brāhnaṇadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: This amounts to saying: in the triple [altar], by the injunction of two layers of twenty-one [bricks each], the triple [altar] is itself the twenty-one-fold fire[-altar], as seen in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
[The layers] may be twelve or ten.
The repetition [of the ending] is for indicating the completion of the chapter (<s>praśna</s>).

In the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, when the twenty-one-fold fire[-altar] is enjoined by scripture, only <s>puruṣas</s> are multiplied, not <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s>. "The primary fire is indeed seven-fold" — the number seven is separately established. It is connected with <s>puruṣas</s> which are of the same kind, not with <s>aratnīs</s> etc. The <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s> are prescribed merely in their own form by the statement "with an <s>aratni</s> to the south," not by a fractional number. Therefore, since in the primary [altar] the number-connection is with <s>puruṣas</s> only, in the <s>Aśvamedha</s> too, in the twenty-one-fold fire[-altar], it is appropriate that the number-connection be with <s>puruṣas</s> only — the <s>aratnīs</s> and <s>prādeśas</s> should remain unmultiplied.
Thus ends the sixth section in the <s>Śulbapradīpikā</s> composed by <s>Karavindasvāmin</s>.
<s>Sundararājīyā</s> commentary

children.translated_text: Likewise in the northern wing, [placed] facing east.
All these [total] seventy-two.
Now, in the body, there should be nine rows facing east.
In the first [row], a fifth-part and a second-[type brick].

This [statement] "one should pile the hawk-altar" — whatever hawk-resemblance is prescribed by it, as far as what is handed down — "curved wings, reversed tail" — that is stated; otherwise, the prescriptions for modifications of wings and tail would become purposeless — this is the implication. On this interpretation, the brick-types (<s>karaṇas</s>): with a cord of two <s>puruṣas</s>, for the wing-bending, one-fourth of a <s>puruṣa</s> in length, one-fifth in breadth, bent as appropriate — that is the first; its one diagonal is eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, the other is fifteen-and-a-quarter <s>aṅgulas</s>. Two-by-two joined as before — that is the second. The first and fifth <s>karaṇas</s> joined [form] the third; the fourth, fifth, and sixth are just as in the previous hawk-altar. In the tail, whatever sixth-part and fourth-part [bricks] are to be placed — their other <s>karaṇas</s> [are defined]. Therein, for the fourth-part, the sides are as before: one transverse side of thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s>, another of forty-four-and-a-half <s>aṅgulas</s>. For the sixth-part, one plank of fifteen [parts]. The second is thirty-three <s>aṅgulas</s>; the third is thirty-six with eight <s>tilas</s>. The transverse sides of the seventh are each one <s>aratni</s> in measure. The lateral side is twenty-nine <s>aṅgulas</s>. And one diagonal. The other diagonal is forty-five <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by eleven <s>tilas</s>. The sides of the eighth are twenty-nine. The transverse sides are twelve and thirty-six. Because there is no head, the ninth <s>karaṇa</s> does not exist. Without <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> [extensions], the tail-bricks are just as in the previous hawk-altar. And the bending of wing-[bricks] follows proportionally. In the placement, in the first layer, in the wings, eighty first-[type bricks placed] facing north. The tail is as before. At the tail-junction, [bricks of] eighteen <s>aṅgulas</s> for the fourth-part [bricks]. In the tail, as in the previous hawk-altar. In the tail, fifteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks] in the body. In the body, nine rows facing north — with northward-facing bricks. Of those, the middle seven [rows]. With eight fourth-part [bricks] in the fourth row, in the southern row; then four sixth-part [bricks], two fourth-part [bricks]. Likewise the sixth row. At the hips and shoulders, four-by-four sixth-part [bricks]. In the remainder, six fifth-part [bricks]. This is the layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], at the curvatures, four-by-four second-[type bricks]. And at the junctions, third-[type bricks]. In the remainder of the wings, fifty-six first-[type bricks placed] facing east. The tail is as before. Seventh-[type] and eighth-[type bricks] in the body, nine rows facing east — with eastward-facing bricks. There, behind and in front of those at the wing-junctions, five-by-five fifth-[type] and six sixth-[type bricks]. Those in the middle of the southern and northern rows — seven rows as in the previous layer. In the middle of the second and sixth rows, sixteen-by-sixteen sixth-[type bricks]. Those in the middle of the southern and northern rows, as in the previous layer. In the middle of the second and eighth rows, sixteen-by-sixteen sixth-[type bricks]. Thus the layer of two hundred. In the other layer, in the wings, second-[type bricks]. From the wing-middle, second-[type bricks]. At the junction, in the remainder, first-[type bricks].
At the first wing-junction, two sixth-part [bricks] and a fifth-part likewise.
A fifth-part in the penultimate row; then two sixth-parts at the junction in front.
One sixth-part and a fifth-part should be in the second [row]; and in the row,
in the middle, sixteen sixth-parts should be — thus [constituting] the eighth row.
The fourth and sixth rows are like the first and the subsequent respectively.
The remainder of the body [is filled] with fourth-parts ... those pertaining to the tail.
Twelve seventh-[type bricks] and thirteen eighth-[type], as before.
Thus the second layer in the second [performance] is desired.

children.translated_text: Even on the interpretation that the body's bricks are as in the primary form, the wing-bricks should be seen as proportional to that.

But some [say]: because of the statement "as in the primary form," the bricks too [should follow the primary]. In the body, as in the primary form — thus they say. Accordingly, the sides of the first <s>karaṇa</s> are forty <s>aṅgulas</s>. The transverse sides are exactly one <s>aratni</s> each. One diagonal is twenty-five with seventeen <s>tilas</s>; the other is sixty-one <s>aṅgulas</s> diminished by three <s>tilas</s>. Two joined form the second <s>karaṇa</s>. [The first] augmented by the <s>aratni</s>-<s>prādeśa</s> of the first, bent as appropriate, [forms] the third. The tail, ninth, fourth, sixth, seventh, and eighth [<s>karaṇas</s>] are as before, as in the primary form. The body's bricks are fifth-part [bricks]. There, <s>prādeśa</s>-[bricks] should be made six <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth. In the body, to the south and north, ten-and-a-half [bricks placed] facing north. In the remainder of the body, ten rows of fifth-[part bricks] facing north. In the middle, having removed two, [place] eighteen-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. At the tail-junction, two fourth-parts. "The body with an <s>aratni</s>" — two on each side, four six-<s>aṅgula</s>-breadth [bricks]. Behind those at the tail-junction, five halves facing east. The tail-remainder is as before. In the wings, thirty-by-thirty first-[type bricks placed] facing north. This is the layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], three-by-three at the curvatures, second-[type bricks]. In the remainder of the wings, forty-two first-[type bricks placed] facing east. The tail is as before. In the body, nine rows facing north. Of those, the first and last rows with eastward-facing half-[bricks]; the last [rows] with fifth-[type bricks]; of the five middle rows, the first and others are half-[bricks] — placed facing east. Of the second [row], having removed from the end, there eight six-<s>aṅgula</s>-breadth [bricks] should be placed; there, behind and in front, two-by-two facing north. In the middle, four facing east. In the eighth row, at the first and last [positions], having removed the second and last, nine-by-nine eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. Layer of two hundred. When placed with square [bricks], the wings are likewise. But the tail is just as before. At the wing-junction, two <s>aṇūkās</s>. Having reached the body with a <s>prādeśa</s>, on both sides, two-by-two six-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]; these six should be encompassed with ten <s>prādeśas</s>. In the remainder of the body, <s>aratni</s>-[bricks]. Layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], in the joint-intervals, forty-five <s>aratni</s>-[bricks]. At the hips and shoulders, twelve-by-twelve <s>aṇūkās</s> and quarter-bricks. In the remainder, twenty <s>aṇūkās</s>. Having removed the body-middle, nine eight-<s>aṅgula</s> [bricks]. When the wing-bending is with a cord of six hundred <s>aṅgulas</s>, then one-fifth of a <s>puruṣa</s> in length and one-sixth in breadth is one [option for] the first <s>karaṇa</s>. Bent as appropriate — its diagonal is twenty-three <s>aṅgulas</s> with twenty-one <s>tilas</s>; the other is thirty-seven with eleven <s>tilas</s>. Having drawn on the ground an oblong quadrilateral of twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> in length with thirteen <s>tilas</s> and fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth, extending eastward, with a cord of sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> with loops at both ends, one should bend it like the wing. That [is] the second (third). Of the first, the sixth-part should be augmented by an eighth-part, bent as appropriate — that [is] the third. The others are as before. In the placement, in the first layer, at the curvatures, six-by-six second-[type bricks]. In the remainder of the wings, seventy-two first-[type bricks placed] facing north. The tail and body are as before. At the hips and shoulders, two-by-two sixth-part [bricks]. Layer of two hundred. In the other [layer], in the wings, seventy first-[type bricks],
Triple ... is prescribed

children.text: "dvistāvātristāvā vediḥ' ityatra liṅgasyāvivakṣitatvāda gneś ca vedeś ca vivakṣi (vihi) tatvātsamāsāntaḥ /

children.translated_text: It is the basic fire-altar itself, the seven-fold one, that is tripled here.

children.text: na tvanantara (guṇasya) kṛtasyābhyāsasya sarvābhyāso viśeṣo 'taḥsarvasya sāratniprādeśasyaivābhyāsaḥ; tristāvasya vidhau vidhābhyāsavat puruṣāṇāmiti viśeṣāśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: But it is not the case that the repetition of the immediately [preceding] constructed one is a repetition of all — the distinguishing point is this: the repetition is of the entire [altar] with <s>aratni-prādeśa</s> only; because no specification 'of the <s>puruṣas</s>' is heard in the rule for the tripled [altar], just as in the repetition of the ritual forms.
Thus the fire-altar becomes twenty-three and a half <s>puruṣas</s>.
The <s>veṇu</s> (measuring reed) of three <s>karaṇīs</s> of the <s>puruṣa</s> — eighteen [times] two <s>aṅgulas</s> less five <s>tilās</s> — serves as the <s>puruṣa</s>-equivalent.

In the [statement] 'the altar is twice as large, thrice as large,' since the gender [of the compound] is not intended, and since both the fire[-altar] and the altar are intended, [the compound takes] the final suffix.
'The rectangle — is stated' —

children.text: tulyayoś caturaśrayor ity atraiva prakāra uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of two equal squares' — the method is stated in that very [passage].
And of the transverse measure and the side measure, the side measure is the <s>trikaraṇī</s> (triple-root).
'Twenty-one — is obtained' —

children.text: śākhāntare "ekaviṃśatiḥ puruṣaḥ parimāṇa' ityekaviṃśaḥ satomor'dhavidhaṃ pañcāśadadhyardhāḥ ityatropadheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In another <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic school), 'twenty-one <s>puruṣas</s> is the measure' — [this] twenty-one is to be applied in 'the <s>Atoma</s> [-sacrifice], half-ritual, [altar of] fifty-[bricks], with an extra half.'
Because of being generally [applicable], in the <s>Atoma</s> also.
There, because of non-conjunction —

children.text:
saṃkhyā hi tulyajātīyasya saṃkhyāntarasyaiva nivartikā; yathā vidhābhyāseṣviti bhāvaḥ /
asmin pakṣe ardhadvāviṃśāḥ puruṣāstatra dve śate tisraśvāṅgulayaḥ ṣaṭtilāḥ puruṣasthānīyo veṇuḥ /
tasya caturthapañcamaṣaṣṭhadaśamā aṇūkāratnyūrvasthiprādeśā avagantavyāḥ /
aratniprādeśābhāve 'pi pakṣadvaye 'pyekaviṃśatireva puruṣāḥ /
śrīmadrāmāyaṇe tvaṣṭādaśapuruṣatvamasvamedhāgnerdṛśyate ----
children.translated_text:
For a number is the remover only of another number of the same kind; just as in the repetitions of ritual forms — this is the meaning.
In this view, the <s>puruṣas</s> are twenty-two and a half; there, two hundred and three <s>aṅgulas</s> and six <s>tilās</s> [constitute] the <s>veṇu</s> serving as the <s>puruṣa</s>-equivalent.
Its fourth, fifth, sixth, and tenth [parts] should be understood as the <s>aṇūka</s>, <s>aratni</s>, <s>ūrvasthi</s>, and <s>prādeśa</s> [measures].
Even without the <s>aratni-prādeśa</s>, in both wings there are twenty-one <s>puruṣas</s> only.
In the glorious <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, however, the <s>Aśvamedha</s> fire-altar is seen as being of eighteen <s>puruṣas</s> —
That fire-altar of the lion among kings was constructed by skilled <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
[It was] of the <s>Gāruḍa</s> (eagle) type, with golden wings, indeed tripled, of eighteen [<s>puruṣas</s>].

sa tu śākhāntare (ṇa) ṣaḍvidhasyāpi kṛtitvadarśanāt /
tristāvo 'vagantavyaḥ /
uktaṃ hi ṣaḍvidhasyāpi prakṛtitvaṃ bodhā yanena -- "ṣaḍvidhaṃ saptavidhaṃ dvādaśavidhaṃ vā yāvadvidhaṃ vā ceṣyamāṇo bhavati' iti /
atra trayodaśavidhāntānagnīn citvāśvamedhamārabhate /
sa tataḥ paramagniṃ cinvāno dvāviṃśatyādividhameva cinvīta /
na tu pūrvavidham /
na jyāyāsaṃ citvā kanīyāsaṃ cinvīta' iti /
atha yo dvāviṃśatividhādūrdhvamapi vidhāmabhyasya tataḥ paramaśvamedhamārabhate yathā triṃśadvidhānte; tasyāpyaśvamedhāgnistristāvaka ekaviṃśo vā tasya prakārāntarābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Now, one who, having repeatedly performed rituals beyond the twenty-two-fold form, then undertakes the supreme <s>Aśvamedha</s>, as at the end of the thirty-fold — for him too the <s>Aśvamedha</s> fire-altar is either tripled or of twenty-one [<s>puruṣas</s>], since there is no alternative method for it.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ tu pūrvakṛtādārabhyaikattriṃśadvidhādikam eva cinvīta /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, he should construct only the thirty-one-fold and higher, beginning from the previously performed one.

children.text: pūrveṣāṃ kṛtatvāt; vyañjitaṃ caitatsarvaṃ bodhāyanena -- "aśvamedhaḥ prāptaśvedāharedata ūrdhvāṃ vidhāmabyasyennetarānādriyeta /
children.translated_text: Because the earlier ones have been performed; and all this has been indicated by <s>Bodhāyana</s> — 'At the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, [if] one who has attained [a certain level] brings this, he should repeat the higher ritual form and not attend to others.
If [the level] has been passed, having brought [it], at the end of what has been done, he should take up from the basic [form].'

Thus.
But that, in another <s>śākhā</s>, since even the six-fold [altar] is seen to have been constructed,
it should be understood as tripled.
For the basic nature even of the six-fold [altar] has been stated by <s>Bodhāyana</s> — 'He who is about to sacrifice performs the six-fold, seven-fold, twelve-fold, or whatever-fold [altar].'
Here, having constructed fire-altars up to the thirteen-fold, one undertakes the <s>Aśvamedha</s>.
Thereafter, one constructing the supreme fire-altar should construct only the twenty-two-fold and higher forms.
But not the earlier form.
'Having constructed a greater one, one should not construct a lesser one.'

children.text: iti śrī sundararājīye śulbapradīpe ṣaṣṭhaḥ paṭalaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth chapter in the <s>Śulbapradīpa</s> of Śrī <s>Sundararāja</s>.

children.text: iti sundararājīyaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ samāptaḥ savyākhya āpastambīyaśulbapraśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sundararājīya</s> [commentary] is complete. The <s>Āpastambīya Śulbapraśna</s> (Āpastamba's Śulba Questions) with commentary is concluded.
